title: Fix matplotlib.use() compatibility with Matplotlib >= 3.3.0
description:
### Intent

Fix a `TypeError` during Matplotlib initialization in RStudio sessions using reticulate.

The `warn` argument of `matplotlib.use()` was deprecated in Matplotlib 3.2.0 and removed in Matplotlib 3.3.0.

RStudio still passes `warn = FALSE`, which causes the following error with newer Matplotlib versions:

```text
TypeError: use() got an unexpected keyword argument 'warn'
```

This can prevent TensorFlow and Keras3 from initializing correctly in the RStudio IDE.

### Approach

Remove the unsupported `warn = FALSE` argument from the call in `SessionReticulate.R`:

```diff
- matplotlib$use("agg", warn = FALSE, force = TRUE)
+ matplotlib$use("agg", force = TRUE)
```

The `force = TRUE` argument is preserved. No other behavior is changed.

### Automated Tests

No automated tests were added for this one-line compatibility fix.

The change was manually validated in an installed RStudio environment.

### QA Notes

Tested on Debian 12 with:

- Python 3.11
- Matplotlib 3.6.3
- reticulate 1.47.0
- TensorFlow and Keras3

Before the fix, initialization could fail with the `TypeError` above.

After applying the change and restarting RStudio, TensorFlow and Keras3 initialized and ran successfully on the first attempt.

### Documentation

No user-facing documentation changes are required.

title: feat(jenkins): dispatch e2e-docker GHA from daily builds (rstudio-ide-automation#6105)
description:
## Summary

Every daily `main` and `rel-*` build now also dispatches the GHA docker e2e suite (`rstudio-ide-automation` `e2e-docker.yaml`) next to the existing Jenkins `qa-opensource-automation` trigger, so the two run side by side (rstudio/rstudio-ide-automation#6105, Stage B rstudio/rstudio-ide-automation#6122). **The Jenkins trigger is unchanged.**

- New stage `Trigger Docker E2E (GHA)` in `Trigger Testing Jobs`, after `Trigger Automation Testing`. It inherits the parent guards (`DAILY`, `PUBLISH`, branch not `release-ghost-orchid` or `v1.4-juliet-rose`) and adds `BRANCH_NAME` is `main` or starts with `rel-`, plus the OS/ARCH/FLAVOR filters allowing jammy, x86_64 and Server (so a filtered rebuild without that `.deb` does not dispatch).
- Inputs: `product=os`, `version=${RSTUDIO_VERSION}` (exact), `product_branch=${BRANCH_NAME}`. Shards and retries stay at the workflow defaults.
- Wrapped in `catchError(buildResult: SUCCESS, stageResult: FAILURE)`: a failed dispatch turns only the stage red, never the build.
- `jenkins/utils.groovy`: ports `githubApiRequest` and `triggerGitHubWorkflow` verbatim from rstudio-pro (plus its optional `timeoutSecs`, default 0 = unbounded, so existing callers are unchanged). The stage passes 60 so a stalled GitHub call fails fast. A trial rstudio -> rstudio-pro upstream merge is conflict-free.

`rel-*` branches dispatch too. A release branch cut before the suite move has no `e2e/rstudio-pro` for the workflow to clone, so the dispatched GHA run fails at clone time. The Jenkins stage still goes green, because the dispatch returns 204 and Jenkins does not wait for the run.

## QA Notes

- Jenkins declarative linter: `Jenkinsfile successfully validated.`
- Exact-version dispatch checked by hand (runs 39347306721 Pro, 39347336503 OS): `Prepare` resolved the version and passed the `.deb` check.
- First real check is the next daily on `main` (and the next `rel-*` daily): the stage log shows `Dispatched rstudio/rstudio-ide-automation workflow ...` and a matching `e2e-docker` run appears. If the GitHub App token cannot dispatch cross-repo, the stage goes red and the build result stays SUCCESS.

Companion PR: [rstudio/rstudio-pro#13282](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/pull/13282) (same stage text, plus the `timeoutSecs` helper change this ports).

title: scroll by one row when continuing a comment on a new line
description:
### Intent

With "Continue comments on new lines" enabled, pressing Return on a `#` (or `#'`, `#|`) line near the bottom of the editor jumped the viewport so the cursor landed about seven rows from the top, instead of scrolling by one row the way a plain Return does. Shift+Return in the same configuration did not scroll at all, leaving the cursor just below the viewport.

Fixes #19185.

### Approach

The comment-continuation handlers insert the newline themselves (so Ace's `insertstring` command, which scrolls minimally, never runs) and then called `ensureCursorVisible()`. That helper jumps the cursor to near the top of the viewport whenever the cursor row is not fully visible -- and right after an insert it never is, because Ace's layer config is only refreshed on the next render.

This adds a `scrollCursorIntoView()` binding to Ace's `renderer.scrollCursorIntoView()` and uses it in the two continuation handlers and the Shift+Return branch. `ensureCursorVisible()` is unchanged for its other callers (go to definition, code browser, console), which want the near-top placement after a long jump.

Not a regression: the handler has behaved this way since it was written; the 2026.10 smooth-scrolling change on this path is a no-op with that pref off, and the jump reproduces with it off.

### Automated Tests

New Playwright spec `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/comment_continuation_scroll.test.ts` parks the cursor at the end of the last fully visible row and checks that Return on `# `, Return on `#' `, and Shift+Return each move the viewport by exactly one row and keep the cursor fully visible. It fails on main (first visible row off by 13) and passes with this change.

### QA Notes

Enable Tools > Global Options > Code > Editing > "Continue comments on new lines". In a script long enough to scroll, put the cursor at the end of a `# comment` line on the last visible row and press Return: the view should scroll by one line, not jump. Repeat with a `#' roxygen` line, and with Shift+Return on any line.

### Documentation

None needed; no UI or behaviour beyond the fix.

title: Resolve Snyk Code medium and low findings in core and shared_core
description:
### Intent

`snyk code test` on the Launcher repository reports 12 medium and low findings in `src/cpp/core` and `src/cpp/shared_core` that https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/19153 does not fix. Launcher gets these folders from rstudio-pro, which merges this repository, so the fixes must land here. This PR removes all 12 findings without Snyk ignores. It is the upstream part of https://github.com/rstudio/launcher/pull/1800.

| Rule | Severity | File |
|---|---|---|
| `cpp/CodeInjection` | medium | `core/libclang/LibClang.cpp` |
| `cpp/UseAfterFree`, `cpp/DoubleFree` | medium | `core/tex/synctex/synctex_parser.c` |
| `cpp/UnsafeFunctionStringHandling` | medium | `core/tex/synctex/synctex_parser_utils.c` |
| `cpp/TooSmallKeySize` (2) | medium | `shared_core/system/encryption/EncryptionVersion.cpp` |
| `cpp/PT` | low | `core/StartupTiming.cpp` |
| `cpp/WeakGuard` | low | `core/include/core/http/URL.hpp` |
| `cpp/PT` (test, 3) | low | `core/Win32FileLockTests.cpp` |
| `cpp/PT` (test) | low | `core/system/XdgTests.cpp` |

Review found one more real bug next to these findings, in the SyncTeX updater.

### Approach

Each fix is a separate commit. The real fixes and the rewrites with no behavior change are in different commits. Each rewrite has a short comment that says why to keep its form, so that a later edit does not bring the finding back. I tested each candidate form with `snyk code test` before I used it.

#### Real fixes

**SyncTeX updater allocation** (da240e053d). `synctex_updater_new_with_output_file()` allocated `sizeof(synctex_updater_t)`. That type is a pointer, so the allocation is 8 bytes. The function then writes the `fprintf` and `flags` fields past the end of it, and the append functions later use `length` there. The fix allocates `sizeof(_synctex_updater_t)`, the struct. No RStudio code calls the updater API, so this does not change what RStudio does today.

**`vsprintf` in `_synctex_error()`** (e1bfe0789d). The `SYNCTEX_RECENT_WINDOWS` branch now writes with `vsnprintf()` and the buffer length. It also skips the message and returns -1 if `malloc()` fails, because the old code then wrote to a NULL pointer. Current builds probably do not compile this branch: `_WIN32_WINNT_WINXP` comes from `<sdkddkver.h>`, and the file includes `<windows.h>` only after the check.

#### Change with a small, documented behavior change

**`RSTUDIO_LIBCLANG_PATH`** (3edffa0283). Snyk Code accepts an environment variable path for `dlopen()` only after `realpath()` resolves it. `std::filesystem::canonical()`, `weakly_canonical()`, Boost `canonical()`, prefix checks, and file name checks do not clear the finding. The fix uses the existing `core::system::realPath()` for the load path of the environment variable only. That function calls `realpath()` on POSIX and `GetFullPathNameW()` on Windows.

- The diagnostics, the embedded-library check, and the clang header search (`defaultCompileArgs()`) still use the path as given.
- The embedded and system candidates load the same paths as before.
- If the variable names a symlink, `dlopen()` now receives the target path. Then `$ORIGIN` in the library's RUNPATH is the directory of the target, not of the link.
- If the variable is a relative path, the loader now receives the absolute path of the file that the `exists()` check found in the working directory. Before, a bare name such as `libclang.so` made `dlopen()` search the library path.

#### Rewrites with no behavior change

| Commit | Change | Why the result is the same |
|---|---|---|
| 2dd4a1b4dd | The SyncTeX updater error path has no `goto` into other blocks | Each path frees `synctex` and the updater once, as before. The success path does not change. |
| b0e81facfc | `StartupTiming` resolves the file with `core::system::realPath()` before each write. On POSIX, it first creates a missing file with `FilePath::openForWrite(..., false)`. | On POSIX, `openForWrite(..., false)` opens the same `std::ofstream` append mode as before. On Windows, `GetFullPathNameW()` does not need the file to exist. The session still creates a missing file and appends one line for each checkpoint. |
| 6efd821e1f | v0 and v1 call `EVP_aes_128_cbc()` through `s_aes128Cbc`, a const function pointer | It is the same function. The new known-answer tests (4e20219840) check the exact bytes. |
| fa0b4535ad | `URL::clientHost()` compares with a table of the four wildcard strings | The same four strings map to `localhost`. |
| a4b2ee35c1 | The Windows lock test uses `FilePath::tempFilePath()`, not `%USERPROFILE%` | The test checks the same lock behavior on a new temporary file. |
| e8f9e154c2 | The XDG test removes its symlink with `FilePath::remove()`, not `::unlink()` | Boost `remove_all()` deletes the link and does not follow it. A new check confirms that the target is still there. |

**Why AES-128-CBC stays.** The v0 and v1 formats are AES-128-CBC, and `defaultMaximumEncryptionVersion` is 0. Stored data and other components depend on these bytes. For example, the Launcher Local plugin decrypts the password that Workbench sends with `crypto::decryptAndBase64Decode()`. A cipher change would break them. The v2 format already uses AES-256-GCM. To lock this down, 4e20219840 adds a known-answer test. It uses the CBC-AES128 example from NIST SP 800-38A, appendix F.2.1, plus the PKCS#7 padding block. The test fails if the v0 or v1 cipher, key length, or padding changes.

### Automated Tests

- New: `SharedCoreTest.LegacyEncryptionVersionsMatchAes128CbcKnownAnswer` checks v0 and v1 encryption and decryption against the NIST vector.
- Changed: `XdgTest.TemporaryUserDataDir` now also checks that removing the symlink keeps its target.
- Build: macOS arm64, apple-clang 21, Conan Boost 1.91.0 and OpenSSL 3.5.8, RelWithDebInfo. I built inside the Launcher tree, which compiles the same `core` and `shared_core` sources. All changed files compile with no warnings. `Win32FileLockTests.cpp` compiles to nothing on macOS. I did not build on Linux or Windows, and I did not build `session` or the desktop.
- `rstudio-shared-core-tests`: 21 passed, including the new known-answer test.
- `rstudio-server-core-tests`: 46 passed, 11 skipped.
- `rstudio-core-tests`: 792 passed, 9 skipped, 2 failed: `PosixTests.FindSubprocessNameViaPgrep` and `PosixTests.FindSubprocessNameMac`. Both fail the same way on this Mac without this PR.
- `StartupTiming`: a small program calls `checkpoint()` against the built library. It gives the same result as before for a missing file (the file is created with two lines), an existing file (two lines appended), a missing folder (nothing written), a relative path, and an unset variable.
- `LibClang::load()`: a small program built once with the old and once with the new `LibClang.cpp` prints the same diagnostics and loads the same library in six cases: no variable, a missing path, a real path, a symlink, a bare relative name, and a relative path with a slash. This used the macOS Command Line Tools libclang 21.
- `snyk code test` on Launcher, with this diff applied to its synced folders and with the next rstudio-pro sync merged in: 0 issues.

### QA Notes

No QA is needed. The changes are internal. The only runtime difference is for an `RSTUDIO_LIBCLANG_PATH` that is a symlink or a relative path, as described above.

### Documentation

No documentation changes. `RSTUDIO_LIBCLANG_PATH` is not documented. No `NEWS.md` entry, because users do not see these changes.

### Checklist

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [x] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: Match build-info.ts R minimum placeholder to 3.6.0
description:
The checked-in \`src/node/desktop/src/main/build-info.ts\` had placeholder values of 3.0.1 for the minimum required R version. Dev builds use this file. The CMake build writes its own copy into \`desktop-build-<arch>/\` from \`build-info.ts.in\`, and that copy takes the minimum from \`RSTUDIO_R_VERSION_REQUIRED\` (3.6.0, set in \`cmake/globals.cmake\`). Nothing in the Desktop code reads these fields.

This changes the placeholder from 3.0.1 to 3.6.0 so it matches the actual minimum. Behavior does not change.

title: classify base environment bindings without a frame cell on R < 4.6
description:
Fixes #19189.

### Intent

On R < 4.6, `getBindingType` falls back to `R_findVarLocInFrame()` and reads the result as a frame binding cell. The base environment and base namespace keep their bindings on the symbol (`SYMVALUE`), so R returns the symbol there (R >= 3.6) or raises an R error (R < 3.6). `CAR()` of a symbol is its print name, not its value, so delayed and missing bindings in base were reported as plain values, and the Environment pane forced them when listing `package:base`.

### Approach

- `src/cpp/r/RRuntime.cpp`: for `R_BaseEnv` / `R_BaseNamespace`, read the symbol's value slot directly instead of calling `R_findVarLocInFrame()`, and classify from there. The active-binding bit is the same on symbols and frame cells, so that check is shared. Frame-cell handling is unchanged.
- `EnvironmentBindingTypeTests.cpp`: covers delayed (`.Last.value`, reassigned with `delayedAssign()` since the base frame is locked), active, forced lazy-load (`pi`), plain (`.Machine`) and unbound bindings in both base environments, plus `isUnevaluatedPromise()`, which the Environment pane uses.

R >= 4.6 is unaffected: `R_GetBindingType()` handles base bindings itself.

### QA Notes

Ran the new test under R 4.6.1 (native path) and R 4.5.3 (fallback path). With the fix reverted it fails on 4.5.3 and passes on 4.6.1.

### Checklist

- [x] Changes and QA notes are described
- [x] Includes a NEWS entry
- [x] Includes tests

title: Make panes hidden by zoom inert
description:
Fixes #19181.

A column collapsed by a zoom command, or dragged shut with a column splitter, stayed in the accessibility tree and the Tab order. Its panes are now inert.

### Inert columns

`MainSplitPanel` marks a column's layout container `inert` (with `aria-hidden`) while the column is narrower than 20px, and clears it once the column widens. It checks after every layout pass and at the end of every animated resize. That covers:

- the column zooms (left/center, right, sidebar)
- pane zooms such as Zoom Console or Zoom Files
- splitter drags, by mouse or keyboard
- window resizes

Splitters sit outside the containers, so they stay reachable.

Quadrants needed no change: a maximized pane's sibling, or a quadrant snapped shut with the row splitter, is already `display:none`.

### Focus

When a zoom, splitter drag or window resize hides the element that has focus, the browser would drop focus to the page body. `PaneManager` instead moves it to a pane that is still showing:

- A pane zoom, or zooming another tab of the zoomed pane, focuses the zoomed pane.
- When a layout pass makes the column holding focus inert (a column zoom, a mouse drag of a splitter, a window shrink), `MainSplitPanel` reports it, and focus goes to the topmost visible pane with a tab in the widest column, falling back to the topmost visible pane.
- Within the pane, focus goes to the selected tab without changing which tab is selected, so a Console pane showing Terminal keeps Terminal.
- A pane with no tabs, such as an empty sidebar, gets its first control (Configure Panes), then its frame buttons.

Focus is left alone when the focused element stays visible, or when something else moved focus during the zoom.

### Tests

`e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/layout/zoom_inert.test.ts` covers the accessibility tree and inert state for:

- column, pane and sidebar zooms
- mouse and keyboard splitter drags
- quadrant maximize and splitter snap

It also covers focus after zooms that hide the focused pane, quadrant, or tab, after a mouse drag or window shrink that shuts the focused column, and after zooming another tab of a zoomed pane. `panes.test.ts` adds the empty-sidebar and empty-tabset focus cases, which need the Pane Layout dialog.

title: Resolve Snyk Code integer overflow findings
description:
Snyk Code reports 22 `cpp/IntegerOverflow` findings: 19 in production code and 3 in tests. They trace back to four places. One place has a real unsigned wraparound. At the other three, the arithmetic cannot wrap, but Snyk does not recognize the existing guards. Review found two more real issues nearby. The real fixes and the false-positive rewrites are in separate commits.

## Real issues

**Update-check output parsing** (f74667c387, tests in f16589edca)

`jsonFromProcessResult()` in `SessionUpdates.cpp` tested `pos > 0` after `line.find('=')`. For a line with no `=`, `find()` returns `npos`, which passes that test. Then `pos + 1` wraps to 0, and the whole line becomes both the key and the value.

The parser now skips lines that have no `=`. Lines that contain `=` give the same key and value as before. The frontend reads only the `update-message`, `update-urgent`, `update-url`, and `update-version` keys (`UpdateCheckResult.java`), so it does not see the dropped entries. The function is now `parseUpdateCheckOutput()`. It takes the output string and is declared in `SessionUpdates.hpp`, so that `SessionUpdatesTests.cpp` can test it.

**Negative Content-Length in assistant responses** (81730c5eb0)

`onStdout()` in `SessionAssistant.cpp` added the parsed Content-Length, an `int`, to `bodyStart`. A negative value wrapped `bodyEnd` to a position before `bodyStart`, and the parser moved backwards. For example, a first response of `Content-Length: -23` and a blank line is 23 bytes, so `bodyEnd` is 0 and the loop never ends. The parser now logs an error and stops on a negative length. Other values behave as before.

**Off-by-one in `obfuscatedUserId()`** (eb7ecae8c7)

A uid above `MAX_UID` is remapped to its difference from the minimum uid when that difference fits in the 5-digit ID. The check was `uid - minUid < MAX_UID`, but a difference of exactly `MAX_UID` also fits. The check is now `<= MAX_UID`. This changes the ID for one uid, `minUid + 0xFFFFF`: with a minimum of 1000, uid 1049575 now gets `fffff` instead of `1003e`.

## False positives: rewrites with no behavior change (75e7d0ad52, comments in e6a474ae34)

| Function | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `obfuscatedUserId()`, `RSessionContext.cpp` | `uid >= minUid && ...` | `minUid <= uid && ...` |
| `substring()`, `StringUtils.hpp` | `substr(startPos, endPos - startPos)` | returns `substr(startPos)` when `endPos < startPos`, else the same call as before |
| `utf8ToSystemImpl()`, `StringUtils.cpp` (Windows only) | `0x10000 + ((hi - 0xD800) << 10) + (lo - 0xDC00)` | `0x10000 + (((hi & 0x3FF) << 10) \| (lo & 0x3FF))` |

Why each rewrite gives the same result:

- `obfuscatedUserId()`: the comparison is the same, with its operands swapped. Snyk accepts the guard only in this order.
- `substring()`: when `endPos < startPos`, the old count wrapped to a value larger than the rest of the string, so `substr()` returned the rest of the string. The new branch returns the same thing. `substr()` still throws `std::out_of_range` when `startPos` is past the end.
- `utf8ToSystemImpl()`: the existing range check limits the high surrogate to `0xD800..0xDBFF` and the low surrogate to `0xDC00..0xDFFF`. In those ranges, `& 0x3FF` gives the same value as the subtraction. The two parts use separate bits, so `|` gives the same value as `+`.

Comments in the code give the reason for each form, so that a later edit does not restore the form that Snyk flags.

## Verification

- A standalone harness ran the old and new code on the same inputs:
  - Update-check parsing: 21,845 single lines and 200,000 random documents. Old and new agree on every line that contains `=`.
  - `substring()`: 31,452 calls on `std::string` and `std::wstring`. The results and the `std::out_of_range` throws match, including 14,322 calls with `endPos < startPos`.
  - Surrogate decode: all 1,048,576 valid pairs match.
  - `obfuscatedUserId()` operand swap: about 4 million `(uid, minUid)` pairs match.
  - `obfuscatedUserId()` off-by-one: old and new differ on 8 of 1.8 million pairs, all at `uid - minUid == MAX_UID`. The new unit test fails on the old code and passes on the new code.
  - Content-Length: on `Content-Length: -23`, the old loop hits a 1,000-iteration cap and the new loop stops. Inputs without a negative length give the same responses as before.
- With `-fsanitize=unsigned-integer-overflow`, the new code gives zero reports. The old code triggers it in `jsonFromProcessResult()` and `substring()`.
- `snyk code test` reports 0 `cpp/IntegerOverflow` findings on this branch, down from 22. The other findings do not change.
- I did not compile these changes locally. The `StringUtils.cpp` change is in Windows-only code.

title: e2e: dismiss on-open suggestions before nes renames
description:
Hardens the Posit AI / Copilot next-edit suggestion specs against two things seen in the server-linux failure of `NES gap rename` on PR #19158 (run 38982090628, [report](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-19158/38982090628-1/all-platforms/index.html)).

What happened there: the moment the test file opened, the model answered the on-open request with a next-edit suggestion that inserted a copy of lines 7-9. The test then typed the rename, the pre-edit suggestion survived it (as suggestions are meant to), and `acceptNesRename` applied it. The stale lines went in and `print(order_total)` was never renamed. On the retry the model declined every request, which is the live-model behavior already documented in `waitForSuggestion`.

Changes:

- `SourcePaneActions.dismissSuggestionsFromOpen()`: new helper that presses Escape until no suggestion is on screen and no completion request is pending, so the only suggestion a test can accept is one made for the edit it typed. Called after the open in every NES spec that edits and then waits for a suggestion. It replaces the "stale NES gutter icon" warning in the adjacent-rename spec, since Escape clears that marker too.
- `SourcePane.ghostText`: filtered to elements that carry text. Multi-line ghost text is an inline token for the first line plus a line widget for the rest; when the suggestion starts with a newline that token is empty, so `ghostText.first()` landed on a zero-size span and `acceptNesRename` reported no ghost text while the widget was plainly on screen. That is why the failing run fell through to the gutter click instead of logging the suggestion it accepted.

Test-only change; no NEWS entry. The `@ai` specs need live provider credentials, so this was checked with `npm run typecheck` and `playwright test --list` locally and relies on CI for the run.

title: Expose DataGrid header and body as one table to screen readers
description:
GWT's `DataGrid` keeps its header fixed while the body scrolls by rendering the header and body as separate `<table>` elements. Screen readers saw a table of column headers with no data and a separate data table with no headers, so moving through cells in the Files pane, the Environment grid view and other grids announced no column header.

## Changes

- Uses GWT `2.13.1-montauk-daisy-3`, built from rstudio/gwt#21. In it, the `DataGrid` element is a `role="table"`, its inner tables are presentational, and rows and cells get explicit `row`, `columnheader`/`rowheader` and `cell` roles, so the header and body read as one table. The loading and empty-table messages read as a row of that table.
- Rows that exist only for layout are marked `role="presentation"`, so they don't read as blank rows: the padding rows `VirtualizedDataGrid` adds above and below the rendered window (Files pane, object explorer), and the width-setting row of the Environment pane's list view.
- NEWS entry.

## Testing

New e2e tests:
- Files pane, in a directory of 300 files so the virtualized grid adds padding: one table, whose header row holds the five column headers and whose rows hold the file cells; padding rows are `presentation`, and every row the table exposes is a header or file row.
- Environment grid view with `x <- 1:3`: one table with the column headers and the `x`/`integer` cells.
- Empty Environment grid view: one table, whose second row is a cell reading "Environment is empty".

Against `2.13.1-montauk-daisy-2`, the Files and empty Environment tests fail with two tables. Against the published `2.13.1-montauk-daisy-3`, `files_column_headers.test.ts` and `environment_pane.test.ts` pass (12 tests). `ant javac` builds from clean against the published SDK.

## Manual verification

| Grid | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Files pane | VoiceOver, Chrome and Safari: moving through cells | Column headers announced |
| Environment grid view | VoiceOver, Chrome and Safari: moving through cells | Column headers announced |
| Empty Environment grid view | VoiceOver, Safari (before the message row roles were added) | "Environment is empty" read as row 2 of the table |
| Files pane | Chrome accessibility tree (CDP) | One table: header row of five column headers, then file rows; no nested table |

Not checked with a screen reader: Packages, Connections, the object explorer, and the Modify Keyboard Shortcuts, Browse Addins, renv and Packrat dialogs (all use the same `DataGrid`), or NVDA.

Fixes #19173.

title: Keep the path breadcrumb fade decorative and at the visible edge
description:
Fixes #19172.

The fade at the left edge of a scrolled path (Files pane and file dialogs) had no alt text. In light editor themes its wrapper wasn't positioned, so the fade image sat at the start of the scrolled content: out of view while the bar was scrolled, and over the root `/` link, taking its clicks, once the bar scrolled back (e.g. when focus moved to that link). The fade was also only updated when the widget scrolled the bar itself.

Changes in `PathBreadcrumbWidget` and `FileDialogStyles.css`:

- The fade image has `alt=""`.
- The wrapper is absolutely positioned in every theme, with `pointer-events: none`.
- The fade is placed on every scroll of the bar, not just when the widget scrolls it.
- Visibility is toggled with a class instead of an inline `display`, so the dark file dialog rule that hides the fade still applies. The fade also starts hidden.
- In the main window, where each theme paints the wrapper with a gradient of its own background, the fixed-color fade image is hidden, so the fade matches the theme. File dialogs sit outside the themed container, so light ones keep the image.

In light editor themes the fade is now visible at the left edge while the path is scrolled. Before, it was always out of view.

Tests, in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/files/files_breadcrumb_fade.test.ts`:

- Files pane: the fade image has empty alt text and is hidden in favor of the wrapper's theme gradient; the fade sits at the bar's left edge while scrolled, and after focus moves to `/` it is hidden and `/` takes the clicks.
- Dark file dialog (server only): the fade stays hidden. This test fails against an inline `display: block`.

title: Give editor status bar icons alt text naming their type
description: The icon before editor status bar messages (e.g. "Copilot: No completions available.", "Posit AI Pass: ...", notebook render errors) was an `` with no alt text. It now has alt text naming the message type: - Info and OK messages: "Information" - Warning messages: "Warning" - Error messages: "Error". For assistant errors the text is just `"{assistant}: {message}"`, so the icon is the only sign that the message is an error. The notebook-rendering spinner is now a `DecorativeImage` (`alt=""`), because the text next to it already says rendering is in progress. New `StatusBarWidgetTests` check the alt text on the visible message icon for each type, that the spinner is decorative, and the switches from loading to error and from an icon to a plain message. Fixes #19176.

title: Keep columnheader semantics on sortable grid headers
description:
Fixes #19170. Sortable column headers put `role="button"` on the `` itself, which replaced its columnheader role. Screen readers got no column header for sortable columns, the sort direction couldn't be exposed with `aria-sort`, and axe's `empty-table-header` rule skipped these cells. The markup comes from the GWT fork, fixed in rstudio/gwt#20 and published as `2.13.1-montauk-daisy-2`. ## Changes - **GWT 2.13.1-montauk-daisy-2** (`install-gwt`, `install-dependencies.cmd`): - A sortable `` keeps its columnheader role, and the sorted column's `` has `aria-sort="ascending"` or `"descending"`. - The sort control is a `
` inside the ``. - The sort icon's alt text is now empty, since `aria-sort` reports the direction. - The fork adds `AbstractHeaderOrFooterBuilder.enableHeaderHandlers()`. - **Environment pane, grid view:** its custom header builder doesn't use the fork's default header code, so it now does the same itself: - sets `aria-sort` on the sorted column and wraps each header in a `role="button"` div; - marks each `` with `enableHeaderHandlers()`, so a click anywhere in the header, including on the button itself, reaches the `ClickableTextCell` that does the sorting; - gives the wrapper its own ellipsis, because `text-overflow` on the `` doesn't apply to text inside a child block. The sorted column's text box beside the sort icon gets one too; it was clipped without an ellipsis before this change. - **Files pane:** the file-type icon column's header was `
`, where `aria-label` isn't permitted, so the header had no name. It's now visually hidden, localized "File type" text (English and French). The `
` stays, so the sort button keeps a line of height. - **Git/SVN changelists:** `.cellTableSortableHeader > div` padded the sorted header's icon container, which used to be the ``'s child. With the new wrapper it would have matched every sortable header's button, so it's now `.cellTableSortableHeader > [role="button"] > div`. - **Empty tables:** GWT tables redraw their headers only when rows are pushed, and sorting an empty list in place pushes none, so the sort icon (and now `aria-sort`) kept showing the previous sort. The Files pane, the changelists, Browse Addins, and the Environment grid now redraw their headers after each sort. Modify Keyboard Shortcuts already pushed its rows on every sort. - NEWS entry. Affected tables: the Files pane, the Git and SVN changelists (including Review Changes and the SVN commit dialog), the Environment grid view, and the Modify Keyboard Shortcuts, Browse Addins, and Packrat dialogs. Not changed: sort buttons still aren't in the tab order and Space doesn't sort, as before. The legacy Packrat dialogs' header clicks still don't sort (their handler is a stub), so their headers can show a sort that the rows don't have, as the sort icon did before. In `DataGrid`-based tables, body cells still aren't associated with their column headers, because `DataGrid` renders the header and body as separate tables; that's #19173. ## Testing - New e2e test `tests/panes/files/files_column_headers.test.ts`: the Files pane's headers (including "File type") are column headers, and each click on the Name sort button puts `aria-sort` on that header alone: ascending if Name wasn't the sort column, otherwise reversed. Passes with `test:server-dev` against the installed daisy-2 build, and fails against daisy-1. - New e2e test `tests/menus/tools/browse_addins_sort.test.ts`: with the Browse Addins filter matching nothing, each Name click moves `aria-sort` to ascending, then descending. Fails without the redraw. - New e2e test in `tests/panes/environment/environment_pane.test.ts`: in grid view with an empty environment, the grid's headers are column headers, sorting moves `aria-sort` to the clicked column, and a second click reverses it. Fails without the Environment redraw. - On a dev server: - **Sorting:** the Files pane, Git changelist, Environment grid, and Modify Keyboard Shortcuts and Browse Addins dialogs sort once per click, and `aria-sort` follows. Chrome's accessibility tree shows column headers named "File type", "Name", "Size" and "Modified". - **Layout:** the Files pane's column resize handles stay on the column borders, and the changelist's sort icon spacing applies only to the sorted column. - **Header-click workaround:** the Modify Keyboard Shortcuts dialog's workaround still prevents a stray cell selection. - **axe:** now evaluates the sortable headers, and they pass `empty-table-header`. - `ant javac` passes. The fork's tests are described in rstudio/gwt#20.

title: Give the Files pane checkbox column a hidden header
description: Fixes #19169. The Files pane's checkbox column was added without a header, so its `` was empty and axe reported `empty-table-header` ("Table header text should not be empty"). The column is too narrow for visible text, so the header is now "Selected" in the existing `visuallyHidden` style: ```html Selected ``` This names the column's ``. Screen readers still don't announce it while moving through the checkbox cells, because `DataGrid` renders its header row and body rows as separate tables, with no association between them; that affects every `DataGrid` column and is tracked in #19173. The string is localized (English and French). Verified on a dev server: axe-core 4.13 passes `empty-table-header` on the Files checkbox header, and the column's width (30px) and appearance are unchanged. No automated test was added. The adjacent file-type icon column header has a related problem in the GWT fork's sortable headers, tracked separately in #19170. Also prefixes the accessibility entries in NEWS.md (those whose issues carry the `accessibility` label) with "[Accessibility] ".

title: Bundle rig 0.11.0 with RStudio
description:
### Intent

Ship rig 0.11.0 with RStudio so R discovery and installation can use a known version without first downloading rig at runtime.

### Approach

Add a shared, checksum-verified dependency installer for Windows, Linux, and macOS, including a universal macOS binary. Package rig's supporting files and license notices alongside the executable. Expose the bundled location to the session and prefer it after an explicit `RSTUDIO_RIG` override, retaining system and download fallbacks.

### Automated Tests

- Added discovery-order and bundled-binary tests, and extended version filtering coverage to Windows.
- Focused standalone rig tests pass (13 expectations); the installed bundled binary reports 0.11.0 and is selected successfully.
- Verified all six archive checksums against cached release metadata, installer shell syntax, and a repeated Windows install that correctly does no work. Earlier packaging checks exercised corrupt-archive rejection and a staged Windows session (109 passes, three platform skips).
- A fresh isolated native-session rerun encountered the local startup crash. Linux and macOS packaging still need CI/platform validation.

### QA Notes

Verify a packaged installation without rig on PATH, explicit override precedence, and fallback behavior. Check that Windows helpers and Linux certificates are present, and that macOS builds contain the requested architectures.

### Documentation

Updated `NEWS.md`, dependency/license metadata, and the generated session option for the bundled rig path.

title: Install renv project dependencies together
description:
### Intent

When individual dependency installation is enabled, a renv project currently receives one `renv::install()` call per package. Install requested packages together so renv can resolve dependencies and use its parallel installation support.

### Approach

Route renv projects through the existing combined installer regardless of the individual-install preference. Keep individual installation for other projects and remove the unused renv branch from that path. The combined installer continues to separate packages explicitly requested from source.

### Automated Tests

All ten existing `SessionDependenciesTest` tests pass in the staged native session, including combined renv installation, source-package handling, and installation-result verification. No new tests were added for this routing change.

### QA Notes

In a renv project, enable individual dependency installation and request multiple missing dependencies. Confirm they reach renv together. Also check a non-renv project with that preference enabled.

### Documentation

Added a `NEWS.md` entry.

Addresses #19168.

title: Use dark theme colors in renv snapshot and restore tables
description:
### Intent

The package tables in renv Snapshot and Restore dialogs retain a white background in dark themes. Make their backgrounds, headings, borders, and text follow the dialog theme.

### Approach

Apply existing theme colors to the shared renv action table and set a dark color scheme for its scrollbars. Light-theme styles remain unchanged.

### Automated Tests

GWT draft compilation passes. A rendered preview using the source styles was checked in light and dark themes. No new behavioral tests were added for this styling change.

### QA Notes

Open both Snapshot and Restore with enough packages to scroll. Check headings, rows, borders, and scrollbars in light and dark themes, including switching themes while the dialog is open.

### Documentation

Added a `NEWS.md` entry.


Addresses #19167.

title: Skip renv restore prompts when only renv is recorded
description:
### Intent

Do not offer to restore an empty project library when `renv.lock` records only renv itself: renv is already available in an active renv project, so there is nothing to restore.

### Approach

Exclude renv when deciding whether the lockfile contains packages to restore. Keep the prompt when any other package is recorded.

### Automated Tests

Extended tests cover missing/empty package records, renv alone, and renv with another package, including the project R-version check. Both affected test cases pass in a native session (21 expectations). The complete renv suite was not rerun.

### QA Notes

Open a project whose lockfile contains only renv with an otherwise empty project library; no restore prompt should appear. Add another package to the lockfile and confirm the restore prompt returns.

### Documentation

Added a `NEWS.md` entry.

title: Align Windows Packages toolbar labels and search fields
description:
Addresses #19165.

### Intent

Align the Packages pane's text-only Help and repository actions with nearby icons, and improve the vertical alignment of search fields on Windows.

### Approach

Add a class to those two Packages toolbar actions and move their labels up two pixels on Windows. Move shared search widgets up one pixel on Windows.

### Automated Tests

GWT draft compilation passes. Browser layout checks verified the two-pixel label and one-pixel search shifts. No new behavioral tests were added for these visual offsets.

### QA Notes

Check Packages with renv active and its repository selector visible, plus search fields in other panes, at common Windows display scales. Confirm non-Windows layouts are unchanged.

### Documentation

Added a `NEWS.md` entry.

title: Show a browser icon in web hyperlink previews
description:
### Intent

Show an Open in Browser icon beside the URL in web hyperlink previews so the destination's action is easier to recognize.

### Approach

Place the existing browser command icon and URL in a vertically centered row. Use the command's localized description as the icon's alternative text. Link activation behavior is unchanged.

### Automated Tests

GWT draft compilation passes with this change. No new behavioral tests were added for the preview decoration.

### QA Notes

Hover HTTP and HTTPS links and check icon alignment with short and long URLs in light and dark themes. Confirm clicking still opens the expected page, and check the icon description with a screen reader.

### Documentation

Added a `NEWS.md` entry.

Addresses #19166.

title: Offer R install and switch choices with destination confirmation
description:
### Intent

When a project requests R 4.5.3 but only R 4.5.2 is installed, the Console now offers both **Install and Switch to R 4.5.3** and **Switch to R 4.5.2**. Choosing installation first opens a dialog where the user can confirm, edit, or browse for the installation folder. Cancel leaves the Console offer available and starts no installation.

### Approach

- Show project R-version and renv restore notices in the Console, with theme-aware buttons, wrapping layouts, dismissal, and screen-reader announcements.
- Show only the switch action when an installed version satisfies the request, including major/minor requests.
- Fetch rig's default user installation folder and validate the selected path before starting a background job. Pass the confirmed folder to the installer without changing the session environment or rig configuration.
- Remember custom installation roots across restarts, and locate the requested R in the selected folder when installation completes.

### Automated Tests

- Added R tests for default folders, path validation, custom-root discovery, and exact-version selection. The focused `test-rig.R` suite passes with four platform skips using a standalone source-backed harness.
- Added desktop end-to-end coverage for both buttons, editing/clearing the folder, canceling without an install request, and switching to the nearby installed version. Focused TypeScript checking passes.
- GWT draft compilation and focused C++ compilation pass. Rendered previews were checked for layout and light/dark theme styling.
- Full desktop end-to-end execution and the native session test runner remain unverified because the local app encountered a locked native module and a session startup crash.

### QA Notes

Verify an exact installed match, a missing patch with a nearby installed match, and a missing version without a nearby match. Check the installation dialog in light and dark themes, keyboard navigation, Browse, empty/invalid folders, cancellation, and installation into a custom folder containing spaces. After installation, confirm RStudio restarts with the requested R and can discover it again after a later restart.

### Documentation

Added a release note in `NEWS.md`. The dialog explains the per-user installation folder and the restart after installation; no separate guide changes are included.

### Checklist

- [x] Includes an entry in `NEWS.md`.
- [ ] Updated UI meets accessibility standards (labels and announcements included; full app audit pending).
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned.
- [ ] All local unit tests pass (focused checks pass; full native runner blocked as noted above).

title: Put select-all checkbox aria-label on the input, not the label
description:
Fixes #19156.

The Files pane's select-all checkbox (`CheckBoxHiddenLabel`) set `aria-label` on the checkbox's empty `<label>`. `<label>` has no ARIA role, so axe reports `aria-allowed-attr`. The attribute now goes on the `<input>`:

```html
<!-- before -->
<input type="checkbox" id="fp_select_all"><label for="fp_select_all" aria-label="Select all files"></label>
<!-- after -->
<input type="checkbox" id="fp_select_all" aria-label="Select all files"><label for="fp_select_all"></label>
```

Chrome gives the checkbox the name "Select all files" either way; the old markup relied on a prohibited attribute to get it.

Verified on a dev server that the rendered markup matches "after". No automated test was added.

title: Restore reduced_motion after the minimized-console render spec
description:
The server fixture sets `reduced_motion` to `true` when it launches a session, so pane zoom and maximize apply synchronously. `console_minimized_after_render.test.ts` sets it to `false` for one test, and its `afterEach` then called `clearPref`, which reverts to the schema default (`false`) rather than the fixture's value. Every later spec in the same worker ran with animations on.

`tabs.test.ts` "layoutZoomEnvironment zooms the environment pane and toggles back" measures the Environment panel right after the restore, so with animations on it caught the panel mid-transition (e.g. 639px vs. 574px before the zoom, outside the 10% tolerance). It passes alone and fails when `tests/panes/layout/` runs as a folder.

The `afterEach` now sets `reduced_motion` back to `true`.

Verified with `npm run test:server-dev`:
- before: `tabs.test.ts` alone with `reduced_motion` forced `false` fails; the console spec + `tabs.test.ts` fails
- after: the console spec + `tabs.test.ts` passes (13 passed); `tests/panes/layout/` passes (74 passed, 3 skipped)

In CI, across the 69 completed PR e2e runs from Oct 8–16, this test failed its first attempt in 19 runs (linux-server, linux-desktop, macOS) and passed on retry every time, so it surfaced only as flaky. Every one of those failures ran after the console spec in the same shard. Two `panes.test.ts` zoom tests ("Closing a source column while a pane is zoomed ends the zoom", "Closing the sidebar while its column is zoomed restores the columns") show the same pattern, in 10 and 2 runs, but I didn't reproduce those locally.

title: Report pane splitter positions with aria-valuenow
description:
Pane splitters are focusable separators (`role="separator"`, `tabindex="-1"`), and ARIA requires a focusable separator to have `aria-valuenow`. Neither kind of splitter set it, so axe reported `aria-required-attr` (critical) on them and screen readers couldn't report a splitter's position.

Each splitter now sets `aria-valuenow` to its position: a whole-number percentage of the distance it can travel, from 0 at the left or top edge of its panel to 100 at the right or bottom edge. That matches the default `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`, so neither is set. The value is updated after every layout, so it follows dragging, keyboard resizing, window resizes, and sizes set programmatically (restoring state, zooming a column), and it is clamped to 0-100.

- **Column splitters** come from `SplitLayoutPanel` in the GWT fork. The fix is in rstudio/gwt#19, published as GWT build `2.13.1-montauk-daisy-1`; `install-gwt` and `install-dependencies.cmd` now use it.
- **Row splitters** come from `BinarySplitLayoutPanel`, which now updates the value in `onResize()`. Every `setSplitterPos()` reaches it through the layout callback.

Fixes #19151.

## Testing

- New GWT unit tests (`BinarySplitLayoutPanelTests`): position measured from the top and from the bottom, clamping in a panel shorter than two splitters, and no value while detached. `ant unittest` passes (712 tests).
- New e2e tests (`tests/panes/layout/splitter_aria.test.ts`) check that `aria-valuenow` matches each splitter's drawn position on load, after keyboard resizing of a column and a row splitter, and through a column zoom. Run on a Server dev build against the installed `2.13.1-montauk-daisy-1`: all pass. Against the previous GWT build without the row splitter change, all four fail.
- The a11y initial-state scan (`PW_A11Y=1`) no longer reports `aria-required-attr`. It still fails on an unrelated violation: `aria-prohibited-attr` on the Files pane's "Select all files" label.
- The rest of `tests/panes/layout` passes, except `tabs.test.ts` "layoutZoomEnvironment zooms the environment pane and toggles back", which fails the same way without these changes when the whole folder runs, and passes on its own. #19155 fixes that failure.

Not tested on Desktop.

title: restore maximized desktop windows correctly on wayland
description:
### Intent

Fixes #19136.

On Linux with Wayland (the default backend since Electron 38, i.e. RStudio 2026.01), RStudio Desktop closed while maximized restarts in a small window that is nonetheless marked maximized: the title bar shows the "restore" button, and the window sits in the top-left corner at its old unmaximized size. Restoring and re-maximizing it shrinks the remembered size by 44x44px each time, which is how the reporter's window decayed to roughly 995x200.

Probably also the cause of #14615 ("Initial window size on Wayland gets smaller and smaller"), and possibly of #19137 (window shrinks after sleep/wake, same reporter); the latter isn't verified.

### Approach

Two code paths misbehave on Wayland:

1. `restoreMainWindowBoundsImpl()` calls `setBounds()`/`setSize()` and then `maximize()` before the window has been mapped. With `WAYLAND_DEBUG` on, mutter sends its initial `0x0` configure followed by the maximized `2560x1440` one; Chromium acks the stale initial configure with the `setBounds()` size and never acks the maximized one, so mutter adopts the smaller size while keeping the window maximized.
2. The `unmaximize` guard from #12992 captures `getBounds()` when the event fires -- on Wayland a transient value, the maximized geometry less the 44px frame shadow -- and `setBounds()` it 75ms later. That overrides Chromium's correct restore to the normal size and, from the stuck state above, commits the smaller size.

The fix:

- Create the main `BrowserWindow` at its saved size (new `initialSize` window option, fed by `initialMainWindowSize()`), so a maximized window has the right size to unmaximize to without any resize before it is mapped.
- On Wayland, restore a maximized window by calling `maximize()` alone. Wayland clients can't position their windows, so the skipped `setBounds()` was only resizing.
- On Wayland, skip the `unmaximize` guard: the compositor places windows, so they can't be restored offscreen.

Other platforms, and Wayland windows that were not maximized, keep the existing behavior; creating the window at its saved size first is invisible there, since it is still hidden when `setBounds()` runs. Wayland is detected from the `--ozone-platform` switch Electron records for the backend it picked.

Alternatives tried and rejected (patched into the packaged app and run under mutter):

- Deferring `maximize()` to `show`: still loses the race.
- Deferring to `ready-to-show`: racy; one relaunch in two got stuck.
- Skipping `setBounds()` without the initial size: maximizes reliably, but forgets the unmaximized size (falls back to 800x600).

### Automated Tests

Unit tests:

- `desktop-options.test.ts`: a maximized window is restored by `setBounds()` and then `maximize()` elsewhere, and by `maximize()` alone (no `setBounds`/`setSize`/`setPosition`) on Wayland; `initialMainWindowSize()` returns the saved size, clamped to the 300x200 minimum.
- `desktop-browser-window.test.ts`: `initialSize` sizes the `BrowserWindow`, and the `unmaximize` guard runs everywhere except on Wayland.

Both Wayland tests fail with the behavioral changes removed. The full desktop suite passes locally except `Utils findComponents`, which needs a built `rsession` that this worktree doesn't have.

Wayland itself isn't available to the unit tests, so the fix was also verified by hand: Ubuntu 22.04 (amd64) in Docker, headless mutter 42.9 (the reporter's version) as the Wayland compositor, with this branch's main-process bundle dropped into the 2026.11 daily:

- 6/6 launches with saved `{1000x600, maximized}` come up maximized at 2560x1440 (stock 2026.06 through the current daily come up at 1000x600, still marked maximized).
- Unmaximize returns to 1000x600 and stays there; re-maximize, quit, and relaunch come up maximized again, with `{1000x600, maximized}` saved.
- An unmaximized 1800x1000 window restores unchanged.
- The reporter's state (`995x150`, maximized) comes up maximized; unmaximizing gives 995x200.
- Under XWayland (`--ozone-platform=x11`) the existing path is unchanged and works.

### QA Notes

On Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 with a GNOME Wayland session (`echo $XDG_SESSION_TYPE` prints `wayland`):

1. Start RStudio, maximize the window, and quit.
2. Start RStudio again: it should fill the screen. Before this change it came up small in the top-left corner, with the title bar's middle button showing "restore".
3. Click the title bar's restore button: the window should return to its earlier unmaximized size. Maximize, quit, and restart a few times; the window should come up maximized each time, and the unmaximized size should not shrink.
4. Repeat 1-3 with an unmaximized, resized window: it should restart at the same size.

Spot-check on macOS, Windows, and an X11 session that maximized and unmaximized windows still restore as before.

### Documentation

None needed.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: Avoid bind() in PDF.js viewer loading-bar timeout
description:
Snyk Code reports the `setTimeout` call in `PDFViewerApplication.progress()` (`src/cpp/session/resources/pdfjs/web/viewer.full.js`) as code injection (`javascript/CodeInjection`). It treats the bound callback as tainted, because `PDFViewerApplication` holds a value from `document.location.hash`. `setTimeout` gets a function, not a string, so nothing is evaluated. The finding is a false positive.

This change captures `this` in a variable instead of calling `bind()`. The behavior does not change. The same edit is in the minified `viewer.js`, which is the file that `viewer.html` loads, so the two files stay in sync.

## Testing

- `snyk code test --severity-threshold=high` reports 0 issues. Before the change, it reported this one finding.
- `node --check` passes for both files.
- A Node test ran `progress()` from each file with a stub loading bar. In both files, the timer callback hid the loading bar and set `disableAutoFetchLoadingBarTimeout` to `null`.
- Not tested in a running RStudio.

title: Move application role inside the main landmark; add best-practice a11y scans
description:
Addresses #19139.

### Landmarks

`role="application"` was on `#rstudio_container`, which wraps the whole UI. axe counts `application` as a landmark, so it reported `landmark-main-is-top-level` and `landmark-banner-is-top-level`. It reports `landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level` too when the warning bar is showing.

The application role now goes on the pane area (`MainSplitPanel`) instead, and the main landmark ("Workbench") moves to that panel's container in `ApplicationWindow`:

```
div#rstudio_container                      (no role; was role=application)
  <header> banner, nav "Main menu and toolbar"
  div [role=main "Workbench"]
    MainSplitPanel [role=application]       (was role=main)
  warning bar [role=contentinfo]
```

Satellite windows keep their own window-wide application role. They contain no banner or main landmark.

Checked with axe best-practice rules against a dev server:
- Before (the old roles restored in the page): `landmark-banner-is-top-level` and `landmark-main-is-top-level` both fail.
- After: both pass, and `region`, `landmark-one-main` and `landmark-no-duplicate-main` still pass.

**Needs manual screen-reader testing (NVDA/JAWS).** The menubar, toolbar and warning bar are no longer inside the application region. Menus put screen readers into focus mode on their own, but toolbar buttons don't. Check that RStudio keyboard shortcuts still work when focus is on a toolbar button.

### Best-practice rules in the a11y e2e suite

The suite selected only axe's WCAG tags, so best-practice rules (including the landmark rules above) never ran. `PW_A11Y_BEST_PRACTICES=1` adds the `best-practice` tag. The Accessibility workflow gets a matching `include_best_practices` input, and the Server workflow gets `a11y_best_practices`. Best-practice violations show `tags: best-practice` in `axe-violations.txt` and on the Summary page. The rule set label records the option, e.g. `WCAG 2.2 AA + best practices`. The `scan-config` self-test covers best practices with and without experimental rules.

title: Give the Server header logo an accessible name
description:
Fixes #19146.

The RStudio Server header logo was rendered with `alt=""`. It is the only content of the banner landmark, so screen readers found an empty banner, and Axe DevTools reported "Informative images must have accessible names".

The logo now has alt text:

- "RStudio" (new localized `rStudioLogoAltText` constant)
- "Posit Workbench" (`rStudioServerHomeTitle`) when the session has a user home page URL. Only Workbench sets that URL, and the logo then links to the Workbench home page. The image is the link's only content, so its alt text names the link. The `title` tooltip is unchanged.

`e2e/rstudio/tests/header/server-logo.test.ts` (`@server_only`) asserts the image's accessible name in both cases. The axe-core scans under `tests/a11y/` accept an empty alt, so they don't catch this. The test failed before the change (`""`) and passes after it with `test:server-dev`, which covers the unlinked case. The Workbench case has not been run.

`WebApplicationHeader.java` is identical in rstudio-pro, and the patch applies cleanly there.

title: hide the row-number column in the import dataset preview
description:
### Intent

Fixes #19138.

Since the data viewer rewrite (#17382, shipped in 2026.05), the Import Dataset preview shows a "(rownames)" column of row numbers, and it gets the column-type menu like any other column. That column's name is empty, so picking a type for it generates `read_delim(..., col_types = cols("" = col_integer()))`, which R refuses to parse:

```
attempt to use zero-length variable name
```

Every later change then fails the same way, until that column is set back to Guess.

Two more problems turned up while reproducing this:

- After any preview refresh (a delimiter change, or a column type change), the column-type menu no longer opened: clicking a header opened the menu and closed it again on the same click.
- The italic "(type)" labels under the column names overflowed narrow columns (e.g. `(numeric)` under a one-letter name).

### Approach

All changes are in `DataViewer.js`:

- `getColumnOrder()` leaves out column 0 when `rowNumbers` is false, as the old DataTables viewer did. The import dialog and the Data Output pane are the only hosts that turn row numbers off. The column layout math already counts data columns from index 1, and already handles a column order with no row-names column.
- `createColumnTypesUI()` adds a click listener to the header cell. The header UI is applied twice per refresh (the `postInitActions` replay in `initGrid`, then the host's own `setColumnDefinitionsUIVisible` call), so after a refresh each header had two listeners, and the second one dismissed the menu the first had just opened. The handler is now assigned through `th.onclick`, so a second pass replaces it instead of adding another.
- `autoSizeColumns()` now measures the type label too while the column-type UI is on, and `setColumnDefinitionsUIVisible` re-runs auto-sizing when it first applies the labels, because the host turns them on after `setData` has already sized the grid. A refresh skips this pass, since `initGrid` already sizes for the labels recorded in `postInitActions`. Wider columns can narrow the column window, so after re-sizing it re-renders the rows and refreshes the pinned offsets and scrollbars, the same sequence a column resize uses.

### Automated Tests

Three new tests in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/environment/import_dataset.test.ts`:

- **preview has no row-number column**: no `th[data-col-idx="0"]`, the first header is the first data column, and every type label ends inside its header cell.
- **column-type menu opens again after a type change**: sets two columns to Character one after the other through the menu, checks that clicking an open column's header again closes the menu, then checks the labels fit again (`(character)` is longer than `(numeric)`).
- **wide preview keeps its rows aligned with its headers**: an 80-column preview, where sizing for the labels narrows the column window. Checks the labels fit and that each header pairs with a first-row cell at the same left edge.

These failed before the fix: the "(rownames)" header was present, the menu for the second column never opened, and the wide preview had 12 headers over 17 body cells. With only the width change reverted, the label check reported e.g. `(character) by 9.6px`. With the fix, `npm run test:desktop-dev` passes for the import spec plus all of `tests/panes/data-viewer/` (92 passed, 3 skipped).

### QA Notes

1. Create `table.csv` containing `col1;col2`, `A;1`, `B;2`. Choose Import Dataset > From Text (readr), set Delimiter to Semicolon, and load the file. The preview should show only `col1` and `col2`, with no row-number column.
2. Change `col1`'s type through its header menu, then open the menu on `col2`. It should open and apply.
3. The `(type)` labels should fit inside their columns.

### Documentation

None needed.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: Mark the Assistant toolbar separator as decorative
description: Addresses #19141. The separator after the Posit Assistant button in the main toolbar was a plain `` with no `alt` attribute, which axe reports as `image-alt` (WCAG 1.1.1, Level A). `Toolbar.getSeparator()`, its only source, now returns a `DecorativeImage`, which sets `alt=""` and `aria-hidden="true"`. The other toolbar separators use `ToolbarSeparator`, but that class's primary style name makes `Toolbar`'s separator manager hide and show it. `GlobalToolbar` controls this separator's visibility itself, so it keeps the plain image style. Checked against a dev server: - Before: one visible `` without `alt` (the separator after the Assistant button), and `image-alt` reports one node. - After: no visible `` without `alt`, and `image-alt` passes. - `PW_A11Y=1` `initial-state` scan: `image-alt` is gone; the existing `aria-prohibited-attr` and `aria-required-attr` violations remain.

title: preserve runs of spaces in paged table and data viewer cells
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

Fixes #19117.

A data frame printed inline in an R Markdown / Quarto document rendered `"test     this"` as `test this`, and copying the cell yielded one space. The Data Viewer had the same problem. The data itself was intact; only the display (and so the copy) was wrong.

### Approach

Both widgets styled body cells with `white-space: nowrap`, which keeps a cell on one line but also collapses runs of spaces. They now use `white-space: pre`, which still forbids wrapping (so the no-vertical-growth intent from 42d828724d and the ellipsis truncation are kept) but renders every space.

`pre` also renders newlines and tabs, and makes leading padding visible, so each path has to account for that:

- The notebook path already escapes control characters: `.rs.formatDataCapture` runs values through `encodeString()`. It also trims leading and trailing whitespace (that trim is what removes `format()` padding there), so inline tables preserve only the spaces inside a value.
- The Data Viewer receives values as-is, so they can carry real newlines and tabs. The grid (`renderCellContents`) now draws `\n`, `\r`, and `\t` escaped, in the muted NA color so a real newline can't be mistaken for a literal backslash-n, and escapes nothing else (so e.g. Windows paths keep single backslashes). Only the display is escaped: the cell tooltip and Ctrl/Cmd+C copy keep the value itself, as before, and search highlighting indexes the raw value the server searched.
- Some class `format()` methods (e.g. hms, `survival::Surv`) pad values to a common width despite `trim = TRUE`; `.rs.formatDataColumnDispatch` now trims that padding for non-character, non-factor columns, so it doesn't show as an indent. Character data keeps its own leading and trailing spaces.
- The `.sidebar-stats-table` cells keep `white-space: normal` so that widget is unaffected.

Rendered `df-print: paged` output uses rmarkdown's bundled copy of the same widget, which has the identical rule; that needs a matching change in rstudio/rmarkdown and is not covered here.

### Automated Tests

- `test-dataviewer.R`: `.rs.formatDataColumn()` sends character values (spaces, newlines, tabs, backslashes) unchanged, and drops `format()` padding from a `Surv` column while keeping a character column's leading spaces.
- e2e `notebook_paged_table_whitespace.test.ts`: runs a chunk printing the reporter's example and asserts the cell's `innerText` (the rendered text, which is what a copy yields) keeps all five spaces.
- e2e `data_viewer.test.ts`: `View()` of the same value plus a multi-line one; asserts the rendered text, that the escaped row did not grow, and that the multi-line cell's tooltip and Ctrl/Cmd+C copy carry the raw value.

Both e2e tests were run with the stylesheet change reverted to confirm they fail on the old behavior; the tooltip/copy assertions were also confirmed to fail with escaping done on the R side.

### QA Notes

In a `.qmd` or `.Rmd`, run a chunk containing `data.frame(text = "test     this")`: the inline table should show all five spaces, and copying the cell should keep them. `View(data.frame(text = c("test     this", "a\nb")))`: the first cell keeps its spaces; the second shows `a\nb` (with a muted `\n`) on a single row of normal height, and hovering or copying it gives the two-line value. `View(data.frame(t = hms::hms(c(5, 360000))))`: values are not indented.

### Documentation

None needed.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
