title: e2e server: record and replace a wedged rsession; provision python for reticulate
description:
## Intent

Run [37965911829](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/37965911829/job/113948195705) lost a whole Linux Server shard to one hang. The rsession's main thread stopped inside reticulate's REPL error path (the `_` NameError that `py_last_value()` always raises, then `rlang::trace_back()`), and because an external server keeps routing the account to its existing session, every later sign-in in the shard timed out on `client_init`: eleven specs plus the auth teardown, with nothing in the logs to say where the session was stuck. The hang itself is not reproduced (plain-R loops of the same REPL input pass 140/140 locally and in an Ubuntu 24 container with the CI package set, and the re-run of the same head passed); this PR makes the next occurrence diagnosable and contained.

## Approach

- `e2e/rstudio/scripts/ci/rsession-diagnostics.sh` dumps each rsession's threads and `gdb` backtraces into a directory, and with `--kill` then kills them.
- `signInToServer` runs `PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_RECOVER_CMD` once when the post-login console wait times out, then reloads and retries the sign-in. The harness has no reach into an external server by itself, so the command is the caller's hook; documented in the README.
- The Linux Server workflow installs `gdb`, points the hook at the script with `--kill` (run as root, since the sessions belong to the per-run test user), runs the same dump without `--kill` at the end of a failed shard, and uploads `rsession-diagnostics/` as `rsession-diagnostics-linux-server-<shard>` on every outcome, so a shard that went green on retry still keeps the backtrace of the session it replaced.
- The packaged `rsession` is stripped, with a `.gnu_debuglink` naming the `rsession.debug` that `add_stripped_executable` splits off into the build tree. The build job uploads that file (`rsession-debug-ubuntu-24`, one-day retention) and the e2e job installs it beside the binary, where gdb picks it up through the debuglink, so the backtraces name RStudio's own frames rather than only libR's and libc's.
- The workflow provisions a venv with numpy and sets `RETICULATE_PYTHON` in `Renviron.site` (the one place that reaches sessions rserver starts for the test user). Until now the first Python spec of every shard made reticulate 1.47 build a uv-ephemeral environment, downloading a standalone Python plus numpy inside the test.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` in `e2e/rstudio`; workflow YAML parses; `shellcheck` clean on the script.
- Against the CI-built `.deb` from the failing run, in an Ubuntu 24 amd64 container: with a live rsession frozen by `SIGSTOP`, the next sign-in timed out, the hook ran, the script wrote the dump (all threads in state `T`) and killed the session, and the sign-in retried. Under Rosetta the relaunch is slow enough to exceed Playwright's 120 s test budget, so the retried specs still failed there; on the native runner a session starts in about 2 s, so the 60 s login wait plus recovery fits.
- The shipped binary's `.gnu_debuglink` was confirmed to name `rsession.debug`. The symbol install step prints gdb's `info line` for `rConsoleRead` as a check that the debuglink was accepted.
- The Python provisioning step, the symbol artifact, and the `gdb` backtrace path can only be exercised by the workflow itself.

title: Run the GWT build's node tools under the pinned build-time node
description:
yarn and npm are scripts that start whichever `node` is first on `PATH`. `src/gwt/build.xml` didn't put the pinned node on `PATH`, so `ant` run directly (`ant draft`, `ant panmirror`, a plain `cmake --build`) used the developer's default node even when the pinned 24.21.0 was installed. The packaging scripts (`package/*/make-package*`) already prepend the pinned node to `PATH`, so official builds are unaffected. This matters now because the panmirror branch pinned in #19076 declares `"engines": {"node": ">=24"}`.

Changes in `src/gwt/build.xml`:
- The yarn and npm execs (panmirror `install`/`build`, acesupport watcher `install`, testpage `npm ci`) run with the pinned node's directory first on `PATH`. If the pinned node isn't found, `PATH` is left unchanged.
- The acesupport watcher starts with the pinned node (`${node.bin}` on Unix; pinned node first on `PATH` for `cmd /c node` on Windows).
- The `node.dir` lookup checks the `<version>-arm64` folder first. On Apple Silicon, `install-npm-dependencies` installs only that folder, so before this change the lookup found nothing there and every node tool came from `PATH`.

Also corrects the comment in `dependencies/common/install-npm-dependencies`, which said an x64 node was installed alongside the arm64 one on Apple Silicon; only the arm64 node is installed.

Testing, on macOS arm64 with a fake `node` that exits with an error placed first on `PATH`:
- `ant panmirror`: fails before this change (yarn invokes the fake node); succeeds after it and writes `panmirror.js`.
- `ant panmirror -Dnode.dir=/nonexistent` (no fake node): succeeds using the node on `PATH`.
- `ant testpage`: 677 passed, 0 failed.
- `ant acesupport-watch`: the watcher runs as `dependencies/common/node/24.21.0-arm64/bin/node watch.js`.

The Windows side (`Path` vs `PATH` handling, the watcher's `cmd /c`) has not been run.

title: Deny fsevents install script in desktop allowScripts
description:
npm 11.19 blocks dependency install scripts that aren't listed in `allowScripts`, and `npm ci` in `src/node/desktop` on macOS warns that `fsevents@2.3.3` is not covered.

fsevents is a macOS-only optional dependency, pulled in via `@electron-forge/plugin-webpack` → `webpack-dev-server` → `chokidar`. Its registry metadata lists `install: node-gyp rebuild`, but the published package ships a prebuilt `fsevents.node` and no `binding.gyp`, so there is nothing to build. This adds an explicit `"fsevents": false` entry (written by `npm install-scripts deny fsevents`).

With the change, `npm install-scripts ls` reports no unreviewed packages, and `npm ci` exits 0 with no `install-scripts` warning and with `fsevents.node` in place.

title: Raise macOS deployment target to 13.0
description:
Electron 44 requires macOS 13, so this raises `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` in `dependencies/tools/rstudio-tools.sh` from 12.0 to 13.0. That value also feeds `CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` (`cmake/compiler.cmake`), so the C++ build now targets 13.0 as well.

The PR also removes the macOS version check on the Desktop launch-failure page (`addMacOSVersionError()` in `gwt-callback.ts`). It could not run in the case it was written for. It flagged Darwin < 20 and said "RStudio requires macOS 11 (Big Sur) or higher". But the app bundle's `Info.plist` gets `LSMinimumSystemVersion` from Electron: 13.0 now, and 12.0 with the previous Electron. On any older macOS, LaunchServices refuses to open the app before our code starts, so this check never ran. The `desktop.consoleLog` bridge method goes with it: nothing called it, and its only main-process listener was registered inside that check.

No NEWS entry. Official macOS support is 14+, and the 13.0 deployment target only matches Electron's minimum.

Notes for existing environments:
- Boost and other dependencies built for 12.0 don't need rebuilding. Objects with an older minimum link cleanly into a 13.0 target, and `install-boost` skips the build if Boost is already installed.
- A CMake build directory whose cached `CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` is empty picks up 13.0 on its next configure. One first configured from a shell that exported `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` has 12.0 cached and keeps it until `CMakeCache.txt` is removed. `package/osx/make-package` already removes the cache before configuring.

Addresses #19063.

title: Stream large proxied responses instead of buffering them whole
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

Open-source companion to https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/12209, which is "only" the session proxy.

This only applies to responses that are not `Transfer-Encoding: Chunked`: chunked ones already are sent through `rserver` one chunk at a time.

### Approach

Builds on the new `FixedBufferProxy` capabilities to buffer only up to a certain amount of upstream response data before delivering it that were introduced recently but only used for localhost proxying: now that we have some more confidence in this base capability, use it on the session proxy as well. Mostly this required refactoring some side-effecting hooks that used to run at the end of connection handling and that had access to the request body so that they now always run once we have the response headers, and some auth cookie refresh handling.

Give AsyncClient a headers-received hook (ResponseHeadersHandler) that fires once per upstream attempt, right after headers are parsed, the same way whether the body ends up streamed or buffered. This gives a proxy site one place for per-response side effects and non-framing header rewrites that must happen regardless of delivery strategy, since the site's own completion handler never runs for a response that is actually streamed.

FixedBufferProxy gains a shared size gate (isBelowStreamingThreshold): below it, holding a response whole and writing it in one shot has no real memory cost, so it isn't worth giving up the things only a held response can do. /p/'s existing ad-hoc buffering lambda becomes the named, testable shouldBufferLocalhostResponse policy, now also OR'd with this size gate. /s/ gets the equivalent treatment from scratch: an analogous shouldBufferLocalStreamResponse policy plus the setStreamNonChunkedResponses/setBufferPredicate wiring /p/ already had.

Moving /s/'s pending-launch cleanup into the new headers hook was mechanical, but its auth-cookie stamping was not: that only ran in the old completion handler, which streamed responses now bypass, so it would have silently stopped carrying refreshed auth cookies onto large responses. Compute the cookie allow list once and hand it to FixedBufferProxy explicitly, so the streamed and buffered delivery paths end up with identical cookies on the wire instead of the streamed path falling back to an unfiltered copy of every cookie on the connection.

### Automated Tests

> Indicate whether this change includes unit tests or integration tests, or link a work item or pull request to add those tests to another repo. If the change cannot or will not be covered by a test, indicate why.

Adds coverage for the new headers-hook contract and size gate in AsyncClient/FixedBufferProxy, buffering-policy tests for both proxy sites, and a regression test pinning the auth-cookie allow list so the two delivery paths can't diverge on which cookies survive.

### QA Notes

I've run this locally and passed an unchunked 1GB file originating in a session-proxied shiny app through it. Before this change, there is a noticeable delay before the download begins to arrive / the browser's download manager comes alive with a progress bar and ETA, and `rserver`'s `rss` jumps to a bit more than the size of the download while it is transferring. After this change, `rserver`'s `rss` doesn't appreciably change and the download begins immediately.

### Documentation

> Specify which documentation has been added or modified and why (User Guide? Admin Guide?). If no documentation was added for a new feature, indicate why. If documentation was added in a separate PR, link the PR here.

This is an optimization that users get for free by upgrading, no need to document beyond NEWS.

title: Update build-time Node.js to 24.21.0
description:
Updates the build-time Node.js (`RSTUDIO_NODE_VERSION`) from 22.22.2 to 24.21.0, so it now matches the installed Node. The next panmirror source branch (`release/rstudio-montauk-daisy`) declares `"engines": {"node": ">=24"}`, and Yarn 1 enforces that during `yarn install`.

- Version pins: `cmake/globals.cmake`, `rstudio-tools.sh`, `rstudio-tools.cmd`, `src/gwt/build.xml`, `src/node/CMakeNodeTools.txt`, `src/node/desktop/envvars.sh`, `src/node/desktop/.vscode/settings.json`, `e2e/rstudio/scripts/dev-common.ts`.
- `src/node/desktop/package-lock.json`: Node 24 bundles npm 11.19, whose `npm ci` (run by `npm run package`) rejected the old lockfile with `Missing: js-yaml@5.4.3`. npm 11 also applies the `json-schema-to-typescript` → `js-yaml ^5` override to that package's `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser` dependency. The refreshed lockfile adds that one nested dev-only entry, and npm 10's `npm ci` still accepts it.
- `src/node/CMakeNodeTools.txt`: `find_program()` reuses a cached result, so reconfiguring an existing build tree kept `NODEJS`, `NPM`, `NPX` and `NODEJS_PATH` at the previous Node version. The cached node tool paths are now cleared and resolved again on every configure.
- Windows e2e workflows: removed the step that swapped npm's bundled node-gyp for v12 (needed for VS 2026). Node 24.21.0's npm 11.19.0 already bundles node-gyp 12.4.0.

Verification:
- The 24.21.0 archives for all six platforms were already in `s3://rstudio-buildtools/node/v24.21.0/` (uploaded for the installed Node), so nothing new was uploaded. `install-npm-dependencies` downloaded and installed it fresh from S3.
- With Node 24.21.0 first on `PATH`: `ant panmirror` succeeded. In `src/node/desktop`, `npm ci` succeeded and so did `npm test` (465 passing), `npm run lint` (0 errors), and `npm run typecheck`.

Node 24 requires macOS 13.5 or later. The macOS Jenkins builders run macOS 15.

title: Link macOS builds against static OpenSSL 3.5.9
description:
Addresses rstudio/rstudio-pro#13101.

macOS builds linked Homebrew's `openssl@3` and bundled its dylibs in `Frameworks/`. The build machines don't upgrade Homebrew, and Homebrew no longer publishes Intel bottles, so the shipped OpenSSL (3.6.3) was behind on security releases, and the 3.6 series loses support on 2026-11-01. This builds OpenSSL 3.5.9 (the LTS series, as on Windows since #19066) from source and links it statically.

**Building and publishing OpenSSL**
- `dependencies/osx/build-openssl` builds static libraries for x86_64 and arm64 (deployment target 12.0), runs `make test`, and packages the headers and libraries as `openssl-3.5.9-macos-<arch>.tar.gz`. The source tarball is checked against a pinned SHA-256.
- `OPENSSLDIR` is `/etc/ssl` and the engine and module directories are under `/usr/lib`, all root-owned, rather than the default `/usr/local`, which is user-writable under Homebrew. It configures with `no-autoload-config`; RStudio ships no `openssl.cnf`.
- `dependencies/tools/upload-openssl.sh` copies OpenSSL archives (these, or the Windows zip) to the rstudio-buildtools bucket. It refuses to replace an existing key: only a 404 from `head-object`, or the 403 S3 returns for a missing key to a caller without `s3:ListBucket`, counts as free, and the upload uses `put-object --if-none-match`.
- Both archives were built with `build-openssl` (all tests passed) and uploaded with `upload-openssl.sh`.

**Using it**
- `install-dependencies-osx` runs the new `dependencies/osx/install-openssl` for each architecture, instead of installing `openssl@3`. It checks each archive against a pinned SHA-256, unpacks it into a staging directory, and moves it into the tools root only once it has the headers and both libraries for the right architecture.
- The version is set once, as `RSTUDIO_OPENSSL_VERSION` in `dependencies/tools/rstudio-tools.sh`.
- `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` links the static libraries from the tools root and fails at configure, naming `install-openssl`, if they're missing. An explicit `-DOPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` is still honored. The Homebrew root older configures cached is replaced, and configure fails if the headers or libraries it found lie outside the chosen root.
- `prepare-package.cmake` no longer copies OpenSSL dylibs or rewrites library paths, so `fix-library-paths.sh` is removed. `verify-library-paths.sh` now fails the package build if a binary in `bin/`, or a library bundled in `Frameworks/`, loads anything other than a library under `/usr/lib` or `/System/Library`, or one present in the bundle's `Frameworks/` (where pro's license-manager loads TurboActivate from).
- The Jenkins Install Dependencies stage no longer puts Homebrew's `openssl@3` on `PATH`.

With `OPENSSLDIR` at `/etc/ssl`, default certificate verification now finds macOS's CA bundle at `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`. Previously it found certificates only on machines with Homebrew installed. Statically linking adds about 5 MB to `rsession` (77.2 → 82.3 MB in an arm64 build).

Development builds that include the server components (on macOS, only `rserver-dev`) get an `ld: warning: ignoring duplicate libraries` for `libcrypto.a`/`libssl.a`. CMake already listed OpenSSL twice on those link lines; Apple's linker warns now that the libraries are static. Shipped Electron-target builds list it once.

Rest of the pro companion: pro's `prepare-package.cmake` still copies `openssl@3`. The upstream merge should take this version, keeping pro's license-manager block.

**Verified locally**
- arm64 `make-package --build-dmg=0`: `rsession`, `rpostback` and `diagnostics` load only system libraries and embed OpenSSL 3.5.9, `Frameworks/` is gone, and the built app launches.
- `core` C++ tests pass (786), including `CryptoTest`.
- A program linked against the x86_64 archive, run under Rosetta, reports 3.5.9 and the expected paths.

**Needs a Jenkins run:** the universal package (x86_64 build plus the `lipo` merge of `diagnostics` and `rpostback`).

title: Guard stopReadingAndRespond() in AsyncClient rather than in each override
description:
Every stopReadingAndRespond() override compared response_.body() against contentLength(), and each had to remember that a chunked or streamed body is never accumulated there -- with no Content-Length the compare reads "0 >= 0" as complete and ends the response before relaying any of it. NamedPipeAsyncClient never got the streaming half of that guard.

readSomeContent() now only consults the hook for a buffered, non-chunked body, so overrides no longer need either check. isStreamingResponse(), which existed only for the overrides, is removed, and the LocalhostAsyncClient and NamedPipeAsyncClient overrides drop their chunked and streaming checks. No behavior change for any client that streams today: each already returned false in those modes.

The guarded test subclass becomes StopReadingOnContentLengthAsyncClient, an override with no guard of its own, and a new ChunkedSplit server mode adds a chunked counterpart to the streamed EOF-delimited test, so each half of the base guard has a test that fails without it.

Suggested in review:
https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/18825#discussion_r4198038935

title: e2e: accept a home-aliased project path in openProject
description:
## Intent

`openProject()` in `e2e/rstudio/utils/commands.ts` waits until the bridge reports the requested project as active, comparing `rstudio.project.path()` with the requested `.Rproj` path exactly (modulo case and slashes). The session reports `active_project_file` through `createAliasedPath`, so a project under the rsession's home directory comes back as `~/sub/proj.Rproj` and the exact comparison never matches: every project open times out after 60 s.

This can't happen on CI, whose workspace sits outside the user profile, and it can't happen on macOS or Linux at all, since the desktop fixture redirects `HOME` into the sandbox and the project directories are siblings of that home. On Windows, though, the session's home resolves to the user profile rather than the redirected `HOME`, and the default sandbox root is `os.tmpdir()`, i.e. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp` inside the profile. So a plain local run of any project spec on Windows fails in `openProject`.

## Approach

Accept the home-aliased form the same way `waitForActiveDocument` and `files.ts` already do: a reported `~/...` path matches when the requested path ends with it minus the `~`. Still a full home-relative comparison, so it can't confuse same-named projects in different directories.

## Verification

On a Windows 11 VM, running `tests/projects/renv_r_version_switch.test.ts` (from #18935) against an installed build with the default sandbox root under the profile:

- before: all three project-opening tests fail with `openProject: session did not become ready with the active project "C:/Users/.../AppData/Local/Temp/..." ... (active project: ~/AppData/Local/Temp/...)`;
- after: 5 passed, 5 skipped.

Pointing `PW_SANDBOX_ROOT` outside the profile (`C:\pw-sandbox`) also avoids it, which is how the failure was first diagnosed.

`npx tsc --noEmit` in `e2e/rstudio` is clean.

title: ignore quoted @claude mentions in the relay
description:
The relay's `contains(body, '@claude')` is a substring test, so quoting someone else's `@claude ...` (GitHub's quote-reply, email replies, or just discussing the bot in backticks) re-triggered the assistant.

This adds a first step that decides whether the body has an *effective* mention, and makes the rest of the job conditional on it. A mention counts only outside:

- blockquote lines (`> ...`, including nested quotes)
- code spans and fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~; an unclosed fence runs to the end)
- HTML comments, which GitHub hides

and must be a whole token, so `@claude-code` and `x@claude.ai` do not count. Case-insensitive, as before. The job-level `contains()` stays as the cheap prefilter so the job never starts for bodies with no `@claude` at all. The eyes reaction is also skipped, which tells the author the quote did not trigger anything.

The receiver in rstudio-pro re-verifies the mention independently; its companion PR applies the identical filter (rstudio/rstudio-pro#13152). Merge this one first or together: the relay being stricter than the gate is always safe, the reverse would make the gate reject dispatches for quoted mentions.

Verified locally by extracting the step's `run:` text from the YAML and executing it against quoted, nested-quoted, fenced, inline-code, HTML-comment, `@claude-code`, email-address, unclosed-fence, and CRLF bodies; `actionlint` passes.

No NEWS entry: workflow-only.

title: run python chunks from run all chunks above in console mode
description:
### Intent

With chunk output sent to the console (the "Chunk Output in Console" gear option, or `rmd_chunk_output_inline` off), "Run All Chunks Above" / "Run All Chunks Below" / "Run All" skipped Python chunks. Worse, the console was switched to the language of the chunk under the cursor, so with a Python chunk under the cursor the Python REPL opened and any R chunk text above was typed into it (`NameError`). Inline output mode goes through the notebook queue and was never affected, which is why the reporter saw it work on one machine and not another.

Fixes #17196.

### Approach

`TextEditingTarget.executeChunks()` filtered the collected chunks with `isRChunk()` (from 2015, before the console could run Python) while picking the console language from the cursor position (added in 2018 with the Python REPL). The two were never reconciled.

The fix collects both R and Python chunks and switches the console between them in document order:

- the first chunk's language is passed with the `SendToConsoleEvent`, so the console adapts from whatever language it is in right now (the existing `adapt_to_language` RPC checks the live state);
- later switches are written into the code itself, as the same console input the session enqueues for `adaptToLanguage()` (`reticulate::repl_python()` / `quit`). The session already splits multi-line console input line by line and tracks entering/leaving the REPL while doing so (`fixupPendingConsoleInput`), so the switches land in order and Python indentation fixups still apply.

Firing one event per language group instead would not work: `adaptToLanguage()` compares against the *active* language at RPC time and suppresses consecutive transitions until the next prompt, so a second group's switch would be dropped while the first was still queued.

As with the notebook queue, the console is left in the language of the last chunk that ran. Non-R/Python engines (bash, sql, Rscript) are skipped as before. When nothing is collected, nothing is sent (previously an empty command was sent, which still switched the console language).

### Automated Tests

New Playwright spec `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/run_chunks_above_console_python.test.ts` covers R-then-Python (console ends in the Python REPL, both chunks ran, R chunk ran as R) and Python-then-R (console ends back in R). Both fail on main and pass with this change. The spec skips when reticulate or a Python interpreter is unavailable.

### QA Notes

Set Chunk Output in Console on a .qmd/.Rmd with an R chunk followed by two Python chunks, put the cursor in a later chunk, and use Run All Chunks Above: all three chunks should run, the console should end in the Python REPL, and the Python objects should exist. Repeat with Python chunks first and an R chunk last: the console should end back in R.

None needed.

title: don't reset the editor when the extended type is re-detected unchanged
description:
### Intent

Saving a document could clear the spelling and diagnostic markers that the save had just rendered. Fixes #19054. Addresses #7833.

### Approach

Every save makes the session fire `source_extended_type_detected`. With autosave off (the default), `TextEditingTarget.adaptToExtendedFileType` re-adapts the view even when the type is unchanged (#8055, so the R Markdown toolbar picks up YAML changes). That path called `AceEditor.setFileType` with the type the editor already had, and `updateLanguage` starts with `clearLint()`, with nothing scheduling a relint. Client events are dispatched incrementally, so the clear raced the lint-on-save render; when it landed second, every marker in the document disappeared until the next edit or save.

`TextEditingTargetWidget.adaptToFileType` now only calls `setFileType` (on the editor and the split editor) when the type actually differs. The toolbar logic below it still runs on every call, so the #7833 refresh is preserved. The same shortcut also stops the autosave preference handlers and `manageCommandUI` from resetting the editor's completion and keyboard handlers for no reason.

Follow-ups from review:

- The guard compares file types by `getTypeId()` rather than by reference, matching how `TextEditingTarget.onCompleted` already decides "type changed".
- `VisualMode.manageUI` now clears lint explicitly: it used to rely on `manageCommandUI` resetting the file type, and the mode switch replaces the whole source document.
- The autosave gate in `TextEditingTarget.adaptToExtendedFileType` (#8055) is gone. It only existed to avoid the side effects this PR removes, so autosave users now get the #7833 toolbar refresh too. To keep idle autosaves from rebuilding (and so closing) an open Knit menu, `updateRmdFormat()` only runs when the extended type or the front matter changed since the menu was last built.
- The code browser's `softWrapRFiles` handler is removed: word wrap is only read by `TextEditingTargetWidget`, so that handler only ever reset the editor.
- `AceEditor.setRainbowParentheses` and `setRainbowFencedDivs` only retokenize when the (global) flag changed since that editor last tokenized, via a generation counter. The toolbar pass syncs both on every save, which used to cost two full-document retokenizes per save.

Found via the `spelling_language_switch` e2e spec, which flaked on server-linux and desktop-macos in the PR #19052 run ([report](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-19052/37524647247-1/all-platforms/index.html)): the first "flagged" assertion after a priming save never saw a marker, while the trace showed `check_spelling` had reported the word as misspelled and the lint-on-save pass had run.

### QA Notes

With default preferences, open an Rmd with a misspelled word (or an R file with a diagnostic), edit, and save repeatedly: the markers should stay put. Also check that changing the `output:` format in an Rmd YAML header and saving still updates the Knit toolbar options, and that Save As to a different file type (e.g. `.R` to `.Rmd`) still switches the editor mode. Repeat the YAML `output:` check with autosave on, and confirm an open Knit menu is not closed by an idle autosave. Toggle an Rmd with markers into visual mode, edit, and toggle back: no stale squiggles should remain in source mode.

### Automated Tests

New spec `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/save_extended_type_redetect.test.ts`:

- Parks the `get_events` long-poll while the document is saved, so `source_extended_type_detected` is delivered only after the lint-on-save marker has rendered, then asserts the marker survives. Fails at that assertion without the guard.
- With commit-mode autosave, changes `output:` by typing, waits for the autosave, and checks that "Knit to github_document" appears in the Knit menu (#7833).

The existing `spelling_language_switch` spec exercises the race on every run as well.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, the NEWS file has been updated

title: fix: debugSource error when keep.source is FALSE #12375
description:
### Intent

`debugSource()` warns when `options(keep.source = FALSE)` because `parse()` leaves `srcref` NULL and `makeSourceEquivFunction()` still calls `structure()` on it. #12375

### Approach

`.rs.makeSourceEquivFunction()` returns early in two places:

- right after `parse()`, when the file has no expressions (empty or comment-only). Before, `1:length(content)` iterated with `i = 1` and failed with `subscript out of bounds`.
- after the expressions are copied into `fun`, when `length(refs) == 0`. With `keep.source = FALSE`, `parse()` leaves `srcref` NULL, and the old code failed with `attempt to set an attribute on NULL`. Only the source-reference metadata is skipped, so the file still runs; breakpoints have no effect without srcrefs.

### Automated Tests

Two tests in `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-debugger.R` call `.rs.makeSourceEquivFunction()` on:

- a one-line file with `keep.source = FALSE`, checking that it still runs and assigns into the target environment
- empty and comment-only files, with `keep.source` both on and off

Run with `./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope r --filter debugger`.

### QA Notes

Not yet checked by hand in RStudio. The new tests fail against `main`'s `SessionBreakpoints.R` and pass with this change. To check manually, run the reporter's snippet; it should print `Hello, world!` with no error:

```
options(keep.source = FALSE)
rfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines("print('Hello, world!')", con = rfile)
debugSource(rfile)
```

Also run `debugSource()` on an empty file and on a file containing only a comment, with `keep.source` on and off; each should finish without error.

### Documentation

title: Update Electron to 44.7.0 and other desktop dependencies
description:
Updates Electron from 43.7.7 to 44.7.0 and takes the in-major updates for the other `src/node/desktop` dependencies.

## Clipboard migration

Electron 44 [rearchitected the clipboard module](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v44.7.0/docs/breaking-changes.md#api-changed-clipboard-module-rearchitected-to-align-with-the-w3c-clipboard-api) around the W3C Clipboard API. Reads and writes now return promises. `readImage`, `writeImage`, `readHTML`, `writeBuffer`, and `availableFormats` were removed, and the Linux selection clipboard moved to `clipboard.selection`. The affected code:

- `gwt-callback.ts`: the text, URI-list, image, and global-mouse-selection handlers are now async. Copying a page region writes a PNG `ClipboardItem`. The mouse-selection handlers no-op on non-Linux platforms, where `clipboard.selection` is undefined. Their only caller is gated to Linux Desktop.
- `text/uri-list` now maps to the OS's native copied-files format (`CF_HDROP` / `NSFilenamesPboardType` / `text/uri-list`), and entries are CRLF-separated, percent-encoded `file://` URIs. Lines are now split on `\r?\n`, empty entries are dropped, and entries are decoded with `fileURLToPath()` (forward slashes on Windows, which the visual editor expects) instead of having the `file://` prefix sliced off. Anything that isn't a valid file URI is logged and dropped.
- `context-menu.ts`: "Copy Image Address" writes through the same queue as the handlers below.
- `clipboard-queue.ts` (new): the write queue and the queued text and MIME-type reads, shared by `gwt-callback.ts` and `context-menu.ts`.
- `native/desktop.test.ts`: the `cleanClipboard` tests use the new API, with raw pasteboard flavors reached via `electron application/osclipboard;format=...`. On macOS, `cleanClipboard(true)` removes the HTML flavor entirely. The old test passed only because Chromium's `readHTML` fell back to plain text. The test now asserts that no `text/html` remains and that the plain text survives.
- `gwt-callback.test.ts` adds tests for the text, URI-list, image, page-region, and paste handlers, including the empty, failed-read, and ordering cases.

### Write ordering

Writes used to finish before the IPC handler returned. Now they're async, and the renderer doesn't wait for them, so a read straight after a write (an Emacs kill and then a yank, or a Linux selection and then a middle-click) could return the old contents. Every main-process clipboard write now goes through one queue in `clipboard-queue.ts`. The text, selection, URI-list, and image reads and the `desktop_clipboard_paste` handler wait for it first. Paste is skipped if its window closes while it waits. `desktop_clean_clipboard` rewrites the pasteboard synchronously, so it also takes its turn in the queue.

The renderer bridge reports a rejected IPC call without invoking its GWT callback, so a clipboard handler that rejects leaves a paste or the copy-plot dialog stuck. The text, selection, URI-list, and image reads and the page-region copy now log any failure and return an empty result. That covers failures in reading, in decoding the payload, and a synchronous throw from `capturePage()`. Electron resolves an empty Blob when it can't convert the clipboard bitmap to PNG, and that is treated as no image.

The queue can't cover Chromium's own paste paths: the Cmd/Ctrl+V menu role and the context-menu Paste paste inside the page and never go through `GwtCallback`. I couldn't reproduce the race on macOS (200 back-to-back unawaited `writeText`/`readText` pairs all read the new value), so the queue makes ordering explicit where we can rather than fixing an observed bug.

Electron 44 also requires macOS 13. The deployment target stays at 12.0 for now; #19063 tracks raising it.

## node-abi under @electron/rebuild

Forge 7 depends on `@electron/rebuild` 3.7.2, which resolves its own `node-abi ^3.45.0` rather than the top-level 4.x. The locked 3.92.0 has no Electron 44 entry, so the postinstall `electron-rebuild` failed under `npm ci` with "Could not detect abi for version 44.7.0". The lockfile now has 3.97.0, which includes it.

## Updated

    electron                     43.7.7  -> 44.7.0
    @types/node                  26.5.1  -> 26.6.4
    @typescript-eslint/*         8.70.0  -> 8.71.1
    chai                          6.2.2  -> 6.3.0
    eslint                       10.10.0 -> 10.12.0
    globals                      17.12.0 -> 17.13.0
    lint-staged                  17.5.1  -> 17.6.0
    nan                           2.28.0 -> 2.29.0
    node-abi                      4.35.0 -> 4.36.0
    prettier                      3.9.6  -> 3.9.9
    vue                           3.5.42 -> 3.5.43
    webpack                     5.110.3  -> 5.111.1

`npm audit fix` (transitive lockfile bumps only) runs on top. `npm audit` goes from 35 findings (2 low / 5 moderate / 26 high / 2 critical) to 28 (2 low / 4 moderate / 21 high / 1 critical).

## Held back

| Package | Available | Why not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| @electron-forge/cli, plugin-webpack | 7.11.2 -> 8.0.1 | major version |
| @vueuse/core | 14.4.0 -> 15.0.0 | major version |
| @vercel/webpack-asset-relocator-loader | 1.7.3 -> 1.11.0 | pinned, see `.ncurc.yml` |
| mocha | 11.8.0 -> 12.0.3 | `electron-mocha` 13.1.0 depends on `mocha ^11` |
| typescript | 6.0.3 -> 7.0.2 | `typescript-eslint` 8.71.1 peer range is `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0` |

## Testing

On macOS arm64:

- `npm test`: 465 passing, 1 skipped (the selection-clipboard failure test is Linux-only). The clipboard tests use the real system clipboard and aren't run in CI.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors. The 2 `no-empty-function` warnings in `session-launcher.test.ts` are already on main.
- `npm run package`: `npm ci` (including `electron-rebuild`), the webpack bundles, and native dependency preparation pass. It then stops on the CMake-generated `Info.plist`, which only exists in a CMake build directory.

Not yet exercised in a running Desktop build:

- pasting an image, or files copied in Finder/Explorer, into the visual editor
- copying a plot to the clipboard. The page-region copy now writes an `image/png` `ClipboardItem` instead of calling `writeImage()`. Electron 44 decodes that PNG and calls the same `writer.WriteImage()` that 43.x used, so native Windows apps should get the same bitmap formats as before.
- Linux middle-click paste

title: Update Windows OpenSSL from 3.1.4 to 3.5.9
description:
Addresses rstudio/rstudio-pro#13103.

Windows builds link a prebuilt static OpenSSL 3.1.4, and the 3.1 series is end of life. This moves them to 3.5.9, the latest release of the 3.5 LTS series.

- `install-dependencies.cmd`, `install-openssl.R` and `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` now reference 3.5.9.
- `install-openssl.R` no longer passes `--prefix`/`--openssldir`, so the paths OpenSSL compiles in for its config, engines and modules (`OPENSSLDIR`, `ENGINESDIR`, `MODULESDIR`) are its Program Files defaults (`(x86)` for 32-bit) rather than the build machine's build tree. The install is staged with `nmake install_sw DESTDIR=...` instead, which leaves out the HTML docs and SSL directories RStudio does not use (the uploaded zip predates this and still contains the docs).
- `install-openssl.R` also configures with `no-autoload-config`; RStudio ships no `openssl.cnf`.
- `openssl-3.5.9.zip` was built with `install-openssl.R` (VS 2026 Build Tools; `nmake test` passed for all four configurations) and uploaded to the buildtools bucket.
- `install-openssl/.gitignore` now ignores the `build-*/` folders the script creates.

Verified locally:
- `openssl version -a` in each build tree reports Program Files paths for the three directories.
- In a 64-bit debug build, `rsession.dll` and `rpostback.exe` report OpenSSL 3.5.9 and the same Program Files paths, and the `core` C++ tests pass, including `CryptoTest`.
- did a full multi-arch package build, installed the resulting setup package, and verified it launches

The libraries still embed nine OpenSSL source-file paths from the build machine, which OpenSSL uses only in error and assert messages.

title: avoid per-function-call filesystem checks when linting R documents
description:
### Intent

Resolves https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/19056.

With R diagnostics enabled, opening a large R script on a WSL-mounted Windows drive took ~23 seconds versus ~3 seconds with diagnostics disabled. The reporter's `strace` sample showed thousands of `statx` calls on the script itself and on `<working-directory>/DESCRIPTION` during the stall.

The cause is in the R parser used by the diagnostics system. Two functions that run for every function call in the document (`mightPerformNonstandardEvaluation` and `getInfoAssociatedWithFunctionAtCursor`) each called `projectContext().isPackageProject()` and `status.filePath().exists()`. Both hit the filesystem, so a document with thousands of calls issued thousands of stat calls per lint. That is invisible on a local filesystem but dominates on a slow one (WSL `drvfs`, network drives), and because the lint RPC runs on the session's main thread the whole IDE stalls for the duration.

The `DESCRIPTION` lookup landing in the working directory is a second, smaller bug: with no project open, `ProjectContext::directory()` is empty, so `r_util::isPackageDirectory()` resolved `DESCRIPTION` relative to the current working directory.

### Approach

- `ParseStatus` now resolves the package-project flag, the package name, and the source index's inferred packages for the document lazily, on first use and at most once per parse. The two per-call lookups read these cached values instead. Nothing about the parse can change these values mid-parse, since linting is synchronous on the main thread. Parses that never look up a function (e.g. of code fragments) do no filesystem access at all.
- `ProjectContext::isPackageProject()` returns `false` when no project is open, instead of falling through to a working-directory-relative check.
- The indexed `DESCRIPTION` (`s_pIndexedPackageInfo`, kept current by the project file monitor) was resolved against `buildTargetPath()`, which is empty for build type `None`. For those projects it was therefore read relative to the working directory at startup, and the file monitor never matched its (relative) path, so it was never refreshed. It is now resolved against the project directory for every build type other than `Package`. The unindexed fallback in `isPackageProject()` still checks the project directory itself, as before, so a package project whose package lives in a subdirectory (`PackagePath`) is classified as it was on `main`. The indexed value is used by all callers on the lint path (`addTestPackageSymbols`, `getAllAvailableRSymbols`) and by the code-search indexer, so those no longer re-read `DESCRIPTION` on every call either; when nothing is indexed (no `DESCRIPTION` at startup and none seen since) the fallback costs one `stat` per call, and the parser now makes that call once per parse rather than once per function call.
- `SessionCpp.cpp` drops a now-redundant `hasProject()` check ahead of `isPackageProject()`.

### Side effects of the no-project change

- The session-init hook in `SessionDiagnostics.cpp` and the native-symbols step in `SessionCodeSearch.cpp` previously ran their package branch with an empty package name whenever the working directory happened to contain a `DESCRIPTION`. They now skip it, as intended.
- `getAllAvailableRSymbols()` in `SessionDiagnostics.cpp` chooses the symbol set used when linting. With no project open, `FilePath::isWithin()` on the empty project directory returns `true` for every path, so if the working directory contained a `DESCRIPTION` the lint previously used the restricted package symbol set (base, `.packageName`, Rcpp, and `library()`-inferred symbols only). It now uses the project symbol set, which also includes the search path. Lint results in that configuration change accordingly: fewer spurious "no symbol named ..." warnings for functions that are on the search path. Package projects that are actually open are unaffected.

### Automated Tests

`SessionProjectsTests.IsPackageProjectFalseWithoutProject` covers the no-project change: with no project open and a `Type: Package` `DESCRIPTION` in the working directory, `isPackageProject()` returns `false` (it returned `true` before). The number of filesystem calls per lint is not something the existing harness can observe; the refactored parser paths are covered by the existing `DiagnosticsTest` suite (16 tests, all passing locally), including `RStudioFilesCanBeSuccessfullyLinted`, which lints RStudio's own R sources from disk and so exercises the lazy file-existence and source-index lookup. The `DESCRIPTION` index refresh depends on the project file monitor and is covered by the QA steps below.

### QA Notes

To reproduce, with no project open and `show_diagnostics_r` enabled, open a large R script (thousands of function calls) stored on a slow filesystem such as a Windows drive mounted in WSL (`/mnt/c/...`), with the working directory on the same mount. Before this change, the editor and console stall for tens of seconds while the file is linted; after, linting takes a few seconds at most. On Linux, `strace -f -e trace=statx -p <rsession pid>` during a lint should now show at most a couple of `statx` calls for the script and for `DESCRIPTION`, rather than one per function call.

Diagnostics in package projects should be unchanged: functions defined in the package's `R/` directory are still recognized when linting files in the package, and `library()` calls in a document still inform symbol lookup.

For the `DESCRIPTION` indexing change: open a plain project (build type not `Package`) and an R script inside it that calls a function from an attached non-base package, e.g. `tibble()` after `library(tibble)` in the console but not in the script. Add a `DESCRIPTION` file with `Type: Package` and `Package: foo` to the project root. Once the Files pane shows the new file, re-lint the script (edit and save it): the call should now be flagged as not in scope, because files in a package project are linted against the package symbol set. Delete `DESCRIPTION` and re-lint, and the warning should go away. Neither step should need a restart. Also try the reverse order (start with the `DESCRIPTION` present, then delete it): before this change the deletion was not noticed until restart.

For the no-project symbol-set change: with no project open, `setwd()` to a directory containing a `DESCRIPTION`, then open an R script that calls a function from an attached package. Previously that call could be flagged as "no symbol named ... in scope"; it should not be flagged now.

### Documentation

None needed; user-facing behavior is unchanged apart from the speedup. `NEWS.md` entry added.

title: target the e2e-playwright environment again, without creating deployments
description:
## Summary

#18925 dropped `environment: e2e-playwright` from the eight e2e engine workflows to stop every shard job from recording a deployment on the PR. The environment was a security-team requirement, though: it scopes the `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` used to pull the Posit Assistant test-account credentials from 1Password, and the environment-scoped copy of the secret is the one that is kept current.

GitHub Actions now has a supported way to get both: `jobs.<job_id>.environment.deployment: false` gives the job the environment's secrets and variables without creating a deployment object ([workflow syntax reference](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#jobsjob_idenvironment), [roadmap item](https://github.com/github/roadmap/issues/1215), GA). This PR puts the environment back on the same eight jobs in that form:

```yaml
environment:
  name: e2e-playwright
  deployment: false
```

The only documented limitation is that `deployment: false` cannot be combined with custom deployment protection rules; `e2e-playwright` has none.

## Verification

- All eight files parse as YAML, and `actionlint` reports nothing new.
- The e2e PR workflow run on this PR should show no "requested a deployment to e2e-playwright" timeline events, and the "Check for OP service account token" step should still report the token as present.

## Follow-up

The `e2e-playwright` environment was never deleted after #18925, so no repo-settings change is needed. The repo-level `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` (2026-06-12) can stay as a fallback or be removed; the environment-scoped copy takes precedence again once this merges.

title: support building against openssl 4
description:
Homebrew's unversioned `openssl` formula moved to `openssl@4` on 2026-09-28 (Homebrew/homebrew-core#313581), and OpenSSL 4.0 changed `X509_get_subject_name()` to return a `const X509_NAME *`. The self-signed certificate generator in `core::system::crypto` mutated that name in place, so it no longer compiled. That was the only OpenSSL 4 incompatibility in the backend: every other use of libcrypto/libssl, plus Boost 1.91's Asio SSL layer, compiles unchanged against 4.0.3.

Changes:

- `generateRsaCertAndKey()` builds the subject name with `X509_NAME_new()` and sets it via `X509_set_subject_name()` / `X509_set_issuer_name()`, which copy it into the certificate. This is the same code on OpenSSL 1.1, 3, and 4. The first commit is Gary's from #19042, cherry-picked before it was reverted there; `GenerateRsaStringCert` now also asserts the cert is self-signed.
- The OpenSSL include directory is now added as a non-SYSTEM `BEFORE` include rather than `include_directories(SYSTEM ...)`, for the same reason we do that for the bundled {fmt}: on macOS, clang searches the driver-added `/usr/local/include` ahead of every `-isystem` directory, so an OpenSSL installed under `/usr/local` (an x86_64 Homebrew on Apple Silicon) silently shadowed the headers of the OpenSSL we link against. On my machine that meant compiling against 3.6.2 headers while linking `libcrypto.4.dylib`, which is also why the compile error above never showed up locally. clang drops a `-I` that duplicates a later `-isystem`, so the SYSTEM entry had to go rather than just adding a `BEFORE` one.

This is independent of #19042, which decides which OpenSSL the macOS package ships with; this PR just makes the code build against either. The two touch adjacent lines in `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`, so whichever merges second needs a trivial conflict resolution.

Tested on arm64 macOS with a fresh configure against `openssl@4` (4.0.3): full backend build, then `rstudio-core-tests` (786 pass, including the crypto and SSL tests), `rstudio-server-core-tests` (12 pass) and `rstudio-shared-core-tests` (19 pass); `rserver` and `rsession` link `libcrypto.4.dylib`. The OpenSSL-using translation units were also syntax-checked against `openssl@3` (3.6.5) with the same flags.


Fixes #19059.

title: Stop linking and bundling unused libraries in Desktop
description:
### Intent

Open-source merge of rstudio/rstudio-pro#13113, part of rstudio/rstudio-pro#13101. RStudio Desktop linked or bundled libraries it never uses; they show up in security scans and, on x86_64, can no longer be updated through Homebrew.

This carries everything from the Pro PR except `src/cpp/activation/CMakeLists.txt`, which exists only in Pro.

### Approach

- `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`: link SOCI's PostgreSQL backend and libpq, and define `RSTUDIO_HAS_SOCI_POSTGRESQL`, only when `RSTUDIO_PRO_BUILD AND RSTUDIO_SERVER` (new `RSTUDIO_USE_POSTGRESQL` flag). Previously this happened for any `RSTUDIO_PRO_BUILD`, and the define keyed off a cached `find_library` path, so a server build directory reconfigured for Desktop kept libpq linked. Also removes the unused `SOCI_DEPENDENCIES`.
- `package/osx/cmake/prepare-package.cmake`: copy only `openssl@3` from Homebrew. `gettext` and `sqlite3` (and, in Pro, `krb5` and `libpq`) are no longer bundled.
- `package/osx/scripts/verify-library-paths.sh` (new): runs at the end of `prepare-package.cmake` and fails the package build if a binary in `bin/` or `Frameworks/` loads an `@executable_path/../Frameworks/...` library that isn't in the app, or still loads a library from an absolute `/opt/homebrew` or `/usr/local` path.
- `package/linux/CMakeLists.txt`: drop the Pro-only `libpq5`/`postgresql-libs` dependency from Linux Desktop packages.

#### Platform impact

- **Open-source macOS Desktop:** the app no longer bundles `gettext` or `sqlite3`; the new check runs during packaging. Nothing links gettext, and rsession already uses the system `/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`.
- **Open-source Linux, Windows and Server:** no change; the CMake conditions only affect Pro builds.
- **Pro:** see rstudio/rstudio-pro#13113.

### Automated Tests

None: these are build and packaging changes. `verify-library-paths.sh` adds a check to the macOS package build itself.

### QA Notes

Local verification is described in rstudio/rstudio-pro#13113. This PR's macOS package build exercises the new check against the open-source app.

### Documentation

None. NEWS entry added under Dependencies.

title: reopen the project menu when polling recent projects in the worktrees e2e test
description:
## Summary

Fixes a desktop-windows flake in `panes/git/worktrees.test.ts` ("lists worktrees and opens one as a project"), seen in the [PR #19051 report](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-19051/37507841729-1/all-platforms/index.html).

After switching into the linked worktree, the test opened the project menu once and then polled its items for the new Recent Projects entry. The trace shows the `list_changed` event carrying that entry reached the client about two seconds after the menu was already open. Two things make that poll hopeless:

- On Windows the monitored lists directory is not watched natively; `initializeMonitoredUserScratchDir()` polls it with a 3-second idle-only scan, so the recent-projects update trails the `list_prepend_item` RPC by 0-3 s (7.98 s once in this worker's trace, while the session was busy).
- `AppMenuItem` only refreshes its label in `onShow()`, so an already-open popup never reflects the change.

The retry passed only because the entry was already on disk from the first attempt.

## Changes

- Replace the `expect.poll` over the open menu with an `expect(...).toPass()` block that reopens the menu on each attempt (click, read, assert, Escape), with a 30 s budget to cover the Windows scan lag.

No other spec asserts Recent Projects contents right after a project switch. Test-only change; no NEWS entry.

title: Pin macOS builds to Homebrew openssl@3
description:
Homebrew's unversioned `openssl` formula pointed to `openssl@3` for five years, from September 2021 ([Homebrew/homebrew-core@92d985a](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/commit/92d985af3e), which moved it from `openssl@1.1`). On September 28, 2026, [Homebrew/homebrew-core#313581](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/313581) changed it to `openssl@4` (now 4.0.3). macOS builds found OpenSSL through `opt/openssl`, so a `brew upgrade` switched them to OpenSSL 4. That breaks compilation at `src/cpp/core/system/Crypto.cpp:395`: `X509_get_subject_name()` now returns a `const X509_NAME *`. It would also change which OpenSSL the macOS package ships with, without anyone deciding to.

This keeps macOS on OpenSSL 3, which the Linux (jammy, rhel9) and Windows builds also use:

- `install-dependencies-osx-arch` installs `openssl@3` instead of `openssl`, into both the arm64 and x86_64 Homebrews.
- `cmake/globals.cmake` prefers `${HOMEBREW_PREFIX}/opt/openssl@3` and falls back to `opt/openssl`. It drops the `Cellar/openssl/*` glob; current Homebrew has no `Cellar/openssl` directory, so that check never matched.
- `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` fails the configure step of a macOS package build if OpenSSL isn't 3.x. It runs separately for the x86_64 and arm64 halves of a universal build. Developer builds aren't checked.
- The Jenkins macOS dependency step puts `/usr/local/opt/openssl@3/bin` on the PATH instead of `/usr/local/opt/openssl/bin` (which was listed twice).
- `package/osx/cmake/prepare-package.cmake` copies the bundled `libssl`/`libcrypto` dylibs from `opt/openssl@3` instead of `opt/openssl`. Where `opt/openssl` points to OpenSSL 4, the package would otherwise contain `libssl.4.dylib` and `libcrypto.4.dylib`. `rsession`, `diagnostics`, and `rpostback` load `libssl.3.dylib` and `libcrypto.3.dylib`, so they would fail to start.

Developers with an existing build directory need to clear the cached OpenSSL paths once:

    cmake -U 'OPENSSL_*' -U 'pkgcfg_lib__OPENSSL_*' ..

Tested on arm64 with both `openssl@3` and `openssl@4` installed:
- A fresh configure selects `/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3`.
- A package-build configure succeeds against `openssl@3` and fails with the new error against `openssl@4`.
- Running the generated `prepare-package.cmake` into a scratch install prefix bundles `libssl.3.dylib` and `libcrypto.3.dylib`, even though `opt/openssl` points to `openssl@4` on this machine.
- The full build and the `CryptoTest` tests pass.

The x86_64 half wasn't tested locally, because this machine has no `/usr/local` Homebrew.

title: draw color preview boxes with an outline instead of a border
description:
### Intent

Fixes #17215.

Color previews in the editor pushed the cursor and bracket highlighting off the character grid, by about one character after twelve hex colors on a line. It only shows at a non-integer effective zoom: Windows display scaling of 125/150/175%, or RStudio's own zoom levels of 1.1/1.25/1.5/1.75. At 100% or 200% it is invisible, which is why it was never seen on a Retina Mac.

### Approach

The preview box was drawn with a 1px border cancelled out by -1px margins on each side. That cancels in CSS pixels, but Chromium floors border widths to whole device pixels while margins stay fractional, so each box came out `2 * (1 - floor(z)/z)` px narrower than its text (0.67px per box at 150%) and the error accumulated along the line. Ace positions the cursor and markers at `column * characterWidth`, so they drifted right of the text.

The box is now drawn with an `outline`, which paints in the same place (1px outside the text) but takes no layout space, so widths stay exact at every zoom.

The change is in the Ace fork: rstudio/rstudio-ace#14, now on the new release branch `rstudio/montauk-daisy`, and `sync-ace-commits` is pinned to that branch here. The artifacts were built from the rstudio-ace#13 head plus that commit, which reproduces the committed `ace-uncompressed.js` byte-for-byte as a baseline, so the diff is the single style line.

### Automated Tests

New Playwright spec `tests/panes/editor/color_preview_width.test.ts`: opens the reporter's line of twelve hex colors next to the same text with `.` instead of `#`, applies a CSS zoom of 1.25 (a non-integer product with both common device scale factors), and asserts the two rows end at the same x. It passes with the fix and fails with the old style re-applied (5.8px drift).

### QA Notes

On Windows at 125% or 150% display scaling, or on any platform after View > Zoom In once or twice, open a script containing

```r
colors <- c("#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000")
```

with Tools > Global Options > Code > Display > "Highlight R and YAML colors" on. Press End on that line: the cursor should sit right after the closing paren, and bracket matching on the parens should highlight the parens themselves.

### Documentation

None needed.

title: [backport] fix incorrect help/lint/marker rendering
description:
### Intent

Backports fixes for corrupted ANSI / HTML rendering from rstudio-pro.

Even after the previous PR, the ANSI parser had a variety of edge cases that would result in garbled text or junk characters appearing in contexts that didn't know how to render them. The lint and help renderers also weren't consistently handling characters that require HTML escaping, also resulting in broken rendering.

### Approach

A rendering-safe subset of formatting codes are now recognized (mostly color codes), and other ANSI control codes (hyperlinks, cursor positioning, etc.) are removed when converting from ANSI formatting to HTML formatting for rendering in places like the markers view, and _all_ ANSI control codes are removed in contexts that don't even support those (e.g., gutter tooltips for lint messages). Additionally, we now do a better job of tracking whether lint/help messages are prerendered HTML or not and make sure that expressions like `x < y && a > b` show up properly.

### Automated Tests

This PR contains both unit tests and E2E tests.

### Documentation

Intended user-facing behavior is unchanged, so no doc changes are necessary. NEWS file is updated.

title: re-resolve a terminal file link whose cwd changed before the click
description:
A terminal file link's `activate` handler bailed out silently whenever the terminal's cwd had changed since the link was resolved on hover. The link was still underlined with a pointer cursor, so the Ctrl/Cmd+Click simply did nothing.

In practice this hits a fresh terminal: the session reports the shell's cwd about two seconds after it starts (`kCheckCwdDelay`), and that first `terminal_cwd` event clears the link cache. A link hovered just before it arrives and clicked just after is dropped. This is exactly what the e2e flake in `terminal_file_links.test.ts` ("an absolute path with a :line suffix opens the file at that line") looked like on linux-server shard 2 of the #19031 run: the trace shows the `get_events` carrying `terminal_cwd` returning between the hover's `process_resolve_file_paths` and the click, and no RPC at all after the click.

Now `activate` opens the resolved path when nothing has changed, and otherwise resolves the link's text again against the current cwd and opens that result, so a click on a visible link always does what a fresh hover would.

The unit harness test that encoded the old rule ("a delivered link cannot open a file from a previous cwd") is replaced by two tests: a stale link is re-resolved on click, and a stale link whose text no longer names a file opens nothing.

Validation:

- `node --test src/gwt/test/terminal_file_links.test.cjs`: 16 tests pass.

No NEWS entry: this fixes a feature (#18804) that has not shipped yet.

title: fix worktree e2e assertions and test isolation
description:
The E2E failures in #19029 came from the worktree test expecting the toolbar label in Recent Projects, followed by project cleanup and search state leaking into the Console render test. These failures also occurred in #19019's CI run.

Expect the intended `<worktree directory> (<primary project>)` recent-project label, including its parent-path qualifier when duplicate names are retained across Server retries. Make project cleanup use an already-open menu, add an E2E regression for that state, and surface cleanup errors instead of logging and continuing. The Console test now selects its sandbox as the search directory and clears the remembered query before typing; typing preserves the keyboard events GWT needs to enable Find.

Validation:

- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- Both affected suites pass with `--no-deps --workers=1 --retries=0`: 13 tests in macOS Desktop and 13 in macOS Server.
- Desktop used the application artifact from #19029's failing CI run. Server used those same UI assets with an existing local server build whose worktree backend source matches main. The temporary Desktop launcher override is excluded from this PR.
- `git diff --check` passes.

No NEWS entry: this changes only E2E tests and their helpers.

title: zero-padded format diagnostic: follow-ups from code review
description:
Follow-ups to #19013 (the `%05s` diagnostic for `sprintf()` / `gettextf()`), from a code review pass that landed after the PR merged. Addresses #19012.

- **Correct remedy in the message.** The warning recommended `formatC()` with `flag = "0"`, but `formatC()` only space-pads character input (`formatC("ab", width = 5, flag = "0")` gives `"   ab"` on R 4.6.1), so following the advice silently changed behavior. It now suggests a numeric conversion or explicit string padding.
- **No warning without a width.** `'%0s'` pads nothing on any platform, so the `0` flag is only flagged when a literal or `*` width follows.
- **Partial matching of `fmt`.** `sprintf(f = '%05s', x)` is now inspected and `sprintf('%05s', fm = f)` is no longer a false positive.
- **Methods named `sprintf` are skipped.** `x$sprintf(...)` / `x@sprintf(...)` are left alone; `base::sprintf(...)` is still checked.
- **Preference gate.** The check now follows *Run diagnostics on R function calls*, like the other call-level diagnostics, so there is a way to turn it off.
- **Cleanup.** The callee check moved into `checkSprintfCall()` next to the sibling `checkPackageInstalled()`, and the row/column mapping uses `count` / `rfind` instead of a manual walk.
- **Tests** assert the actual message rather than "any lint", check the marker position (including after an embedded newline), and cover the preference gate and the new cases.

No NEWS entry: this adjusts a feature that is unreleased.

## Testing

`rstudio-tests --scope rsession`: 673 tests pass, including `DiagnosticsTest.ZeroPaddedStringFormatsAreFlagged`.

title: list and open git worktrees from the git pane
description:
## Summary

Makes it easier to move between git worktrees of a project from the Git pane.

- The branch menu now has a **(worktrees)** section listing every worktree of the repository (from `git worktree list --porcelain`), showing each one's branch and path, with the current worktree checked. Paths nested inside the main worktree are shown relative to it.
- Selecting a worktree opens it as an RStudio project in this window. On Desktop and Workbench, a right-hand icon on each entry opens it in a new session instead (mirroring the project MRU menu). If the worktree has no `.Rproj`, RStudio offers to create one first. A project in a subdirectory of the repository is looked for at the same offset in each worktree.
- Branches that are already checked out in another worktree (which `git branch -a` marks with `+`, and which previously appeared as ordinary entries whose checkout failed with "already checked out at ...") are now labelled `<branch> (worktree)` and open that worktree instead of attempting a checkout.
- **More > New Worktree...** runs `git worktree add` for a new or existing branch. The directory name follows the branch name (`feature/x` -> `feature-x`) and the parent defaults to the directory holding the repository's other linked worktrees, else the main worktree's parent directory. On success, RStudio offers to open the new worktree. The New Branch dialog can also create its branch in a new worktree.
- **More > Remove Worktree...** runs `git worktree remove` for a chosen worktree, with a force option for worktrees that have uncommitted changes or are locked.
- A project opened from a worktree is labelled with the primary checkout's name and the worktree directory, e.g. `rstudio [feature-x]`, in the project toolbar and the window title; the Recent Projects list shows the primary checkout's name next to the worktree directory, e.g. `feature-x (rstudio)`.
- The branch menu also no longer throws if it is opened before the first status refresh completes.

Backend: `git_list_branches` (and therefore `git_all_status`) now includes a `worktrees` array, each entry carrying the worktree's project directory and `.Rproj` path when one exists; new `git_add_worktree` and `git_remove_worktree` RPCs.

Fixes #19026.

## Testing

- New Playwright spec `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/git/worktrees.test.ts` builds a repo with a linked worktree, checks the menu contents, switches to the worktree through the menu, creates worktrees through the New Worktree and New Branch dialogs, and removes one through the Remove Worktree dialog (passes in `test:server-dev`).
- New gtests in `SessionGitTests.cpp` cover the porcelain parser (locked / detached / prunable / bare entries, CRLF, empty output).
- The "open in new session" icon is only shown on Desktop and Workbench, so that path was verified by inspection only.

title: tutorial pane filter: follow-ups from code review
description:
Follow-up to #19020, which merged before these two review-fix commits reached the branch. Addresses the remaining findings from the review of the Tutorial pane filter box (#10173).

Filter behaviour:

- Filter visibility is decided from the frame's real document instead of the iframe's `src` attribute, which lags navigation that happens inside the frame. A cross-origin or still-loading frame counts as nothing to filter, so a keystroke can no longer throw.
- Launching or opening a tutorial no longer hides the box ahead of time; the load handler alone decides, so a failed launch does not leave the box stuck hidden.
- The home page's footer links open in a new window, like links inside a running tutorial.
- `SearchWidget` also fires on the `input` event, so a context-menu paste or a drop filters immediately. This applies to every user of the widget.
- `data-tutorial-title` carries the displayed `[Untitled tutorial]` placeholder, so untitled entries can be found by the text shown.
- The presenter asks the pane whether the home page is showing rather than re-deriving it from the `src` attribute; the term loop stops at the first miss.

Start button:

- The `onclick` handler is JavaScript inside an HTML attribute, and the parser decodes the attribute before JS reads it. The tutorial name and package are now JS-escaped before HTML-escaping, so a name containing an apostrophe or backslash still starts. (Pre-existing, but the function was already being reworked.)

Tests:

- learnr is preinstalled from `required-packages.txt`, since a copy installed mid-session is never indexed.
- A new spec covers the paste path.
- Expectations count only learnr's entries, so a matching tutorial from another installed package does not fail the run.

No NEWS entry: these are fixes to the still-unreleased filter box.

title: warn about zero-padded '%s' format strings in sprintf()
description:
## Intent

Fixes #19012.

R diagnostics now warn when a format string passed to `sprintf()` or `gettextf()` uses the `0` flag with a `%s` conversion (e.g. `%05s`). The C standard leaves that combination undefined, and in practice some C libraries zero-pad while others space-pad, so the result differs across operating systems. The warning suggests `formatC()` with `flag = "0"` instead.

Companion to #19011, which adds the same check as a repository lint over RStudio's own R sources.

## Approach

- Follows the existing `glue()` precedent in `SessionRParser.cpp`: when an argument list follows `sprintf` or `gettextf` (including `base::sprintf`), `checkSprintfCall()` locates the format string the way R does -- the argument named `fmt` if present, otherwise the first positional argument. Other arguments are data and are not inspected, so `sprintf("%s", "%05s")` is not flagged.
- `checkZeroPaddedStringFormat()` scans the literal for `%` conversions, handling `%%`, positional `%2$`, flags, `*` widths, and precision. Only an `s` conversion carrying the `0` flag is reported; `%05d`, `%10s`, and `%-10s` pass.
- The warning is anchored to the specifier within the string rather than the whole literal, and works for multi-line strings.
- The check runs whenever R diagnostics are enabled, rather than behind the off-by-default "check arguments to R function calls" preference, since the pattern has no realistic false positives.

## QA Notes

- New gtest `DiagnosticsTest.ZeroPaddedStringFormatsAreFlagged` covers positional, named (`fmt =`), namespaced, nested, positional-argument, `*`-width, and precision forms, plus negatives (`%%`, numeric formats, plain widths, data arguments, other functions) and malformed calls. All `DiagnosticsTest.*` tests pass.
- Checked end to end through `.rs.lintRFile()`: warnings land on the specifier's row and column range with type `warning`.
- False-positive sweep: linted every `.R` file under `src/cpp` plus R-devel's `src/library/*/R` (1012 files) with the new check; zero hits.

## Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, I have added a `NEWS.md` entry
- [x] If this PR changes UI, I have reviewed the changes for accessibility (no UI changes)
- [x] I have included tests for my changes

title: add a filter box to the tutorial pane
description:
## Intent

The Tutorial pane lists every learnr tutorial from every installed package in one alphabetical list, so a student who installed one course package sees it buried under learnr's own examples and whatever else came along as a dependency (#10173, #7566). This adds a filter box to the pane's toolbar.

Fixes #10173. Addresses #7566.

## Approach

- The home page generator (`SessionTutorial.cpp`) marks each tutorial entry with a class and `data-tutorial-package` / `data-tutorial-name` / `data-tutorial-title` attributes.
- The pane (`TutorialPane.java`) adds a `SearchWidget` next to Refresh. On each keystroke it walks the entries in the (same-origin) home iframe and hides the ones that don't match. No new RPCs.
- Matching: the query is lower-cased and split on whitespace and punctuation; every fragment must appear somewhere in the title, package name, or tutorial name. So `learnr: ex-data` (copied from the "package: name" line as displayed) and `learnr data` both work, and adding a word always narrows the list. Only the query is split, so a fragment of a hyphenated name still matches it.
- A "No tutorials match the filter." line shows when the filter hides everything; it is not shown while the page is explaining that learnr is missing or indexing is still running.
- The box is hidden while a tutorial is running and re-applied when returning Home, so the filter survives a round trip into a tutorial.
- Filter text is session-only on purpose: persisting it would hand a student an empty pane next semester.

## QA Notes

- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/tutorial/tutorial_pane_filter.test.ts` covers package-name filtering (case-insensitive), multi-term narrowing, the `package: name` form, the empty state and clearing, and re-application after Home. It installs learnr if needed and skips if that fails.
- Manually: install learnr, open the Tutorial pane, type a package name, then add a word from a tutorial title. Start a tutorial (the box disappears), press Home (the box returns with the filter still applied).

## Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, the NEWS file has been updated
- [x] Includes automated tests

title: Apply --ozone-platform from electron-flags.conf at startup on Linux
description:
### Intent

Addresses #16594.

On Linux, Chromium picks its Ozone backend before `main.ts` runs, so an `--ozone-platform` from `electron-flags.conf` reached only the child processes. RStudio could then open with a blank window.

### Approach

On packaged Linux builds, startup checks for a requested `--ozone-platform` before anything else starts (R detection, the login-shell query, startup timing). If the request differs from the backend Chromium started with, RStudio relaunches once with the switch placed ahead of the original arguments.

- Precedence: an explicit `--ozone-platform` (or `-ozone-platform`) on the command line wins, then `RSTUDIO_CHROMIUM_ARGUMENTS`, then `electron-flags.conf`. After startup, neither the env var nor the conf file re-applies the switch in any spelling `app.commandLine.appendSwitch` accepts, so child processes match the browser process.
- Only `x11` and `wayland` are accepted. Other values are ignored and logged as warnings, and the relaunch decision is printed to the console.
- There's no relaunch for `--help`, `--version`, `--version-json`, or `--run-diagnostics`, whose output would go to `/dev/null` in the relaunched process. There's also none in development builds, where exiting stops electron-forge's dev server.
- If `electron-flags.conf` can't be read, the existing startup error dialog reports its path.

The relaunch decision is a pure function, `planOzoneRelaunch` in `electron-flags.ts`, so its cases are unit-tested.

### Automated Tests

- `electron-flags.test.ts`: conf parsing and loading (including an unreadable file), and the relaunch cases: matching, differing, and absent backends; env over conf; command line wins; switch spellings; arguments around `--`; unsupported values; dev builds; no second relaunch.
- `utils.test.ts`: `augmentCommandLineArguments` leaves `--ozone-platform` unchanged.

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test` pass on macOS. Lint reports no errors and two warnings already on main, in `session-launcher.test.ts`.

### QA Notes

Not yet verified on Linux. With `--ozone-platform=wayland` in `~/.config/rstudio/electron-flags.conf`:

- In a Wayland session, the complete IDE opens under Wayland, and project/file arguments are preserved.
- In an X11 session, `rstudio --ozone-platform=x11` stays on X11.
- `rstudio --version` prints the version and exits without relaunching.
- With `--ozone-platform=bogus` instead, RStudio starts on its default backend and rdesktop.log has the warning.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards (no UI changes)
- [x] A reviewer is assigned to this PR
