title: Run the bundled Posit Assistant when the admin selects no version
description:
Fixes #19010.

The administrator's Posit Assistant storage directory now contributes a candidate only when its `selected.json` names a usable slot for the session's protocol. When the file is missing or malformed, has no entry for the protocol, or names a slot that is missing, fails verification, or serves another protocol, the administrator's tier contributes nothing and the bundled copy and the user's slot compete as before. Removing the protocol's entry from `selected.json` returns sessions to the bundled copy.

- `ChatSelector`: adds `selectedSlot(storageDir, protocol)`, which returns only the recorded selection. `resolveSlot()` uses it before falling back to the newest slot, so the user's storage directory keeps its fallback and repair.
- `ChatInstallation`: resolves the administrator's directory with `selectedSlot()`. When working admin slots exist but none is selected, a debug-level log says they were skipped. The "no installation found" log names the administrator's `selected.json`.
- `SessionChat`: when installation is managed and nothing resolves, the error now names the administrator's `selected.json` alongside `versions/`.
- Header comments in `ChatSelector.hpp` and `ChatSlots.hpp` point to rstudio-pro's upgrade CLI (`src/go/upgrade-cli/internal/assistant`), which writes administrator slots and `selected.json` by these rules.
- Tests: the two admin-fallback tests now expect the bundled copy (or nothing without one) and still check that `selected.json` is not written. New cases cover a malformed admin selector, a selection of a slot for another protocol, an entry only for another protocol, `userInstallWouldBeSelected()` ignoring an unselected admin slot, and `selectedSlot()` directly.

No NEWS entry: administrator-installed versions (#18973) have not shipped in a release yet.

Follow-up CLI work in rstudio/rstudio-pro#13036. rstudio-pro's upgrade CLI reports the old fallback until that issue lands; the two should ship in the same release.

title: Add XDG-compliance for vimrc loading
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent
This allows for users to store their vimrc at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vim/` I added xdgUserConfigHome() to search for the vimrc in XDG_CONFIG_HOME when the previous two options ~/.rstudio-vimrc and ~/.vimrc are absent. Vim added XDG base directory specification support in version 9.1. It also supports loading from `~/.vim/vimrc` as well, which can be added.

This builds on top of vimrc loading support from #7350.

Fixes  #19027

### Approach
I added `xdgUserConfigHome()` to be able to get host's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; if this is empty, it falls back to `$HOME/.config/` by default (full path: `$HOME/.config/vim/`.

### Automated Tests

`XdgTest.XdgUserConfigHome` in `src/cpp/core/system/XdgTests.cpp` covers `xdgUserConfigHome()` (default, explicit `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, tilde expansion).

### QA Notes
- With `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set to a custom directory, vimrc loads from that location
  - DevTools shows `VimrcLoader: applied 1 command(s) from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vim/vimrc`
- Higher-priority paths (`~/.rstudio-vimrc`, `~/.vimrc`) still win when present
- Suspended session data can restore a stale `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; completely quit sessions before making any changes.

### Documentation
The tooltip/description in *Global Options → Code → Editing* now lists all three paths.

title: lint for zero-padded '%s' format strings in R sources
description:
## Intent

Add a lint to `test-linter.R` that flags string literals in R sources under `src/cpp` which use the `0` flag with a `%s` conversion (e.g. `%05s`, `%-010s`).

The `0` flag is only defined for numeric conversions. With `%s`, C's `printf()` zero-pads on some platforms and space-pads on others, so these formats behave differently across operating systems. Code that wants zero-padding should use `formatC(x, width = n, flag = "0")` or `sprintf("%05d", as.integer(x))` instead.

## Approach

- Parses each `.R` file and inspects `STR_CONST` tokens only, so comments and symbols can't trigger the check. Files that fail to parse are skipped, matching the existing `.Call()` lint.
- Pattern is `%[-+ #]*0[0-9]*s`, so `%10s`, `%100s`, and `%05d` are left alone.
- Reports `file:line` for each offender.

No existing R or C++ source uses one of these formats, so no code changes were needed. This is a developer-only check, so there is no NEWS entry.

## QA Notes

Ran `./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope r --filter linter`:

- With a planted file containing `sprintf("%05s", "a")`, `sprintf("%-010s", "b")`, a valid `"%10s %05d %s"` format, and a comment mentioning `%05s`, the test failed on exactly the two offending lines.
- After removing the planted file, the suite passes (`FAIL 0 | PASS 81`).

## Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, I have added a `NEWS.md` entry (not needed: developer-only check)
- [x] If this PR changes UI, I have reviewed the changes for accessibility (no UI changes)
- [x] I have included tests for my changes

title: keep unsaved documents when a popped-out source window closes without a prompt
description:
### Intent

On RStudio Server, closing a popped-out editor window that holds unsaved changes is supposed to bring up the browser's unsaved-changes prompt. Browsers only show that prompt in a window the user has clicked or typed in since it loaded; a window that was popped out and then closed without ever being touched (for example after editing in the main window first) just closes. Chrome logs:

```
Blocked attempt to show a 'beforeunload' confirmation panel for a frame that never had a user gesture since its load.
```

Since #18990 the main window hears about that close and closes the window's documents, so the unsaved edits are gone for good (on 2026.09.0 they lingered in the source database and came back on reopening the file).

Fixes #19008.

### Approach

The satellite's `beforeunload` handler still runs when the prompt is suppressed; only the dialog is withheld. So when there are unsaved documents and `navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive` is false (the condition browsers use to withhold the prompt), the handler hands those documents back to the main window with the same `DocWindowChangedEvent` a tab drop uses. The main window adopts them, and the later `closeSourceWindowDocs` pass skips them since they no longer belong to the closed window.

Where the prompt can be shown, nothing changes: the user is asked, and choosing Leave still closes the documents, which matches Desktop's Don't Save. Desktop is unaffected; its windows close through RStudio's own Save / Don't Save prompt.

One limit: the document moves with whatever the window had already backed up to the server, so an edit typed in the window within the autosave debounce right before closing is not carried over.

### Automated Tests

A server-mode e2e test in `source_window_close.test.ts` edits a document in the main window, pops it out, closes the window without touching it, and checks that the document is back in the main window with its edit, still unsaved, and stays there across a reload. It fails without the fix. The pop-out window is driven only through raw CDP, because Playwright's evaluate and locators run as user gestures and would make the browser show the prompt after all.

### QA Notes

Verified on Chromium 147 and Chrome for Testing 154 against a dev server, closing the window through the browser's own window-close path: before the fix the file reopened without the edit; after the fix the document returns to the main window with its edit.

To check by hand on RStudio Server in Chrome: open a file, type something, pop the tab out with "Show in New Window", and close the new window with its close button without clicking into it. The tab should reappear in the main window, still marked unsaved. Clicking into the new window first still gives Chrome's "Leave site?" prompt.

### Documentation

None; no user-facing behavior changes beyond the fix.

title: Ignore Find in Files refresh when no search has run
description:
Clicking Refresh in the Find in Files pane before any search had been run in the project threw `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'resultsCount')`, because `findInFilesBeginFind()` dereferences the persisted dialog state, which is null until a search runs. `onRefreshFindInFiles()` now returns early in that case.

Adds an e2e test that opens a fresh project, clicks Refresh in the empty pane, and asserts no client exception is recorded. It failed with the reported TypeError before the fix and passes after (full `find_in_files_replace.test.ts` spec green under `test:desktop-dev`).

Fixes #19005.

title: Skip connections registry for packages without connections.dcf
description:
Installing a connection package from the New Connection dialog calls `connection_add_package`, which looks up the package's `rstudio/connections.dcf` with `system.file()`. For packages that ship no such file (e.g. odbc), `system.file()` returns `""`, and the empty path was passed to `ConnectionsRegistry::add`, which logged `system error 2 (No such file or directory) [path: ]` to the session log.

The handler now returns early when there is no `connections.dcf`. Packages that ship one (e.g. sparklyr) are registered as before.

Adds a testthat case in `test-connections.R` that fails without the fix.

Fixes #19003.

title: Add status_message to the default session property set in Workbench builds
description:
### Intent

Workbench is adding a Workbench-only `status_message` column to `active_session_metadata`, holding the reason the Job Launcher reported for a session's job ending. This PR brings the shared parts of that change upstream, so the open source and Workbench copies of these files stay the same, apart from the overlay file each repo implements differently.

Open source builds do not change. The default property set gets its Workbench additions through a new overlay, and the column mapping is under `RSTUDIO_PRO_BUILD` next to the existing Workbench-only `suspend_size`.

Reviewed in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/pull/13025

### Approach

- Adds the `ActiveSession::kStatusMessage` property.
- Maps it to a column in `DBActiveSessionStorage` under `RSTUDIO_PRO_BUILD`.
- Moves the default property set, which a batch read with no fields expands to, out of the inline `ActiveSession::readProperties()` and into `ActiveSession::defaultProperties()` in `RActiveSessions.cpp`, so every caller uses one definition.
- Adds `RActiveSessionsOverlay.hpp` and `RActiveSessionsOverlay.cpp`. `defaultProperties()` calls `overlay::addDefaultProperties()` after building the shared set. The open source copy is a no-op stub. Workbench's copy at the same path adds `kStatusMessage`.

Without `kStatusMessage` in the default set, Workbench's homepage made one extra session metadata RPC for each exited session on every refresh.

### Automated Tests

Adds `DefaultPropertiesAreAllReadable`, which checks that database storage can read every property in the default set. In open source builds it fails if a Workbench-only property is ever added to the default set without its guard. The Workbench-only tests stay in Workbench, as with `suspend_size`.

Built and tested in a Workbench build only, not in an open source configuration.

### QA Notes

No user-visible change in open source builds.

### Documentation

None needed.

title: Don't relaunch slow-starting sessions while their process is alive
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

A session that takes over a minute to start was launched a second time on top of itself, and the duplicate failed fighting the first over its socket and project locks.

Similar issues was fixed in #18572; but there's another variant over here: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/12960


### Approach

- The change lives in `ServerSessionManager.cpp`. Sessions we can't identify a process for (custom launchers) keep the one-minute rule.
- Past three minutes a still-running session is relaunched anyway, so a hung start is still replaced, but it can leave two processes behind.
- The session manager now takes its clock and "is this process running?" check as settings, so tests can control them. Production uses the real ones.
- Also fixes a race where server option lookups from simultaneous launches could write to shared state (ThreadSanitizer found it).

### Automated Tests

New `SessionManager` unit tests use a fake clock and fake process checks to cover the one- and three-minute cutoffs, failed requests while a session is starting, old sessions exiting after a replacement starts, and many simultaneous launches. Tests that start real child processes cover crashes, a program that can't run, exited-but-not-yet-cleaned-up processes, and the arguments passed to a session. All 32 `SessionManager` tests pass locally. 

### QA Notes

This change is split between the pro + rstudio side. Expanded coverage to also have better hooks on that side.

### Documentation

No documentation changes; this is internal session-launch behavior.

### Checklist

- [400dacbbd6](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/400dacbbd6) - Don't insert into overlay options on lookup
- [111ad4fd75](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/111ad4fd75) - Drive SessionManager tests with a fake clock and liveness check

title: Give C, C++, and header file types distinct labels
description:
Fixes #9075.

All four C/C++ file types (`.c`, `.cpp`, `.h`, `.hpp`) used the label "C/C++". The status bar's file type menu lists only C++, and appends the current file's type when it isn't already listed. So for a `.c` file the menu showed "C/C++" twice, and once a file was switched to C++ it couldn't be switched back to C.

Changes:
- `CppFileType` now takes a label. The types are labeled "C", "C++", "C/C++ Header" (`.h`, which is treated as C++) and "C++ Header" (`.hpp`, `.hh`), using i18n constants with French translations.
- C is added to the status bar menu, before C++.
- The Edit Snippets dialog keeps the "C/C++" name for its entry, because those snippets apply to both languages. Its error message for invalid snippets now uses that same name, not the file type's label.
- The create-file-types e2e sweep expects the new labels and matches the footer label exactly, so "C" can't pass by matching "C++".

Testing: `create_file_types.test.ts` passes in desktop-dev mode. On a dev server, a `.c` file shows "C" in the status bar, the menu lists C and C++ once each, and switching C → C++ → C works.

title: add more r diagnostics for common errors
description:
This adds a batch of new checks to the R parser / diagnostics system, all of which correspond to hard R errors or near-certain bugs:

- **Repeated formal arguments**: `function(x, x) {}` (R rejects this at parse time).
- **Named argument matched more than once**: `rnorm(n = 1, n = 2)`. Only exact matches against a known formal are flagged, so names absorbed by `...` (e.g. `c(a = 1, a = 2)`) are left alone. Requires argument checking to be enabled.
- **Invalid assignment targets**: `TRUE <- 1`, `1 <- x`, `x -> NULL`. Strings remain valid (`"x" <- 1`).
- **Bare `return`**: `if (x) return` evaluates to the primitive rather than returning. Only flagged when `return` is a statement of its own, so references to the function such as `quote(return)` or `lapply(x, return)` are left alone. Skipped when `return` is a variable in scope (grid has a formal named `return`).
- **`if (x<-1)`**: flagged (as a warning) only when `<-` is glued to both operands, the right-hand side is a numeric literal, and we're in an `if` or `while` condition, so `if (x <- foo())` is untouched.
- **Too many arguments to a zero-argument function** (#9156): `validateFunctionCall()` previously bailed whenever a function reported no formals, since some primitives (`if`, `return`) have none. It now only bails for primitives, so `f <- function() {}; f(1)` and `Sys.time(1)` are reported. The package index now records which exports are primitives, so those (e.g. `rlang::is_null`, `magrittr::add`) are left alone too. Calls wrapped in `.Internal()` are skipped, since they target the internal entry point rather than the R wrapper.
- **Empty trailing argument** (#9157): `c(1, 2, )`. Reported for builtin primitives (which always evaluate every argument, so an empty one errors) and for an allow-list of base closures that forward `...` into one (`paste`, `data.frame`, `cat`, ...). Specials like `switch()` and closures from other packages are left alone, since tidyverse functions deliberately accept a trailing empty argument. `FunctionInformation` gains an `isBuiltin` flag for this.
- **Package not installed**: `library(foo)` / `require(foo)` for a package that isn't installed gets an inline warning. `require()` is only flagged as a statement whose value is discarded (not as the value of a function or an `else` branch), since it's an availability check whenever its result is used (`if (!require(foo))`). `requireNamespace()` and `loadNamespace()` are excluded since they take strings (often variables) and the former is usually an availability check; `character.only = TRUE` is respected, and calls that name `lib.loc` are skipped. The existing on-save info bar ("Package foo required but is not installed" with an Install button) remains the install UI; this provides the marker while typing.
- **Better messages for invalid characters**: error tokens now get a specific message instead of "unexpected token": a pasted smart quote suggests the straight quote, and an unterminated raw string or a lone `%` are named as such.

Also fixed while here: source-resolved functions were constructing `FunctionInformation` with the name and origin swapped.

To check for false positives, I linted every `.R` file in RStudio and in the R-devel `src/library` tree (734 files) with all diagnostics enabled. The remaining hits from the new checks were all real (e.g. `requireNamespace("V8")` before that exclusion was added), and the two leftover "too many arguments" hits are pre-existing behaviour unrelated to this change.

Fixes #9156.
Fixes #9157.
Fixes #18977.

title: harden math preview e2e specs against in-flight typesets
description:
## Summary

Hardens the math preview e2e specs against a race with in-flight typesets. The
popup spec failed on both attempts in the linux-desktop shard of
[run 36594902532](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/36594902532/job/109508532233)
(PR #18993, which does not touch this area):

```
Error: strict mode violation: locator('mjx-container:not(.rstudio-mathjax-root mjx-container)') resolved to 2 elements
```

## Cause

Typesets render into a `visibility: hidden` scratch element inside their target
before being swapped in (`MathJaxTypeset.java`), so for the length of a typeset
the target holds a second `mjx-container`. Each preview also has two render
triggers:

- popup: the document-changed timer (200ms), then the cursor-idle monitor (700ms)
- line widget: `renderAllLatex()` on document load, then the cursor-idle monitor

The popup spec waited for the first re-render and then asserted, which on a
slow runner landed the assertions on top of the second typeset. The CI traces
show the failing assertions at +724ms and +726ms after the keystroke. A
strict-mode violation is thrown at once rather than retried.

This is test-side only; the scratch element is never visible to the user.

## Changes

All in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/math_preview.test.ts`:

- Add a `visibleMath` helper (`.filter({ visible: true })`) and use it for the
  line-widget, popup, Escape and visual-editor locators.
- The popup spec now waits for the re-renders to settle (a quiet window longer
  than the cursor-idle delay) before asserting, so its "no error output was
  ever shown" check covers the idle re-render as well.
- The popup spec installs its observers through the locator rather than a
  hand-rolled `querySelectorAll` search.
- The visual-editor spec folds its two `toBeVisible()` checks into
  `toHaveCount(2)` on the visible-only locator.

## Verification

Run locally with `npm run test:desktop-dev` on macOS:

- With `MathJax.typesetPromise` held for 1500ms to simulate a slow runner, the
  spec on `main` fails the line-widget and popup tests with strict-mode
  violations; the hardened spec passes 5 of 5.
- The hardened spec passes with `--retries=0 --repeat-each=3`.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean.

title: keep unsaved changes when a popped-out source window is closed
description:
### Intent

Fixes #19008.

On RStudio Server, closing a window opened with "Show in New Window" could lose the unsaved changes in its documents. The source window asks the browser to prompt (`beforeunload`), but Chrome skips that prompt in a window that never had a user gesture -- for example, a document edited in the main window and then popped out. Chrome logs:

```
Blocked attempt to show a 'beforeunload' confirmation panel for a frame that never had a user gesture since its load.
```

Since #18990 the main window learns that the window closed, and `closeSourceWindowDocs` then closed every document it held, discarding the edits. (Before #18990 the notification never arrived on Chrome, so the documents lingered with the closed window and came back on reload.)

### Approach

In web mode, `closeSourceWindowDocs` asks the server whether each document is dirty -- the main window's copy doesn't see edits made in the satellite -- and moves dirty ones back to the main window through the same `DocWindowChangedEvent` a tab drop uses. Clean documents close as before. If the lookup fails, the document is left as it is.

Desktop keeps the old behavior. Electron routes the close button through RStudio's own Save / Don't Save prompt (`satellite-window.ts`), and after "Don't Save" an untitled document is still dirty on the server, so moving it back would undo the user's answer.

When the browser does show its prompt and the user chooses Leave, documents with unsaved changes now also come back to the main window. That matches RStudio Server's main window, where closing the browser tab keeps unsaved edits.

### Automated Tests

In `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/source_window_close.test.ts`:

- `unsaved changes come back to the main window (#19008)` (`@server_only`): edits a file in the main window, pops it out, closes the window; the document must reappear in the main window with the edit. Fails without the fix (the tab never comes back).
- `unsaved changes are discarded after "Don't Save" (#19008)` (`@desktop_only`): edits an untitled document, pops it out, closes it through the handler Electron's close event calls, and answers "Don't Save"; the document must be closed. Fails if the move-back also applies on Desktop.

The whole spec passes on `test:server-dev` and `test:desktop-dev` (3 tests each); `ant unittest` passes.

I also checked the reported flow against a dev server in headless Chromium 147, closing the popup through the browser's own window-close path (`chrome.windows.remove` from an extension) without interacting with it first: Chrome still suppresses the prompt, and the edit is back in the main window.

### QA Notes

RStudio Server, Chrome:

1. Open a saved `.R` file and type something in the main editor without saving.
2. Show in New Window. Don't click in the new window.
3. Close the new window with its close button. No prompt appears (the browser suppresses it).
4. The document reappears in the main window with the unsaved change.

Also: click in the new window before closing it -> the browser prompts; choose Leave -> the document comes back to the main window. On Desktop, closing a popped-out window with unsaved changes still shows RStudio's prompt, and "Don't Save" discards the changes.

### Documentation

None needed.

title: stop reduced-motion transitions delaying the data viewer's spacers
description:
## Summary

Fixes #18988.

After #18994 the reporter still could not reach the last row of `view(mpg)`: the grid rested exactly one row short of the bottom, both panes aligned, and a wheel or scrollbar drag that reached the bottom was pulled back a row. The cause is the reduced-motion rule in `DataViewer.css`:

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
   *, *::before, *::after {
      animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
      animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
      transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
   }
}
```

`transition-property` defaults to `all`, so with that rule every inline style write on every element starts a transition, and an element whose transition has just started is laid out at its old value for that frame. `renderVisibleRows` grows the top spacer in the same task that removes the rows it replaces; the removal is immediate but the spacer's growth now lands one frame late, so for one frame the content is one recycled window short. The browser clamps both panes' `scrollTop` to it (no JavaScript writes anything), and when the range recovers the position stays behind: one row for an arrow key, four for a wheel notch. The grow-before-shrink ordering from #18994 cannot help, because all the writes land in the same style recalc.

Chrome reports `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` when Windows' "Animation effects" (Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects) is off, which is presumably the reporter's setup and why it never reproduced elsewhere.

The rule now uses `transition: none !important`. The animations are only ever started by the header and sidebar flash classes, so shortening them stays as it was.

## Evidence

Chrome 154.0.8037.59 on macOS, `main`'s grid files, reduced motion emulated, a 234 x 11 frame at the reporter's geometry:

| Input | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| ArrowDown onto the last row | 23px short, "Showing 188 to 233" | at the bottom, "Showing 190 to 234" |
| 100px wheel notches into the bottom | 92px short | at the bottom |
| Continuous scroll (23px every 16ms) into the bottom | 23px short | at the bottom |
| Same three, native scrollbars | short | at the bottom |
| Same three, no reduced-motion preference | at the bottom | at the bottom |

"Showing 188 to 233" is the text in the reporter's latest screenshot; at their earlier 753px viewport the same emulation gives "Showing 203 to 233" and "Showing 199 to 229", the two strings measured from their recording. Frame by frame, after the render the top spacer has an inline height of 4048px but is laid out at 3841px with 24 animations running on the document; both panes' maximum and `scrollTop` drop from 4623 to 4416, and a frame later the maximum is back at 4623 with `scrollTop` still 4416.

## Testing

One e2e test in `data_viewer.test.ts`, with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated for the page (it reaches the grid's iframe, which the test checks): wheel a 500-row frame to the bottom and confirm it settles there with the last row clear of the scrollbar, then arrow-key away from the bottom and back onto the last row.

On macOS, desktop-dev:

- The test fails against `main`'s stylesheet (the wheel never reaches maximum scroll) and passes with this change.
- `tests/panes/data-viewer/`: 87 passed, 3 skipped.

title: only relay @claude mentions from rstudio/rstudio
description:
The Claude relay (`os-claude.yml`) dispatches a mention's issue/PR number to the receiver, which always acts on rstudio/rstudio. A copy of the workflow running anywhere else -- a fork, or a downstream repository that picks it up through a merge -- would therefore point the receiver at this repository's unrelated item with the same number.

This gates the relay job on `github.repository == 'rstudio/rstudio'`, so copies elsewhere are inert (and forks no longer fail at token generation on every mention).

Internal CI change only; no NEWS entry.

title: Read admin Posit Assistant versions beside the bundled copy
description:
Addresses #18973.

Administrator-installed Posit Assistant versions now live in the directory that holds the copy bundled with Workbench, `<resource>/bin/posit-assistant` (`/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/posit-assistant` on Linux), in the same layout as a user's own `pai` directory. The `posit-assistant-path` session option is no longer used.

### Layout

```
/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/posit-assistant/
  dist/  package.json  protocol.json   <- bundled copy, where Workbench installs it today
  versions/<slot>/                      <- administrator-installed versions
  selected.json                         <- {"selected": {"<protocol>": "<slot>"}}
```

- The bundled copy stays at the directory's root, so rstudio-pro's install rule does not change.
- `versions/` and `selected.json` are read through the existing slot and selector code (`ChatSlots`, `ChatSelector`). `selected.json` is optional. A missing or stale entry falls back to the newest verifying slot for this protocol. RStudio never writes anything in this directory.
- The package owns neither `versions/` nor `selected.json`, so Linux package upgrades leave them in place.

### Resolution

Three candidates compete under the existing ranking: matching protocol first, then newest version.

1. The user's selected slot, when user installation is enabled.
2. The administrator's selected slot.
3. The bundled copy.

Ties keep that order. A selection older than the bundled copy or the user's slot loses to them, so `selected.json` chooses among the administrator's versions but cannot hold users below a newer Workbench bundle. `posit-assistant-installation-enabled=0` removes the user's slot from the competition, as before.

`userInstallWouldBeSelected()` ranks an offered version against the administrator's slot and the bundled copy. `runsUserSlot()` is unchanged in behavior.

### `posit-assistant-path`

The option shipped in 2026.09.0, and rsession rejects an `rsession.conf` that contains an unknown key. So the option stays registered as a hidden, deprecated option (`deprecatedPositAssistantPath_`, following `external-copilot-agent-path`). Sessions ignore it, and log one warning naming the `versions/` directory. Because that warning only reaches each user's session log, rserver also scans the `rsession.conf` sessions use (the `rsession-config-file` override, or the standard XDG lookup) at startup, and logs a warning when the option is set to a non-empty value. Commented-out lines are skipped. `SessionOptions.gen.hpp` is regenerated. Because hidden options are not documented, regenerating the rstudio-pro `rsession.conf` reference removes the entry.

### Other changes

- `bundledPositAssistantInstallPath()` is replaced by `systemStorageDir()`, which returns `<resource>/bin/posit-assistant`. The macOS app-bundle fallback is removed: only Workbench on Linux ships a bundled copy.
- `InstallSearchPaths::adminDir` and `bundledPath` are replaced by `systemStorageDir`. `kBundledPositAiDirName` becomes `kSystemPositAiDirName`.
- In managed mode, the "installation not found" message names the `versions/` directory. Otherwise it points the user at the Posit Assistant pane.
- `runsUserSlot()` reads the user's storage directory directly instead of building the full search paths while holding the resolution lock.
- A `-Wdangling-else` warning in `ChatConstantsTests.cpp` is fixed.

### Tests

`ChatInstallationTests.cpp` is rewritten against the new layout. It covers:

- the three sources competing, and tie order;
- the administrator's selector: followed; not holding back a newer bundled copy; resolved around when stale; never rewritten or created;
- administrator slots for another protocol;
- installations outside `versions/` not being read;
- the bundled copy and administrator slots sharing the directory;
- managed mode;
- `userInstallWouldBeSelected()` against an administrator slot.

`ChatStaticFilesTests.cpp` serves through the bundled copy.

```
GTEST_FILTER='Chat*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession
```

All 239 tests pass. An `rsession.conf` that sets `posit-assistant-path` still parses, and one with an unknown key is still rejected, checked against the built `rsession`.

### NEWS

The two unreleased #18973 entries are rewritten: one under New for the location and ranking, one under Deprecated / Removed for `posit-assistant-path` and `/etc/rstudio/pai`.

### Related

- rstudio/rstudio-pro#12981 tracks the admin guide updates.
- An `rstudio-server upgrade` subcommand that installs versions into this layout is planned as a separate rstudio-pro change.

title: fix session hang when a child process exits during memory accounting
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18991.

On Linux, the R session could spin forever at 100% CPU, and stop responding, when a process it had started exited while RStudio was computing memory usage. Sessions running parallel workloads with many short-lived workers are the ones most likely to hit it.

### Approach

A process can be reaped between the `open` and the `read` of its `/proc/<pid>/status`. The kernel then fails the read with `ESRCH`. Through a `std::ifstream` that sets `badbit | failbit` but never `eofbit`, so the `while (!stream.eof())` loop in `readProcFileKeys` never ended. The `try`/`catch` around it never fired, because the stream does not have exceptions enabled.

The loop dates from 2021, when it only read `/proc/meminfo`. It became reachable in 2025.05, when #15667 started using it for per-process status files.

This change:

- Reads procfs files with `read(2)` rather than a stream, so a failed read is reported with its errno. A read is capped at 1 MB, so a descriptor that never reports end-of-file can't be read without end.
- Takes each process's parent and size from a single read of its status file, parsed in one pass. Previously each descendant's status file was opened a second time to get its size. The session's own process is sized by the same code, and its status file is read once per poll.
- Treats a process that exits while `/proc` is scanned as expected: it is left out, rather than logged at error level. A memory line that is missing counts as 0: zombies keep a status file without them. A value that can't be read is an error, but a process whose parent could still be read keeps its place in the process tree, so that its descendants are still counted.
- Reads `/proc/self/cgroup` the same way. It had the same loop, though it could not hit this race. Its lines are now split at the first two colons only, so a cgroup path that contains a colon is no longer skipped.

I also checked the other procfs readers (`processInfo`, `getSubprocesses`, `isProcessZombie`, `ProcessInfo::creationTime`). They go through `readStringFromFile`, which enables stream exceptions, and each returns promptly with an error in this situation, so they are unchanged.

### Automated Tests

New Linux-only tests in `EnvironmentTests.cpp`:

- `ProcFileReadFailsOnceProcessIsReaped` opens a child's status file, reaps the child, then reads: the reader fails with the error that `read(2)` reports, which is `ESRCH` on Linux. Opening the file again fails with `ENOENT`.
- `ZombieProcessHasNoSize` reads the status of an exited, unreaped child.
- `ChildProcessSizeIsCounted` starts a child that holds 64 MB, and compares the memory reported for the process while the child is alive with the figure once it has been reaped.
- `ProcFileReadIsBounded` reads `/dev/zero`, which fails rather than being read without end.
- `MemoryCgroupIsParsed` covers cgroup v1 and v2 files, cgroups shared with other users, and a path that contains a colon.
- `ProcFileReadReturnsProcessStatus`, `ProcFileKeysAreParsed` and `ProcessStatusIsParsed` cover reading and parsing, including a status file with no `VmSwap` line, a repeated line, and an unreadable value.

The first two skip, rather than fail, on a procfs that doesn't behave as Linux's does in these cases. I have not run them on one (gVisor's, for example).

Run on Linux arm64 (Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 6.18, g++ 11.4): the `ResourcesTest` suite passes, including over 200 repeated runs, and so does the full core suite (777 passed, 12 skipped for Postgres or root privileges).

Beyond the unit tests, I checked the following with a harness that polls `core::system::getProcessMemoryUsed()` while 20 short-lived worker processes turn over:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Child reaped between open and read | never returns | returns in 0 ms |
| 60s of worker churn | hangs after about 200 polls | 207,839 polls, no hang |
| Error-level log entries during churn | 578 in 20s | 0 in 60s |
| Memory attributed to 5 children of 50 MB | 255 MB | 257 MB |
| Memory attributed to a child of 50 MB, and its own child of 50 MB | | 152 MB |

Each child also carries the pages it inherited from its parent, which is why the figures exceed the memory allocated, and why they differ a little between the two builds of the harness.

### QA Notes

Needs Linux. In a session with "Show Current Memory Usage" on (the default), run a parallel workload with many short-lived workers from the console or the terminal, for example:

```r
invisible(lapply(1:200, function(i) parallel::mclapply(1:40, function(j) Sys.sleep(0.01), mc.cores = 20)))
```

The session should stay responsive, the memory usage gauge should keep updating, and the session log should not fill with errors mentioning `/proc/<pid>/status`. The original hang was timing-dependent, so it may not reproduce on demand in an unfixed build.

### Documentation

None needed.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: stop the data viewer pulling its own scroll position back
description:
## Summary

Fixes #18988.

The report is that the Data Viewer does not scroll smoothly, flickers, and is pulled back up from the bottom of a table, leaving the last row cut off. There are two changes here. The first fixes a bug measured in Chrome 154. The second removes a fragility that reproduces the positions in the reporter's recording, though what triggers it on their machine is still unknown.

## 1. The two panes pulled each other's scroll back

The grid and its frozen row-number pane each mirror the other's `scrollTop`, so each write comes back as a scroll event on the pane written to. The handlers told that echo apart from a scroll of the pane's own by comparing the two panes' positions.

Chrome 154 delivers the scroll event for a programmatic write in the frame after the write. While a scroll is in progress, the scrolled pane has moved on by then, so the echo read as a scroll back to the previous frame's position and was mirrored.

| Browser | Echo delivered | Pulled back |
|---|---|---|
| Chromium 147 (Playwright) | same frame | no |
| Chrome 150 (Electron 43, RStudio Desktop) | same frame | no |
| Chrome 154 | next frame | yes |

Measured in Chrome 154 on Windows 11, with a real mouse, on `main`:

- A wheel gesture asking for 1300px moved the grid 663px. `onPinnedScroll` wrote the position back 15 times, for the other 636px.
- A scrollbar drag through the table was written back on every frame, 23 times for 1860px in total.

Each handler now records the position it gave the other pane, and the other pane's handler ignores a scroll event that finds the pane still there. This covers both directions: scrolling the grid, and scrolling with the pointer over the row numbers.

## 2. Scroll content could be short in the middle of a render

If the browser lays out while a render is part-way through, after rows have been recycled off the top of the window but before the top spacer has grown to cover them, the content is short by the height of those rows and `scrollTop` is clamped to it. Forcing a layout at that point gives the positions in the reporter's recording:

| | Forced layout | Reporter's recording |
|---|---|---|
| Wheel notch into the bottom (2026.09.0, native scrollbars) | settles at "Showing 199 to 229" | settles at "Showing 199 to 229" |
| Down Arrow onto the last row (overlay scrollbars) | one row short, "Showing 203 to 233" | one row short, "Showing 203 to 233" |

Nothing in `renderVisibleRows` forces a layout between those steps, and it did not happen in Chrome 154 on Windows without being forced. The grid did depend on the browser never laying out mid-render, and no longer does:

- **Incremental render:** a spacer that ends up taller is resized before the rows it replaces are removed, and one that ends up shorter is resized after the rows that replace it are added.
- **Full rebuild:** spacers are sized while detached and each `<tbody>` is swapped with `replaceChildren`, instead of being emptied and refilled.
- **Summary sidebar:** its virtualizer had the same gap and gets the same two changes.

## Testing

Three e2e tests in `data_viewer.test.ts`:

- **Late echo:** the suite's browsers still deliver the echo within the frame, so it is replayed by hand in both directions: move one pane on, then dispatch the scroll event on the other while it is still where the last mirror left it.
- **Grid, layout mid-render:** with a layout forced after every DOM change and spacer resize the virtualizer makes, wheel to the bottom, trigger a full rebuild there, and arrow-key away from and back onto the last row.
- **Sidebar, layout mid-render:** with the same hooks, wheel a 600-column list to the bottom and check it stays there.

On macOS, desktop-dev:

- All three fail against `main`'s grid and pass with this change.
- `tests/panes/data-viewer/`: 86 passed, 3 skipped.

In Chrome 154 against a dev server built from this branch:

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 11, real mouse: wheel through the whole table | 1300px asked, 663px moved, position written back 15 times | top to bottom and back, position written back 0 times |
| Windows 11, the same with a layout forced after each recycled row | stuck about 22px short of the bottom | reaches the bottom |
| macOS, a write every 5ms to the bottom, as a scrollbar drag makes | not run | written back 0 times, both panes finish where sent |

On Windows the two panes agreed at every one of the 199 grid scroll events and 126 renders in the recording; they differ only at the moment the late echo arrives, which is the event now ignored.

The echo handling was also run on a reduced two-pane page in Chromium 147 and Chrome 154. In Chrome 154 the current handlers write the scrolled pane back 20 times and finish 75px short of where it was sent; the new ones never write it back and finish where it was sent, in both directions.

Still to come: confirmation from the reporter on a daily build.

title: notify the main window when a satellite window is closed
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18987.

On RStudio Server, a satellite window closed with its own close button did not tell the main window that it was gone. Two things went wrong as a result:

- A document or Data Viewer window opened with "Show in New Window" was reopened on the next session restore (page reload, project switch). Each pop-out gets a new window id, so closed windows accumulated over time.
- A Plumber API run with "Run in Window" kept running after its window was closed.

Two related problems with Shiny application windows, on Server and Desktop, are fixed along the way:

- A Shiny application kept running after its window was closed, if the application's page had cancelled an earlier attempt to close the window (an app that prompts before leaving, for example).
- On Desktop, the main window ignored Electron's report that a Shiny application window had closed, so nothing stopped the app when the window's own notification was lost.

### Approach

Each of these windows notifies its opener from a listener registered on the satellite's top-level window (`$wnd`) for `unload`, by code running in the GWT module's frame. Chromium tears down child frames before it fires `pagehide` / `unload` on the parent document, and does not run a listener owned by a detached frame. So when the window was closed the listener was silently skipped: the popup fired `unload`, but our handler never ran. This reproduces on Chromium 134, 140, and 147, so it is long-standing behavior rather than a recent browser change.

The fix registers the listener on the module's own frame (`window`), which is still alive when its `pagehide` fires, and switches from `unload` to `pagehide`, which also keeps this working as Chrome phases out `unload`. The handlers now check that the opener is still there before calling it. This is applied to the three places that used the pattern:

| Window | Notification | Before |
|---|---|---|
| Source window (`Satellite`) | `notifyRStudioSatelliteClosed` | Never sent on Server |
| Plumber API (`PlumberAPIPresenter`) | `notifyPlumberAPIClosed` | Never sent on Server |
| Shiny application (`ShinyApplicationPresenter`) | `notifyShinyAppClosed` | Sent, but only by the `beforeunload` listener added alongside in 2019; the `unload` one was dead |

#### Shiny: cancelled close

The Shiny window's `beforeunload` listener is removed rather than kept next to the new one. `beforeunload` runs while the close can still be cancelled, and the window remembered having reported its closure (`closed_`), so that the two listeners would not both report. When the application's page cancelled the close, the window stayed open with that flag set, and the real close that followed reported nothing. With `pagehide` as the only listener, the window reports once it is really going away, and the flag is no longer needed.

#### Shiny: Desktop fallback

On Desktop, Electron also tells the main window when a child window has been destroyed, and `ShinyApplication.onWindowClosed()` uses that to stop the app when the window's own notification never arrived. The check on the window's name has been inverted since 0e873eaddc (2019): it returned early for Shiny application windows and carried on for every other window. The Plumber equivalent has the check the right way around. This adds the missing negation.

With the fallback working, a closed window is reported to the main window twice on Desktop: by the window itself, and by Electron. The same is now true of Plumber API windows, whose own report used to go missing. On a normal close the second report is harmless.

Moving a running app from its window to the Viewer pane also closes the window, and neither report may stop the app then. The main window expects that close (`stopOnNextClose_`), but only until it has handled the first report, so a report from Electron that arrived later was taken for the user closing the window. `ShinyApplication.onWindowClosed()` and `PlumberAPI.onWindowClosed()` now ignore Electron's report when the app is no longer shown in a window.

A `pagehide` that is not a real close (a reload of the satellite, for example) is already handled: every receiver of these notifications (`SourceWindowManager`, `ChatPresenter`, `PlumberAPI`, `ShinyApplication`) polls the window through `WindowCloseMonitor` before acting.

Desktop was not affected, since Electron notifies the main window through its own close path. The explicit call added for #10906 in `SourceWindow.closeSourceWindow()` is left as is; a second notification for the same window is a no-op.

Other listeners on `$wnd` were checked and left alone: `Window.addWindowClosingHandler` uses `beforeunload`, which fires before the frames are torn down, and the `unload` listeners in `PdfJsWindow` and `HelpPane` are owned by the main window's frame, which outlives the window they watch.

### Automated Tests

- Adds `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/source_window_close.test.ts`, covering a Data Viewer window and an editor window: pop the document out, close the window from inside the page, wait for the `close_document` RPC, then reload and check that no source window reopens.
- Adds `e2e/rstudio/tests/plumber/plumber-api-window-close.test.ts`: run an API in a window, close the window from inside the page, and check that R goes idle. A second test (Desktop only), "API keeps running when it is moved to the Viewer pane", holds Electron's report back by a second and checks that R is not interrupted.
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/shiny/shiny-app-window-close.test.ts` was Desktop-only as a whole. Only its `beforeunload` test is specific to Electron, so the other two now run on Server as well. It also gains three tests:
    - "app stops when the window is closed after a cancelled close" (Server only, since the e2e harness does not let a close be cancelled on Desktop).
    - "app stops when the window cannot report that it closed" (Desktop only), which swallows the window's own notification so that only Electron's report is left.
    - "app keeps running when it is moved to the Viewer pane" (Desktop only), which holds Electron's report back by a second and checks that the app is not stopped.

| Build | Spec | `test:server-dev` | `test:desktop-dev` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Without the fix | source window close | 2 failed (timeout waiting for `close_document`) | 2 passed |
| Without the fix | Plumber window close | 1 failed (R still busy after 15s) | not run |
| With the fix | source window close | 2 passed | 2 passed |
| With the fix | Plumber window close | 1 passed | 2 passed |
| Without the fix | Shiny: closed after a cancelled close | 1 failed (closure reported while the window was still open) | Server only |
| Without the fix | Shiny: window cannot report that it closed | Desktop only | 1 failed (R still busy after 15s) |
| Without the viewer type check (2e23d5df06) | Shiny: moved to the Viewer pane | Desktop only | 1 failed (`stop_shiny_app` requested) |
| Without the viewer type check (2e23d5df06) | Plumber: moved to the Viewer pane | Desktop only | 1 failed (interrupt requested) |
| With the fix | Shiny window close | 3 passed | 5 passed |

Moving a running Shiny app or Plumber API from its window to the Viewer pane is covered by the new tests on Desktop. On Server, where the window's own report is the only one, it has no committed test, and was checked by hand on `test:server-dev`.

`show_document_directory.test.ts`, which also uses popped-out source windows, passes on desktop with the fix. The Posit Assistant satellite specs could not be exercised locally (no Posit AI sign-in on this machine), so CI is the check for those.

### QA Notes

On RStudio Server in Chrome or Edge:

1. Run `tbl1 <- data.frame(a = 1); View(tbl1)`.
2. Click "Show in new window" in the Data Viewer toolbar.
3. Close the new window with its close button.
4. Reload the browser tab, or switch to another project and back.

The closed window should not reopen. Repeat with an R script popped out of the Source pane.

For Plumber, also on RStudio Server:

1. Open a Plumber API file and choose "Run in Window" from the Run API menu.
2. Run the API, then close its window with the window's close button.

The API should stop, and the console should return to the prompt. The same steps with a Shiny app should behave as before.

For the cancelled close, on RStudio Server, with Shiny apps set to "Run in Window":

1. Run an app whose page prompts before leaving, such as:

    ```r
    library(shiny)
    ui <- fluidPage(
      tags$script("window.addEventListener('beforeunload', function(e) { e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = ''; });"),
      "click here, then close the window"
    )
    shinyApp(ui, function(input, output) {})
    ```

2. Click inside the app, close the window, and choose to stay on the page.
3. Wait ten seconds, then close the window again and choose to leave.

The app should stop, and the console should return to the prompt.

title: attribute session request outcomes to the process that produced them
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18963.

rserver keeps one pending-launch entry per session context so a session is not launched twice, and clears it when a proxied request for the context succeeds or fails. It could not tell which process produced that outcome. During a restart, the session being replaced can still answer or fail a request after the replacement was spawned, and that outcome erased the replacement's entry; the next request that found the session unavailable launched it again. #18572 and #18944 each closed one window; the three gaps listed in the issue remained and all reproduce as unit tests against main.

### Approach

- `LocalStreamAsyncClient` records the peer pid of each connection it makes (`SO_PEERCRED` on Linux, `LOCAL_PEERPID` on macOS, via a new `socketPeerPid()` next to `socketPeerIdentity()`), exposes it, and stamps it on errors as a `peer-pid` property so the error handlers, which never see the client, can read it.
- `SessionManager::removePendingLaunch()` and `removePendingSessionLaunch()` take the peer pid. Both now share one policy: an entry still marked as launching is kept (as before); an outcome attributed to a process other than the launched one is kept; an outcome that cannot be attributed (no connection made, or a session reached over TCP) falls back to the existing liveness guard from #18572; anything else ends the launch. The by-session-id variant used to erase unconditionally, ignoring both guards; it is the variant Workbench's launcher-session RPC forwarding calls, so those callers pick up the guards through the merge.
- `launchSession()` clears the entry and its launching flag when the launch function throws, instead of leaving the context suppressed until the pending window expires.

Sessions reached over TCP (Workbench launcher sessions) still cannot attribute outcomes, since there are no peer credentials on a TCP socket. They keep the fallback guards; a generation stamp echoed by the session would close that gap and is left for a pro follow-up.

### Automated Tests

- `ServerSessionManagerTests.cpp`: six new cases covering an outcome from another process (success and error) keeping the entry, an error from the launched process itself clearing it, a launch without a recorded pid ignoring the peer pid, the by-session-id variant applying the same guards both after and during the launch, and a throwing launch function clearing the entry. Each of the three gaps fails on main.
- `LocalStreamAsyncClientTests.cpp` (new): a real local-stream server in-process verifies the client records the peer pid on connect, stamps it on a hang-up error, and reports none when nothing was listening.
- `PosixSystemTests.cpp`: `socketPeerPid()` on a socketpair and on a non-socket.
- `ServerSessionProxyTests.cpp`: two cases run the rpc and content error handlers against a pending launch, verifying that the peer pid stamped on an error reaches the session manager. The response handler, which reads the pid from the client instead, is not covered.

### QA Notes

On RStudio Server, restart R repeatedly (Session > Restart R) and restart the session from the session menu; the session should come back each time with exactly one rsession process for the user. The rserver log at debug level reports "came from process N, not the launched one" when the guard fires.
