title: match both not-found codes in the file and path error helpers on windows
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to #18993.

Windows has two "not found" codes: `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (2) for a missing file, and `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` (3) for a missing parent directory. `isFileNotFoundError()` matched only the first and `isPathNotFoundError()` only the second, so a caller using either one missed the other code. On POSIX the two helpers were already identical, which is why the choice between them never showed up in testing on macOS or Linux.

Both helpers now behave as `isNotFoundError()`, which matches either code.

## Effect on existing callers

There are 22 callers. No caller branches differently on "file" versus "path", so none relies on the distinction. On Windows, before this change:

| Group | Sites | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| POSIX-only code | 4 | None |
| Checks an error created with the matching constructor | 3 | None |
| `isPathNotFoundError()` on `realPath()` | 1 | None; `GetFullPathNameW` doesn't check existence |
| `isPathNotFoundError()` on a failed file read (`Job.cpp`, `SessionCodeSearch.cpp`, `SessionPlots.cpp`) | 3 | A missing file in an existing directory was logged as an error |
| `isFileNotFoundError()` on `getChildren()` (`SessionSourceDatabaseSupervisor.cpp`) | 1 | Always mismatched, since `getChildren()` creates the path variant; logged as an error |
| `isFileNotFoundError()` on a file operation | 10 | Wrong only when the parent directory is missing: five log, one loses a friendlier message, four return the error instead of treating the file as absent |

This is from reading the code, not from observing it on Windows. Nothing here is known to be user-visible beyond log entries, so there is no issue and no NEWS entry.

## Testing

Two new tests in `FilePathTests.cpp`:

- `NotFoundHelpersMatchFileAndPathErrors`: each helper accepts the errors made by both `fileNotFoundError()` and `pathNotFoundError()`.
- `NotFoundHelpersMatchMissingFileAndMissingParent`: each helper accepts what `openForRead()` returns for a missing file and for a file whose parent directory is missing.

Results:

- macOS: `rstudio-tests --scope core` passes (core: 777 passed, 12 skipped; shared_core: 19 passed). Only the `rstudio-core-tests` and `rstudio-shared-core-tests` targets were built, not the full backend.
- Both tests pass on macOS with or without the fix, since POSIX has one code. To check the first test, I temporarily gave `pathNotFoundError()` a second code on macOS: with the old helpers it fails on `isFileNotFoundError(pathError)` and `isPathNotFoundError(fileError)`, and with the new helpers it passes. The second test can only tell the difference on Windows.
- Not run on Windows. `rstudio-tests.bat` runs the shared_core tests in the Windows build, so the next one after merge is the first real confirmation.

## Notes

- rstudio-pro has three more callers of `isPathNotFoundError()` (`ProcessInfo.cpp`, `MonitorClientOverlay.cpp`, `AdminMain.cpp`). All are server-side and none depends on the distinction.

title: treat a missing directory as not found on windows
description:
## Summary

The Windows build has been failing in `rstudio-tests.bat --scope core,rsession`:

```
RActiveSessionsTests.cpp(83): Value of: dir.getChildrenRecursive(...)   Actual: true   Expected: false
RActiveSessionsTests.cpp(121): Value of: sessionDir(validId).exists()   Actual: false  Expected: true
RActiveSessionsTests.cpp(123): Expected equality of these values: 1u, valid.size() (which is 0)
[  FAILED  ] ActiveSessionsTest.RemovesLongAbandonedInvalidSessions
```

`FileActiveSessionStorage::writeProperties` creates the session's `properites` directory only when the first write fails with error code 2 (`no_such_file_or_directory`). Windows reports a missing parent directory as `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` (3); code 2 there is `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`. So on Windows the directory was never created and no property was written. `ActiveSessions::create()` discards the result of that write, which is why this showed up as assertions further down instead of a failed `create()`.

The test has failed on Windows since it was added in #18910. Windows desktop sessions don't write through this storage, so nothing here is user-facing (hence no NEWS entry).

## Changes

- `writeProperties` uses `isNotFoundError()`, which covers both Windows codes.
- New test `CreateWritesPropertiesOfNewSession`, which checks directly that `create()` writes the new session's properties.
- The other places that compared against `no_such_file_or_directory` directly now use `isNotFoundError()` as well:

| File | Error comes from | Effect on Windows before |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionChat.cpp` (2 write sites) | `writeStringToFile` | "Directory does not exist" was never reported; the generic failure was |
| `SessionChat.cpp` (2 read sites) | `readStringFromFile` | a missing directory was reported as a generic read failure |
| `Settings.cpp` | `readStringMapFromFile` | `initialize()` failed when the settings directory was missing |
| `RInit.cpp`, `TexLogParser.cpp`, `http/Util.cpp`, `RToolsInfo.cpp` | file, `realPath` and registry calls | logging or message wording only |
| `NotebookCache.cpp`, `SessionJobs.cpp`, `SessionQuartoXRefs.cpp` | internal "no such id" errors | none; behavior is unchanged |
| `MacFileMonitor.cpp`, `LinuxFileMonitor.cpp` | `stat`-style calls | none; POSIX-only, same meaning |

## Not changed

- `LinkBasedFileLock.cpp` (`isClaimDirectoryRetryError` compares against `ENOENT`): it decides claim-directory retries inside the lock, and the Windows path can't be exercised locally. It likely has the same blind spot.
- `SocketUtils.hpp`: socket connect checks, with the Windows named-pipe codes already listed beside them.
- `SocketOwnership.cpp`: Linux-only, compares against an error it creates itself.
- `FilePath::safeCurrentPath`: compares a boost `error_code` with an `errc` condition, which already maps both Windows codes.

## Testing

- macOS: full backend build; `core` (778 passed) and `rsession` (680 passed) have no failures.
- Replacing the check with one that never matches reproduces the three assertions above on macOS, and fails the new test.
- Not run on Windows. `RToolsInfo.cpp` is Windows-only and `LinuxFileMonitor.cpp` is Linux-only, so neither was compiled locally. The next Windows build after merge is the first confirmation there.

## Possible follow-ups

- `isFileNotFoundError()` matches only code 2 on Windows and `isPathNotFoundError()` only code 3. About 17 cross-platform callers use one or the other and miss the sibling code.
- `SessionChat.cpp` compares against `errc::permission_denied` (13), while Windows returns `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (5).
- `ActiveSessions::create()` ignores the result of `writeProperties`.

title: Remove the Posit Assistant slot manifest
description:
Removes `.slot-manifest.json` from Posit Assistant slot installs. The manifest recorded each file's size and SHA-256. Every time a slot was resolved, RStudio re-checked the recorded sizes and walked the tree looking for symlinks. The slot mechanism hasn't shipped yet, so there are no existing manifests to stay compatible with.

The manifest isn't needed to catch interrupted installs. A package is extracted into a dot-prefixed staging directory, and `allocateSlot()` verifies it and then renames it to its slot name, so a partial install never appears under a name the resolver reads.

A slot now verifies when:
- it is a real directory, not a symlink or junction
- `protocol.json` declares a protocol and `package.json` declares a version
- `dist/client` exists, and `dist/server/main.js` and `dist/client/index.html` are non-empty

The e2e seeder (`fixtures/pai-seed.ts`) no longer writes a manifest, and its tests no longer check for one.

**Tradeoff:** if a slot loses a file other than those checked, after install, it still verifies. Before, it would have been skipped in favour of another slot or a fresh download; now the backend fails when it runs. A normal install of the same version also reuses the slot rather than replacing it, so only a forced reinstall repairs it. This is the same level of checking the unversioned installs (`posit-assistant-path`, the administrator's `pai/bin`, the bundled copy) have always had.

Addresses #18658.

> [!NOTE]
> This was some overengineering that snuck in and I missed initially. Removing to simplify the code and make it easier for admins to manually install Posit Assistant in the future.

title: Write Posit Assistant log to the user's log directory
description:
Addresses #18975.

The Posit Assistant backend is now started with `--log-dir` set to `xdg::userLogDir()`, the directory rsession uses for its own log (`~/.local/share/rstudio/log` by default, or under `XDG_DATA_HOME`). Before, it used `LogOptions::defaultLogDirectory()`, which in a Pro build is `/var/log/rstudio/rstudio-server`. The session user can't write there, so Workbench sessions never wrote a `positai.log`.

Desktop and open-source Server running as a non-root user already got this same directory, so nothing changes for them. Open-source Server running as root, and Workbench, now write `positai.log` next to `rsession-<user>.log`.

Not yet tested in a Workbench session.

title: Skip the wedge screenshot when the test turns screenshots off
description:
When a page stops responding (the #18394 wedge), `attachWedgeDiagnostics` in `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/rstudio.fixture.ts` takes its own screenshot. Unlike Playwright's automatic failure screenshots, it ignored the test's `screenshot` option. So a spec that sets `screenshot: 'off'` because its pages show sensitive data still got one when the page froze.

`perTestReset` now passes the `screenshot` option through, and the wedge screenshot is skipped when it's `'off'`. The page URL and the fail-fast error are unchanged, and tests on the default setting behave exactly as before.

title: Close the session listener's acceptor after its thread has stopped
description:
`HttpConnectionListenerImpl::stop()` closed the acceptor on the calling thread while the listener thread was still running the io_context. If an accept completed at that moment, `handleAccept()` re-armed `async_accept` on the listener thread just as `close()` cleared the acceptor's reactor data, and the listener thread crashed with a null dereference in `epoll_reactor::start_op`. asio acceptors are not thread-safe.

The `LocalStreamHttpConnectionListenerTest` cases added in #18944 hit this intermittently. Each one connects to a listener and then stops it right away. This caused the `rsession` C++ unit test segfault in the CI run for #18972 (in `ReplacesStaleStream`).

`stop()` now:
1. Runs `cleanup()` while still listening, as before.
2. Stops the io_context.
3. Joins the listener thread.
4. Closes the acceptor. This step is skipped if the join timed out and the thread was abandoned, since closing the acceptor then would still race with it.

## Testing

Ran `LocalStreamHttpConnectionListenerTest.*` in 10 processes of 500 repeats each (`GTEST_REPEAT=500`):
- Without the change, 3 of 10 processes segfaulted. A gdb backtrace showed the listener thread in `handleAccept` → `acceptNextConnection` → `async_accept` with null `descriptor_data`, while the main thread was in `stop()`.
- With the change, 0 of 20 processes failed.

The full `rsession` C++ suite passes (668 tests).

title: Keep the active column's commands when another column refreshes
description:
Fixes #18955.

When more than one source column is open, a refresh that runs in an inactive column alone could hide or disable commands for the active document. For example, File > Publish disappeared for an R Markdown document in the main column after Save All saved a script in another column. The same happened after closing an unselected tab in another column.

An inactive column's refresh writes some shared commands directly (the Publish, Synctex, and R Markdown format commands, plus commands its previous editor supported). When the manager refreshes every column, the active column runs last and restores them. A column's own refresh (from its dirty-state handler, a tab close, or a tab selection) had no such pass after it.

- `SourceColumn.manageCommands(forceSync)`: when the column isn't active, run `SourceColumnManager.manageCommands`, which refreshes the active column last.
- `manageSynctexCommands`: drop the unconditional `setVisible(false)`/`setEnabled(false)` on `synctexSearch`. The active column always sets the command through the `(active, ...)` calls that follow, and the resets let the per-column `SynctexStatusChangedEvent` handler hide the command after the active column had shown it.

The issue proposes that inactive columns never write shared commands. That would break column switches: the previous column's commands are hidden by exactly those writes, so they would stay visible after switching to a column whose document doesn't support them.

### Tests

`e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/source_column_commands.test.ts` covers Save All and closing a tab in an inactive column. Both tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. The existing column suites (`source_column_activation`, `show_document_directory`, `active_tab_restore`, `close_open_race`, `source_pane_reset`, `vim_open_documents`) pass in desktop-dev mode. The synctex path has no automated test.

title: Read admin Posit Assistant installs only from posit-assistant-path
description:
Fixes #18973.

An administrator-provided Posit Assistant now exists only when `posit-assistant-path` names one. The session no longer reads `<systemConfigDir>/pai`.

### Resolution

- **`posit-assistant-path` unset:** the user's slot and the bundled copy compete under the #18774 rules. Ties go to the user.
- **Set to `P`:** `P` contributes up to two candidates.
  - The slot `P/selected.json` names. If that selection is missing or stale, the newest verifying slot for this protocol is used, and `P/selected.json` is never written.
  - `P` itself as a single unversioned installation, the 2026.09 layout. `P/bin` is not read.

  The two compete under the #18774 rules, and ties go to the slot. The winner always runs, ahead of the user's slot and the bundled copy whatever their versions. It also runs when it declares another protocol; the session reports that as a protocol mismatch.
- **`P` holds no valid installation:** the bundled copy is not used. The user's slot is used when user installation is enabled. A warning naming `P` is logged once per session.
- **`userInstallWouldBeSelected()`:**
  - false whenever `P` has a valid installation;
  - true when `P` is invalid and user installation is enabled;
  - otherwise ranked against the bundled copy.
- **"Installation not found" messages:** they name `P` when it is set. Otherwise they say installation is managed and nothing has been configured, or tell the user to install from the Posit Assistant pane.

### Code changes

- `InstallSearchPaths::systemStorageDir` and `pinnedPath` are replaced by one `adminDir` field.
- `kLegacyInstallDirName` is removed.
- The `posit-assistant-path` option description is rewritten, and `SessionOptions.gen.hpp` is regenerated.
- The doc comments on `InstallSearchPaths`, `locatePositAssistantInstallation()`, `userInstallWouldBeSelected()` and `isPositAssistantInstallationEnabledByAdmin()` are rewritten.

### Tests

The `ChatInstallationTests.cpp` resolution tests are rewritten against `P`. Tests of a default-location copy competing by version are deleted. `NeverReadsTheSystemConfigDirectory` redirects `RSTUDIO_CONFIG_DIR` and `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` to a temp directory and stages a slot and a `bin/` in the old default location. It then checks that the session's own sources find neither. `ChatStaticFilesTests.cpp` serves through `P` as an unversioned directory.

```
GTEST_FILTER='Chat*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession
```

All 268 tests pass.

### NEWS

- Added an entry under New for how `posit-assistant-path` is now read.
- Added an entry under Deprecated / Removed for dropping the default system location. It covers setting `posit-assistant-path=/etc/rstudio/pai/bin` for existing Server deployments, and notes that Desktop now runs only the user's own install.
- Revised the #18658 and #18774 entries, which described the default system location.

title: terminate the shell when a terminal is closed
description:
Fixes #18976.

### Root cause

Closing a terminal (`TerminalSession.terminate()`, also `rstudioapi::terminalKill()`) sent `process_interrupt` and then reaped the process record. Since #15700 (Feb 2025) `ConsoleProcess::interrupt()` only sends `SIGINT` (a hard stop follows only after three interrupts, for the VCS progress dialog's Stop button). An interactive shell ignores `SIGINT` and just redraws its prompt, so after the close:

- the shell kept running under `rsession` (verified: the `bash` child was still there 10s after the close);
- its prompt redraw arrived after the client had reaped the record and closed the websocket, so every output chunk failed in `sendText` with `Unknown handle` and was logged at ERROR level (the lines in the report);
- that output also recreated the buffer file `process_reap` had just deleted, leaving an orphan under the `console07` directory.

The doubled log lines are a separate desktop-only bug: `SessionMain` initializes logging before options are read and again for desktop mode, and `initializeLog()` never removed the file destination the first call created (only `reinitLog()` did), so both wrote every line.

### Fix

- New `ConsoleProcess::terminate()` and `process_terminate` RPC, used by the terminal close path and `rs_terminalKill`; `process_interrupt` keeps its SIGINT-first behavior for the VCS dialog.
- `enqueOutputEvent` skips the websocket push while no client is attached (output stays in the buffer, which the client reloads on connect) and drops output once termination was requested, so the reaped buffer file is not recreated.
- `initializeLog()` / `initializeStderrLog()` remove the previous reloadable destinations before creating new ones.

### Tests

- `LoggingTest.ReinitializingLogReplacesPreviousDestinations` (fails before the fix with two copies of the line).
- e2e `closing a terminal terminates its shell process` in `panes/terminal/terminal.test.ts`: captures the shell pid from `rstudioapi::terminalContext()`, runs Close current terminal session, and polls until the OS no longer reports the pid.

title: Populate What's New content for 2026.10 (Blue Mistflower)
description:
Replaces the placeholder on the 2026.10 What's New page with entries drawn from NEWS.md.

I will do this one more time at the end of coding.

## Included

New Features: fixed plot size and save resolution (#4422), hiding data viewer columns (#17787), Show Hidden Objects in the Environment pane (#9755), active tab highlight (#18692), look-alike character diagnostics (#14485), Select Current Statement (#16102), Change Spelling Language (#12223), Show Document's Directory (#6781), terminal changes in one entry (#18804, #14226, #1687), `+` from the pipe shortcut in ggplot2 chains (#15261), editor shortcuts in the Console (#12379), smooth scrolling (#14696), Markdown outline (#13505), Quarto render with "(No Preview)" (#12838), faster startup and smaller installs (#18739, #18738), and Posit Assistant updates (#18658).

Deprecated: removal of the Uninstall Posit Assistant command (#18658), linking to the user guide section on removing it. The link and its anchor were checked.

## Left out

- Small behavior changes that read as fixes: the minimized Console staying minimized after a render (#11622), the scrollback limit applying immediately (#16386), and the R version showing at startup (#18857).
- Internals: atomic state-file writes (#18911), renderer and GPU crash logging (#18803), and choosing which Posit Assistant install to run (#18774).
- The macOS libomp warning (#18937). It is niche, and it shows up when it applies.
- Dependencies: none of this cycle's bumps (Copilot Language Server, Electron, Node.js) are visible to users, and Quarto did not change.

title: Bump the CI Node.js version from end-of-life 20 to 24
description:
Every workflow that installs Node.js through `actions/setup-node` was still pinned to `node-version: 20`. Node 20's security support ended on 2026-04-30, so CI has been building and testing on an unpatched runtime since then. This changes all 21 of those lines to `24`, across 11 files under `.github/workflows/`. Nothing else changes.

Node 24 also clears the `EBADENGINE` warning from `npm ci` in `e2e/rstudio`, since `better-sqlite3` requires Node 22 or newer. The desktop build isn't affected: it uses the bundled Node from `RSTUDIO_NODE_VERSION` through CMake, not the Node that `setup-node` installs.

Validated with 23 dispatched runs on this branch, one per engine environment (every Linux config, macOS 14/15/26/27, Windows Server 2025, Windows 11 ARM, and Ubuntu 24 Server). All passed on Node 24.

Addresses #18850.

title: Add Show Hidden Objects and Show .Last.value toggles to the Environment pane
description:
Fixes #9755.
Fixes #18929.

## What this does

Adds two checkable items to the Environment pane's List/Grid menu:

- **Show Hidden Objects** – new `show_hidden_objects` user pref (default off). When on, objects whose names begin with a dot are listed, including hidden arguments such as `.data` in a debugger frame.
- **Show .Last.value** – the existing `show_last_dot_value` pref, which was previously only in Global Options > General > Advanced.

Changing either pref refreshes the pane immediately. Previously, changing "Show .Last.value" in Global Options had no effect until the next refresh.

## Backend

- The pane's listing and the environment monitor share one set of helpers in `EnvironmentUtils`. The pane lists names per the two prefs; the monitor tracks every name (hidden objects and `.Last.value`) whatever the prefs say, and applies the prefs only when it emits pane events. A pref change therefore needs no re-baselining of the monitor, and a change made to a hidden object before it was shown is still reported once it is.
- `.Last.value` is listed by its own pref alone. It lives in `baseenv`, so listing globalenv with all names doesn't include it on its own, and listing baseenv with all names would include it as a hidden object.
- A function frame's `...` is never listed. It holds the caller's unevaluated arguments, and the pane's describe/size code isn't built for it. A user-assigned object named `...` is still listed.
- When either pref is written, the session sends a refresh to the client (a write made while the pane shows Python does nothing).
- The assistant's variable-change signal skips dot-prefixed names, whatever the pane shows. This matches its full variable listing, which uses `ls()`; both use the same predicate. It also stops `.Last.value` being sent when "Show .Last.value" is on.
- The monitor's single-refresh shortcut (workspace cleared, or nothing yet created) now fires only when a visible object appears or disappears, since `.Last.value` and `.Random.seed` are always tracked and `.Last.value` changes after every command. The per-object diff is computed on that path too, so the first object created in an empty global environment now reaches the assistant (#18929).
- Hidden arguments that haven't been evaluated yet are shown as promises and are not forced. This uses the same code path as other arguments.

## Behavior notes

- Clear Workspace keeps its own "Include hidden objects" checkbox, which is not tied to the new pref.
- The toggle applies to R environments only. Python listings are unchanged.
- With Show Hidden Objects on, `.Random.seed` is listed in the global environment, as `ls(all.names = TRUE)` lists it, and the pane updates it after each use of the RNG.
- With Show Hidden Objects on, viewing an S4-heavy package environment is slower, because each hidden S4 class/method table is described. For example, `package:methods` takes about 1.3s and `package:Matrix` about 1.7s, compared with 0.1–0.25s for their visible objects. The global environment and debugger frames are unaffected.

## Tests

- `test-environment.R`:
  - hidden objects are listed only when the pref is on
  - `.Last.value` is listed once when both prefs are on
  - function frames list hidden arguments without forcing them, and omit `...` (including when no dots were passed)
  - a user-assigned `...` is listed
- `EnvironmentMonitorTests.cpp` (new, runs against the live global environment):
  - toggling the pref in either direction reports no changes
  - a modification, creation, deletion, or promise evaluation in the same evaluation as the pref change is still reported
  - hidden objects update the pane only while shown, including a change made before they were shown, and are never sent in the assistant signal
  - the first object created in an empty global environment is reported to the assistant as created
  - a `.Last.value` change in a workspace with no visible objects sends neither a refresh nor an assistant reset
  - `.Last.value` follows its own pref, in the pane's listing of baseenv too, and is always tracked by the monitor

Manually verified in an `rserver-dev` session: both toggles, live updates, a `browser()` frame with `.data` and `...`, and sync between the menu item and the Global Options checkbox.

title: align session launch and listener init signatures with workbench
description:
Two signature changes that Posit Workbench has carried on top of these files for a long time, brought here so that future upstream merges stop conflicting on them. Neither changes behavior in RStudio Server.

## `SessionManager::launchSession()` and `SessionLaunchFunction` take a `json::JsonRpcRequest`

Workbench threads the parsed RPC request through the session launch so its launcher can read launch parameters from it. RStudio Server has no use for it, so the one caller (`launchSessionRecovery()`) passes a default-constructed request, which is what Workbench's equivalent caller does too. The trailing `extraArgs` parameter on `launchSession()` is the same story: a pass-through into the session arguments, defaulted to empty.

This delta is the one that hurts most: every launch function in `ServerSessionManagerTests.cpp` differs by one parameter, so any upstream change to those tests (most recently #18944) conflicts in the Workbench merge.

## `initializeHttpConnectionListener()` returns `core::Error`

Workbench can fail here (it restricts standalone sessions to a configured port range). RStudio Server's implementations always succeed, so this only threads a `Success()` through, and `startHttpConnectionListener()` now checks the result before starting the listener.

## Verification

Syntax-only compile of the five touched translation units (`ServerSessionManager.cpp`, `ServerSessionProxy.cpp`, `ServerSessionManagerTests.cpp`, `SessionPosixHttpConnectionListener.cpp`, `SessionHttpMethods.cpp`) against a configured macOS build. The Windows listener change mirrors the Posix one.

title: fix vim commands that open documents
description:
Fixes #18948.

With Vim keybindings, three commands that open documents throw instead of doing anything:

| Command | Client exception |
|---|---|
| `:e <file>` (also `:tabe`, `:badd`) | `source.getColumnManager is not a function` |
| `:e` with no file | `source.onNewSourceDoc is not a function` |
| `]f` / `[f` | `source.onOpenNextFileOnFilesystem is not a function` |

### Cause

When source code moved from `Source` to `SourceColumnManager` (29ab246060, 0f1748d525c, both in 1.4), these JSNI callbacks in `SourceVimCommands` were left calling methods through `Source` (or a nonexistent `getColumnManager()`) on what is now a `SourceColumnManager`. JSNI doesn't check the qualifier's class, so the code compiled; the calls only fail at runtime.

### Fix

The callbacks now call three private helpers on `SourceColumnManager`:

- `vimEditFile` resolves the typed path through a new R RPC, `ensure_editable_file`, then opens the file. The backend stores a document's path as given, so without this `:e foo.R` opened a document whose path was the relative `foo.R`. The RPC resolves only the file's folder against R's working directory, so a symlinked file keeps its own path, as with `file.edit()` and the Files pane. Unlike `rstudioapi::documentOpen` (which the issue suggested following), it does not resolve the whole path: that would open a second, independent editor for a symlinked file that's already open under the link. As before, a missing file is created; a missing folder is not.
- `vimNewSourceDoc` creates a new R script, as the `newSourceDoc` handler does.
- `vimOpenAdjacentFile` executes `openNextFileOnFilesystem` / `openPreviousFileOnFilesystem`, whose implementation lives in `Source`.

Now that `:e` runs, its callback also:

- takes the whole argument as the file name, with Vim's backslash escapes (`\ `, `\%`, `\#`). File names with spaces now work, and `:e! <file>` opens the file (`:e!` alone still reverts the current document).
- shows an error instead of doing nothing when the name is a folder, the file can't be created, or the name uses Vim's `%` (current file) or `#` (alternate file), which RStudio doesn't expand. Otherwise `:e#` would create and open a file named `#`.

`SourceColumnManager.editFile` is unchanged: its other callers (`documentOpen`, file hyperlinks) already pass aliased paths.

### Tests

New `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/vim_open_documents.test.ts` covers:

- `:e <file>`, relative to R's working directory
- `:e` creating a missing file whose name has an escaped space, and `:e! <file>`
- `:e` on a symlink, which opens under the link's path (skipped on Windows)
- the error dialog for `:e#`, `:e %`, a file in a missing folder, and a folder, with no file created
- `:e` with no file
- `]f` / `[f` across three files. The directory listing isn't sorted, so the test checks that `[f` undoes `]f` and that a second `[f` reaches the third file.

Each test waits for the lazily loaded Vim keybindings before typing. On `main`, the `:e <file>`, `:e`, and `]f` / `[f` cases fail with the exceptions above. With only the JSNI fix and without the path resolution, the `:e <file>` case still fails: the file opens, but its document path is the relative name. The symlink case fails if the whole path is resolved. With the full fix, all pass (`test:desktop-dev`), as does `vimrc_keybindings.test.ts`.

That vimrc test's canary checks that an `edit ~/vimrc-canary-e2e.R` line in a vimrc does not run. Since `:e` threw before this change, the check could not fail; it now exercises the vimrc loader's command allowlist, and still passes.

title: atomic write follow-ups: windows rename fallback, in-place chmod, group carry-over
description:
Follow-ups to #18918 from a second review pass, all in `FileSerializer.cpp`. Addresses #18911.

## Windows rename

- The POSIX-semantics rename fell back to `MoveFileExW` only on `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` or `ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`. Some network redirectors and filter drivers reject `FileRenameInfoEx` with a code of their own (e.g. `ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION`, or `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`). On such a volume every atomic write failed with no fallback. Now any failure other than a target in use also gets a legacy rename attempt. The POSIX rename is only switched off for the two "unsupported" codes, so later retries still try it first: it's the only rename that can replace a file our readers have open.
- `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` was treated as "in use" unless the target had the read-only attribute. So a target whose ACL denies `DELETE` stalled each write for up to `maxRetrySeconds` before failing. Now a read-only target fails at once. Any other target is opened for `DELETE` with full sharing: a sharing violation (or success) means it was in use, so the rename is retried, and `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` fails the write immediately. A target that doesn't exist yet still retries, because that denial most likely comes from a scanner holding the new temp file.
- Trade-off: a target that is delete-pending (deleted while a reader still has it open, on filesystems without POSIX delete semantics) also answers the `DELETE` probe with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`. It used to be retried until the reader closed it; now that write fails.

This code compiles only on the daily Windows build, as before.

## In-place fallback

`writeInPlace()` made a `chmod(0600)` failure fatal for owner-only files. Before #18918, `UserStateLayer` logged that failure and wrote anyway. The in-place path is exactly what a file owned by another user gets (bind-mounted into a container, or in a directory we can't write), and `chmod` fails on such a file even when it's already private. The failure is now an error only when the file grants group or other access, i.e. when there was something to fix; otherwise it's logged at debug level, with the file's owner.

## Group carry-over

If the replacement can't keep the target's group (e.g. a file left `root:root` by `sudo rstudio`), it stays in the group it was created in: ours, or the directory's. It used to keep the target's mode as-is, so a 0640 file's group access went to a group the owner never chose. Now that group gets exactly the access everyone else gets. That means no more, and also no less, since members of a file's group are checked against its group bits instead of its other bits (0640 becomes 0600, 0604 becomes 0644). `fchown()` still decides whether the group can be carried over, and if the temporary file's group can't be read, it's treated as different from the target's.

## Tests

- `WriteStringAtomicPreservesGroup`: a target in another group the process belongs to keeps that group. Groups that `chown` refuses (e.g. unmapped groups in a rootless container) are passed over, and the test skips if none is left.
- `WriteStringAtomicForeignGroupGetsOtherAccess`: a target in a group we don't belong to is replaced with its group access set to the other access (0624 becomes 0644, so both a reduction and an increase are checked). It runs where new files take the directory's group (macOS /tmp) and skips elsewhere.
- `WriteStringAtomicReadOnlyTargetFailsWithoutRetrying` (Windows): a read-only target fails well before a 10s retry budget and keeps its contents.
- The chmod and root-owned cases need another uid and can't be unit-tested; the existing in-place fallback tests still cover a `chmod` that succeeds.

title: keep the folder chooser's path across listing arrivals
description:
Fixes #18938.

Since #18923, the GWT directory chooser (`ChooseFolderDialog2`: RStudio Server, or Desktop with native dialogs off) hands its caller an empty path. As a result, `DirectoryChooserTextBox` fields (New Project wizard, Find in Files, options panes, ...) are blanked, and Create Project silently does nothing.

### Cause

#18923 moved `browser_.setFilename(context_.pwd())` ahead of `super.onNavigated()` so a deferred accept would see it. But `super.onNavigated()` refreshes the browser, and `RowTable.clear()` fires a null `SelectionEvent`, which `ChooseFolderDialog2.onSelection()` answered by blanking the filename. This happened on every listing arrival, not only for a deferred accept: opening the chooser, double-clicking a folder, and clicking Choose also returned `""`.

### Fix

- `FileSystemDialog.onNavigated()` is now `final` and runs the browser refresh, then a new `onBrowserNavigated()` hook, then any deferred accept. This replaces the "adjust the filename before `super.onNavigated()`" rule, which subclasses couldn't follow. `FileDialog` and `OpenFileDialog` now do their arrival work in the hook. `OpenFileDialog`'s filename clear now runs after the refresh again, as it did before #18923.
- In `ChooseFolderDialog2`, a null selection now means "the directory being shown" (`pwd`) instead of `""`. Every redraw of the listing clears the selection, both when a listing arrives and after a failed navigation (`FileSystemDialog.onError`), so this one handler keeps the path current in both cases. The chooser ignores the clear from the progress view, one second into a slow navigation, because `pwd` is still the directory being left at that point.

Two older problems with the deferred accept turned up in review and are filed separately: #18959 (a typed folder that doesn't exist falls back to the project or home directory, and the accept runs there) and #18960 (with two overlapping navigations, the accept runs on whichever listing arrives first).

I left `RowTable.clear()` unchanged, even though firing a null selection during a routine refresh is the underlying hazard: other widgets use `RowTable` and may depend on that event.

### Tests

New `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/files/choose_folder_dialog.test.ts` drives the chooser from Find in Files' "Search in" field. It first goes to a fresh sandbox folder through the breadcrumb's Go To Folder prompt, because the chooser's starting directory depends on earlier specs. Two cases:

1. Double-click into a folder, click Choose; the field gets that folder's path.
2. The reported flow: New Folder, then Choose while the new folder's listing is held with `holdListFiles()`. After release, the field gets the new folder's full path.

Both failed without the fix (`Received string: ""`) and pass with it (`test:desktop-dev`). A temporary check also confirmed that, while the chooser's listing was held past the progress view, the field kept the double-clicked folder rather than showing its parent. The existing chooser tests in `plots_pane.test.ts` and `open_file_dialog_typed_navigation.test.ts` still pass; the latter is server-only, so I ran it on desktop through an untagged temporary copy.

This PR also fixes an e2e flake from #18923 that failed `open_file_dialog_typed_navigation.test.ts` on server-linux, here and in other PRs' runs. When a page's last route is removed, Playwright turns request interception off, and a request paused during that switch is never continued. When that request was the `get_events` long-poll, the client stopped receiving events and the spec's `afterAll` console wait timed out. `fixtures/request-interception.ts` now installs a route that matches nothing when either launcher starts a session, so no spec's route is ever the last one. That protects every spec that routes. Interception does have side effects: it turns off the HTTP cache, it pauses each request until Playwright (running in the worker process) continues it, and Playwright answers CORS preflights itself. Because the session lasts for the whole worker, turning interception on only in the specs that route would still leave these in place for whichever specs happen to run after them. Installing the route at launch makes every spec run under the same conditions. `request-interception.ts` documents these trade-offs.

A local stress spec toggled a route 60 times per round while console output streamed. Without the launch-time route it hung in round 4 on one run and round 7 on another; with it, it passed all 15 rounds. The other specs that route (`interpreter_version`, `spelling_language_switch`, data viewer `refresh-recovery`) pass with it too.

No NEWS entry: the regression only exists in unreleased 2026.10 dailies.

title: warn when a second copy of the OpenMP runtime is loaded on macOS
description:
## Intent

On macOS, having two copies of the LLVM OpenMP runtime (`libomp.dylib`) loaded in one R process can crash the session the moment a package runs an OpenMP region. #18937 is one instance: the reporter's session died in data.table's `gforce` while "Run examples" loaded data.table for the first time. RStudio can't prevent the crash (a dylib can't be unloaded), but it can tell the user what happened and how to fix it *before* the crash, which is what this PR adds.

## Background

R's bundled `libomp.dylib` and other builds of it (Homebrew's, in the reporter's case) export the same weak C++ template symbols (e.g. `__kmp_suspend_64<false,true>`), and dyld coalesces weak definitions across images. When a second copy loads, its internal calls to those symbols are redirected to the copy that loaded first. If that first copy was never initialized (the package that linked it doesn't actually use OpenMP), the redirected call reads `__kmp_threads[gtid]` off a null table and R segfaults.

Verified locally with the same libomp builds as the crash report: a stub package linked against Homebrew's libomp, loaded before data.table, makes `dt[, sum(a), by = b]` segfault; loaded after data.table it runs fine. The usual origin is a `~/.R/Makevars` that adds `-fopenmp` / `-lomp` globally (which data.table's own macOS install guide recommends), so every package later built from source links the Homebrew copy while CRAN binaries link R's.

## Changes

- `SessionPackages.cpp`: two macOS-only routines. `rs_loadedOpenMPRuntimes` walks dyld's image list for loaded OpenMP runtimes (`libomp.dylib`, and Intel's `libiomp5.dylib`, which shares its code and its coalesced symbols); `rs_openMPRuntimeUsers` reads each image's `LC_LOAD_DYLIB` load commands to pair the images that link an OpenMP runtime with the runtime they link. Both return empty results on other platforms.
- `SessionPackages.R`: `.rs.notifyPackageLoaded` (the per-package `onLoad` hook RStudio already registers) now calls `.rs.checkOpenMPRuntimes` first, and `.rs.registerPackageEventHooks` runs it once more after each package scan, so copies loaded before any hooks existed (e.g. from `.Rprofile` during startup) are reported too. When more than one runtime is loaded, it logs a warning and writes a message to stderr naming each copy, the packages linking it (from each namespace's registered DLLs), and the `install.packages(..., type = "binary")` call that removes the extra copy. On an R that can't install binaries (e.g. Homebrew's or conda's), the advice is to rebuild the listed packages from source against one copy instead. The message goes to stderr rather than through `message()`, so `suppressMessages()` or a notebook chunk with `message = FALSE` can't hide it. It is shown once per set of runtimes, and again when another package linking the extra copy loads, so the reinstall list stays complete (on an R without binaries, whose advice names no packages, only once per set of runtimes). `options(rstudio.openmp.checkRuntimes = FALSE)` disables the check. A failure in the check is logged and never turns into an error from `library()`.

Sample output from a real session, with a stub `omptest` package linked against Homebrew's libomp loaded before data.table:

```
> library(data.table)
More than one copy of the OpenMP runtime (libomp) is now loaded in this R session:

  /opt/homebrew/Cellar/libomp/23.1.2/lib/libomp.dylib
    linked by: omptest
  /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.6/Resources/lib/libomp.dylib (bundled with R)
    linked by: data.table

Loading more than one copy can crash R as soon as a package runs OpenMP code.
To fix this, reinstall the packages linked to the copy not bundled with R as binaries:

  install.packages("omptest", type = "binary")

and remove OpenMP flags (-fopenmp, -lomp) from ~/.R/Makevars, so that packages
built from source use the copy bundled with R.

Set options(rstudio.openmp.checkRuntimes = FALSE) to disable this check.
data.table 1.18.2.1 using 7 threads (see ?getDTthreads).  Latest news: r-datatable.com
```

Images that link a runtime through an `@rpath` reference (e.g. a Python extension loaded via reticulate) can't be tied to a specific copy, so they are listed separately and the advice stays generic.

If the package that brings in the second copy runs OpenMP code in the same request that loaded it (e.g. "Run examples" loading data.table and running `gforce` right away), the session can crash before the console output reaches the client. The warning is written to the rsession log before that point: verified by crashing a dev session in that order, where the log line survives the segfault.

## Testing

- New testthat cases in `test-packages.R` for the message formatter (package attribution from namespace DLLs, bundled-copy detection, reinstall advice limited to packages linking the non-bundled copy, a one-line reinstall call for long package lists, advice for R builds without binaries, `@rpath` fallback), `.rs.loadedPackageDLLs`, and the disable option; `rstudio-tests --scope r --filter '^(packages|linter)$'` passes (176 tests).
- Manually verified in a dev `rsession` with stub packages linked against Homebrew's libomp: the message appears inside `suppressMessages()`, is not repeated for the same runtimes and packages, is shown again when a second stub package linking the Homebrew copy loads, and a single loaded runtime produces no output. With both copies loaded before any hooks were registered, the message appears once when the package scan completes and is not repeated by later scans.

Addresses #18937.

title: don't let a duplicate session launch take over a live session's socket
description:
### Intent

On RStudio Server, a duplicate launch of a user's session locked the user out: the duplicate unlinked the live session's stream socket before binding its own, aborted on the source-database lock the live session holds (since #18853), and removed the socket it had bound on the way out. The live session was left listening on an unlinked inode, so every recovery launch repeated the abort until the original rsession was killed by hand.

Fixes #18941.

Note: the issue names `LocalStreamAsyncServer`; the session's listener is actually `LocalStreamHttpConnectionListener` (`HttpConnectionListenerImpl::start()` ran `cleanup()` before binding, and `stop()` / `/rpc/abort` ran it again on exit). Same mechanism, different class.

### Approach

Session side:

- **Claim the socket first thing.** `rsessionMain` now calls `claimSessionStream()` right after logging is up, before it touches anything a second process for the same session would share (active-session metadata, project settings, source database). The listener is split into `bindEndpoint()` (bind and listen now, so connections wait in the backlog) and `start()` (accept). A duplicate of a running session stops here with a single warning naming the owning process, and exits before writing anything:

  ```
  WARNING Not starting: this session is already running in process 55600 [stream=.../rstudio-rsession/kevin-d]
  ```

- **Bind first, probe on `EADDRINUSE`** (`claimLocalStream` in `LocalStreamSocketUtils.hpp`). The path is no longer unlinked up front. If the bind fails with address in use, a non-blocking `connect()` decides whether a process is listening there: if so, fail with `address_in_use` and leave the path alone; if not (a socket left by a crashed or killed session), remove it and bind again. Of two processes racing for a missing path, the kernel picks one and the other fails.
- **Only remove what we bound.** The listener records the socket's device and inode at bind time, and `cleanup()` removes the socket and pid file only if the path still leads to that socket, so a supplanted session cannot take its successor's socket with it. The pid file is written after the bind succeeds. `stop()` runs cleanup before closing the acceptor, so an exiting session unlinks its path while still listening and a successor never sees a refused-but-about-to-release socket.
- **Keep the socket from children.** The claimed socket is opened close-on-exec, so a process R starts with `system()` can't inherit it and, once the session has been killed, keep the path answering the probe as though the session were still running.
- **Release the claim if startup fails.** `rsessionMain` removes the socket and pid file (with the same identity check) on any early return after the claim, so a session that fails to start doesn't leave behind a pid file naming a dead process.
- `waitWithTimeout` chains the last error that kept it waiting into its timeout error.

Server side (`ServerSessionManager.cpp`): the launch that produced the duplicate got through the #18572 dedupe because that guard needs a recorded pid, and the pid is only recorded after the launch function returns. A request for the context ending in that window -- an RPC to the exiting predecessor dying with EOF, or a last-gasp response from it -- erased the fresh pending launch, and the next recovery pass launched again. The entry now carries a `launching` flag that keeps it through both request errors and successes until the launch function has returned; `endLaunching` matches on launch time so it cannot clear a newer entry. Custom launchers keep their clear-on-error behavior after that point.

Test runner (`rstudio-tests.in`): a session no longer takes over a socket another process is listening on, so concurrent test runs (several worktrees, or the `rsession` and `r` scopes side by side) each get their own `RS_SESSION_TMP_DIR`, cleaned up on exit.

The `address_in_use` check in `startHttpConnectionListenerWithTimeout` compares against a generic-category code, so it never matches asio's system-category bind error and that retry loop has never run (`Error::operator==` matches on category name; see #18946). Server sessions no longer reach the loop for the in-use case, and making it match would also switch on retries for TCP sessions that leak a listener per attempt, so it's left for #18946.

Not covered here: two launches claiming the same stale socket at the same instant can still both proceed (the gap between the probe and the rebind is microseconds; closing it needs a lock around the claim: #18962). rserver still can't attribute a request outcome to the process that produced it, which the `launching` flag and the #18572 guard each cover only in part: #18963. A live session whose socket path vanished for some other reason (nothing answers, so the probe treats it as stale) still needs the "self-detect being supplanted" follow-up noted in #18572.

### Automated Tests

- `src/cpp/core/http/LocalStreamSocketUtilsTests.cpp` (new): the probe on a missing path, a regular file, a listening socket, and a socket left by a closed listener; identity survives a close and differs after a rebind; `claimLocalStream` binds a missing path, refuses a live listener with `address_in_use` and leaves it intact, replaces a stale socket, and opens the socket close-on-exec. The two identity tests hard-link the old socket so its inode stays allocated: Linux hands a freed inode number straight to the next socket (20 of 20 rebinds in a jammy container got the old inode; 0 of 20 with the link), which is what failed Jenkins `c++-unit-tests`.
- `src/cpp/session/http/SessionLocalStreamHttpConnectionListenerTests.cpp` (new): starts real listeners on temp paths; `bindEndpoint()` claims the stream before `start()` and refuses a duplicate; a stale socket is replaced; a live one refuses a second listener and is left intact; a supplanted listener leaves its successor's socket and pid file in place on stop; stop tolerates a path that is already gone; `releaseEndpoint()` removes a stream that was claimed but never started.
- `src/cpp/server/ServerSessionManagerTests.cpp`: request outcomes (error and success) raised from inside the launch function no longer clear the pending launch, and a failed launch still clears it.

Ran locally on macOS: `rstudio-core-tests` (774 passed), `rstudio-tests --scope rsession` (666 passed), `rserver-tests --gtest_filter='SessionManagerTest.*'` (9 passed; server code unchanged since).

### Manual verification

With `npm run rserver-dev` for this branch: launched a session through rserver, then started a second `rsession` with the live session's exact arguments and environment. The duplicate exited with status 1 at once with the warning above; the original process kept its socket and pid file, and proxied requests kept reaching it with no relaunch.

### QA Notes

- Restart R and browser refreshes on RStudio Server, including rapid ones, should never produce the "recovery data is locked" R Session Aborted page.
- A session killed with `SIGKILL` (stale socket left behind) should still be replaced by the next launch as before.
- Desktop is unaffected in practice (each relaunch gets a fresh socket path or follows the previous process's exit), but restart and "Start New Session" flows are worth a pass.
- Windows sessions listen on TCP and are unaffected; `claimSessionStream()` is a no-op there.

### Documentation

No NEWS entry: the lockout needs the source-database lock from #18853, which hasn't shipped in a release.

### Checklist

- [ ] Includes a linked `NEWS.md` entry (not needed; see Documentation).
- [x] Local regression tests pass.
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned.

title: pass PACKAGE = "(embedding)" to all .Call() invocations
description:
### Intent

Ensure every `.Call()` in our R sources passes `PACKAGE = "(embedding)"`, so the symbol lookup goes straight to the routines registered by the embedding `rsession` binary rather than searching every loaded DLL.

### Approach

A parse-based scan (via `getParseData()`) over every `.R` file under `src/cpp` found 75 `.Call()` sites in 20 files without a `PACKAGE` argument, including multi-line calls that a line-oriented grep would miss. Each now passes `PACKAGE = "(embedding)"`, on the same line for single-line calls and on its own line for one-argument-per-line calls.

The three calls that resolved their routine via `getNativeSymbolInfo(..., PACKAGE = "")` (`ModuleTools.R`, `SessionPresentation.R`) now name it directly with `PACKAGE = "(embedding)"`, since an empty `PACKAGE` also searches every loaded DLL.

The dynamic `.Call(routine, ...)` in `.rs.doListIndex` is included, since every caller passes an `rs_*` routine name.

### Automated Tests

`test-linter.R` now fails on any `.Call()` in `src/cpp` R sources without `PACKAGE = "(embedding)"`, listing each offending `file:line`. Calls that target another DLL are exempt: a literal routine name without our `rs_` prefix, or a namespaced native symbol such as `grDevices:::C_foo`. Files that fail to parse are skipped rather than aborting the test. Existing R tests exercise many of the touched functions.

### QA Notes

- Re-running the scan after the change reports zero remaining sites.
- All touched files still parse, and the diff is ASCII-only.

### Documentation

None; internal change.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` (N/A, internal change)
- [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility) (N/A)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [ ] This PR passes all local unit tests (`test-linter.R` passes locally in rsession; relying on CI for the rest)

title: grow the options dialog so the code editing tab fits
description:
## Intent

With a project open, the Code > Editing tab of Global Options overflows its container: the "Some settings may be overridden by project options" row pushes the "Enable code snippets" row behind a scrollbar (17px over on Desktop). Follow-up to #18762, whose ggplot2 `+` checkbox tipped the tab over; that change is unreleased, so there's no NEWS entry.

## Approach

Grow the dialog 30px taller (600 -> 630). The width stays at 640.

The sizes that depend on the dialog are now computed from `PreferencesDialogConstants`, so changing its dimensions doesn't need follow-up edits elsewhere:

- `PANE_CONTENT_WIDTH` (and `PROJECT_PANE_CONTENT_WIDTH`) replaces the width arithmetic repeated across panes. The no-chooser width used by Help > Accessibility > Accessibility Options derives from it instead of a hardcoded 516.
- Pane Layout sizes its tab lists from the dialog height, capped by the window height the same way the dialog is, rather than `PANEL_CONTAINER_HEIGHT - 375`. Its grid used to grow twice as fast as the dialog; now it grows at the same rate and fits windows down to about 600px tall (previously about 730px). The grid also loses the 2px it overflowed the pane by.
- The Appearance preview width is measured from the pane width.

Moving rows off the Editing tab was considered, but Code > Display, where they'd fit, has only about 26px to spare.

## QA Notes

With a project open, in a window at least ~760px tall, Tools > Global Options > Code > Editing should show the Snippets row without a scrollbar. In shorter windows the dialog shrinks and the pane scrolls, as before.

Also check Pane Layout (no scrollbar, including in shorter windows) and Help > Accessibility > Accessibility Options (no horizontal scrollbar).

`e2e/rstudio/tests/preferences/global_prefs_layout.test.ts` now checks that every section and tab fits the full-size dialog, with and without a project open; that the standalone Accessibility Options dialog fits; and that Pane Layout fits a dialog capped by a short window. These pass on Desktop and Server, and fail against the previous revision of this PR and at the old 600px height.

title: e2e: wait for the fixed plot size dialog focus before filling it
description:
`fixed_plot_size.test.ts` "changing units in the dialog keeps the size" failed on both attempts on macOS in #18944's run: after `fill('4')` on width and `fill('2')` on height, switching to centimeters showed a width of 106.68 (42 in) and a height of 12.7 (the previous 5 in).

`ModalDialogBase.showModal` focuses the dialog's first control 100ms after the dialog is shown (`Timers.singleShot` -> `onDialogShown` -> `focusInitialControl`). `openFixedSizeDialog` returned as soon as the dialog was visible, so the height `fill()` could race that timer: focus jumped back to the width box between the fill's focus and its text insertion, and the "2" was appended to the "4".

Wait for the width field to be focused before returning from `openFixedSizeDialog`.

Verified locally on desktop-dev: all 11 `fixed_plot_size` tests pass.

title: e2e: keep the plots pane save tests in their own sandbox
description:
Two `plots_pane.test.ts` failures from the open PRs' CI runs:

- "save plot as image dialog opens and accepts the save" has failed on its first attempt in most runs since `fixed_plot_size.test.ts` landed (#18895), passing only on the retry's fresh worker. `ExportPlotUtils` remembers the directory of the session's last export (a client-side static), so after `fixed_plot_size` runs in the same worker the chooser opens in that spec's sandbox -- the trace's breadcrumb shows exactly that -- and `Rplot.png` lands there while the test polls `list.files(getwd())`.
- "file chooser accepted before a new folder is listed saves into it" failed on Windows shard 5 in #18947's run. `createPlot` waited on the plot iframe, which is visible even while empty, so the Export click landed about 350ms after `plot(1, 1)` was submitted, before the plot arrived: the export items were still disabled and the dialog never opened.

The first save now names the file by its full sandbox path, which also makes the working directory the remembered one for the rest of the suite (whose tests accept the default path and check `getwd()`), and `createPlot` waits for the toolbar to enable, which happens on the same plots-changed event that shows the image.

Verified locally on desktop-dev with `fixed_plot_size` running before `plots_pane` in the same worker (the leaking arrangement): all 14 `plots_pane` tests pass on the first attempt.

title: e2e: focus the console by command instead of clicking its tab
description:
`linux-server / e2e-server-ubuntu (2)` has failed on every run since #18950 merged (including #18950's own run, and the open PRs that have merged `main` since): two or three tests in `show_document_directory.test.ts` time out clicking the selected source tab with "element is not visible". The trace shows the Source pane minimized and the Console maximized at that point, and the screencast frames pin the collapse to the second of two console-tab clicks about 390ms apart.

`ModuleTabLayoutPanel` treats two clicks on a pane tab within 500ms and 3px as a double-click and maximizes the pane (`DoubleClickState`); maximizing the Console minimizes the Source pane with it. The page-level `executeInConsole` in `pages/console_pane.page.ts` clicked `#rstudio_workbench_tab_console` before every command, and `seedSandboxFile` runs two R-side commands back to back (`dir.create` + `writeLines`) only on Server-on-Linux, where the runner cannot write the rsession-owned sandbox. Desktop writes the file from Node, so it never saw this, and a retry (fresh worker, same timing) failed the same way.

This routes the page-level `executeInConsole`, `typeInConsole` and `clearConsole` through `focusConsole` (the `activateConsole` command), which is what `ConsolePaneActions.executeInConsole` already does for the same reason.

Verified locally on desktop-dev (macOS): `console_pane`, `show_document_directory`, `fixed_plot_size` and `plots_pane` all green. The server-only double-click path itself needs the CI server shard to confirm.

title: close the typed-nav marker document before deleting it
description:
Since #18950 landed, `show_document_directory.test.ts:114` fails on linux-server e2e shard 2 for every PR (e.g. #18936, #18947, #18957, and #18950's own branch). The cause is a leak from the spec that sorts just before it.

`open_file_dialog_typed_navigation.test.ts` opens `~/pw-typed-nav-*/marker-*.txt` in its second test, and its `afterAll` then deleted that directory while the document was still open. That raises a modal "File Deleted" prompt. The per-test reset would dismiss it, but the next spec's `beforeAll` runs first: `show_document_directory` uses `useSuiteSandbox()`, whose sandbox setup clicks the Console tab and times out behind the prompt's glass.

The retry fails too, for a related reason: the failed worker's teardown closes every document (leaving the Source pane in its zero-tab hidden layout) and then can't `quit()` behind the same prompt, so the retry attaches to the same session with that layout persisted. Its Source pane collapses on the next Console click and the doc-tab click times out.

The fix closes the marker document (`resetSourcePaneState`) before deleting its directory.

### Verification

Ran both specs in one server worker (`npm run test:server` with this branch's GWT and a current C++ build, `--retries=0`):

- Without the fix: the per-test reset logs `dismissing leaked modal dialog -- [File Deleted] ... marker-*.txt`. Locally the prompt landed just after the next `beforeAll` click, so the reset caught it; on CI it lands before that click.
- With the fix: no leaked dialog; 15 passed.

title: Move contextMenuLayout's comment back above it
description: In `show_document_directory.test.ts`, the comment describing `contextMenuLayout()` ended up above `resetToUntitled()` when that helper was added in #18950. This moves it back. Comment-only change.

title: Add Show Document's Directory to navigate the Files pane
description:
Adds a way to show the folder containing a document in the Files pane:

- **Document tab context menu:** a "Show Document's Directory" item after Set Working Directory. Rename is now separated from the path items by a divider.
- **Command Palette:** "Show Current Document's Directory in Files Pane" (`showActiveDocDirInFiles`), enabled for documents that have a path. It is not added to a menu or the editor toolbar.

Both bring the Files pane to the front and work from extra source columns and popped-out source windows. For the latter, `DirectoryNavigateEvent` is now a cross-window event: a satellite forwards it to the main window, which is raised only when the pane should be shown. Server-raised instances are dispatched locally in each window and are not forwarded. As a result, the tab menu's Set Working Directory now also moves the Files pane when used from a popped-out window (previously only `setwd()` ran there, unless the Files pane was syncing with the working directory).

Related changes:

- A document directly under `/` now gets `/` as its directory, via the new `FileSystemItem.getContainingDir()`. Previously the tab menu's Set Working Directory ran `setwd("")`, and Session > Set Working Directory > To Source File Location threw on the null parent.
- Source commands are refreshed whenever a save changes a document's path (a new `FilePathChangedEvent`). After a first save, Rename and the new command are available without switching tabs; after a Save As into or out of a project, the VCS commands are current.
- `FileTypeChangedEvent` is handled once by `SourceColumnManager`, which manages the active column last. Each column used to handle it separately, and an inactive column could hide Publish after a file type change.
- Commands are refreshed when a document's extended type changes, so saving a new R script as `.Rmd` offers Publish straight away.

Inactive source columns can still hide the active document's commands through other refreshes (e.g. Save All); that is filed as #18955.

Tests: `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/files/show_document_directory.test.ts` covers the menu item and palette entry from the main column, an extra column, and a popped-out window; Set Working Directory from a popped-out window; enablement for untitled and newly saved documents; the VCS commands after a Save As into a version-controlled project; and Publish visibility after first saves and file type changes. `FileSystemItemTests` covers `getContainingDir()`.

Fixes #6781.
Fixes #18949.
Fixes #18956.

title: Update Posit Assistant user guide and remove install-view links
description:

title: tidy up NEWS.md for 2026.10
description:
Tidies up the 2026.10 release notes in `NEWS.md`. No functional changes.

title: Update provider wording in Posit Assistant not-installed view
description:
