title: write state files atomically
defer file chooser accept until its directory listing arrives
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18922.

With RStudio's own file chooser (RStudio Server, or Desktop with native file dialogs disabled), clicking Save/Open before the directory listing arrived closed the chooser without saving or opening anything, and without an error.

### Approach

`FileDialog.getSelectedItem()` resolves the typed name with `PosixFileSystemContext.itemForName()`, which returns null while the `list_files` response is pending. `FileSystemDialog.accept()` then ran the operation with a null item, which callers such as `SavePlotAsImageDialog` treat as a cancel.

- `FileBrowserWidget` now tracks whether a listing is in flight (`isNavigating()`: from construction and each `cd()` until the matching `onNavigated()`).
- `FileSystemDialog.maybeAccept()` defers the accept while navigating and runs it from `onNavigated()`. This generalizes the deferred accept `FileDialog` already had for typed paths with a directory component (`attemptAcceptOnNextNavigate_`), so that flag is replaced by the shared one.
- `ChooseFolderDialog2` is covered too: accepting it before the first listing produced a directory item with an empty path. Subclasses that adjust the filename on navigation now do so before `super.onNavigated()`, since that may run the deferred accept.
- A failed navigation (both the requested and fallback directories unlistable) drops any deferred accept and ends the browser's loading state, so the dialog stays usable rather than waiting on a listing that will never come.
- Closing the dialog (Cancel, Escape) does not detach it from the file system context, so a listing that arrives afterwards still reaches `onNavigated()`. `onUnload()` drops any deferred accept so it cannot run the operation from a closed dialog. (This gap already existed for the typed-subpath deferral, but the initial-listing deferral widens the window to every dialog open.)

Pro's `OpenSharedProjectDialog` hosts a `FileBrowserWidget` with its own `maybeAccept()` and is unaffected.

### QA Notes

- `ant javac` passes.
- New e2e test in `plots_pane.test.ts` holds the chooser's `list_files` RPC with `page.route`, clicks Save while it is held, checks the chooser stays open with no `save_plot_as` request, then releases the listing and checks the save runs on its own (one `save_plot_as` request, one new PNG). The full spec passes on desktop-dev (14/14). Run against a GWT build without the fix, the new test fails at the "chooser stays open" assertion.
- A second e2e test clicks Save while the listing is held, cancels the chooser, releases the listing, and checks that no `save_plot_as` request is issued and no PNG appears. Run against a build without the `onUnload()` guard, it fails because the deferred accept saves the plot and closes the format dialog. Full spec: 15/15 on desktop-dev.
- Manual: RStudio Server, Plots > Export > Save as Image, click Save on the chooser as soon as it appears; the plot is saved once the listing arrives. Same for Open File and Choose Directory.

title: Offer to reinstall Posit Assistant when it is up to date
description:
Fixes #18658.

Step 5, the last in the plan in #18658. When Check for Posit Assistant Updates finds the user's own installation is already the latest version, the result dialog offers Reinstall, which downloads a fresh copy into a new slot. It is the in-product recovery for an install that passes verification but misbehaves.

## What changes

- The update check sets `reinstallAvailable` when the installed version equals the manifest's version for this protocol, the install is not blocked as unsupported, the session runs one of the user's own slots (`runsUserSlot()`, new in `ChatInstallation`), and a fresh user slot would still be selected (`userInstallWouldBeSelected()`, the update offer's gate). The manifest's download URL and SHA-256 are kept for that version.
- Copies from `posit-assistant-path`, the administrator's directory, or the RStudio bundle are never offered Reinstall: a user slot beside them would shadow that copy rather than repair it.
- `reinstallAvailable` is carried through a throttled skip in `throttle::PendingUpdate`, under the same installed-version-unchanged rule as a pending update, so a skip while the dialog is open doesn't make the click fail.
- `chat_install_update` takes an optional `reinstall` flag. With it, `performInstall()` checks `reinstallAvailable` instead of `updateAvailable`, skips the select-an-existing-slot shortcut, and publishes with `SlotPolicy::AlwaysFresh`, so a collision bumps the suffix (`1.5.0-2`) rather than adopting the existing slot. The old slot is left in place. Managed mode refuses it, as it refuses install and update.
- The dialog shows **Reinstall** and **OK**, with OK as the default. When Posit Assistant isn't selected as chat provider or assistant, the plain up-to-date message is shown instead, since the backend would refuse the install. en and fr strings.
- NEWS entry.

## Testing

    GTEST_FILTER='Chat*:SessionAssistant*:PositAssistant*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession

283 tests pass, including new ones for `runsUserSlot()` and for carrying the reinstall offer through a throttled skip. `ant unittest` passes (606), including new `dispatchUpdateCheck` cases. `check-for-updates-command.test.ts` passes in desktop-dev with a new test for the Reinstall dialog.

A real reinstall was run once in desktop-dev from a throwaway spec against the live manifest: before, `pai/versions` held `1.5.0` with `{"selected":{"11.0":"1.5.0"}}`; after, it held `1.5.0` and `1.5.0-2` with `{"selected":{"11.0":"1.5.0-2"}}`, and no staging directory was left behind.

title: Honor the editor mode choice in the New Quarto Document dialog
description:
Fixes #11506.

When visual editing was the default for new documents (or the Quarto project set `editor: visual`), unchecking "Use visual markdown editor" in the New Quarto Document dialog had no effect. The dialog only ever wrote `editor: visual`, so a source choice left the YAML without an `editor` field, and the new document fell back to the visual default in `SourceColumn.applyDocPropertyDefaults`.

- `QuartoCommands` now writes `editor: source` when the user chooses source and the new document would otherwise default to visual. When the default is already source, the generated YAML is unchanged.
- The Shiny and Observable JS templates now show the checkbox and follow it like the other templates. Previously the dialog hid it and always treated these documents as source. Both open and round-trip in visual mode.

The checkbox starts from the project's editor mode, else the user's last choice in the dialog (visual on first use). So Shiny and Observable JS documents now open in visual mode unless the user unchecks the box, matching the Document and Presentation templates.

## Tests

`e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/quarto_new_doc_editor_mode.test.ts` turns on the visual-by-default preference and creates Document, Shiny, and Observable JS documents with the box checked and unchecked. The unchecked cases assert `editor: source` in the YAML and that the visual toggle stays off for 5 seconds. Without the fix, the Document source-mode test fails on both assertions (each checked separately). All six pass in `test:desktop-dev`.

title: Remove the Posit Assistant cross-session install lock
description:
Addresses #18658.

Step 4 of the plan in #18658. Since #18892, an install publishes a new version slot and never modifies a directory another session could be running from, so the lock added in #18276 no longer protects anything.

## What changes

- `ChatInstallLock.{hpp,cpp}` and `ChatInstallLockTests.cpp` are deleted (1,713 lines), along with the `installLock()` accessor, its owner-id helper, and `kPositAiLocksDirName`.
- `performInstall()` no longer takes a `MutationScope`, so an install or update is no longer refused while another session is running Posit Assistant.
- The chat backend start and the NES agent start no longer acquire or release an in-use lock, and their exit handlers drop the lock token.
- The e2e seed no longer skips a `locks/` directory, and the harness test's lock assertions are gone.
- The existing #18658 NEWS entry gains a clause: an update no longer requires closing other sessions that are running Posit Assistant.

Two #18276 fixes that are not about locking stay in `SessionAssistant.cpp`: `onError` does not clear agent tracking state on a stream error, and the helper launch environment is set with `setenv` rather than appended. #18276 made no changes under `core/`, so nothing else becomes unused.

Without the lock, concurrent `selectSlot()` writes from sessions on different protocols can drop one another's `selected.json` entry. #18658 accepts this ("Lost-selection downgrade is accepted, not made durable"), and `ChatSelector.hpp` documents it.

## Testing

    GTEST_FILTER='Chat*:SessionAssistant*:PositAssistant*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession

277 tests pass. `npx playwright test tests/harness/pai-seed.test.ts` passes.

title: fix handling of several console escape sequences
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18916.

Follows #18915, which reworked the same OSC parsing.

An audit of `VirtualConsole` after #18914 turned up several more places where console output diverges from how terminals handle escape sequences. The worst: any CSI sequence the old regex didn't recognize, such as `ESC[4:3m` (curly underline), was taken for an incomplete sequence, and everything printed after it was held back and lost. In the console that lasts until the next prompt; in the Build pane or chunk output, it lasts for the rest of the run.

### Approach

- **CSI sequences** are matched by their ECMA-48 structure (parameter bytes, intermediate bytes, final byte), replacing the narrow `CSI_REGEX` / `CSI_PREFIX_REGEX` pair and the fallback to chalk's `ANSI_REGEX`. Only sequences with numeric parameters are acted on (SGR, cursor movement, erase in line); anything else is discarded whole. An SGR sequence that mixes in a sub-parameter (`ESC[1;31;4:3m`) still applies the parameters we support. Output is held back only when it ends partway through a sequence whose parameters so far are numeric, so a dangling `ESC [` can no longer swallow what follows, including the `> ` and `+ ` prompts, which consist of CSI parameter and intermediate bytes. A missing or zero cursor-movement count means 1, as in xterm. The 8-bit CSI (U+009B) is treated like `ESC [`. `ANSI_REGEX` itself stays, since the terminal's local echo uses it.
- **Empty SGR parameters mean 0 (reset)**, so `ESC[m` (git, `grep --color`, `tput sgr0`) and `ESC[;1m` reset as they should. The branch that was meant to handle `ESC[m` checked for a 2-character code, but `ESC[m` is 3 characters.
- **An unknown extended color format** (`ESC[38;3m`) made `processCode()` return null, and `setCurrentClazz()` then threw a `TypeError`. It now resets fully (colors, inverse mode) and returns the reset styles instead.
- **Every OSC string is consumed** up to its terminator, not just hyperlinks (OSC 8). Other commands (window titles, working directory, ...) are discarded rather than printed. An OSC that ends a chunk of output is held back, up to 1 MB, so later chunks can complete it. A console control character inside it, or output of another class (stderr after stdout), means it's malformed: its introducer is dropped and the rest is shown as before, with the class it arrived with, so a stray `ESC ]` costs at most the rest of its line. The console also flushes held-back input before each prompt, where it starts a fresh `VirtualConsole` and would otherwise drop it (as it already did for a split SGR sequence). This replaces `HyperlinkMatch`.
- **Other escape sequences** (`ESC ( B`, ...) are consumed through their final byte. A malformed one stops before the unexpected character instead of always swallowing the next character, so `ESC` followed by a newline keeps the newline. `ESC [ [` is a CSI sequence ending in `[`, as in xterm (the Linux console's `ESC [ [ <char>` is keyboard input, not program output). Two tests from #2248 that spelled erase-in-line as `ESC [ [ K` are corrected to `ESC [ K`.
- **Overwriting text** (`\r`, cursor movement) now compares hyperlinks as well as classes when deciding whether to merge with the text underneath. Before, plain text written over a link became part of it, a link written over plain text wasn't a link, and a second link kept the first one's URL.
- **BEL** is discarded rather than written into the output, in every ANSI mode.
- **`AnsiCode.strip()`** follows the same ECMA-48 structure, so what it removes matches what the console discards.
- `__OSC__` in `AnsiEscapes.hpp` was defined as `\x1b\x5c` (ST); it's now `\x1b\x5d`. Nothing uses it yet.

### Automated Tests

34 new GWT unit tests (`ant unittest`), 30 in `VirtualConsoleTests` and 4 in `AnsiCodeTests`, covering each item above. The full suite passes (638 tests).

### QA Notes

In the console:

```r
# 1. colors reset (plain should not be red)
cat("\033[31mred\033[m plain\n")

# 2. nothing lost after an unsupported sequence (should print "ab" then "next")
cat("a\033[4:3mb\n"); cat("next\n")

# 3. no crash on an unknown color format (should print "text")
cat("\033[38;3mtext\n")

# 4. other OSC sequences are hidden (should print "text")
cat("\033]0;title\007text\n")

# 5. a link rewritten with \r (only "ab" should be a link)
cat("abcdef\r\033]8;;https://example.com\007ab\033]8;;\007\n")
```

Also worth a quick look: `system("git -c color.ui=always log -3")` should not leave colors bleeding into later output, and cli progress bars and colored testthat output should look unchanged.

title: keep sessions starting when user data files are unusable
description:
### Intent

Fixes #8729.

A problem with a single file in the user data directory (`~/.local/share/rstudio`) could stop the R session from starting. The error comes up every launch until the user finds and fixes the file by hand. A common cause is running RStudio with `sudo` once, which leaves files and directories owned by root. #8729 is the directory-level version: `~/.local/share` owned by root, so `rstudio` can't be created there.

These failures all stopped startup, and are now logged instead:

- **`persistent-state` / `session-persistent-state` unreadable.** `Settings::initialize` only forgives ENOENT. Since #17134 made `FilePath::openForRead` report the real errno, a permission error became fatal (previously it read as "not found").
- **User state file (`rstudio-desktop.json` / `rstudio-server.json`) not writable, with a non-default editor theme.** `syncThemePrefs` rewrote the state file during `themes::initialize` and returned the write error, which aborts `rInit`.
- **Project MRU list unreadable, or its migration/normalization rewrite fails.** `lists::initialize` returned these errors.
- **An unwritable leftover source database directory (`sources/session-*`).** The orphan scan adopted it (renaming it after the current session), then failed to lock it. Since the rename gives it the next session's name, every later start adopted it and failed again. Unwritable directories are now skipped before adopting; ownership and contention checks are unchanged.
- **A saved working directory that exists but can't be entered.** It was checked with `exists()` only, then `chdir` failed. It now falls back to the default working directory, then home, and says so in the console (a project can otherwise appear to have opened somewhere else). On Windows, the long-working-directory warning now checks the directory actually entered.
- **Server mode: the per-session `graphics-r3` directory can't be created.** It now falls back to a temporary graphics directory, as desktop mode already does.

When the data directory itself can't be written (the #8729 case, or a read-only or full home), the session now keeps its state in a private temporary directory instead of failing (macOS and Linux). This applies to Desktop and to sessions rserver starts without a scope; Workbench multi-session and Launcher sessions are left as before (see Approach). It also prints this in the console:

```
WARNING: RStudio can't write to its data directory, so this session is keeping its state in a temporary directory instead.

    Data directory:      /home/user/.local/share/rstudio (Permission denied)
    Temporary directory: /tmp/rstudio-data-user

State kept in the temporary directory, including unsaved documents, may be deleted by the system, and it will not be moved back once the data directory is fixed. To fix it, make sure the data directory is owned by you and writable; this can happen if RStudio was previously run as another user, e.g. with sudo.
```

Two more fixes for saved session state:

- **A suspended session whose restore crashes R is no longer restored again on every start.** Nothing deleted the saved state until the user quit cleanly, so if restoring it crashed R (e.g. loading a package segfaults) or ran out of memory (a huge environment), every later start crashed the same way. Saved restart state (`ctx/ctx-<port>`) had the same problem when the port was reused.
- **Singleton mode (RStudio Server) cleans up invalid sessions.** A session left with an empty `project` property, e.g. by a crash while its properties were being written, can't be resumed. It was still validated on every start, with 150 ms of retries and a syslog error each time, and never removed.

Smaller fixes found in the same audit:

- **Restart-file age check.** The orphan scan compared a restart file's age in seconds against `1000 * 60 * 5`, so a leftover restart file protected its directory for about 83 hours rather than the 5 minutes the comment claimed. The window is now an explicit one day. A restart can wait a long time for the Launcher to schedule the new session, and another session adopting its directory in the meantime would take its documents. A restart that really failed only has its documents recovered later, not lost.
- **Context ID ordering.** `context_id` was generated in `prefs::initialize` (inside `rInit`), after `projects::startup` had already used it to name the project scratch path. A session opening a project with new or reset user state used `.Rproj.user/` itself as its scratch path. The ID is now assigned in `prefs::initializeState()`, before projects start. If the state file can't be written (e.g. it's owned by root), the ID is kept in memory for the session, in the computed state layer, rather than left empty. The one-time migration from RStudio 1.2 settings keeps that ID unless the old settings have their own.
- **Corrupt `trust.json`.** Startup already failed closed, but granting, revoking or resetting trust returned the parse error, so trust couldn't be granted until the file was fixed by hand. Updates now replace contents that can't be parsed, after moving them to `trust.json.invalid` (then `trust.json.invalid-2`, and so on) so they can be recovered by hand. Moving rather than copying means a rewrite that then fails leaves nothing to back up again, so copies can't pile up. If the file can't be moved, the update fails as before.
- **`console07/INDEX001`.** The persisted console process index wasn't type-checked before `getArray()` / `getObject()`.

### Approach

Where a module `initialize()` returned an error for non-essential state, it now logs and continues. Every error returned during `rInit` ends the session (`R_Suicide`), and nothing cleans up the state behind it, so the next start fails the same way.

**Temporary directory.** `core::system::xdg::redirectUnwritableUserDataDir()` runs at the top of `rsessionMain`, before logging, since the log lives there too. It probes the data directory by creating and removing a file, so a read-only filesystem or an exhausted quota is caught as well as permissions. If the probe fails, it points `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` at `$TMPDIR/rstudio-data-<user>`. Setting the variable means every `userDataDir()` caller and child process agrees on the location.

- The temporary directory is created 0700, and a path owned by someone else or a symlink is refused, since `/tmp` is usually shared.
- If the temporary directory can't be used either, startup continues with the original directory and logs both errors.
- The one-time `~/.rstudio` migration is skipped while the temporary directory is in use, so old state isn't moved somewhere the system may purge.
- The console message is held until deferred init, like the existing long-working-directory warning.
- Not on Windows, matching `verifyUserDirs()`.
- Server-side code that reads a user's data directory (not the session itself) still looks in the usual place.
- Skipped when the session is started with a scope (`-s` / `--scope`), which is how rserver starts Workbench multi-session and Launcher sessions. Other processes, possibly on other hosts, look for those sessions' state (e.g. a suspended session) in the data directory, so a node-local temporary directory would hide it. These sessions behave as before this PR. The check parses argv for just that option with `boost::program_options` (so `-s ID`, `-sID`, `--scope ID`, `--scope=ID` and unambiguous prefixes are all recognized, as in `Options::read`), because the options themselves are parsed after the data directory has to be settled.

**Restore crash loops.** A `restore_started` file marks saved state only while it is loading: `restoreSession()` writes it around the synchronous `state::restore()`, and `ensureDeserialized()` writes it again for the deferred restore, which removes it as soon as the saved state has loaded, whether or not it reported errors, and before the rest of deferred init runs (a crash in an unrelated module's `onDeferredInit` doesn't count against the state). An R error escaping the restore is caught by `ensureDeserialized()`, which then clears the marker too. A resumed session waiting for a client isn't marked, so closing or killing it then doesn't count against the state. Saving the state again also clears the file. At the next start, before R starts, `setAsideUnfinishedRestores()` checks both the restart context and the suspended state. If the file is still there, that state is moved to `<name>-unrestored` (`-unrestored-2` and so on if that's taken, so an earlier copy is never replaced). The console says where the saved session was kept, and whether a new session was started or, if other saved state exists (e.g. suspended state alongside set-aside restart state), that it was restored instead. Set-aside state is removed after 30 days, checked at each start. The message also covers a session closed before it finished loading, which the marker can't tell apart from a crash. Moving the state rather than deleting it keeps the environment recoverable by hand. The check runs before the `.Rprofile` decision, so the fresh session starts like any new one. The saved state is otherwise still kept after a resume, as before, so a later crash still comes back to the last suspended state.

**Invalid singleton sessions.** `activeSession()` in singleton mode now collects the sessions `list()` finds invalid and passes them to the new `ActiveSessions::removeStaleInvalidSessions()`. That removes a session only if nothing in its directory has changed for a day. The age check protects a session whose properties are being written right now, which is what the validation retries exist for. A session is also kept if its properties can't be read (it may be fine, e.g. a file left owned by root), if any timestamp in its directory can't be read, or if it holds a live suspended workspace (`suspended-session-data`); set-aside copies age out with the rest of the session. Valid sessions are never touched, including ones this mode doesn't select. This only applies to file-based session storage (`FileActiveSessionsStorage`): a session whose properties live in a database has a directory that says nothing about its age.

Directory-level failures that remain fatal: the data directory itself (once the fallback also fails) and `sources/`. A resumed session whose own source database directory can't be locked is also still fatal, as are genuine lock contention and ownership refusals, which #18744 made fatal on purpose.

### Automated Tests

- `XdgTests.cpp` (core): `CheckDirectoryWritable`, `TemporaryUserDataDir` (mode, reuse, refusing a symlink or file), and `RedirectUnwritableUserDataDir`, which also checks the redirect ends with the environment that carried it (so it doesn't leak into later tests).
- `SessionSourceDatabaseSupervisorTests.cpp`: `RecoversSessionsWithStaleRestartFiles`, `LeavesSlowRestartsAlone` and `LeavesUnwritableDirectoriesAlone`.
- New `RActiveSessionsTests.cpp` (core): a day-old invalid session is removed, including one holding only a set-aside workspace. A recent one, an old one whose properties were just rewritten, an old valid session, and old invalid sessions holding a live suspended workspace or unreadable properties are kept.
- New `SessionStateTests.cpp` (rsession): marked state is set aside and the returned path names where; unmarked or finished state is left alone; a second set-aside keeps the first; saving clears a stale marker; set-aside state older than 30 days is removed while newer copies and the live state are left alone.
- New `FileUtilsTests.cpp` (core): `firstUnusedPath()`, shared by the set-aside and `trust.json` backup naming.
- New `SessionTrustTests.cpp`: grant, revoke and reset with an unparseable, wrongly shaped or empty `trust.json`, plus a check that existing entries are kept. The replaced contents are kept, a further update makes no more copies, successive recoveries keep separate copies, and the update fails if the file can't be moved aside.

The new supervisor and trust tests fail without the fix. The full `core`, `rsession` and `r` scopes pass locally on macOS.

I also ran `rsession --run-script` in desktop mode against a data directory broken in each of these ways, comparing the build without the fix to the build with it:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| data dir not writable | fails to start | starts (temporary directory) |
| data dir can't be created (#8729) | fails to start | starts (temporary directory) |
| `persistent-state` unreadable | fails to start | starts |
| state file not writable + non-default theme | fails to start | starts |
| `project_name_mru` unreadable | fails to start | starts |
| unwritable orphaned `sources/session-*` | fails to start | starts |
| suspended state with a leftover `restore_started` | restores it again | starts fresh; state moved to `suspended-session-data-unrestored` with a console warning |

Through a dev server with an unwritable data directory, the session starts and the console shows the warning above. On a dev server (singleton mode), I also checked two things:
- A two-day-old invalid session dir was removed at startup.
- A forced suspend (`SIGUSR2`) and resume in a new process restored the environment. The saved state had no marker after the suspend and none after the resume, and nothing was set aside.

Those manual checks predate a review round that narrowed the restore marker, added the scope check and changed the backups, which the tests above cover. With an unwritable data directory, `rsession --run-script` redirects to the temporary directory without a scope, and doesn't with `-s <id>` or `--scope=<id>`.

### QA Notes

On macOS or Linux (Desktop or Server), each of these should start normally, with the details in the session log:

1. **#8729** (Desktop, or open-source Server): with RStudio closed, `mv ~/.local/share/rstudio ~/.local/share/rstudio.bak && sudo chown root ~/.local/share`, then start RStudio. The session should start and show the warning in the console. Restore with `sudo chown $USER ~/.local/share` and move the directory back.
2. `chmod 000 ~/.local/share/rstudio/persistent-state` (create it by running a session first).
3. Set a non-default editor theme, then `sudo chown root ~/.local/share/rstudio/rstudio-desktop.json` (`rstudio-server.json` on Server). The file is normally mode 0600.

4. Suspend a session (RStudio Server), then create an empty `restore_started` file in its `~/.local/share/rstudio/sessions/active/session-*/suspended-session-data/` directory and reload. A new session should start, the console should explain that the previous session wasn't restored, and the data should be in `suspended-session-data-unrestored`.

### Follow-ups

- #18911: use atomic writes by default for state files.

### Documentation

None. The console message explains the fallback and how to fix it.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] ~~If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards~~ (console text only)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: stop creating deployments from e2e shard jobs
description:
## Summary

Every e2e shard job in the eight engine workflows declared `environment: e2e-playwright`. GitHub records a deployment for each job that targets an environment, so a single push to a PR produced one "requested a deployment to e2e-playwright" timeline event per shard (6 Windows shards, 2 macOS, plus the Linux desktop and server jobs), and the PR sidebar picked up a Deployments entry that never means anything.

The environment was introduced in #18504 solely so an environment-scoped `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` would take precedence over the repo-level secret of the same name. It has no protection rules, no branch policy and no variables. Removing the `environment:` lines makes the jobs read the repo-level secret directly; the callers already forward it by name, so nothing else about the jobs changes.

## Follow-up (repo settings, not in this PR)

- The repo-level `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` (set 2026-06-12) predates the environment-scoped copy (2026-08-07). If the values differ, the repo-level secret should be updated to the current 1Password service account token so the Posit Assistant e2e sign-in keeps working.
- Once this merges, the `e2e-playwright` environment can be deleted from repo settings; nothing will reference it.

## Verification

- `grep -rn e2e-playwright .github/` returns nothing after the change.
- The diff is exactly eight one-line deletions.

title: fix console hyperlinks terminated with ESC \
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18914.

Console hyperlinks (OSC 8) terminated with the standard string terminator `ESC \` were printed as raw text (`8;;https://example.comlink8;;`) instead of as links. Only BEL-terminated links worked. cli uses BEL by default, but switches to `ESC \` when `R_CLI_HYPERLINK_MODE=posix` is set, so that setting garbled every cli link in the console.

The cause is a typo from #13883 (2023): the rewritten parser looked for `ESC )` as the terminator rather than `ESC \`. That also meant a stray `ESC )` could end a link, and a link with no BEL or `ESC )` after it made the parser scan ahead into later output, taking the text in between as the URL.

### Approach

- `VirtualConsole.HyperlinkMatch` now ends the link at BEL or `ESC \`. Any other ESC also ends it, as in xterm, but is left in place and parsed as the start of the next escape sequence. The scan for the link's params stops at BEL or ESC too, so a malformed link can't run into later output.
- `AnsiCode.strip()` had the opposite gap: it removed only `ESC \`-terminated OSC sequences, leaving cli's default BEL-terminated links in the notebook chunk message/warning bars. It now handles both.

### Automated Tests

New GWT unit tests (`ant unittest`):

- `VirtualConsoleTests.testHyperlinkStringTerminator`: a link terminated with `ESC \`.
- `VirtualConsoleTests.testHyperlinkStringTerminatorSplitAcrossSubmits`: the `ESC` and `\` of the terminator arrive in separate chunks of output.
- `VirtualConsoleTests.testHyperlinkEndedByOtherEscape`: the reporter's third and fourth examples (an `ESC )` ends the link without being taken as the terminator).
- `AnsiCodeTests.testStripHyperlinks`: `strip()` removes links with either terminator.

All four fail on `main` and pass with this change; the full suite passes (604 tests).

### QA Notes

Run the reporter's examples in the console:

```r
cat("\033]8;;https://example.com\007link\033]8;;\007\n")
cat("\033]8;;https://example.com\033\\link\033]8;;\033\\\n")
cat("\033]8;;https://example.com\033\\link\033]8;;\033)\n")
cat("\033]8;;https://example.com\033)link\033]8;;\033)\n")
```

The first three should each print `link`, linked to example.com. The fourth should print `ink`, linked to example.com (the `ESC ) l` is a character-set designation that consumes the `l`, matching other terminals). The `>` prompt after each should not be linked.

Also worth checking: with `Sys.setenv(R_CLI_HYPERLINK_MODE = "posix")`, `cli::cli_text("See {.url https://example.com}")` should show a working link.

title: Seed PW_SEED_PAI from the selected slot, not bin/
description:
`npm run deploy:rstudio` now publishes `pai/versions/<version>` and `pai/selected.json` instead of `pai/bin` (posit-dev/assistant#2499). Pointing `PW_SEED_PAI` at a freshly deployed `pai` therefore failed setup with `missing bin/package.json`.

The build under test now comes from the slot the seed's `selected.json` names:

- `inspectSeed()` reads `selected.json` and validates the slot it names: a runnable package, a usable slot name, and a `package.json` version and `protocol.json` protocol. Setup fails if `selected.json` is missing or unreadable, doesn't select exactly one protocol (a deploy writes one), or names a slot that isn't there.
- `seedPaiSlot()` copies that slot to the sandbox `versions/<version>`, records its manifest from the copied files, and writes the sandbox `selected.json`. The seed's other slots, a legacy `bin/`, and `locks/` are not copied. Other top-level entries (`ai-logs`, `manifest-check.json`) are copied as before.
- A `bin/`-only tree (`deploy:rstudio:legacy`, or an older assistant checkout) is refused, since this RStudio never reads `bin/`.
- `README.md` and the `sandbox-setup.ts` comment describe the new source. The README also notes that an IDE run against the deployed directory can move its selection, so check the seeded version in the setup log.

The `locks/` exclusion stays until the lock code is deleted (#18658, step 4).

Testing: `tests/harness/pai-seed.test.ts` builds its fake seed in the slot layout and covers each refusal. `npx playwright test tests/harness/pai-seed.test.ts --project=desktop --no-deps` passes (16 tests), and `npm run typecheck` is clean. Seeding from a real post-#2499 `~/.local/share/rstudio/pai` produces the selected slot in the sandbox.

Fixes #18898.

title: use inspect.signature() for python argument completions and help
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18903.

Python argument completions (`name=` after an open paren) and the parameter help shown next to them came back empty. RStudio found the arguments with `inspect.getargspec()`, which Python 3.11 removed. Even before 3.11 it raised for any function with keyword-only arguments or annotations. That covers most modern library code, e.g. `pandas.read_csv()`, `numpy.mean()`, and classes whose constructors take keyword-only arguments.

### Approach

- A new `.rs.python.getSignatureArguments()` uses `inspect.signature()`. It keeps only parameters that can be passed as `name=value` (positional-or-keyword and keyword-only), so positional-only parameters like `len(obj, /)` and `*args`/`**kwargs` aren't offered. `signature()` also covers classes (their constructor, without `self`), bound methods, `functools.wraps` decorators and partials, so the special case for classes is gone.
- The existing docstring-parsing fallback still runs when `signature()` can't introspect something (e.g. `dict`). It also runs when a signature accepts `**kwargs` but names no keyword parameters, as with a `(*args, **kwargs)` wrapper that hides the real arguments. Any other signature is taken as complete, even an empty or positional-only one. So a zero-argument function whose docstring reads "Same as g(a, b)" doesn't borrow `a=` and `b=`, and `f(x, /)` doesn't offer `x=`.
- On Python 3.14, `inspect.signature()` evaluates lazy annotations by default and raises `NameError` for a name bound only under `TYPE_CHECKING`. When `annotationlib` is available, annotations are left as forward references instead; only parameter names and kinds are used.
- Python 2 has no `inspect.signature()`, so there the previous `getargspec()` lookup (including the class `__init__` handling) is kept as-is.
- `.rs.python.getParameterHelp()` now reuses `.rs.python.getFunctionArguments()`, so it looks up descriptions for exactly the names shown in the completion list.
- A function with no arguments got a single `=` completion, because `paste(character(), "=", sep = "")` returns `"="`. `.rs.python.getCompletionsArguments()` now returns no completions when there are no arguments. This bug predates the change.
- The loop that collects a parameter's multi-line description could read past the end of the docstring. The error was swallowed, and the last documented parameter showed a blank description. Python 3.13+ strips docstring indentation, which makes this happen whenever the Parameters section ends the docstring. The loop is now bounds-checked.

### Automated Tests

Six new tests in `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-reticulate.R` (`rstudio-tests --scope r --filter reticulate`):

- argument discovery for a function with annotated, keyword-only and variadic parameters, and for a class
- argument discovery when an annotation names something that isn't bound (Python 3.14+)
- positional-only parameters aren't offered, and signatures with nothing else to offer don't fall back to the docstring (Python 3.8+)
- the docstring fallback for a `(*args, **kwargs)` wrapper, and not for a zero-argument function
- no completions for a function with no arguments
- parameter help for a function whose docstring ends with its last parameter's description

They skip unless `RETICULATE_PYTHON` is set, because starting Python with nothing configured can make reticulate provision an interpreter over the network. Locally, every new test has failing assertions on `main` and passes with this change, on both Python 3.10 and 3.14 (the lazy-annotation test runs on 3.14 only).

### QA Notes

With reticulate using Python 3.11 or newer, and pandas installed:

1. In a Python script or chunk, run `import pandas as pd`.
2. Type `pd.read_csv(` and press Tab.
3. The argument list should appear, and selecting an argument (e.g. `sep=`) should show its description next to the list.

Also worth checking a class (e.g. `pd.DataFrame(`), a function you define yourself with keyword-only arguments, and a function with no arguments (Tab after `f(` should offer no `=` completion).

### Documentation

None.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] ~~If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards~~ (no UI)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: Stop passing ignored arguments to the Posit Assistant backend
description:
`startChatBackend()` no longer passes `--storage`, `--config` or `--workspace-id` to the Posit Assistant backend, and no longer computes a workspace ID with `projectToProjectId()`. The assistant has ignored all three since posit-dev/assistant `5a507b1ba` (2026-01-26): it keeps its storage and settings under `~/.posit/assistant` and derives the workspace ID from `--workspace`. Sending them risked a launch failure if the assistant ever drops the "(Ignored)" option declarations. The `pai/` directory is still created, since RStudio keeps `manifest-check.json` and the install locks there.

Also corrects comments that described `pai/` as the assistant's storage, or described the single `pai/bin` install that was replaced by versioned slots in #18892:

- `positAiStorageDir()` in `ChatInstallation.hpp`, `kPositAiStorageDirName` in `ChatConstants.cpp`, and two `paconfig.json` mentions in `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/pai-seed.ts`
- `stopAgentForUpdate()` is now called after an install, not before one that overwrites the agent's files
- the agent-start lock comment in `SessionAssistant.cpp` is marked vestigial, matching the backend's
- `promptToInstallUpdate` in `ChatPresenter.java` no longer says the install swaps the installation

Comments in the lock machinery (`ChatInstallLock.*`, `installLock()`) are left for the follow-up that deletes it (#18658, step 4).

Verified by starting Posit Assistant 1.5.0 by hand with the remaining launch arguments: it serves HTTP and begins the JSON-RPC handshake. No automated test covers the launch arguments.

Addresses #18889.

title: don't take locks between fork and exec when launching sessions
description:
## Summary

rserver launches each rsession by forking and, in the child, dropping privilege to the session user before `exec`. On Linux, `permanentlyDropPriv()` refreshed the log destinations there, which takes the logger's write lock. Every log write holds the read side of that lock, so if any rserver thread is mid-write when the fork happens, the child inherits a reader that nothing will ever release. The child then waits forever and never becomes the session. Since #18573, rserver keeps waiting on a pending launch whose process is alive, so a restart stalls for a full minute of "Unable to connect to service". This is the server-linux flake in the rmarkdown and interpreter-version restart e2e tests. #18899 has the evidence, including a reproduction with a CI build and a memory read of a hung child.

The same hazard applies to every lock a forked child might touch before it execs: the user cache, and the NSS locks inside `initgroups()`. Rather than steering one call site around the logger, this PR fixes the class of bug at its source:

- **The logger holds its lock across `fork()`** via `pthread_atfork`, the way `EnvironmentLock` and the file-lock registries already do, so a child is never created while another thread is mid log write. The child cannot unlock the recursive mutex the parent's thread held (glibc records the owner's thread id), so it swaps in a fresh mutex that the prepare handler allocated ahead of the fork (the child of a multithreaded process may not allocate). Handlers for other fork-guarded mutexes whose holders log (the file-lock registries) register after the logger's, so the logger's prepare handler runs last and never waits on a thread they are holding up; `log::registerForkHandlers()` documents and enforces the order.
- **The user cache mutex is held across `fork()`** likewise.
- **The user a child switches to is resolved before the fork**, supplementary groups included (`ResolvedUser` / `resolveUser()`), by both `launchChildProcess()` and `ChildProcess::run()`. The child sets the groups with `setgroups()` instead of `initgroups()`, so nothing between fork and exec consults the password or group databases. The resolved user always travels with the launch, so there is no name comparison against `config.user` that NSS canonicalization could defeat. The group lookup that `initgroups()` made in the child now runs on the launching thread (in open source, the connection's io thread) instead; total launch latency is unchanged. It bypasses the group cache on purpose, so each session still starts with the user's current groups.
- **Nothing a child logs between fork and exec goes through the logger.** The best-effort diagnostics in `runProcess()` (limits that could not be set, a keyring that could not be reset) take an error sink, and `launchChildProcess()` hands its child `safeLogToSyslog()`, the way its own after-fork error path and rserver-launcher already report. The child therefore does not depend on the fork handlers for its logging. Callers outside a fork child (rsandbox's `setProcessLimits()`, the launcher's stdin-mode `runProcess()`, the name-based drops) keep logging as before.
- The resolved-user drop is named `permanentlyDropPrivAfterFork()`, so the overload that takes no locks is told apart at a glance from the name-based ones that do.
- The three `permanentlyDropPriv` overloads are hoisted out of the `setresuid`/`setreuid` `#if`, which now covers only the id setters. The non-`setresuid` branch gains the log-destination refresh the other one had.
- `removeLogDestination()` recomputes the logger's maximum level instead of leaving it raised forever.
- A failed `getgrouplist()` no longer publishes its zero-initialized buffer as the user's groups (100 entries of gid 0, which the group cache then served as root-group membership for five minutes). `queryUserGroupIds()` returns the error with an empty list, and a failed refresh stays out of the cache so the next lookup retries. macOS fills a short buffer and fails without reporting the size it needs, so when the count comes back unchanged the buffer doubles (up to 65536) before that counts as a failure. The lookup is injectable so tests can drive both.

The name-based overloads keep their behavior for callers outside a fork (in pro: rserver's `run-unprivileged` drop, the pam-session helper and rsandbox). They remain unsafe after a fork: NSS has locks of its own, and with a group name `permanentlyDropPriv()` also takes the group cache's mutex, which has no fork handler. The header says to use `permanentlyDropPrivAfterFork()` there.

## Testing

- `PosixTests.ForkWaitsForInFlightLogWriteAndChildCanLog` forks on one thread while another is inside a blocking log destination, and checks that the fork waits for the write, that the child can then log and refresh the destinations, and that the parent can too. The scenario runs in a process of its own that the test kills on a hang, since a regression hangs the forking thread or the parent's next logger call and nothing inside that process could abandon them. With the logger's fork handlers disabled the test fails in ten seconds ("the child hung logging after the fork") rather than hanging.
- `PosixTests.ResolveUserReturnsCurrentUserAndGroups` and `PosixTests.PermanentlyDropPrivAfterForkReturnsInChild` cover the new API; `PosixTestsRequiresPrivilege.PermanentlyDropPrivAfterForkSetsIdsAndGroups` (root only) verifies the ids and supplementary groups a child ends up with.
- `PosixTests.SetProcessLimitsReportsFailuresThroughCallback` checks that a limit which cannot be set reaches the caller's sink rather than the logger. It runs where the hard file limit is finite (Linux; macOS reports it unlimited and rejects `RLIM_INFINITY` for `RLIMIT_NOFILE`), skips its EPERM half as root, and restores the limits on every exit path.
- `PosixTests.QueryUserGroupIdsPublishesNothingWhenTheLookupFails` injects a lookup that fails without touching the count or the buffer and checks for an error and no groups; `PosixTests.QueryUserGroupIdsGrowsTheBufferToFit` covers the retry with the size glibc reports, and `PosixTests.QueryUserGroupIdsGrowsTheBufferWhenTheCountIsUnchanged` the macOS behavior.
- macOS: full core suite passes (749 tests, 12 skips), so the non-`setresuid` branch is now exercised, not just compiled.
- Native Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 arm64) build: the full core suite passes as root; the Posix suites pass both as root (42 tests, 1 skip) and as an unprivileged user (39 tests, 4 skips), and the three `DISABLED_PermanentlyDropPriv*` tests pass individually as root.
- The throwaway harness from the first round (`launchChildProcess()` as rserver does, root with a dropped effective user and a run-as user, while six threads log at debug level) launched 300 children with 0 hung, now going through the fork handlers and the resolved-user drop.

Fixes #18899.

title: avoid exit() when leaving the session from a background thread
description:
## Intent

Follow-up to #18881, which leaked the statics that background threads can reach while the process exits. This closes the remaining hole from that audit: places where a background thread *itself* calls `::exit()`.

Addresses #18318.

## Problem

`exit()` runs atexit handlers and static destructors on the calling thread while every other thread keeps running. `session::exitEarly()` ends in `::exit()`, and it is reached from two background threads:

- **macOS parent termination monitor** (`detectParentTermination`): calls `exitEarly()` when `getppid() == 1`. The Windows and Linux variants of the same function called `std::_Exit` directly.
- **HTTP listener accept-error bailout** (`SessionHttpConnectionListenerImpl.hpp`): after too many consecutive accept errors, calls `exitEarly()` from the listener's `io_context` thread, on all platforms. This fires when the process is already out of file descriptors or memory.

In both cases the main thread can still be inside R while the statics it uses are destroyed underneath it.

## Approach

Off the main thread, `exitEarly()` now hands off straight to `session::exitFromBackgroundThread()`, which leaves with `std::_Exit`:

- It skips the monitor, server-RPC and offline worker stops. Those join and detach `boost::thread` handles that the main thread may be stopping (in `rCleanup`) or destroying (in `exit()`) at the same moment, and `_Exit` destroys nothing the workers use.
- It flushes stdio, which `exit()` did and `_Exit` does not. Output written to R's `file()` and `pipe()` connections sits in stdio buffers until then.
- It removes the fallback library path, as the main-thread path does. `s_fallbackLibraryPath` is now leaked, so it is safe to read even if the main thread is already inside `exit()`.
- It releases every link-based lock, as `exitEarly()` always has, and does so last, with nothing between the release and `_Exit`. These locks stay on disk marked as held, and only a reader on the same host that is not load-balanced treats a dead owner's lock as stale at once; any other reader would wait out the lock timeout. The release is best effort: the main thread may still be taking or using locks, so a successor that reads the release could act on a directory this process is still writing to. Keeping the release last confines that window to the release itself, and the main-thread path has always released before `exit()` too.
- A detached watchdog thread, started before any of the above, `_Exit`s after 2 seconds regardless. Unlike `exit()`, `fflush()` waits on each stream's lock, which a thread blocked in a read or write can hold indefinitely, and the lock release writes to a session directory that may sit on a stalled network mount. Flushing before releasing means a hung flush costs a successor some waiting rather than costing the user buffered output. If the watchdog cannot start, the process leaves at once and skips the rest.
- Each step above is wrapped in its own `try/catch(...)`, so one failing does not skip the others and `_Exit` is always reached. Otherwise an exception (e.g. `bad_alloc` in the out-of-memory bailout) would be swallowed by the listener and keep a session running, or `terminate()` the macOS monitor thread.

`rpc/abort` (`checkForAbort`, used by Terminate R) already ended in `std::_Exit` on the listener thread, but never released its locks; in load-balanced deployments a reloaded session could then fail to take its session directory for up to 30 seconds. It now ends in `exitFromBackgroundThread()` too.

The Linux and Windows parent monitors now call `exitEarly(EXIT_FAILURE)` as well, so all three share one exit path. `LinkBasedFileLock`'s test hooks (present whenever unit tests are enabled) are leaked for the same reason as the other statics.

On Windows, `_Exit` still delivers `DLL_PROCESS_DETACH`, so `rsession.dll` destroys its own statics; that is strictly less teardown than the `exit()` the listener path used before. The main-thread path is unchanged.

An audit of the other `exit()` call sites in `src/cpp` found nothing else: the remaining callers run on the main thread, already use `_Exit`, or are forked children using `_exit`.

#18318 rejected `_exit` partly because it skips a load-bearing `atexit` handler in `PosixParentProcessMonitor`. That handler is only registered by `wrapFork()`, which has no callers in this repo, so rsession has no atexit handlers to skip. No log lines are lost either, since the file log destination flushes on every write.

## QA Notes

`SessionMainTests.cpp` forks a child (in load-balanced mode) that registers an `atexit` handler replacing the exit status, takes a link-based lock, leaves a write buffered in a `FILE*`, and calls `exitEarly()` from a new thread. The parent checks that the requested status survived (no exit-time teardown ran), that the lock was released (through `isLocked()`), and that the buffered write reached the file. The child logs file locking straight to a file (`FileLock::setLogFileForTesting()`), since it is a fork of a multithreaded process and may inherit the logger's locks held. Mutation-checked: removing the main-thread routing in `exitEarly()` yields the atexit status, removing the release leaves the lock held, and removing the flush leaves the file empty. POSIX only.

The watchdog was checked separately: with another thread holding a stream's lock, `fflush(nullptr)` hangs indefinitely, and the watchdog ends the process after 2 seconds with the requested status.

The race itself is not testable. On macOS desktop, force-killing the RStudio desktop process should still take the rsession down promptly, with no crash report generated for rsession.

title: remove log destinations from sections they share with other destinations
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18905.

`log::removeLogDestination()` with an empty section is supposed to remove the destination from the default destinations and from every section it was registered to. The section loop copied each section (`for (auto secIter: ...)`), so the `erase` only changed the copy. A destination that shared a section with other destinations stayed registered there and kept receiving that section's messages. A section the destination was alone in was still removed, because the copy came out empty and the cleanup pass erased the real entry.

### Approach

Loop over the sections by reference.

There are no production callers of the all-sections form in this repo or in rstudio-pro today, so no user saw this. That's why there's no NEWS entry.

### Automated Tests

New `src/cpp/shared_core/LoggerTests.cpp` (in `rstudio-shared-core-tests`, run under `rstudio-tests --scope core`):

- `LoggerTests.RemoveLogDestinationRemovesItFromSectionsItShares` fails without the fix, since the removed destination still receives the section's message. It passes with the fix.
- `LoggerTests.RemoveLogDestinationDropsSectionsItWasAloneIn` covers the path that already worked: once the destination's only section is dropped, the section's messages fall back to the default destinations.

All 17 shared-core tests pass locally on macOS.

### QA Notes

None; covered by the unit tests.

### Documentation

None.

### Checklist

- [ ] ~~If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`~~ (no user-visible effect)
- [ ] ~~If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards~~ (no UI)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests
