title: cache git and svn installation status to reduce redundant probes
description:
## Intent

`isGitInstalled()` launched `git --version` on every client init (reload or reconnect) and every time Project Options opened, although startup had already found the answer. Right after #18751, startup also ran the same probe twice in a row.

Fixes #18759.

## Approach

- `isGitInstalled()` remembers a working git, so once git has answered, client inits and `vcsContext()` stop launching it. A missing or failing git is still probed on every call, as before. Installing git or the macOS Command Line Tools mid-session, putting git on the PATH from `.Rprofile`, or accepting the Xcode license is therefore still picked up.
- The probe now runs on first use rather than in `git::initialize()`, so startup launches git once. `initialize()` still resolves the path and logs a failed Windows detection.
- Changing the Git executable in Global Options re-resolves the path and clears the remembered answer. The next `isGitInstalled()` runs the new binary, so a slow or hanging git can't block saving prefs.
- svn works the same way: `isSvnInstalled()` no longer runs `svn help` on every client init.
- `s_gitVersion` is removed rather than refreshed. Nothing has read it since #7913, so the stale version described in the issue had no visible effect.
- The Xcode license check stays in `gitExec()`, which already runs it on exit status 69.

## Testing

- New r-scope `test-vcs.R`, using a stand-in `git` script:
  1. A git that worked through an explicit path stops being offered once the pref is cleared and no git is on the PATH.
  2. A git that appears on the PATH mid-session is picked up.

  Test 1 fails on the PR's original head (21788c4718). Test 2 fails on a variant that also remembers a "no" answer. Both pass here. They skip on Windows, where detection also scans the standard install locations.
- In a dev-build `rsession` with `RSTUDIO_GIT_LOG=1`, three `read_project_options` calls launched `git --version` once.
- The Windows-only branches (`detectAndSaveGitExePath()` in `resolveGitExePath()` and `probeGit()`) were not compiled locally; CI covers that build.

No NEWS entry: in released builds, the only change is fewer process launches.

title: Resolve Posit Assistant from versioned install slots
description:
Addresses #18658.

Step 3 of the plan in #18658: the resolver switch and install path rewrite, plus the step 2 adjustments the issue lists. The slot machinery merged inert in #18666 is now what the session uses.

## What changes

**Resolution.** `locatePositAssistantInstallation()` ranks candidates from four sources: the user's `pai/versions` slot named by `pai/selected.json` (repairing a stale selection), the system-wide `<systemConfigDir>/pai/versions` slot named by its own `selected.json` (read-only, never repaired), the legacy `<systemConfigDir>/pai/bin`, and the bundled copy. The #18774 rules are unchanged: compatible protocol first, then highest version, ties user > system slot > system legacy > bundled; `posit-assistant-path` is used outright and ends the search when it does not verify; `userInstallWouldBeSelected()` still gates the update offer; managed mode skips the user tier. The user's legacy `pai/bin` is never read.

**One resolution per session.** The session resolves lazily on first need and every consumer reads that answer: backend start, agent start, the `/ai-chat/` asset handler and its CSP, and installed-version reporting. It is mutex-guarded because the asset handler reads it from HTTP threads, re-validated structurally on each read, and cleared only by the session's own install. An empty resolution is not held. This replaces the separate `staticfiles::setInstallationPath()` pin; the CSP cache is keyed on the served installation path, and the asset handler passes its one resolution into the CSP build.

**Install.** Download, SHA-256, extract into a private staging directory (`.tmp-<host>-<pid>-<nonce>`, removed by the call that created it when the install fails, never reclaimed by anyone else), check the extracted `package.json` version and `protocol.json` protocol against the manifest entry with `verifyDeclaredIdentity()`, `allocateSlot()`, `selectSlot()`, then stop the backend and agent so they restart on the new slot. An agent that does not stop in time fails the install with a retry message and leaves the held resolution alone; the retry skips the download. The reported current version is what the session resolves afterwards. A version already present in a verifying slot is re-selected without a download. The `ai.prev` backup and `writeProtocolVersionFileIfMissing()` are gone; a package without `protocol.json` is refused.

**Selector (step 2 adjustments).** `resolveSlot()` gains `SelectorRepair::Disabled` for the system tier; `preferredOver()` is parse-compare, then ordinal, then name, with the prerelease handling removed; `selectInstalledVersion()` prefers the latest reinstall and keeps an existing matching selection; `verifySlot()` builds on `installation::verifyInstallDir()`/`declaredVersion()`/`declaredProtocol()` so there is one definition of a valid install; `verifiedSlots()` takes the protocol and skips other slots before walking their manifests.

**Manifest lookup.** `getPackageInfoFromManifest()` reads the entry for the exact protocol string instead of the highest minor within the major, matching every other protocol comparison. Protocol versions are only ever published as `<major>.0`; `types::isProtocolVersionForm()` is the textual check, a unit test pins `kProtocolVersion` with it, and a manifest key of any other form is warned about. An entry that is absent or unusable (not an object, no version or url, non-HTTPS) reports `protocol_not_supported`, the one code the update check reads as "nothing to offer". Without this, an `11.1` entry on an `11.0` build was offered and then refused by the install identity check on every attempt.

**Test harness.** `PW_SEED_PAI` is laid out as a slot with a manifest and a selector, each spec gets its own `pai` provisioned by hardlink clone (no more symlinked seed), and the version-under-test report follows the selector.

**Docs.** NEWS entry and the user guide's manual-removal section describe the `versions` and `selected.json` layout.

## Deviations from the issue body

- `waitForOwnComponentsReaped()` is deleted here rather than in step 4: with the stop-before-install reap-wait gone it would be an unused static.
- The Windows access-denied install message is dropped: it described a directory swap that no longer happens.
- `MutationScope` and the in-use lock acquire in backend and agent start remain as call sites for step 4, which deletes `ChatInstallLock.*`.

## Follow-ups filed

- posit-dev/assistant#2493: `deploy:rstudio` must publish a slot with a manifest.
- rstudio/rstudio-pro#12897: administrator documentation for the system-wide layout.

## Verification

- `GTEST_FILTER='Chat*:ProtocolVersion*:IsProtocolVersionForm*:SessionAssistant*:PositAssistant*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession`: 314 passed.
- `e2e/rstudio`: `npm run -s typecheck` clean; `tests/harness/pai-seed.test.ts` 13 passed.

title: use the ide font for inline paged table output
description:
## Intent

Inline data frame and `rmarkdown::paged_table()` chunk output rendered every cell in bold on some Windows machines.

## Approach

The paged table is the one piece of chunk output rendered straight into the editor DOM rather than inside an output iframe, and RStudio's copy of `pagedtable.css` gave it a font stack of its own led by `"Lucida Sans"`. On Windows desktop the rest of the IDE uses Segoe UI (the Electron default), so the two diverge. "Lucida Sans" ships with Office, not Windows, and a machine holding only its Demibold face satisfies the family request with that face, so weight-400 text renders demibold. The rmarkdown copy of the stylesheet declares no font at all, which is why knitted HTML looks normal.

This drops the hardcoded stack and has `ChunkDataWidget` apply the IDE's proportional font to the widget element, matching every other proportional-font surface in the IDE.

## Testing

New e2e test (`notebook_paged_table_font.test.ts`) runs a bare data frame and a `paged_table()` chunk and asserts the cell's computed font family equals the document body's and its weight is 400. It fails on `main` (the cell resolves to the old standalone stack) and passes with this change, in server-dev mode on macOS.

Fixes #18874.

title: silence dependency deprecation warnings on cmake 4.4
description:
## Intent

Configuring with CMake 4.4 prints four warnings at every run: a CMP0218 policy warning from `src/cpp/ext/CMakeLists.txt`, plus "Compatibility with CMake < 3.10 will be removed" deprecation notices from gsl-lite, libgit2 and yaml-cpp's own `cmake_minimum_required()` calls. This makes configures quiet again on CMake 4.4 without changing anything on older CMake.

## Approach

CMake 4.4 deprecated the `CMAKE_WARN_DEPRECATED` variable (policy CMP0218) in favor of `cmake_diagnostic()`, and no longer honors the variable for the dependency deprecation notices. The `set(CMAKE_WARN_DEPRECATED FALSE)` line is replaced with:

```cmake
if(COMMAND cmake_diagnostic)
   cmake_diagnostic(SET CMD_DEPRECATED IGNORE)
else()
   set(CMAKE_WARN_DEPRECATED FALSE)
endif()
```

The block is placed *before* `include(FetchContent)`. Like policies, the diagnostic state is captured when a function is defined, and the dependencies are added from inside `FetchContent_MakeAvailable()`; placed after the include, the CMP0218 warning goes away but the three dependency warnings remain. A comment in the file documents this ordering requirement.

Raising `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM` to 3.10 would also silence the notices, but it would flip the 3.6-3.10 policies inside every fetched dependency (the last policy change broke libgit2's feature detection on Linux in #18877), so it was not used.

No NEWS entry: build-only change.

## QA Notes

- A clean configure of this branch from the repo root with CMake 4.4.3 (fresh dependency clones, Ninja, Debug) reports no warnings.
- The fallback branch keeps the exact line the file had before, so CMake 3.25 through 4.3 behave as on `main`. Not exercised locally (only 4.4.3 installed).

title: link dependents before their dependencies to stop duplicate static libs
description:
## Intent

A clean macOS build emits `ld: warning: ignoring duplicate libraries` for eight targets: `rsession`, `rserver`, `rserver-pam`, `rpostback`, `rstudio-core-tests`, `rstudio-shared-core-tests`, `rstudio-server-core-tests` and `rserver-tests`. This is the last warning category left in the backend build after #18867, and it is caused by our own link lists.

## Approach

`target_link_libraries()` records each library's dependencies, and CMake appends them after the library on the link line. The affected link lists named a dependency *before* the target that depends on it (`rstudio-core` before `rstudio-server-core`, `rstudio-shared-core` before `rstudio-core`) and re-listed Boost, SOCI and the system libraries that `rstudio-core` already carries. CMake preserves the explicit order and then has to place the dependency a second time after the dependent, so the same static archive appeared twice.

Each list now names only the outermost libraries and lets the link graph supply the rest:

- `rserver`, `rserver-tests`, `rserver-pam`, `rstudio-server-core-tests`: drop the explicit `rstudio-core`, Boost, SOCI and `CORE_SYSTEM_LIBRARIES` entries; `rstudio-server-core` carries them.
- `rstudio-core` now declares `rstudio-core-synctex`, which its `TexSynctex.cpp` uses. Callers used to list synctex after `rstudio-core` by hand; that entry goes away from `SESSION_LIBRARIES` and `rstudio-core-tests`.
- `rstudio-core-tests`, `rstudio-shared-core-tests`: drop `rstudio-shared-core`, the vendored deps and Boost; `rstudio-core` carries them.
- `rpostback`: link `rstudio-server-core` on server builds, `rstudio-core` otherwise, instead of both.
- `rsession` / `rsession-shared`: `rstudio-server-core` moves to the front of `SESSION_LIBRARIES`, and `rstudio-core` moves after `rstudio-monitor`, `rstudio-r` and `rstudio-session-workers`, which depend on it. The two trailing `target_link_libraries(... rstudio-server-core)` calls go away.

No NEWS entry: build-only change.

## QA Notes

- Compared the generated link lines (`LINK_LIBRARIES` in `build.ninja`) before and after for every executable: the *set* of libraries is identical for each target; only the order and the duplicate archive entries changed. After the change no target lists a static archive twice.
- Clean Debug build on macOS arm64 with CMake 4.4.3: the eight duplicate-library warnings are gone, no compiler warnings, no other new warnings.
- `rstudio-tests --scope core`, `--scope rserver` and `--scope rsession` all pass on the relinked binaries.
- Linux and Windows links not exercised locally; CI covers them. Apple's linker resolves static archives in any order, so a macOS build can't catch ordering mistakes; GNU ld can. The first CI run caught one: `rstudio-core-synctex` was not a declared dependency of `rstudio-core`, so moving it ahead of `rstudio-core` left `rsession` with undefined `synctex_*` references on Linux. Fixed by having `rstudio-core` declare it.
- Re-checked `LINK_LIBRARIES` in `build.ninja` (Server, unit tests on) for all 10 executables: synctex follows `librstudio-core.a` everywhere, and no target lists a static archive twice.

title: fail the dependency install job when a package fails to install
description:
## Summary

When a feature needs R packages, the dependency manager installs them in a background job. That job printed "✔ Package 'x' successfully installed." and finished as **Succeeded** even when the installation had failed. The client then re-checked the dependencies, found them still unsatisfied, and silently abandoned the user's action.

The install script in `SessionDependencies.cpp` assumed "the script aborts on error", but `install.packages()` reports a failed installation as a *warning*, so the script carried on to the success message.

The script now ends with a check that every requested package is installed at its required version, and stops with `Failed to install 'x'` otherwise. The job is then reported as **Failed**, which the client already handles. The version check matters for updates: a failed update leaves the old version in place, so checking for presence alone would still pass.

### e2e

This surfaced through a server-linux failure of `create_file_types.test.ts` ("create Plumber API via newRPlumberDoc"). The runner's library had `plumber` but not `sodium`: `plumber` lists `sodium` in `Imports` but never imports it in its `NAMESPACE`, so it installs and loads without it. The test's `requireNamespace("plumber")` gate passed, the IDE's dependency walk (which reads DESCRIPTION files) prompted for `sodium`, the source install failed for want of the `libsodium` headers, and the dialog never opened.

`ensurePackage()` now treats a package as available only if it loads *and* `.rs.findUnsatisfiedRuntimeDependencies()` finds nothing missing, so a partial library triggers a reinstall (which pulls in the missing dependency), and if that still fails the test skips with a clear reason rather than timing out on a dialog. Builds that predate the dependency walk fall back to the old check.

I did not add `plumber` to `required-packages.txt`: `sodium` needs system headers wherever PPM has no binary, the deps action installs no system libraries automatically, and a required package that fails to install fails the whole job.

## Testing

- Three new gtests execute the generated check in R: packages present, a package missing, and an installed version that is too old. `rstudio-tests --scope rsession`: 632 passed.
- Ran the generated R directly for those cases plus a malformed version string, which passes rather than failing the job.
- Not exercised end to end in a running IDE. That the job ends up Failed rests on existing script-job behavior: `ScriptJob` reports success only for a zero exit status with the completion marker emitted.
- The e2e change was not run locally; the availability expression was checked in R with and without the `.rs.` function defined.

Fixes #18882.

title: Install only the native architecture's macOS dependencies off Jenkins
description:
Addresses #18890.

`install-dependencies-osx` installed both x86_64 and arm64 dependencies on every Apple Silicon machine, which needs Rosetta 2 and a second Homebrew that a routine development build never uses. Only Jenkins builds the universal package.

## Changes

- `dependencies/osx/install-dependencies-osx` is driven by an architecture list. Jenkins on Apple Silicon gets both architectures (via `is-jenkins`, as before); everywhere else the default is the machine's own architecture. `--arch=x86_64,arm64` opts into a universal setup. Requesting x86_64 on Apple Silicon checks for Rosetta 2 and the x86_64 Homebrew up front and says how to install each. Empty or unknown architectures and unknown options fail with a message.
- `package/osx/make-package` gets the matching default (native off Jenkins, universal on Jenkins) and validates the `--arch` list and each architecture's tools root before `set-version`, so a missing set fails before `npm ci` runs or package.json is touched.
- `dependencies/osx/README.md` moves the Intel Homebrew step into a new Universal Builds section covering Rosetta 2 and `--arch`. `package/README.md` documents the new default.
- The four macOS e2e workflow comments that described the old dual-arch default are updated. Those workflows already call the per-arch script directly and pass `--arch` to make-package explicitly, so they are otherwise unaffected. The Jenkinsfile is unchanged.

## Verification

- Ran the install script through a harness with a stubbed per-arch script: the default installs arm64 only with the arm64 Homebrew first on PATH; a fake Jenkins environment and `--arch=x86_64,arm64` both install x86_64 then arm64 into the sibling tools roots; bad architectures, an empty list, unknown options, and a simulated missing Rosetta all exit 1 with the intended message.
- Ran make-package against an empty tools root: off Jenkins it fails naming arm64, under a fake Jenkins environment it fails naming x86_64, both before `npm ci`. `--arch=`, `--arch=ppc`, and `--arch=arm64,ppc` fail the same way.
- Not verified: Intel behavior (no Intel machine available) and the missing-Homebrew error path (needs root to fake). No full universal build was run.

title: Remove the Uninstall Posit Assistant command
description:
First of the PRs in #18658 (side-by-side versioned Posit Assistant installs). Re-implements #18662 (reverted in #18679) against current `main`: #18691, #18815 and #18832 had each changed the uninstall handler since.

Removed:

- `chat_uninstall_posit_assistant` RPC (`SessionChat.cpp`) and its registration
- the `uninstallPositAssistant` command, its Help > Diagnostics menu entry, the `Commands.java` stub, and the en/fr command strings (`Commands.cmd.xml.MD5` regenerated)
- `ChatPresenter.onUninstallPositAssistant()` / `performUninstall()`, the `ChatTab.Shim` binding, the `ChatServerOperations` declaration, the `RemoteServer` binding, and the chat en/fr dialog strings
- the `PaneManager` carve-out that kept the command visible with Posit Assistant disabled
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/uninstall-posit-ai.test.ts`

The "Removing Posit Assistant" section of the user guide is replaced rather than deleted: it now says how to delete the downloaded `pai` directory by hand on each platform (with RStudio closed), that chat history and provider settings live under `~/.posit/assistant` and survive, and that administrator-installed and bundled copies are not the user's to remove. The managed-installation message no longer mentions uninstalls.

Comments in `SessionChat.cpp`, `SessionAssistant.hpp`, `ChatInstallLock`, `ChatStaticFiles` and the e2e fixtures that described uninstall as a live path now describe install and update only. The install and update paths keep the locking, `ai.prev` backup and reap helpers the handler shared with them; later PRs in #18658 remove those.

Not done here: `relaunchAfterRestart()` / `snapshotRStudioProcesses()` in `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/desktop.fixture.ts` are now unused (the deleted spec was their only caller). Kept as-is since they encode the rstudio#18522 CDP-port lesson and the Reinstall PR may need them.

Verification: `ant draft`, `cmake --build . --target rsession`, `rstudio-tests --scope rsession` (629 passed), `npm run typecheck` in `e2e/rstudio`.

Addresses #18658.

title: skip chat e2e tests when posit ai fails on its side
description:
The Posit Assistant chat specs fail whenever Posit AI does. In [run 34994843398](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/34994843398/job/104474040859) (PR #18825, macOS shard 2), the runner lost its connection to `gateway.posit.ai` partway through the run. The assistant answered "Error making request", the specs failed on their content assertions, and the retry of one suite failed during setup because the install manifest download from `cdn.posit.co` timed out. The reachability gate from #18806 didn't catch it: it probes once per worker, before the outage began, and only the code-suggestion specs re-probe after a failure.

This change makes a failure on Posit AI's side a skip, while failures a product change could cause still fail:

- **The service answered with a failure.** Rate limited, overloaded, or a 5xx: the test skips outright. The chat actions recognize these from Posit Assistant's own error messages (databot's `formatApiError`), which end the assistant's reply.
- **The request failed without an HTTP status** ("Error making request", alone or with a network error like `read ETIMEDOUT`): the test skips only if re-probing the Posit AI hosts from the runner confirms the outage. The request comes from the assistant's backend, which RStudio launches, so a failure the runner can't reproduce may be ours. That case is logged and left to the test's own checks, since some tests pass on an error reply. Errors on a loopback address never skip.
- **Setup or a reply that never arrives.** A failure in `dismissSetupPrompts`, or a timeout in `waitForResponse` / `pollWithAllowDialogs`, re-probes the same way. Since setup runs in `beforeAll`, a confirmed outage there skips the whole suite.

The checks sit in `ChatPaneActions`, so none of the chat specs change. They only look at a finished turn, because the assistant can still run tools after a failed request. They also ignore an error left over from the previous turn, so the next test still sends its message. Other HTTP errors (4xx, credits, account setup) and unrecognized errors behave as before. `PW_AI_AUTH_STRICT` turns off all of these skips, as it already does for the gate. `code_suggestions.test.ts` now uses the shared `failUnlessAiServiceGone()` in place of its own copy.

### Testing

- New harness self-test `tests/harness/chat-provider-failure.test.ts` covers the classifier: Posit Assistant's error strings, messages that must not match, and the rendered DOM shape from the failing run.
- Checked against a mocked chat pane (throwaway specs, not committed):
  - A service-side failure skips.
  - A network failure is logged and left to the test while the hosts answer, and skips when they don't (`fetch` stubbed).
  - A setup stall inside `beforeAll` during an outage skips every test in the suite.
  - A failure shown while the turn is still active is ignored, and so is one left over from the previous turn.
  - `PW_AI_AUTH_STRICT=1` doesn't skip.
- `npm run typecheck`
- The real `@ai` specs need Posit AI credentials, so CI is the first place they run with this change.

title: leak statics that background threads can touch at exit
description:
## Summary

Follow-up hardening for #18318. rsession exits through `exit()`, which runs destructors for every object with static storage duration while background threads may still be running. A thread that touches an already-destroyed static is a use-after-destroy at exit. This extends the `core::make_leaked<>` approach from #18320 / #18327 to the rest of the statics those threads can reach.

Which threads can outlive `exit()`:

- The stdout/stderr capture thread is never stopped on any path.
- In desktop mode, `rCleanup` does not stop the http listener, static asset, or client event service threads (it only does so in server mode).
- `exitEarly()` and the failsafe `::exit(0)` in `RQuit.cpp` skip most of the stops that `rCleanup` does.
- Everything stopped with `joinOrAbandonThread` is detached if the bounded join times out.

### The original motivation

`userPrefs()` and `userState()` were function-local statics. `~PrefLayer` unregisters its file monitor, and the layers live for the life of the process, so that destructor only ever ran during static teardown -- after the file monitor's own statics (constructed later, hence destroyed earlier) could already be gone. Before #18320 leaked the file monitor's queues this was a real crash: on libc++, pushing onto a destroyed `std::deque` placement-constructs the element at address 0, which shows up as a null `this` in `RegistrationCommand::RegistrationCommand`.

### Always reachable

Touched constantly by threads that are provably alive at exit:

- `session::options()` -- read by the http listener on every request (CSRF, request signature, upload paths), and by the websocket, offline service and console input threads
- `clientEventService()` -- its own thread loops over the instance's members
- `r::session::consoleActions()` and the console annotation regexes in `SessionConsoleOutput.cpp` -- reached from `ClientEventQueue::flushBufferedOutput` on the client event and output capture threads
- the stderr suppression regex in `SessionConsole.cpp`
- `uri_handlers::handlers()` and `s_defaultUriHandler`
- the http date facets in `core/http/Util.cpp`
- Windows: the file monitor's `s_handleMutex` / `s_handleRegistry`, which the monitor thread uses in its own cleanup path

### Reachable after a join timeout, or in a narrower window

- `consoleInputService()` -- its destructor abandoned the thread after 1s and then destroyed the queue it reads
- `s_projectContext` -- the file monitor thread's filter reads `directory()`
- `persistentState()`, `module_context::events()`, `processSupervisor()`, the cached `activeSession()` pointer, `s_offlineableUris`, `s_sessionExecutingMutex` -- offline service thread
- `s_uploadMutex` / `s_uploadStateMap` -- uploads are parsed on the listener thread
- `s_terminalSocket` -- its destructor also joined the websocket thread with no timeout, mid-teardown
- the `FileLock` refresh timer and `FileLock::s_logFile`
- Linux: the memory provider statics in `LinuxResources.cpp`

### Other changes

- `Options`, `ClientEventService`, `ConsoleActions` and `PersistentState` have private constructors, so each befriends `core::make_leaked<>`. That keeps one greppable idiom and the LeakSanitizer annotation.
- `Options::getOverlayOption()` used `overlayOptions_[name]`, which inserts on a miss. It is called from background threads, so it now uses `find()`.

Nothing is lost by skipping these destructors: `~PrefLayer` and `~ConsoleInputService` were the only ones with logic, and the `onShutdown` hook still unregisters the pref file monitors on normal quits.

Not addressed here: on macOS `detectParentTermination` calls `exitEarly()`, and so `::exit()`, from a background thread while the main thread is still running. Leaking individual statics doesn't fix that; the Linux and Windows variants use `_Exit`. That is worth its own discussion.

No NEWS entry, since this is internal hardening (as with #18318 itself).

## Testing

Built all backend targets on macOS from this branch, then ran `rstudio-tests`:

- `--scope core`: 731 + 12 + 15 tests passed
- `--scope rsession`: 629 tests passed
- `--scope r`: 4029 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped

`LinuxResources.cpp` and `Win32FileMonitor.cpp` are not part of the macOS build, so CI is the first compile of those two edits. There is no test that exercises the exit-time race itself.

Addresses #18318.

title: retype terminal input lost to a pty resize in e2e tests
description:
## Summary

Fixes a Windows-only flake in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/terminal/terminal.test.ts`, seen in [this run](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/35464517675/job/105958171347) (on an unrelated PR):

- `terminal keeps rendering after WebGL context loss` failed: the second command arrived as `cho "pw_ctx2""loss_ok"`, so bash answered `cho: command not found` and the marker never rendered. (The WebGL fallback itself worked.)
- On the serial group's retry, `we can run commands in the terminal` failed the same way: `expr 1 + 1` arrived as `expr 1+ 1`. That is also why the WebGL test "did not run" a second time.

## Cause

In both traces a `process_set_size` RPC completed 20-60ms before the lost keystroke. A hidden terminal is not re-fit (`XTermWidget.onResize` returns early when not visible), and `openTerminal()` polls through the Console tab, so a size change that comes up meanwhile is only sent once the Terminal tab is shown again -- just as the test starts typing. In the WebGL test, switching `terminal_renderer` from `dom` to `canvas` re-fits the same way.

I found no loss point in RStudio's input path (websocket -> `ConPty::writeInput`), and the client already skips same-size resizes, so the drop appears to happen below RStudio (conhost / the MSYS runtime). That part is inferred from reading the code; it does not reproduce on macOS.

## Fix

`ResizePseudoConsole` is asynchronous and nothing signals that the shell has finished handling a resize, so there is no condition to wait on. Instead, detect the loss and retype:

- New `retryTerminalInput(page, input, landed)` in `e2e/rstudio/utils/terminal.ts`: type, check, and on failure refocus the terminal, send Ctrl+C, and do both once more. A retry records a `terminal-input-retry` test annotation, so lost input stays visible in the report.
- All five typed-command sites in `terminal.test.ts` use it. The other terminal specs force the DOM renderer (or are skipped on Windows) and are unchanged.

Retyping cannot mask a real bug: a broken renderer shows nothing no matter how often the command is typed, and a Shift+Backspace that does nothing leaves the `...txtQ` file from the first attempt behind, which keeps that check false.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npm run test:desktop-dev -- tests/panes/terminal/terminal.test.ts`: 7/7 pass on macOS.
- A temporary local-only test that dropped the leading `e` on the first attempt recovered on the second and recorded the annotation.
- Not yet exercised on Windows, where the flake occurs; this PR's CI is the first run there.

title: modernize cmake: require 3.25, stop using findboost
description:
## Summary

Modernizes the CMake setup:

1. **require cmake 3.25**: raises the minimum CMake version and handles what that changes on Windows.
2. **find boost through its cmake config, not findboost**: stops using CMake's deprecated FindBoost module.

The later commits address review findings, and fix two Linux regressions that the newly enabled policies caused (see [What the new policies changed on Linux](#what-the-new-policies-changed-on-linux)).

## CMake 3.25

Raises the minimum CMake version from 3.6.3 to 3.25 everywhere one is declared (the `CMakeLists.txt` files, the macOS package scripts, `CMakePresets.json`, and `dependencies/linux/README`).

3.25 is the oldest CMake any official build uses: `package/linux/install-dependencies` builds 3.25.2 on the Jenkins images, and Windows/macOS pick up current CMake from choco/brew. The code already needed 3.19 without a version check (`COMMAND_ERROR_IS_FATAL` in `compiler.cmake`), and CMake 3.31+ warns on every configure when the minimum is below 3.10.

With the new minimum, these are dead and removed:

- the 3.19 check around the gzipped GWT symbol-map install
- the 3.24 check around `find_package(... GLOBAL)`
- the explicit `CMP0048` / `CMP0077` / `CMP0141` settings (`CMP0141` in `sccache.cmake` never took effect: it ran after `project()`, inside an `include()` policy scope)
- the rest of sccache's MSVC block (`add_compile_options(/Z7)` and its `/Zi` cache strip): `CMAKE_MSVC_DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT` already puts `-Z7` after every target's other flags, including the `/Zi` that libgit2 writes into its own

The symbol-map `install(CODE)` block is also rewritten, as a bracket argument filled in with `string(CONFIGURE ... @ONLY)`, which removes its backslash-escaped quotes and `\${...}` references. The generated install script is unchanged apart from the blank line that opened the old string.

## What the new policies changed on Linux

Raising the minimum turns on every policy up to 3.25. Two of them changed the Linux build while leaving macOS untouched, which is why a macOS-only comparison did not show them.

- **CMP0067: libgit2 failed to compile** (`#error GIT_USE_NSEC defined but unknown struct stat nanosecond type`; this was the first Jenkins failure on this PR). CMake's check modules are include-guarded globally and wrap `try_compile` in a function, and a function keeps the policies of whoever defines it. `src/cpp` includes them before the dependencies are added, so every dependency's configure checks now run under our policies, whatever its own `cmake_minimum_required` says. With CMP0067, `try_compile` honors `CMAKE_C_STANDARD`. libgit2 builds as strict C90 and only adds `-D_GNU_SOURCE` to its flags *after* its checks have run, so the checks compiled as `-std=c90` without it, glibc hid `struct stat`'s `st_mtim`, and no nanosecond stat member was detected. Fixed with a per-dependency `CFLAGS` option in `src/cpp/ext` (next to the existing `CXXFLAGS`) that defines `_GNU_SOURCE` while libgit2 configures, on non-MSVC platforms.
- **CMP0128: the C++ dialect silently went from gnu++17 to strict C++17.** On `main` every C++ file is compiled with `-std=c++17 -std=gnu++17`: the first flag is added by hand in `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`, the second by CMake for `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17`, and the last one wins. With CMP0128, CMake leaves its flag out when the compiler already defaults to that standard (GCC 11+), so the hand-written `-std=c++17` became the only one. AppleClang's default is older, so macOS still gets CMake's flag. The hand-written flag is now `-std=gnu++17`, which pins the dialect that has actually been in effect on every platform.

## Windows changes

Raising the minimum turns on CMP0091 and CMP0141, so CMake no longer puts `/MD` and `/Zi` in `CMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS_<CONFIG>`, and selects the runtime library and debug information format itself, tree-wide. CMP0092 also drops the default `/W3`.

- `compiler.cmake` sets `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY` (same `/MD` vs `/MDd` choice as before) and `CMAKE_MSVC_DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT` (embedded, i.e. `/Z7`, for Debug and RelWithDebInfo) instead of rewriting the flag strings.
- `/W3` is kept for C++ (in `compiler.cmake`) and for C (in `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`, since `compiler.cmake` runs before C is enabled in a root configure).
- Build directories configured before this change still have `/MD` and `/Zi` in their cached C and C++ flags. `compiler.cmake` removes them from the cache entries in place, so a reused build directory ends up with the same flags as a fresh one. It edits the cache rather than setting variables, because a normal variable set at the root would hide the defaults CMake gives C once `src/cpp` enables it.
- libgit2 is built with `STATIC_CRT OFF`. It hard-codes `/MT` into its own flags by default; with the new runtime selection it would otherwise get `/MT ... /MD` on every file.

Two deliberate behavior changes on Windows:

- **Our C sources now get CMake's default C flags.** `compiler.cmake` used to write the `CMAKE_C_FLAGS*` variables at the root, before C is enabled (the root project enables CXX only). Those empty normal variables hid the C defaults in every subdirectory, so sundown, synctex, and our zlib build compiled with no optimization, no `NDEBUG`, no debug info, no `/W3`, and the compiler's default static CRT inside DLL-runtime binaries. They now get `/O2 /DNDEBUG /W3` etc. plus `/MD /Z7`, matching macOS and Linux.
- **libgit2 moves from the static to the DLL C runtime**, like the rest of rsession.

## Boost

CMake 3.30 deprecated its FindBoost module (CMP0167) in favor of the `BoostConfig.cmake` that Boost installs itself (Boost 1.70+; we require 1.91).

- **Windows** already skipped `find_package(Boost)`; only its comment is corrected (3.30 deprecated FindBoost; 4.x still ships it).
- **rstudio-tools Boost** (macOS, official Linux): was already found in config mode (via `HINTS`). Now explicit: `CONFIG`, searching only `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_BOOST` (`PATHS ... NO_DEFAULT_PATH`), since that copy uses its own namespace.
- **System Boost** (`RSTUDIO_USE_SYSTEM_BOOST`, e.g. distribution packagers): went through FindBoost, with a CMP0167 warning on CMake 3.30+. Now a single `find_package(Boost ... CONFIG COMPONENTS ...)`. When system Boost wasn't requested, `NO_CMAKE_SYSTEM_PATH NO_SYSTEM_ENVIRONMENT_PATH` replaces FindBoost's `Boost_NO_SYSTEM_PATHS`.
  - This path now needs Boost's CMake package files; FindBoost could also find a Boost installed without them (`b2 --no-cmake-config`, or a distribution package that leaves them out). The lookup is therefore not `REQUIRED`: when it fails, our own error explains that, says when the system locations were skipped (and that `-DRSTUDIO_USE_SYSTEM_BOOST=1` searches them), and points at `Boost_ROOT` / `BOOST_ROOT`. `dependencies/linux/README` has the same note.
  - `BOOST_ROOT`, which FindBoost honored, keeps working: `find_package` only reads it from CMake 3.27 (CMP0144), so it is handed over as `Boost_ROOT`, from the variable or the environment. CMP0144 is also set to NEW so that newer CMake doesn't warn about the variable, but only around this one call, because it changes where every package is looked for.
- `src/cpp` opts into CMP0167 where available, so a future plain `find_package(Boost)` can't fall back to the module.
- Dropped the dead `signals` checks and the FindBoost-only settings; `shared_core` now reads `Boost_INCLUDE_DIRS` (same path) instead of the `BOOST_INCLUDEDIR` hint.
- **SOCI build scripts** (`dependencies/common/install-soci`, `dependencies/windows/install-soci/install-soci.R`): SOCI 4.0.3's own `find_package(Boost)` is pointed straight at our Boost's `BoostConfig.cmake` with `Boost_DIR` (plus `CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_CMP0167=NEW`), replacing FindBoost-only hints and the `rstudio_boost_date_time.a` symlink workaround. SOCI's lookup is optional and quiet, so on a miss it would build without Boost, or against a system Boost, without saying so; both scripts now fail up front if `BoostConfig.cmake` is missing. On Windows, Debug and Release are configured in the same build directory, and CMake keeps using the Boost component packages (`boost_headers_DIR`, ...) that the first configure cached, even when `Boost_DIR` changes; the script drops them with `-U "boost_*_DIR"`. We still need SOCI's Boost support: `Database.hpp` defines `SOCI_USE_BOOST`. These only take effect when the SOCI prebuilts are rebuilt.

## Verification

- **Linux, against the merge base**, in a jammy container with the Jenkins toolchain (CMake 3.25.2, GCC 11.4), configured the way `make-package` does (`RSTUDIO_PACKAGE_BUILD`, RelWithDebInfo, Server):
  - Every RStudio source has the same effective `-std` as before. The only compile commands that differ are fmt's two files, which inherit our flag and go from c++17 to gnu++17 (what they already were on macOS), and libgit2's, which get `-D_GNU_SOURCE` a second time. The rest of `build.ninja`, including all link and custom commands, is identical.
  - All cached configure-check results are identical, and libgit2's feature detection and generated `git2_features.h` are identical to `main`'s.
  - Install scripts contain the same rules; the only change is that subdirectory installs (`pam`, `workers`, `postback`) now run where they are declared (CMP0082). None of them overlap with other installed files.
  - The libgit2 failure reproduces in that container without the fix (same `#error` as Jenkins), and libgit2 compiles with it.
  - `BOOST_ROOT` (variable and environment) resolves Boost on CMake 3.25.2, and `Boost_ROOT` still takes precedence.
- **macOS, against the merge base**, development configure: the same two textual differences in the compile commands (the hand-written standard flag, and libgit2's extra `-D_GNU_SOURCE`), with the effective `-std` unchanged for all 872 files. `build.ninja` otherwise differs only in PDB variables that no rule references. A system-Boost configure honors `BOOST_ROOT` without CMP0167 or CMP0144 warnings; with RStudio's Boost missing and system Boost not requested, Homebrew's Boost is not picked up.
- **Windows flag logic**, checked by cross-configuring a small project with `clang-cl` (which goes through CMake's MSVC flag logic) that includes the real `compiler.cmake`, enables C in a subdirectory like `src/cpp`, and has a libgit2-style dependency: C++ flags are equivalent to before in RelWithDebInfo and Debug (a fresh build directory no longer spells out `/GR`, which is MSVC's default; CMP0117). A build directory first configured from `main` and then reconfigured ends up with the same C and C++ flags as a fresh one, its cached `/MD /Zi` removed, and a further configure changes nothing. The dependency's hard-coded `/Zi /MT` is followed, and so overridden, by `-MD -Z7`, with and without sccache.
- **Policies**: went through every policy introduced between 3.7 and 3.25 for anything else this tree could trip over. Beyond the ones above: no license file is given to CPack, so the DMG is unaffected by CMP0133; no source is listed without its extension (CMP0115), including in Windows-only lists; nothing depends on `set(CACHE)` or `option()` replacing a normal variable (CMP0126, CMP0077).
- **SOCI, macOS**: with the first version of the script changes (`Boost_ROOT`), built SOCI 4.0.3 with the old and new flags, and with CMP0167 forced OLD (as on CMake < 3.30): all compile/link commands, `soci-config.h`, and every object in the three static libraries were identical. The final flags (`Boost_DIR`) were checked at configure level against the real SOCI sources: SOCI finds our Boost (`SOCI_HAVE_BOOST` and `SOCI_HAVE_BOOST_DATE_TIME` on, linking `Boost::date_time`), and a missing Boost fails the script. The cached-component-package problem and the `-U` fix were reproduced with two Boost trees of the same version.
- **SOCI, Windows**: not built. The Boost prebuilt zip has `lib/cmake/Boost-1.91.0/BoostConfig.cmake` and the per-component configs under all four roots (32/64-bit, debug/release), which is what the new check and `Boost_DIR` rely on. The script was parsed and its `build()` function exercised with stubs.
- **Not built on Windows.** Everything Windows-specific above is from the `clang-cl` simulation and from reading; this PR's CI covers the real build. CI uses prebuilt SOCI, so the SOCI script changes are exercised only when SOCI is rebuilt.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `set(CMAKE_WARN_DEPRECATED FALSE)` in `src/cpp/ext` triggers the CMP0218 warning on CMake 4.4 and doesn't hide the dependencies' deprecation warnings; a guarded `cmake_diagnostic(SET CMD_DEPRECATED IGNORE)` does both.
- A build directory that was first configured against a system Boost, and is then switched to the rstudio-tools Boost of the same version, keeps its cached `Boost_DIR` / `boost_headers_DIR` (`PATHS ... NO_DEFAULT_PATH` does not override them). Pinning `Boost_DIR` in that branch would close it; a fresh build directory avoids it today.
- rstudio-pro has its own CMake files with old minimums: `docs/*/CMakeLists.txt` (2.6), `package/linux/selinux` (3.10), `src/go/*/CMakeLists.txt` and `src/rust/user_service_nss/CMakeLists.txt` (3.4.3). Its own copies of `cmake/compiler.cmake`, `cmake/modules/sccache.cmake` and `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` will also conflict when this is merged there.

title: Wait for a live FSEvents stream in file monitor tests
description:
`FileMonitorTest.NonRecursiveDetectsFileAdded` failed on macOS hourly build 2026.10.0+124 after its 8 s wait for the `FileAdded` event expired. It passed in +117, and no file monitor code changed between the two builds.

`FSEventStreamStart` returns before fseventsd is delivering to the stream, and streams created with `kFSEventStreamEventIdSinceNow` don't report changes made before that point. Every test writes a file right after `startMonitor()` returns, so on a slow machine that write can be lost rather than just delayed.

Test-only changes in `src/cpp/core/FileMonitorTests.cpp`:

- `startMonitor()` writes probe files (a new one every 2 s, up to 15) until one is observed, so each test starts against a live stream.
- The default `waitFor` timeout goes from 8 s to 20 s. Passing runs return as soon as the event arrives.
- Assertions that wait for events print the events received, so a lost event (`0 event(s) received`) can be told apart from a wrong event type.

Testing, locally on macOS (arm64):

- I couldn't reproduce the CI failure: 1,800 runs of the unmodified suite under full CPU load plus file churn all passed.
- With this change, 1,200 runs under the same load all passed. The suite takes about 1 s longer per test (17 s → 24 s).
- I broke the tests on purpose to check the new failure paths: a wrong expected event type lists the event that arrived, and an unmonitored probe directory fails after about 30 s with `0 event(s) received`.

title: wait for a slow restart to answer before giving up on it
description:
### Intent

`SessionOpener.sendPing` waits for a restarted session to answer a ping, and fires `ConsoleRestartRCompletedEvent` when it does. Two things made it give up while the session was still on its way back:

- It ticked every 200ms and spent one of its 50 retries on **every tick**, including ticks where a ping was already in flight and nothing was sent. The budget was therefore a flat ~10.2s of wall clock however many pings were actually attempted. On exhaustion the loop marked itself completed, so the ping that answered a moment later was discarded by the `completed_` guard in `onSuccess` and the event never fired. A ping can legitimately sit unanswered for much longer than 10s: rserver holds an RPC aimed at a session it is still relaunching (`rsession-proxy-max-wait-secs`, default 30s), and the new session then has to restore the workspace and search path.
- A **failed** ping ended the wait outright, so the retry that would have reached the new session was never sent. That half dates to #17906, which correctly made `onCompleted` fire exactly once but also made the first failure terminal, leaving `maxRetries` unused.

Either way the restart looked fine -- `onCompleted` ran, the progress indicator was dismissed, `RESTART_COMPLETED` fired -- while everything hanging off `ConsoleRestartRCompletedEvent` was silently skipped: `Shell.onRestartRCompleted` leaves the console unfocused with a stale prompt, and `ConsoleTabPanel` never refreshes the Console pane's interpreter version.

### Approach

Budget the wait in wall-clock time (60s) rather than in ticks, wait for an outstanding ping instead of spending the budget on ticks that send nothing, keep pinging after a failure, and announce the restart whenever a ping answers -- including one that answers within 5s after the wait timed out, since an answer means R really is back; later than that, refocusing the console would pull the user away from whatever they moved on to. `onCompleted` still runs exactly once, on an answered ping or on timeout.

### Tests

`SessionOpenerTests` covers both halves directly; each test fails against the current implementation:

- a failed ping is retried, and the ping that answers announces the restart and completes the wait once
- an outstanding ping is awaited rather than piled on, and a response that arrives after the timeout still announces the restart

It also covers the bound on that late announcement: an answer that arrives past the 5s grace period does not announce the restart.

`e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/console/interpreter_version.test.ts` (added in #18858) is where this surfaced. It restarts R twice on RStudio Server, where each restart takes 9-11s -- straddling the 10.2s budget -- and has been failing on essentially every linux-server run, e.g. [run 35259099463](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/35259099463/job/105336330462), with the second restart's ping answered at 10.9s and its success discarded. It held the completion ping until the session was ready to work around the related failure case; that workaround is what pushed the wait past its budget, and it is removed here.

Verified locally: `ant unittest` (600 tests) and the interpreter-version spec on desktop. The Server case is covered by this PR's own CI.

Fixes #18870.

title: Preload libR for rsession in the script-startup test on macOS
description:
Fixes the macOS \`r\` test failures in \`test-script-startup.R\` (added in #18853), e.g. hourly build 2026.10.0+117:

```
dyld: symbol not found in flat namespace '_GEkillDevice'
[ FAIL 4 | WARN 0 | SKIP 19 | PASS 3963 ]
```

On macOS, rsession is linked with `-undefined dynamic_lookup` and gets libR through `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, which `rstudio-tests` sets when it launches rsession. The test launches its child rsession under `/usr/bin/script`, which SIP protects, so dyld strips `DYLD_*` from the environment. The parent rsession also unsets `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` at startup (`SessionMain.cpp`), so there is nothing to inherit.

The test now runs `script ... /usr/bin/env DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=<R lib>/libR.dylib rsession ...`, setting the preload after `script` starts, as `rstudio-tests` does.

Verified locally on macOS: `rstudio-tests --scope r --filter script-startup` went from `FAIL 4` to `FAIL 0 | PASS 9`.

title: only highlight terminal file links while ctrl/cmd is held
description:
Follow-up to #18801 (terminal file links).

The xterm link provider underlined every resolved path under the pointer and switched the cursor to a hand as soon as the mouse crossed it, even though opening the file needs Ctrl held (Cmd on macOS). Sweeping the mouse across ordinary terminal output lit up every token that happened to name a file.

Links now carry decorations that follow the modifier:

- xterm reads a link's `decorations` when a hover begins and then swaps in live accessors of its own, so the initial state comes from a getter and later changes are written through xterm's object -- a hovered link lights up the moment the modifier is pressed and goes dark when it is released, with no pointer movement needed.
- The modifier is tracked from capture-phase key events on the document and from the terminal's own mouse events; the latter also covers moving into the terminal with the modifier already held (a press that happened while another window had focus is never delivered as a keydown).
- The hover hint naming the modifier ("Ctrl+Click to open <path>") still appears on a plain hover, so the feature stays discoverable now that nothing is underlined until the modifier is down.

Testing:

- `src/gwt/test/terminal_file_links.test.cjs` (run by `ant testpage`) gains cases for the decorations following the modifier, the hovered link being repainted on press and release, a re-hover consulting the modifier rather than the previous hover's state, the mouse reporting a modifier pressed while the document was unfocused, and a plain click not opening the file.
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/terminal/terminal_file_links.test.ts` now holds the modifier while hovering, and a new spec checks that releasing it unmarks the link and pressing it again marks it once more.

No NEWS entry: this is a fix to a feature that has not shipped yet (its entry for #18804 is already in NEWS.md).

title: silence compiler warnings in the backend build
description:
A local `cmake --build .` of `src/cpp` on macOS emits three kinds of compiler diagnostic. None of them indicate a live bug, but they're noise that makes a real warning easy to miss. This clears all three; the build is now warning-free apart from linker warnings (see below).

### `Database.cpp` -- `-Wunused-function` (x3)

`pgEncode()`, `getPostgresqlPassword()` and `parseConnectionUri()` are defined unconditionally in the anonymous namespace, but their only caller -- `parsePostgresqlConnectionOptions()` -- has its entire body inside `#ifdef RSTUDIO_HAS_SOCI_POSTGRESQL`. When SOCI is built without PostgreSQL support, all three become dead.

Hoisted the guard out to wrap the whole anonymous namespace, and dropped the now-redundant inner `#ifdef`/`#else` pairs in two of the functions -- their `#else` branches were already unreachable, since no caller survives the outer guard.

Verified both configurations compile: the normal build, plus a `-DRSTUDIO_HAS_SOCI_POSTGRESQL` syntax check against a local libpq.

### `FixedBufferProxyTests.cpp` / `FormProxyTests.cpp` -- `-Wdelete-non-abstract-non-virtual-dtor`

`IAsyncClient` has virtual functions but no virtual destructor (it inherits from `Socket`, which has neither), so `boost::make_shared` on a non-`final` subclass warns that a polymorphic delete would be UB.

`FakeAsyncClient` and `FakeDownstreamClient` are both leaves -- nothing derives from either -- so marking them `final` is the accurate fix and keeps the change to test code. Adding `virtual ~Socket()` would also silence it, but that adds a vtable slot to every socket implementation in the tree for a warning that only fires in tests; happy to do that instead if reviewers prefer fixing the interface.

### `synctex_parser.c` -- `-Wsign-compare`

Vendored SyncTeX. Its `CMakeLists.txt` already says "third-party code we try to avoid changing" and suppresses the MSVC equivalent (`/wd4018`), so this adds the GCC/Clang counterpart rather than patching upstream source.

One wrinkle worth flagging for review: the suppression has to go in `target_compile_options`, **not** `CMAKE_C_FLAGS` alongside the MSVC ones. `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt:70` does `add_definitions(-Wall ...)` for the whole tree, and directory-level options land *after* `CMAKE_C_FLAGS` on the command line -- so a `-Wno-sign-compare` in `CMAKE_C_FLAGS` gets re-enabled by that `-Wall`. I confirmed this the hard way: the first attempt built with the flag present and still warned.

### Testing

`./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope core` passes (729 + 12 + 15 tests, 0 failures), including the two proxy suites whose fakes changed. Rebuild is clean of compiler warnings.

### Not addressed here

- **`ld: warning: ignoring duplicate libraries`** (8 targets) -- real CMake redundancy, e.g. `rpostback` lists `rstudio-core` explicitly *and* inherits it transitively from `rstudio-server-core`. Fixing it means editing `target_link_libraries` on 8 targets, and static-library link order matters more on ELF than on Mach-O, so it's a cosmetic-warning fix with cross-platform link risk. Worth its own PR.
- **`ld: warning: building for macOS-12.0, but linking with ... openssl@3 ... built for newer version 26.0`** -- purely a local toolchain artifact (homebrew OpenSSL built for macOS 26 vs our `-mmacosx-version-min=12.0`), nothing in the repo to change.
- `Database.cpp` also has a small correctness issue in how it builds its Postgres connection string. That's a behavior change rather than a warning fix, so it gets its own PR rather than riding along with this cleanup.

Developer-only change, so no NEWS.md entry and no associated issue.

title: Support Zotero 10 WAL-mode databases in citation lookup
description:
Zotero 10 keeps `zotero.sqlite` in WAL journal mode. `connect()` copied only the main database file into the session scratch directory and opened that copy read-only, which causes two separate problems.

**On macOS, Zotero doesn't appear as a citation source at all.** A WAL header requires a `-wal` file, and a read-only connection cannot create one, so the open fails with `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` — logged as "database error 7 ... unable to open database file".

This symptom is specific to Apple's SQLite. On macOS and Linux rsession links the system sqlite3 (`src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt:347`), which on macOS resolves to `/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; that build refuses to create the sidecar files for a read-only connection. Windows links a vendored 3.31.1 amalgamation (`:324`), and Linux resolves to the distribution's build. Both of those allow a read-only connection to create `-wal`/`-shm` in a writable directory — and the copy lives in one — so the open succeeds there. Verified directly against all three builds with a WAL-header database and no `-wal`: 3.31.1 and upstream 3.53.4 both open it, Apple's 3.51.0 returns error 14. Version is not the variable; the vendor is.

The trigger is the header rather than the presence of a `-wal`. A cleanly shut down Zotero 10 checkpoints and removes its `-wal`, but the main file's header still declares WAL, so a bare copy of it fails the same way.

**On every platform, recently added references go missing.** Commits that are still in an uncheckpointed `-wal` are not in the main database file, so copying that file alone leaves them out. A WAL commit also leaves `zotero.sqlite`'s mtime untouched, so the staleness check never noticed them and the copy was treated as current indefinitely.

## What this does

- Copies `zotero.sqlite-wal` alongside `zotero.sqlite` when one exists, then normalizes the copy by opening it read-write once and running `PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE`. That checkpoints the copied `-wal` into the main file and rewrites the header to rollback mode, leaving a self-contained file that the read-only query connection opens as it did before.
- Reads that pragma's result back and fails with the copy path and the resulting mode when the conversion is refused. sqlite reports a refused conversion by returning the unchanged mode rather than by failing.
- Judges staleness against the later of the `zotero.sqlite` and `zotero.sqlite-wal` mtimes.
- Stamps the copy after normalizing rather than before, since normalizing writes to it.
- Removes the copy's `-wal`/`-shm` when refreshing and on the error paths. macOS keeps those sidecars across a clean close.
- Closes the read-only connection before deleting the copy on the query-failure path. Windows refuses to delete a file that still has an open handle, and a copy left behind keeps the mtime that makes it look fresh, so the same unusable copy would be reused on every later call.

No Zotero version detection is involved; the behavior follows the database's own journal mode. A Zotero 9 rollback-journal database copies as before and the pragma leaves it in rollback mode.

## Testing

`ZoteroCollectionsLocalTests.cpp` builds its source databases through `core::database` itself, so no Zotero install is needed. It covers a closed WAL-mode source, a WAL source with commits still in an uncheckpointed `-wal`, a Zotero 9 rollback-journal source, and a refresh where only the `-wal` is newer. Each case asserts the prepared copy's header reports a rollback journal and that a read-only connection can query it.

Only the closed-WAL case is macOS-specific in what it guards — on Windows and Linux it passes with or without this change. The uncheckpointed-`-wal` and `-wal`-mtime cases fail without the change on every platform, since they test the copy's contents and its staleness rather than whether the open succeeds.

Manually verified on macOS against Zotero 9 and 10. Verification on the other platforms is in progress; on those, the symptom to look for is a reference added in Zotero not reaching citation completion. Check it without leaving the machine idle for five minutes, since Zotero's idle handler checkpoints the WAL and hides the symptom -- see the comment below on when Zotero checkpoints.

- update: I confirmed the fix works on Windows (without the fix, new citations don't show up immediately in RStudio, with the fix, they do); still need to test Linux Desktop

Addresses #18845.

title: Fix crash when downloading a file with no read permission (#18864)
description:
## Summary

Fixes #18864 — downloading/exporting a file the user has no read permission on (e.g. `chmod 000`) from the Files pane crashes RStudio Server with a segfault (the browser shows a 502 and the session enters a failed state).

### Root cause

In `Response::setStreamFile()`, when `streamResponse_->initialize()` fails (opening the file returns `EACCES`), `setError()` is called but `streamResponse_` is left set. `Response::isStreamResponse()` (`static_cast<bool>(streamResponse_)`) therefore still returns `true`, so `AsyncConnectionImpl` routes the response to `StreamWriter`, which calls `FileStreamResponse::nextBuffer()`. That dereferences `fileStream_` at `Response.cpp:89` — but `fileStream_` was never opened, so it is null → segfault.

### Fix

1. **Clear `streamResponse_` on `initialize()` failure** — the general fix. It stops the null deref *and* makes `isStreamResponse()` return `false` so the HTTP error body is actually sent. Covers every caller of `setStreamFile()`.
2. **Defensive null-stream guard** in `FileStreamResponse::nextBuffer()`.

### Platform scope

Affects the Unix/Linux gzip streaming path. Windows uses a different code path.

### Testing

Manual repro: create a `chmod 000` file, export it from the Files pane. Before: session segfaults (502 / failed). After: the download fails with an HTTP error and the session stays up.

Closes #18864

title: address review findings on debug frame resolution
description:
Follow-up to #18846, which fixed #18754 but left a few loose ends found in review.

That PR changed what `context_depth` means in the environment-state payload: it
now names the frame the browser is halted in rather than being forced to 1 while
stepping. Two client-side predicates still read it as "execution is halted here",
and two source-reference paths needed narrowing.

### Changes

- **Report the browse frame's depth separately.** `context_depth` also follows the
  frame the user selects from the call stack, so it cannot answer "is this the
  executing frame". The payload now carries `browse_frame_depth` alongside it, and
  `EnvironmentObjects.enableClickableObjects()` and the `CodeBrowserNavigationEvent`
  executing flag compare against that instead of hardcoding 1. Without this, clicking
  a data frame in the Environment pane stopped calling `View()` and the code browser
  lost its executing-line arrow whenever the browsed frame was not innermost -- any
  `tryCatch`, `withCallingHandlers` or `suppressWarnings` wrapper, or a Shiny
  reactive. This also fixes the same question being answered wrongly after selecting
  an outer frame from the call stack, which predates #18846.

- **Keep the call-site fallback for a browsed frame that has source of its own.**
  The new branch nulled the srcref unconditionally, including when the function
  carried source references -- reachable when `R_GetCurrentSrcref()` returns the
  `<in-bc-interp>` symbol for byte-compiled code. That sent the client to a deparsed
  copy of the function with an unnavigable filename instead of to the file. #18754
  is about functions with *no* source of their own, so the null-out is now gated on
  that.

- **Resolve the browsed frame to the outermost context sharing the browser
  environment**, matching what `.rs.getFunctionContext` reports to the client. More
  than one context can share an environment -- `eval(expr, envir = <a frame env>)`,
  or top-level code under `source()` -- and the previous per-frame identity test
  marked every one of them current, so the frame the client reads could fall into
  the wrong branch and simulate a wrong line.

- **Repeat the last browser position when a step cannot be resolved.** Suppressing
  the event entirely left the client's requery timer armed; it stalled 500 ms and
  then issued a `requery_context` RPC that resolved to nothing again.

- **Drop `src_context` from `.rs.callFrames`**, which no longer has a reader on the
  C++ side.

- **Assert the trace installed** in the deep-stack e2e test. It asserted
  `FRAME_BUILDS: 0`, which is also what a `trace()` that never installed leaves
  behind, so the test would have kept passing if the regression returned.

### Testing

Added a testthat case covering the restored fallback; it fails on two assertions
with the `hasSourceRefs` gate reverted.

- `rstudio-tests --scope r --filter 'debugger|environment|linter'` -- 205 pass
- `npm run test:desktop-dev -- tests/panes/debugger` -- 33 passed, 5 skipped
- `npm run test:desktop-dev -- tests/panes/environment` -- 9 passed, 3 skipped

No `NEWS.md` entry: this corrects work from #18846, which has not shipped in a
release yet.

title: escape the postgres password in the connection string
Backport four e2e hardening changes to rel-autumn-hawkbit
description:
Follows #18792 and #18795. Test-side only -- no product code changes.

Each of the four commits is cherry-picked from a main-branch PR whose test
half stands on its own. Every touched file is byte-identical to `origin/main`,
so this branch merges forward without conflicts.

| Commit | Upstream | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| `460c3eff` | e2e half of #18785 | `closeProjectIfOpen` reads the visible dialog's text when its wait times out, instead of reporting a bare 30s `waitForFunction` timeout with nothing naming the modal that blocked the close. Returns whether the save-workspace sweep fired. |
| `98680ec0` | #18806 | `requireAiCredentials` probes each provider's services from Node, so a runner that cannot reach Posit AI or GitHub skips those suites instead of failing inside the feature's own timeout. `aiServiceOutageReason()` re-probes after a completion times out, turning a mid-run outage into a skip while a timeout with the service still answering stays a failure. The Posit AI host list includes the install manifest on cdn.posit.co, since a timed-out manifest download leaves the agent NotSignedIn and reads as a completion timeout. |
| `01657cfd` | e2e half of #18797 | The re-requesting wait #18789 gave ghost text becomes `SourcePaneActions.waitForSuggestion`, shared with the next-edit sites and `acceptNesRename`. Those sites previously blocked on a provider that had already answered "No completions available", which is terminal, so a declined context burned the full budget on every platform at once. `openProject` reloads once when the switched-to session never installs the automation bridge -- GWT's bootstrap has no retry, so a failed fetch of the main cache.js leaves the window blank. |
| `bfc94c34` | #18837 | `openProject` observes `ready` and the target project path in one predicate, and `closeProjectIfOpen` gates on `ready` as well. Either helper could otherwise return into a session still finishing deferred initialization. Adds `tests/harness/project-readiness.test.ts`. |

## Not backported

- #18797's `dev-common.ts` GWT gating: local dev launchers only, never run in CI.
- Specs added or changed alongside product fixes not on this branch (#18805, #18812, #18827, #18846, and #18785's `close_project_after_open.test.ts`).
- The vimrc lazy-vim-module guard, which only matters after #18716's startup work.
- #18856 sandbox license scrub, #18655 run-environment reporting, and the
  `actions/upload-artifact` v4-to-v7 pins.
- `Jenkinsfile.windows` `--scope core` to `core,rsession`, which adds tests rather
  than stabilizing existing ones.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` in `e2e/rstudio` is clean.
- `tests/harness/project-readiness.test.ts` runs standalone: 2 passed at HEAD;
  both fail when `commands.ts` and `project.ts` are reverted to their parent, so
  it guards the change rather than restating it.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflicts.
