title: Use session-info callbacks for startup data consumers
description:
### Intent

Follow up on #18858 by using `Session.withSessionInfo()` for other startup consumers that only need session data. Exception-based readiness checks can skip initialization when data arrives later, while event-only listeners can miss initialization when constructed after the event.

### Approach

Adopt the helper in seven places: editor keybindings, Console language setup, Chat satellite restoration, workbench lists, Assistant state, error-handler state, and Desktop session settings. Each initializes once when session data is available. Remove the redundant event handlers, broad catches used for readiness, and unused dependencies.

Keep lifecycle handlers that coordinate pane activation or depend on preferences and other workbench initialization. The helper guarantees data availability, not completion of workbench startup.

### Automated Tests

- Added four GWT regressions for workbench lists and error-handler state, covering construction before and after session initialization and subsequent state updates. All four passed, along with both existing `SessionTests` (six tests total).
- Java compilation and a GWT draft build passed.
- All four Windows Desktop checks passed: the three Console editor-keybinding regressions and the startup smoke test.

### QA Notes

Check reloads with saved editor shortcuts, active Python console mode, a detached Chat pane, and saved workbench lists/error-handler selection. Confirm later list and error-handler changes still update the UI.

### Documentation

Internal initialization cleanup; no user-facing documentation or NEWS entry.

title: Fix multipart payload terminator and form parser resume contract
description:
Addresses #18727 — the parser items deferred from #18726.

This also upstreams rstudio-pro#12420 ("some test cleanups", Jeffrey Vroom), which fixed the flaky test independently on 2026-08-25 and never made it to open source — which is why the issue still listed it as open. Where that PR and this one solved the same problem, this takes its implementation verbatim so the merge back into pro stays small.

### Terminator omitted from payload

`parseMultipartForm()` built its `string_view` of the body ending just before the closing `\r\n--boundary--`, which left the final part unterminated and working only because `BoundaryFinder` tolerates a missing terminator. The view now includes it.

This is a fidelity change with no behavioral effect, which is what the issue asked for. `BoundaryFinder` anchors its match at the same CRLF whether or not the terminator bytes are in the view, so the parts come out byte-identical; the only difference is a trailing zero-length token that gets skipped for having no `Content-Disposition`. There is correspondingly no new test — nothing observable changed to pin. The existing tests, including the 2 MB random-payload ones that compare contents exactly, cover the no-regression side.

### Flaky `ComplicatedFormParsingWorksRandomByteBoundaries`

Real, and it reproduces. `RequestParser::parse()` saves an offset into the chunk it just consumed and resumes from it, so a caller has to re-invoke with that exact same buffer; all three connection handlers (`AsyncConnectionImpl`, `SessionHttpConnectionImpl`, `SessionNamedPipeHttpConnectionListener`) do, and say so in comments.

`FormTester::parseBytes` did not. After `headers_parsed` it kept the same start pointer but recomputed the end from a fresh `rand() % 8192 + 1`. When that block came up shorter than the header block, `begin += bufferPos_` landed past `end`, `copyRangeToBuffer`'s `std::distance` went negative, the unsigned `neededCapacity` wrapped to ~2^64 and `reserve()` threw `std::length_error`:

```
[ RUN      ] HttpTest.ComplicatedFormParsingWorksRandomByteBoundaries
unknown file: Failure
C++ exception with description "basic_string" thrown in the test body.
```

The harness now holds the chunk back until the parser has consumed it, on both `headers_parsed` and `pause`. The test also drew from `rand()` unseeded while `Base64Tests` calls `::srand(1)` and `::srand(42)`, so its block sizes depended on test ordering; it now uses a self-contained `mt19937` with an `RSTUDIO_TEST_SEED` override for reproducing a failure locally. Both are pro#12420's implementation.

`parse()` enforces the contract rather than just documenting it. It records the length of the range the offset was saved against and requires the replay to match, then reports a mismatch and returns `error` — matching how the existing max-content-length check reports a request it cannot parse. An opaque `std::length_error` from inside `std::string` was not an actionable way to learn you had replayed the wrong buffer, and a replay that merely cleared the offset while dropping the tail did not raise anything at all: it returned `incomplete` with those body bytes silently gone.

This is the one place that deliberately diverges from pro#12420, which compares against `bufferPos_` alone and so accepts the tail-dropping case. It keeps that PR's comment and message wording so the difference on merge is the comparison itself.

All five resume paths already comply — the recursive `handleRead`, `requestFilterContinuation`, the posted resume off `bytesTransferred_`, `SessionHttpConnectionImpl`, and the named pipe loop, which sets `skipWrite` so `buff` and `bytesRead` survive.

### Added coverage

- `FormParsingRejectsShrinkingResumeBuffer` — pro#12420's test, unchanged; still passes against the stricter check.
- `FormParsingRejectsTruncatedBufferOnResume` — a resume that clears the offset but drops the tail is rejected. Returns `incomplete`, losing the tail, without the length check.
- `FormParsingResumesAfterPause` — a pause/resume round trip, which had no coverage at all. `FormTester` models `FormProxy`'s contract, where a handler returning `false` has not consumed the data and expects redelivery.
- `FormParsingResumesWithSmallerChunksAfterHeaders` — big chunk finishes the headers, every chunk after it is far smaller. Throws without the harness fix.
- `FormParsingKeepsFirstFileForDuplicateFieldName` — two files under one field name, first wins.
- `FormParsingNestedBoundaryIsPrefixOfOuter` / `FormParsingOuterBoundaryIsPrefixOfNested` — a nested multipart whose boundary is a prefix of the outer one, and the mirror case. Both directions already worked; these prove it.

### Not in this PR

- Percent-encoded filenames — split out to #18854. Browsers escape only `%0A`/`%0D`/`%22` and leave `%` alone, so decoding is not reversible and non-browser clients escape nothing; picking a behavior is its own decision.
- The duplicated multipart code in `SessionFiles.cpp` — still tracked by #18727. It streams chunks to a temp file as they arrive while `parseMultipartForm()` needs the whole body buffered, so sharing an implementation means writing a streaming multipart parser.

### Testing

`rstudio-core-tests` passes: 726 tests, 22 in `HttpTest.*Form*`. The 10 skips are the usual environment gates (postgres, root, Darwin ACLs). Full `cmake --build . --target all` is clean.

`git merge-tree` against current `rstudio-pro` main: conflicts in this PR's files go from 2 to 1, and the one left is the comparison above.

### Note for the rstudio-pro merge

`git merge-tree` against pro main at `7bab52e56`: the only conflict in this PR's files is the resume comparison in `RequestParser.hpp` described above. Resolve it toward this side — pro's `< bufferPos_` accepts a replay that drops the tail. `RequestParserTests.cpp` merges clean.

(The unrelated `.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml` conflict is pre-existing divergence from other commits, not this PR.)

One known defect is deliberately left alone here: in `parseBytes`, `parseIter + count` forms a pointer past the end before the clamp catches it. It is pre-existing and identical in both repos, test-only, and invisible to the build's only sanitizer option (opt-in ASan, which does not implement `-fsanitize=pointer-overflow`). Fixing it in open source would have re-conflicted `RequestParserTests.cpp`; since that file is byte-identical in both repos once this lands, it is cheaper to fix once in pro afterward and correct both copies.

title: Fix Windows compilation of source database lock tests
description:
### Intent

Fix the Windows C++ build failure introduced by #18853 and observed in [the Windows build for #18859](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/35180249606/job/105070798382). `FreshAdvisoryLockTest` places `#ifndef _WIN32` inside the argument list of `INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P`, producing MSVC errors C2121 and C2065. Preprocessor directives inside macro arguments have undefined behavior under C++20, so this is a portability bug in the test code.

### Approach

Build the supported lock types in `freshAdvisoryLockTypes()` and pass them through `testing::ValuesIn`, following the existing `lockTypes()` pattern. This moves the conditional outside the macro invocation and preserves the parameter sets: advisory locking on Windows, and advisory plus link-based locking on other platforms.

### Automated Tests

- Reproduced the failure by syntax-compiling the complete unmodified `SessionSourceDatabaseSupervisorTests.cpp` with MSVC 14.51.36231, C++20, and the existing local session build definitions and includes: exit 2 with the same C2121/C2065 errors as CI.
- Syntax-compiled the complete modified test file with the same compiler and settings: exit 0.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing test cases are preserved; no new runtime test is needed for this compilation fix. The full build and test execution remain for CI.

### QA Notes

Confirm the Windows build succeeds and the source database lock tests remain registered on all platforms. No UI changes.

### Documentation

No documentation or NEWS entry is needed for this test compilation regression on main.

title: protect source recovery ownership and isolate session tests
description:
### Intent

Improve the source-recovery behavior discussed in #18744 and #18746 with source-database ownership checks, test-launcher isolation, and failure handling for headless script startup. Sessions using different lock types must not mistake each other's live recovery data for abandoned documents.

### Approach

- Check both advisory and link-based ownership before recovering or reusing a source directory. Report an explanatory startup error on contention, including contention encountered during acquisition.
- Stop `--run-script` on initialization errors with a nonzero exit status and abnormal cleanup, so scripts cannot continue after source-database ownership checks fail. Log the error and exit directly to avoid Windows modal fatal-error dialogs.
- Preserve adopted documents when acquiring their lock fails. Continue tolerating explicitly unsupported locking, including advisory probes on filesystems that support only link-based locking; propagate other errors.
- Retry ambiguous empty lock files until they expire or their ownership becomes clear, with a maximum wait of 30 seconds per directory. This handles recently released advisory locks without treating an unfinished link-lock publication as abandoned.
- Give each C++ session-test and R-test scope fresh data/config directories on Unix and Windows. Use GUID-based directory names on Windows to avoid repeated cmd random sequences. Create the migration sentinel before startup so legacy user state is not moved into the temporary test directory; stop if setup fails.

Desktop/Server recovery namespaces and persistent-document sharing remain follow-up work in #18746. This change does not establish an atomic ownership-transfer protocol for older binaries. A moved, released symlink lock can still prevent advisory takeover; the documents are preserved and a link-based session can recover them.

### Automated Tests

Validated on macOS arm64:

- Built `rsession` and `rstudio-core-tests`.
- Source-database regression tests: **38 passed**, covering mixed lock types, recovery/reuse, acquisition failures, recent advisory release, unsupported advisory probes, and incomplete link publication.
- Existing file-lock tests: **73 passed, 2 skipped** (root-only ACL coverage and a case-sensitive-filesystem test).
- Shell syntax and `git diff --check` passed.

Additional ad hoc Windows launcher checks used stub session executables: **4 passed, 1 Unix-only check skipped**. These covered inherited state, combined scopes, repeated invocations, and temporary-directory creation failure. GUID-generation failure was also verified to prevent startup in both session scopes. `git diff --check` passed.

Focused Windows startup regressions passed through `rstudio-tests.bat --scope r --filter script-startup`: **2 test cases, 9 assertions passed**, with no warnings or skips. The success case executes its script; a source-database initialization failure exits with status 1 without executing the script. These tests use isolated child environments and clear inherited POSIX locale settings on Windows.

For this validation, `RScriptCallbacks.cpp` was rebuilt and relinked against existing local Windows build objects in an isolated directory. This does not validate the complete PR's Windows lock/recovery changes. The new startup tests have not been run on macOS or Linux, and the full unrelated test suite has not been run.

### QA Notes

- With Desktop and Server configured to use different lock types, keep unsaved documents in one session and launch the other. The live session's source directory and contents should remain intact.
- A second session targeting an owned recovery directory should show a startup error explaining that the recovery data is locked.
- Run a headless script with source-database initialization blocked. It should log the error, exit with failure, and leave the script unexecuted.
- Check rapid restart/recovery with advisory locking. A recently created empty lock file may delay startup while its ambiguity expires, up to the limit described above.
- Run the `rsession` and `r` test scopes with inherited data/config settings; each scope should use fresh temporary state and preserve the user's existing state.
- Verify the Windows launcher in Windows CI or a Windows development environment.

### Documentation

Added a NEWS entry linked to #18744.

### Checklist

- [x] Includes a linked `NEWS.md` entry.
- [x] Relevant local regression tests pass.
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned.
- [ ] Full Windows lock/recovery runtime verification is complete.

title: show the R version in the console pane at startup
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18857.

Show the Console pane's R version as soon as session info is available, without waiting for an RPC queued behind R startup work.

### Approach

- Add `Session.withSessionInfo()`: invoke the callback immediately when session info exists, otherwise register a one-time `SessionInitEvent` handler and remove it before invoking the callback.
- Initialize the console's cached R version through that helper and remove the exception-based readiness checks.
- Refresh the cached value after R restarts and transitions back from Python. Later refreshes display the last known version instead of rereading the startup snapshot, and RPC failures preserve that value.

### Validation

- Java compilation and a GWT draft build passed.
- Both new `SessionTests` passed, covering immediate callbacks, deferred callbacks, and listener removal.
- E2E TypeScript checking passed.
- Both Windows Desktop regression tests passed, checking that startup sends no version RPC, a delayed refresh applies a distinct returned version, and a subsequent RPC error retains the refreshed value. The test uses real server responses to accommodate Electron's HTTP interception behavior and holds the restart-completion ping until the new session is ready.

title: fix source navigation when debugging nested package functions
description:
### Intent

Closes #18754. When `lm()` is called inside a function, `debugonce(lm)` or stepping into it with `s` can leave the editor showing the caller's source. The debugger now opens the generated `lm` source and highlights the correct statements as execution advances.

### Approach

Prevent functions without source references from inheriting the caller's location, either through `R_GetCurrentSrcref()` or the source reference on their own call. Preserve real references for primitive evaluation and top-level source contexts. Use the same resolved or simulated reference for context changes and subsequent stepping.

### Automated Tests

Added five Playwright E2E tests covering direct debugging, wrappers loaded from a file or defined in the console, stepping into `lm`, and source navigation inside `evalq` in a local environment. The tests check the displayed source and the highlighted statements.

Validation on macOS Desktop with R 4.6.1:

- Before the fix, all three wrapper scenarios failed against RStudio 2026.09.0+175; direct debugging and the `evalq` control passed.
- With the fix, the complete debugger E2E suite passed: **25 passed, 2 skipped**. Both skips are existing package-build-cycle placeholders.
- C++ session and GWT builds, TypeScript typechecking, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The full local unit-test suite was not run; Windows, Linux, and Server validation remain for CI/QA.

### QA Notes

Define `fit_lm <- function(data) { lm(mpg ~ wt, data = data) }`, then run `debugonce(lm); fit_lm(mtcars)`. Confirm the editor shows `lm` and that successive `n` commands highlight `ret.x <- x`, `ret.y <- y`, and `cl <- match.call()`.

Repeat by running `debugonce(fit_lm); fit_lm(mtcars)`, advancing to the `lm` call with `n`, and stepping into it with `s`. Check both console-defined and file-sourced wrappers. Ordinary source-file breakpoints and debugging inside `evalq` should retain their source locations.

### Documentation

Added a NEWS entry linked to #18754.

- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards (no new UI controls or layout changes)

title: Scrub license files from sandbox and add an optional globalSetup extension
description:
`scrubCredentials()` removes every provider's credential material from each sandbox `user-home*` before a sandbox is left on disk, so a preserved sandbox never carries real tokens. This adds `.lic` files under each home's license directory to the same sweep, using the existing `remove` closure so a file that can't be deleted surfaces in the same warning as a credential that can't.

Also adds an optional extension point to globalSetup. If `utils/license` resolves, it's called to prepare sandbox state ahead of the warmup launch; it isn't present here, so nothing happens. This lets a downstream copy of this directory add its own setup step without modifying a file that merges from here.

title: keep quarto renders running when source tabs close
description:
### Intent

Closing a Quarto document while a render is running with **(No Preview)** cancels the render and removes its background job. Let these one-shot renders finish and retain their result when the source tab closes, Close All is used, or the client reloads.

Fixes #18799.

### Approach

Skip preview cleanup in both source-document removal handlers when the job is render-only. Use the job's mode captured at launch so changing the preview preference during a render does not change its lifetime. Preview and Shiny servers retain their existing cleanup behavior, as do job replacement and Windows shutdown/suspend.

### Automated Tests

Added E2E coverage that holds a render at a file-based checkpoint, closes its tab or all tabs (or reloads the client), then releases the render and verifies output creation and a retained Succeeded job. The tab-close case also changes the preview preference while rendering. Additional checks verify preview and Shiny jobs are removed when their source closes.

Validation on macOS Desktop:

- All 8 tests in `quarto_render_no_preview.test.ts` and `quarto.test.ts` passed.
- C++ session build and `npm run typecheck` passed.
- The tab-close regression reproduced the cancellation with the unpatched session.

### QA Notes

Render a Quarto document containing a slow R chunk with **(No Preview)** selected, then close its source tab or use Close All before it finishes. The render should produce its output and remain in Background Jobs as Succeeded. Closing a document running a preview or Shiny server should still stop and remove that job.

### Documentation

Added a `NEWS.md` entry linked to #18799.

### Checklist

- [x] NEWS entry with an issue link
- [x] Regression E2E coverage
- [x] Relevant local build, typecheck, and E2E checks pass

title: make the data viewer robust against masked generics and invalid text
description:
Two ways `View()` could fail outright, both landing in the column-width hint that `.rs.describeCols()` computes without a guard. Reported from a UCLA class on Posit Cloud (2026.07.1) using the `mobilizr` package.

### Masked summary generics (#18842)

`tools:rstudio` is attached at position 2 during session init, so later `library()` calls sit above it -- but a package attached from `.Rprofile` ends up *below* it, and then our own unqualified calls resolve to that package's replacements.

`mobilizr` exports a `range()` whose `...` is forwarded into a call that already fixes `na.rm`:

```r
range <- function(x, ...) {
  if (any(is.na(mosaic::mean(x = x, na.rm = FALSE, ...)))) { ... }
  mosaic::range(x = x, ..., na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

so `colMaxChars()`'s integer branch, which calls `range(col, na.rm = TRUE)`, died with:

```
Error in mean_(x = x, na.rm = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) :
  formal argument "na.rm" matched by multiple actual arguments
```

The double branch calls `range(finiteCol)` with no `na.rm`, so it never duplicates -- which is why converting the integer columns to double was a working workaround, and why a frame with no integer columns was fine.

Fixed by namespace-qualifying the summary generics on the `View()` path, including `.rs.digest()` in `Tools.R`, which is reached through the column fingerprint and was the first site to blow up.

### Invalid multibyte text (#18843)

```r
View(data.frame(x = c("ok", "caf\xe9")))
# Error in nchar(col, type = "width") : invalid multibyte string, element 2
```

`nchar(type = "width")` throws on text that is invalid in the session encoding. Now called with `allowNA = TRUE`, reporting no hint when an element cannot be measured so the client falls back to sampling. A regression from #17382, present 2026.05 through main; also hits `mobilizr::nutrition`.

### Also

The hint's call site is now wrapped in `.rs.tryOr()`. It only drives initial column sizing, so no failure there should be able to take down the grid.

### Testing

Two regression tests in `test-dataviewer.R`: one attaching a masking environment below `tools:rstudio` and asserting the integer column still gets its histogram, width hint and summary; one describing a frame with invalid UTF-8 in a character column and in factor levels. Both fail against unfixed sources and pass with the change; full `--scope r --filter dataviewer` suite is green (258 passing), as is `--filter linter`.

Verified separately that `View()` on the reporter's actual data (`mobilizr::atus`, with mobilizr attached ahead of `tools:rstudio`) reproduces the reported error before the change and succeeds after.

Fixes #18842.
Fixes #18843.

title: Apply queued ConfigFileBacked commands when the read settles instead of giving up
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

Custom **application** keyboard shortcuts saved in `keybindings/rstudio_bindings.json` are sometimes not applied when a session starts: the file is read correctly, but the shortcut never gets attached to the `AppCommand` or the keymap until another editor opens or the page reloads. `ConfigFileBacked.execute()` waited for its `read_config_json` RPC by polling a 20 ms `Timer`, and silently dropped the queued command if the read had not settled within ~100 polls. `ApplicationCommandManager.loadBindings()` is only re-triggered by `EditorLoadedEvent`, which since #18716 fires from the console editor while rsession may still be busy initializing -- if the read settles after the poll budget expires (an `asyncHandle` completed later over the event stream, or a saturated renderer main thread), the bindings load into `object_` but the command to apply them is never run. Fixes #18847.

### Approach

Replace the polling `Timer` and its 100-poll give-up with a pending-command queue: `execute()` queues the command and starts the read (`load()` already guards against a second read while one is in flight); both `onResponseReceived` and `onError` already mark the object loaded, so flushing the queue from both of them means nothing is ever dropped, whether the read succeeds or fails.

This is a small, deliberate behavior change: commands that used to be silently dropped after ~2s now always run, just possibly later than before. All three callers of `ConfigFileBacked` -- `ApplicationCommandManager`, `EditorCommandManager`, `AddinsCommandManager` -- are idempotent binding loaders, so running late instead of not at all is the intended fix. `git blame` puts the give-up in the original `FileBacked.java`; #18716 only made it reachable at startup by moving `initializeWorkbench()` earlier.

I considered also adding a `SessionInitEvent` re-trigger to `ApplicationCommandManager`, mirroring #18797's fix for the sibling `EditorCommandManager`, but left it out: it would not have fixed this on its own (the drop happens after any such trigger fires), and it isn't needed once the drop itself is gone.

### Automated Tests

Added `ConfigFileBackedTests`, a new GWT unit test that stubs `FilesServerOperations` to capture the `readConfigJSON` callback instead of answering it, so the queue/flush behavior can be exercised deterministically without a real Timer: a command queued before the read settles doesn't run until `onResponseReceived`/`onError` fires (with the right value in each case), `execute()` after loading runs synchronously, multiple queued commands all run in order, and a second `execute()` while a read is in flight doesn't issue a second RPC. I confirmed these tests fail against the reverted (unfixed) polling implementation and pass with the fix.

Also verified against the real end-to-end symptom on a build containing this fix: a fresh user with `keybindings/rstudio_bindings.json` set and a `Sys.sleep(6)` in `.Rprofile` to simulate a slow session start, both before and after the fix.

Verified locally (macOS arm64, via the project's `devbase:autumn-hawkbit-jammy-arm64` container, since GWT deps aren't installed on this host):
- `ant javac` -- compiles
- `ant unittest` -- full suite green, `OK (590 tests)`, including the new `ConfigFileBackedTests`
- Reverting only `ConfigFileBacked.java` and rerunning `ant unittest` fails all 5 new tests (`BUILD FAILED`, `Tests run: 590, Failures: 5`), confirming they are load-bearing

### QA Notes

Reproduction recipe is in #18847.

### Documentation

None -- internal behavior fix, no user-facing documentation to update.

### Checklist

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` -- N/A: this bug was introduced by unreleased #18716 (2026.10 dailies only), and the repo's own NEWS.md guidance excludes bugs introduced since the last release.
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility) -- N/A, no UI change.
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)

title: Don't re-add PATH entries that are already in effect
description:
When a terminal is restored after a session restart, its saved `PATH` is reloaded and the non-PATH git and svn bin dirs are appended again, so each restart added another copy of each.

`core::system::addToPath` now leaves the `PATH` unchanged when appending an entry that is already present, or prepending the entry that is already first; neither addition could change which program is found. Empty entries are always added, since TeX relies on a trailing separator. The terminal's own check for the postback scripts dir is removed, as `addToPath` now covers it.

`core::system::addToSystemPath` had the same problem. Its only caller adds the TinyTeX bin dir when `pdflatex` isn't found, and Restart R and suspend/resume restore the saved `PATH` before that runs again, so a TinyTeX bin dir without a runnable `pdflatex` gained a copy each cycle. That caller now uses `addToPath`, and `addToSystemPath` is removed; rstudio-pro has no other callers.

Entries are compared as exact strings, so on Windows the same directory written with different case or slashes is still treated as distinct.

New `EnvironmentTest` cases cover appending a present entry, whole-entry matching, prepending, and empty entries.

Fixes #18777.

title: test whole-project quarto rendering without preview
description:
### Intent

Closes #18798. The existing no-preview tests cover individual Quarto documents but do not exercise building a whole website through `QuartoPreview`.

### Approach

Add a separate project suite in `quarto_render_no_preview.test.ts`. Seed a minimal website before opening its RStudio project so startup detects the Quarto configuration, set `rmd_viewer_type` to `none`, and invoke `buildAll`. Assert that the Background Jobs pane shows a successful `Render: <project>` job rather than a preview job and that `_site/index.html` exists. Teardown closes the project and clears the preference.

### Automated Tests

- macOS arm64: all four tests in `quarto_render_no_preview.test.ts` passed against this worktree's freshly built session and GWT UI (44.1 seconds).
- `npm run typecheck` and `git diff --check` passed.
- `ant draft` and the `rsession` / `rpostback` CMake targets built successfully.
- Roborev Refine branch review passed with no findings; no LOW findings were ignored.

The initial run against an older local session binary failed both the existing single-file test and the new project test because that binary still started preview servers. Both passed after rebuilding the session. Windows, Linux, and Server were not run locally.

### QA Notes

The new test covers website project detection, the Build command, render-job completion, HTML output, and project teardown. The fixture has no executable code chunks.

### Documentation

Test coverage only; no user-facing behavior, documentation, or NEWS changes.

title: Read the chat pane Content-Security-Policy from the installation being served
description:
`loadCspDirectives()` cached `dist/csp.json` in a function-local static, so the
directives were read once and kept for the session. Updating Posit Assistant
from the chat pane stops the backend, installs, then restarts it and reloads
the UI, which re-reads nothing: the new client was served under the previous
version's Content-Security-Policy until RStudio itself was restarted. A version
needing a directive the old one did not -- another `connect-src` origin, an
`img-src`, a worker or font source -- has it blocked by the browser, and the
chat pane is broken with nothing connecting it to the update the user just
accepted.

## What the code does now

The directives are read on every header rebuild, and a rebuild happens whenever
RStudio changes what it serves:

- `setChatBackendPort()` rebuilds, as it already did, so every backend start
  re-reads `csp.json` from the installation that start resolved.
- `setInstallationPath()` now rebuilds too, so the policy follows the
  installation rather than depending on callers pairing the two. Uninstall did
  not pair them -- it stops the backend, which rebuilds while the pin is still
  set, and clears the pin afterwards -- so a user-level install removed while a
  system-wide or bundled copy remained served that copy's assets under the
  removed installation's policy for the rest of the session.
- The rebuild holds `s_cspMutex` across the read as well as the store, so the
  rebuild that commits last is also the one that read last. Without it, a lazy
  rebuild on an HTTP handler thread racing the first backend start could commit
  the older installation's directives last, with `s_cspHeaderBuilt` set so
  nothing rebuilt it until the next restart.

The header string itself is still cached, so this is one small file read per
backend start rather than per request. Lock ordering is unchanged:
`s_cspMutex` -> `s_installationMutex` is the only direction taken, and
`setInstallationPath()` releases the installation lock before rebuilding.

## Why the read is tied to the backend start

Keying the cache on the installation path -- the option #18831 suggests --
would not fix this. `installPackage()` moves `pai/bin` to `ai.prev` and
extracts into `pai/bin`, so the path a restart pins is unchanged and a
path-keyed cache stays stale. Tying the read to the events that change what is
served is correct both for that and for the versioned layout of #18658, where
the path does change.

What remains outside this fix is a third party replacing the pinned directory
in place, which triggers neither event -- an administrator upgrading a
system-wide install under live sessions. That is recorded in #18658, which also
carries the follow-up to derive the policy from the same per-request resolution
as the asset root.

## Testing

`rstudio-tests --scope rsession`: 583 pass. Three new tests on the existing
`ChatStaticFilesPin` harness, each confirmed to fail without the change:

- `csp.json` overwritten in place under an unchanged pin, which is what an
  in-session update does today. A test that swapped directories instead would
  pass even with a path-keyed cache.
- A restart onto a different installation, which is what a versioned install
  will do.
- A pin change with no port change, which is the uninstall case.

The fixture now also clears the backend port, and its comment records that both
setters rebuild from whatever is resolvable on the machine running the tests,
so a test asserting on the header has to pin an installation of its own.

Fixes #18831.

title: Add an orientation diagram to the e2e auth-credentials skill doc
description:
The `auth-credentials.md` skill doc opens straight into details -- credential
paths, the SQLite child-process read, the SIGTERM scrub -- with nothing that
orients a reader first. This adds a short "How the pieces fit" section at the
top: an ASCII diagram tracing the flow from each provider's `setup()` block
through the sandbox user-home to the credential gate and the tests, plus two
paragraphs on how the pieces couple.

The point it makes explicit is that nothing calls a provisioner and nothing
imports from `auth.setup.ts`. The credential store on disk is the entire
contract between the setup project and everything downstream, which is why
the gate re-reads it rather than trusting what setup reported.

Docs only -- no test or product code changes.

title: Add a macOS 27 arm64 e2e test engine and schedule it
description:
Adds a per-OS E2E engine for macOS 27 arm64 and wires it into the scheduled rotation.

GitHub ships macOS 27 only under the Xcode-versioned label `xcode-27` -- there's no `macos-27` alias -- so that's what `runs-on` says, while the file and job are named for the OS under test to match the macOS 14 and 15 siblings. `xcode-27` is the free standard arm64 runner, not the billed `-xlarge` variant. The image is still a public preview, and the header comment records what to change when GitHub promotes it to GA.

The engine is patterned on the macOS 26 engine, with every cache key, sccache prefix, artifact name, and report label version-scoped to `macos27`. That scoping isn't cosmetic: on the Sunday cron all five macOS and Windows engines run as reusable workflows inside one caller run and share a single artifact namespace, so unscoped names would have had macOS 27 download macOS 26's binary and report it as macOS 27 results.

Scheduling is twice a week. The `ENGINES` entry puts it in the Sunday 16:00 UTC macOS+Windows run, and it's also in the Tuesday 08:00 weekday slate.

Validated with a real run on this branch before the temporary push trigger was removed: 743 passed, 0 failed, 39 skipped, 4 flaky, against the Blue Mistflower daily. Both `runs-on` jobs picked up runners within seconds, so the preview label provisions normally.

Deliberately not included, since the issue defers them: no PR-gate wiring, no certification-matrix cell, and no cache-seed workflow. The last of those matches every rotation-only engine, where nobody's blocked on a nightly run and a cold cache only costs run time.

This PR also drops the hardcoded engine counts from the rotation's comments. They went stale twice during this change alone, and correcting them generates review noise for no benefit, so the comments now describe the structure without asserting a number. Counts pinned to something other than engine population -- trigger types, cron slots, architectures -- are left alone.

Addresses #18821.

title: wait for project session readiness before continuing e2e tests
description:
### Intent

Fix premature returns from the project-switch E2E helpers found while investigating [the macOS assistant/restart failure in PR #18828](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/35026625600/job/104580004251).

`closeProjectIfOpen()` could return when the new session reported no active project but had not completed deferred initialization. A subsequent `openProject()` could observe that outgoing session's `ready` flag, then the replacement session's project path, and return before the replacement was ready. The recorded first close returned before the no-project assistant backend finished starting; the next close hung.

### Approach

- Require readiness and the expected project identity in the same browser evaluation, for both open and close.
- Check console idle after the replacement session is ready, rather than accepting the outgoing session's idle console.
- Keep the existing session timeouts and modal handling.

This fixes confirmed helper races. The original macOS hang lost its trace during watchdog shutdown, so the change is not yet proof that every cause of the #18394 session-transition failure is resolved.

### Automated Tests

- Two controlled browser lifecycle regressions: both fail against the original helpers with `ready === false`, and both pass with this change.
- The close regression also delays the new session's idle console until after readiness.
- `close_project_after_open.test.ts`: passed against the original macOS PR build (99.9.9-pr+1027, R 4.6.1), using the fixed helper.
- `npm run typecheck` and `git diff --check` passed.

### QA Notes

Run `restart-under-agent.test.ts` on macOS with Posit Assistant active, plus the project open/close suites. Confirm that all restart cycles complete without the heartbeat watchdog firing. The local machine has no Posit Assistant credential store, so the authenticated restart scenario remains for CI; the ordinary project-close check above did not enable the assistant.

### Documentation

Test harness change only; no user documentation or NEWS entry needed.

title: stabilize terminal selection during xterm redraws
description:
### Intent

Fix the terminal clipboard test failure in [PR #18828's E2E run](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/35026625600/job/104585109222). Both Windows attempts found the expected text, then failed before pressing Ctrl+Shift+C because the row span no longer had a bounding box.

### Approach

xterm replaces row spans during redraws. Read the word position and cell geometry in one browser evaluation so a redraw cannot detach the span between separate Playwright calls. Retry selection with fresh coordinates if the output moves before the double-click. Keep the clipboard-content assertions unchanged.

### Automated Tests

- Chromium stress test using RStudio's bundled xterm DOM renderer with continuous redraws: the original helper failed 8/100 attempts; the new helper selected the exact word in 100/100 attempts.
- `terminal_clipboard.test.ts`: both copy and paste passed against the original macOS PR build (99.9.9-pr+1027, R 4.6.1), using the fixed test.
- `npm run typecheck` and `git diff --check` passed.

### QA Notes

Run `terminal_clipboard.test.ts` on Windows, including both copy and paste cases. The local stress test covers selection in Chromium; cross-platform RStudio clipboard behavior remains covered by E2E CI.

### Documentation

Test harness change only; no user documentation or NEWS entry needed.

title: Make XdgTest.DirectoryResolution hermetic against ambient XDG env vars
description:
userConfigDir/userDataDir/userCacheDir consult RSTUDIO_*_HOME/XDG_*_HOME env vars ahead of any explicitly-supplied home directory - intentional, documented precedence, exercised deliberately by the EnvironmentOverrides test right below this one. DirectoryResolution instead asserts on the explicit-home-dir fallback path, but never accounted for those same env vars being set in the ambient environment: if they are, resolution takes the env-var branch instead of the explicit-home-dir branch this test means to exercise, and the assertions fail against whatever those vars resolve to instead of the expected path under s_defaultHome.

Add a ScopedEnvUnset RAII guard - the unset counterpart to the existing EnvironmentScope helper used elsewhere in this file, which only ever sets a variable to a given value - and use it to clear the six vars Xdg.cpp consults for config/data/cache resolution for the duration of this test.

title: Revert running all test scopes on Windows CI
description:
### Intent

Windows CI is red. #18822 dropped the `--scope core,rsession` restriction so `rstudio-tests.bat` runs every scope, including `r`, which needs testthat. #18830 tried to install testthat into the Windows docker image and instead broke the image build. Revert both to get Windows builds green again.

### Approach

Revert #18830, then #18822, restoring `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows`, `dependencies/common/install-packages.cmd`, and `dependencies/windows/install-dependencies.cmd` to their pre-#18822 state.

#18830 could not have worked. `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.windows` installs R 3.6.3, and:

- CRAN serves no Windows binaries below `bin/windows/contrib/4.0`; `contrib/3.6/PACKAGES` is a 404.
- Current sources need a newer R anyway — testthat 3.3.2 and purrr 1.2.2 require R >= 4.1.0, rlang 1.3.0 requires R >= 4.0.0.

So `install.packages()` left the package list unsatisfied, the `stop()` #18830 added on missing packages failed the `RUN install-dependencies.cmd` layer, and the image build failed. In hourly build 2332 — triggered 33 seconds after the merge — the `windows` cell of `Rebuild Docker Images` failed, but `Setup and Trigger Builds` ran regardless, so `windows-pipeline` 3858 built against the unchanged `jenkins/ide:windows-x86_64-blue-mistflower-msvc145` tag and the `r` scope failed exactly as before.

Getting the `r` scope onto Windows CI needs either a newer R in the image or package versions pinned to ones that still support R 3.6. Reopening #17825 to track that.

Two adjacent problems found while diagnosing this, not addressed here:

- `Setup and Trigger Builds` in `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.build` does not depend on `Rebuild Docker Images` succeeding, so any failed rebuild silently ships platform builds against a stale image.
- The `rhel8` cell of the same rebuild also failed, at a boost header copy. Unrelated to these commits and still unexplained.

### Automated Tests

None; CI configuration and image provisioning only. Verified the reverted tree is byte-identical to the pre-#18822 state for all three files.

### QA Notes

None.

### Documentation

title: respect rprofile graphics options and honor dev.args in notebooks
description:
## Summary

Follow-ups to #2142 (aliased plots on Windows). The Windows "(Default)" graphics backend stays the GDI device, to avoid surprising existing users; these changes make the existing Graphics preferences easier to use and to configure site-wide.

Fixes #9275. Addresses #2142. Addresses #4067.

## Changes

- **Rprofile values are respected (#9275).** The session mirrored the `graphics_backend` / `graphics_antialiasing` preferences onto `RStudioGD.backend` / `RStudioGD.antialias` unconditionally at startup, after `Rprofile.site` had run, so `options(RStudioGD.backend = "cairo")` there was always overwritten by the "default" preference value. `SessionGraphics.cpp` now remembers the last value it wrote: a value found in the option that RStudio didn't write is treated as what "(Default)" resolves to. An explicit preference still wins, and switching back to "(Default)" restores the profile's value.
- **Notebooks honor `dev.args` (#4067).** Inline chunk output read only the knitr `dev` chunk option, so `dev.args = list(type = "cairo")` worked when knitting but was ignored inline. The option is now passed through to the notebook graphics device (flat or per-device forms), and through the replay that re-renders plots when the editor is resized.
- **Resized notebook plots keep the backend preference.** The replay runs in a vanilla R process where `RStudioGD.backend` is unset; the device-argument code treated that as an override and cleared the `type` argument carried by the preference, so resized plots fell back to the default device.
- **Preferences note.** Global Options > General > Graphics shows a note that the Windows device antialiases text only, suggesting Cairo or AGG, when that device is selected or is the session's default.

Docs for the preference, `rstudio-prefs.json`, and the Rprofile route are in rstudio/rstudio-pro#12779.

## Tests

- New `test-graphics.R`: for both preferences, an option set as an R profile would is kept when the preference is saved at "default", overridden by an explicit preference, and restored when switching back.
- `test-notebook.R`: device-argument resolution covers preference-only, backend option, chunk `dev.args` precedence, per-device lists, multiple devices, malformed input, and the replay case with the option unset.
- `rstudio-tests --scope r --filter "graphics|notebook|prefs|linter"`: 135 passed on macOS. `ant javac` clean.

## Not covered

- Not exercised on Windows, where the preferences note and the GDI device live.
- No e2e test for the preferences note.

title: fix file lock correctness
description:
### Intent

Fix correctness and security defects in advisory and link-based file locks. Same-process advisory probes could release an active process-scoped lock, while stale link-lock cleanup and release could affect a successor lock. Malformed link metadata and filesystem inspection errors could also produce unsafe stale or unlocked results.

### Approach

- Keep advisory lock files on a stable inode and coordinate all same-process operations through a canonical-path registry.
- Retain the exact link-lock inode through acquisition, refresh, and release; use inode validation and an atomic cleanup claim before replacing stale locks.
- Parse PIDs without a shell, preserve the existing PID-only on-disk format, and support legacy owner files during cleanup.
- Give each symlink lock a unique owner file, handle aliased parents and broken links, and treat incomplete lock publication as held until timeout.
- Preserve inspection and creation errors so callers can fail closed, including the Posit Assistant installation-lock probe.
- Reject lock timeout and refresh settings below one second or with non-finite values.

### Automated Tests

Expanded the core file-lock tests with concurrent thread/process acquisition, stale takeover, successor safety, symlink aliasing, metadata compatibility, malformed metadata, destructor cleanup, and error-propagation coverage. Posit Assistant installation-lock integration tests cover non-destructive and fail-closed probes.

- Core: 672 tests run; 664 passed and 8 skipped (3 disabled).
- Posit Assistant installation locks: 25 tests passed.

### QA Notes

The automated tests exercise the advisory and link-based implementations directly, including concurrent and cross-process behavior.

### Documentation

No user-facing documentation changes; this updates internal lock behavior.

title: add ctrl+shift+c / ctrl+shift+v copy and paste in the terminal
description:
## Summary

Ctrl+Shift+C copies the selection and Ctrl+Shift+V pastes in the Terminal pane, the copy/paste keys of most terminal emulators (gnome-terminal, Windows Terminal, VS Code's terminal). Cmd+C / Cmd+V on macOS and Ctrl+Insert / Shift+Insert keep working as before.

Fixes #1687.

## Why it didn't work

- xterm.js sends nothing to the shell for either combination (its Ctrl+letter mapping requires Shift to be up), so both fell through to the browser's default action.
- Ctrl+Shift+V: Chromium's default is a plain-text paste, which fires the paste event xterm already handles, so this already worked in Chrome, Edge and the desktop app on Windows and Linux (as the last comment on the issue reports). Firefox has no such default for text areas, and macOS has no Ctrl binding at all.
- Ctrl+Shift+C: no browser has a copy default for it. In a browser it opens the developer tools' inspector. On Windows and Linux desktop the unhandled key falls back to the Electron menu accelerator for Comment/Uncomment Lines (`Cmd+Shift+C` in `Commands.cmd.xml`), a binding the shortcut manager deliberately passes over when the terminal has focus.

## How it works

All in xterm's custom key event handler in `XTermNative.createTerminal`, on keydown with Ctrl+Shift and no other modifier:

- **C**: if there is a selection, run the browser's `copy` command. That dispatches the copy event xterm already handles (the same path as Ctrl+Insert and the context menu) and, unlike the async clipboard API, works over plain http, which is how RStudio Server is often reached. `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is the fallback if the command is unavailable. The key is consumed even with no selection, so it neither opens the inspector nor reaches the menu accelerator.
- **V**: the browser's own paste runs first. A capture-phase `paste` listener on the container notes whether a paste event arrived; if none did by the next tick, the terminal reads the clipboard itself: through the desktop bridge (`desktop.getClipboardText`) in RStudio Desktop, otherwise `navigator.clipboard.readText()`. On Firefox that read shows Firefox's own "Paste" confirmation button; over plain http the API is unavailable and behaviour is unchanged (Shift+Insert still works there).

## Tests

- New e2e spec `tests/panes/terminal/terminal_clipboard.test.ts`: double-clicks a printed word, presses Ctrl+Shift+C, and reads the clipboard back through a plain paste into the Console input; then copies again and pastes at the prompt with Ctrl+Shift+V. It forces the DOM renderer so the word can be located in the DOM, and grants `clipboard-read` on the Chromium context for the macOS fallback path.
- Ran the new spec plus the existing terminal specs in desktop-dev (13 passed) and server-dev (12 passed) on macOS; `ant draft` clean; e2e `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Not covered here

- The terminal page of the Workbench user guide (`docs/user/rstudio/ide/guide/tools/terminal.qmd` in rstudio-pro) only mentions mouse selection for copying; a one-line docs follow-up there could list these keys.
- Not exercised locally: Windows/Linux desktop (where the accelerator fallback lives) and Firefox. CI covers the former.

title: keep the data viewer's frozen pane on the viewport's scroll range
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18620.

The overscroll tail from #18652 fixed the last row hiding under the *custom* horizontal scrollbar, but with "Use overlay scrollbars" turned off the reporter still sees the grid snap back up as soon as it reaches the bottom (video in the issue), and at the bottom the row numbers sit a row out of step with the data.

### Approach

The frozen row-number pane and the body viewport are synced scrollers with different vertical ranges. The viewport always overflows horizontally (the overscroll padding is applied even when every column fits), so in native mode its horizontal scrollbar takes a 14-17px gutter out of `clientHeight`; the frozen pane has no gutter, so its maximum `scrollTop` ends a gutter short. `syncPinnedScrollTop` clamps it early at the bottom, and `onPinnedScroll`'s "is the frozen pane already clamped?" check compares a fractional `scrollTop` against integer `scrollHeight - clientHeight`. Under non-integer display scaling (Windows at 125%) the clamped value reads e.g. 681.5 against a computed max of 682, the check fails, and the viewport is set back to the frozen pane's position, i.e. yanked under the bar. Windows' animated wheel then fights that every frame, which is the multi-row bounce in the video.

- `syncPinnedPaneGutter` (run from `applyPinnedColumns`, whose padding decides the horizontal overflow) insets the frozen pane by the viewport's measured gutter so both panes share one scroll range: no early clamp, and the row labels stay aligned at maximum scroll. Zero in overlay mode and wherever the platform floats native bars.
- The clamp check gets a pixel of slack for the whole-pixel measurement of a fractional layout.

Reproduced and verified with headless Chromium at a forced 1.25 device scale factor and layout-taking native scrollbars: before, each wheel tick that reached the bottom was followed a frame later by a 14.5px pull-back to the frozen pane's position; after, both panes end at the same maximum with no pull-backs.

### Automated Tests

The native-scrollbar half of the existing #18620 e2e test now asserts that the frozen pane's inset equals the viewport's gutter, that the two panes' maxima and bottom offsets match, that the position settles under further wheeling, and that the inset is dropped again on switching back to overlay mode. The settle check is shared with the overlay-mode test. The fractional-offset trigger itself does not occur in CI, but the shared range removes the early clamp it depended on.

### QA Notes

On Windows at 125% or 150% display scaling, open the data viewer's toolbar options menu and uncheck "Use overlay scrollbars", then `View()` a frame of 100,000 rows and wheel to the bottom. The last row should stay visible above the horizontal scrollbar, the row numbers should line up with the data, and further wheeling should not move the grid back up. Switching the option back on should behave as before.

### Documentation

None; behavior fix.

title: give rserver-dev sessions their own rstudio config and data homes
description:
### Intent

Developer tooling only, no issue. `npm run rserver-dev` sessions used the developer's real `~/.config/rstudio` and `~/.local/share/rstudio`, so a preference toggled while testing, or written by a script through `.rs.writeUserPref()`, changed everyday RStudio settings (that is how the #18620 reproduction turned off overlay scrollbars in my own RStudio), and two worktrees' instances shared state.

title: fix inline notebook table colors across editor themes
description:
### Intent

Fixes #13292. Inline R Markdown tables should follow editor theme changes while retaining readable text on their own backgrounds. Plain `knitr::kable()` output can retain black text under Cobalt; Bootstrap DT and HTML with white backgrounds can instead inherit white text and become unreadable.

### Approach

Use low-priority foreground defaults and normal table inheritance without changing the document's rendering mode or layout. A first CSS cascade layer preserves authored declarations, including colors inherited from ancestors.

For solid and translucent painted backgrounds, select the neutral foreground with the better contrast against the composited background. Two synchronous style probes distinguish theme-derived foregrounds from authored colors, so custom text colors remain under the output author's control. Batch updates after DOM/style changes and stylesheet loading to cover tables and backgrounds added or changed after the iframe loads. Existing opt-outs for body classes and inline body backgrounds remain in place.

Also guard queued theme callbacks when a source tab's iframe no longer has a content window. The expanded integration tests exposed that race when closing a tab immediately after changing themes.

Save and restore the test's original theme in TypeScript, wait for the restored stylesheet, and remove the misleading `@parallel_safe` tag while keeping the tests independent.

### Automated Tests

- All 11 notebook theme tests pass against the rebuilt macOS Desktop frontend with R 4.6.1. They cover first render, theme changes, reruns, source-tab switching, authored colors and cascade layers, mixed table/row/cell/wrapper backgrounds, translucent backgrounds, document backgrounds and opt-outs, dynamic updates, and default/Bootstrap DT.
- GWT draft compilation and the Playwright TypeScript check pass.
- Ten cases generated through the notebook R capture hooks pass focused browser checks in Chromium 147, Firefox 148, and WebKit 26.4, including dark/light/dark transitions. These checks execute the production native theming code against generated HTML; they are not full Server application runs.
- A focused Chromium check with 1,000 rows completed the initial update in approximately 16 ms and confirmed that an observed content mutation settles without a mutation feedback loop.

The local Desktop run reused the existing C++ runtime. The full unit and application suites were not run.

### QA Notes

With a dark editor theme, run plain `kable()` output, default `DT::datatable()`, Bootstrap DT, and HTML tables with white or dark backgrounds. Verify readable text immediately, switch themes, rerun chunks, switch/close source tabs, and change backgrounds after loading. Explicit text colors should remain unchanged. Full application QA on Windows, Linux, and Server is still needed; the original narrower frontend change was previously tested on Windows.

### Documentation

Updated the linked `NEWS.md` bug-fix entry.

### Checklist

- [x] Includes an entry in `NEWS.md`.
- [x] Restores theme-appropriate text contrast without adding controls or changing keyboard behavior.
- [x] Focused integration tests and frontend compilation pass.
- [ ] Full unit and application suites have been run.

title: Serve Posit Assistant chat assets from the installation the backend runs
description:
`handleAIChatRequest()` resolved the Posit Assistant installation on every `/ai-chat/` static asset request, and loading the chat pane issues dozens of them. Since #18815 that search ranks every tier rather than returning the first hit, so each request ran `verifyPositAiInstallation()` plus a `package.json` read and a `protocol.json` read for up to three tiers. On a workstation that is microseconds; on RStudio Server with a network-mounted home directory it is per-request latency multiplied by the number of assets in the chat UI.

## What the code does now

`startChatBackend()` hands the installation it resolved to the static file handler once `runProgram()` has succeeded, together with the backend port and the auth token. Asset requests serve from that installation, so the tier search and its JSON reads no longer run per request.

Publishing all three only after the launch succeeds means a failed start never pins its installation or announces its port and token: asset requests keep serving whatever was pinned before -- nothing, before the first successful start -- and no failure path has to undo a pin. The lock-refusal and launch-failure paths still call `clearChatBackendPort()`, as they did before this change, which resets the handler's port and token.

The installation is published before the port because `setChatBackendPort()` rebuilds the CSP header, and the session's first rebuild reads `dist/csp.json` from the served installation and caches it for the rest of the session (#18831). If an HTML request, a backend stop, or a lock or launch failure has already rebuilt it, this ordering has no effect.

The pinned installation outlives the backend, so a page whose backend exited can still load lazily-loaded chunks. It is replaced by the next start, which is how an install or an update takes effect, and cleared by uninstall once the directory is actually gone.

It also invalidates itself. `servedInstallationPath()` tests the pin with `verifyPositAiInstallation()`, the same definition the resolver requires of a tier before it will rank it, so a path that stops holding a complete installation falls back to the tier search rather than answering from a directory that cannot serve. That covers a rolled-back update, a removal out of band, and a `pai/bin` left half-extracted by a failed `unzip` whose cleanup and backup restore both failed (`installPackage()` reports those with a log and carries on). The check costs four stats per asset request, against twelve stats and up to six JSON reads before.

## Behaviour change worth noting

An out-of-band change to the installation -- an administrator replacing the system-wide copy mid-session -- now takes effect at the next backend start rather than on the next asset request. In exchange, the assets served and the backend process they talk to come from the same installation.

## Testing

Five tests in `ChatStaticFilesTests.cpp` drive `handleAIChatRequest()` directly against staged installations, requesting a `.js` asset so the request skips the handler's HTML branch and its dependence on session options and the editor theme:

- assets are served from the pinned installation;
- a later pin replaces an earlier one, which is what a backend restart does;
- a pinned installation whose directory is gone is not served from;
- a pinned installation left half-extracted is not served from;
- with nothing pinned, the previously pinned installation is not served from.

The two negative tests were each checked against the weaker implementation they exist to rule out, so neither passes vacuously: without the existence check the dead-pin test fails on the status code (403, which is the signature of the pin having been used), and without `verifyPositAiInstallation()` the half-extracted test fails on the served body, since that installation still holds the requested asset.

`./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession` -- 580 tests from 53 test suites, all passing.

## No NEWS entry

The per-request cost arrived with #18774 and #18815, both inside the unreleased 2026.10.0 cycle, so no official-release user has encountered it.

## Related

Reviews of this branch twice raised that `loadCspDirectives()` caches `dist/csp.json` for the lifetime of the session, which predates this change (#17132) and is out of scope here. Filed separately as #18831, since an in-session update restarts only the backend and therefore keeps serving the previous version's CSP.

Fixes #18819.

title: Prompt to save on window close after a cancelled quit
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18818.

On RStudio Desktop, cancelling the quit that a window close triggers left the window's close button disarmed for the rest of the session: later closes exited immediately, with no prompt for unsaved documents and no workspace save.

`MainWindow.closeEvent()` set `quitConfirmed = true` as soon as `desktopHooks.quitR()` returned. `quitR()` is `void` and only dispatches the quit sequence — the promise resolves while the save prompts are still on screen, so the flag was set whatever the user answered. Nothing cleared it except a session restart, which is why a morning cancel persisted all afternoon.

The assignment was also redundant: on a confirmed quit, GWT sets `PENDING_QUIT_AND_EXIT` and the session exits, `SessionLauncher.onRSessionExited()` calls `MainWindow.quit()`, and `quit()` sets `quitConfirmed = true` before `window.close()`. This change drops the assignment in `closeEvent()` and leaves `quit()` as the sole setter.

`closeEvent()` held a second piece of state with the same problem. It recorded the window bounds on the first close attempt and set `geometrySaved` so later attempts skipped it, so cancelling froze the saved geometry at the cancel-time bounds and every move or resize for the rest of the session was discarded. The bounds are now saved in the branch that lets the window close, which is the only point where the geometry is final, and the flag is gone.

Desktop only. `quitConfirmed` has no server-side counterpart, and closing a browser tab in Server mode is not a quit.

### Approach

- `src/node/desktop/src/main/main-window.ts`: remove the `.then()` that confirmed the quit on dispatch; move the `saveWindowBounds()` call into the closing branch and delete `geometrySaved` along with its reset in `onWorkbenchInitialized()`.
- `src/node/desktop/test/unit/main/main-window.test.ts`: four cases in the style of the existing crashed-renderer fake — a `closeEvent` whose `quitR()` resolves leaves `quitConfirmed` false; a second `closeEvent` still calls `preventDefault()` and re-runs `quitR()`; the closing pass saves the current bounds; the cancellable pass saves nothing. The options singleton is pointed at a temp directory so no test touches the real user config.

The close-after-confirmed-quit routes were checked: `onSessionQuit()`, `onRSessionExited()` (`PendingQuitAndExit`), the `launchSession()` failure dialog, and `runDiagnostics` all go through `quit()`, which closes the window and so reaches the geometry save. `SessionLauncher.onLaunchError()` closes the window directly but is covered by the existing `!this.sessionProcess || exitCode !== null` guard, and by the `!!window.desktopHooks` probe when an error page is loaded.

Two consequences worth naming. Clicking the close button repeatedly while the save prompt is up now dispatches the quit sequence again instead of closing the window, because the main process is never told whether a quit was cancelled or is still being answered. Suppressing that would need a signal `ApplicationQuit` does not send — it abandons a quit at seven independent exits with no common funnel — and a pending flag without one would leave the close button dead, which is the same bug in a less visible form. Stacked prompts also replace what used to happen on that second click: the window closed with the prompt still on screen. Separately, geometry is no longer persisted for a cancelled close, so a session that is cancelled and then hard-killed keeps its previous bounds rather than the cancel-time ones.

### QA Notes

Open RStudio Desktop, click the window close button, cancel the prompt. Create a variable in the console and edit an open document, then click close again: the unsaved-documents and save-workspace prompts appear, and confirming writes `.RData`. Before this change the second close exited silently.

For the geometry half: cancel a close, then move and resize the window, then quit and restart. The window comes back where it was left, not where it sat when the close was cancelled.

title: Move SessionHttpConnectionListener unit tests upstream from pro
description:
`SessionHttpConnectionListenerTests.cpp` lived only in rstudio-pro, even though everything it covers is open source: `handleAccept`'s consecutive-error ladder, `kMaxConsecutiveErrors`, and the `SESSION_EXIT_TOO_MANY_OPEN_FILES` / `SESSION_EXIT_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY` exits.

Three test cases come over:

- `DetectsConsecutiveErrors` — 100 accept errors log on a throttle and return 0; the 101st exits `EXIT_FAILURE`
- `DetectsOOMCondition` — the 101st exits `SESSION_EXIT_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`
- `DetectsFDExhaustion` — the 101st exits `SESSION_EXIT_TOO_MANY_OPEN_FILES`

## Seams in SessionHttpConnectionListenerImpl.hpp

The fixture subclasses `HttpConnectionListenerImpl<boost::asio::ip::tcp>` and drives `handleAccept` directly with synthetic error codes. Three override points make that possible. None change behavior:

- `acceptNextConnection()` is now `protected virtual`, so the fixture can stub it and keep the accept loop from running.
- `exitEarly(int)` is a new `protected virtual` wrapper around `session::exitEarly(status)`, so the fixture captures the status instead of terminating the test process.
- The three `LOG_ERROR(error)` calls in `handleAccept` are now `logAcceptError()`, a `private virtual` defaulting to `core::log::logError(...)`, so the fixture captures the error instead of writing to the log.

## Error codes

The fixture feeds `handleAccept` the codes Boost.Asio actually reports per platform — `ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY` and `WSAEMFILE` on Windows, `ENOMEM` and `EMFILE` elsewhere. Constructing them as errno values in `boost::system::system_category()` is only coherent on POSIX; on Windows that category holds Win32/Winsock values, so Boost maps neither to a generic condition and both `errc` comparisons in `handleAccept` miss.

`handleAccept` itself needed no change — Boost does map the real Windows codes, so the production path was already correct there.

## Build

No build changes. `src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt:443` already does `file(GLOB_RECURSE SESSION_TEST_FILES "*Tests.cpp")`, which picks the file up in the `rsession` scope.

## Verification

`./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession` — 558 tests pass, including the 3 new ones. Compiles warning-free.

Mutation-checked for non-vacuity: changing `exitEarly(SESSION_EXIT_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY)` to `exitEarly(EXIT_FAILURE)` in `handleAccept` fails `DetectsOOMCondition` and only that test; reverting returns the suite to green.

Windows coverage for this logic in this repo was zero and stays zero while the tests live only in pro — that path is exercised by CI here now.

Closes #18811.

title: Run the newest compatible Posit Assistant installation
description:
## Intent

Posit Assistant discovery picks the newest compatible installation across the user, system-wide, and bundled tiers, instead of the first one found in a fixed order.

Fixes #18774.

## Approach

`locatePositAssistantInstallation()` collects the valid installations among the tiers the settings allow and ranks them: an installation whose `protocol.json` matches this build outranks one that does not (a missing file counts as a mismatch, as in `hasProtocolMismatch()`), then the higher `package.json` version wins, and ties keep the previous order (user, system, bundled). An installation with no readable version ranks lowest but is still used when it is all there is.

A pinned `posit-assistant-path` stays outside the race. It is the administrator's explicit choice, so it is used as-is when it holds an installation, even over a newer user install; when it holds none it still ends the search for read-only copies rather than falling back to the bundle. Managed mode (`allow-posit-assistant-installation=0`) still skips the user tier, and already fell through to the bundled copy before this change.

Once a read-only copy can outrank the user tier, the update check needs a guard: a manifest version that ranks below the copy in use would be offered on every check, because each accepted install lands in the user data directory and loses the race. `userInstallWouldBeSelected()` reports whether an install of the offered version would actually be used, and `onUpdateCheckComplete()` makes no offer when it would not. The existing user install never competes there, since it is what the install overwrites, so a manifest rollback of a user-only install still takes effect.

## Testing

`ChatInstallationTests.cpp` covers the ranking (newer bundle or system copy over a stale user install, tie order, versionless lowest, protocol compatibility over version, pinned path over a newer user install, invalid pinned path still honouring a user install) and the predicate (nothing installed, replacing the user tier, below and above a read-only copy, incompatible and versionless read-only copies, valid pinned path, managed mode).

```
GTEST_FILTER='Chat*:SessionAssistant*:PositAssistant*' ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession
[  PASSED  ] 266 tests.
```

Not exercised manually: open-source builds ship no bundle, so the bundled tier was driven only through the `InstallSearchPaths` seam.

title: Apply npm audit fix to desktop dependencies
description:
Result of running `npm audit fix` in `src/node/desktop`. Only `package-lock.json` changes; `package.json` is untouched.

Bumped (all dev-only, all transitive):

- body-parser 1.20.5 -> 1.20.8
- express 4.22.2 -> 4.22.3
- qs 6.15.3 -> 6.16.0
- path-to-regexp constraint ~0.1.12 -> ~0.1.13

`npm audit` goes from 20 advisories to 17. The three moderate ones are resolved:

- qs array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing
- qs denial of service via attacker-controlled isBuffer

The remaining 17 (2 low, 15 high) are all electron-forge and mocha transitive dependencies that `npm audit fix` cannot resolve without `--force`, which would pull in breaking major upgrades.

title: fix notebook kable theme e2e failures
description:
### Intent

Fix the notebook theme E2E failures seen in the [Windows shard for PR #18747](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/34914115857/job/104215578965). The gallery test timed out twice because Ace's scrollbar intercepted the `html` selector click. The stylesheet case also intermittently matched two output frames.

### Approach

Scroll gallery controls to the center of Ace's virtual viewport before clicking them normally. Give each parameterized case its own notebook path so cached output from a previous case cannot overlap newly generated output. Existing color, marker, and gallery assertions remain intact.

### Automated Tests

- `npm run typecheck` passed.
- Full `notebook_kable_theme.test.ts` suite: 12 passed on macOS Desktop with retries disabled, using this worktree's compiled GWT and notebook R modules.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### QA Notes

Windows CI should confirm that gallery controls remain clickable after theme changes and that the stylesheet case consistently resolves one output frame.

### Documentation

Test-only change; no product documentation or NEWS entry required.

title: fix kable colors in inline notebook output
description:
HTML tables produced by `knitr::kable()` can retain dark text in a dark editor theme because their HTML fragments use quirks mode and table colors can remain stale after the body foreground changes. Mark kable output in the existing print hook, preserve that marker through notebook output metadata, and apply `color: inherit` to its tables in both single-output and gallery views. There is no restriction on kable's output format: this includes HTML generated directly by kable and HTML rendered from its Markdown output.

The inheritance rule is placed in an initial cascade layer so explicitly authored table colors retain precedence. Generic as-is Markdown, custom HTML, and DT retain their existing color/background behavior. Previously cached output needs to be rerun once to acquire the marker. Small callback guards also prevent exceptions when gallery pages are detached or reconstructed without a completion callback.

This is the kable-specific alternative to #18809, which remains open unchanged for consideration of broader background handling.

Validation:
- GWT draft compilation and E2E TypeScript typecheck passed.
- All 12 regression cases passed on macOS Desktop using the rebuilt frontend and this branch's R modules: default/Markdown/simple/HTML kable through theme changes, reruns, tab switching, and cached reopen; inline, stylesheet, and cascade-layer colors; mixed-output gallery selection; exclusion of generic Markdown, custom HTML, and default/Bootstrap DT. The complete test invocation reported 14 passed and 3 unrelated setup/teardown skips.

Fixes #13292.

title: fix native select scrollbars in dark dialogs
description:
### Intent

The editor-theme list in Global Options > Appearance retains a light native scrollbar when the dialog uses a dark IDE theme.

### Approach

Add `color-scheme: dark` to the existing dark dialog `select`/`.gwt-ListBox` rule, matching the adjacent input and textarea styling. This lets native select scrollbars use dark colors while keeping the change scoped to dark dialogs.

### Automated Tests

`git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passes. No automated tests were added for this one-line CSS change; native scrollbar appearance requires visual verification.

### QA Notes

Visual verification in the running IDE remains outstanding. With dark modal dialogs enabled and a dark IDE theme, open Global Options > Appearance and confirm the editor-theme list has a dark scrollbar. Switch to a light theme and confirm the list retains its normal light appearance. Check other select controls in dark dialogs for rendering regressions.

### Documentation

No documentation changes; this corrects existing visual styling.
