title: Add slot, manifest and selector machinery for versioned Posit AI installs
description:
PR 2 of the five-PR sequence in #18658. Pure addition under `src/cpp/session/modules/chat/` — no existing call site changes, and nothing is wired up. The resolver switch and install rewrite are PR 3, deleting `ChatInstallLock` is PR 4, the Reinstall button is PR 5.

## What lands

**`ChatSlots`** — slot allocation and verification.

The install API is `prepareStagingDir` → extract → `allocateSlot`. `allocateSlot()` records the slot manifest, verifies the result, and only then renames the staged tree into `pai/versions/<version>`, or `<version>-2`, `-3`, ... when that name is taken. Recording and verifying inside the call rather than asking callers to do it first means "a slot only reaches a final name once it has been checked" holds by construction, not by an ordering each install path has to remember.

Slot names are never read for identity. The name comes from the staged package's own `package.json`, and a slot is adopted only when it verifies *and* declares the same version and protocol as what was staged — a directory named `1.1.0` is not evidence that it holds `1.1.0`. `SlotPolicy::AlwaysFresh` never adopts, which is what PR 5 needs.

`isUsableSlotName()` gates both untrusted sources of a name (the archive's `package.json` and `selected.json`), rejecting anything that cannot round-trip as a directory name. The Windows rules are applied on every platform so a home reached from both Windows and Linux agrees on which names are slots.

`prepareStagingDir()` returns a directory no other session can name. See the deviation note.

`verifySlot()` requires the expected paths to exist and be non-empty, `package.json` to parse with a `version`, `protocol.json` to parse with a `protocol`, the slot not to be a link, and every manifest entry to be intact. The check it replaces in PR 3 tests only that three paths exist, so a zero-byte `main.js` passes it.

**`ChatSlotManifest`** — relative path to size and SHA-256 for every regular file in a slot, recorded after extraction while the tree is known to match the verified package. Verification compares sizes only, so it stays a stat walk cheap enough to run at every resolve; the hashes are recorded for a deeper check later, as the issue specifies. Symlinks are excluded and paths reached through a symlinked or junction-backed directory are rejected, so a slot cannot come to depend on a tree it does not contain.

**`ChatSelector`** — `pai/selected.json`, holding `{"selected": {"11.0": "1.1.0-2", "10.0": "0.4.8"}}`. Read, write (temp file then rename, last-writer-wins), and the fallback: when the named slot is missing, unusable, or serves another protocol, resolution picks the best verifying slot for the protocol and records it. Ordering is release version, then a release over a prerelease of it, then — only between slots holding the very same version — the later reinstall.

Legacy `pai/bin` is not read, written, or deleted. There is no garbage collection; slots accumulate, as the issue specifies.

## One deviation from the issue text

The issue specified staging at `pai/versions/.tmp-<pid>/`, cleared first. This PR uses a unique name per install (`.tmp-<host>-<pid>-<nonce>`) and clears nothing. Two sessions sharing an NFS home can compute the same pid-based name — under container runtimes they routinely do, since each session pod has its own PID namespace and low pids repeat — and the second session's prepare would delete the first's half-extracted tree. Because the manifest is recorded from whatever is on disk when it runs, the victim would record a manifest describing the damage, verify it against itself, and publish a truncated slot that keeps verifying forever.

The issue body has been updated to match, with the reasoning in [this comment](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18658#issuecomment-5446077208).

## Testing

91 new unit tests: rename arbitration and adoption (including refusing to adopt a different version or protocol), forced mode, ordinal allocation past `-2` and past `-9`, staged installs being unresolvable and not disturbing each other, name validation from both sources, manifest round trip, symlink and junction hardening, every verification failure mode separately, selector round trip, and fallback and repair including absent or malformed `selected.json`.

    cmake --build build --target rsession
    ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession    # 519 tests, all passing

No NEWS.md entry: nothing user-visible ships until PR 3, so the versioned-install entry lands there.

Addresses #18658.

title: give the data viewer grid an overscroll tail past the last row
description:
### Intent

Addresses #18620.

The report has two halves -- the Data Viewer "bounces" at the bottom of a large
frame, and the last row is blocked from view. This PR fixes the second half,
which reproduces reliably on every platform.

### The bug

The Data Viewer's horizontal scrollbar is a floating overlay
(`.custom-scrollbar.horizontal`: `bottom: 0; height: 11px` inside `#gridPanes`),
so it covers the bottom 11px of the grid rather than taking layout space. The
virtualizer sized the bottom spacer to exactly `(activeRows - newEnd - 1) *
ROW_HEIGHT`, so the grid's scroll content ended at the last row: at maximum
scroll that row sits flush against the viewport bottom, permanently half hidden
under the bar, with nowhere left to scroll.

`visibleBodyHeight()` already discounted those 11px -- that is how
`ensureActiveCellVisible` clears the bar for every other row. The last row was
the one target that could never reach the same place, because the scroll range
stopped 11px short of where it needed to end.

Measured in RStudio Server on macOS with `View(as.data.frame(matrix(seq_len(500
* 30), nrow = 500)))`, scrolled to the bottom, the last row's bottom edge sits
11px below the top of the scrollbar -- the bar covers just under half of it:

```
lastRow: 499  lastRowTop: 482  lastRowBottom: 505
viewportBottom: 505  scrollbarTop: 494   ->  11px occluded
```

### The fix

Add a matching overscroll tail to the bottom spacer, so the last row can be
scrolled out from under the bar. This mirrors two affordances the grid already
has for exactly this reason: the summary sidebar's tail (`renderSidebarWindow`)
and the horizontal overscroll padding that keeps the rightmost column reachable
(`applyPinnedColumns`, #17612).

The tail is gated on overlay-scrollbar mode, since a native horizontal scrollbar
takes layout space and is already excluded from `clientHeight`.
`visibleBodyHeight` now shares that gate through the new
`hScrollbarOverlayHeight()` helper, instead of subtracting 11px in a mode where
nothing overlays the rows.

Two consequences of letting `scrollTop` run past the last row are handled:

- the render window's start is clamped against its end, so a viewport shorter
  than the header plus the tail cannot push `firstVisible` off the end of the
  frame and render an empty window;
- the tail is part of the render window's identity (`renderOverscroll`), so a
  change in horizontal overflow re-sizes the spacer even when the row window is
  unchanged.

### The "bounce" half

I could not reproduce a moving scroll position on macOS, in either RStudio
Server or a standalone harness driving the real grid resources. Ruled out with
measurements: the pinned-pane/viewport scroll mirror (Blink drains newly
enqueued scroll events in the same dispatch pass, so `onPinnedScroll` never
observes a stale mirror -- 356 events during a smooth scroll, 0 mismatches),
scroll anchoring (already opted out in #18222), `scrollHeight` instability,
fetch-driven relayout, device pixel ratios 1-2, and page zoom 0.8-2.

Both previous bugs in this component (#18221, #18378) were Windows/RHEL-only, so
this one likely is too. The new test asserts the scroll position settles at the
bottom as well as the geometry, so the Windows CI matrix will report on that
half the way it did for #18378.

### Testing

New e2e test `the last row clears the horizontal scrollbar at maximum scroll
(#18620)` in `data_viewer.test.ts`: views a 500x30 frame so both axes overflow,
wheels to the bottom, and asserts the scroll settles, the last row is rendered
inside the viewport, and its bottom edge clears the top of the scrollbar.

Verified against a session serving each version of the grid resources:

- with the fix: passes (last row bottom == scrollbar top)
- without it: fails on the scrollbar assertion -- `Expected: <= 108.5,
  Received: 119`, i.e. the 11px overlap

The full `tests/panes/data-viewer/` suite passes (66 tests).

title: repair the windows locale when it is changed behind r's back
description:
Addresses #18139. Related: #15008.

## What is actually going wrong

rsession and UCRT builds of R (R >= 4.2) share a single C runtime, so a `setlocale()` call anywhere in the process moves R's locale too -- but silently, without R's cached view of the encoding (`localeCP`, `utf8locale`, `native_enc`, all computed in `R_check_locale`) being updated to match.

Code that saves the locale, switches to `"C"` for a conversion and then restores it is a ready source of exactly that, because the saved name is narrow. A locale name holding non-ASCII characters -- `Turkish_Türkiye.utf8` on Windows 11, `Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8` -- cannot be parsed back once the process is in the `"C"` locale, so the restore fails and the session is left in `"C"` while R goes on reporting a UTF-8 locale.

This part is reproducible with R alone, RStudio not involved (confirmed on Windows 11, system code page 65001):

```r
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8")
before <- Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE")
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C")
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", before)
#> [1] ""
#> Warning message:
#> OS reports request to set locale to "Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8" cannot be honored
Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE")
#> [1] "C"
```

Marking the encoding on `before` does not help; UCRT rejects the name however it is encoded.

That mismatch -- C runtime in `"C"`, R believing UTF-8 -- is what produces the reported symptoms. Console input runs through a per-character `wctomb()`, which follows the C runtime locale: in `"C"`, `Ç` (U+00C7) truncates to a raw `0xC7` byte and `ı`/`ş` fail and come through as `\u131`/`\u15f` escapes, which is the reporter's `Error: unexpected '\\' in "al\"` exactly. It also explains why `Sys.setlocale()` repaired a session by hand and why `View()` broke it again (#15008).

The reporter's own diagnostics rule out the theory the previous attempt (#18141) was built on: a fresh broken session reports `Sys.getlocale()` as `"C"` while `l10n_info()` reports MBCS `TRUE`, UTF-8 `TRUE`, code page `65001`. Those flags come only from `R_check_locale()`, and in a `"C"` locale they would be `FALSE`/`FALSE`/`0` -- so R started in the right locale and the C runtime was moved afterwards.

## What this changes

- **`synchronizeLocale()` detects and repairs the divergence.** It runs on each R busy transition; it now compares the code page implied by the C runtime's `LC_CTYPE` against R's `localeCP` and, when they disagree, restores a *wide* copy of the locale recorded while the two last agreed -- or re-adopts the operating system's locale when the divergence predates any such observation, which is what affected users have been doing by hand with `Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "")`. `localeCP` is the arbiter, so a deliberate `Sys.setlocale()` (which moves R and the C runtime together) is left alone.

  This replaces the codepage-equality guard, which disabled the function in exactly this case: `localeCP` never changes while the locale drifts, so the two always compared equal. It also drops the `Sys.getlocale()` call the function made from inside the busy callback, and with it a latent bug -- that string is native-encoded and was being read as UTF-8.

- **Console input no longer depends on the C runtime locale.** It goes through a new `r::util::utf82rconsole()`, which encodes for the code page R reports rather than the one `LC_CTYPE` implies, so input survives a drift even before it is repaired. That uses a new explicit-codepage overload of `string_utils::utf8ToSystem()` converting with `WideCharToMultiByte()` instead of `wctomb()`; text destined for a UTF-8 code page is passed through untouched, which also stops surrogate pairs from being split. `WC_NO_BEST_FIT_CHARS` means an unrepresentable character is escaped for R rather than silently transliterated into a lookalike that means something else.

- **Corrected the comment on the startup `_wsetlocale()` added in #18141.** R adopts the operating system locale itself at the top of `setup_Rmainloop()` on Windows (`src/main/main.c`, `#ifdef Win32`), so that call is not what gives R its locale. It still earns its place when a locale environment variable names something Windows rejects and R's own call fails, so the call stays; only the reasoning was wrong.

## What this does not do

It does not find the code that moves the locale in the first place -- narrowing that on an affected machine is still outstanding, and `View()` remains the most reliable trigger. This makes the session self-healing rather than eliminating the clobber, so it wants manual verification on a Turkish or Bokmål Windows box before we call #18139 closed.

The `Sys.setlocale()` half is arguably an R bug: `Sys.getlocale()` hands back a name that `Sys.setlocale()` then refuses, where going through `_wsetlocale()` internally would round-trip. Worth reporting upstream separately.

## Testing

- A core gtest asserting that conversion for a UTF-8 code page is independent of the C runtime locale, and that an unrepresentable character is escaped rather than transliterated.
- An rsession gtest asserting that `synchronizeLocale()` puts back a locale clobbered behind R's back.

Both are Windows-only, so Windows CI is what exercises them; the POSIX side of every touched file compiles locally.

title: handle failed handler copies in AsyncClient safely
description:
### Intent

Addresses #18625, a follow-up from #18541.

`AsyncClient` moves `boost::function` handlers across `socketMutex_` in two directions, and both were unsafe if a copy threw. Copying a `boost::function` allocates whenever the target is too large for its small-object buffer, so allocation failure -- the memory pressure streaming exists to relieve -- is the realistic trigger. Both directions used `LOCK_MUTEX` / `END_LOCK_MUTEX`, whose unexpected-exception path logs and continues, so in every case execution ran on over half-finished state.

**Reading handlers out (snapshots), where the empty local reads as "no handler installed":**

- `deliverChunks()` -- the decoded piece is appended to `response_`, which nothing in streaming mode ever reads, and the consumer is then told the body is complete, one piece short.
- `closeAndRespond()` -- `responseHandler_` is copied first, so a failure on the `fixedBufferHandler_` copy leaves the surviving response handler to be invoked: a "successful" empty-body response for a body that in fact streamed in full.
- `handleWrite()` -- the connect notification is dropped, and a caller gated on it (`FormProxy`) buffers the upload until it times out.

Both `deliverChunks()` and `closeAndRespond()` additionally read an indeterminate `disabled` flag if lock acquisition itself threw, since the flag was declared uninitialized and assigned inside the critical section.

**Writing handlers in (installs), where a failure leaves the client half-configured:**

- `execute()` -- a response handler installed with no error handler behind it, and the request set in motion anyway, so the exchange can complete with nobody left to notify.
- `setFixedBufferHandler()` -- the installed handler is detached before the replacement is copied into its place, so a failure leaves no fixed buffer handler at all, silently flipping a streaming consumer into accumulating into `response_`.
- `setConnectHandler()` -- the connect notification stored while the downstream-closed handler that reports its loss is lost, leaving a caller with no way to be told either way.

### Approach

**Snapshots** go through a small `snapshotHandlers()` helper taking an explicit `boost::lock_guard` and reporting `Ready`, `Disabled`, or `Failed`. The lambda it runs keeps each site's own `handlersDisabled_` test in the same critical section as its own copies, which is the property `disableHandlers()`'s contract comment depends on; `Failed` takes the client's ordinary error path (`handleUnexpectedError()`), which closes the client, reports through the `ErrorHandler`, and detaches the handlers. Two details are load-bearing:

- `closeAndRespond()` takes its snapshot *before* the close. `handleError()` ignores anything raised after a deliberate close, so a failure discovered afterwards would be dropped without reporting or detaching anything.
- `handleWrite()` sets `requestWritten_` only after a successful copy. `close()` and `disableHandlers()` read that flag as "the connect notification was reported"; a failed copy can never report it, so leaving it false routes the still-pending notification to the downstream-closed handler -- the answer a caller gated on the connect needs to hear.

**Installs** use copy-then-swap: every copy happens before the lock, and only `swap()` runs under it. An install now either lands whole or changes nothing, and the exception reaches the caller -- which, unlike these `void` setters, has a stack to handle it on. This is a deliberate change from "swallow and continue half-configured" to "propagate with nothing changed"; the callers (`FixedBufferProxy::proxy()`, `ServerSessionProxy`, `FormProxy::initialize()`) all run inside the connection's existing exception guards.

### Automated Tests

Six fault-injection tests in `AsyncClientContentLengthTests.cpp`, one per site, driven by a `ThrowOnCopy<F>` callback target whose copy constructor throws `std::bad_alloc` once armed. Each was confirmed to fail against the unfixed code with exactly the symptom described above:

| Test | Symptom without the fix |
| --- | --- |
| `FixedBufferHandlerSnapshotFailureMidBodyFailsRatherThanDroppingPiece` | `sawFinalSignal == true` after only the first of two pieces was delivered |
| `ResponseHandlerSnapshotFailureAtCompletionFailsRatherThanRespondingEmpty` | `ResponseHandler` invoked with an empty body for a fully streamed response |
| `ConnectHandlerSnapshotFailureReportsDownstreamClosedRatherThanDropping` | neither notification delivered; the request read to completion behind the caller's back |
| `ExecuteHandlerInstallFailureLeavesNothingInMotion` | the connection ran to failure anyway, and left the client closed so a retry reported nothing |
| `FixedBufferHandlerInstallFailureKeepsTheInstalledHandler` | the installed streaming consumer was lost; the body silently fell back to being buffered |
| `ConnectHandlerInstallFailureKeepsTheInstalledPair` | the previously registered pair was destroyed, so the settle had nowhere to report |

`ExecuteHandlerInstallFailureLeavesNothingInMotion` deliberately aims at a dead port rather than a `LocalServer`: what it asserts is that nothing is set in motion at all, and `LocalServer`'s accept loop blocks until a connection arrives, so a regression there would hang the harness teardown instead of failing.

Full `rstudio-core-tests` suite passes (621 passed, 8 environment-dependent skips). The one unrelated failure seen in a whole-suite run, `AsyncConnectionImpl.ContinueParsingResumesOnTheConnectionsStrand`, is the known pre-existing flake tracked in #18634 and passes in isolation.

### QA Notes

No user-visible behavior change on any path that does not throw. The failures this addresses are not reachable by ordinary operation, so there is nothing to exercise manually; the coverage is the fault-injection tests above.

### Documentation

None required.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`

  Not applicable: the streaming proxy this hardens (#18546 / #18541) is itself unreleased, so no official-release user has encountered this.
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: don't bounce OS focus when surfacing the main window behind a satellite
description:
### Problem

With the Source editor popped out into its own window on RStudio Desktop, running code moves the caret to the console even when **Tools > Global Options > Code > Execution > "Focus console after executing code from the source pane"** is unchecked. Docked editors are unaffected. Reported on Ubuntu 24.04; not reproducible on macOS.

### Cause

The preference is read and propagated correctly. What moves focus is a window-level action that only runs when the editor is a satellite window:

1. `EditingTargetCodeExecution.executeRange()` fires `SendToConsoleEvent` with `focus = false` (the preference).
2. `SendToConsoleEvent.focusMode()` returns `MODE_FOCUS` when focus is on and `MODE_AUXILIARY` when it is off, so turning the preference **off** is what routes execution into `EventBus`'s auxiliary branch:

   ```java
   else if (crossWindow.focusMode() == CrossWindowEvent.MODE_AUXILIARY &&
            Desktop.hasDesktopFrame())
      Desktop.getFrame().bringMainFrameBehindActive();
   ```

3. `MODE_AUXILIARY` means "make the window visible if possible but don't give it focus". The Electron implementation got there by bouncing OS focus:

   ```ts
   // bring main window under active window by focusing main window then back to active
   if (activeWindow && mainWindow !== activeWindow) {
     mainWindow.show();      // activates the main window
     activeWindow.focus();   // asks the WM to hand it back
   }
   ```

   Window managers with focus-stealing prevention (GNOME on Ubuntu) refuse the second half, so focus stays on the main window -- where the caret lives in the console. macOS and Windows honor the bounce, which is why this looks platform-specific.

This is a regression from the Qt -> Electron port. The original implementation (cfe94e7a4e) was `SetWindowPos(..., SWP_NOACTIVATE)` -- no focus change at all, and an explicit no-op outside Windows. #11407 asked the Electron port to do "the same thing it did in Qt"; c4dd4c2bae implemented the focus bounce instead, on every platform.

### Fix

Never touch focus. A main window that is already on screen needs nothing done to it, so the common case becomes a true no-op; a hidden or minimized one is surfaced with `showInactive()`. The minimized-main-window case fixed by #11646 is preserved.

### Testing

Unit tests over the `desktop_bring_main_frame_behind_active` handler cover the visible, hidden, minimized, main-window-is-active, and nothing-focused cases. The three behavioral tests fail against the previous implementation and pass against this one.

`npm test`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run typecheck` all pass in `src/node/desktop` (the one failure, `Utils > findComponents`, is a worktree artifact -- it needs a built rsession binary).

### Verification still needed

The user-visible symptom is window-manager dependent and could not be reproduced on macOS, so this needs a manual check on Ubuntu/GNOME: pop the Source editor out, uncheck the preference, run a line, and confirm the caret stays in the source window. Worth also confirming on Windows that a minimized main window still surfaces (#11646) and that a background command run from a satellite still brings the main window up behind it (#11407).

Addresses #18635.

title: Tolerate Posit Assistant 1.1.x chat UI changes in e2e tests
description:
The Posit Assistant release gate (`os-test-e2e-rstudio-posit-assistant.yml`)
runs the `@ai` suite against the pre-release manifest before a build is
promoted to GA. Two tests fail there on 1.1.6 and 1.1.7 while passing against
GA 1.1.0, so the gate has been reporting a stale signal for two cycles.

Both failures are assistant-side UI changes, not RStudio regressions. The
scheduled run earlier the same day
([32705859276](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/32705859276),
GA manifest) installed the same RStudio daily, `RStudio-2026.09.0-daily-109`,
and both tests passed; only the assistant version differs.

## settings-button

The provider-settings menu item was relabeled a third time, to "Configure AI
providers". The locator already matches the two earlier names, so this adds
the new one to that alternation.

The test stops at the first assertion, so nothing past it -- the About dialog,
Copy to Clipboard, Close -- has run against 1.1.7 yet. That part may need
follow-up once the gate gets far enough to exercise it.

## conversation-history

Recent assistant builds close the history panel themselves when a conversation
is selected; older ones only close it via the toolbar toggle.
`closeConversationHistory` decided once, from an instantaneous `isHidden()`
reading, which is wrong in both directions: it could click into an auto-close
that was still finishing and re-open the panel, or accept a fade-out frame
with a re-open queued behind it.

It now waits for the panel to reach the hidden state and holds it there across
`PANEL_CLOSED_SAMPLES` samples before acting on or returning from it, the same
way `isTurnIdle` handles the stop button flickering off between streaming
phases. Toggling is capped at two clicks and the closing assertion fails the
test if the panel survives. This is correct on builds that auto-close and on
those that only respond to the toggle.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` passes. The suite itself cannot be run outside CI without
assistant credentials, and the auto-close behavior exists only in the
pre-release, so confirmation needs a gate run with
`posit_assistant_test_manifest: true`.

No NEWS.md entry: test-only change with no user-facing effect.

title: Revert the assistant selection when a Posit Assistant install is declined
description:
Fixes #18356.

Switching the code assistant away from GitHub Copilot persists the new selection immediately: `disableCopilot()` stops the Copilot agent by writing the `assistant` preference, because the backend picks the agent to run from that preference and not from `copilot_enabled` (`isAssistantEnabled()` in `SessionAssistant.cpp`). That write lands before OK or Cancel, so anything that backs the switch out has to undo it.

`checkPositAssistantInstallation()` read its revert target after that write had already replaced it with `"posit"`. Declining the Posit Assistant install prompt therefore reverted to `"posit"` and early-returned, leaving the assistant pointing at an addon that was never installed and code suggestions reporting "Posit AI: No completions available." Cancelling the Options dialog did not undo it either.

## What changed

A `RevertTarget`, captured when the check starts, carries the two values the check may have to put back:

- **the selection the user had**, restored to the selector. It is not the preference: a choice made earlier in the same dialog is not written until OK, so from `(None)` a Copilot pick followed by Posit AI has to fall back to Copilot.
- **the preference saved behind it**, restored only when it actually changed. Writing unconditionally would persist a selection the user never confirmed, which Cancel could then no longer discard.

The revert also restores `copilot_enabled` alongside the preference it mirrors, as `onApply()` derives it. Nothing gates the agent on that preference, but `disableCopilot()` gates its own write on it: left false under a reverted Copilot selection, the next switch away from Copilot would not persist.

Threading one object replaced the three `previous*` parameters that ran through the check, prompt, install, and revert path, so those signatures got shorter.

## Tests

`e2e/rstudio/tests/preferences/assistant_provider_switch.test.ts` drives Global Options and forces the install prompt through the `chat_set_update_check_override` automation RPC, so it needs no credentials, no network, and no particular addon state. Each case was confirmed to fail on the commit preceding its fix:

| Case | Failure without the fix |
|---|---|
| Copilot -> Posit AI -> decline | selector left at `posit` |
| `(None)` -> unsaved Copilot -> Posit AI -> decline | selector reverted to `none` |
| saved Posit AI -> unsaved Copilot -> Posit AI -> decline | `assistant` persisted as `copilot` |

Tagged `@desktop_only`: GitHub Copilot is offered in the selector only when the `copilot-enabled` session option is set, which defaults on in Desktop mode alone.

All 30 tests in `tests/preferences/` pass on a desktop-dev build.

## Known gap, not addressed here

The `assistantVerifyInstalled` error path (`AssistantPreferencesPane.java:598`) still leaves `"posit"` persisted when that RPC fails: it logs and sets a status label without reverting. It predates this change and is a different trigger from the one the issue describes, and closing it means deciding what the user sees -- every other revert path pairs the revert with an error dialog, whereas reverting there would swap panels and overwrite the status label, so the selector would snap back with no explanation. Worth a follow-up issue.

title: Fix assistant cookie path derivation and validate cookie paths
description:
Addresses #18621.

## The reported problem is a configuration gap

The Posit Assistant chat WebSocket depends on two cookies — `port-token` and `posit-assistant-auth` — whose `Path` is derived from the server's own view of its URL. Behind a path-prefixing reverse proxy the server has not been told about, that path cannot contain the external prefix, so the browser omits the cookies and the connection fails.

`www-root-path` exists for exactly this: *"The path prefix added by a proxy to the incoming RStudio URL. This setting is used so RStudio Server knows what path it is being served from."* Set it to the full browser-visible prefix and both cookie paths come out correct, with no code change — I verified this by tracing the pre-existing derivation. Where the prefix varies per session, as with Open OnDemand's `/rnode/<host>/<port>/`, the proxy can send it in `X-RStudio-Root-Path` instead. A proxy that sends that header must *set* it rather than forward one: `Request::rootPath()` takes the first value it sees and prefers it over `www-root-path`, so an inbound copy would win.

So this PR does not add a mechanism to recover an unannounced prefix. An earlier revision did, by having the IDE report its own base URL; that meant trusting a client-supplied value for a cookie path, which then needed authorizing against the base recorded at `client_init`, plus a decline path for every way the two could disagree. All of it existed only to paper over missing configuration, so it is out.

## What is fixed in code

Defects found while in this code, none of which involve a proxy and none of which configuration can fix:

- **`www-root-path` containing the route name collapses the assistant cookie path.** The `/ai-chat` route was located with a plain substring search, so `www-root-path=/ai-chat-hub` matched at offset 0 and the derived path became `/`, scoping the token to every application on the origin. The route is now matched only at a path-segment boundary, and the query string is excluded from the search. This one gets *more* likely as deployments lean on `www-root-path`.
- **The token-bearing response was cacheable.** `index.html` carries the auth token cookie and is always requested with query parameters; cache headers were classified from the raw request path, so it matched the long-lived `public, max-age=31536000` rule meant for images and fonts. Classification now reads the resolved file's extension, folded to lower case, so neither a query string nor a percent-encoded spelling (`%69ndex.html`) evades it. The case folding also matters on Windows, where `realPath` is purely lexical and leaves an uppercase extension as written.
- **The route matched anywhere in the URI.** `/ai-chat?x=/ai-chat/assets/app.js` served the file named in its own query string, and `/ai-chatXYZ/ai-chat/index.html` served index.html. Neither escaped the client root, but a cache rule or WAF reasoning about the URI path saw something other than what was served. The handler now matches `request.path()` at the start.
- **The assistant auth token could be scoped to the whole origin.** When the proxied URI carried no path the server could read — `proxiedUri()` returns the `X-RStudio-Request` header verbatim, so it need not be a URL that parses — the derived prefix came back as `/` and the token was offered to every application on the host. That case is now refused and no cookie is set. The check runs before the route is stripped, since stripping a route at offset 0 also leaves an empty string and that one legitimately means the origin root.
- **Cookie paths were never validated.** They are written into `Set-Cookie` without escaping, and both the client-reported path used in the default-root branch and the header-derived path used in the other were taken as-is. `isValidCookiePath` now gates both: it requires an origin-absolute path and refuses control characters, space, non-ASCII, and `;` `\` `?` `#`, along with `.` and `..` segments. On rejection the assistant cookie is not set at all and the port token cookie retreats to the configured root path. That retreat can still land on the origin when the configured root path is itself unusable, which the comment there now says outright: the IDE does not work without the port token cookie, so unlike the assistant cookie it cannot simply be withheld. All refusals are logged.

The validator deliberately accepts an empty path segment and a comma. Both are things a browser really sends, and since every caller falls back to a broader path on rejection, refusing them would widen the cookie rather than narrow it.

## Tests

- `HttpUtilTest.*` (core, 5 cases): cookie path validation, including the characters that could break out of the header, non-ASCII independent of whether `char` is signed, and root path normalization.
- `ChatStaticFiles.*` (rsession, 11 new cases): prefix derivation, segment-boundary route matching, query and fragment handling, refusal of an unusable derived path, and request-level tests driving `handleAIChatRequest` against a temporary installation for route matching, extension classification and traversal.

Both scopes pass in full. The `handleAIChatRequest` tests use a JavaScript asset rather than `index.html`, since rendering `index.html` reads client state and user preferences that are not initialized in the test binary.

## Also worth knowing

`Request::rootPath()` now calls a shared `normalizeRootPath` instead of applying the slash rule inline, so the session can give a configured root path the same shape. Same rule, no behavior change — but it is the widest-reach line here, since `rootPath()` feeds every server-issued redirect and, in Workbench, the sign-in cookies.

Workbench has its own cookie sites with the same derivation, and nothing strips inbound `X-RStudio-*` headers at any layer; both are tracked separately in the pro repo.

title: Show What's New once per release, not once per patch
description:
RStudio Desktop's What's New window is now shown once per release rather than once per patch.

The seen-state was keyed by release name **and** patch level, and the check required the stored patch to be at least the running patch, so a user who dismissed What's New on 2026.08.0 saw it again after installing 2026.08.1. The content is keyed by release slug only (`assets/whats-new/<slug>/index.html`), so what reappeared was the page they had already dismissed.

`hasSeenRelease(releaseName)` now matches on release name alone.

`markReleaseSeen(releaseName, patch)` still records the patch level the release was seen from, and that value is never read. The state file is shared with builds that gate on `entry.patch >= patch`; such a build reads an entry with no patch as unseen, and its update path (`patch > existing.patch`) never repairs it, so dropping the field would make What's New appear on every launch of that build after a downgrade within one release.

State files written by earlier versions are read unchanged: entries carrying a patch field still match by name, so users who have already dismissed What's New are not shown it again after updating.

### Testing

`test/unit/main/whats-new-state.test.ts` covers a patch of a seen release not showing again, the patch level being written into the entry, re-marking a seen release leaving it alone, and an entry written in the older `{name, patch}` form still counting as seen.

449 desktop unit tests pass; `npm run typecheck` is clean and `npm run lint` reports only two warnings that predate this branch. Not exercised in a packaged desktop build.

Fixes #18631.

title: core: reap child processes that exit before tracking
description:
## Summary

- close a SIGCHLD registration race in `ChildProcessTracker::addProcess` by probing the child with `waitpid(WNOHANG)` immediately after registration
- add a regression test that starts with an already-exited, unreaped child and verifies that registration reaps it and delivers its raw exit status
- keep the Playwright restart timeout at 60 seconds

## Root cause

The linux-server shard on [PR #18628](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/18628) did launch replacement rsession processes, pids 9805 and 10179. Neither ever created the session socket, neither produced an rsession log, and neither triggered the pending-launch exit callback. rserver consequently logged that each pid was still live until the one-minute pending-launch window expired; the next replacement then connected in 1-3 seconds.

There is a race between `launchChildProcess` and `ChildProcessTracker::addProcess`:

1. the child exits very early during the restart-boundary launch
2. rserver's SIGCHLD waiter consumes the signal while the tracker does not contain the pid yet
3. `addProcess` records the pid after the only notification has passed
4. the unreaped child remains a zombie, for which `kill(pid, 0)` still succeeds
5. the live-process guard added for #18572 therefore retains the pending launch until its one-minute expiry

That accounts for the otherwise contradictory evidence: no socket or exit callback, but a pid reported as live for exactly the pending-launch window.

Probing once after insertion closes the missed-notification window. If the child still runs, `waitpid(WNOHANG)` is a no-op. If it already exited, the normal exit handler clears the pending launch immediately and the buffered request can launch another session.

## Testing

- `rstudio-core-tests --gtest_filter='PosixTests.ChildProcessTrackerReapsChildThatExitedBeforeRegistration'`
- `rstudio-core-tests --gtest_filter='PosixTests.*'` (31 passed)
- `rstudio-core-tests` (615 passed, 8 skipped)

title: make a decorated section header flat in both directions
description:
Follow-up to #18613, from a review of that PR after it merged. Three shapes still reproduced #18602, and the outline half of the rule could never fire.

### Folding

A header whose leading `#` run is decoration now carries no heading level at all, and a header with no heading level neither contains another header nor nests inside one -- it ends the sections above it, and the next header of any kind ends it. Previously a depthless header folded as an h1 (`sectionHeadDepth(...) || 1`), which only moved the problem:

| shape | before |
| --- | --- |
| `## A ----` / `##########` / `## B ----` | the bar folds as an h1, adopts `## B ----` as a child, and folds it away |
| `##### #####` / `###### ######` | interior whitespace fails the delimiters-only test, so 5 and 6 compare as h5 containing h6 -- folds to end of document |
| `##### A #####` / `###### B ######` | both runs are within h1..h6, so the `> 6` cap does not apply -- folds to end of document |

The last one is the example the release note for #18613 names as fixed.

A header is decoration when it has no label, when its label is boxed in by a trailing run of `#`, or when its leading run is deeper than `######`. Labelled `#` / `##` / `###` hierarchies nest as before.

### Outline

`closeMarkdownHeaderScopes()` compares heading levels, so it could never close a section that has none: after a banner file header

```r
##############################
# Analysis script
##############################

# Load data ----
```

the closing bar stayed open forever and every later section nested inside it, indented one level deeper in the outline -- the opposite of the agreement between outline and folding that #18613 set out to establish.

Depthless sections are now marked `ScopeNode.DEPTH_NONE` and closed before a levelled header is added. Sections that predate the notion of a heading level, such as an R Markdown YAML block, keep an absent depth and are left alone, so they do not newly match the level comparison.

### Tests

Four new cases in `code-folding.test.ts`, one per shape above. The existing cases are unchanged except for `depth: undefined` becoming `depth: 0` where a header now reports "no heading level" explicitly, and `##### Section A #####` reporting 0 rather than 5.

All 14 cases in `code-folding.test.ts` pass locally (desktop-dev), as do `markdown`, `rmarkdown`, and `sweave` as a regression check on the outline change.

Addresses #18602.

title: install R from the rstudio-buildtools mirror instead of rig
description:
## Why

`rig` resolved and downloaded R at job time, reaching GitHub's API and CRAN or
the r-builds CDN on every e2e run. A hiccup at any of them failed jobs that had
nothing to do with R, and it has been a recurring flake source.

## What

Mirror the official installers into `s3://rstudio-buildtools` under a flat
scheme, and install from there:

    R/<version>/R-<version>-<platform>.<ext>

- **`dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh`** syncs CRAN (Windows, macOS) and Posit's
  r-builds CDN (Linux) into the bucket. It absorbs upstream's layout churn so CI
  never sees it: CRAN retires Windows installers into `base/old/<version>/` as
  they age, and shifts macOS builds between codename directories (arm64 R >= 4.6
  is `sonoma-arm64`, 4.1-4.5 `big-sur-arm64`; x86_64 R >= 4.3 is
  `big-sur-x86_64`, <= 4.2 is bare `base/R-<v>.pkg`). A full sweep is strict: if
  any CI platform is not available upstream, the command fails instead of
  leaving a pin only partly mirrored.
- **`.github/actions/os-install-r-unix`** and **`os-install-r-windows`** replace
  the two rig actions. Because the mirror is flat, they name the asset they need
  from the runner's own `uname` / `/etc/os-release` -- one unauthenticated GET,
  no lookup call. Both verify the installed version. The Unix action validates
  the same PATH that later steps receive; Windows exports `RSTUDIO_WHICH_R` so a
  per-user registry entry cannot shadow the R it just installed.

All nine call sites move over: the three macOS engines, Windows (both jobs),
Ubuntu 24 Server, the twelve Linux certification engines, the e2e-deps cache
seed, and the autocomplete scheduled run. Engine configs rename
`r_install: "rig"` to `"mirror"`; Fedora stays `"distro"` (r-builds has no
Fedora build).

## Exact versions and one shared pin

There is no resolver behind the mirror, so `r_version` is now an exact `X.Y.Z`
everywhere -- `release`, `oldrel`, `devel` and `next` are gone.

The default version lives once as `RSTUDIO_R_VERSION="4.6.1"` in
`dependencies/tools/rstudio-tools.sh`, alongside the Node and Workbench Go
pins. Reusable-workflow defaults are empty and call sites that want the shared
pin omit the input; certification cells still pass exact older versions when
they need them.

Most lanes already resolved `release` to 4.6.1. The PR orchestrator intentionally
moves from its historical 4.5.3 pin to the shared 4.6.1 pin, eliminating the
former coupling between the orchestrator, cache seed, and sentinel. The sentinel
now derives its cache prefix from `RSTUDIO_R_VERSION`. That transition costs one
cold R-library/pak cache cycle on PRs until the seed next runs on `main`, the
same one-time cost as any R pin bump.

The certification matrix validator enforces the exact-version shape, and the
same check is extended to the `r_overrides` dispatch input, which previously
only had to be non-empty: an override like `macos26=devel` would otherwise have
failed deep inside a cell that had already spent minutes provisioning.

## Before merging

The mirror has to be populated first, or e2e jobs fail at their R install:

    dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh 4.6.1
    dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh 4.1.3 macos-arm64
    dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh 4.2.3 debian-13-amd64 debian-13-arm64
    dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh 4.3.3 ubuntu-2204-amd64 ubuntu-2204-arm64
    dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh 4.4.1 ubuntu-2404-amd64 ubuntu-2404-arm64
    dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh 4.4.3 macos-x86_64 rhel-9-aarch64 rhel-9-x86_64
    dependencies/tools/upload-r.sh 4.5.1 macos-arm64

The first is the full 15-platform sweep, since the scheduled rotation runs every
engine at the default pin; the rest are the certification matrix's own pins,
narrowed to the platforms that use them.

## Verification

- Ran the Unix action's actual script in Docker against a local fake mirror: a
  full install on `ubuntu:24.04` and `rockylinux/rockylinux:9` -- both package
  managers, dependencies resolved, `/usr/local/bin` symlinks, `GITHUB_PATH`,
  and the version assertion. Platform detection additionally confirmed on
  `debian:13`, `ubuntu:22.04` and `rockylinux/rockylinux:10`.
- Confirmed all 14 version/platform pairs CI actually needs resolve upstream,
  including the CRAN fallback paths.
- Cross-checked that the platform keys the actions derive and the table in
  `upload-r.sh` match exactly (15/15).
- Mocked a partial full-platform mirror sweep (one existing asset followed by a
  missing platform); it exits 1 at the missing platform rather than reporting
  success.
- `actionlint`: zero findings introduced relative to `main`. `shellcheck` clean.
  `upload-r.sh` verified against bash 3.2 as well as 5.x.
- Every committed certification cell still passes the stricter validator.

CI on `dab6f162df` passed 27 jobs with 6 expected skips and no failures. The R
install path ran on Windows, macOS, Linux Desktop, and Linux Server, and every
lane resolved `RSTUDIO_R_VERSION=4.6.1` from
`dependencies/tools/rstudio-tools.sh`.

title: Avoid process environment races in R tests
description:
## Summary

- skip the monitor worker and its log destination for both `--run-tests` and `--run-script`

This addresses the intermittent CI crash in which an R-side environment mutation could overlap libc environment access from the monitor worker.

title: e2e: harden chat turn-completion wait and pref writes against transients
description:
Fixes the two flakes from [this pr-18586 e2e run](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18586/32160614087-1/all-platforms/index.html) (1911 tests, 2 flaky).

### chat-messaging "multi-turn conversation" (desktop-macos)

`waitForResponse` treated a single "stop button not visible" sample (500ms polling) as turn completion. But the stop button flickers off during the approval -> tool-execution handoff -- the trace shows the helper returned ~1.5s after clicking Allow, while the assistant was still streaming its post-tool continuation. The next `sendChatMessage` then timed out (15s) waiting for the send button, which stays replaced by the stop button until the turn actually ends; the failure screenshot shows exactly that state (message typed, red stop button, response still streaming).

- `waitForResponse` now requires the stop button to stay hidden across 4 consecutive samples (~2s) before concluding the turn is done.
- `sendChatMessage` first waits out a still-streaming previous turn (stop button hidden, 60s budget) before requiring the send button, so it is robust even if a caller misjudged turn completion.

### project_editor_theme "ignored appearance settings" (desktop-windows)

`setPref('ignore_project_appearance', ...)` rejected with the bridge's generic "writeUserPrefs failed" message. The trace has the real cause:

```
6: Unable to establish connection with R session when executing 'set_user_prefs'
Failed to load resource: net::ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE
Failed to load resource: net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET
```

i.e. the XHR died at the transport layer (winsock buffer exhaustion / connection resets around the preceding project close's session rebuild), error code 6 = TRANSMISSION.

- A pref write is a full-payload `set_user_prefs` RPC and thus idempotent, so `setPref`/`clearPref` now retry that specific failure signature (up to 2 retries, short backoff). Deterministic failures (e.g. unknown pref) still surface immediately.
- The automation bridge now includes the underlying RPC error detail in the rejection (via a `writeUserPrefs` overload that carries the error message), so future failures name the real cause in the report instead of requiring trace archaeology.

No NEWS entry: test-harness and automation-bridge (developer-only) changes.

title: Symbolize libSegFault backtraces in test runs
description:
## Summary

- capture `libSegFault` diagnostics to a temporary file
- extract executable-relative frame offsets and resolve them with `addr2line`
- use the exact adjacent split-debug file produced by package builds
- replay the original crash report and retain the existing GDB/core-dump fallback

This makes package-build crash logs useful even when Apport or another core collector consumes the core dump. It also resolves local and static functions without exporting additional symbols from the executable.

## Validation

- exercised the watchdog in Ubuntu 20.04 with a deliberately crashed, stripped PIE executable and adjacent `.debug` file; `crash_here(+0x...)` resolved to its function and exact source line
- `build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope rsession` (432 tests passed)
- Bash syntax and `git diff --check`

title: Stream localhost proxy responses
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

> Describe briefly what problem this pull request resolves, or what new feature it introduces. Include screenshots of any new or altered UI. Link to any Github issues that are related.

OSS components for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/11740 - Proxied non-chunked responses are fully buffered in rserver memory.

Fixes #18546 

### Approach

> Describe the approach taken and the tradeoffs involved if non-obvious; add an overview of the solution if it's complicated.

This adds the proxying implementation itself that is capable of avoiding buffering entire response bodies, but does not actually employ it against session proxying in `rserver`, where such a thing is probably highest value. It _does_ go ahead and make use of it for the localhost proxy. In [a follow-up](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/12209), I'll enable it for session proxying.

The basic idea is to
 * Use as good an http client implementation as possible to deal with exchanges with the upstream server
 * Use as good an http server implementation as possible to deal with exchanges with the downstream client
 * Attach them via a decoded, pure body byte buffer from the client; let the server re-chunk / encode the data as it sees fit.

The reasons for this approach, as opposed to e.g. reverting to acting like a layer 2 dumb proxy as soon as we're done looking at headers, was
  1. We actually already had most of the bits needed in our server implementation to perform chunked transfer encoding; this was the `ChunkHandler` / `ChunkProxy` code. It survives with some improvements, but has been renamed because now it handles proxying of unchunked responses. It's now `FixedBufferProxy`.
  2. This is the model employed by other OSS reverse proxying software I surveyed.

### Automated Tests

> Indicate whether this change includes unit tests or integration tests, or link a work item or pull request to add those tests to another repo. If the change cannot or will not be covered by a test, indicate why.

Extensive integration tests are included covering a decent range of badness that proxies can see in the real world. These are inspired by scenarios the Go team has coverage for in their standard library.

### QA Notes

> Ensure you have updated the QA Notes in the original issue.

### Documentation

> Specify which documentation has been added or modified and why (User Guide? Admin Guide?). If no documentation was added for a new feature, indicate why. If documentation was added in a separate PR, link the PR here.

### Checklist

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)

title: e2e: scale the pressSequentially timeout with the text being typed
description:
Playwright applies the one configured `actionTimeout` (10s) to a whole `pressSequentially` call however long the string is, so the per-character budget shrinks as the text grows. Two helpers type unbounded-length input:

**The assistant composer.** `shiny-app-r`'s prompt is ~940 characters, which leaves ~10ms per character to cover a CDP key-event round trip plus a ProseMirror transaction. A loaded CI runner does not reliably beat that. It showed up as a flaky first attempt on `desktop-macos` in the run for #18589:

```
TimeoutError: locator.pressSequentially: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('iframe[title=\'Posit Assistant\']').contentFrame().locator('.tiptap-input-editor')
    - locator resolved to <div ... contenteditable="true" data-testid="chat-input" ...>
    - elementHandle.type("Create a Shiny for R web app for a tip calculator. ...
  at ChatPane.typeMessage (e2e/rstudio/pages/chat_pane.page.ts:148:26)
```

That reads like a stuck composer, when the composer was fine and the budget was simply too small for the input.

**`typeInConsole`**, which also takes a per-keystroke delay. At the default 50ms a 200-character command spends the entire 10s in delays alone, so it could never pass. No caller is near that today -- the longest is 89 characters in `shiny-app-python.draft.ts`, which already spends 8.9s of the 10s budget -- so this half is headroom, plus consistency between the two typing helpers, rather than a fix for a failure happening now.

### Change

Adds `typingTimeout(text, delayMs)` to `utils/constants.ts` and uses it at those sites. It keeps the configured `actionTimeout` as a floor, so short strings behave exactly as before:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `"hi"` | 10s | 10s |
| 940-char assistant prompt | 10s | 47s |
| 200-char console command, 50ms delay | 10s | 20s |

`playwright.config.ts` now reads `actionTimeout` from `TIMEOUTS.action` so the floor cannot drift from the config.

Also corrects two stale comments in `chat-user-skills.test.ts`. `createSkillFile` moved from `typeInConsole` to `executeInConsole` in #17723 -- which writes the command with `editor.setValue` rather than typing it -- but the comments kept describing a per-character path, so the "~300 chars for `pressSequentially` reliability" note read like a live constraint on a path that has none.

This does not change the input mechanism -- `pressSequentially` is still required for both widgets (ProseMirror ignores `fill()`, and GWT needs real key events).

### Verification

`tsc --noEmit` passes, and the config still resolves `actionTimeout` to 10000 through the new import. The behavioral check is CI: `shiny-app-r` and the console-typing specs are `@ai`/desktop tests that need credentials this checkout does not have.

Follows up on the flaky attempt observed in #18589; no product code is touched.

title: e2e: stop the console completion helper from cancelling its own request
description:
Fixes `Autocomplete extras > new local variables show up as prefix completions`, which failed both attempts on desktop-macos in [this pr-18589 run](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/32179366367/job/95854791119).

### What the trace shows

The server answered correctly. The only `get_completions` on the wire returned exactly what the test asserts:

```json
{"token": ["foo"], "results": ["foobar", "foobaz"], "packages": [".GlobalEnv", ".GlobalEnv"], ...}
```

...and yet no popup ever appeared, and no second request was made.

`getCompletionsInConsole` typed the trigger text, slept 500ms, sampled `#rstudio_popup_completions` **once**, and pressed Ctrl+Space if it was not up yet. But typing already schedules a completion request: RStudio issues one `code_completion_delay` ms (250 by default) after the `code_completion_characters`'th character, and immediately after a trigger like `$` or `(`. With the RPC round trip at ~275ms on a loaded runner, the popup lands around 530ms -- just past the 500ms sample -- so the fallback fires straight into the window where that request is in flight or the popup has only just opened.

Neither ordering recovers, which is why both attempts hung for the full 15s:

- **Attempt 1** -- Ctrl+Space at monotonic `501428`, response due `501438.8`. Popup not yet showing, so `RCompletionManager.previewKeyDown` took the `beginSuggest` path, whose first act is `invalidatePendingRequests` (`RCompletionManager.java:1163`). The in-flight response then hit `token_.isInvalid()` (`CompletionRequestContext.java:95`) and was dropped -- and no replacement request appears on the wire.
- **Attempt 2** -- response arrived `~542079`, popup showing; Ctrl+Space at `542119` fell through the popup-showing branch to the catch-all `invalidatePendingRequests(); return false;` (`RCompletionManager.java:663`), which **hides** the popup. The helper then waited out its timeout on a session its own keypress had just cancelled.

### The change

Wait for the popup rather than sampling once, and force a request only after the implicit one has had its chance -- so Ctrl+Space is never pressed while a request is in flight. The forced request is retried once, since a slow enough response can still land in that window.

The implicit budget (3s) is spent in full only when the typed text raises no implicit request. Triggers ending in an identifier character or in `$` / `::` (`foo`, `lef`, `test_ls$`, `geom_line(linet`, ...) raise one, so those return as soon as the popup opens.

Triggers ending in `(` -- `cat(`, `stats::rnorm(`, `a(` -- raise none, and so do wait out the budget: `checkCanAutoPopup` rejects `(` as an identifier character, the `c == '('` branch (`RCompletionManager.java:858`) only forces an auto-popup for `library`/`require`/`requireNamespace`/`data`, and `previewKeyPress` has already cancelled the timer the preceding character scheduled (`:729`). Pressing Ctrl+Space there is the safe case -- nothing is in flight to cancel -- so the budget stays at 3s rather than being tuned down to reclaim the ~9s per console run. Ctrl+Space landing in an empty pipeline costs time; landing in a live one is the flake this PR removes.

Only the console helper is touched. The editor helper writes its content with `writeLines` and positions the cursor via `gotoLine` -- nothing is typed, so no implicit request is ever scheduled there and Ctrl+Space remains the sole trigger.

### Follow-up worth a look

In the attempt-1 ordering the explicit request invalidates the in-flight implicit one and **no replacement `get_completions` reaches the server** -- so a user pressing Ctrl+Space during the completion delay gets nothing until they type again. I traced that to the early-return region of `beginSuggest` after `invalidatePendingRequests` (`RCompletionManager.java:1163+`) but could not pin the exact branch from static reading; the missing second request in the trace is the evidence. Not addressed here.

No NEWS entry: test-harness only.

title: fix(jenkins): skip submodules when restoring commit history
description:
## What's wrong

Restoring full commit history for the version calculation surfaces old commits that pin submodule revisions from before a submodule's remote was changed. Git's default is to chase those revisions, and it looks for them on the remote currently configured — where they have never existed. The fetch fails, and takes the build with it.

This broke every Workbench platform build as soon as the `agentsview` submodule was moved to a different repository:

```
+ git fetch --filter=blob:none --unshallow origin
Fetching submodule dependencies/submodules/agentsview
fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref 68d2d5db261f5ce6b970920befdb93db9b0bb542
Errors during submodule fetch:
	dependencies/submodules/agentsview
```

That revision is the submodule's *old* pin. Nothing is wrong with the current one — the shallow clone had simply been hiding the old ones, since only recent commits were present and those all pin the current revision. Restoring history is what drags them into view.

## The change

The history fetch exists solely to make commit counting work. It has no reason to touch submodules, so tell it not to. Submodules are still checked out normally elsewhere in the build.

## Verified

Reproduced against a clone configured the way the pipelines are, with the submodule initialised:

| | exit | result |
|---|---|---|
| `--unshallow` (current) | 1 | `not our ref`, identical to the build failure |
| `--unshallow --no-recurse-submodules` | 0 | clean |

And confirmed the fix doesn't defeat the purpose of the fetch:

- repository fully unshallowed
- build number and suffix both correct, cross-checked against a full clone
- submodule still checked out at the expected revision

## This is a fix on top of a stopgap

`--unshallow` itself is not where we want to end up. It replaced a date-cutoff fetch that deepened history only partially and produced silently wrong build numbers, and it was chosen for being deterministic rather than cheap. It pulls the branch's entire ancestry when the version calculation only counts over a range a couple of weeks deep — roughly 18 seconds and 370 MB per cold workspace.

A separate issue is being raised to look at getting the same numbers more cheaply. Two approaches have been measured so far and neither is a drop-in: the GitHub compare API gives an exact commit count but cannot express the `--ancestry-path` walk the pro suffix depends on, and a `tree:0` partial clone is faster and smaller but makes the docs pipeline's path-filtered count time out.

Until that lands, builds need to work. This change is small, targeted, and does not make the eventual cleanup harder — if the history fetch goes away entirely, this goes with it.

## Notes

There are no submodules in this repository, so this cannot occur here today — it is landing here because the file is shared, and it will reach Workbench on the next upstream sync. **Workbench builds stay broken until that sync runs**, so it wants to happen promptly.

The same hazard applies to any future submodule remote change, not just this one.

title: 1Password integration + unblock @ai tests in CI (macOS, Windows)
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

Github issue: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-ide-automation/issues/5045

Two scoped chunks of CI/test work, kept together because they share the credential plumbing:

1. **1Password integration.** Move `CONNECT_API_KEY` (E2E Test Insights reporter) and a new Posit AI test account (`POSIT_AI_EMAIL` / `POSIT_AI_PASSWORD`) out of raw GitHub Actions secrets and into the `RStudio OSS GitHub Actions` 1Password vault. The only GitHub secret needed by the e2e workflows now is `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` (the bootstrap key); everything it fetches can be rotated in 1Password without re-issuing GitHub secrets.

2. **Unblock `@ai` tests on macOS and Windows CI.** Wire the Posit Assistant device-code OAuth flow into the Playwright test harness so the existing `@ai`-tagged tests (~50 tests across chat-pane and code-suggestions) actually run in unattended CI runs, instead of being silently skipped via `grep_invert: "@ai"`.

### Approach

**1Password (applies to both macOS and Windows reusables):**

- New `Load secrets from 1Password` step uses `1password/load-secrets-action@v3.2.1` (pinned by SHA, `export-env: true`) to fetch:
  - `CONNECT_API_KEY` → `op://RStudio OSS GitHub Actions/CONNECT_API_KEY/credential`
  - `POSIT_AI_EMAIL` → `op://RStudio OSS GitHub Actions/Login/username`
  - `POSIT_AI_PASSWORD` → `op://RStudio OSS GitHub Actions/Login/password`
- `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` is scoped to that single step (not the job env) so PR-controlled test code never sees the vault credential. A separate `Check for 1Password token` step gates the Load step via a boolean output (the `secrets` context isn't available in step-level `if:`).
- All caller workflows (PR orchestrator, scheduled, seed) updated to pass `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`. Fork PRs (no token) skip the Load step cleanly — reporter uploads warn, `@ai` tests skip with reason.

**`@ai` test enablement (Playwright side):**

- `e2e/rstudio/utils/ai-credentials.ts` adds `getPositAiAccount()` (reads env creds) and `buildPositVerificationUrl(userCode)` (constructs the `login.posit.cloud/login?redirect=/oauth/device?user_code=…` URL).
- `e2e/rstudio/actions/chat_pane.actions.ts`:
  - `signInWith(account)` clicks the chat pane's "Sign In" button, waits for the device-code view (`"Open Browser to Authorize"` visible), extracts the `XXXX-XXXX` user_code from the chat pane text, launches a **separate Chromium browser** (`chromium.launch()`, because Electron's CDP context doesn't support `Target.createTarget` — `page.context().newPage()` throws "Not supported"), and drives the login.posit.cloud form (email → Continue → password → Log in → optional intermediate Continue → Authorize → assert "Access Authorized"). Returns once posit.cloud confirms; the IDE's polling picks up the token within a few seconds.
  - `waitForChatReady` priority order: **(1) dismiss Trust Workspace modal** (it's an `aria-modal="true"` overlay; while it's up every element behind it including `signInBtn` reports `isVisible` but is unclickable), **(2) drive sign-in** if Sign-In is visible and env creds are available, **(3) check `isChatInputReady`**. The order matters because the tiptap composer's `contenteditable="true"` is set even in pre-sign-in welcome state, so a naive ready-check short-circuits sign-in.
  - On the sign-in path, `waitForChatReady` extends its own deadline by 30s after `signInWith` returns to give the IDE-polling phase its own budget.
- `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/sandbox-setup.ts`:
  - When no host `~/.posit/assistant` exists but `POSIT_AI_EMAIL` + `POSIT_AI_PASSWORD` are set, flips `PW_AI_SEEDED_POSITAI=1` so `requireAiCredentials` lets `@ai` tests run.
  - The warmup launch (already part of globalSetup) drives the OAuth flow once per CI shard, so the resulting token lands in the shared sandbox `user-home/.posit/assistant`. Per-spec IDE relaunches inherit it — tests that never open the chat pane (e.g. `code_suggestions.test.ts`) still see a fully authenticated Posit AI.
- `grep_invert: "@ai"` removed from the three caller workflows and from the macOS reusable's default; `@ai` tests now run unattended in CI.

**Carried in from the merge with main:**

- Windows workflows added by #17850 migrated to 1Password (same shape as macOS).
- Consolidated PR orchestrator (`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-pr.yml`) `macos:` and `windows:` jobs both pass `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`.
- Fixed macOS daily-manifest lookup: the resolve step queried `mac-arm64` / `mac` platform keys that don't exist in the manifest; corrected to `macos` (the universal build entry).

### Automated Tests

No new tests added — this PR is CI infrastructure plus the test-harness wiring that makes the existing `@ai` test suite actually run in CI.

Verifications:

title: add cross-platform E2E cert workflow + dispatcher script
description:
Adds `.github/workflows/cert-e2e-rstudio.yml`, a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow that fans out to the existing mac/win/linux-server reusables against three pinned installer URLs (a cert candidate's `.dmg`/`.exe`/`.deb`), and `scripts/run-cert-e2e.sh`, a thin `gh` CLI wrapper that drives the dispatch from one command on a release branch.

A `validate-inputs` job HEAD-checks each URL and asserts file extensions before the per-platform jobs start, so a typo'd or 404'd URL fails fast without burning hours of cross-platform runner time. The summary job emits a per-platform pass/fail table and fails the overall run if any platform did not succeed.

Draft until #17939 merges — the Linux Server reusable on the release branch still has the pre-#17939 input shape (no `build_from_source` / `post_pr_comment` / `workflow_call.secrets`); the `linux-server` job comment notes what to add once #17939 lands.

### Intent

Give release engineering a one-command way to drive the full E2E Playwright suite across macOS, Windows, and Linux Server against a *specific* cert candidate — the binaries the team has decided to certify, not a fresh source build and not "latest daily." Previously a cross-platform run against pinned installers meant manually dispatching three separate reusables, copying the same URL/R-version/grep_invert inputs into each, and hand-aggregating results. This collapses that into one dispatch on the release branch, with a single per-platform results table on the run summary.

### Approach

One dispatcher workflow + one shell wrapper, sitting on top of the existing per-platform reusables (no duplication of build/install/run logic):

- `validate-inputs` (Ubuntu, seconds): HEAD-checks each URL with `curl -sSL -I --fail` and asserts the file extension matches the slot (`.dmg`/`.exe`/`.deb`). Catches the most common paste error (wrong URL in the wrong slot) and 404'd builds before any expensive runner spins up. Also writes the run inputs to the step summary so the run page is self-documenting.
- Three platform jobs run in parallel via `workflow_call` into the existing reusables, all passing `build_from_source: false`, the corresponding `*_installer_url`, the shared `r_version` and `grep_invert`, and `post_pr_comment: false` (no PR context on a cert dispatch).
- `cert-summary` runs `if: always()`, prints a per-platform pass/fail table, and fails the overall run if any platform didn't succeed.
- Concurrency group is `cert-e2e-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` — one cert at a time per release branch; re-dispatching the same branch cancels the previous in-flight cert rather than queueing.
- Default `grep_invert: '@ai'` skips credential-gated tests for unattended cert runs.

#### How to kick off a cert run

**Prereqs**

- `gh` CLI installed and authenticated against `rstudio/rstudio` (`gh auth status`).
- The three installer URLs from the cert candidate build (typically `dailies.rstudio.com`).
- This workflow already merged into the release branch you want to certify — `--branch` / `--ref` controls *both* which workflow file runs *and* which `e2e/` test cut is checked out on each runner, by design.

**Recommended: the wrapper script**

```bash
cd rstudio
scripts/run-cert-e2e.sh \
  --branch rel-blue-plumbago \
  --mac   https://dailies.rstudio.com/mac/RStudio-2026.06.0-123.dmg \
  --win   https://dailies.rstudio.com/windows/RStudio-2026.06.0-123.exe \
  --linux https://dailies.rstudio.com/ubuntu-24/rstudio-server-2026.06.0-123-amd64.deb
```

Optional flags:

- `--r-version <ver>` — R version to install via rig (default `release`). Keep consistent across platforms for a meaningful cert.
- `--grep-invert <pattern>` — Playwright `--grep-invert` (default `@ai`).

The script also extension-checks the URLs locally before touching GitHub, so a typo errors out instantly.

**Alternative: direct `gh`**

```bash
gh workflow run cert-e2e-rstudio.yml --repo rstudio/rstudio \
  --ref rel-blue-plumbago \
  -f mac_installer_url=https://... \
  -f win_installer_url=https://... \
  -f linux_installer_url=https://...
```

**Where to read the results**

- Run page → **Summary** panel: the "Certification run inputs" table (what was tested) and the "Certification results" table (which platform passed/failed).
- Per-platform Playwright reports uploaded as artifacts: `playwright-report-mac`, `playwright-report-win`, `playwright-report-linux`. Download, unzip, open `index.html` to triage failures.
- Each platform's job page links to its own merged report under "Upload Playwright report".

### Automated Tests

Workflow-of-workflows; no application code changed. Validated locally:

- `python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(...))'` parses the workflow.
- `bash -n scripts/run-cert-e2e.sh` parses.
- `./scripts/run-cert-e2e.sh --help` prints the full usage block.
- Local extension assertions exercised via dummy `.dmg`/`.exe`/`.deb` paths.

End-to-end validation is by definition the cert dispatch itself; once merged into a release branch we'll dispatch a dry run against a known daily and confirm the per-platform table renders and the summary gate fails if a platform fails.

### QA Notes

To smoke-test after merge:

1. From a release branch with this workflow present, dispatch via `scripts/run-cert-e2e.sh` with three valid daily URLs.
2. Confirm `validate-inputs` prints all three "OK" notices and the inputs table appears on the run summary.
3. Confirm the three platform jobs spin up in parallel against the pinned URLs (not a fresh build).
4. After completion, confirm the `cert-summary` results table is on the run summary and the three artifacts (`playwright-report-{mac,win,linux}`) are attached.

Negative path: dispatch with a `.dmg` URL pasted into the Windows slot. The wrapper's local check should reject it before `gh`; if you skip the wrapper, `validate-inputs` should fail-fast in <1 minute.

### Documentation

Inline:

- `cert-e2e-rstudio.yml` header documents the trigger and the `--ref` coupling between workflow file and `e2e/` test cut. Each job's comment block notes the reason for its inputs/secrets (the mac/win secrets block explains why `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` is threaded through rather than `CONNECT_API_KEY`; the linux-server block notes what to add post-#17939).
- `scripts/run-cert-e2e.sh` header is the canonical usage doc — it's what `--help` prints.

No external docs (user/admin guides) are affected; this is internal release-engineering tooling.

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests
