title: Add Linux Desktop E2E engines for the missing architectures
description:
Until now every Linux Desktop E2E engine ran on one CPU architecture only. Of the eight Linux OS versions covered, five were tested on x86_64 alone, two on ARM64 alone, and only Ubuntu 24 on both. This adds the missing architecture for the other seven, so each Linux OS version can now be tested on x86_64 and on ARM64.

It also schedules the ARM64 Ubuntu 24 engine, which already existed but had never been wired into the nightly rotation, and moves the dedicated macOS 14 cron from Monday to Friday.

## New engine configs

Five Linux OS versions were tested on x86_64 only and now have an ARM64 engine:

`fedora-43-arm64`, `fedora-44-arm64`, `rocky-9-arm64`, `ubuntu-22-arm64`, `ubuntu-26-arm64`

Two were tested on ARM64 only and now have an x86_64 engine:

`debian-13-x86_64`, `rocky-10-x86_64`

Each is a new JSON file under `.github/e2e-linux/`, copied from the engine of the same OS version on the other architecture, with every key that must not collide between architectures given a distinct value: `sccache_key_prefix`, `installer_artifact`, `e2e_deps_cache_scope` and `pw_label`. The three *build* cache keys are deliberately shared where the two architectures' builds are byte-compatible, which the README already documents.

All seven are dispatch-only: they appear in the engine workflow's `os` choice list for hand dispatches but have no row in the nightly rotation, so they cost no scheduled runner time. Wiring any of them into the rotation stays a separate decision, one engine at a time.

## Fixes to shared hooks, found by running the new engines

Adding a second architecture exercised shared code that had only ever run on one, surfacing four real defects. Three affect engines already on a schedule.

- `ubuntu-22/build-setup.sh` read `JAVA_HOME_17_X64` and fell back to an `amd64` JVM path unconditionally, so the arm64 engine exported a nonexistent `JAVA_HOME` and the GWT build could not find javac. Now selected by `dpkg --print-architecture`.
- `debian-13/post-r-setup.sh` rewrote `/etc/os-release`'s `VERSION_CODENAME` to `noble` unconditionally. Its own comment gives the reason that must not apply to x86_64 ("PPM already serves trixie x86_64 binaries; arm64 is the only gap"), so the rewrite is now arm64-guarded.
- `fedora/e2e-setup.sh` was missing `libgit2-devel`, so `gert` failed to configure, cascading through `usethis` to `devtools`, which is in `required-packages.txt`. **This affects the two x86_64 Fedora engines in the rotation**, which appear to have been surviving only on a warm R-library cache.
- The four Fedora configs were the only container engines not passing `--shm-size=2g`. Docker's 64 MB default `/dev/shm` crashed the Electron renderer mid-suite (`Target crashed`, concentrated in reload- and repaint-heavy tests, alongside ~20 flaky results). **Also affects both x86_64 Fedora engines.**

`ubuntu-22-arm64` additionally needs `PKG_INCLUDE_LINKINGTO=TRUE` and a `-dev` header set: PPM publishes no jammy arm64 binaries, and pak plans the install assuming binaries, which omits `LinkingTo` dependencies and then cannot recover when PPM serves source.

## Rotation changes

- `ubuntu-24-arm64` joins the rotation on Thursday and in the Sunday full-matrix run. Its config already existed and was hand-dispatchable but had no rotation entry, so no cron path could select it. `ubuntu22` moves from Thursday to Wednesday to make room.
- The dedicated macOS 14 cron moves from Monday 16:00 UTC to Friday 16:00 UTC. All three co-dependent places are updated together (the `cron:` string, the concurrency group expression, and the `pick` job branch); a mismatch in any one changes behavior silently rather than failing. Friday 16:00 lands inside three of the eight October 2026 brownout windows for the deprecated `macos-14` image (Oct 16, 23 and 30), against Monday's four -- that cost is now recorded in the comment, along with the exact dates, verified against actions/runner-images#13518.

## Other

- `ubuntu-26-x86_64`'s `daily_platform_key` becomes `resolute-amd64` rather than `noble-amd64`, with the matching `resolute_amd64` output added to the scheduled workflow's resolve job so the version-pinned path stays correct. Both keys alias the same jammy-built deb today, so this is self-documentation, not a change of artifact.
- Three Ubuntu `installer_artifact` values gain their arch suffix, per the convention the README already states. `rstudio-desktop-deb-ubuntu-24` was a prefix of `ubuntu-24-arm64`'s value, and the merge job collects blobs by glob.
- The two Fedora x86_64 engines' `build_timeout_minutes` rise from 90 to the 150 every other container engine uses. A measured fully-cold container build in this work took 119 min 45 s, so 90 is not enough for that shape. Addresses #18404.
- `uninstall-posit-ai.test.ts` guards its `beforeAll` on `isPositAiAuthenticated()`. `requireAiCredentials` gates via `beforeEach`, which Playwright runs *after* `beforeAll`, so this file -- the only one managing its own session rather than taking the `rstudioPage` fixture -- turned what should be a clean skip into a failed test whenever its setup failed.
- Header and README claims that this work falsified are corrected, including the "no two engines share a cache key" statement and the examples of engines reusing another's daily build.

## Validation

Validated pre-merge with a temporary push-triggered caller, removed again in this PR. Eleven runs per iteration: eight daily-install plus three source-build, the latter chosen to cover the distinct build shapes (bare arm64 twice, container arm64 once).

Final state: 10 of 11 green, plus separate dispatches confirming the three x86_64 rotation engines this PR modifies (`fedora-43-x86_64`, `fedora-44-x86_64`, `ubuntu-26-x86_64`).

Both remaining failures are pre-existing intermittent test problems on dispatch-only or already-scheduled engines, not config defects, and neither reproduces reliably:

- `s4_unloaded_package.test.ts:192` fails intermittently under a full suite on Ubuntu 26, **both** architectures -- it failed a scheduled `ubuntu-26-x86_64` run during this work and passes when run alone.
- `ubuntu-22-arm64` failed one test per run but a different one each time, alternating between build paths.

title: Restrict localhost proxy connections to the correct address family
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

> Describe briefly what problem this pull request resolves, or what new feature it introduces. Include screenshots of any new or altered UI. Link to any Github issues that are related.

Fixes #18501

Open-source companion to 
  -- **Issue**: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/12142
  -- **PR**: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/pull/12181

### Approach

> Describe the approach taken and the tradeoffs involved if non-obvious; add an overview of the solution if it's complicated.

Main notable part of the approach is that instead of reverting to just connecting to some specific address such as `127.0.0.1` leading to v4, or `::1` leading to v6, we continue to keep DNS resolution in the loop. Not sure if this is important or not, but I figured I'd leave it as unchaged from current as possible in case some deployment is relying on atypical address resolutions for `localhost`.

So now we limit the address families accepted by our name resolution based on the incoming request's path `/p/` or `/p6/`.

TcpIpAsyncConnector::connect() gains an optional ipFamily parameter (mirrors the existing tri-state any/v4/v6 pattern in NodeResolver.cpp); TcpIpAsyncClient/TcpIpAsyncClientSsl gain a protected setIpFamily() setter; LocalhostAsyncClient/LocalhostAsyncClientSsl gain a public setIpv6() convenience setter built on it. ServerSessionProxy.cpp's proxyLocalhostRequest() now threads its existing ipv6 flag through to the LocalhostAsyncClient it constructs (and to the overlay hook), for defense-in-depth parity with the Launcher-mode fix that lives in the pro repo's SessionProxy.cpp.


### Automated Tests

Added tests that create listeners and confirm correct address family is connected to. It's perhaps a bit nondeterministic since it also relies on the environment producing both v4 and v6 values for `localhost`.

title: Restore native checkbox rendering under Windows contrast themes
description: ### Intent Closes #18493. With a Windows contrast theme enabled, checkbox state was invisible in RStudio dialogs such as Global Options. RStudio replaces the native checkbox with a CSS-drawn box plus a fixed black glyph image (`macCheck_2x.png`). CSS forced colors mode overrides `background-color`, `border-color` and `color`, but leaves background images at their authored color. On a contrast theme with a black background the box became `Canvas` (black) while the checkmark stayed black, so the checked state disappeared. It stayed legible under Desert only because that theme's `Canvas` is tan. The same applies to radio buttons where RStudio restyles them, which on Windows is the desktop client at >= 192 DPI (`windows-highdpi`, see `BrowseCap.java:253-262`). At standard DPI, and for Server in a browser, radio buttons already use native rendering and were unaffected. ### Approach While a contrast theme is active, hand the checkbox and radio button back to the browser's native rendering, which follows the system palette. Rendering with contrast themes off is untouched. The override is wrapped in `@supports` because GWT's legacy `CssResource` parser (`org.w3c.flute.parser.Parser`, a CSS2 parser) accepts media types only. A bare `@media (forced-colors: active)` block parses as an error, is dropped from the generated CSS, and the build still succeeds with only a warning -- the fix would silently not exist. GWT passes the body of an unrecognized at-rule through untouched, so the media query reaches the browser intact. Two constraints on that wrapper, both noted in a comment in the source: - Only `@external` class names may appear inside, since obfuscation does not run on a passed-through body. All classes used here (`macintosh`, `linux`, `windows-highdpi`, `gwt-CheckBox`, `gwt-RadioButton`) are declared `@external` at lines 23 and 56. - The `@supports` condition is trivially true. GWT ignores it, and the browser must not gate on it: naming a forced-colors property would drop the fix on browsers that shipped the `forced-colors` media feature before that property, as Firefox 89 through 112 did. The block is placed after the rules it overrides, since a media query adds no specificity. ### Verification - `ant draft` succeeds; the block reaches the compiled bundle immediately after the rules it overrides, so the cascade order is correct. - Running the checked-in `gwt-user.jar` parser over the stylesheet produces no new warnings (7 before, 7 after). - Extracted the checkbox and radio section verbatim from `themeStyles.css`, substituted the real image resources, and rendered it in Chromium with forced colors off and active, in both light and dark RStudio themes. With forced colors off the rendering is unchanged; with forced colors active both controls are native and the checked state is legible. Not covered: a manual pass in the running IDE against a real Windows contrast theme, which is worth doing before merge (Left Alt+Left Shift+Print Screen). The radio button path in particular needs a display at 200% scaling to exercise at all, and was verified only through the rendering above. ### Out of scope Check states drawn as `` elements do not participate in forced colors and are not fixed here; there is no CSS-only fix for them. Filed as #18494, covering the menu checkmarks (`menuCheck_2x.png` measures 1.42:1 against a black `Canvas`) and the cell-table tri-state checkboxes in the Packages pane, VCS changelist and unsaved-changes dialog.

title: Update Electron to 42.8.1
description:
Bumps the pinned Electron version from 42.7.1 to 42.8.1.

- `src/node/desktop/package.json`: `electron` dependency pinned to the exact version `42.8.1`, and the `allowScripts` key updated from `electron@42.7.1` to `electron@42.8.1` so npm's install-script gating still permits Electron's install script.
- `src/node/desktop/package-lock.json`: regenerated by `npm install --save-exact`.
- `NEWS.md`: Electron entry added under `### Dependencies`.

Verification: `npm test` in `src/node/desktop` passes (451 tests). The unit suite does not launch the packaged app, so `npm run package` is worth a manual check before merge.

title: data viewer: skip hidden-panel summary work, keep working copy across prompts
description:
A follow-up batch of performance fixes for the Data Viewer, from a code audit of the remaining #17806 hot paths.

### Changes

- **Hidden Summary panel no longer pays for summaries.** Every search keystroke and filter change ran `refreshSidebarSummaries()`, which issues `show=cols&filtered=1` -- a full per-column statistics describe of the fetched window (up to 200 columns) on the R main thread -- with no gate on the panel actually being visible. The refresh is now skipped while the panel is hidden and deferred to the next reopen, so closing the Summary panel genuinely makes search/filter cheap. Superseded filtered-summary requests are also aborted now, instead of each queued keystroke holding a connection.

- **The sort/filter working copy survives console commands.** `onDetectChanges` called `.rs.removeWorkingData()` for every open viewer on every REPL evaluation, before any change detection -- so sorting a large frame, typing `1+1`, and scrolling forced a full re-sort of the entire frame. The working copy is now discarded only when the viewed object actually changed. data.table objects keep the conservative per-prompt wipe, since `:=` mutates in place without changing the SEXP pointer, class, dims, or names -- none of which the change detection can observe.

- **Passive wheel listener on the frozen pane.** The pinned (row name) pane registered a non-passive `wheel` listener, which forces the compositor to wait for the main thread before scrolling anything under the pointer -- so a wheel notch over the frozen pane stalled for the duration of whatever the main thread was doing. The listener is now passive; the `preventDefault` it existed for is unnecessary because `#pinnedPane` cannot scroll horizontally and its `overscroll-behavior: none` already blocks scroll chaining.

- **Less per-scroll-frame layout work.** Each grid scroll frame updated all three custom scrollbars -- including the Summary sidebar's, forcing a layout of a panel that hadn't moved -- plus the column-overflow state, whose inputs scrolling cannot change. Scroll frames now update only the two grid bars; the full update still runs on scrollend, resize, and layout changes.

### Testing

- New e2e test covering the deferred-summary behavior: with the panel hidden, searching filters the grid without issuing any `filtered=1` request; reopening the panel fires the deferred refresh and shows filtered summaries (asserted via request sniffing, stable across `--repeat-each=3`).
- Full `data_viewer.test.ts` e2e suite passes (40 tests) against the modified grid.
- R-scope `dataviewer` testthat suite passes (207 tests).

### Out of scope (follow-ups from the same audit)

Larger items that each need their own design/testing round: fetching only rendered columns in row requests (currently 500 rows x 200 columns per block), incremental column-window header/body updates instead of full rebuilds, server-side memoization of `describeCols`, and working-copy caching for unbound `View(<expression>)` tabs.

Addresses #17806.

title: avoid leaking escape handlers in MiniPopupPanel
description:
## Summary

`MiniPopupPanel.show()` registered a new Escape `NativePreviewHandler` on every call without removing the previous one. `MathJax.renderPopup()` calls `show()` twice per render (once offscreen before typesetting, and once more in the async typeset-complete callback), so every inline math preview render leaked a handler that stayed registered for the lifetime of the app.

Once the popup was dismissed, each Escape keydown fired the leaked handler(s), which cancelled the Escape preview event app-wide and threw on the nulled `escapeHandler_` field -- surfacing as `(TypeError): Cannot read properties of null (reading 'real')` in optimized builds. Each show/hide render cycle leaked one more handler, so N leaked handlers produced N exceptions per Escape press.

## Fix

`addEscHandler()` now removes any previously registered handler before registering a new one (matching the existing `addDragHandler()` pattern), and the handler body uses the null-safe `removeEscHandler()` instead of dereferencing the field directly.

## Tests

Added an e2e regression test to `math_preview.test.ts`: render the inline math popup, dismiss it with Escape, press Escape again, and assert no uncaught client exceptions were recorded.

Verified the test fails against the pre-fix build (leaked-handler TypeErrors on the Escape presses, one per leaked handler) and passes with the fix, along with the rest of the `math_preview` suite.

Fixes #18474.

title: invalidate following rows when tokenizer context changes
description:
## Summary

An edit that changes only tokenizer *context* data -- the nesting depth tracked for rainbow parentheses / rainbow fenced divs, the indent recorded for a YAML multiline string, chunk fence widths -- left stale syntax highlighting on every row below the edit. The Ace background tokenizer propagated invalidation to following rows only when a row's end *state* changed, and tokenizer contexts (an rstudio-ace extension) were invisible to that check.

In R / R Markdown / Quarto documents the bug is masked by an unrelated mechanism: modes with a code-model scope tree rebuild the scope tree after every edit, and that path (`TokenIterator.tokenizeUpToRow`) force-retokenizes every row from the edit point to the end of the document. Plain Markdown and YAML documents have no such rebuild and showed the stale highlighting indefinitely -- confirmed by inspecting the tokenizer caches: after inserting a fence at the top of a 160-row `.md` document with rainbow fenced divs enabled, 79 of 81 fence rows still held their old colors.

## Changes

- Updates the `ace.js` / `ace-uncompressed.js` builds with rstudio/rstudio-ace#13: `BackgroundTokenizer.$tokenizeRow` now snapshots the incoming context with `structuredClone` (so contexts can hold nested objects and arrays, and each row's stored context is an independent snapshot that in-place mutation by a highlight rule cannot corrupt), compares the newly-computed context against the stored one with a structural equality helper (key-order independent, never throws, depth-capped), and invalidates the following row when they differ, exactly as for a changed end state. Review hardening: non-plain objects (Date, Map, Set, RegExp, class instances) compare unequal rather than silently equal, the clone is skipped for missing and empty contexts (the common case for modes that never touch their context), and the helpers are unit-tested in the fork. The rebuilt artifact also drops a stray hand-patched comment left from the #13605 investigation (now handled in the fork source).
- Adds regression tests for both unmasked modes. YAML: re-indenting a multiline string's `|` opener changes only the recorded indent (the opener's end state is unchanged), and an off-screen content row must be re-highlighted. Plain Markdown (the symptom reported in #18472): an unclosed fenced div opener inserted at the top of a tall document deepens every following block, and an off-screen block's fence must take the next nesting-depth color (colors are depth-based since #18467) -- a positive assertion, where the YAML test's is an absence. Both tests pin exact token type/value pairs on both sides of the edit, assert the target row sits below the last rendered row before editing (the off-screen premise the tests' validity rests on -- rendered rows are incidentally re-tokenized by the fold gutter's `getState()` sweeps), and fail against the previous ace build while passing with this one.
- Adopts the `cloneContext` / `equalContexts` helpers exported from `ace/background_tokenizer` in `RCodeModel.$tokenizeUpToRow`, whose parallel per-row cache had both halves of the same bug: a shallow `Object.assign` context copy (so a rule mutating a shared nested object retroactively corrupted the previous row's stored context) and an `assumeGood` short-circuit keyed only on the end state (so a context-only change stopped invalidation and following rows kept stale cached tokens, feeding indentation, folding, and the scope tree). Verified against the GWT testpage suite and a code-model e2e regression set.
- Adopts the same helpers in `TokenUtils.$tokenizeUpToRow` (the parallel cache used by `cpp_code_model.js`, touched on main by #18470), which had the identical shallow-copy and end-state-only-resume pair, and removes the comment there describing the limitation as shared with RCodeModel and the BackgroundTokenizer -- no longer true with this change.

The rebuilt artifact was diffed against the committed one before applying the fix to confirm a clean baseline, and again after, to confirm the artifact change is exactly the intended tokenizer change.

Merging note: after #18467 landed, the Markdown regression test was adapted to the depth-based color scheme (a closing fence at depth 0 no longer changes anything; the test now inserts an unclosed opener, which deepens -- and so recolors -- every following block). rstudio/rstudio-ace#13 should be merged into the ace fork alongside this PR so the committed artifacts and the fork source stay in sync.

Fixes #18472.

title: make console home/end span the whole wrapped command
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18447.

In the Console, `Home` / `End` -- and, on macOS, `Ctrl+A` / `Ctrl+E` and `Cmd+Left` / `Cmd+Right`, which Ace maps to the same commands -- stopped where a long command soft-wraps onto the next line, instead of moving to the ends of the command. R itself, R.app, Positron's console, and a terminal all move to the ends of the whole command, which is what readline does.

### Approach

Ace's `Selection.moveCursorLineStart` / `moveCursorLineEnd` are wrap-aware by design: they route the cursor's document position through `documentToScreenRow` and operate on that *screen* row. Since the console input runs with wrap mode on (`ShellWidget`), each visual row of a wrapped command behaves as its own line. That is the right behavior for a text editor and the wrong one for a command line.

`AceEditorNative.useDocumentLineNavigation()` replaces the six line start / line end commands on a single editor's Ace command table with versions that use document-line positions:

- `gotolinestart` / `gotolineend`
- `selecttolinestart` / `selecttolineend` (`Cmd+Shift+Left/Right`, `Ctrl+Shift+A/E`)
- `selectlinestart` / `selectlineend` (`Shift+Home` / `Shift+End`)

Both selection pairs are needed because which one a key reaches varies by platform -- on macOS `Shift+Home` is not bound to `selecttolinestart` at all. Overriding at the command level rather than intercepting keystrokes means every binding that maps to these commands is covered on every platform.

`ShellWidget` opts the console input in, next to where it turns wrap mode on.

**Scoping.** Each Ace editor gets its own `CommandManager` with its own command table, and the override installs *clones* rather than mutating the shared `default_commands` objects, so source editors are untouched. I verified this in the running IDE: after the console applies the override, `require("ace/commands/default_commands")` still holds the stock implementations (`function(e){e.navigateLineStart()}` and friends) for all six commands.

### Testing

Two Playwright tests in `tests/panes/console/console_pane.test.ts` put a command long enough to wrap into the console -- asserting via `getScreenLength()` that it really wrapped, so the assertions can't pass vacuously -- then check that `Home` / `End` land at column 0 and at the end of the command, and that `Shift+Home` / `Shift+End` select all of it.

Verified as a negative control: with the `ShellWidget` opt-in commented out and GWT rebuilt, both tests fail (`Shift+Home` selects only `", 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80)"`, the tail of the last visual row); with it restored, both pass. The full `tests/panes/console/` suite passes (46 tests, macOS desktop).

title: e2e: consolidate R package provisioning in the os-e2e-deps action
description:
Addresses #18488.

Stacked on #18487 (base branch); GitHub will retarget this to `main` when that merges. The diff shown here is just the consolidation.

## What changes

**The `os-e2e-deps` action now owns the whole provisioning contract.** `install-required-packages` defaults to `"true"`, and the action exports `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` (pointing at its `r-libs-user` input) to `GITHUB_ENV` itself, the same way it already exports `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`. The export is skipped when the caller already defines the variable (a job-level override wins) or opts out of the install. It is no longer possible to configure the install without the lookup or vice versa -- the half-configured states behind #18390 and the pr-18449 Windows CRAN-outage hangs.

With the action owning both halves, the per-workflow wiring is deleted:

- Windows main + Windows autocomplete-scheduled: the `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` job env and the explicit flag are gone.
- macOS x3: same (the `cache-scope` inputs stay -- they encode real ABI boundaries).
- Linux desktop: the conditional `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` expression on the test step is gone. The per-engine `preinstall_r_packages` pass-through stays as the escape hatch: an engine passing an empty value still opts out of both halves (a provided-but-empty input does not take the action default).

**The Linux Server workflow provisions the test user's library instead of a root-owned system library.** rserver rebuilds each rsession's environment from scratch (#18348), so no env var from the job can reach the sessions -- only R's own default user library path can. After `os-e2e-deps` populates the workspace `R-libs` tree, a new step expands the per-run test user's `R_LIBS_USER` template (`~/R/%p-library/%v`, resolved the same way `r-libs-setup.ts` does), copies the tree there, and chowns it. Sessions then resolve every required package with zero test-time installs, and because the user owns the copy, uninstall-flow tests (`missing_packages_banner`'s `remove.packages`) work -- which the root-owned seed this replaces could never allow. A real copy rather than a hardlink clone: `chown` on hardlinks would flip the owner of the runner's cached tree too (shared inodes).

The retired seed's curated list is folded into the single manifest: `readr` is genuinely used (`import_dataset.test.ts`) and moves into `required-packages.txt`; `tidyverse` is referenced by no test and is dropped. Note the DBI uninstall test (`s4_unloaded_package`) is `@desktop_only`, so nothing on server uninstalls anything seeded.

## Notes

- Net -33 lines, despite the new server step.
- Server's R-library cache key gains the `-req<hash>` suffix (it now carries the required set); `restore-keys` bridges from the old key, and the scheduled main runs save the new one.
- The `sudo -H -u` expansion relies on sudo's `env_reset` keeping the job's `R_LIBS_USER` out of the child environment so R's own default template is what expands; a guard fails the step if the resolved path lands outside the user's home.
- Verified: YAML parses; `actionlint` finding counts identical to `main` on every touched workflow (the new server step contributes none); the expansion one-liner tested locally with the template both set and unset.
- Out of scope (per #18488): `packageRepo()` in `r-libs-setup.ts` and the per-test `ensurePackageInstalled` still point at cran.r-project.org; with the library pre-populated everywhere these reduce to presence checks.

title: Resolve e2e daily builds per branch, not via /rstudio/latest
description:
## Problem

The e2e workflows installed the build named by
`dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/latest/index.json` while running the tests from the
checked-out branch. Those are two different branches whenever the alias lags a
rollover, and its `index.json` does lag: after the 2026.08 branch cut, the
`/rstudio/latest/` page served Autumn Hawkbit (2026.09) while
`/rstudio/latest/index.json` still named a Yellow Yarrow (2026.08) build.

CI reads the JSON. So the scheduled rotation installed a 2026.08 binary and ran
`main`'s tests against it, and every test covering behavior added after the cut
failed on every platform with nothing wrong in either the test or the product.
Both #18454 and #18470 landed that way: 8 of the 9 tests #18454 added failed,
and the only one that passed was the one asserting behavior that predates it.

## Change

- New `.github/actions/os-resolve-daily-manifest` derives the manifest URL from
  `version/RELEASE`, turning it into the "flower" path segment the same way
  `docker/jenkins/publish-build.sh` does when it writes the manifest. Reader and
  writer stay in step, and a manifest named after its own branch cannot be
  mis-pointed by an alias.
- The nine workflows that read `/rstudio/latest/index.json` now consume that
  output.
- The action validates the derived segment, so a malformed `version/RELEASE`
  fails instead of resolving to some other object on the dailies host.
- The scheduled workflow's `resolve` job gains a checkout, since it cannot read
  `version/RELEASE` otherwise.
- A missing platform key now fails with the branch and key named, and says that
  a source build is how to test a branch without a daily.
- The PR workflow's `paths` filter picks up the new action and `version/RELEASE`,
  so a change to the resolver, or to the input that selects which branch's daily
  it resolves, triggers the workflow that exercises it.

The action computes a URL and makes no network request, so it is safe in the
jobs that end up using an override installer URL instead of a manifest.

## Verification

- `actionlint` over all nine workflows reports the same 17 pre-existing
  shellcheck items as `main`, and no new ones. `shellcheck` is clean on the
  action's script.
- The slug derivation resolves `Autumn Hawkbit` and `Yellow Yarrow` correctly,
  with and without a trailing newline, and rejects `../../evil`, `foo/bar`, an
  empty file, `-leading-dash`, and `Autumn Hawkbit?x=1`.
- Both resolved manifest URLs return HTTP 200 with the expected branch.
- Every `daily_platform_key` in `.github/e2e-linux/*.json`, plus `macos` and
  server `noble-amd64`, resolves in the per-branch manifest.

No NEWS.md entry: this is CI wiring with no user-facing change.

Addresses #18498.

title: add support for split editors (two views of one document)
description:
Adds split editor support to the source pane: an editor tab can show a second view of its document, either side by side ("Split Editor Right") or stacked ("Split Editor Down"), so different parts of a file can be viewed and edited at the same time.

## Behavior

- The two views share the document and undo history; selection, cursor, scroll position, and code folds are per-view. This follows Ace's own `Split` implementation: the secondary view gets a cloned `EditSession` over the shared `Document` and `UndoManager` (sharing a single session is not possible, as Ace sessions own the selection and scroll state).
- New commands: `splitEditorRight`, `splitEditorDown`, `removeEditorSplit`, `toggleEditorSplit` (re-enables the most recent orientation), and `focusOtherEditorSplit` for keyboard navigation between the views. All are user-bindable, appear under View > Split Editor, and are also reachable from a new editor toolbar menu button. When a source editor already holds focus and the document is split, `activateSource` (Ctrl+1) also toggles focus between the two views.
- The split state is stored in a document property (`editorSplit`), so it is restored per-document when the IDE reloads.
- Commands that read the selection follow the view that last held focus: the run line/selection/statement/paragraph family, run-to/from-line, run function/section, re-run previous, `rstudioapi::getEditorContext()` and friends, and the status bar cursor position and scope. Everything bound to the document itself (persistence, autosave, lint/spelling/debug markers, chunk output, navigation, find/replace) stays on the primary view; the distinction is documented in `TextEditingTarget.Display`.
- Splits are a source-mode feature: the commands are disabled while the visual editor is active, and the split hides with the source editor when visual mode is on (the property survives the round trip).
- Inline chunk output and chunk toolbars in R Markdown / Quarto documents continue to render in the primary view only, and breakpoints remain managed through the primary view's gutter (clicks in the secondary view's gutter deliberately don't create breakpoints, rather than creating ones that wouldn't register with the debugger). The architecture deliberately keeps the secondary view a full `AceEditor` with its own line-widget manager, so chunk-output mirroring can be added later without rework.

## Notes for reviewers

- The 2015 proof of concept (#486) swapped the session after construction, which left the cursor-changed handler (bound to the old session's `Selection`) and the background highlighter pointing at a dead session. Here the cloned session is installed inside the `AceEditorWidget` constructor, before any session handlers bind.
- Sharing one `UndoManager` across two sessions over one document is safe: both sessions report the same delta object, and `UndoManager.add` dedupes it (`delta == this.$lastDelta`).
- The secondary view reuses `TextEditingTargetPrefsHelper.registerPrefs()` (the same path visual-mode chunk editors use), so editor prefs -- including Vim/Emacs keybindings -- apply to both views, and completion contexts are forwarded from the editing target.

Includes Playwright coverage (`e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/split_editor.test.ts`) for document/undo sharing across views, per-view cursors, focus switching, split state toggling, and run-line following the focused view.

Fixes #2129.

title: e2e: pre-install required R packages on the windows and macos runners
description:
## Problem

In the [pr-18449 all-platforms e2e run](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18449/31218669330-1/all-platforms/index.html), all three unexpected failures were desktop-windows tests hung in mid-suite package installs: `s4_unloaded_package.test.ts` stuck on `.rs.ensurePackageInstalled("DBI", repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")` with

```
warning: unable to access index for repository https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib:
  cannot open URL 'https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES'
```

and `shinytest2.test.ts` stuck on `install.packages("shinytest2", ...)` with no output, both until the test timeout.

The root cause is that the Windows and macOS e2e workflows never pass `install-required-packages` to the `os-e2e-deps` action, so the cached R library contains only the harness's DESCRIPTION dependencies. The `required-packages.txt` set (which already includes DBI and shinytest2) is instead installed from **cran.r-project.org at test time on every run** -- by globalSetup when CRAN is reachable, and by per-test `ensurePackages` self-healing when it is not. A CRAN outage therefore surfaces as mid-suite hangs rather than a fast, clearly-attributed setup failure.

Linux already works the way we want: PR #18390 flipped `preinstall_r_packages` on for every Linux engine, installing the set from PPM into the cached library before tests run.

## Change

- Pass `install-required-packages: "true"` to `os-e2e-deps` in the Windows main workflow, the scheduled Windows autocomplete workflow, and all three macOS workflows, matching the Linux engines. The set installs from PPM (not cran.r-project.org) in the deps step, lands in the cached `R-libs` tree, and a warm cache installs nothing at all. A cold-cache install failure now fails the "Install e2e test dependencies" step instead of hanging tests.
- Add the `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` wiring (pointing globalSetup at that same library) to the macOS and autocomplete workflows; the main Windows workflow already had it. Without it, globalSetup provisions the harness-default per-host path, which is a different, uncached directory on these ephemeral runners.
- Refresh the comments in `os-e2e-deps/action.yml`, `required-packages.txt`, and `r-libs-setup.ts` that described the required-set install as Fedora-only.

The Linux Server workflow is deliberately unchanged: it seeds a root-owned system library with its own curated list, because its sessions run as a per-run user and tests that exercise uninstall flows (fortunes, DBI) cannot remove packages from a root-owned library.

## Notes

- The R-library cache key gains a `-req<hash>` suffix when the flag is set; `restore-keys` still prefix-matches the old caches, so the first runs restore the existing library and top up the missing packages. The scheduled main-branch runs then save the complete library under the new key.
- Test-time `ensurePackages`/`ensurePackageInstalled` calls still exist as a self-heal path, and they still point at cran.r-project.org; with the library pre-populated they reduce to presence checks. Repointing them at PPM would be a possible follow-up but is not needed for this fix.

## Verification

- YAML parses; `actionlint` reports only pre-existing shellcheck style notes (identical count on `main`).
- `e2e/rstudio` source changes are comment-only.

title: e2e: fix the assistant workspace-trust click race
description:
Two `@ai` chat specs failed in a desktop run -- `chat-messaging` ("chat app
loads with root element") and `chat-guardrails` ("1: write to project
directory is allowed") -- both with a 5s `locator.click` timeout on the
Posit Assistant trust overlay.

`waitForChatReady` clicked "Trust this workspace", slept 500ms, and polled
again. The overlay disables both of its buttons while the `trustWorkspace`
round-trip runs -- about two seconds, since the assistant tears down and
rebuilds the conversation view on a grant -- so the next poll still saw the
overlay, clicked a second time, and that click sat in actionability retries
(`element is not enabled`) until the overlay unmounted (`element was detached
from the DOM`) and the timeout expired. The first click had already worked.

Changes to `e2e/rstudio/actions/chat_pane.actions.ts`:

- Click the trust affordance once per appearance and wait for it to
  disappear, rather than sleeping a fixed interval and re-clicking. Both
  steps are best-effort: the overlay can be torn down by a grant the poll
  didn't make, and a failed grant re-enables the buttons for the next poll to
  retry, so the caller's deadline stays the thing that fails the test.
- Cap the click and the hide wait at the time left on that deadline, skipping
  a step when the budget is exhausted rather than passing a 0 timeout, which
  Playwright reads as "wait forever".
- Sample the composer once more after the poll loop, so a grant that consumed
  the tail of the budget is still observed before an error is raised.
- Report a still-showing trust overlay at the deadline ahead of the sign-in
  check. The overlay renders over the sign-in panel without hiding it, so the
  sign-in check would otherwise win and blame credentials for a trust grant
  that never landed.

Verification: the full `@ai` suite passes on desktop; `chat-messaging` and
`chat-guardrails` were each also re-run on their own, with the log showing a
single trust click followed by an editable composer. `npm run typecheck` is
clean.

title: Don't let ConPTY teardown abort rsession at process exit
description:
On Windows, `ConPty::teardownLocked()` closes the pseudoconsole on a short-lived `std::thread`, and it is reached from `~ConPty`. Thread creation fails during process shutdown, so `std::thread`'s constructor threw out of a destructor and `std::terminate()`d the process.

rsession always exits through R's `exit()`. R.dll's C runtime is a separate CRT, and it calls `ExitProcess` without flushing rsession's onexit table, so rsession's statics -- including the `ProcessSupervisor` that may still own a live terminal -- are destroyed later, from DLL detach inside `LdrShutdownProcess`. `CreateThread` returns `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` there.

## User impact

`terminateAllChildren()` waits up to one second for the supervisor's children and then proceeds, so a terminal that outlives that window is still registered at exit. Measured in a Release build: rsession exits `0xC0000409` (`abort()` reaching `__fastfail`) instead of `0`, writing an `Application Error` event and a WER bucket, with no dialog and no hang. Cleanup and workspace save have already run, so nothing is lost. The effect is a crash report filed on ordinary quits, which is also why it went unnoticed.

Debug builds instead block on a modal "abort() has been called" dialog, which is how this surfaced: `rstudio-tests.bat --scope r` never finished, after the tests themselves passed.

## Changes

- When the closer thread cannot be started, the pseudoconsole close is skipped rather than performed inline. Before Windows 24H2 `ClosePseudoConsole` blocks until the output pipe drains, and on the shutdown path the reader that would drain it has already been terminated, so an inline close could hang exit. The OS reclaims the pseudoconsole and its client as the process goes away.
- `~ConPty` catches as a backstop, and teardown reaps both of its threads through `noexcept` helpers. `std::thread` needs both: `join()` reports failure without clearing its handle, and `~thread` calls `std::terminate` on a thread that is still joinable, so catching an exception on its own does not prevent the abort.
- Launch failures log `GetLastError()`, which distinguishes causes; MSVC reports every `_beginthreadex` failure as "resource unavailable try again" whatever the reason. An allocation failure that precedes the launch is reported without an error code, since `GetLastError()` would be stale.

## Accepted tradeoff

`teardownLocked()` also runs mid-session (the child-exit poll, and a failed `start()`), where nothing reclaims a skipped pseudoconsole, so a failure there leaks it and orphans the child. Left as is, and stated in the comment rather than described as impossible: the throw only occurs when `_beginthreadex` fails, which in a 64-bit process with no per-process thread cap means resource exhaustion under which a stray HPCON is the lesser problem. Discriminating the two cases (for example via `RtlDllShutdownInProgress`) adds a branch that would otherwise never execute.

## Testing

`rstudio-tests.bat --scope r` exits 0 with no dialog: 3869 pass, 0 fail, 11 skip. The guard logs `error 5` on the exit path, and a clean run leaves no orphaned `conhost --headless` or `cmd.exe` processes.

`Win32ConPtyTest` is 16/17 on my machine. The one failure, `CtrlCByteTerminatesBusyChild`, fails identically on unmodified `main` here and passes for other developers and in CI, so it is environment-specific and unrelated.

No automated test. The failure occurs only inside process shutdown, and `std::thread` offers no way to make its constructor fail on demand; adding an injectable seam for it would be test-only machinery.

title: Restore CALENDAR_VERSION to <YYYY>.<MM> form
description:
Sets `version/CALENDAR_VERSION` back to two components:

```
-2026.09.0
+2026.09
```

## Why

The branch update for 2026.08.0 (#18483) set the file to `2026.09.0`.
`docker/jenkins/rstudio-version.sh` composes the build version as
`<calver>.<patch><buildtype>`, so the extra component produced a four-part
version, `2026.09.0.0-daily+N`.

`jenkins/utils.groovy` keeps only the first three components when it derives
`RSTUDIO_VERSION_MAJOR`/`MINOR`/`PATCH`, so CPack named the Windows installer
`RStudio-2026.09.0-daily-N-RelWithDebInfo.exe`, while `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows`
built its expected path from the full version string and looked for
`RStudio-2026.09.0.0-daily-N-RelWithDebInfo.exe`. The Sign Installer stage failed
with `SignTool Error: File not found`, which has broken every Windows build on
`main` since the branch.

Linux and macOS glob for the package CPack actually wrote, so they were
unaffected, as was `rel-yellow-yarrow`, whose `CALENDAR_VERSION` is `2026.08`.

## Verification

`docker/jenkins/rstudio-version.sh` now prints `2026.09.0-daily+12` rather than
`2026.09.0.0-daily+12`, so the name Jenkins constructs matches the one CPack writes.

## Notes

Two follow-ups are out of scope here:

- `jenkins/utils.groovy` truncates a malformed version silently, so this class of
  typo surfaces during installer signing rather than at the Versioning stage.
- The same edit was made in June (3a340bc, reverted by ec91f62), which suggests the
  branch-update automation passes the full release version where `new-version.sh`
  documents a `<YYYY>.<MM>` calendar version.

title: e2e: don't race Chromium's Local State write in sibling config dirs
description:
The sandbox layout test polls for `electron-userdata/Local State` in every `config_*` dir of the shared per-run sandbox. Chromium writes that file through a delayed committer (~10s after launch), and `shutdownRStudio` SIGTERMs the process group -- so any Desktop instance that lives less than ~10 seconds (the sandbox-setup warmup probe, the multi-instance specs) can leave a sibling config dir that permanently lacks `Local State`. One such dir makes this test fail on every retry for the rest of the run.

The `Local State` check only proves something for an instance that is still alive, so:

- Sibling `config_*` dirs are now validated against synchronously written markers only (`config-home/rstudio-prefs.json`, `electron-userdata/`, `data-home/`), which is deterministic regardless of how long the sibling instance lived.
- The `Local State` poll is kept for the current worker's own config root (its instance is guaranteed alive), with the poll budget raised to 15s so it covers the committer's ~10s post-launch delay even when launch readiness comes up fast. The worker fixture now exposes its `configRoot` to make that scoping possible.

Verified locally: typecheck clean, and the desktop test passes both in a plain run and with `PW_WARMUP_LAUNCH=1` forcing a short-lived (~5s) sibling launch ahead of the worker's own.

Fixes #18475.

title: Keep pane-zoom state in sync with the visible layout
description:
> [!NOTE]
> The NEWS.md will need to be cleaned up before I merge this (once we've branched for release of 2026.08 and reset the NEWS file back to a clean state).

Fixes #18444.

`PaneManager` tracks a pane zoom in `maximizedWindow_` and `maximizedTab_`. Only
`restoreLayout()` cleared them. Several routes changed the visible layout without
going through it, so the bookkeeping stayed live while the layout looked normal.

While it is live, the `WindowEnsureVisibleEvent` handler re-zooms the next pane that
raises itself: a new plot, a package-list refresh, a render, a `?help` lookup. That
pane takes over the window and its neighbours disappear. An escape from that zoom
left the state live again, and the next raise repeated it.

`View > Panes` is a live readout of the tracked state. A check-marked `Zoom <pane>`
beside a normal-looking layout is the stale condition.
`View > Panes > Show All Panes` is the recovery.

## What changed

**One replaceable maximize action.** Every frame-level maximize gesture now goes
through `WindowFrame.maximize()`, which reads a settable action. Three gestures come
here: the maximize button, a double-click on the Console title bar
(`PrimaryWindowFrame`), and a double-click on a tabset's tab bar
(`ModuleTabLayoutPanel`). `PaneManager` installs one action per pane. The action ends
the zoom with `restoreLayout()` when that pane is the zoomed one, and calls
`maximizeDefault()` otherwise. This replaces `setMaximizeClickHandler`, which covered
only the button.

The javadoc records the two paths that still bypass the frame: the button on
`MinimizedWindowFrame`, and `EnsureHeightEvent.MAXIMIZED` through
`LogicalWindow.onEnsureHeight`.

**Sidebar.** The sidebar maximizes by a zoom of its column, not its quadrant. But it
can still be the pane-zoomed window, because Zoom Chat goes through `zoomTab` and
`fullyMaximizeWindow`. It gets the same zoom-aware dispatch. The matching menu path
is covered too. The un-zoom branch of `zoomColumn` calls `restoreLayout()` when a
pane zoom is tracked, so `View > Panes > Zoom Sidebar` and its shortcut restore the
widths and clear the bookkeeping together.

**Sidebar visibility.** A sidebar show or hide lays out the columns again, which can
undraw a zoom. `showSidebar` therefore ends an active zoom when visibility changes.

**Startup.** `MainSplitPanel` discards zoomed column widths (#16688), so a replay of
a persisted zoom always desynced. `ZoomedTabStateValue.onInit` now undoes the
persisted zoom instead. That includes the quadrant half, which
`DualWindowLayoutPanel` restores from its own state. A source window that holds no
documents is `HIDE`, which is also the quadrant state a zoom gives the zoomed pane's
sibling. So the doc-count rule moved out of `initPanes` into
`syncSourceWindowVisibility`, and the undo re-asserts it afterwards. That keeps an
empty Source pane hidden.

`getWindowForTab` now returns null instead of dereferencing a missing tab panel.
`Tab.SourceColumn` names a quadrant, not a tabset member, but `fullyMaximizeWindow`
can still persist it. When the persisted tab does not resolve, the undo normalizes
every pane rather than leave a sibling hidden, and logs a warning that names the tab.

## Tests

Nine Playwright tests in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/layout/panes.test.ts`. They cover
each clearing route, the reported consequence, and the non-zoomed maximize path
through the new indirection. Each one failed without its fix and passed with it. The
full `tests/panes/layout/` suite is 53 passed on desktop.

Two of the waits needed care, because the obvious signal passes before the thing
under test can happen:

- The pane-raising test waits for the Plots pane to be selected, not for the console
  prompt. The session queues the prompt event and wakes the event poller before it
  runs change detection, so at the prompt the plots event can be unqueued,
  undelivered, or not yet rendered.
- The reload test waits for the `set_client_state` RPC that carries the zoom. Client
  state reaches the server on a passive 5s timer, so a reload otherwise outruns the
  save and there is nothing to replay. Its post-reload assertions then sample across
  a window instead of once, because `expect.poll` returns on its first passing
  sample and the pre-replay layout is the passing layout.

## Manual verification

- The Console title-bar double-click ends a zoom correctly. The default
  configuration does not render that header: `ConsoleTabPanel.managePanels` calls
  `setFillWidget` while any secondary console tab is visible. The gesture is live
  only with the Terminal and jobs tabs closed, which is why it is not automated.
- The animated paths behave correctly with animations at the shipping default. The
  e2e suite runs with `reduced_motion: true`, so CI never exercises the 300ms
  restore. All four Zoom Chat escape routes were checked by hand.

Still not covered either way: a genuine session restart, as opposed to a UI reload,
and a window resize while zoomed.

## Follow-up

#18448 collects five pre-existing routes in the same family that this PR leaves
alone. One is a two-click reproduction that hides a whole pane column.

title: clean up tokenizer stack when R raw strings close
description:
## Summary

The R raw string rules save the entry state and expected exit suffix in the Ace tokenizer stack (`stack[0..2]`), but never removed them when the raw string closed. Since the tokenizer returns a non-empty stack as the row's saved state, every row after the first `r"(...)"` -- through the end of the document -- carried an array state such as `["#tmp", "start", "r-start", "r-rawstring", ")\""]` instead of the string `"start"`.

This breaks consumers that compare states with string equality. Most visibly, `rmarkdown_folding.js` compares row states with strict `!==` when searching for the next header, which never matches two array instances -- so in an R Markdown document, folding a header located below a raw string swallowed all subsequent headers to the end of the document. The array states also defeat the strict-equality caching in `r_code_model.js`, forcing full re-tokenization below the raw string on every scope-tree pass.

The fix splices the saved entries back off the stack when the raw string closes, following the sh-mode heredoc rules (`stack.splice`). While a multi-line raw string is still open, the stack legitimately persists (as with heredocs) so that the exit suffix round-trips through the per-row states; keeping the suffix in the state (rather than the tokenizer context) also means an edit to the raw string delimiter correctly invalidates the rows below it.

A review round surfaced a second path for the same leak: the chunk-end escape rule that `Utils.embedRules` installs is unshifted by Ace into every embedded state, so a chunk fence closing over a still-open raw string (or sh heredoc) exited the embedded mode without touching the stack -- a state passed through on every keystroke while typing `r"(` inside a chunk. The chunk-end rule now clears the stack when it closes a chunk; the host markdown modes never use the stack, so anything left there belongs to the interrupted embedded mode.

## Testing

Added a Playwright test asserting that rows after closed raw strings (both single-line and multi-line) carry plain string states, that raw strings still highlight as strings, and that folding a header below a raw string stops before the next header -- including below a chunk whose raw string is never closed. The state and folding assertions fail without the fix. `code-folding.test.ts` passes as a regression check.

Also added `src/gwt/test/highlight_test_r.html` to the headless testpage runner (`ant testpage`), driving the raw tokenizer the way `BackgroundTokenizer` does over delimiter permutations (dashes, two raw strings on one line, near-miss suffixes), plain R mode (unprefixed states), and chunk ends escaping unterminated raw strings and heredocs. 11 of its 27 assertions fail against the pre-fix tokenizer, and 4 without the chunk-end stack clear.

Fixes #18469.

title: fix C++ chunk indentation in R Markdown documents
description:
## Summary

Pressing Enter inside a C++ (e.g. Rcpp) chunk of an R Markdown or Quarto document raised an uncaught exception and skipped auto-indent whenever another completed chunk appeared earlier in the document:

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'width')

`TokenUtils.$tokenizeUpToRow` (used by `CppCodeModel` for C++ chunk indentation) called `getLineTokens(line, state, row)` without threading a tokenizer context, so every `onMatch` handler received a fresh empty object; the chunk-end highlight rule then dereferenced the missing chunk information unguarded. Broken since eafc5faf44 (September 2024), which introduced context-based chunk tracking.

## Changes

- `token_utils.js`: thread a per-row context through `$tokenizeUpToRow`, mirroring `RCodeModel` (including the `$invalidateRow` / `$insertNewRows` / `$removeRows` bookkeeping).
- `utils.js`, `markdown_highlight_rules.js`: guard the chunk-end rules so that a missing chunk context degrades to "this fence closes the chunk" (the pre-context behavior) instead of crashing; same for the quarto `#|` exit rules and the YAML multiline indent checks. The fallbacks derive their target from the current state name, so embedded modes (e.g. `r-quarto-yaml-*`) exit to the enclosing mode rather than escaping to top-level `start` (a dynamically assigned `this.next` is not prefix-rewritten by Ace's `addRules`), the markdown fence guard recovers the fence width from the `github-block-<N>` state name, and each guard warns once on the console when it fires so context-threading regressions stay observable.
- `Tokenizer.java`: thread a single tokenizer context through `doTokenize` (used by Reformat Code), fixing a pre-existing `TypeError` raised when reformatting R code containing Quarto `#|` comment lines.
- Same-class hardening for the shared-context hazards found in the same audit: the chunk / quarto / YAML multiline openers now store fresh context objects instead of mutating an inherited one (the per-row context snapshots kept by `TokenUtils.$tokenizeUpToRow` and `BackgroundTokenizer.$tokenizeRow` are shallow copies, so in-place mutation retroactively corrupts the snapshots saved for earlier rows), and the Sweave `\Sexpr{}` brace count is now stored as primitive context fields so per-row snapshots capture it.

## Testing

- New Playwright test: Enter inside an `{Rcpp}` chunk below a completed R chunk indents the new line (asserting the exact indent and the `r-cpp-` tokenizer state); the e2e fixture fails any test raising a client exception, so this also guards the TypeError directly. The test fails without the fix (exception raised, no indent).
- New `src/gwt/test/context_test_rmd.html` testpage (run by `ant testpage`) pins the chunk / quarto `#|` / YAML multiline / `\Sexpr` context fixes at the tokenizer level, including the missing-context fallbacks; it fails against the pre-fix code.

Fixes #18468.

title: color fenced divs by nesting depth
description:
## Summary

The rainbow fenced div highlighting in the source editor assigned colors from a counter that only advanced on closing fences, so colors did not follow the document's nesting structure: nested divs shared their parent's color, and sibling divs at the same level received different colors.

This regressed in #14744, which replaced the original color stack (it abused the Ace tokenizer stack, breaking editor tools) with a simple counter that tracked the wrong thing.

Fences are now colored by nesting depth, mirroring the rainbow parentheses logic in `rainbow_paren_highlight_rules.js`: a nested div gets a different color than its parent, siblings at the same depth share a color, and opening/closing fences of the same div always match. This also matches Positron's behavior for nested fenced divs.

## Testing

- Added a Playwright test covering the nested fenced div example from the issue, asserting the fence color at every fence row.
- Updated the existing sibling-callout test: two top-level divs now share a color (same depth) instead of cycling.
- Full `syntax-highlighting.test.ts` suite passes locally (desktop-dev).

Fixes #18464.

title: Disable library validation for bundled node in ad-hoc builds
description:
Closes #18450.

Ad-hoc signed macOS packages sign every file in the bundle with `--options runtime` and `entitlements/default.plist`, which grants only `allow-jit` and `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. The hardened runtime enforces library validation, and ad-hoc signatures carry no Team ID, so the bundled `node` was refused every `*.node` module in the package. The Copilot language server exited with `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` on `watcher.node`, and the assistant pane reported that the assistant was not running.

`rsession` and `Contents/MacOS/RStudio` are already re-signed with `disable-library-validation` from their `*-adhoc.plist` files. This adds the same treatment for the bundled Node.js.

## Changes

- `entitlements/node-adhoc.plist` — the two keys from `default.plist` plus `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation`.
- `entitlements/node-ci.plist` — the two default keys only. Signed builds re-sign every file in the package with Posit's Developer ID, so `node` and the modules it loads share a Team ID and library validation passes without the entitlement.
- `codesign-package.sh` — re-signs `bin/node/bin/node` with `entitlements/node-${entype}.plist`, and `bin/node-arm64/bin/node` when present.

`bin/node` is installed unconditionally (`src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt`), so it is signed with no existence test: a layout change fails the build. `bin/node-arm64` is copied only for universal builds (`package/osx/cmake/prepare-package.cmake`) and keeps an existence test. The distinction matters because a skipped re-sign leaves `node` validly signed with the wrong entitlements, and `codesign --strict` checks seals rather than entitlement content, so nothing downstream would report it.

The node re-sign is placed before the `Contents/MacOS/RStudio` re-sign, which re-seals the bundle and repairs the resource seal that re-signing a nested binary invalidates. Moving it after that step fails packaging with `a sealed resource is missing or invalid`.

Signed and notarized builds get the same entitlement set they had before.

## Verification

Ran `codesign-package.sh` against synthetic bundles:

| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| ad-hoc | `allow-jit`, `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`, `disable-library-validation` on both node binaries |
| ci | the two default keys only |
| `node-arm64` absent | skipped, exit 0 |
| `bin/node` relocated | exit 1, naming the missing path |

Confirmed the original failure and the fix directly:

```
$ .../bin/node-arm64/bin/node -e "require('.../darwin/arm64/watcher.node')"
Error: dlopen(...) ... ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED

# after re-signing with node-adhoc.plist
OK: watcher.node loaded
```

A from-scratch ad-hoc package build installed to `/Applications/RStudio.app` now signs in to Copilot and the assistant pane works.

No NEWS.md entry: ad-hoc signing is the local developer path (`make-package` uses credentials on Jenkins), so no released build is affected.

title: Document three e2e completion signals that pass vacuously
description:
Adds three entries to the "Waits and markers that lie" section of the
`rstudio-create-playwright-tests` skill. No product change; guidance only, so no
NEWS entry and no associated issue.

Each of these was found the hard way while writing the regression tests for
#18444 (#18454): in every case a test passed while never exercising the code it
was written to guard.

1. **A console prompt does not mean R-side change detection has run.** The
   session enqueues `kConsolePrompt` before calling `onDetectChanges`
   (`SessionConsoleInput.cpp`), so `executeInConsole` -- which resolves on the
   prompt counter -- returns before a plot raising the Plots pane, a package-list
   refresh, or a file change has been queued. A test that waits on the prompt and
   then measures asserts against the pre-effect state.

2. **Client state is pushed on a passive 5s timer.** `persistClientState()` fires
   `PushClientStateEvent` with `active=false`, so `ClientStateUpdater` reschedules
   rather than nudging. A test that changes persisted state and reloads outruns
   the save and restores nothing. The entry gives the `set_client_state`
   `waitForResponse` predicate, and notes that all state values ship in one RPC,
   so the wait also gates state written by other components in the same push.

3. **`window.rstudio.ready`, not a pane selector, gates post-reload state.**
   Workbench pane elements attach at construction, well before client state is
   applied, so `waitForSelector('#rstudio_TabSet1_pane')` returns while startup
   state handling is still pending -- including work deferred on a timer, such as
   `PaneManager.ZoomedTabStateValue.onInit`.

title: Provision AI credentials for Server-mode Playwright tests
description:
Adds AI credential delivery for Server-mode Playwright tests, covering both deployment types the suite supports. For the spawned in-tree server, a generated `--rsession-path` wrapper now carries `HOME`, `R_LIBS_USER`, and an unset `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` into each rsession. For an external server, whose environment the harness cannot set directly, a new provisioning step pushes credentials through a live session instead.

- Credential bytes for external servers travel over the Files pane's HTTP `/upload` endpoint rather than the R console, so they never enter the account's console history.
- Remote probes are guarded against false positives from an unreadable store or a stale console read (nonce-tagged results), and the scrub manifest is written incrementally so a crash mid-run doesn't strand tokens.
- Verified against a spawned in-tree server and an external VM, both credential sources, both providers.

Addresses #18348.

Two related but out-of-scope issues surfaced during verification and are filed separately: #18446 (pre-existing Server-mode sandbox data-home conflict) and #18457 (Posit AI credential gate doesn't account for token refresh).

title: Bugfix: Select localhost proxy uid check strategy per-kernel via startup probe
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

Fixes #18439

Kernels lacking upstream commit c51da3f7a161 ("net: remove sock_i_uid()", first in v6.17) intermittently report owner uid 0 for an established TCP socket that hasn't been accept()'d yet, causing 403 flapping when proxying to a busy or slow-to-accept localhost app (e.g. RHEL 10's 6.12 kernel).


### Approach

> Describe the approach taken and the tradeoffs involved if non-obvious; add an overview of the solution if it's complicated.

Extend the NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG startup probe to classify the running kernel using a deterministic repro (connect without accepting), and select one of three per-request verification strategies: Established (fast path, used when the kernel is confirmed reliable), Listener (queries the listening socket instead, safe on every kernel version), or Disabled. Root-run rserver always uses Listener, since a buggy kernel's uid-0 answer is indistinguishable from a legitimately root-owned listener. Falling back to Listener mode is likewise validated to actually work (and degrades to Disabled if not) before being committed to, including when the initial capability probe itself times out.

**Additional improvements**

* Fix log message generated when a request is rejected due to this check so that it now includes the uid number it believes owns the socket and the uid number the socket would have needed to be owned by to proxy the request.
* Also make the exact-match query itself state-aware: it's possible for more than one socket to exist in kernel hash tables matching the connected 4-tuple, for example an old lingering socket in state `TIME_WAIT`. The kernel's exact-match lookup path doesn't filter by idiag_states, so a TIME_WAIT/NEW_SYN_RECV decoy (or even a transient double-entry race in the ehash) might have previously been returned and its UID used. Now we reject matches outside the requested state (by just looking at the state ourselves in userspace) and fall back to the listener check on any inconclusive result -- including the handshake-timing window where our own connect() completes before the peer has processed the final ACK, which exists on every kernel version.

### Automated Tests

> Indicate whether this change includes unit tests or integration tests, or link a work item or pull request to add those tests to another repo. If the change cannot or will not be covered by a test, indicate why.

Updated unit tests

### Manual tests

I've built this on kernel 7.0 and confirmed the established-socket path is used, and built this on kernel 5.15 (Ubuntu 22.04) and confirmed the listening-socket path is used. Neither seem to be demonstrating intermittent proxy forwarding rejections anymore.

### QA Notes

> Ensure you have updated the QA Notes in the original issue.

### Documentation

> Specify which documentation has been added or modified and why (User Guide? Admin Guide?). If no documentation was added for a new feature, indicate why. If documentation was added in a separate PR, link the PR here.

None required, bugfix to an unreleased feature.

title: guard R runtime access on non-main threads
description:
## Background

Investigation of a customer crash report (internal escalation IDEESC-783): rsession on Windows faulting in `boost::algorithm::ends_with`, reached from `isMethod()` inside `http_methods::waitForMethod()`, with a stack `std::string`'s size/capacity fields clobbered by a stray write. Five occurrences, not reproducible on a clean install.

Code analysis initially suggested a live path on which the R runtime could be touched from a background thread: the offline service thread's `processSupervisor().poll()` reaching `AsyncRProcess::onContinue()`, which processes pending rstudioapi IPC requests with `r::exec::RFunction(...).call()`. Review feedback established that this specific path is already blocked upstream: `ProcessOptions::callbacksRequireMainThread` defaults to `true`, `AsyncRProcess::start()` never clears it, the session enables enforcement at startup (`SessionMain.cpp`), and `AsyncChildProcess::poll()` returns before invoking *any* callback when off the main thread. The only in-tree opt-out is the terminal's console process.

So the root cause of IDEESC-783 remains unconfirmed (WinDbg analysis of the dumps is still pending), and this PR is hardening rather than a fix for a known-reachable race. The hazard it closes is real but latent: `RFunction` previously had only a single `ASSERT_MAIN_THREAD` inside `call()`, and it ran after the constructor and `addParam()` had already called `Rf_install()`, allocated R objects, and pushed the R protect stack, and after `CodeExecutingScope` and the function-exists evaluation. Any off-main-thread use — from a caller that opts out of `callbacksRequireMainThread`, or any other background-thread code path — would race main-thread R evaluation and GC largely undetected.

## Changes

- `r::exec::RFunction` now refuses to touch the R runtime off the main thread at every entry point: both constructors, `addParam` / `addUtf8Param` / `addQuotedParam`, and `call()`, whose guard runs ahead of `CodeExecutingScope` and the function-exists evaluation. Any off-main-thread use also **poisons** the object, so a later `call()` -- even one subsequently made from the main thread -- fails with a clear error (carrying a `symbol` property) rather than executing with silently-dropped parameters. The poison flag is atomic, since it is written by the offending thread and read by the main thread.
- Guards are expressed via a new `REQUIRE_MAIN_THREAD()` macro in a new lightweight `core/MainThread.hpp`, which now also hosts `ASSERT_MAIN_THREAD`, `isMainThread`, and `assertMainThread`. Unlike `ASSERT_MAIN_THREAD`, it does no work at all on the main-thread fast path -- the thread check short-circuits before the `ErrorLocation` or any diagnostic string is built (`RFunction` methods are among the hottest code in the session layer). On failure it captures the calling function and file:line at the expansion site, so guard-failure logs identify the actual offending method; failures are logged once per object rather than once per touched entry point. The header is deliberately free of `core/Thread.hpp`'s heavy includes, since that header cannot be used from `r/RExec.hpp` (it pulls in `mach/boolean.h`, whose `TRUE` macro breaks `R_Interactive = TRUE` in `REmbeddedPosix.cpp`).
- The guard in `commonInit` runs before everything else, including the empty-name early return, so an off-thread `RFunction("")` is poisoned like any other; it also stops `sourceManager().reloadIfNecessary()` (which can evaluate R to re-source files in developer builds) from running off the main thread.
- `SEXPPreserver` now refuses to preserve objects from a background thread, and deliberately leaks its preserved objects, with a logged error, rather than calling `R_ReleaseObject` when destroyed on a background thread: either operation would mutate R's precious list off-thread, the same corruption class this PR closes. (`RFunction` destruction is the main way this can happen; the destruction-thread requirement is now documented on the class.)
- `AsyncRProcess::onContinue()` defers rstudioapi request processing to the next main-thread supervisor poll when invoked from a background thread, and `SessionRUtil`'s `Process::onContinue` defers its R-level `continue` callback the same way. As above, these callbacks should never fire off the main thread while `callbacksRequireMainThread` is in force; the deferral is defense-in-depth should a caller ever opt out.
- `SessionRUtil`'s R-level process callbacks now log errors from callback invocation, tagged with the event name, instead of discarding them.
- The regression test `SessionRTest.RFunctionRefusesNonMainThread` covers: the full off-thread construct/add/call chain, off-thread construction via both constructors leaving the function poisoned for later main-thread calls, and off-thread `addParam` poisoning a main-thread-constructed function. Sub-cases use calls that succeed with the arguments they end up with (`identity("x")`, `getwd()`, `list()`), so a missing guard yields `Success()` rather than an unrelated evaluation error, and every case asserts the specific "non-main thread" error.

## Notes

- Candidate follow-ups, deliberately not in this PR: `PreservedSEXP` has the same unguarded preserve/release pair as `SEXPPreserver` had; `r::sexp::getNamedListSEXP` and `r::util::iconvstr` can still run on the offline thread (the latter via offlineable `save_document`); and marshaling module R callbacks onto the main thread if an opted-out use case ever appears.
- The new error logs ("was called from non-main thread") are intentionally loud: they identify any remaining off-main-thread R usage in the field.

title: use word-level diffs for edit suggestion previews
description:
## Summary

Edit suggestion previews (Copilot / Posit AI next edit suggestions, and suggestions shown through the RStudio API's internal `showEditSuggestion`) previously highlighted changes with a character-level diff (`JsDiff.diffChars`). For semantically word-level edits -- most visibly variable renames -- the preview fragmented into interleaved character-level highlights around whatever characters the old and new words happened to share, e.g. `count -> total`:

```
[-c] [+t] o [-un] t [+al]
```

This PR switches the preview diff to word level:

- Adds a `diffWordsWithSpace` binding to `JsDiff` and a shared `DiffUtils.computeDeltas()` helper used by both preview code paths (`TextEditingTargetAssistantHelper.EditDeltas` for in-document rendering and classification, and `AceEditorDiffView` for the inline diff view).
- `diffWordsWithSpace` is used rather than `diffWords`: the latter ignores whitespace and its output does not reconstruct the original/replacement text by concatenation, an invariant both call sites rely on for position bookkeeping.
- Replaced token pairs where one side is a prefix or suffix of the other (pure extensions, truncations, whitespace-run changes) are refined back to a character-level diff of the pair, so e.g. `foo -> foobar` still previews as an insertion of `bar` (ghost text) rather than a whole-word replacement. The refinement is only accepted when it collapses to a single clean edit; pairs that jsdiff would fragment around extra shared characters (e.g. `total -> count_total`) stay whole-word replacements.
- Adds an `edit_suggestion_diff_granularity` preference (word / character, default word), surfaced in Tools > Global Options > Assistant, to restore the previous character-level behavior.

A pleasant side effect of the word-level diff is that single-word renames now classify as clean single replacements and render in-document, where the fragmented character diff previously forced them into the heavier inline diff view.

## QA Notes

Playwright coverage added in `edit_suggestions.test.ts`:

- a single-word rename previews as a whole-word replacement (whole-word insertion preview + whole-word deletion highlight);
- a rename sharing an affix (`total -> count_total`) stays a whole-word replacement rather than fragmenting;
- a word extension (`foo -> foobar`) still previews as a pure insertion, and a truncation (`foobar -> foo`) as a pure deletion;
- a multi-edit suggestion renders the inline diff view with whole-word markers, on the correct rows for multi-line edits;
- setting the preference to `character` restores the fragmented character-level preview;
- the granularity selector renders in Global Options with its saved value (`global_prefs_panels.test.ts`).

To verify manually, run e.g.:

```r
.rs.api.showEditSuggestion(c(1, 1, 1, 19), "total <- total + 1")
```

in a document whose first line is `count <- count + 1`, with the cursor at the start of the document.

Fixes #18437.

title: backport quality-of-life SQL tooling
description:
### Intent

Backporting a series of developer-experience improvements from `rstudio-pro` intending to make it easier to write good SQL code.

### Approach

Each improvement in this PR is meant to address a developer annoyance:

* QueryBuilder
    * SOCI's bound parameters have to be references to variables with a lifetime longer than the Query object. Failing to obey this rule leads to segfaults, but obeying it requires putting all bound parameters in variables, which feels clumsy and tedious.
    * Queries with dynamic column lists or dynamic where clauses require tedious string manipulation and memory management to ensure that the SQL is syntactically valid and the bound parameters have an appropriate lifetime.
* SqlIdentifier
    * Primarily exists to let the QueryBuilder classes distinguish between columns and string values.
    * Helps detect mistakes earlier in the development process (e.g., idiomatic use of `static const SqlIdentifier` allows column usage to be validated at compile time)
* SqlPreprocessor
    * The version of SQLite shipped with RHEL 8 doesn't support `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, which forces awkward workarounds to maintain compatibility.

The remaining changes are cleanups that were enabled by these new tools.

### Automated Tests

The new components are covered by unit tests.

### Documentation

Since these are internal developer-experience improvements, no user-facing docs need to be updated.

The new code components have API documentation comments in their header files.
