title: Group the --setup-db overlay flags in a public struct
description:
### Intent

`rserver --setup-db` (#18122, implemented in #18172, flags prefixed in #18282) dispatches to an overlay hook after it finishes provisioning the main database, so downstream builds can provision additional databases while reusing the master connection already opened — meaning the master password is prompted for only once per run.

That hook receives nothing about the flags the command was invoked with. An overlay implementation therefore cannot honor `--setup-db-print-only` or `--setup-db-show-password` for the databases it sets up, even though the base command honors both. The extension point is inconsistent with the command it extends, and the fully flag-driven non-interactive path — the one that makes this usable from a container or a one-shot provisioning job — is unavailable to anything running through the overlay.

Separately, two `--setup-db` failures that an admin can actually hit exited 1 with nothing on the terminal.

### Approach

Add `SetupDbOverlayFlags` in a public header (`src/cpp/server/include/server/ServerSetupDbOverlay.hpp`) carrying the two flags that apply to an overlay, and pass it to `overlay::setupDb`.

A struct rather than two `bool` parameters, because parameter names are not part of a C++ signature: adjacent same-typed bools mean a downstream override that transposes them links cleanly and inverts both behaviors silently — `--setup-db-print-only` would write the config file the admin opted out of and echo the generated password, `--setup-db-show-password` would leave a password neither persisted nor displayed. Field order matches `SetupDbFlags` and the argv accessors.

Not the full `SetupDbFlags`, because `ServerSetupDb.hpp` is private to `src/cpp/server` and should not become part of a cross-repo contract — and because most of its fields do not apply to an overlay. `host`, `port`, and `masterUsername` hold raw command-line values that are empty when the admin was prompted; `server::setupDb()` deliberately uses `masterConnectionOptions`' resolved values instead. `masterPasswordFile` is already consumed by `connectAsMaster`. `databaseName` and `databaseUser` name the main database.

Print `[FAIL]` before exiting on the two hard-error paths that can actually be reached: `connectAsMaster` and `server::setupDb`. Previously an unreadable or empty `--setup-db-master-password-file` produced a bare exit 1, indistinguishable from a refused connection or a bad master username, both of which do print `[FAIL]`. Because `--setup-db` returns before `daemonize()`, the detail reached only the file logger, which is not where an admin looks after a command they just typed.

Expand the hook's contract comment to cover what an overlay cannot infer from the signature: that `*pPassed = false` must be accompanied by a `[FAIL]` line, since that path is neither printed by `ServerMain` nor logged; that neither flag suppresses provisioning (the base creates its database and role either way, then `printOnly` redirects credentials and `showPassword` echoes the password); that the gate is `createDatabaseAndUser`'s `pUserCreated`, narrower than "no password was generated"; and that `masterConnectionOptions.database` is the `postgres` maintenance database, which an overlay must override before connecting to anything it creates.

### Automated Tests

No new tests. The OSS stub ignores the flags and is a no-op before and after, and the new `[FAIL]` lines sit in `main()` — `ServerMain.cpp` is not in the `rserver-tests` target, so that output is not reachable from a unit test.

Worth being explicit that the existing suite does not cover this hook either: no test in `ServerSetupDbTests.cpp` calls `overlay::setupDb`, and `overlay::checkConfig` is likewise untested, so "the suite passes" is not evidence about this change.

What does check the contract is the linker. The declaration in `ServerMain.cpp` and the definition in `ServerMainOverlay.cpp` are separate translation units, so a mismatch is a link error — and using a struct restores the property that a mis-specified override cannot link, which two bare bools had removed.

Added an `out` assertion to `ServerSetupDbTests.ResolveMasterPasswordFailsOnUnreadableFile`, which previously asserted only that an `Error` was returned, unlike its neighbouring EOF tests.

Verified in a devbase container: `rserver` links, `rserver-tests` links, `ServerSetupDbTests` 31/31 passes, no errors.

Note for downstream: Workbench Pro's override of this hook must be updated in lockstep with this signature change, or that build will fail to link.

### QA Notes

No user-visible change in this repo except that `--setup-db` now prints `[FAIL] setup-db: <summary>` before exiting on a master-connection or setup failure, rather than exiting 1 silently. Reproduce with a bad `--setup-db-master-password-file` path.

### Documentation

None. Internal extension point with no user-facing surface.

### Checklist

- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: recover from corrupt ace multi-select editor state
description:
Addresses #13605.

### The problem

An exception escaping into Ace's multi-select machinery permanently corrupts a source editor tab, producing the long-reported symptom cluster from #13605 (and the related #13436): mouse text selection stops working, typed input is silently discarded, multi-select mode cannot be exited, and editor commands (e.g. Ctrl+Shift+M) can land in a previously focused tab. Only reloading the IDE recovers.

Root cause: Ace's `forEachSelection()` and `$moveLines()` temporarily mutate selection state -- swapping in a throwaway `Selection`, silencing the real selection's `_eventRegistry`, setting `inVirtualSelectionMode`, detaching the range list -- and restore it only on the way out, with **no exception protection**. One mid-operation throw (from any document/selection listener) strands all of it. The stranded state is silent: with the listeners gone, nothing throws afterward; the editor just stops responding.

### The fix (RStudio-side only; bundled Ace untouched)

Ace behavior is deliberately left as-is so the defects can be filed upstream against stock Ace with the deterministic repro developed here (a follow-up task).

- **`acesupport/acemixins/multi_select_guard.js`** (the load-bearing piece): wraps `Editor.forEachSelection` / `Editor.$moveLines` with snapshot/restore semantics. The wrappers know nothing about what the wrapped code does in between, so they should survive Ace updates. Exceptions still propagate; only cleanup becomes unconditional.
- **`AceEditorNative.isMultiSelectStateCorrupt()` / `resetMultiSelectState()`**: extends the #13436 mouse-handler recovery to detect and repair leftover multi-select corruption (stranded temporary selection, editor/selection mode-flag disagreement, empty or desynced range bookkeeping, detached range list). Runs on tab activation and now also (deferred) on editor focus, with a `Debug.log` line so dailies show which corruption fires in the wild.
- **`AceEditor.focus()`** eagerly updates `s_lastFocusedEditor`, so `EXECUTION_POLICY_FOCUSED` command routing cannot go stale when the DOM focus event doesn't re-fire (the "shortcuts appear in another tab" symptom).
- **`applyChanges()` / `doSetCode()`** exit multi-select mode first; these run from async contexts (e.g. visual-mode canonical save) and previously drove Ace command streams through multi-select handling mid-corruption-window.
- **`AceEditorNative.setHandler()`** is now `$entry`-wrapped -- it was the one Ace-to-GWT callback that let GWT exceptions propagate raw into Ace's synchronous dispatch.
- Removed a stray `debugger;` statement that has shipped in **both** ace bundles since the #14804 null guard (June 2024); it froze the IDE whenever devtools were open and the guard line was reached -- exactly the situation when we ask reporters to debug. Note: the corresponding patch in the `rstudio/rstudio-ace` fork branch (`rstudio/globemaster-allium`) should also be amended, or the next `sync-ace-commits` will resurrect it.

Reviewed but intentionally not changed: `ShortcutManager`'s `disableCount_` (a stuck counter kills app-wide shortcuts). The `ModalDialogBase` open/close pairing is already idempotent and correctly ordered; a heuristic reset risks enabling shortcuts during a modal, so it stays as-is.

### Testing

New Playwright spec `multiselect_recovery.test.ts`:

1. **Exception during multi-cursor edit**: injects a one-shot throwing document `change` listener, types with 3 cursors active, and asserts the abort was real (marker exception recorded, partial per-range application) and that the editor survives (no stranded temporary selection, `inVirtualSelectionMode` clear, Escape exits multi-select, typing still lands).
2. **Recovery on reactivation**: manually plants the stuck flags, switches tabs away and back, and asserts the corrupt state was detected and reset.

Negative control (validated locally, not committed): with only the mixin's `require` commented out, test 1 deterministically reproduces the #13605 corruption -- `inVirtualSelectionMode` stuck `true`, temporary selection (`selection.index === 2`) still installed -- and fails. This doubles as the upstream repro recipe.

Companion spec `multiselect_basic.test.ts` pins the everyday multi-select behaviors the guard wrappers must leave intact -- typing at keyboard-added cursors, single-step undo of a multi-cursor edit, `splitIntoLines`, and moving lines with multiple cursors -- driven through the real keyboard shortcuts (so Ctrl+Alt+Down dispatches the `addCursorBelow` AppCommand, also exercising the `EXECUTION_POLICY_FOCUSED` routing).

Also run locally: `ant test` (572 unit tests OK; 608 testpage assertions pass, exercising the modified acesupport), `ant draft`, and e2e typecheck.

Note for reviewers: `ant acesupport` alone does **not** update what the dev shim serves -- `acesupport.js` is inlined into the compiled GWT output as a `ClientBundle` resource, so acesupport changes need `ant draft` to be visible.

title: fix inverted AssignProcessToJobObject success check
description:
Fixes #18430.

`initJobObject` tested `AssignProcessToJobObject` backwards -- the API returns nonzero on **success**, so the "error" branch ran on success (reading a stale `GetLastError()`), while a genuine assignment failure fell through to `return Success()`. The inversion has been present since the original 2011 commit (180f7d0f41, the Vista PCA fix) and survived the 2018 error-handling cleanup (7778b6edb4) unchanged.

Changes:

- **Invert the check.** A genuine failure now reports an error, and the `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` recovery -- relaunching with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` when the process was started inside a job that blocks assignment, the entire reason the branch exists -- becomes reachable for the first time. The success path no longer builds a `systemError` from a stale error code.
- **Check `SetInformationJobObject`** before assigning: a job whose limit flags never applied kills nothing on close (`KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`) and would trap children that must break away (`BREAKAWAY_OK`, required by Chrome), so joining an unconfigured job is worse than running without one.
- **Close the job handle on the failure paths** (the job has no members there, so `CloseHandle` just destroys it). On success it is deliberately left open -- kill-on-close fires when the process exits and the handle closes -- now stated in a comment.
- **Surface setup failures** (review follow-up): `initHook()` now returns the error -- it runs before logging is initialized, but its single caller `rsessionMain()` initializes logging 70 lines later, so the error is logged there with the consequence spelled out (child processes may not be cleaned up when the session exits). The relaunch path returns its `CreateProcess` failure into the same deferred log (and drops the now-unconsumed `_RSTUDIO_LEVEL` guard), and the exit-code relay reports `EXIT_FAILURE` instead of a stale `GetLastError()` when the child's exit code cannot be determined.

Reviewer notes:

- The one behavior change to weigh: the breakaway relaunch has been effectively dead code for 15 years and now can run. It only triggers when `AssignProcessToJobObject` genuinely fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` -- rare on Windows 8+ where nested jobs make assignment inside another job succeed -- and it is bounded: `_RSTUDIO_LEVEL` caps it at one relaunch, and if `CreateProcess` with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` is itself denied (confining job without breakaway rights), `initHook` returns and the process continues as before, just without its own job. Known caveat, accepted for this rare path: after a relaunch the desktop frontend keeps tracking the relay's PID, not the real session's, so PID-scoped integrations (such as the #18270 dialog watcher) do not see the relaunched process; this is stated in a comment in `initHook()`, with PID re-reporting to the Electron layer left as a possible follow-up.
- Verified by inspection and Windows CI only: this TU is Windows-only, so nothing compiles on the macOS dev box. The Windows e2e workflow's build job covers the compile; a manual check that child processes are still cleaned up on exit (and that startup inside a constraining job behaves) is worth doing on a Windows box before release testing.

title: fix intermittent console_actions restore error
description:
## Summary

Fixes the intermittent "Error restoring session (console_actions): An error occurred while parsing json. Offset: NNNNN" error seen when resuming a session.

### Root cause

Since #17606 (v2026.05.0), `json::Value::parse` routes input through rapidjson's `AutoUTFInputStream`, which transcodes and therefore *validates* UTF-8 in strings; previously, invalid UTF-8 inside JSON strings was accepted silently. The console actions writer, however, has always been able to produce invalid UTF-8:

- `ConsoleActions::flush()` chunks long console lines at fixed 512-byte boundaries, splitting multi-byte UTF-8 characters across two actions. Any single line longer than 512 bytes containing multi-byte characters (CJK text, or the Unicode block characters that cli progress bars redraw on one line) is nearly guaranteed to be torn mid-character.
- Raw non-UTF-8 bytes in console output (e.g. `cat("\xff")`) are captured verbatim.

The serializer writes these bytes into `console_actions` unvalidated, so the save succeeds and the failure only surfaces at the next session resume, as a parse error at the byte offset of the torn character. Reproducible with `cat(strrep("\u2588", 400))` followed by a session suspend/resume (on any platform, despite the issue title).

### Fix

- `ConsoleActions::flush()` now backs chunk boundaries off incomplete UTF-8 suffixes (via the existing `string_utils::utf8IncompleteSuffixLength`), so multi-byte characters are never split across actions.
- Action data is sanitized with `string_utils::utf8Clean` at capture time, so genuinely invalid bytes (raw `cat("\xff")` output, output torn at a flush boundary) can no longer poison the saved state.
- `ConsoleActions::loadFromFile` now discards unparseable or malformed `console_actions` files with a logged warning instead of failing session restore -- console actions are just a replay of prior console output, and this lets state written by affected releases (v2026.05.0 through v2026.07.1) recover cleanly. Real I/O errors are still reported as before.

Note: `utf8Clean` accepts a few sequences rapidjson rejects (e.g. overlong encodings), so the load-time tolerance also serves as the backstop for such residual cases.

### Tests

- Unit: added `SessionConsoleActionsTests.cpp` (rsession scope) covering: chunking of long multi-byte lines produces individually-valid chunks that reassemble to the original output; invalid bytes survive a save/load round trip sanitized; and unparseable/malformed `console_actions` files are discarded without error. Full `rsession` test scope passes (409 tests).
- E2E: added a case to `session_suspend.test.ts` that emits a long multi-byte console line, suspends, resumes, then reloads the page so the console re-renders purely from the restored console actions, asserting the replay is intact and no "Error restoring session" message appears. Verified to fail against the unfixed backend with the exact error from the issue (the reload step matters: without it the client's surviving console DOM masks the lost replay). Full suspend spec passes in server-dev mode.

Fixes #18382.

title: publish windows debug symbols to rstudio-debug-symbols
description:
Addresses #18435.

Windows builds compile as `RelWithDebInfo`, so the linker produces PDBs for all of our binaries, but nothing ever collected or published them -- only the Linux pipeline uploads debug symbols to `s3://rstudio-debug-symbols`. This PR adds the Windows equivalent:

- `package/win32/scripts/upload-debug-symbols.ps1` collects the linker PDBs for the shipped binaries into `<product>-windows-x86_64.zip` and uploads it to `s3://rstudio-debug-symbols/<version>/`, following the naming convention of `package/linux/scripts/upload-debug-symbols`. A zip is used rather than tar.xz since these symbols are consumed on Windows. The archive keeps `x64/` and `x86/` folders because the 32-bit session slice's PDB file names collide with the 64-bit ones.
- A new "Upload Debug Symbols" stage in `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` (gated on `PUBLISH`, like the installer upload) runs the script after packaging.

Collected PDBs: `rsession.exe`, `rsession-utf8.exe`, `rsession.dll` (as `rsession-shared.pdb`, which carries most of the session debug info), `consoleio.exe`, `rpostback.exe`, `diagnostics.exe`, plus the multiarch x86 `rsession.exe`/`rsession.dll`. The list intentionally mirrors the executables signed in the "Sign Executables" stage; `rstudio.exe` is the prebuilt Electron binary and has no PDB of ours.

### Notes for review / verification

- The upload assumes the `build` role in the build account (same role the Linux symbol upload uses), via `withAWS` with an explicit region since the Windows container cannot reach the instance-metadata endpoint. If that role cannot be assumed from the Windows agents, this stage will fail at upload time and the role/permissions will need an infra tweak.
- The script uses `[System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]` directly instead of `Compress-Archive`, which on Windows PowerShell 5.1 fails on files larger than 2 GB (`rsession-shared.pdb` can exceed that).
- This cannot be exercised by PR builds (the stage is gated on `PUBLISH`), so it needs verification against the first hourly/daily build after merge.

title: Backport the E2E rotation workflow and engines to Pacific Dogwood
description:
Backports the unified E2E rotation workflow (`os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml`) from `main` so the full engine slate can be dispatched manually against Pacific Dogwood daily builds with the branch's own test code.

All five files are verbatim copies from `main`:

- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml`—the rotation workflow (manual dispatch only on this branch; cron fires solely from the default branch)

title: strip OSC escape sequences from terminal buffer
description:
## Summary

The `stripAnsi` path used by `rstudioapi::terminalBuffer()` and the "Copy Terminal to Editor" command only removed CSI-style escape codes and BEL-terminated OSC 0 (window title) sequences. Any other OSC sequence passed through payload and all -- most visibly the OSC 3008 context sequences ([systemd.io/OSC_CONTEXT](https://systemd.io/OSC_CONTEXT/)) that systemd 258+ emits around every shell prompt on recent Linux distributions (Ubuntu 26, Fedora 44). Their payloads carry machine id, hostname, user, and cwd, which is the "metadata" reported in the issue; and because the per-command context sequence is emitted after the echoed command line, it glues onto the front of the command's first output line, which is what broke e2e greps like `grepl("^2$", terminalBuffer(...))`.

`stripAnsiCodes()` now removes string-type sequences -- OSC (`ESC ]`), DCS (`ESC P`), SOS (`ESC X`), PM (`ESC ^`), APC (`ESC _`) -- with either a BEL or ST (`ESC \`) terminator, payload included. This also covers OSC 7 cwd reports, OSC 8 hyperlinks (e.g. from the cli R package), and OSC 133/633 shell-integration marks. The payload match excludes newlines so an unterminated sequence cannot swallow subsequent lines, and the terminator is optional so a sequence truncated at end of line is still removed. This pass runs before the existing patterns, which would otherwise consume just the introducer (e.g. `ESC P`) and leave the payload behind as visible text.

The second commit replaces the CSI pattern (an old snapshot of chalk's ansi-regex that enumerated specific final bytes) with the ECMA-48 CSI grammar -- parameter bytes 0x30-0x3F, intermediate bytes 0x20-0x2F, one final byte 0x40-0x7E -- so colon-separated SGR parameters (`ESC[38:5:196m`, ITU T.416) and sequences with intermediate bytes (e.g. DECSCUSR `ESC[1 q`) no longer leave partial tails like `:5:196m` behind. Non-CSI forms the old pattern happened to catch (`ESC ( B` charset designation, `ESC =` / `ESC >` keypad modes, `ESC 7` / `ESC 8`) move to a dedicated pattern. The 8-bit CSI introducer `0x9B` is no longer matched: `stripAnsiCodes()` operates on UTF-8 bytes, where `0x9B` is a valid continuation byte, so matching it could corrupt multibyte text (e.g. `"dějm"`-style sequences containing U+011B).

Both the R API (`rs_terminalBuffer`) and the GWT `sendTerminalToEditor` RPC (`process_get_buffer`) share this helper, so one change covers both paths. `terminalBuffer(id, stripAnsi = FALSE)` still returns the raw stream, unchanged.

## Tests

Added gtest coverage in `AnsiCodeParserTests.cpp`: ST-terminated OSC 3008 context sequences (the issue's exact shape, including the payload glued to an output line), BEL-terminated OSC 0/7, OSC 8 hyperlinks (targets stripped, link text kept), DCS, an unterminated OSC confined to its line, colon-form SGR, CSI with intermediate bytes, non-CSI escape forms, and UTF-8 text containing a `0x9B` continuation byte surviving intact. Full `rstudio-core-tests` suite passes (464 tests).

Fixes #18194.

title: stop win32 output capture from logging unboundedly on echo write failure
description:
## Summary

Windows twin of #18398 / PR #18399. `standardStreamCaptureThread` in `Win32OutputCapture.cpp` had the same unbounded-logging shape in two places:

- A failed `WriteFile` to the saved `CONOUT$` console handle was logged on every failure, with no "skip further writes" flag. With a stderr log destination active (`log-stderr=1`, the same option that enables the echo in the first place), each logged error lands on the redirected stderr pipe, is read back by the stderr capture thread, fails to echo again, and logs again -- the same self-sustaining full-CPU loop fixed for Posix in #18399.
- A `ReadFile` failure was logged inside `while (true)` with no bound or backoff, so a persistent read error would also log unboundedly (and spin at full speed).

Reachability is lower than on Posix: in Desktop mode there is no console, so the echo path is disabled at startup. The exposure is a Windows session launched with a console attached and `log-stderr=1`, where the console handle later becomes unwritable.

## Fix

Mirrors #18399:

- On the first echo-write failure, stop echoing to the console for the rest of the session and log the error once. The error code is captured inside the mutex, immediately after the failed `WriteFile`, so an intervening call cannot clobber `GetLastError()`.
- Log only the first `ReadFile` failure, and back off with a short sleep on failed reads so a persistent read error cannot busy-spin.

Client-visible console output is unaffected -- it flows through the capture handlers, not the echo path.

## Verification

This is a Windows-only translation unit, so it cannot be compiled from this macOS checkout; the Windows CI build on this PR is the compile gate. Reproducing the full loop requires a console-attached Windows session with stderr logging whose console becomes unwritable, so this has not been exercised end-to-end.

Addresses #18414.

title: Fall back to DOM renderer on terminal WebGL context loss
description:
Fixes #18393.

Since the xterm.js 6.0 upgrade (#16820), the default `"canvas"` value of the `terminal_renderer` preference maps to the xterm.js WebGL addon, but RStudio never subscribed to `WebglAddon.onContextLoss`. When a terminal's WebGL context was lost (GPU process crash, graphics driver reset, or the browser reclaiming a context when too many were live), the addon stayed loaded with a dead context: input still reached the shell, but nothing painted, so the terminal appeared hung until it was closed or the IDE reloaded.

## Changes

- `XTermNative.onWebGLContextLoss()` subscribes to the addon's `onContextLoss` event, which fires once the addon has given up waiting (~3s) for the browser to restore a lost context; losses the browser restores within that window recover silently inside the addon. At most one handler is installed per loaded addon, guarding against the two concurrent `enableWebGL()` calls made at terminal startup (the startup enable plus the pref binding).
- `XTermWidget.enableWebGL()` registers a handler that disposes the addon and reverts to the DOM renderer via `disableWebGL()`, so the terminal keeps rendering — the recovery pattern the xterm.js API documents for this event.
- `unloadWebGLAddon()` clears the handler-installed flag so a handler is registered again when the addon is reloaded (e.g. toggling the renderer preference back on after a fallback).

## Test

New Playwright test in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/terminal/terminal.test.ts` ("terminal keeps rendering after WebGL context loss"):

- Forces a real context loss with the `WEBGL_lose_context` extension on the addon's webgl2 render canvas, then asserts that the output of a subsequently typed command appears in the terminal's rendered DOM rows (`.xterm-rows`, which only exists under the DOM renderer). The output marker is split across shell quotes so the echoed command line cannot satisfy the assertion, and `rstudioapi::terminalBuffer()` is deliberately not used — the server-side buffer keeps receiving output while client rendering is broken, which is the bug being tested.
- The command is typed during the addon's ~3s dead window, so the assertion also proves already-buffered content is repainted after the fallback.
- A second round toggles the renderer preference dom → canvas and loses the context again, covering handler re-subscription on an addon reload (verified by mutation testing: removing the flag clear in `unloadWebGLAddon` fails this round).
- Skips only when the environment cannot create WebGL2 contexts at all (probed on a detached canvas). If the environment is capable but the addon's render canvas never attaches, the test fails rather than skips, so a broken addon load reads as a regression instead of an environment limitation.

The test fails without the fix and passes with it; the full terminal suite passes on macOS Desktop.

title: Document the package/ build scripts in INSTALL
description:
Adds `package/README.md`, documenting how to use the scripts in `package/` to
produce a redistributable installer, and references it from `INSTALL`.

`INSTALL` previously covered only the CMake-plus-`make install` path, which
installs RStudio onto the machine that built it. The new document covers the
packaging scripts instead:

- Linux: `make-package`, `make-server-package`, `make-electron-package` for
  DEB and RPM, Desktop and Server
- Linux without a local toolchain: `docker/docker-compile.sh`
- macOS: `package/osx/make-package` for the app bundle and DMG
- Windows: `make-package.bat` and `make-dist-packages.bat` for the NSIS setup
  and ZIP

Each section gives the command, the directory the artifact is written to, and
the command to install the result. The document also records the version
environment variables, notes that RStudio Server can only be built on Linux,
and lists gotchas: the hardcoded `LIBR_HOME=C:\R\R-3.6.3` on Windows, the
`Desktop` target rerouting to `Electron`, ad-hoc code signing on macOS outside
of CI, and the build type appearing in package file names.

`INSTALL` gains a pointer in its introduction and a new section 5 with an
example command for each platform.

Two corrections in files this documents:

- `dependencies/windows/README.md` gave the setup package path as
  `rstudio\package\build\RStudio-99.9.9.exe`. It is written to
  `rstudio\package\win32\build`, and the file name carries the version suffix
  and build type.
- The header comment in `docker/docker-compile.sh` said packages are placed in
  `package/linux/`; the script copies them to `package/`.

The commands and paths were taken from the scripts and their help output. No
package build was run as part of this change, so the example file names should
be confirmed against a real build.

Fixes #18228.

title: Add a macOS 14 arm64 E2E engine to the scheduled rotation
description:
Adds a macOS 14 arm64 end-to-end Playwright engine, giving RStudio's oldest
still-supported macOS its own coverage lane alongside the existing per-OS
engines.

**Changed since this PR was opened:** the engine originally ran on
`macos-14-large` (Intel, billed even on public repos). It's now on bare
`macos-14`, the free arm64 standard runner. The cache seed workflow and its
cache-seed-sentinel registration were also dropped: the scheduled rotation
always runs this engine against the daily `.dmg` (`build_from_source:
false`), so the build job the seed maintains is skipped on every scheduled
run and its caches are never read on that path.

**What's here**

- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-14-arm64.yml` — the reusable engine
  (`workflow_call` and `workflow_dispatch`), patterned on the macOS 26 arm64
  sibling and running on bare `macos-14`.
- `os-test-e2e-rstudio-scheduled.yml` — adds `macos14` to the engine roster
  and gives it a dedicated Monday-afternoon cron (`0 16 * * 1`) rather than a
  weekday slate slot. `macos-14` is a deprecated image (GitHub retires it
  2026-11-02), and that slot is timed to land inside four of the October 2026
  brownout windows, so failures there double as early warning ahead of the
  hard retirement. The cron also gets its own concurrency group, since it
  would otherwise share a single pending slot with the Monday morning slate
  and could be delayed out of the window it is aimed at.

**Cache scoping**

Cache keys use a `macos14-arm64` namespace, versioned on both architecture
and OS version — architecture alone isn't enough, since macOS 26 is also
arm64 and would otherwise collide.

**Validation**

The engine had never executed before this PR. It was run three times against
a temporary push-triggered trigger (removed in this same PR before merge):
- Daily `.dmg` install path: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- From-source build: succeeded in ~28 minutes (well inside the 90-minute
  timeout), `rig default` succeeded without `sudo` as expected on Apple
  Silicon, 7 passed, 0 failed.
- From-source build, full default suite: 481 passed, 0 failed, 85 skipped,
  1 flaky.

title: fix(macos): pass -f pkcs12 to security import
description:
## Problem

`security import` in the **Build and Sign** stage infers the input format from the file's extension when `-f` is omitted.

The path it is given comes from a Jenkins **Secret file** credential (`MACOS_DEVELOPER_CERTIFICATE`, uploaded as `posit.p12`). That filename turns out not to be a stable contract. `credentials-binding` **728.v902a_273b_8947** ([PR #534](https://github.com/jenkinsci/credentials-binding-plugin/pull/534)) changed `FileBinding` to write secrets to a random temp name:

```diff
-String baseName = new FilePath(new File(credentials.getFileName())).getName();
-FilePath secret = dir.child(baseName);
+FilePath secret = dir.createTempFile("file", null);
```

So the file arrived as `fileNNNNN.tmp`, the `.p12` extension was gone, and signing died:

```
+ security import **** -k .../buildagent.keychain -P **** -T /usr/bin/codesign
security: SecKeychainItemImport: Unknown format in import.
```

Because the `sh` step runs with `-e`, the block aborted there — which is why none of the `security find-identity` verification output appears in the failing logs.

Every macOS hourly and daily build failed from **2026-07-28** (when the plugin was upgraded) until the controller was rolled back to `credentials-binding` 725 today.

## Fix

Pass `-f pkcs12` explicitly. The credential is a PKCS#12 keystore, so this is what the extension was resolving to anyway — it just no longer depends on the filename.

## Why this is worth landing even though the plugin is rolled back

The rollback is a stopgap. #534 is deliberate hardening (it addresses [#532](https://github.com/jenkinsci/credentials-binding-plugin/issues/532)) and is not going to be reverted, so the plugin will move forward again eventually. Until this is in, that upgrade re-breaks macOS signing. This change makes the step version-independent.

## Testing

Not yet exercised on a build — the controller is back on 725, where signing works via extension inference. `-f pkcs12` is correct under both 725 and 728: it states the format the credential already is, rather than changing it.

A macOS build has been requested to confirm the rollback restored signing; I will verify green before merging this.

title: Bind SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE_2026 secret file credential directly
description:
Follow-up to #18401. The hourly build after that merge failed in the Prepare Client Certificate stage with the guard added there: `SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE_2026` is a Jenkins secret file credential, so `credentials()` binds a path to the certificate file rather than base64 secret text.

- Binds `SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE` directly to the `SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE_2026` credential, giving the DigiCert tools the client certificate path with no intermediate step.
- Replaces the Prepare Client Certificate stage with a Validate Signing Credentials stage that keeps the `SM_HOST` check and verifies the certificate file exists before the build starts.
- Removes the base64 decode step and the workspace cleanup for the decoded `sm_client_cert.p12`, which is no longer written. The `cert.pem` cleanup in the post block remains.

The failed build confirms the direct binding resolves inside the build container: the secret file is materialized under the workspace `@tmp` directory, which is mounted into the container, and the previous run located it there.

Verification requires a Jenkins build; running with `PUBLISH=false` exercises executable signing without publishing anything.

title: add tasks for starting and stopping dev rstudio server instances
description:
Adds a repo-level `package.json` and a `tasks/` directory with three scripts for managing development RStudio Server instances, so bringing one up for manual testing (including for a git worktree) is a single command:

```sh
npm run rserver-dev                          # this checkout
npm run rserver-dev -- ../some-worktree      # another checkout
npm run rserver-status -- --all              # what is running
npm run rserver-stop                         # tear it down
```

`rserver-dev` configures `<checkout>/build` if it has never been configured, runs an incremental `cmake --build`, picks free ports, starts `rserver` with a private data dir and secure-cookie key, starts `ant devmode`, waits for both to answer, and prints the URL. Both processes are detached and outlive the task; state and logs land in `<checkout>/.rstudio-dev/` (gitignored). `--gwt=draft` does a one-shot `ant draft` instead, `--gwt=none` reuses `src/gwt/www` as-is, and `--help` lists the rest.

The tasks are TypeScript run directly by node's built-in type stripping (Node 22.18+) -- no dependencies, no build step, no `node_modules` at the repo root. `tasks/package.json` scopes ESM to that directory so the repo root keeps its default CommonJS resolution for stray `.js` files elsewhere in the tree.

### Concurrent instances

Ports, data dir and cookie key are per instance, so several worktrees can serve at once. The GWT code server port has to vary too, because it is baked into the bootstrap written to `src/gwt/www`, so `build.xml` gains `codeserver.port` and `server.port` properties and passes `-codeServerPort` to DevMode. The defaults (9876 / 8787) reproduce the existing behavior exactly -- 9876 is what `SuperDevListener.chooseCodeServerPort` picks when the flag is unset -- so `ant devmode` run on its own is unchanged.

### Why not the rserver-dev wrapper

`rserver` is spawned directly rather than through `build/src/cpp/rserver-dev`. That wrapper's SIGINT trap runs `killall -SIGUSR2 rsession`, which would suspend the R sessions of every *other* dev server and any desktop RStudio on the machine; it also deletes the shared `/tmp/rstudio-server` and hardcodes the port in its banner. The flags passed here otherwise reproduce the wrapper, and it is left in place unchanged.

The server binds `127.0.0.1` by default. It runs `--auth-none`, so the wrapper's wildcard bind exposed a passwordless R session to the network; `--www-address` still allows that but warns.

### Port probing

Worth a look during review. A single bind test cannot establish that a port is free on macOS: a specific-address bind and a wildcard bind coexist, and the more specific socket then silently takes `localhost` traffic from whatever was already there. Measured against a running `rserver` on `*:8787` and a devmode on `127.0.0.1:9876`:

| port | bind `127.0.0.1` | bind `0.0.0.0` | connect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8787 (wildcard held) | **OK** | EADDRINUSE | ANSWERED |
| 9876 (specific held) | EADDRINUSE | **OK** | ANSWERED |
| free | OK | OK | ECONNREFUSED |

Each bind test misses the opposite binding style, so `isPortFree` requires both plus a refused connect. An explicit `--port` is validated the same way instead of bypassing the scan.

### Testing

Verified locally on macOS: start/probe/stop; two concurrent instances (8787 + 8788) across two worktrees; idempotent double start; `--restart`; recovery from stale state; per-instance temp dir cleanup; that the probe skips a port held by an already-running server and rejects an explicit one; and that `-D` overrides survive ant's `<antcall>` chain with the defaults reproducing today's values.

The `--gwt=devmode` path has since been exercised end to end as well: `rserver-dev` brought up `rserver` and `ant devmode` for a separate checkout, and a headless-browser load booted the full workbench (live R session at the console) through the Super Dev Mode on-demand compile. That run also surfaced a trap worth guarding: a checkout whose `build.xml` predates the `codeserver.port` property silently ignores `-Dcodeserver.port`, so the code server starts on 9876 while the task polls the requested port until its timeout. `rserver-dev` now fails fast in that case.

### Snyk

The diff-scoped Snyk Code scan reported every argv-derived path handed to `fs` as path traversal, and the `rserver` spawn as command injection -- for a local developer tool whose purpose is operating on the checkout you point it at. Snyk Code has no per-finding suppression (`.snyk` supports only whole-file excludes), and its taint tracking survives `path.resolve` and `fs.realpathSync`. Instead, `resolveCheckout` now rebuilds the canonicalized path one component at a time from `readdirSync` listings (which also re-verifies each component exists), and `--www-address` is validated and rebuilt numerically -- so the values reaching the sinks are no longer derived from command-line strings.

No NEWS.md entry: developer tooling, not user-facing.

title: Use documented SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE_2026 credential ID for Windows signing
description:
Follow-up to #18388. The internal signing docs we followed had errors in the credential names; the correct set is `SM_API_KEY_2026`, `SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE_2026`, `SM_CLIENT_CERT_PASSWORD_2026`, `SM_HOST_2026`, and `SM_KEYPAIR_ALIAS_2026`. Four of the five already match (the keypair alias was corrected in e1d335f390); the client certificate credential was bound as `SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE_B64_2026`.

- Binds the client authentication certificate from `SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE_2026` and updates the error message in the Prepare Client Certificate stage to reference that ID.
- Adds a fail-fast check before base64 decoding: if the credential value is a file path (i.e. the credential is a secret file rather than base64 secret text), the stage fails with a message saying to bind it directly to `SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE`.

Verification requires a Jenkins build; running with `PUBLISH=false` exercises executable signing without publishing anything.

title: pin data viewer cell line-height so rows render at row-height everywhere
description:
The data viewer's virtual-scroll math assumes every data row is exactly `ROW_HEIGHT` (23px), but `height` on a table cell is only a *minimum*. The grid's font stack starts with DejaVu Sans, whose 11px line box (13px) fits inside the 14px available (23px minus 8px vertical padding and 1px border). On platforms where DejaVu Sans is not installed, the resolved font's normal line box is 15px -- Segoe UI on Windows, Noto Sans on Fedora and RHEL 10+ (which dropped DejaVu from the default font set) -- so every *rendered* row grew to 24px while the spacer rows standing in for off-window rows stayed at 23px per row. Ctrl+End computes its scroll target from the 23px constant, so the jump landed one pixel short per rendered row (~24px in the e2e layout), leaving the last row cut off below the bottom edge.

This explains the platform matrix in the issue exactly: Ubuntu, Debian, and Rocky 9 ship DejaVu Sans (13px line box, 23px rows, pass); macOS resolves Lucida Grande (13px, pass); Windows, Fedora 43/44, and Rocky 10 resolve a 15px-line-box font (24px rows, fail). Architecture is irrelevant, matching the observed results.

The fix pins `line-height: 14px` on the grid `td` so 14px line + 8px padding + 1px border = `--row-height` exactly, independent of platform font metrics. Since `line-height` applies uniformly to all font-fallback runs, this also keeps rows at 23px for cell text drawn with fallback fonts (e.g. CJK). Verified in headless Chromium with the real Noto Sans TTF: with normal line-height the row measures 24px (line box 15px); with the pin it measures exactly 23px, even under fonts with far taller metrics (Zapfino's 38px line box).

Also removes the `test.fixme` Windows CI guard from the "End scrolls to the last row of the current column, fully visible" e2e test -- it was skipping exactly this failure (the observed ~24px shortfall in its comment is the per-rendered-row pixel deficit) -- so Windows CI now verifies the fix.

The full data viewer e2e spec passes on macOS desktop-dev (40/40) with the fix in place; dispatched e2e runs on Fedora 43 and Windows Server 2025 validate it on platforms that reproduce the bug.

Fixes #18378.

title: make rsession long path aware on Windows
description:
Addresses #12806.

### Why R's own long path support never reached RStudio

R Core made R long-path aware in R 4.3.0, including `<longPathAware>true</longPathAware>` in the manifests for `Rterm.exe`, `Rgui.exe`, `Rscript.exe` and friends. But the manifest is a property of the *process*, and rsession loads `R.dll` into its own address space (`REmbeddedWin32.cpp`, plus `LIBR_LIBRARIES` linked into `rsession-shared`). R's front-end manifests therefore never apply under the IDE. R's [announcement](https://blog.r-project.org/2023/03/07/path-length-limit-on-windows/) calls this out: *"Applications embedding R must declare long-path awareness separately."* We hadn't.

So since R 4.3, R has supported long paths everywhere except inside RStudio.

### What's here

**Manifests.** `longPathAware` added to `rsession.exe`, `rsession-utf8.exe`, `consoleio.exe` and `diagnostics.exe`; `rpostback.exe` gains a manifest (and `.rc`) since it had none. All four existing manifests already declared the Windows 10 `supportedOS` GUID, which is the other precondition.

Note that Boost.Filesystem does not paper over `MAX_PATH` on its own — I checked its release history, and it never prepends `\\?\`. It calls the wide Win32 APIs directly, which means the whole of `FilePath` (`exists()`, `create_directories()`, `copy_file()`, …) inherits the process setting. That's why the manifest flip is the high-leverage change rather than a `\\?\` sweep.

**Buffer fixes the manifest newly exposes.**

| Site | Problem |
|---|---|
| `Win32System.cpp` `executablePath()` | `wchar_t[MAX_PATH]` with no truncation check — `GetModuleFileNameW` signals truncation by returning the buffer size, and only `== 0` was tested. Feeds `installPath()` and every derived resource path. Now grows and retries. |
| `Win32System.cpp` `ensureLongPath()`, `Win32FileMonitor.cpp` `ensureLongFilePath()` | `char[521]` + **ANSI** `GetLongPathName`, treating any non-zero return as success. On insufficient buffer that API returns the *required size* and writes nothing, so we built a `FilePath` from uninitialized stack. Both now go through a new `file_utils::longPathName()` using the two-pass wide pattern. The file monitor one also passed a UTF-8 string straight to an ANSI API. |
| `FilePath.cpp` `isWriteable()` | Probed with `GetTempFileNameW`, whose `lpPathName` is documented to fail above `MAX_PATH-14` (246 characters), so a deep directory reported as read-only. |
| 4x `SHGetFolderPathW` / `SHGetFolderPathAndSubDirW` | Contractually `MAX_PATH`-bound. Now `SHGetKnownFolderPath`, which allocates. This also fixes a leak in `userSettingsPath()`, which never called `CoTaskMemFree`. |
| 5x `PathFindOnPath` | Documented to take "a string of length MAX_PATH" and writes at most that regardless of the buffer given, so it cannot find programs under a long path. Replaced with `findProgramOnPath()`, which walks PATH and then the system directories. |

`SHGetKnownFolderPath` has no `A`/`W` pair — its out param is `PWSTR*`, so it's wide-only. Worth noting because this codebase never defines `UNICODE`, so every TCHAR-generic call (`GetModuleFileName`, `GetLongPathName`, `PathFindOnPath`, `ExpandEnvironmentStrings`, …) silently resolves to ANSI, and ANSI APIs cannot express long paths at all.

**Notebook path shortening.** The deepest path RStudio itself creates under a project was ~116 characters before the project path is even counted:

```
/.Rproj.user/shared/notebooks/<id8>-<stem>/1/<ctx16>/<chunk13>_t/<uuid32>.snapshot
```

The transient plot and snapshot leaf names are purely internal — they're renamed to their ordinal form (`000001.png`) when the chunk is committed, and nothing outside `NotebookPlots.cpp` matches on them. Shortening the snapshot id and the plot prefix takes 24 characters off the worst case with no compatibility cost and no cache version bump.

This matters because it's the failure users actually reported. [The second comment on the issue](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/12806#issuecomment-2981929334) describes a ~150-character project directory where notebook plotting failed: 150 + 116 > 260. At 150 + 92 it now fits, so that case is fixed *even on machines where long paths are not enabled*.

I deliberately stopped there. Getting another 8 characters would mean shortening the persisted `<ctx16>` directory, which requires bumping `kCacheVersion` and invalidating every user's chunk cache — not worth 8 characters.

### One POSIX-visible change

`findProgramOnPath()` is shared, so the new qualified-name handling landed on both platforms. On POSIX it fixes a latent bug: a rooted name previously fell through to `completeChildPath()`, which rejects an absolute child, so the function returned `Success()` with an **empty** `FilePath` while logging an error per PATH entry -- undetectable by callers such as `SessionNodeTools.cpp`. Covered by `PosixTests.FindProgramResolvesQualifiedNames`.

Calling it out because this PR is otherwise Windows-scoped in both its title and its NEWS entry. A *relative* qualified name (`bin/foo`) now resolves against the current directory instead of being joined onto each PATH entry. That is `execvp`'s rule and it does not turn this into a current-directory search -- a bare `foo` still will not find `./foo` -- but it is a Linux/macOS behavior change and belongs in the description rather than only in the diff.

### Explicitly out of scope

A project whose *own* directory exceeds `MAX_PATH`. Per the [`SetCurrentDirectory` docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-setcurrentdirectory), *"Setting a current directory longer than MAX_PATH causes CreateProcessW to fail."* rsession sets its working directory to the project directory, so such a project would lose git, terminals, builds and `R CMD` entirely. That's an OS constraint, not something we can work around here; it's documented in a comment where the working directory is set, and in the NEWS entry. Files *below* a shorter project directory may now exceed `MAX_PATH` freely, which is the case that actually comes up.

### Tests

- `Win32SystemTests.cpp`: `executablePath()` resolves; `findProgramOnPath()` finds `cmd.exe`, returns empty for a missing program and for `""`, and handles an already-qualified path; `longPathName()` round-trips a short (8.3) name back to its long form and passes non-existent paths through unchanged.
- `FilePathTests.cpp`: a directory of exactly 247 characters reports as writeable. This is the regression test for the `GetTempFileNameW` probe, and 247 is chosen deliberately -- `CreateDirectoryW` accepts up to 248 characters with no OS opt-in while `GetTempFileNameW` gives up at 247, so it reproduces the original bug on a stock machine with neither the manifest nor `LongPathsEnabled`. It skips cleanly if the platform will not create a path that long.

### Verification status

All cross-platform translation units compile locally. **The Windows-only code is not yet verified** — I developed this on macOS, so `Win32System.cpp`, `Win32User.cpp`, `Win32ChildProcess.cpp`, `Win32FileMonitor.cpp` and the `_WIN32` branches of `SessionGit.cpp` / `SessionSVN.cpp` have not been compiled, and nothing here has been run on Windows. Needs a Windows build plus manual confirmation that a >260-character path under a normal project now works with `LongPathsEnabled` set.

One thing I could not check: whether the shipped Electron `rstudio.exe` is long-path aware. Electron Forge only sets version metadata via `rcedit` (`forge.config.js`), not the manifest, and the Chromium `chrome.exe.manifest` revision I looked at does not set the flag. Worth a follow-up look, though rsession is what matters for R's file access.


---

### Corrections since first posting

- I originally claimed this PR also fixed a dangling pointer, `LPCWSTR folder = m_impl->Path.wstring().c_str()` binding to a destroyed temporary. **That was wrong.** Under `BOOST_FILESYSTEM_WINDOWS_API`, boost 1.91 `path::wstring()` returns `std::wstring const&` (`boost/filesystem/path.hpp:885`) -- a reference to the internal member -- so the pointer was valid. Rewriting `isWriteable()` is still correct for the `MAX_PATH` probe, but it was never a use-after-free. Thanks for catching it.
- `findProgramOnPath` no longer adds a new function: review pointed out that `Error findProgramOnPath(const std::string&, FilePath*)` already existed and was never `MAX_PATH`-bound. The system-directory fallback and PATH quote trimming were folded into it instead, so all callers share one search. Note this means the lookup no longer consults the current working directory the way `PathFindOnPath` did; `resolveCommand` already checks a CWD-relative name before reaching it.
- Two more from the second review round, both confirmed and fixed. The Windows `MAX_PATH` warning at session start measured `getAbsolutePath().length()`, which is UTF-8 *bytes*, against `MAX_PATH`, which counts UTF-16 units -- so a ~90-character CJK project path measured 270+ and printed an emphatic, wrong warning to the console on every start. It now measures `getAbsolutePathW()`. And `findProgramOnPath()` read the extension of a qualified name with `getExtension()`, a bare `rfind('.')` over the whole path, so any dotted *directory* (`R-4.4.1`, `first.last`) read as an extension and silently suppressed the `.exe`/`.com`/`.bat`/`.cmd` probing; the extension is now taken from the last component, with `FindProgramOnPathProbesExtensionsUnderDottedDirectories` covering it.
- `DeepDirectoryIsWriteable` had an environment-dependent hard failure: its padding step was skipped when the computed remainder came out as 1, leaving the path at 246 characters and failing its own assertion. That happens whenever the temp directory's length is congruent to 6 mod 11 -- including 39, i.e. `C:\Users\<11-character user>\AppData\Local\Temp`. Reproduced locally by pointing `TMPDIR` at a 39-character path, and the rewrite now lands on exactly 247 for every temp path length. `FindProgramOnPathTrimsQuotedEntries` was separately asserting nothing, since the system directories are searched before PATH and so `cmd.exe` resolved before the quoted entry was ever read; it now probes for a name only the quoted entry can supply.
- The two most important manifests were malformed: my comment prose contained `--`, which XML forbids inside a comment. `ManifestTests.cpp` now guards against that and against silently dropping `longPathAware`.


- Fourth round, all minor. `findProgramOnPath()` now rejects an empty name up front on both platforms rather than probing extensions of `""` against every search directory; the `System.hpp` docs note that the executable's own directory is no longer searched (`PathFindOnPath` searched it, alongside the CWD); and `DeepDirectoryIsWriteable` measures its 247-character target in UTF-16 units, so a non-ASCII temp path cannot land the probe short of the boundary the test exists to hit.

title: treat an empty PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER as unset
description:
## Problem

The consolidated Linux e2e workflow (#18360) sets, in *Run Playwright tests*:

```yaml
PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.preinstall_r_packages == 'true'
                           && format('{0}/R-libs', github.workspace) || '' }}
```

with the stated intent that the empty branch means "the harness default". But an Actions `env:` value of `''` is exported as a **defined empty string**, and `rLibsUserTemplate()` read it with `??`:

```ts
return process.env[RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER_ENV] ?? defaultRLibsUserTemplate();
```

`''` is not nullish, so it won, and the R_LIBS_USER template became `""`.

R treats an empty `R_LIBS_USER` as unset and computes its HOME-relative default. globalSetup runs with the real HOME, so it installed REQUIRED_PACKAGES into `/home/runner/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5`; the session under test runs with HOME redirected into the per-run sandbox (`desktop.fixture.ts`), so it resolved a *different*, empty library. That is precisely the hazard `r-libs-setup.ts`'s header comment warns about. The default template is immune because `os.homedir()` is resolved before the redirect, producing an absolute path.

One line in the job log shows it, comparing the same branch before and after #18360 landed:

| | `[r-libs] user library:` |
|---|---|
| before | `/home/runner/.cache/rstudio-playwright/r-libs/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/4.5` |
| after | `/home/runner/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5` |

Everything else in those two runs is identical, including the GWT cache hash.

## Impact

`citations.test.ts:147` "inserts an R Package citation into the document" fails both attempts, deterministically, on linux-desktop shard 1 of every branch that has main merged in (runs 30296790097, 30429212918). The panel calls `getRPackageState()` and Fuse-searches the session's installed packages; with the empty library there is no knitr, and the trace contains "No matching packages".

Affected: the five engines with `preinstall_r_packages: ""` -- `ubuntu-22-x86_64`, `ubuntu-24-x86_64`, `ubuntu-24-arm64`, `ubuntu-26-x86_64`, `debian-13-arm64`. Fedora/Rocky pass a real path; macOS, Windows, and Linux Server never set the variable.

Beyond the one red test, the harness's REQUIRED_PACKAGES pre-population was landing in a library the session never saw, so those engines were quietly running against a much thinner library.

## Fix

`??` -> `||`, which makes the workflow's documented intent true and also covers `server.fixture.ts`, and the prep log now names where the resolved library came from:

```
[r-libs] user library: /home/runner/.cache/rstudio-playwright/r-libs/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/4.5 [harness default]
[r-libs] user library: /home/runner/work/rstudio/rstudio/R-libs [PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER=/home/runner/work/rstudio/rstudio/R-libs]
[r-libs] user library: ... [harness default (PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER set but empty)]
```

so a future override mismatch is visible in the job output instead of surfacing as a missing package.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean in `e2e/rstudio`.
- Resolution checked directly against both revisions -- `unset` and `explicit path` are unchanged; `''` returns `""` on main and the default template here.
- Confirmed at the first push: `linux-desktop / E2E (ubuntu-24-x86_64)` went green, shard 1 passed `citations.test.ts:147`, and the log read `[r-libs] user library: /home/runner/.cache/rstudio-playwright/... [harness default]`.

## Review follow-ups (089f2fd129)

From the [review](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/18390#issuecomment-5121501231), the items worth taking, all in the same file:

- **CRLF manifest parsing**: `required-packages.txt` was split on `'\n'` only; on a Windows checkout the trailing `\r` defeats `/#.*$/` (`\r` is a regex line terminator, so `.` stops at it and `$` anchors past it) and every comment line was passed to `install.packages()` as a package name -- which is exactly the permanent `[r-libs] WARNING: failed to install: # R packages ...` noise every Windows shard has been printing. Now `split(/\r?\n/)`. Verified against a CRLF rendition of the real manifest: old parse leaks 6 comment lines, new parse is byte-identical to the LF parse. (The action-side parser is R, not bash, and R's `.` crosses `\r`, so it needs no change.)
- **`tools:::` -> `base:::`**: `.expand_R_libs_env_var` lives in `base`, so `tools:::` errored on every call and the reduced `gsub` fallback ran unconditionally. Harmless for the `%p`/`%v` templates in use (verified both paths expand identically), but `%U`/`%S`/`%%` would have been wrong. The fallback now writes a marker so a silent downgrade shows up in the prep log as a `WARNING`.
- **Provenance before the early returns**: the template + source line now prints as the first thing `prepareRLibs()` does, so skip-prep runs and expansion failures are no longer diagnostic-free.
- **Docs**: module header and the README env-var table now state that an empty value is treated as unset.

Deliberately not taken: `console.warn` for the "set but empty" case (empty is the intended per-engine signal in the Linux workflow -- warning on it would fire on every run of five engines, permanently).

## Preinstall on every engine (aa7dbc6326)

The review also observed that with the resolution fixed, the five `preinstall_r_packages: ""` engines install the 23-package set into the harness-default library -- which no workflow cache covers -- on **every run**. This flips `preinstall_r_packages: "true"` for all five, routing the install through `os-e2e-deps` into the cached `R-libs` tree (keyed on the manifest via `-req<hash>`) and pointing `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER` at it, so a warm run installs nothing.

Two of them (`ubuntu-24-x86_64`, `ubuntu-26-x86_64`) also get explicit cache scopes (`noble-amd64` / `resolute-amd64`): both used the legacy shared `Linux` key, which was tolerable for pak's DESCRIPTION deps but is an ABI hazard once the cache carries the full compiled package set -- whichever engine saved first on main would hand its binaries to the other, and the presence check would count them as installed. Their caches start cold and warm on the next main-scoped run.

The review's own suggested shape (unconditional `PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER`) would not have worked: the R-libs cache is saved inside the action -- before globalSetup runs, and only from main -- so anything globalSetup installs into that tree still never persists; and dropping the conditional would decouple the cache key from the manifest, since `-req<hash>` only applies when `install-required-packages` is set.

With this commit the ubuntu-24 job's expected log line changes from the `.cache/rstudio-playwright` path (verified at the first push, above) to `[r-libs] user library: /home/runner/work/rstudio/rstudio/R-libs [PW_RSTUDIO_R_LIBS_USER=...]`, with `os-e2e-deps` doing the install instead.

No NEWS.md entry: CI-only, and the regression never reached a release.

title: Fix detached logger().logError in desktop promise catch handlers
description:
Fixes #18391.

## What this changes

Ten call sites in `main-window.ts` and `satellite-window.ts` passed `logger().logError` directly to `.catch()`. The method reads `this.logErrorAtLevel`, so when a promise rejected, the detached call threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'logErrorAtLevel')` inside the catch handler — replacing the original rejection with an unhandled meta-error and hiding the real failure (as seen in the logs on #18323). Each site now invokes the method on its logger instance via an arrow function, which also picks up the current logger at rejection time rather than at registration time.

In `MainWindow.closeEvent`, a rejected `!!window.desktopHooks` probe means the renderer is unreachable (e.g. it crashed). That path now logs the error and quits — matching the existing missing-`desktopHooks` branch — instead of leaving a headless process running after the window closes.

To keep the pattern from coming back, the desktop ESLint config now enables the type-aware `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` rule, which flags every detached method reference of this kind. Two adaptations for spots that were already safe: `minimal-window.ts`'s `parentWindowDestroyed` is now an arrow property (replacing its manual constructor `.bind`), and test files are exempted because sinon assertions take stub method references by design.

## Tests

- Two new unit tests for `closeEvent` with a rejecting renderer probe: the original error reaches the log sink, and the app quits instead of lingering. Both fail without the fix.
- Full desktop suite passes (447), plus `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck`.

title: Migrate Windows Jenkins signing to DigiCert KeyLocker 2026 credentials
description:
Updates the Windows Jenkins pipeline to sign with the current DigiCert KeyLocker credential set.

- Binds the year-suffixed `_2026` signing credentials and maps them onto the env var names the DigiCert tools read. The client authentication certificate now arrives as base64 secret text; a new Prepare Client Certificate stage decodes it to a file and checks that the configured host is DigiCert's documented mTLS endpoint, so a misconfigured credential fails before the build instead of at the signing step.
- Signs with signtool via the DigiCert Signing Manager KSP, selecting the key by keypair alias from the credential store instead of by certificate fingerprint. The signing certificate is downloaded at build time with `smctl`.
- Adds `smctl healthcheck` and `smctl keypair ls` checkpoints ahead of the first signing step, and dumps the DigiCert client logs when a signing stage fails.

All credentials are referenced by Jenkins credential ID only; no secret values appear in the pipeline.

Verification requires a Jenkins branch build; running with `PUBLISH=false` exercises executable signing without publishing anything.

title: Correct 2026.08 release notes and What's New coverage
description:
