title: theme the Review Changes window (#9026)
description:
### Intent

Fixes #9026.

The Review Changes window (git/svn commit + history) always rendered light, however dark the editor theme was.

`VCSApplicationWindow` extends `SatelliteWindow`, which opts out of theming by default -- so the satellite's container never got the `rstudio-themes-*` classes and never had the editor theme CSS injected. (Satellites used to get the flat theme unconditionally; 490649125e moved that inside the `supportsThemes()` guard to fix #3153, which was *this window* rendering half dark. So opting back in means finishing the CSS this time.)

### Approach

- `VCSApplicationWindow.supportsThemes()` returns true, so the window gets the global theme classes (`rstudio-themes-dark` et al on an `rstudio_container`) and the editor theme stylesheet, and re-themes live when the theme changes.
- The changelist and the diff pane now follow the **editor** theme, exactly as the changelist does in the Git pane in the main window. The `whitebg` style that pinned them white is gone -- on the changelist it was actually clobbering the `ace_editor_theme` class `ChangelistTable` adds for itself, since UiBinder's `styleName` replaces rather than adds. The tables inside those panes now go transparent for *every* editor theme rather than only dark ones: the base stylesheet paints them a hard-coded white, which a light-but-not-white theme (Solarized Light, Dawn) would otherwise leave as a white slab inside a tinted pane.
- Diff rows tint the editor background with translucent overlays instead of fixed pastels, so insertions/deletions/context read correctly against any editor theme. The chunk/line action buttons (Stage chunk, Discard chunk) drop their sprite pills for flat translucent ones, keyed off `data-action` so Stage keeps its accent.
- The chrome -- toolbars, split panels, commit message box, Commit button, context selects, cell table headers, commit list selection, diff frame headers, commit TOC links -- gets dark styling from the same palette the theme-aware modal dialogs use. The panels and toolbars share one background so the commit area reads as a single surface, with the split draggers left as the seams.

The chrome follows the global theme and the changelist and diff follow the editor theme, which is how the Git pane behaves in the main window. (`global_theme` is `default` or `alternate`; a prefs file still holding the retired `classic` value is migrated to `default` the first time the Appearance pane is opened, and until then *any* window is half-themed -- `editor_dark` is applied but `rstudio-themes-dark` is not -- so this window is no exception to that pre-existing quirk.)

Also in this window, from hands-on review:

- header cells in the commit list carried the base style's light top and left borders, drawing a heavy outline around each one; they now match the changelist, and the commit list gains the label inset the changelist already had
- the history pager sat tight against the commit table above it
- the file list shows "No changes" when there is nothing to review, in place of an empty pane -- in the Review Changes window and in the Git and SVN panes, since they share the widget. Styled to match the Environment pane's "Environment is empty" message: centered, proportional at 90%, inheriting the theme foreground

### Scope of the light-theme change

The light appearance is *not* entirely unchanged. The new `.ace_editor_theme .cellTableWidget { background-color: inherit }` rules are scoped to the editor theme rather than to dark themes, so they deliberately change light rendering for any editor theme that is not pure white (Solarized Light, Dawn). Because `ChangelistTableCellTableStyle.css` is shared with the main window, that includes the Git and SVN panes there, not only this satellite. This is the intended fix -- without it those panes show a white table inside a tinted pane -- but it is a visible change under those themes rather than a no-op.

### Verification

New e2e spec `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/git/review_changes_theme.test.ts`, four tests:

1. creates a git-backed project, applies Cobalt, opens the window, and asserts the theme classes reach the satellite container, the editor theme CSS is injected there, and both editor-themed panes paint dark. Because those pane backgrounds come from the editor theme's own stylesheet, it also asserts two things only the new CSS can produce -- the cell tables inside the panes being transparent rather than white, and a chunk action pill being a flat translucent fill rather than a sprite -- so a dropped `@external` declaration cannot leave the spec green.
2. switches to the History view while Cobalt is still applied and asserts the commit list and commit detail paint dark, the commit list's header cells take the flat dark chrome color, the chrome behind the panes is dark rather than the white the panel used to hard-code, and the commit TOC and "View file @ ..." links move off the base dark blue. This is the coverage for `CommitListTableCellTableStyle.css`, `HistoryPanel.css`, `DiffFrame` and `CommitTocRow`, whose rules are almost all dark-only.
3. switches back to a light theme and asserts the already-open window repaints light, re-running the table probe where there is no base `.editor_dark` rule to produce it.
4. commits everything and asserts the "No changes" placeholder appears in the Git pane, which shares `ChangelistTable` with this window. Keyed on visibility rather than pane text, since `setEmptyTableWidget` leaves the widget in the DOM whether or not the table is empty.

Passes on desktop-dev.

Also inspected by hand on desktop-dev in Cobalt, Textmate (default) and **Solarized Light**, in both the Changes and the History view, with and without pending changes: toolbars, changelist, commit message box, diff, chunk buttons, commit list, commit detail, per-file diff frames and their "View file @ ..." links all read correctly. Solarized Light is the case the other two cannot exercise -- Cobalt is dark and Textmate is pure white, so `inherit` and `white` are visually identical under it. Under Solarized Light both views' panes compute to `rgb(253, 246, 227)` with the tables transparent over them, which is the outcome the rules were written for.

SVN gets the parallel CSS changes but was not exercised at runtime.

title: consolidate linux desktop e2e workflows into one parameterized workflow
description:
## What

Replaces the eight per-OS Linux Desktop E2E workflows (Ubuntu 22/24/26, Debian 13, Fedora 43/44, Rocky 9/10 -- ~6,200 lines, ~94% copy-paste within a distro family) with a single reusable workflow parameterized by an `os` input. Net: **-6,444 / +1,691 lines**.

New structure:

- **`.github/workflows/os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-linux.yml`** -- the one workflow. A small `setup` job loads the engine config and republishes it as job outputs, which parameterize `runs-on`, `container.image`/`options`, timeouts, cache keys, DEB vs RPM, and the daily-manifest key. An empty `image` runs the job bare on the runner, which is how the Ubuntu engines coexist with the container engines.
- **`.github/e2e-linux/<distro>-<ver>-<arch>.json`** -- per-engine scalar knobs (~35 lines each). Every engine name ends in its architecture, so the arch is visible in the dispatch picker, job names, artifact names, and the PW project label. Adding an engine is now "copy the closest config, adjust" -- see `.github/e2e-linux/README.md`.
- **`.github/e2e-linux/<dir>/*.sh`** -- the genuinely distro-specific steps as hooks: Chromium runtime package lists, EPEL/CRB enablement, the jammy pkgconf/Java-17 quirks, Fedora's dnf R install, Debian's PPM codename rewrite, locale exports. Fedora 43/44 share a dir, as do Ubuntu 24/26. The Xvfb-vs-Cage and root-vs-setpriv variants collapsed into one run script driven by two config flags.

Callers updated:

- PR orchestrator: `linux-desktop` now calls the consolidated workflow with `os: ubuntu-24-x86_64` (plus `paths:` filter updates).
- Scheduled rotation: the eight copy-pasted Linux job blocks become **one dynamic-matrix job**; `pick` emits a filtered `linux_matrix`, and each entry's installer URL is looked up via `needs.resolve.outputs[matrix.url_key]`. Slates/crons unchanged.
- The ubuntu-24 scheduled wrapper and cache seed point at the new workflow. The seed's filename, cache keys, and the sentinel's key prefixes are unchanged.

Cache keys, PW project labels, and SHARD_NAMEs are preserved verbatim per engine (dashboard/cache continuity); the ubuntu-24 tools/rlibs keys stay shared with the Linux Server build.

## Deliberate behavior changes

These were points where the eight copies had silently drifted, each with its own justifying comment; the consolidation picks one policy:

1. **sccache**: every engine now uses the S3-with-GHA-fallback backend. Ubuntu 22 and Rocky 9 were still GHA-only (they predate the S3 migration) and now also receive the `AWS_SCCACHE_ROLE_ARN` secret from callers.
2. **GWT cache saves** are gated to main-scoped runs everywhere. Fedora alone still saved from PR-scoped runs -- the same quota pressure #18337 eliminated.
3. The **Fedora-only daily-installer cache** step is dropped (SHA-256 verification is unchanged; the sibling engines' comments argued the cache was net-negative quota pressure).
4. **Artifact names are engine-suffixed everywhere.** This fixes a real bug: in Sunday all-engines runs, ubuntu-24's merge glob `playwright-blob-report-linux-desktop-*` (and fedora-44's `...-fedora-*`) matched other engines' blob artifacts, so those merged reports could silently include foreign results.

## Architecture

Raised in review: architecture is an attribute of each engine rather than a second selection axis, since every config is single-arch.

- Every engine name now ends in its arch (`ubuntu-24-x86_64`, `rocky-10-arm64`), and `pretty_name` matches. Beyond readability this removes a prefix hazard: the merge job globs `playwright-blob-report-linux-desktop-<os>-*`, so a bare `ubuntu-24` would have swept up `ubuntu-24-arm64`'s blobs. Renaming the config files leaves every cache key untouched (they live inside the files), so continuity holds.
- An **`arch` input** on both `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` is cross-checked against the config's `tools_arch`, failing the run on a mismatch. It's an assertion, not a selector -- `auto` (the dispatch default) accepts whatever the config declares. This catches an engine being re-pointed at a different runner without its arch-bearing cache keys, installer artifact, and daily platform key following.
- All four callers now state the arch they expect; the scheduled rotation's engine table carries a per-entry `arch`.
- **New `ubuntu-24-arm64` engine**, so Ubuntu 24 can be run on both arches. It's the bare-runner shape on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, and it shares the arm64 tools/rlibs/GWT cache keys with `debian-13-arm64`, which already builds bare on that same host with `install-dependencies-noble` -- so it starts warm. Dispatch-only for now (not in the scheduled rotation), so it costs no nightly runner time until it's proven.

## Validation

- `actionlint` is clean on all changed workflows (remaining shellcheck notes are the same style classes the untouched macOS/Windows/Server workflows carry).
- All nine configs share an identical key schema, matching the setup job's outputs 1:1; each filename's arch agrees with its `tools_arch` and `pretty_name`; no engine name is a prefix of another; no two engines of different arch share `sccache_key_prefix`, `installer_artifact`, `pw_label`, or `e2e_deps_cache_scope` (an empty scope means `runner.os` alone, so arm64 engines must set it); every caller `os`/`arch` pair resolves to a config that agrees; hook scripts pass `bash -n`; the `pick` matrix mapping was tested locally including the empty-selection case.
- The setup job enforces the contract the rest of the workflow leans on, and each guard was exercised against a synthetic bad config: engine name must end in `-<tools_arch>` (the blob-report glob is only collision-free while no engine name prefixes another), `arch` must be non-empty (`required: true` alone only rejects an absent key, not an expression that resolved to nothing), and every config value must be a single-line string (they are republished as `key=value` job outputs, so a newline could forge output keys).
- Four runner behaviors want a live confirmation before merge, via `workflow_dispatch` of the new workflow from this branch (ubuntu-24-x86_64, one container engine, and rocky-10-arm64 would cover the first three):
  1. **empty `container.image` running bare** -- the highest-consequence one, since all four bare engines (including the PR-gating ubuntu-24 run) depend on it. If GitHub rejects it, the fallback is to emit the whole container mapping as JSON from `setup` and use `container: ${{ fromJSON(...) }}` with `null` for bare engines.
  2. `timeout-minutes` from a `needs` output.
  3. `name: ${{ matrix.name }}` on `uses:` jobs.
  4. `needs.resolve.outputs[matrix.url_key]` in the scheduled rotation -- indexing a `needs` output by a matrix value. This one fails *silently*: an unsupported index yields an empty URL, which means "self-resolve the latest daily", so a version-pinned dispatch would test the wrong build behind a green check. Only a `workflow_dispatch` with `version` exercises it (both crons leave it empty).

macOS, Windows, Linux Server, and the cache-seed files are deliberately untouched; they're natural follow-ups once this pattern is settled.

title: Let rstudio-tests.bat run more than one scope
description:
`--scope` in the Windows test runner accepted exactly one scope, so running two of
the four suites meant two invocations. It now takes several.

`cmd.exe` treats a comma as an argument separator, so `--scope core,rsession` arrives
as two separate arguments. `--scope` therefore collects every argument up to the next
option, which makes three forms equivalent:

    rstudio-tests.bat --scope core,rsession
    rstudio-tests.bat --scope core rsession
    rstudio-tests.bat --scope core --scope rsession

Scope names are validated, case-normalized, and de-duplicated into a delimited list
before any suite runs, so a typo anywhere in the list fails up front rather than after
the first suite finishes. Scopes run in the fixed `core`, `rserver`, `rsession`, `r`
order regardless of the order requested, which keeps the slow `r` scope last.

The `help` and `/?` arguments are not `-` prefixed, so scope collection stops at them
as well; `rstudio-tests.bat --scope core help` prints usage and exits 0.

The Unix `rstudio-tests` script still takes a single scope. Existing single-scope
callers, including `--scope core` in `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows`, are unaffected.

## Testing

Argument handling was exercised against a copy of the script whose scope subroutines
were replaced with stubs that echo instead of running the suites: single scope, all
three multi-scope forms, mixed case, duplicates, `--filter` on either side of
`--scope`, `--filter` alone still implying `r`, each help form both alone and trailing
a `--scope`, and the error paths (unknown scope alone and inside a list, `--scope`
with no value, and whitespace-only).

`rstudio-tests.bat --scope core,rserver` was then run against a real build: the
`core` and `shared_core` suites ran, `rserver` reported that it is not built on this
platform, and the exit code still reflected the one failing test
(`Win32ConPtyTest.CtrlCByteTerminatesBusyChild`, a pre-existing failure under a nested
pseudo-console).

title: Match renamed delete-confirmation button in PA history e2e
description:
## Summary

Fixes the `@ai` e2e test `panes/posit-assistant-chat/conversation-history.test.ts`, which failed at the delete-confirmation step.

Posit Assistant renamed the delete dialog's confirm button from "Delete this conversation" to "Delete conversation" (posit-dev/assistant#1829, shipped in PA 0.9.x). The page object still matched the old label with a `:has-text()` substring locator, so the button was never found. The stale selector went unnoticed until now because the test previously failed earlier, at the rename step (fixed in posit-dev/assistant#1915).

## Changes

- `chat_pane.page.ts`: `getDeleteConfirmButton()` now uses a role-based locator with an exact accessible name (`getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete conversation', exact: true })`). Exact matching avoids ambiguity with the dialog's identically worded title.
- `conversation-history.test.ts`: update the comment referencing the old button label.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` passes in `e2e/rstudio`.
- Verified against a manual run: the test now reaches the delete dialog with the renamed conversation title displayed; the dialog's confirm button renders as "Delete conversation".

title: Add version floors to i18n-helpers Python requirements
description:
## Summary

Snyk flags `src/gwt/tools/i18n-helpers/commands.cmd.xml/requirements.txt` for [CVE-2024-5569](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-5569) / [SNYK-PYTHON-ZIPP-7430899](https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PYTHON-ZIPP-7430899) (infinite loop in `zipp`, CVSS 6.9 medium), introduced through `pytest@7.4.4 → importlib-metadata@6.7.0 → zipp@3.15.0`.

That resolution path only exists when the unpinned manifest is resolved for Python 3.7 — those are the last 3.7-compatible releases. On modern Python, pytest ≥ 8 has no `importlib-metadata`/`zipp` dependency at all, so no actual developer or build machine installs the vulnerable package. This change adds version floors (`pytest>=8.4.1`, `lxml>=6.0.1`) so a vulnerable dependency graph can no longer resolve, closing the Snyk finding without pinning a package the tool never uses.

This is a developer-only tooling change (the i18n helper runs at build time and nothing here ships in the product), so there is no NEWS.md entry.

## Verification

- Fresh venv install from the updated requirements resolves pytest 9.1.1 / lxml 6.1.1 with no `zipp` or `importlib-metadata` present
- `python -m pytest test_commands_xml_to_i18n.py` passes on the new versions
- Regenerating `CmdConstants_en.properties` from `Commands.cmd.xml` with the new versions produces byte-identical output to the committed file

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: e2e: handle assistant AskUser prompts and NES edit batching in the @ai tests
description:
Two failures from a full `--grep @ai` run against 2026.08.0-daily+144 with Posit Assistant 0.7.8.

## Filesystem guardrails, test 3 (write outside the project)

The assistant pauses on an AskUser question ("Write outside project folder") instead of running the `writeLines()` call, and the test passed no answer, so `pollWithAllowDialogs` failed with "paused on a question and no answer was configured".

The prompt now tells the assistant not to ask, and the test answers affirmatively if it asks anyway, so `.rs.chat.withGuardrails` is still what denies the write. The affirmative matcher is shared with test 4 (rename to outside the project) and rejects redirect options: something like "Yes, write it inside the project instead" opens with an affirmative but performs an allowed in-project write, which would satisfy test 4's file assertions without the guardrail being consulted. An option set where nothing matches raises an error listing the options the assistant offered.

## Code suggestions, NES multiple renames

Copilot batched the last three call-site renames into one multi-edit accept, so the document was fully renamed after two accepts. The loop asked for a third: its guard wait saw the outgoing preview, `acceptNesRename` re-checked the same locators after the teardown, and the test failed on a 30s timeout waiting for a suggestion that was no longer needed.

The loop now runs on the call sites still holding the old name rather than a count of accepts, and `acceptNesRename` owns the only wait for a suggestion. A timeout there is logged and falls through to the occurrence assertions, which name the call site that is still wrong. Those assertions also check that each `fn(score)` form is gone, so a suggestion that duplicates a call instead of replacing it fails.

## Verification

Both tests pass on macOS desktop against that daily build. The failures are nondeterministic -- they depend on whether the assistant asks before acting and on how the provider batches NES edits -- so a green run does not by itself exercise the changed paths. The run log shows which path ran: `Answered pending assistant question with ...` for the guardrail test, and `Accepted N NES suggestion(s)` with the per-round remaining-occurrence list for the NES test.

Test-only change, so no NEWS.md entry.

title: e2e: make AskUser answers explicit in the chat guardrail tests
description:
Follow-up to #18372, which stopped the guardrail tests hanging when Posit Assistant pauses on an `AskUser` question. This makes the answers those tests give correct rather than incidental.

**Test 5 (`.env` read) was failing.** Asked to read `.env`, the assistant now pauses and offers to redact: "Show variable names only" (its recommended choice), "Show full contents anyway", "Check for a specific variable". No answer was configured, so the harness raised the fail-fast error added in #18372.

Answering with a redacting option would pass `expect(response).not.toContain('abc123')` on the assistant's own discretion, without the guardrail being consulted at all. The secret-read tests (5, 6, 8) now answer with the option that insists on the raw contents, so the assertion means what it claims: the guardrail denies the read even when the user asks for it outright.

**Test 4's matcher was unanchored** (`/yes|proceed|move it/i`). An option's accessible name is its label followed by its description, and the option set is written by the model, so a negative option phrased "No, don't proceed" or "No, don't move it" matches too. `.first()` resolves in DOM order, so a negative listed first would answer *decline* -- the file stays put, both assertions pass, and the guardrail is never exercised. Not reachable with the labels seen so far, so this one is latent.

Changes:

- `chat-guardrails.test.ts`: `SHOW_RAW_CONTENTS` matcher for tests 5, 6 and 8; test 4's matcher anchored to `/^(?:yes|proceed|go ahead|move it)\b/i`. Anchoring also excludes the description from matching, since it never starts the accessible name.
- `chat_pane.actions.ts`: `answerPendingQuestion()` fails with the offered option labels when nothing matches, instead of a bare click timeout. A too-narrow matcher should be a loud, diagnosable failure; the one thing it must never do is answer the opposite of what the caller intended.

Tests 6 and 8 were skipped by `describe.serial` after 5 failed, so their option labels are unobserved -- they get the same matcher on the assumption they elicit the same redact-or-not question. If the labels differ enough not to match, the failure names the options offered.

Test-only change; no NEWS entry.

Verification: `npm run typecheck` passes; the matchers were checked against the option labels captured in the failing run's snapshot.

title: e2e: match RStudio PIDs case-insensitively on macOS
description:
## Problem

Running the `@ai` e2e suite on macOS left an orphaned RStudio instance running after the run finished, showing "Posit Assistant not installed" in the chat pane.

`getRStudioPids()` ran `pgrep -x rstudio`, which is case-sensitive. The macOS executable is `/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/RStudio`, so the pattern never matched. The trailing `|| true` turned pgrep's no-match exit 1 into empty output, so the miss was silent — no warning, just an empty set.

`relaunchAfterRestart()` kills the post-restart instance by diffing RStudio PIDs before and after the restart. With both snapshots empty, it killed nothing and logged `New PIDs to kill: none`.

Nothing else caught the orphan. It is spawned by `ApplicationLaunch.launchRStudio` as a detached, `unref`'d process with no `--remote-debugging-port`, so the CDP port cleanup in `launchRStudioOnce`, the `process-reaper` backstop (which only tracks processes the fixture spawned), and `shutdownRStudio` (which only touches `session.rstudioProcess`) all miss it by design.

The orphan inherits the sandbox `RSTUDIO_CONFIG_ROOT` / `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` whose `pai` tree `uninstall-posit-ai.test.ts` had just deleted, which is why it renders the "not installed" state. That spec is the last `@ai` file to run under `workers: 1`, so the instance was left over at the end of every run.

Windows was unaffected (`Get-Process` is case-insensitive) and Linux was unaffected (`/usr/bin/rstudio` is already lowercase).

## Change

`pgrep -x rstudio` → `pgrep -ix rstudio`, with a comment recording why the `-i` matters.

## Testing

`npm run test:desktop -- --grep @ai` on macOS: all tests pass and no RStudio instance is left running afterward. `npm run typecheck` passes.

## Note

No NEWS.md entry — this changes e2e test infrastructure only, with no user-facing effect.

title: e2e: answer Posit Assistant AskUser prompts in chat guardrail tests
description:
Posit Assistant 0.7.8 can pause a turn on an `AskUser` question instead of acting. The question renders as a form (`Pending questions` tab strip, radio options, `Submit Answers`) and the turn stays active until it is answered, so `pollWithAllowDialogs` -- which waits for the stop button to disappear -- spun until the test timeout.

This showed up as `4: rename from project to outside is denied` in `chat-guardrails.test.ts` failing with a 120s timeout: asked to rename a file to a path outside the project, the assistant asked for confirmation rather than calling `file.rename()` and hitting the R guardrail.

Changes:

- `chat_pane.page.ts`: role-based locators for the question form (`pendingQuestions`, `submitAnswersBtn`) and an `isPendingQuestionVisible()` probe.
- `chat_pane.actions.ts`: `answerPendingQuestion()` selects a matching option and submits, waiting for the form to unmount. `pollWithAllowDialogs()` takes an optional `answerQuestion` matcher; without one, a pending question throws immediately with the question text instead of spinning to the timeout.
- `chat-guardrails.test.ts`: test 4 pins the prompt to R's `file.rename()` -- the assistant's own file tools and shell commands are not subject to `.rs.chat.withGuardrails`, so an unpinned prompt can move the file for real -- and answers affirmatively if asked, since declining would leave the file in place and pass the assertions without exercising the guardrail.

Test-only change; no NEWS entry.

Verification: `npm run typecheck` passes. These tests are gated on Posit AI credentials (`requireAiCredentials`), which CI does not provision, so they run locally only.

title: Add @chat tag for selecting the Posit Assistant e2e tests
description:
### Intent

The `@ai` tag selects both the Posit Assistant chat suites and the Copilot / Posit AI code-suggestion suites (ghost text, NES). There was no way to run just the Assistant tests. This adds a `@chat` tag for that.

```bash
npx playwright test --grep @chat
```

No associated GitHub issue -- this is test-tooling only.

### Approach

Every suite under `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/` is tagged `@chat`:

- The 17 suites that already carried `@ai` keep it and gain `@chat`, so `--grep @ai` selects exactly what it did before.
- `chat-guardrails-paths.test.ts` gets `@chat` only. It drives the guardrails through `.rs.chat.withGuardrails` from the R console with no AI provider in the loop, so it needs no credentials and must keep running under `--grep-invert @ai`. A note in its header docstring records that, so the missing `@ai` doesn't read as an oversight.

No change to `playwright.config.ts`: `@chat` is a selection tag, not an exclusion, so nothing goes into either project's `grepInvert`. No change to `tests/auth.setup.ts` either -- Playwright does not apply `--grep` to a project's dependencies, so the setup project still runs and provisions credentials under `--grep @chat`.

The CI workflows already forward a `grep` `workflow_dispatch` input to `--grep`, so `@chat` works there with no workflow changes.

`shiny-app-python.draft.ts` is left untagged: it is a `.draft.ts` wrapping a `describe.skip`, so it is never collected and a tag on it would be inert.

### Automated Tests

This change is entirely test metadata. Verified by test selection:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `--grep @chat` | 80 tests / 19 files (78 plus the 2 setup tests) |
| chat files selected by `@chat` | 18 of 18 |
| `code_suggestions` + `edit_suggestions` under `@chat` | 0 |
| `--grep @ai` | 78 tests / 20 files, unchanged |
| `--grep-invert @ai` | still runs `chat-guardrails-paths.test.ts` (31 tests) |
| setup project under `--grep @chat` | both auth tests present |

### QA Notes

None. No product code is touched.

### Documentation

`e2e/rstudio/README.md`: a `@chat` row in the Available Tags table and a `--grep @chat` example in the Filtering by Tag section.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` -- N/A, test tooling only, no user-facing change
- [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards -- N/A, no UI change
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: Harden Posit Assistant e2e tests to fail fast with attributable errors
description:
Four `@ai` chat tests turned any "assistant couldn't run the code" failure into an opaque 120s timeout (or a failure pointed at the wrong subsystem), because they waited for a success signal that never arrives when the assistant's `executeCode` tool is broken. This hardens each to fail fast with an attributable message. Diagnostic hardening only -- no product behavior change, no NEWS.md entry.

## Changes

- **`readline-notification.test.ts`** -- the poll only waited for the readline notification, so when the assistant never ran blocking code, R never blocked and the test hung to the 120s test timeout. Now detects the terminal "turn finished without blocking" state and fails with an attributable message. The poll is bounded below the per-test budget so this assertion reports the failure. Addresses #18365.

- **`shiny-app-r.test.ts`** -- the 300s completion poll ran under the 120s config default because the test body never set its own timeout, so slow Shiny cold-starts died before the poll's more informative timeout could fire. Sets a 360s test-body timeout that outlasts the poll, and fails fast when the turn finishes without the "app started" marker. Addresses #18366.

- **`plots-pane-activation.test.ts`** -- the assistant emits `PLOT_DONE_E2E` because the prompt tells it to, even when no plot was drawn, so a broken execution tool masqueraded as an #18037 regression. Now gates on real plot history (`clearPlots` enables only when the Plots pane has a plot) before the activation assertion. Addresses #18364.

- **`renameConversation` helper (`chat_pane.actions.ts`)** -- logged success right after pressing Enter, so a rename that never persisted surfaced downstream as an opaque `locator.click` timeout. Now asserts the renamed item is visible in the still-open history list before returning. Addresses #18363.

The "turn finished" fast-fail paths require the condition to hold across one short re-check, so a transient Stop-button gap between the assistant's intermediate tool steps does not produce a false failure.

## Notes

These are diagnostic-only. Against builds affected by posit-dev/assistant#1893 (the `r.getLogger is not a function` `executeCode` outage) and posit-dev/assistant#1894 (rename persistence), the tests will still fail -- they just pin the failure to the real cause instead of an opaque timeout.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` passes. The tests require AI credentials and a live Posit Assistant backend, so the runtime behavior needs manual verification against an `@ai` run.

title: Block Options apply while a Posit Assistant install check is pending
description:
Closes #18350.

### Problem

Selecting a Posit Assistant code assistant (or chat provider) starts an asynchronous install/update check that later shows an install prompt. Confirming Global Options with **OK** before that check resolved persisted the selection (`assistant = "posit"`) on an independent path, while the install prompt was orphaned -- so the addon was never installed (`manifest-check.json` present, no `bin/`) and completions failed silently with "Posit AI: No completions available." `showProgress` is a non-modal slide label, so it could not gate OK.

### Change

- **Block apply while a check is pending.** `AssistantPreferencesPane` tracks in-flight Posit install/update checks with a count; `validate()` refuses OK/Apply (with a "Checking for Updates" message) while the count is greater than zero, so the selection cannot be persisted before the install prompt appears. The count is incremented at each user-driven entry point -- the assistant selector (before the `assistantVerifyInstalled` round-trip), the chat selector, and the Install button -- and decremented in every terminal branch (the eight `UpdateCheckCallback` methods plus the verify call's stale-result and error paths). A count (rather than a boolean) keeps overlapping checks from unblocking apply too early.
- **Harden update-check parsing.** `PositAiInstallManager.checkForUpdates` now reads every response flag null-safely and routes a null/malformed payload (a missing required discriminator) to `onCheckFailed` -- which offers to install -- instead of throwing (which would skip every callback and strand the apply guard) or defaulting to "up to date" (which would let the selection persist without a confirmed install). Only the genuinely optional `isDowngrade` and `additionalProvidersAvailable` fields still default to false.
- **Keep the Playwright helpers deterministic.** With OK now blocked during the check, `e2e/rstudio/actions/assistant_options.actions.ts` settles the install prompt before configuring the rest of the pane, and confirms OK with a retry that tolerates a briefly-blocked OK.
- Adds a NEWS entry and two localized strings for the warning dialog.

### Scope / follow-up

This covers the confirm/OK path (fresh-profile None -> Posit and the Posit chat provider). Switching the code assistant **from GitHub Copilot to Posit** persists `"posit"` eagerly through a separate pre-existing path (`disableCopilot`) that this change does not cover; that is tracked in #18356.

### Verification

- `cd src/gwt && ant javac` -- clean.
- `cd e2e/rstudio && npm run typecheck` -- clean.

The `@ai` Playwright suite (which installs the addon and asserts ghost text / NES) is the end-to-end guard for this behavior but requires AI credentials and network, so it was not run locally -- **manual verification of the install flow is recommended before merge.**

title: speed up e2e ci builds
description:
## Summary

Windows e2e PR runs currently take ~100 minutes wall time (~56-63 min build + ~40 min tests, serial). Step-level timing of recent runs shows almost all of it is build-job overhead rather than the tests, with two structural problems and several fixed costs:

- **sccache hits ~0% on PR builds.** The GHA cache backend writes per-object entries into each PR's merge-ref scope; 6,150 of the repo's 6,174 Actions cache entries were sccache objects, pinning the repo at the 10 GB quota and LRU-evicting the main-scoped copies the weekly seeds maintain. (The Windows seed run itself hits 98%.) This affects **all ten** e2e build platforms, not just Windows.
- **NSIS packaging spends ~11.5 min in solid-LZMA compression** (`CPack: Create package`) on a throwaway 99.9.9 installer that is consumed exactly once by the e2e job in the same run.
- ~200 objects are non-cacheable on every Windows run, the disk-space cleanup step blocks for ~4.3 min, and the test step runs ~35 min per shard at 2 shards.

## Changes

- **S3 sccache backend on all ten e2e build workflows** (`AWS_SCCACHE_ROLE_ARN` secret + `AWS_SCCACHE_BUCKET` repo variable, assumed via OIDC): no quota, no ref scoping, so PR and main runs share one cache. Per-platform key prefixes (`win64`, `macos-arm64`, `ubuntu24-x86_64`, ...); the two Ubuntu 24 builds share a prefix deliberately (same toolchain, overwhelmingly the same sources). Falls back to the GHA backend whenever the secret/variable are unset (fork PRs) or the credential exchange fails, preserving today's behavior. Backend selection must precede the `sccache-action` step, which only exports the Actions cache token when `SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED` is already set.
- **`CPACK_NSIS_COMPRESSOR=zlib` for CI Windows builds**, passed through a new `RSTUDIO_CMAKE_EXTRA_ARGS` env hook in `make-package.bat` (official builds are unaffected).
- ~~`/Z7` instead of `/Zi`~~: tried and reverted -- the verification run showed the same 209 non-cacheable compiles with it applied, so /Zi was never the blocker (the seed's 98% hit rate already implied /Zi caches fine). The 209 non-cacheable compiles remain unexplained (deterministic across runs); worth a separate look but orthogonal to this PR.
- **Windows disk-space cleanup runs as a detached background process**, overlapping the cache restores and dependency install; a marker-gated wait before the build step keeps it deterministic.
- **4 Windows e2e shards instead of 2** (per-shard setup is only ~5 min, so this converts nearly 1:1 into wall-clock savings).
- **Cache-seed sentinel now opens an alert issue** when a seed workflow's latest completed run did not succeed. `startup_failure` never runs any job that could report itself, and the Windows seed startup-failed silently on two consecutive weekends (July 6 and 13).

## Infrastructure (provisioned)

Private bucket `rstudio-sccache` (us-east-1, 30-day expiry, public access blocked) and IAM role `rstudio-sccache-github` (GitHub OIDC, `sub` scoped to `repo:rstudio/rstudio:*`, 2 h max session) in the rstudio-ide account; `AWS_SCCACHE_ROLE_ARN` secret and `AWS_SCCACHE_BUCKET` variable are set on this repo.

## Verification

All on branch dispatches of the Windows workflow:

- **Full build-from-source + 4-shard e2e** (GHA fallback path, zlib packaging, background cleanup): [run 29965892500](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/29965892500) -- **478 passed / 0 failed / 84 skipped / 0 flaky**; e2e wall time ~26 min (was ~40 at 2 shards); NSIS packaging 3m45s (was ~11.5 min).
- **S3 backend, cold (seeding)**: [run 29969230675](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/29969230675) -- OIDC role assumption succeeded, 551 objects written to `rstudio-sccache/win64/`; the free-space-gated cleanup wait passed with no stall.
- **S3 backend, warm**: [run 29973183206](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/29973183206) -- **98.50% hit rate** (593 hits, 0.14s avg read), compile phase ~13 min, **build job 22 minutes total** (PR builds were ~56-63 min).
- The nine non-Windows migrations follow the identical, fallback-protected pattern; `actionlint` confirmed byte-identical finding sets against `main` (nothing introduced) across all touched files. The sentinel's seed-failure alerting is validated by lint/YAML only (exercising it requires a failing seed run).

title: revive client event stream after session restart
description:
Fixes #18340.

### Problem

On RStudio Server, after a session restart the client can stop receiving events until the user's next action. See #18340 for the full mechanism and CI-run timeline; in short:

1. `suspend_for_restart` takes the session down; the `get_events` long-poll errors (rserver maps a dead session socket to `Unavailable`, or a bare 503 surfaced as a transmission error). Events requests never initiate session launches, so polling alone cannot bring the session back.
2. `RemoteServerEventListener.onError` stops the listener: immediately for `UNAVAILABLE`, or after at most 5 retries at 500ms otherwise.
3. The existing revival hooks all depend on further client activity: every RPC *send* calls `ensureListeningForEvents()`, but its bounded `ensureListening(10)` burst (2.5s) typically loses the race against the session relaunch that the same RPC triggers; RPC *responses* only call `ensureEvents()` when they report `"ep": "true"`. A client passively waiting for console output sends no RPCs, so nothing ever revives the stream -- including delivery of `DeferredInitCompletedEvent`, which is what runs the queued chunks after "Restart R and Run All Chunks".

### Fix

`RemoteServerEventListener` now schedules a slow-cadence (5s) revival attempt whenever it stops due to errors (both the `UNAVAILABLE` path and the retry-budget-exhausted path), making revival independent of further user/RPC activity. The revival timer:

- is cancelled by `stop()`, so deliberate stops -- hidden multi-session tabs (`ApplicationVisibility`), window close -- are not overridden;
- re-checks `isListening_` / `sessionWasQuit_` / `isDisconnected()` before starting, so it no-ops after quit/disconnect or if `ensureListening`/`ensureEvents` already restarted the listener;
- cannot resurrect a suspended session: rserver's events handler does not initiate session launches, so a suspended-but-not-restarting session just keeps returning `Unavailable` to the (cheap) 5s probes until a real RPC relaunches it.

This is the "another way to restart the listener (perhaps a global timer that checks for isListening every few seconds)" already anticipated by the comment in the listener's constructor.

Defense-in-depth hardening in the same area:

- `listenErrorCount_` now resets when a poll succeeds. It was previously only reset when the give-up branch ran, making the 5-retry budget a lifetime budget: a tab that had absorbed six transient errors over hours would skip the quick retries entirely on the next incident.
- The 500ms quick retries now go through the same guarded revival timer instead of anonymous `Timer` instances, so `stop()` cancels them (an in-flight retry can no longer override a deliberate stop) and they observe the `sessionWasQuit_` / `isDisconnected()` guards.
- A revival attempt logs a single-line breadcrumb to the browser console, so future event-delivery gaps are diagnosable from a trace.

### Tests

Deliberately no e2e timeout changes: a dead event stream is not woken by waiting longer (only by client activity), so extended waits would neither rescue a pre-fix binary nor help a post-fix one. The always-on `rmarkdown.test.ts` "empty chunk does not define variables" spec -- which runs in every PR's server-linux e2e job and exercises exactly the restart -> event-delivery -> run-chunks path -- keeps its tight 60s budget and serves as the regression canary for this fix (now noted in a comment there).

### Verification

- `ant javac` passes; e2e `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- PR-triggered e2e workflow (desktop + server, all platforms) exercises the fix.

title: harden help-popup data-preview test against single-result auto-accept
description:
## Problem

The `help_popup_data_preview.test.ts` e2e test is intermittently failing on loaded CI runners (observed on `macos / e2e-desktop-macos`), timing out at:

```
Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
  Locator: locator('#rstudio_popup_completions')
  Timeout: 20000ms
```

## Root cause

The test creates a **single-member** list, `list(df = head(mtcars))`, then completes `<list>$` and asserts the completion popup appears. Its trigger races:

```js
await consoleActions.typeInConsole(`${LIST_NAME}$`);
if (!(await page.locator(COMPLETION_POPUP).isVisible())) {  // point-in-time sample
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+Space');               // explicit request
}
```

`Control+Space` routes to `RCompletionManager.codeCompletion()` -> `beginSuggest(..., canAutoInsert=true)`. In `RCompletionManager` a request that returns **exactly one** result with `canAutoAccept_` is **auto-accepted without ever showing the popup** (unless `isCompletionPopupForced()`). Because the list has a single member, the completion is unique:

- **Idle machine:** the `$` auto-trigger popup is already visible when `isVisible()` is sampled, the fallback is skipped, and the popup stays up -> passes.
- **Loaded runner:** the `$` popup has not rendered yet at sample time, the fallback `Control+Space` fires, the lone `df` is auto-accepted, and the popup never appears -> 20s timeout on both the attempt and the retry.

The sibling helpers in `autocomplete.actions.ts` already guard against this with `setAlwaysShowPopup(true)`; this test never adopted the convention.

## Fix

Force the completion popup via the automation-only `window.rstudio.completions.setAlwaysShowPopup` override **before** triggering completion (wrapped in `try/finally` to restore it). This defeats the single-result auto-accept, so the popup renders deterministically regardless of runner load, timing, or member count. Mirrors the existing `autocomplete.actions.ts` pattern; no-op on builds predating the knob.

`npm run typecheck` passes.

title: include os in debug symbol archive names to avoid overwrites
description:
## Problem

Debug symbol archives on S3 are named `${product}-${package_format}-${arch}.tar.xz` (e.g. `Server-RPM-x86_64.tar.xz`). The rhel8, rhel9, and opensuse15 builds all produce RPMs, so for each release their x86_64 (and arm64) jobs upload to the same key and overwrite each other -- last writer wins.

This was discovered while investigating a customer rserver core dump on RHEL 9 (Workbench 2026.05.0+218.pro1): the symbols at `s3://rstudio-debug-symbols/2026.05.0+218.pro1/Server-RPM-x86_64.tar.xz` have build ID `f16f630d...`, which does not match the released rhel9 RPM's rserver (`455757ec...`) but exactly matches the rhel8 RPM's rserver. The archive also carries a RHEL 8 GCC 8.5.0 toolchain signature, while the rhel9 binary was built with GCC 11.4.1.

Separately, the `debuginfo` download script shipped with the product expects archives named `${PRODUCT}-${OS}-${ARCH}.tar.xz` (with values baked in from `make-package`, e.g. `workbench-rhel9-x86_64`), so it has never matched what the uploader produced.

## Fix

- `upload-debug-symbols` now takes `<product> <flavor> <package> <os> <arch>`: flavor/package locate the build directory (via `vars.sh`), while product/os/arch name the archive. Archives are now uploaded as e.g. `workbench-rhel9-x86_64.tar.xz`, matching the shipped `debuginfo` script and making the key unique per OS.
- `Jenkinsfile.linux` passes `${PRODUCT}` (from `utils.getProductName()`, the same value baked into `debuginfo`) and `${env.OS}` through to the script.
- Fixed a `bad substitution` (`${prefix.tar.xz}`) in `debuginfo` that aborted downloads at the unpack step.

## Notes

- Symbols for the "losing" OSes of already-published releases were overwritten at upload time and are not recoverable from the bucket; symbolizing those dumps requires rebuilding the release tag on the matching OS.
- The pro repo's `Jenkinsfile.linux` has the identical invocation line, so this should merge cleanly on the next open-source -> pro merge.


## Backfill tooling

Two scripts codify the recovery procedure for releases whose symbols were lost to the collision (validated end-to-end against Workbench 2026.05.0+218.pro1 on rhel9):

- `package/linux/scripts/prepare-symbol-backfill <version>` -- prepares a `rel-*` branch from the release tag (Jenkins multibranch discovery only indexes `main`/`rel-*`) with the OS-aware uploader backported if the tag predates it, and `rstudio-version.sh` pinned to the released version. The pin matters: the version string is compiled in, and an unpinned rebuild shifts code layout enough to misalign symbols. Prints the Jenkins runbook for the rest of the procedure.
- `package/linux/scripts/verify-debug-symbols <binary> <debug-file>` -- dependency-free ELF comparison that checks what symbolization actually requires (section addresses/sizes, `.dynsym` vs `.symtab` addresses), distinguishing benign build-metadata drift in `.rodata` from real incompatibility. A backfilled build's GNU build ID never matches, so gdb needs `symbol-file` to load the result.

title: Ship macOS diagnostics and rpostback as universal binaries
description:
## Summary

On macOS, `RStudio.app` is a universal (x86_64 + arm64) application, but the `diagnostics` and `rpostback` helper binaries shipped Intel-only, forcing them to run under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon. This builds both helpers as universal binaries and removes the now-unnecessary Rosetta 2 handling.

## Universal binaries

- The macOS package build performs an arm64 alternate build of `diagnostics` and `rpostback`, then merges the arm64 and x86_64 slices with `lipo` during packaging. `rpostback` is now built in the alternate build (it was previously skipped there).
- `make-package` sets `RSTUDIO_UNIVERSAL_BUILD` when both architectures are being built, and the merge step is gated on that flag so single-arch builds are unaffected.
- The merge verifies each input slice exists and that the merged binaries carry no Homebrew or `/usr/local` load paths, failing the build otherwise.
- `@electron/universal` is updated to 3.0.6.
- The macOS Boost build is pinned to the target architecture, so an x86_64 primary build links x86_64 Boost.

## Rosetta 2 removal

With every RStudio component now native on Apple Silicon, RStudio itself no longer needs Rosetta 2. The only remaining consumer would be an Intel (x86_64) build of R, but macOS R detection executes the R binary (`detectREnvironment`), which cannot run without Rosetta 2 — so an Intel R is never detected on a machine lacking it, and no Rosetta 2 prompt is reachable. The Rosetta 2 subsystem is therefore removed:

- the skippable startup warning and its `checkForRosetta` user-state preference,
- the `desktop_detect_rosetta` IPC path (main handler, renderer bridge, `DesktopFrame`, startup call), and
- the associated localized strings.

An Apple Silicon Mac with only an Intel R installed and no Rosetta 2 now falls back to the existing "R Not Found" path.

## Testing

- Desktop: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and unit tests pass.
- Universal packaging verified with a full macOS package build; the merged `diagnostics` and `rpostback` binaries contain both architectures.

Closes #12572.

title: Publish Ubuntu 26 (resolute) daily builds via Jammy republish
description:
## Intent

Start producing and publishing Ubuntu 26.04 (`resolute`) daily builds, following the existing Noble republish pattern.

Ubuntu 26 uses the same binaries as Jammy (same as Noble does today), so no new build target is needed. This republishes the existing Jammy dailies under a `resolute-*` platform path, the same way Jammy is already republished as Noble.

Port of rstudio/rstudio-pro#11937 to OS.

## Approach

`jenkins/utils.groovy`:

- **`optionalPublishToDailies`** — the republish mapping was a 1:1 map (`'jammy': 'noble'`), which can't express a second target for the same source OS. Changed the values to lists (`'jammy': ['noble', 'resolute']`) and loop over them, so Jammy now republishes as both Noble and Resolute. RHEL 9 → RHEL 10 is unchanged in behavior.
- **`getArchForOs`** — added `resolute` to the Debian-like OS list so the arch translation (`x86_64` → `amd64`, `noarch` → `all`) applies to the republished Ubuntu 26 packages.

## Note

The Ubuntu 26.04 short name is assumed to be `resolute`. If Canonical's final short name differs, the mapping value and downstream platform keys need updating.

title: Align Ubuntu 26 E2E engine and fix Fedora report publish
description:
Brings the Ubuntu 26 desktop E2E engine up to the conventions every other per-OS engine already follows, and fixes a latent breakage in the Fedora 43/44 engines' report publishing.

Ubuntu 26 was the last engine still missing:
- the `run-with-heartbeat.mjs` hang watchdog around the Playwright run,
- `PW_PROJECT_LABEL` (the dead `PW_PROJECT_NAME` it set was never read by `playwright.config.ts`), with `SHARD_NAME` versioned to match (`desktop-linux-ubuntu26-x86_64`),
- the `defer_merge` input, and
- the S3 report publish (secret, `id-token` grant, publish step, and the online-report link in the sticky comment).

The Fedora 43/44 engines were created after the report publisher migrated from Connect to S3 (#18132), but were patterned on the pre-migration copy: their publish step still passed `connect-api-key`/`title` to an action that now only accepts `role-arn`/`label`. Composite actions ignore unknown inputs, so the step silently did nothing and those engines have never published a report. This corrects the inputs, adds the missing `id-token: write` grant and `AWS_E2E_REPORTS_ROLE_ARN` secret, and updates the stale comment wording.

The scheduled rotation now passes `AWS_E2E_REPORTS_ROLE_ARN` to all three engines, and the stale "(ubuntu26 doesn't upload)" comment is removed.

Both the Ubuntu 26 and Fedora 43/44 daily-download paths were validated pre-merge via a temporary trigger.

No user-facing change (test infrastructure only), so no NEWS.md entry.

title: fix(core): skip FileLogFallsBackToStderrWhenDirectoryNotWritable when…
description:
… run as root

The test makes a log directory read-only (chmod 0500) and asserts that log writes fall back to stderr with a one-time notice. Root bypasses directory permission bits, so the write succeeds, the fallback path is never taken, and the assertions fail. Projects that run these unit tests as root therefore hit a deterministic failure.

Skip the test when the effective user is root, matching the GTEST_SKIP pattern already used for environment-dependent tests in this suite.

title: Add agent-driven GitHub Copilot sign-in for E2E credential parity
description:
Brings GitHub Copilot credential handling to parity with Posit AI in the
Playwright E2E suite. Previously Copilot credentials could only be provided by
copying an already-signed-in store from the host, so a machine that had never
signed in to Copilot couldn't provision it. This adds a live device-flow
sign-in, driven by the copilot-language-server over stdio plus a trusted-click
browser authorize step, so the setup can authenticate from scratch the same way
auth.setup.ts already does for Posit AI.

Included:
- Agent-driven Copilot device-flow sign-in wired into auth.setup.ts, with
  auto-detect: COPILOT_USER/COPILOT_PASSWORD trigger a live sign-in, else the
  host store is copied, else the provider is skipped. Fails loud on bad GitHub
  credentials and on a NotAuthorized status.
- The credential gate reads the on-disk Copilot store (auth.db) via
  better-sqlite3 rather than the sqlite3 CLI, which is absent from PATH on
  Windows; the check fails closed so an empty pre-sign-in store no longer reads
  as authenticated.
- Two debug switches: PW_DEBUG_AUTH_CAPTURE (screenshots/HTML) and
  PW_DEBUG_AUTH_STEPS (step narration), with account identifiers kept out of
  logs.
- Both sign-in flows now narrate their steps consistently under
  PW_DEBUG_AUTH_STEPS, through a shared [authorize-<provider>] logger;
  previously only the GitHub flow narrated steps and Posit AI logged only on
  failure under a different prefix.
- Setup completion messages are mode-aware: on Server they warn that the
  sandbox credentials will not reach the rsession, which reads the logged-in
  user's real home directory. This surfaces (does not fix) a pre-existing
  server-mode HOME gap that affects Posit AI too.
- Fixes an isVisible-with-timeout race in the device-authorize flow, shares a
  single sign-in browser launcher, and documents the new environment variables
  and credential gating.

Addresses #18306.
Addresses #18334.

title: Add Ubuntu 22 x86_64 E2E engine and wire into scheduled rotation
description:
Adds a new per-OS E2E Playwright engine for Ubuntu 22 (jammy) x86_64 desktop, following the conventions of the existing sibling engines, and wires it into the scheduled rotation (Thursday slot; debian13 moved to Friday to keep every weekday at 3 engines).

Along the way this fixes a pre-existing gap in the shared install-dependencies-jammy script (missing libuv1-dev, present on noble/resolute), and works around jammy-runner-specific quirks (pkgconf/pkg-config conflict, default Java 11 instead of 17 for the GWT build).

Both the source-build and daily-download paths were validated pre-merge via a temporary trigger.

Addresses #18307.

title: Install R in the yum build-dependency script
description:
## Summary
`dependencies/linux/install-dependencies-yum` (shared by the Fedora 43, Fedora 44, and RHEL 10 E2E build jobs) never installed an R interpreter before calling `install-common` -> `install-packages`, which assumes `R` is already on `PATH`. This surfaced as `R: command not found` when the Fedora 43/44 build jobs ran with `build_from_source: true` (rstudio/rstudio#18261, #18262). Ubuntu's `install-dependencies-noble` already installs `r-base-dev` for the same reason; this adds the equivalent `R-core`/`R-core-devel` packages here.

title: Remove temporary Rocky 9 pre-merge validation trigger
description: One-line cleanup: deletes `zz-temp-rocky9-trigger.yml`, the push-triggered validation caller used to test the Rocky 9 x86_64 E2E engine (#18343) before it existed on the default branch. It was left in by mistake when that PR merged; this removes it.

title: Add Rocky 9 x86_64 E2E engine and wire into scheduled rotation
description:
Adds a Rocky 9 x86_64 desktop E2E Playwright engine and wires it into the scheduled rotation, extending RHEL-family coverage to RHEL/Rocky 9 (the Rocky 10 arm64 engine already covers v10).

The engine is modeled on the Rocky 10 arm64 engine, with these platform differences:
- Runs in a `rockylinux/rockylinux:9` container on `ubuntu-latest` (x86_64).
- Uses Xvfb for the headless display. Unlike RHEL 10, RHEL 9 still ships the X.Org server, so it does not need the Cage/Xwayland setup the v10 engine uses.
- Installs R via rig and pulls R packages as PPM `rhel9` x86_64 binaries.
- Toolchain fallback uses `zlib-devel` (RHEL 9 keeps classic zlib), not the `zlib-ng-compat-devel` the v10 engine needs.
- Installs the `rhel9-x86_64` daily `.rpm` on the download path.

Rocky (a 1:1 RHEL rebuild) is used rather than Red Hat UBI 9 because UBI 9 omits `xorg-x11-server-Xvfb` from all its public repos, the same blocker that keeps the v10 engine off UBI 10 (missing Xwayland).

Rotation wiring: `rocky9` added to the all-engines list and to Monday weekday slate, with a `rhel9` installer-URL resolver output for specific-version dispatches.

title: immortalize scheduled-command statics to avoid teardown races
description:
## Summary

The scheduled-command lists in `SessionModuleContext.cpp` (and the mutex guarding them, added in #18302) are file-scope statics that background threads reach via `module_context::executeOnMainThread()` (SessionPPM, SessionChat, the installed-package event-hook scan). Both process-lifetime exit paths run C++ static destructors -- `exitEarly()` calls `::exit()`, and the everyday quit path ends with `exit()` inside libR via `Rstd_CleanUp` -- so a detached background thread that unblocks during teardown (e.g. an abandoned package scan on a hung network mount finally returning) could touch destroyed statics.

This PR immortalizes the two command lists and their mutex by binding file-scope references to intentionally-leaked heap objects, via a new `core::make_leaked<T>()` helper (`shared_core/Memory.hpp`):

```cpp
ScheduledCommands& s_scheduledCommands = make_leaked<ScheduledCommands>();
ScheduledCommands& s_idleScheduledCommands = make_leaked<ScheduledCommands>();
boost::mutex& s_scheduledCommandsMutex = make_leaked<boost::mutex>();
```

References are not destroyed at exit and the pointee is never deleted, so there is no destructor for a late-running thread to race; call sites keep their original spelling. The leak is unobservable (the objects live for the life of the process either way), and leak checkers do not flag it: the file-scope reference keeps the object reachable, so Valgrind classifies it as "still reachable" (not reported by default) and LeakSanitizer treats it as rooted; in sanitizer builds `make_leaked` additionally calls `__lsan_ignore_object()` to mark the allocation as intentional.

Switching `exitEarly()` to `::_exit()` was considered and rejected -- see #18318 for the full analysis (it doesn't cover the libR exit path, and it would skip the `PosixParentProcessMonitor` atexit handshake, stdio/log flushes, and coverage/profiling flushes).

No NEWS entry: internal hardening with no observed user-facing failure.

## Testing

- Full `core` (457) and `rsession` (405) C++ suites pass.
- `r` scope `packages` tests pass (116; these pump the scheduled-command queue heavily, including from a background scan thread).

Addresses #18318.

title: fix windows .lnk shortcut tests on ci: short-path home defeats home aliasing
description:
## Problem

The scheduled Windows Desktop e2e workflow has failed on every run since #18275 merged (first failure: [run 29611045439](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/29611045439), most recent: [run 29955359944](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/29955359944)). The three failing tests are the file-shortcut cases in `files_shortcuts.test.ts`.

Root cause: the e2e sandbox derives HOME from `os.tmpdir()`, which on the GitHub Windows runners contains an 8.3 short-name component (`C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...`). `fs.realpathSync` does not expand short names (only `fs.realpathSync.native` does), so rsession runs with a short-form HOME. The shell canonicalizes `.lnk` targets to long form, so `IShellLink::GetPath` reports `C:/Users/runneradmin/...` and `createAliasedPath`'s literal prefix match against home fails. The trace shows the direct consequence: following the shortcut opens the target as a second, path-distinct document (absolute path) alongside the `~/`-aliased one, so `waitForActiveDocument('~/...')` times out and the columns dedupe test sees 3 source panels instead of 2.

## Fixes

- **e2e harness**: canonicalize the sandbox root with `fs.realpathSync.native`, expanding 8.3 short names on Windows (identical behavior on macOS/Linux, verified). This also fixes the spurious `[sandbox] R workdir ... is not under PW_SANDBOX` teardown warnings, which were the same path-form mismatch.
- **rsession**: `resolveWindowsShortcut` now normalizes local targets with `GetLongPathName`, so home aliasing and the client's duplicate-document detection are robust to short-form (or case-mismatched) stored targets regardless of environment. UNC/remote targets are skipped to keep the existing no-network-I/O contract, and a failed lookup (e.g. deleted target) keeps the stored path, preserving the broken-shortcut behavior covered by `ResolveReturnsStoredPathWhenTargetDeleted`.

Includes a new `WindowsShortcutTest.ResolvesStoredShortPathToLongForm` gtest (skips when 8.3 names are disabled on the volume).

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` passes for the e2e change; `fs.realpathSync.native` verified equivalent to `fs.realpathSync` on macOS.
- The C++ change is Windows-only and needs the Windows CI build; the new gtest and the next scheduled Windows e2e run are the end-to-end verification.

title: avoid hardcoded ip comparisons in bind address resolution
description:
## Summary

Snyk Code flags any equality comparison against a hardcoded IP literal as a potential "Authentication Bypass by Spoofing" (two LOW findings in `PosixSystem.cpp`). The flagged comparisons are wildcard bind-address detection -- deciding whether the *locally configured* bind address is `0.0.0.0` or `::` -- not peer authentication, so the findings are false positives. Rather than excluding the file from scans via a `.snyk` policy, this parses the configured address with `boost::asio::ip::make_address()` and checks `is_unspecified()`, which is true exactly for the IPv4/IPv6 wildcard addresses. That expresses the intent more directly and removes the pattern the scanner matches on.

Behavior is unchanged for the addresses that previously matched: `0.0.0.0` and `::` still get wildcard resolution, and specific addresses, hostnames, and unparseable strings still pass through untouched. One deliberate edge-case change: alternate spellings of the IPv6 wildcard (`::0`, `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0`) parse to the unspecified address and now also get wildcard resolution instead of passing through verbatim -- the OS would have treated them as the wildcard at bind time anyway.

## Tests

- Moved the `ResolveBindAddress*` / `IsLinkLocalIpv4*` gtests out of the procfs-only `!__APPLE__` guard; they are platform-independent and now also run on macOS.
- Added coverage for hostname/empty-string passthrough and for the alternate IPv6 wildcard spellings.
- All 14 tests pass locally on macOS via `rstudio-core-tests --gtest_filter='*ResolveBindAddress*:*IsLinkLocalIpv4*'`.

title: Prefix rserver --setup-db flags and harden non-interactive runs
description:
## Summary
Follow-up refinement to `rserver --setup-db` (added in #18172, unreleased).

- Prefixes the eight `--setup-db` value flags with `setup-db-` (e.g. `--setup-db-host`, `--setup-db-port`). They were registered in the general option group parsed on every `rserver` start, so a normal start like `rserver --port 8788` silently parsed them as no-ops. The prefix makes them unambiguously setup-db-only.
- Makes the value prompts fail on end of input rather than silently defaulting. A non-interactive run (empty stdin) that omitted a flag previously fell back to a default — port `5432`, database name/user to the default, host/master-username to empty (which libpq can resolve to the local socket) — so a partially-flagged run could quietly target the wrong database. Each prompt now errors, naming the flag to pass; interactively pressing enter still accepts the documented default.

## Testing
- `rstudio-core-tests --gtest_filter='ProgramOptions*'`: 33/33
- `rserver-tests --gtest_filter='ServerSetupDbTests.*'`: 29/29 (8 new, covering EOF failures per field and flags-honored paths)
- Verified the new EOF tests fail with the fix reverted and pass with it restored.
- OSS build (`RSTUDIO_PRO_BUILD=0`): `rserver` links clean.

title: Add Check for Posit Assistant updates command
description:
Adds a "Check for Posit Assistant updates" command to the Help menu. It runs a forced update check and always reports the result in a modal dialog:

- **Up to date** — informational.
- **Update (or initial install) available** — offers to install it.
- **A newer Posit Assistant requires a newer RStudio** (newer protocol / no compatible build / installed version unsupported with no update) — informational, OK only.
- **Error** (network / manifest) — shows the detail when the backend supplies one.

Accepting an available update reuses the existing install engine (`chat_install_update`): it refuses with a clear message while another RStudio session is using Posit Assistant, stops the backend under a cross-process lock, swaps the installation, and restarts. The in-progress conversation is preserved by the existing resume signal (the `&resume` URL param the reloaded UI already sends), which the databot backend honors regardless of the launch-time persona flag.

Posit Assistant can trigger the command itself via a new `ui/checkForUpdates` JSON-RPC method, advertised through `rstudioCapabilities()` so it can decide whether to surface the option. The request fires a `chat_check_for_updates` client event that runs the same modal flow. The Posit Assistant side of this is not implemented in this PR.

Other details:

- The command is bound via `ChatTab.Shim` (like Uninstall Posit Assistant) so it works before the delay-loaded chat presenter exists, and is visible whenever Posit Assistant is enabled.
- When Posit Assistant is not selected as the chat provider or assistant, the install offer is suppressed (the backend would refuse it) and the user is directed to select it.
- The existing "Check for Updates" menu item is relabeled "Check for RStudio Updates" to disambiguate it from the new command.

title: leak statics reachable from background threads at exit
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to #18320, which added `core::make_leaked<T>()` (`shared_core/Memory.hpp`) and immortalized the scheduled-command statics. A survey of `src/cpp` found the remaining file-scope statics with non-trivial destructors that detached background threads can plausibly touch while `exit()` runs static destructors. This PR converts them to intentionally-leaked objects:

- **Logging / SIGHUP config reload** (the detached, never-joined `logConfigReloadThreadFunc` thread loops in `sigwait` forever and calls `reinitLog()` on SIGHUP, so it can run during teardown):
  - `shared_core/Logger.cpp`: the two property-formatter maps on the log-write path (any thread that logs with message properties)
  - `core/system/System.cpp`: `s_logOptions`, `s_loggingMutex`, and `s_programIdentity`, all read by the SIGHUP reload thread via `reinitLog()` -> `initializeLogWriters()`
  - `core/system/PosixSystem.cpp`: `s_sighupHandler` (a `boost::function`, invoked by the same thread), plus its `extern` declarations of the System.cpp statics updated to reference types to match the new definitions
- **File monitor** (`core/system/file_monitor/FileMonitor.cpp`): the registration-command and callback queues were Meyers function-local statics -- exactly the destructor-at-exit problem -- used by the monitor thread, which `stop()` can abandon (detach) on join timeout and which `exitEarly()` never stops.
- **Chat** (`session/modules/SessionChat.cpp`): the mutex-guarded cross-thread state groups (execution tracking, streaming-notification queue, pending-execution queue, manifest update state, update-check override). Current callers marshal onto the main thread (`callbacksRequireMainThread`, `executeOnMainThread`), so these are defensive: the design anticipates cross-thread access and the leak removes any teardown-order risk at zero cost.

Also migrates the existing hand-rolled leaks to `make_leaked` for consistency and greppability: the `Logger` singleton (`static Logger* = new Logger()`) and the two asio `io_context`s (`SessionServerRpc.cpp`, `SessionMain.cpp`, both already `*new ...` with teardown comments from #18018).

Intentionally left alone:

- `SessionClientEventQueue.cpp`'s `s_pClientEventQueue` -- already teardown-safe (raw pointer assigned in an explicit init, never deleted; its mutex/condition members are heap pointers on the leaked object). Converting it would be restructuring churn with no safety gain.
- `ClientEventService` / `OfflineService` Meyers singletons own joinable `boost::thread` members at exit -- a related but different bug class (destructor of a joinable thread), tracked separately if it proves problematic in practice.
- rserver's `ServerAuthHandler.cpp` statics (touched from the HTTP thread pool) -- different process with a different exit discipline; can be done as a follow-up if desired.

No NEWS entry: internal hardening with no observed user-facing failure.

## Testing

- Full `core` (457, including the `LoggingTests` that exercise `reinitLog()`) and `rsession` (405) C++ suites pass.
- `r` scope `packages` + `chat` tests pass (248).

Stacked on #18320 (the base branch); will retarget to `main` once that merges.

Addresses #18318.

title: retry post-restart chunk command; harden flaky e2e tests
description:
Investigation of the four flaky tests in the pr-18320 all-platforms Playwright report (run 29939747123), with fixes for each root cause.

### Product fix: dropped "Restart R and Run All Chunks" continuation

The server-linux flake of `rmarkdown.test.ts :: empty chunk does not define variables` caught a real product race: `TextEditingTargetNotebook` queues the follow-up command (`executeAllCode` / `notebookClearAllOutput`) in `postRestartCommand_`, and `onDeferredInitCompleted()` executed it only if `isEnabled()` was true at that instant, silently dropping it otherwise. `executeAllCode` is a dynamic source command whose enabled/visible state is re-synced by command management that may not have run yet when the handler fires, so R would restart and the chunks would never run (trace: restart completed to a fresh prompt, then no chunk activity for the full 60s wait). The queued command is now retried briefly (100ms cadence, bounded at ~5s) instead of being dropped, with a logged warning if it never re-enables.

Fixes #18326.

### e2e hardening

- **`vcs_flood.test.ts` / `create_projects.test.ts` (desktop-windows)**: the New Project wizard only shows after `get_new_project_context` returns, and that RPC probes the build toolchain (`canBuildCpp`/packrat) -- observed taking **57.4s** on a cold Windows runner (with `set_client_state` queued ~52s behind it). Raised the 15s wizard waits to 90s.
- **`terminal.test.ts` (desktop-macos)**: `openTerminal` returned as soon as the xterm was visible and the tab selected, but before the shell had attached and echoed its prompt -- keystrokes typed in that window were dropped (the failure's terminal buffer contained only the prompt; every typed line was lost). `openTerminal` now waits for a non-empty terminal buffer line and explicitly restores terminal focus before returning.
- **`create_projects.test.ts` quarto types (desktop-windows)**: `quarto create-project` took 70+ seconds on a cold runner (`quarto_capabilities` also blocked the session ~30s), so the session restart into the new project never began within the 60s ready-wait. quarto is now pre-warmed once per worker in `beforeAll` (throwaway `--version` run; the session prepends its resolved quarto to the PATH, so this warms the same binary), and quarto project types carry a larger restart budget as a backstop.

### Verification

- `ant javac` and e2e `npm run typecheck` pass.
- All four affected specs pass locally on macOS desktop-dev against the worktree build (terminal 7/7, rmarkdown 7/7 + 1 skipped, create_projects 7/7, vcs_flood 2/2).

title: avoid S3 dispatch when subsetting user objects in assistant and notebook output
description:
Fixes #18317. Reported downstream in Rdatatable/data.table#7829.

`.rs.assistant.describeChildren()` subset objects with `value[idxs]`, which dispatches S3. For a data.table, `[.data.table` treats `idxs` as row indices, so `dt[1:50]` returns all columns rather than the first 50. Whenever a monitored data.table had more than 50 columns, the resulting length mismatch in `.mapply()` printed two recycling warnings to the console after any command that created or modified the variable (e.g. `setDT(df)` on a 51-column data.frame).

The fix subsets with `.subset(value, idxs)`, which avoids S3 dispatch entirely; it behaves identically for lists, data.frames, pairlists, and expressions.

Includes regression tests in a new `test-assistant.R`; both new dispatch tests fail against the previous sources (`FAIL 4`) and pass with the fix (`FAIL 0 | PASS 8`), verified via the r-scope testthat suite.

---

An audit for other instances of this pattern found one more real case, fixed here as well: `NotebookData.R` truncated wide objects in notebook chunk output with `x[, c(1:cols.max.print)]`. data.table special-cases *literal* column-number `j` expressions, but with a variable (`cols.max.print`) the expression evaluates in the frame of the table and returns the integer vector `1:n` instead of the leading columns, so a data.table wider than `cols.max.print` (default 1000) rendered as a single column of integers. The truncation logic now lives in a dispatch-safe `.rs.truncateDataCapture()` helper that heads rows first and truncates columns on the coerced plain data.frame, with regression tests in `test-notebook.R` (verified against data.table 1.18.4).

title: Fix mislabeled, non-functional Copilot messages preference
description:
