title: Revert Windows VS 2026 (msvc145) toolchain migration
description:
## Summary

Restores the Windows build configuration to `e4e2b13` -- the last commit with a green Windows build -- backing out the VS 2026 / MSVC 14.5 (msvc145) toolchain migration that landed alongside the setlocale fix in #18141 (the #17986 work). Only the toolchain hunks are reverted: the #18139 setlocale fix and its test fixes are preserved, as are the unrelated e2e cache changes from #18151.

## Why

#18141 bumped `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.windows` to `windowsservercore-ltsc2022`, but the Jenkins Windows agents run Windows Server 2019 (build 10.0.17763). A 2022-based (10.0.20348) container cannot run there under process isolation, so the `jenkins/ide:windows-x86_64-pacific-dogwood` image rebuild fails at the `FROM` step. The ECR tag stayed at the pre-migration image, and every later Windows build pulled that stale VS 2022 image -- which the new `windows-checks.cmake` then rejected for reporting toolset 143. `main` has been red on Windows since the migration merged.

## What's in the diff

- Delete `cmake/windows-checks.cmake` and its `CMakeLists.txt` include.
- Restore the msvc143 boost/SOCI prebuilt handling in `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` and `src/cpp/ext/CMakeLists.txt`.
- Restore `docker/jenkins/Dockerfile.windows` (ltsc2019 / VS 2022) and `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` (VS 2022 VsDevCmd path).
- Restore the `dependencies/windows/*` installers, `INSTALL`, and both Windows GitHub Actions workflows to their pre-migration state.

Because this touches `docker/`, merging re-triggers the `Rebuild Docker Images` stage -- now buildable on the Server 2019 agent -- refreshing the ECR image and unblocking downstream builds.

## Reland

The migration can reland once the Windows CI fleet (both the image-builder and the runner agents) is upgraded to Windows Server 2022.

title: Add Fedora 44 desktop e2e Playwright workflow
description:
Adds a standalone `workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` e2e workflow that runs the Playwright desktop suite against RStudio Desktop on Fedora 44, modeled on the Ubuntu 24 desktop workflow.

Since GitHub has no Fedora-hosted runner, both the build and e2e jobs run inside a `fedora:44` container on `ubuntu-latest` (with `SYS_ADMIN` + unconfined seccomp so the Chromium/Electron sandbox can start). The build produces the Electron `.rpm` via `make-electron-package RPM`; the daily-download path resolves the `rhel10-x86_64` electron key, since there is no separate Fedora daily and the RHEL RPM is what runs on Fedora. Cache keys and the `os-e2e-deps` scope are Fedora-scoped to stay isolated from the Ubuntu and RHEL R libraries.

Not wired into `os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml`: standalone and on-demand for now.

title: wait for dismissal property write before re-running package dependency discovery
description:
Fixes #18148.

`TextEditingTargetWidget.toggleDetectMissingPackages` issued the `modify_document_properties` and `discover_package_dependencies` RPCs concurrently. `DocUpdateSentinel.setProperty` only applies the new value to the local property bag once the modify RPC's response arrives, and the discovery response handler (`showRequiredPackagesMissingWarning`) reads that local property, silently suppressing the banner while it still says `"1"`. So when the discovery response arrived before the property-modification response — realistic over rserver-proxied HTTP, and the cause of the intermittent server-linux failures of `missing_packages_banner.test.ts` — re-enabling detection showed no banner and nothing retried.

The toggle now re-runs discovery from the property write's completion callback (`setProperty` with a `ProgressIndicator`), so the local property is guaranteed to read `"0"` before the discovery response consults it. On RPC error the property is never applied locally and discovery is not re-run, matching the previous error behavior (logged, banner stays hidden).

Verified with the existing e2e test (`missing_packages_banner.test.ts`) passing against a dev desktop build; the race itself is timing-dependent and was only observed in server-mode CI.

title: Desktop automation ergonomics: home-aliased paths, focus stealing, worktree dev shim
description:
Developer-only improvements to the Playwright automation harness and worktree tooling; no user-facing behavior changes (the desktop changes are gated on `--automation-agent`).

### e2e: match home-aliased document paths in open-file waits

RStudio reports document paths home-aliased (`~/sub/file.R`) whenever the file lives under the home directory the rsession resolved. On Windows desktop runs, the default Playwright sandbox under `os.tmpdir()` lands in `C:/Users/<user>/AppData/...`, so `openFile()` (utils/files.ts) and `waitForActiveDocument()` (utils/commands.ts) never saw their expected absolute path and timed out with an opaque `page.waitForFunction` TimeoutError -- even though the file had opened fine. A home-aliased `doc.path` now matches when the expected absolute path ends with the aliased path minus the `~`. This is still a full home-relative comparison, so two open files sharing a basename cannot be confused.

### desktop: don't steal OS focus in automation mode

The main window and splash already show inactive under `--automation-agent`, but several paths still pulled focus mid-run -- most notably `desktop_bring_main_frame_to_front`, which GWT fires on flows like opening a document. These now use `showInactive()` when automated: `raiseAndActivateWindow`, `desktop_bring_main_frame_to_front`, minimal-window `ready-to-show`, and the What's New window. Tests run without yanking focus from whatever the user is doing.

### scripts: materialize a desktop-dev shim build root in bootstrap-worktree.sh

Running the desktop-dev suite from a worktree needs `RSTUDIO_CPP_BUILD_OUTPUT` pointed at a build root whose `rdesktop-dev.conf` serves the worktree's GWT output. Pointing it at the main checkout's build directly is a footgun: that conf serves the main checkout's `src/gwt/www`, which after `ant desktop` / `ant devmode` is a Super Dev Mode stub redirecting to a code server on localhost:9876 -- without it running, RStudio dies at startup with "code server not available". The bootstrap script now creates `<worktree>/build-dev-shim` (session/ linked from the main checkout's build, conf rewritten to the worktree's www) and prints the exact command to run the suite against it.

### QA notes

- `tests/panes/editor/missing_packages_banner.test.ts` passes on Windows desktop-dev with the sandbox at its default `os.tmpdir()` location (previously timed out in `openFile`), running against the bootstrap-generated shim with the focus changes compiled in.
- `src/node/desktop`: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` clean; `npm test` shows no new failures vs. a main-checkout baseline (one pre-existing `FilePath.createDirectorySync` failure on this machine, plus one worktree-environment-only `findComponents` failure that needs a `build/` dir).
- No NEWS.md entry: developer/test tooling only.

title: reduce GitHub Actions cache pressure in e2e workflows
description:
## Summary

The repo's e2e Actions cache was pinned at the 10 GB quota (3,576 active cache entries), which was causing eviction of the caches PR builds most depend on (`rstudio-tools`, R-libs, GWT output). This trims two sources of pure waste:

- **Drop the RStudio installer caches** (`actions/cache@v4`, no branch gate). These steps don't build anything — when `build_from_source == false` they just re-download an already-published daily build from `dailies.rstudio.com` (itself S3/CDN-backed). Because GitHub's cache scoping doesn't let concurrent PRs share a cache entry with each other (only with their base branch), every PR that hit this path was independently downloading and caching its own duplicate multi-hundred-MB copy of identical bytes, with no real time savings over just downloading fresh.
- **Gate the "Save GWT output" step to main-scoped runs only**, matching the main-only-save pattern already used for the `rstudio-tools` and R-libs caches elsewhere in these same workflows. A cache saved from a PR run is only ever visible to that same PR (never to main or other PRs), so PR-side saves were pure one-way quota pressure on main's copy — the one every other PR actually depends on for a fast, warm GWT build.

## Test plan

- [x] All 7 edited workflow YAML files parse successfully (validated with PyYAML)
- [ ] Confirm a PR-triggered e2e run still downloads/installs the daily build correctly with caching removed
- [ ] Confirm a main-branch run still saves the GWT cache, and a subsequent PR run restores it (cache-hit skips recompilation)

title: detach doc tab handlers when a tab is removed from a source column
description:
## Problem

Closing a visual-mode document (e.g. a freshly created Quarto document -- these open in visual mode by default) while its markdown conversion is still in flight throws an uncaught `IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: -1, Size: 1` from `SourcePane.setDirty` / `DocTabLayoutPanel.getTabWidget`.

`SourceColumn.addTab` registers four handlers on each `EditingTarget` (rename, dirty-state, ensure-visible, close) whose lambdas capture the tab `Widget`; their `HandlerRegistration`s were discarded and never detached on tab close. When the visual editor's `withSwitchConfirmation` continuation calls `markDirty()` after the tab was closed (the new-document template is not in pandoc canonical form, so this runs on every fresh visual-mode open), the stale dirty-state handler calls `display_.setDirty()` with a widget no longer in the panel.

The impact goes beyond the exception: `VisualMode.setMarkdownQueue_` is a **static** `PreemptiveTaskQueue` shared by all editors, and its try/catch only covers synchronous exceptions. The throw escapes inside an async `setMarkdown` task before the task's `done` command runs, so the queue's `processing_` flag never clears -- the visual editor then hangs at its loading spinner for every document opened afterwards in the session. This is silent in released builds; #18137 only made the exception *reported*, which is why the `create_file_types` e2e tests started failing (flaky on desktop, consistently on server-linux).

## Fix

- `SourceColumn` now retains the four handler registrations per editing target and detaches them in `closeTabIndex`, which every removal path funnels through (close, move to another column, move to another window). A dismissed target can no longer drive the column's display with a stale widget; this also covers the equivalent latent crashes in the rename / ensure-visible / close handlers.
- `SourcePane.setDirty` additionally ignores a widget that is not in the panel, so this path can never again throw into the shared queue.

## Verification

Reproduced with the in-tree dev build on Windows by running the Quarto / R Markdown tests from `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/create_file_types.test.ts`: before the fix, `create Quarto presentation via newQuartoPres` failed on both of 2 repeats with the exact stack from the CI reports (`getTabWidget -> setDirty -> onValueChange -> markDirty -> withSwitchConfirmation`); after the fix, all 12 tests (4 tests x 3 repeats) pass.

A NEWS.md entry is included because the underlying bug -- the wedged visual editor and the lost dirty flag -- affects released builds; only its visibility as a reported exception is new.

Fixes #18145.

title: Describe environment-like S4 objects in the Object Explorer without class modification
description:
Opening an object containing environment-like S4 objects (e.g. reference class instances, or instances of classes defined with `contains = "environment"`) in the Object Explorer emitted warnings to the console:

```
Warning messages:
1: In class(object) <- "environment" :
  Setting class(x) to "environment" sets attribute to NULL; result will no longer be an S4 object
```

`.rs.explorer.objectDesc()` described environments by temporarily assigning `class(object) <- "environment"`, capturing the default print output, and restoring the previous class. This had two problems:

- For S4 objects wrapping environments, `typeof(x)` is `"S4"` rather than `"environment"`, so the assignment emits the warning above and then errors. The error was swallowed by a surrounding `tryCatch()`, but the warning escaped, and no description was produced.
- Environments have reference semantics, so the temporary class assignment mutated the class of the user's actual object rather than a copy.

This PR:

- describes environment-like S4 objects directly (`Reference class object of class Foo` for reference class instances, `S4 object of class Foo` otherwise), without touching the object's class;
- adds a small `.Call` helper, `rs_environmentDescription()`, that generates the default display for plain environments (`<environment: R_GlobalEnv>`, `<environment: namespace:stats>`, `<environment: 0x...>`, mirroring R's `PrintEnvironment()`), so no class modification, `print` dispatch, or output capture is needed at all.

Includes regression tests covering the S4 cases, the no-mutation guarantee for classed environments, and the descriptions generated for named environments.

Fixes #18143.

title: verify terminal Shift+Backspace via a filesystem side effect
description:
The `Shift+Backspace deletes the last character before submission` e2e test fails on Ubuntu 26.04 desktop runs (seen on the [PR #18141 e2e run](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/28694406226), where it failed on both the initial attempt and the retry). Ubuntu 26.04 is currently the only platform where it fails; older Ubuntu is fine.

### Diagnosis

The failure artifacts show the deletion actually works: the failing run's terminal buffer contains the output line `hell`, and in the retry the buffer even contains readline's redrawn command line `echo hell`. The shell received `echo hell` in both cases.

The test failed anyway because it asserted `grepl("echo hell", buf) && !grepl("echo hello", buf)` against `rstudioapi::terminalBuffer()`. After the deletion, readline may redraw the whole (wrapped) prompt line rather than erasing in place, and the server-side buffer capture keeps the stale pre-erase `echo hello` image, so the negative grep matches stale echo rather than what was executed.

Whether readline erases in place or redraws is a shell implementation detail. The Ubuntu 26.04-only failure pattern fits: 26.04 ships bash 5.3 / readline 8.3, which reworked the redisplay code, while older Ubuntu (bash 5.2) erased in place and kept the grep accurate. Prompt width (hostname and sandbox workdir lengths vary per runner) also feeds the redisplay decision, which is why the failure can look intermittent within a platform.

### Fix

Assert through a filesystem side effect instead: type `touch term_bs_test.txtQ`, delete the trailing `Q` with Shift+Backspace, submit, and check that `term_bs_test.txt` exists and `term_bs_test.txtQ` does not. This is independent of the shell's echo and redisplay behavior, and still fails if the keystroke has no effect (only the `Q` file exists) or deletes too much (neither file matches). The file lands in the suite sandbox and is cleaned up by globalTeardown.

title: fix dangling setlocale restore and log locale sync failures on windows
description:
Addresses #18139. Related: #15008.

While investigating #18139 (console corrupts UTF-8 input at startup on Windows 11 with the Turkish locale, until `Sys.setlocale()` is called), I found two Windows locale-state hazards on the RStudio side. Both matter because rsession (MSVC, `/MD`) and UCRT builds of R share a single `ucrtbase.dll` CRT instance, so an rsession-side `setlocale()` silently clobbers R's locale without R's internal state (`localeCP`, `utf8locale`, `native_enc`) being updated.

### 1. Dangling `setlocale()` pointer restore in `utf8ToConsole()`

`SessionRMarkdown.cpp` saved the pointer returned by `setlocale(LC_CTYPE, NULL)`, switched to the `"C"` locale for the conversion loop, then "restored" from the saved pointer. That pointer refers to an internal CRT buffer which a subsequent `setlocale()` call may overwrite, so the restore could permanently pin the session's `LC_CTYPE` to `"C"` after rendering an R Markdown document. The locale name is now copied into a `std::string` before switching, and a failed restore is logged.

### 2. `synchronizeLocale()` ignored `setlocale()` failure

`r::util::synchronizeLocale()` (runs on every R busy transition) round-trips the compound `Sys.getlocale("LC_ALL")` string back into `::setlocale(LC_ALL, ...)` and discarded the return value. Locale names containing non-ASCII characters (`Turkish_Türkiye.utf8` on Windows 11, `Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8` in #15008) are suspected to fail this round-trip, and a failed `LC_ALL` update can leave only some categories applied. Failures are now logged with the requested and resulting locale so affected sessions are diagnosable.

### Notes

- Both touched code paths are `#ifdef _WIN32`, so local macOS builds don't exercise them; relying on the Windows CI build for compile verification.
- This does not claim to fully resolve #18139 -- the startup-time corruption still needs a Windows repro (diagnostics requested from the reporter on the issue).

title: guard object explorer against non-scalar length() methods
description:
## Summary

`View()` on an `mlogit` model failed with:

```
Error in is.recursive(.$object) && !is.primitive(.$object) && n > 0 :
  'length = 2' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
```

The model's `formula` component has class `Formula`, and the Formula package's `length.Formula()` method returns a length-2 integer (part counts for the left- and right-hand sides). The Object Explorer's `.rs.explorer.createInspectionResult()` used that dispatched `length()` as a scalar element count inside an `&&` chain, which R >= 4.3 treats as a hard error. The code itself dates back to 2017; R 4.3's stricter `&&`/`||` semantics surfaced it.

This adds a `.rs.explorer.length()` helper that falls back to the internal (`unclass`ed) length when `length()` dispatch returns something non-scalar, and uses it wherever the explorer needs a scalar element count: the expandable check, the reported `length` field, child pagination in `inspectList`/`inspectDefault` (where `seq_along()` also honors the dispatched length), and the `more` computations in `objectDesc()` that feed `if`/`||`.

## Testing

- New testthat coverage in `test-object-explorer.R` registers a `length()` method returning a length-2 integer (mirroring `Formula`'s registration) and inspects both the object itself and a model-like list containing it; the test fails with the reported error without the fix.
- Verified `View()` error expression against the real `Formula`/`mlogit` packages reproduces before the fix.
- `rstudio-tests --scope r --filter object-explorer` and `--filter linter` pass.

Fixes #18138.

title: report exceptions thrown from native promise continuations
description:
## Summary

Speculative fix for the intermittent visual-editor activation hang: the editor shows the panmirror loading spinner forever, with no pending RPC, no rsession log output, and no recorded client exception.

### Analysis

Everything that runs between the `pandoc_get_capabilities` / `pandoc_list_extensions` RPCs completing and the initial `pandoc_markdown_to_ast` conversion is synchronous GWT code executed inside a native promise `.then()` continuation (`PromiseWithProgress` -> `PanmirrorWidget.attachEditor` -> the `VisualMode.withPanmirror` ready callback -> the `setMarkdown` queue task). GWT does not `$entry`-wrap native promise continuations, so an exception thrown anywhere in that chain becomes an **unhandled promise rejection**: it never reaches the uncaught-exception handler, so there is no error dialog, no server log entry, and no `window.rstudio.errors` record -- just a spinner that never goes away. That matches the observed failure signature exactly.

### Changes

- `PromiseWithProgress` catches exceptions thrown by its completion callbacks, logs them, and routes them through the uncaught-exception handler, so a failure during visual editor initialization (or any other `PromiseWithProgress` consumer, including `setMarkdown`) surfaces as a real reported error instead of a silent hang.
- The rejected path now uses `String.valueOf(error)` so a null/undefined rejection reason cannot itself throw inside the rejection handler (another way the error dialog and completion callback could be silently skipped).
- The automation agent records unhandled promise rejections into `window.rstudio.errors`, so the e2e fixture attributes and fails the responsible test with a message and stack. Since e2e builds already compile with `-style PRETTY`, the next CI occurrence of #18134 should produce a decoded stack pointing at the actual throw site instead of a 90s timeout.
- Added a harness self-test covering the rejection-capture path.

### Testing

- `ant javac` passes.
- `tests/harness/client_exceptions.test.ts` (including the new unhandled-rejection probe) passes against a dev desktop build.
- `tests/panes/editor/quarto.test.ts` (the spec that flakes in the issue) passes against the same build.

Addresses #18134.

title: isolate concurrent e2e runs on the desktop CDP port
description:
Addresses #18135.

Two changes to the desktop e2e fixture's CDP port handling:

- **Kill the listener only.** The per-launch cleanup (and the subsequent port-free wait) previously matched any process associated with the CDP port; `lsof -ti :PORT` also selects the *client* end of established connections, so a colliding run's cleanup would SIGKILL the other run's Playwright worker process (`worker process exited unexpectedly (code=null, signal=SIGKILL)` at 0ms), not just a leftover RStudio. Both the POSIX (`lsof ... -sTCP:LISTEN`) and Windows (`Get-NetTCPConnection ... -State Listen`) paths now match the listening socket only, which is all the cleanup ever intended to reclaim.
- **Per-checkout port bands.** The default port is now `9231 + (stable hash of the checkout path, folded into [0, 900)) + worker index`, so concurrent runs from different checkouts/worktrees land on disjoint CDP / dev-server (+1000) / logger (+2000) bands and never collide at all. `PW_CDP_PORT` still overrides for single-instance debugging.

Verification (macOS, installed RStudio):

- A two-process repro confirmed `lsof -ti :PORT` matches the connected client's PID while `lsof -ti TCP:PORT -sTCP:LISTEN` matches only the listener.
- `npm run test:desktop -- client_exceptions` run simultaneously from the main checkout and a worktree: the two runs derived disjoint ports (9231 vs 9909) and both passed; before this change this scenario reproducibly SIGKILLed one run's worker.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.

No NEWS entry: test-infrastructure-only change with no user-facing surface.

title: fix ggplot aesthetic completion for aesthetic-only tokens
description:
## Problem

Autocompletion inside a `geom_*()` call would fail to offer a ggplot2 aesthetic when the typed token matched only an aesthetic and not one of the function's formal arguments.

Reproduce with:

```r
library(ggplot2)
geom_line(line   # Tab -> linetype, linewidth, lineend, ... (correct)
geom_line(linet  # Tab -> "No match" (wrong; linetype expected)
```

## Root cause

In `SessionRCompletions.R`, the `geom_*()` aesthetic-completion path is gated on `fguess`. `fguess` is derived from `formals$methods[[1]]`, and `resolveFormals` filters `methods` down to only the formals that match the token.

`geom_line()` has real formal arguments `lineend` / `linejoin` / `linemitre`, so:

- Token `line` matches those formals -> `fguess = "geom_line"` -> aesthetics computed -> `linetype` / `linewidth` offered.
- Token `linet` matches no formal -> `fguess = ""` -> the aesthetics path is skipped entirely -> `linetype` (an aesthetic, not a formal) is never offered -> "No match".

## Fix

Key the aesthetic detection off the function name (`string`) rather than the token-filtered `fguess`, and evaluate the already-resolved `object` directly instead of looking the function up by name. As a bonus this also handles namespaced calls such as `ggplot2::geom_line(...)`, which the old `eval(as.symbol(fguess))` path silently failed on.

## Testing

Added E2E coverage in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/misc/autocomplete.test.ts` (runs in both console and editor contexts): `geom_line(linet` completes to `linetype`, and `geom_line(line` offers both the formal argument `lineend` and the aesthetics `linetype` / `linewidth`.

The `linet` case surfaced a test-infrastructure gap: an explicit completion request (Ctrl+Space) with exactly one result is auto-accepted by the completion managers without ever showing the popup, so popup-reading tests failed deterministically in the editor context. This PR therefore also adds an automation-only bridge knob, `window.rstudio.completions.setAlwaysShowPopup(force)`, which makes a unique match display in the popup instead of auto-accepting. The e2e popup helpers wrap their requests in the knob (feature-detected, no-op on older builds), and a dedicated editor test keeps the knob off to cover the real auto-accept behavior (`geom_line(linet` + Ctrl+Space inserts `linetype = ` directly). Product behavior outside the automation agent is unchanged.

Fixes #18125.

title: make citation source selection resilient to the dialog's one-time init reset
description:
## Summary

The citation e2e tests added in #18116 flaked on linux CI (both desktop and server projects, across several unrelated PRs, e.g. runs [28614679201](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/28614679201) and [28608398057](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/28608398057)).

The Insert Citation dialog's one-time init reset (when the bibliography load resolves, panmirror snaps the active panel back to My Sources exactly once, leaving the tree highlight in place) can fire *before* `selectSource()` / `selectPackageSource()` first sees the requested panel. The existing workaround only re-clicked after the panel had been seen once, so when the reset won that race the initial visibility wait just timed out:

- From DOI: failure screenshots show the "From DOI" node highlighted with the panel still on My Sources ("Paste a DOI to search" never appears).
- R Package: the panel remount wipes the filter text typed mid-reset, so the `@knitr` row never shows.

## Fixes

1. **Init-reset race**: treat click-and-verify as one retryable unit (`expect(...).toPass()`) so a reset landing before the first sighting replays the selection; keep the existing post-sighting revert watch. For the R Package typeahead, clear any leftover filter text with real key events before retyping on each attempt.

2. **External-service outages should skip, not fail**: seven of these tests exercise live third-party services (doi.org, Crossref, DataCite, PubMed) via the rsession's C++ request layer, which Playwright cannot intercept or mock. A new `utils/network.ts` probes each service from Node (cached per worker) and the tests `test.skip()` with a clear reason when the service is unreachable from the runner. Probing Node-side is deliberate: an egress/outage problem skips, while a regression in RStudio's own HTTP layer still fails.

Test-only change; no NEWS entry.

## Verification

All 11 citation tests pass locally on macOS desktop (installed build), including the two that failed on CI. Probe semantics verified directly: a dead host reports unreachable (would skip); all four live services report reachable.

title: publish e2e playwright reports to s3 instead of connect
description:
## What

Switches E2E Playwright report publishing from Posit Connect to a public S3 bucket, so the "View report online" link in PR comments actually works: click it and the report (including screenshots and the embedded trace viewer) opens in the browser with no download and no login.

## Why

The Connect publish path has silently failed on every run since it landed: the CI account behind `CONNECT_API_KEY` has viewer rights only, so `rsconnect deploy` was rejected with a permission error, and the best-effort step degraded to posting just the artifact-zip link. Rather than requesting a Connect role change, this moves to the same pattern Positron uses for its test reports: an S3 bucket in the shared build AWS account, written via GitHub OIDC (no stored keys).

A side benefit over the zip: reports served over HTTPS can run Playwright's embedded trace viewer, which `file://` from an extracted zip cannot (its service worker requires a secure origin), so traces become viewable in-browser for the first time.

## How

- `.github/actions/os-publish-e2e-report` now assumes the IAM role in `AWS_E2E_REPORTS_ROLE_ARN` via `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` and uploads the report with `aws s3 cp --recursive` to `s3://rstudio-playwright-reports/<pr-N|event>/<run_id>-<attempt>/<label>/`. Publishing remains best-effort end to end: a missing secret (fork PRs), missing report, failed credential exchange, or failed upload logs a warning and leaves the `url` output empty instead of failing the job. The link is also written to the run's step summary, which is how scheduled runs (no PR comment) surface it.
- The PR orchestrator, the four platform workflows, and their scheduled wrappers grant `id-token: write` and pass the new secret through. Cache-seed wrappers are left alone (`build_only` runs never publish; the action no-ops without the secret).
- The Connect cleanup cron (`os-cleanup-e2e-connect-reports.yml`) is deleted; the bucket's 14-day lifecycle rule replaces it.
- `CONNECT_API_KEY` stays: the E2E Test Insights reporter still uses it.

## Infrastructure (already provisioned)

In AWS account `749683154838`: bucket `rstudio-playwright-reports` (public `GetObject` only -- no public listing; 14-day expiry) and role `rstudio-e2e-reports-rw-github-action` (trusts GitHub OIDC for `repo:rstudio/rstudio:*`, can only `PutObject`/`ListBucket` on this bucket). The repo secret `AWS_E2E_REPORTS_ROLE_ARN` holds the role ARN.

Note: reports become fully public (anyone with the URL). That is a deliberate choice -- the content is open-source test output already downloadable as a zip by any logged-in GitHub user -- and is easy to tighten later (CloudFront/private bucket) without touching this workflow shape.

## Verification

- `actionlint` reports byte-identical findings on this branch and `main` (all pre-existing style notes in untouched scripts).
- This PR's own e2e run exercises the change end to end: the `paths` filter includes the publish action, and `pull_request` runs use the PR branch's workflows, so the sticky comment below should carry the first working "View report online" link.

title: use RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT for windows build dependencies
description:
Addresses #18129.

## Problem

Windows build dependencies installed into the source tree (`dependencies/common`, `dependencies/windows`), mixing multi-GB downloaded artifacts with the tracked install scripts. The Windows e2e workflow cached those directories wholesale, so when a PR changed an install script, the `restore-keys` prefix restored a stale cache from main whose extraction overwrote the PR's checked-out scripts (this is what broke the Boost 1.91 upgrade in #18128).

## Change

Windows now uses `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` the same way the posix platforms use `/opt/rstudio-tools`:

- `dependencies/tools/rstudio-tools.cmd` defaults `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` to `%SYSTEMDRIVE%\rstudio-tools` (normally `C:\rstudio-tools`) when unset, mirroring `rstudio-tools.sh`. An environment override is honored everywhere.
- `install-dependencies.cmd` still runs the tracked scripts from the source tree, but downloads/extracts everything into `%RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT%\dependencies\{common,windows}`. Setting `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` to a checkout root reproduces the legacy in-tree layout exactly.
- `install-soci.R` places its sqlite/SOCI build artifacts under the tools root when `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` is set; when unset (as in `os-build-dependencies-windows.yml`, which packages the in-tree outputs) it builds in-tree as before.
- `cmake/globals.cmake` resolves the Windows tools root first (env override, else system drive) and prefers `${RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT}/dependencies` when populated, **falling back to in-tree dependencies for older setups**. On Windows `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` now means the root (e.g. `C:/rstudio-tools`) rather than aliasing the dependencies dir; the only Windows consumers of the old alias were `CMakeNodeTools.txt` (whose `${RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT}/dependencies/common/node` probe now resolves correctly) and the panmirror `md-writer.lua` lookup in `src/cpp/session/CMakeLists.txt` (given an explicit `${RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT}/src/gwt/...` probe for the docker layout).
- `make-package.bat` and `src/gwt/build.xml` gain the same prefer-tools-root / fall-back-to-in-tree discovery.
- The Windows e2e workflow sets `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` to `${{ github.workspace }}\rstudio-tools` (no tracked files inside, matching the posix workflows), caches that path, and bumps the cache key prefix to `rstudio-tools-win64-v2-` so cache archives saved under the old in-tree layout can never restore over tracked scripts.

## Compatibility

- **Jenkins docker image**: unchanged behavior. `Dockerfile.windows` copies the dependency tree to `C:\rstudio-tools\dependencies` and runs the installer from there; with the default tools root the installer writes to the same location, and CMake/`make-package.bat` discover it the same way they discovered the hardcoded `C:\rstudio-tools\dependencies` before.
- **Existing developer setups** with in-tree artifacts keep building via the fallback discovery paths; re-running `install-dependencies.cmd` migrates to the tools root (documented in `dependencies/windows/README.md`).
- **`os-build-dependencies-windows.yml`** (Boost/SOCI prebuilt builder) is unaffected: it invokes `install-boost.cmd` / `install-soci.cmd` without `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` in the environment, so outputs stay in-tree where its packaging steps expect them.

## On C: vs SYSTEMDRIVE

The default uses `%SYSTEMDRIVE%\rstudio-tools` with a literal `C:\rstudio-tools` fallback only when `SYSTEMDRIVE` is somehow undefined. `SYSTEMDRIVE` is `C:` on GitHub-hosted runners, the Jenkins Windows containers, and virtually all developer machines, so this is equivalent to hardcoding `C:` in practice while remaining correct on nonstandard images. CI environments where the system drive is space-constrained should (and the e2e workflow does) set `RSTUDIO_TOOLS_ROOT` explicitly rather than rely on the default.

## Validation

- YAML/XML/R syntax checks pass locally; CMake if/endif structure verified.
- Windows e2e build workflow dispatched from this branch (build_only) to exercise the full install + build with the new layout.

title: upgrade boost to 1.91.0
description:
### Intent

Addresses #17986.

Upgrades Boost 1.90.0 -> 1.91.0. Boost 1.91 bundles b2 5.4, the first release that recognizes the Visual Studio 2026 toolset (`vc145` / `msvc-14.5`), which unblocks building the msvc145 prebuilts the VS 2026 pipeline needs -- Boost 1.90's bundled b2 rejects `vc145` outright (`Unknown toolset`).

### What changed

- **Version bump 1.90.0 -> 1.91.0** across the dependency scripts (`install-boost`, `install-soci`, Windows `install-*.cmd` / `install-*.R`), `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`, the Linux README, and the dependency-build workflow default.
- **Namespace-patch fix for Boost.Exception 1.91**: the new compile-time `__PRETTY_FUNCTION__` parser in `boost/exception/detail/type_info.hpp` matches string literals that hard-code `boost::n::`; after our `rstudio_boost` rename nothing matches and a static assert fails the build (clang: "array is too large"; MSVC: C2466/C2070). Both namespace-patch scripts now rewrite those literals too -- with a negative lookbehind so the rewrite is idempotent, since on Windows the patch runs once per build variant over the same tree (the non-idempotent first attempt produced `rstudio_rstudio_boost::n::` on the release pass). Both scripts now document the idempotency requirement.
- **`exec()` error reporting** (`dependencies/windows/tools.R`): when a caller passes `output = TRUE`, the captured output is a character vector; the failure path called `file.exists()` on it and crashed R (`'length = 49503' in coercion to 'logical(1)'`), masking the underlying build error. It now prints the captured output.
- **Windows e2e workflow**: requests `MSVC_TOOLSET_VERSION=145` now that toolset-matched prebuilts exist, so the windows-2025 build stops relying on the msvc143 binary-compatibility fallback in `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` (the fallback itself is kept as a safety net).

### Published artifacts

All uploaded to `rstudio-buildtools` and verified publicly fetchable:

- `Boost/boost_1_91_0.tar.bz2`, `Boost/boost_1_91_0.7z` (sources, SHA-256-verified against boost.org)
- `Boost/boost-1.91.0-win-msvc143.zip`, `Boost/boost-1.91.0-win-msvc145.zip` (from green runs of the dependency-build workflow: [msvc145](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/28611389722), [msvc143](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/28611391516))
- `soci-msvc143-4.0.3.zip`, `soci-msvc145-4.0.3.zip` (built against the new Boost; not yet consumed, published for future use)

### Verification

- macOS (arm64): Boost 1.91 built and installed via `install-boost`; full `src/cpp` build against it succeeds; `rstudio-tests --scope core` passes (421 tests).
- Windows: the dependency-build workflow is green for both toolsets (debug + release, 32/64-bit), which also exercises the double-patch idempotency path end-to-end; prebuilt lib names carry the expected `vc143`/`vc145` tags.
- This PR's own Windows e2e run exercises the msvc145 prebuilt download + link path.

No NEWS.md entry: internal build/dependency change.

title: Add RHEL 10 desktop e2e Playwright workflow
description:
Adds a standalone workflow that runs the RStudio Desktop e2e Playwright suite on RHEL 10, inside a UBI 10 container on a hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner (GitHub has no RHEL-hosted runner). Modeled on the Ubuntu 26 desktop workflow, with RHEL-specific adaptations:

- `dnf`/`yum` dependency install (`install-dependencies-yum`, best-effort EPEL/CRB enablement) and `.rpm` packaging (`make-electron-package RPM`).
- Full `build_from_source` parity: builds the Electron `.rpm` from source, or downloads the `rhel10-x86_64` daily from dailies.rstudio.com.
- RHEL-scoped build caches, plus a new `cache-scope` input on the shared `os-e2e-deps` action so the RHEL e2e R-library/pak caches don't collide with the Ubuntu workflows (all share `runner.os == Linux`, and compiled R packages are ABI-incompatible across distros). Existing callers are unchanged -- an empty scope reproduces the current key.
- Container runs with `--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN --security-opt seccomp=unconfined` so Chromium/Electron's sandbox can initialize; `--no-sandbox` is the documented fallback.

Standalone triggers (`workflow_dispatch` + `workflow_call`); not wired into the PR orchestrator (matching the Ubuntu 26 sibling). Cache-seed/scheduled warming are a deferred, additive follow-up.

Addresses rstudio/rstudio-ide-automation#5191.

title: automate building windows boost/soci prebuilts via github actions
description:
### Intent

Addresses #17986.

Boost (and SOCI) prebuilts for Windows are currently built manually on a developer's machine via `install-boost.cmd` / `install-soci.cmd` and hand-uploaded to the `rstudio-buildtools` S3 bucket. #17986 needs new `msvc145` prebuilts published for the VS 2026 toolset so the CI fallback-to-`msvc143` stopgaps from #17850 can eventually be dropped. This PR automates that build-and-publish step.

### What changed

- **New `workflow_dispatch` workflow** (`.github/workflows/os-build-dependencies-windows.yml`):
  - Inputs: Boost version, SOCI version, MSVC toolset version (default `145`), CMake generator (default `Visual Studio 18 2026`), runner image (`windows-2025` = VS 2026, `windows-2022` = VS 2022), and an `upload` toggle.
  - Builds Boost (debug + release, 32/64-bit static) via `install-boost.cmd`, then builds SOCI against those prebuilts via `install-soci.cmd`, and packages both as zips.
  - Always publishes the archives as workflow artifacts; when `upload` is enabled, pushes them to `s3://rstudio-buildtools` under the same keys `install-dependencies.cmd` downloads from (`Boost/boost-<ver>-win-msvc<toolset>.zip`, `soci-msvc<toolset>-<ver>.zip`).
  - Reuses the vswhere-junction pattern from the Windows e2e workflow so `tools.R`'s hardcoded VS 2022 path check passes on runner images with VS Enterprise / VS 2026.
- **`install-boost.cmd` / `install-dependencies.cmd`**: `BOOST_VERSION` / `MSVC_TOOLSET_VERSION` now honor values preset in the environment (defaults unchanged: `1.90.0` / `143`), so CI can request a different toolset without editing the scripts. Jenkins and local dev flows are unaffected.
- **`install-boost.R`**: the b2 toolset default is now derived from `MSVC_TOOLSET_VERSION` (`143` => `msvc-14.3`, `145` => `msvc-14.5`) instead of being hardcoded to `msvc-14.3`; `BOOST_TOOLSET` still overrides.
- **`install-boost.cmd` / `install-soci.cmd`**: propagate failures via `exit /b 1` instead of always exiting 0 (previously a failed build could be silently packaged/ignored, which would let a broken automated run "succeed").

### S3 upload credentials

The S3 upload step authenticates via GitHub OIDC and expects an `AWS_BUILDTOOLS_UPLOAD_ROLE_ARN` repository secret pointing at a role with write access to `rstudio-buildtools`. No such secret exists yet -- that's tracked in #18124. Until it's configured, run the workflow with `upload: false` and push the artifacts with the new `dependencies/tools/upload-windows-dependencies.sh`, which downloads a run's artifacts via `gh run download` and uploads them with developer SSO credentials (same flow as the other `upload-*.sh` scripts).

### QA Notes

This can only be exercised end-to-end by dispatching the workflow after merge (workflow_dispatch requires the workflow to exist on the default branch). Suggested first run: defaults (`msvc145` on `windows-2025`), `upload: false`, then inspect the artifacts. Note the first run also validates that Boost 1.90's bundled b2 accepts the `msvc-14.5` toolset / `vc145` bootstrap argument on VS 2026 -- if b2 predates VS 2026 support, the `boost_toolset` derivation may need adjusting.

Not adding a NEWS.md entry per the developer-only/build-tooling exception.

### Checklist

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [ ] This PR passes all local unit tests

split page-lifecycle tracing off PW_DEBUG_LAUNCH onto PW_DEBUG_PAGES
description:
Silences the `[debug-launch]` page-lifecycle chatter in CI logs:

```
[debug-launch] +818837ms p2: page created, url=http://127.0.0.1:21577/graphics/plot_zoom?...
[debug-launch] +818885ms p2: domcontentloaded (url=...)
[debug-launch] +818896ms p2: load (url=...)
[debug-launch] +819156ms p2: closed
```

`PW_DEBUG_LAUNCH=1` (set in all four desktop e2e workflows) gated two different diagnostics:

1. the `[launch-timing]` phase timeline (post-CDP wait steps), which the workflows enable on purpose so a launch failure shows which phase exceeded its deadline; and
2. `attachLaunchDebug`'s per-page lifecycle listeners, which attach to every context for the whole run and therefore trace every popup and secondary window (plot zoom, etc.) hundreds of seconds after launch.

This moves (2) to its own opt-in `PW_DEBUG_PAGES` flag, which nothing sets, so CI keeps the launch timeline and loses the page-trace noise. The README env-var table is split accordingly. No workflow changes needed.

Companion cleanup to #18118 / #18119.

Verified with `npm run typecheck` in `e2e/rstudio`.

title: remove per-package install logging from ensurePackage
description:

Installing R package: meditations...
Package meditations is now available.
Installing R package: titanic...
Package titanic is now available.

title: remove per-suite sandbox timeline logging from e2e tests
description:
Removes the `[sandbox]` per-suite timeline logs from the Playwright test output:

```
[sandbox] useSuiteSandbox beforeAll start (panes\environment\import_dataset.test.ts > ...)
[sandbox] createSandbox: workdir D:/a/rstudio/rstudio/pw-sandbox/pw_sandbox_du07zi/workdir_...
[sandbox] useSuiteSandbox beforeAll done: dir=...
```

The genuinely diagnostic `[sandbox]` messages are untouched: the `sandbox.dir` read-while-empty warning (with stack), the workdir-not-under-PW_SANDBOX warning, and the once-per-run seeding/teardown/preserve logs.

Verified with `npm run typecheck` in `e2e/rstudio`.

title: stop e2e cache saves from PR refs and add an eviction sentinel
description:
## Problem

The repo is pinned at the 10 GB Actions cache quota (9.4 GB / 5,300 entries at time of writing), so GitHub's LRU eviction regularly drops main's seeded build caches. Today the `rstudio-tools-linux-x86_64-*` and `rstudio-build-rlibs-linux-*` caches were gone from main's scope even though the Ubuntu 24 seed workflows had run successfully the same morning -- so every Linux PR build went cold (full dependency download) until the next nightly seed.

Worse, each cold PR run then saved its rebuilt caches into its own `refs/pull/N/merge` scope, which no other branch can restore. The split `actions/cache/save` steps (Windows tools, all GWT outputs) even re-saved on exact restore hits, duplicating a ~70-500 MB entry into every PR's scope on every run. Those per-PR copies are pure quota pressure, which evicts more of main's entries -- a vicious cycle.

## Changes

**Stop cache saves from PR refs.** The `rstudio-tools` / build-time R-libs caches in all five e2e build workflows (Ubuntu 24 Desktop/Server, Ubuntu 26, macOS, Windows), and the pak / R-library / Playwright-browser caches in the `os-e2e-deps` composite action, are now restore-only with explicit save steps gated to `refs/heads/main` (the seed and scheduled workflows). GWT saves keep running from PRs that changed GWT sources -- so re-pushes to the same PR still skip the ~15-30 min recompile -- but no save re-saves an exact restore hit anymore.

**Add `os-cache-seed-sentinel.yml`.** Every 2 hours it checks that each seed workflow's cache-key prefixes still resolve on `refs/heads/main` (the caches API matches keys by prefix) and dispatches the owning seed when one has been evicted, so an eviction hole lasts at most ~2 hours instead of until the next nightly seed. It skips dispatching when that seed already has a queued/running run, since the seeds' concurrency groups would otherwise cancel-loop.

A sentinel was chosen over dispatch-on-miss from PR builds because the reusable e2e workflows would all need `actions: write` plumbed through every caller, and fork PRs (read-only token) couldn't dispatch anyway.

## Notes

- Trade-off: a PR that rotates a dependency cache key (edits `dependencies/`) now rebuilds tools on every push to that PR rather than reusing a PR-scoped copy. Dependency bumps are rare, and the seed re-warms main with the new key right after merge (push-path trigger on `dependencies/**`).
- Ubuntu 26 AMD64 gets the same save gating but has no seed workflow yet (it is not in the PR orchestrator), so the sentinel deliberately does not cover it.
- The sccache GHA backend remains the biggest source of entry churn (one Actions cache entry per object file); this PR doesn't change that, the sentinel compensates for the eviction pressure it creates.

## Verification

- All changed workflow files parse as valid YAML.
- The sentinel's shell script was dry-run with a stubbed `gh` (correctly detects an evicted prefix, dispatches only the owning seed, honors the queued/running guard) and its cache-prefix and workflow-runs API queries were verified against the live repo.

title: merge e2e playwright reports across platforms into one report
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to #18112. On PR-triggered e2e runs, this replaces the four separate
per-platform Playwright reports/comments with a **single unified report** that
covers every platform (Windows Desktop, macOS Desktop, Linux Desktop, Linux
Server), and publishes that one report to Posit Connect so reviewers can browse
it online.

## What this does

- **Per-platform project labels**: each platform records its results under a
  distinct Playwright project name (`desktop-macos`, `desktop-windows`,
  `desktop-linux`, `server-linux`) via a new `PW_PROJECT_LABEL` env, so the
  merged report can tell which OS a result came from instead of collapsing every
  desktop platform under one indistinguishable `desktop` group.
  `playwright.config.ts` defaults the label to the mode, so local
  `--project=desktop|server` is unchanged.
- **Collision-safe blob names**: shards write `report-<platform>-<shard>.zip`
  (via `PLAYWRIGHT_BLOB_OUTPUT_NAME`) instead of the default `report-<shard>.zip`,
  which would otherwise clash across platforms when flattened into one directory
  (Playwright's `merge-reports` scans only the top level of the given dir).
- **`defer_merge` input**: each reusable platform workflow gains a `defer_merge`
  input (default `false`). The PR orchestrator sets it `true`, suppressing each
  platform's own merge/publish/comment job.
- **New `e2e-merge-all` job** in `os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml`: downloads every
  platform's blob artifacts (shared across the run), merges them into one HTML
  report, **always** publishes it to Connect via the `os-publish-e2e-report`
  action, and posts a single sticky PR comment with an overall pass-rate plus a
  per-platform breakdown table. A small committed Node script
  (`e2e/rstudio/scripts/summarize-merged-report.mjs`) parses the merged JSON.

Scheduled/standalone platform runs are unchanged -- they don't set `defer_merge`,
so each still produces its own report (they can't cross-merge anyway, being
separate runs).

## Needs live validation

Like #18112, the cross-workflow artifact sharing and the Connect publish path
can only be fully exercised by a real CI run. A run should confirm that the
`e2e-merge-all` job can read blobs uploaded by the reusable platform workflows,
and that the single comment/report render as intended.

Developer/CI tooling change -- no user-facing NEWS entry.

## Review follow-up (second commit)

- **Graceful stop in the watchdog**: `run-with-heartbeat.mjs` now forwards
  SIGINT (Playwright's cancellation signal) and escalates to SIGKILL after a
  grace window (`PW_STOP_GRACE_MS`, default 30s), mirroring `dev-common.ts`,
  instead of SIGKILLing the process tree -- so a cancelled or hung shard can
  still flush its blob report and run teardown.
- **`e2e-merge-all` guards**: the job now skips when the run is cancelled or
  every platform job was skipped (nothing to merge), and the unified comment is
  posted with a warning header when the merge itself fails, instead of being
  silently suppressed by all-zero counts.
- **Blob names derived in config**: `playwright.config.ts` computes the
  platform+shard-unique blob file name from `PW_PROJECT_LABEL` + `PW_SHARD`;
  the `PLAYWRIGHT_BLOB_OUTPUT_NAME` env and the redundant `--project` label
  args are gone (which also restores the loud unknown-mode validation for
  `--project` typos).
- **One summarizer + one merge config**: all merge jobs (per-platform and
  unified) now call `scripts/summarize-merged-report.mjs` and use a committed
  `e2e/rstudio/merge.config.ts`, replacing the inline jq blocks and the
  per-workflow heredocs.

**Heads-up, E2E Test Insights dashboard**: the per-platform project labels also
flow into the dashboard's `project` field (the reporter records the live
Playwright project name), so results now arrive as `desktop-macos`,
`desktop-windows`, `desktop-linux`, and `server-linux` instead of a single
`desktop`/`server`. Dashboard views keyed on the old names will need updating.

title: Fix Ubuntu 26 (Resolute) Desktop E2E dependencies and package sources
description: The Ubuntu 26 ("Resolute") Desktop E2E Playwright CI workflow failed at the build-dependency step: the `fs` R package could not compile from source because the `uv.h` header was missing. `libuv1-dev` provides that header. The sibling `install-dependencies-noble` (Ubuntu 24) already installs the `libuv1-dev` binary—this brings the Resolute script to package parity with Noble.

title: Migrate citation tests from Selenium to Playwright
description:
Migrates `test_desktop_Citations.py` from the Selenium/Selene suite to a Playwright/TypeScript spec at `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/citations.test.ts`, backed by a new `InsertCitationDialog` page object and a `visual-editor.md` skill doc describing the panmirror Insert Citation dialog.

title: publish e2e playwright reports to connect on failure
description:
## Summary

When a Playwright e2e run fails, we currently only archive the merged HTML report as a downloadable artifact (the PR comment links a `.zip` you extract and open locally). This adds an option to also **publish the report to Posit Connect as static content on failure**, so reviewers can open it directly in a browser -- screenshots, traces, and step details -- without downloading anything.

## What this does

- **New composite action `.github/actions/os-publish-e2e-report`**: installs `rsconnect-python`, runs `rsconnect deploy html` on the merged report, sets the new content's `access_type` to `logged_in` (viewing requires a Connect login), and outputs the browsable URL. Fully best-effort: an empty API key (fork PRs), a missing report, a deploy failure, or an unresolved content GUID all log a warning and leave the URL empty -- they never fail the job. This mirrors how the existing Test Insights reporter behaves.
- **All four e2e merge jobs** (Linux Desktop, macOS, Windows, Linux Server) gain a `Publish report to Connect` step gated on `failed != 0` (publishes on failure only), and their sticky PR comment now renders a `View report online` link **only when a URL is available**.
- **New scheduled workflow `os-cleanup-e2e-connect-reports.yml`**: Connect has no per-content TTL, so a daily cron deletes E2E report content older than 7 days (configurable; supports a `dry_run`). It matches only content titled `E2E ...` so it never touches unrelated Connect content.
- Renamed the existing `e2e-deps` composite action to `os-e2e-deps` so both local actions carry the `os-` prefix (avoids collisions with upstream actions); updated all references.

## Access model

Reports are published with `access_type: logged_in`, so the links require authenticating to Connect. Fork PRs run with an empty `CONNECT_API_KEY` today, so they publish nothing and simply get no online link (unchanged behavior) -- the download zip is still there for them.

## Needs live validation

This is a prototype that can't be fully exercised without a real CI run + Connect credentials. Before relying on it, please confirm:

1. **`CONNECT_API_KEY` has publish rights on `connect.posit.it`.** Today that secret is only used to POST to the Test Insights API app; if it's scoped narrowly, `rsconnect deploy` will fail and the step will no-op with a warning.
2. **Content GUID extraction** (read from rsconnect's deployment record, with a log-scrape fallback) against the deployed `rsconnect-python` version.
3. **The `access_type` PATCH endpoint** shape (`PATCH /__api__/v1/content/{guid}`) against the Connect version.

The Connect server URL is currently hardcoded to `https://connect.posit.it` (matching the Test Insights reporter's baked-in host); happy to promote it to a repo variable if preferred.

Developer/CI tooling change -- no user-facing NEWS entry.

title: seed .here in sandbox home to prevent reticulate here::here() failure
description:
## Summary

reticulate's pipenv interpreter probe calls an unguarded `here::here()` (rstudio/reticulate#1909). Run from the rootless Playwright sandbox HOME -- which has no project markers (`.Rproj`/`.git`/`renv.lock`/...) -- `here()` throws "No root directory found". That surfaced as a spurious "Error Listing Packages" modal on session resume, whose `gwt-PopupPanelGlass` overlay then wedged unrelated e2e tests with an opaque pointer-intercept timeout.

## Changes

- **`fixtures/sandbox-setup.ts`**: seed an empty `.here` marker into the sandbox `user-home`. `.here` is the first marker `here`/`rprojroot` looks for, so `here()` resolves to HOME instead of erroring. Only affects code that actually calls `here()`/`rprojroot`; RStudio's own project detection ignores it.
- **`pages/modals.page.ts`**: add `dismissBlockingModals()` helper that clears any out-of-band modal (checked via the automation bridge's `numShowing()`) and logs what it dismissed.
- **`tests/panes/misc/session_suspend.test.ts`**: call `dismissBlockingModals()` after suspend/resume as a cheap safety net for any other stray dialog.

This is test-infrastructure only.

title: fix Cmd+Alt+F collision between Find in Console and Run Current Function Definition
description:
Addresses #18089.

### Problem

On macOS, `Cmd+Alt+F` ("Run Current Function Definition") stopped working and instead triggered "Find in Console".

`Cmd` in a shortcut value expands to both `Ctrl` and `Meta` bindings, so `executeCurrentFunction`'s `Cmd+Alt+F` produces a `Meta+Alt+F` binding. PR #16478 added a standalone `<shortcut refid="consoleFind" value="Meta+Alt+F"/>` that collides with it. When two commands share a key sequence the last-declared binding wins globally (`KeyMap.addBinding` prepends; `getActiveBinding` returns the first enabled), so `consoleFind` hijacked the shortcut even when a source editor had focus.

### Fix

Removed the redundant `consoleFind` `Meta+Alt+F` binding. That same PR already made Find in Console focus-scoped: pressing the Find shortcut (`Cmd+F` / `Ctrl+F`) while the console has focus redirects to `consoleFind` in `ShortcutManager`, and the console toolbar exposes a Find button. So Find in Console remains reachable, and `Cmd+Alt+F` is restored to Run Current Function Definition everywhere.

### Notes

- Updated `Commands.cmd.xml.MD5` to match.
- Added a NEWS.md entry (the regression shipped in released versions).
- No automated test: this is a shortcut-configuration removal that is awkward to exercise via the e2e harness (which drives commands through the automation bridge rather than raw key events). Verified by inspection of the shortcut expansion/resolution path.

title: disable native spellcheck in new document dialog fields
description:
### Intent

The Title/Author/Date fields in the **New R Markdown**, **New Quarto Document**, and **Compile Notebook** dialogs showed the browser's native spell-checking squiggles even when "Use real time spell checking" was disabled in Tools > Global Options > Spelling.

Those fields are plain HTML `<input>` elements, so the browser applies its own spell checker. The `real_time_spellchecking` preference only governs RStudio's editor/visual-mode spelling engine and was never wired to these dialog inputs.

### Approach

Set `spellcheck="false"` on the affected fields, matching the existing treatment of other dialog inputs (citation dialog, Zotero API key, command palette).

### QA Notes

Open File > New File > Quarto Document (and likewise New R Markdown, and Compile Notebook), then type misspelled text into the Title/Author fields. No red squiggles should appear.

Addresses #17796.

title: fix visual editor content width reset with multiple docs open
description:
### Summary

Addresses #14040.

With two or more R Markdown / Quarto documents open in visual mode, the "Editor content width" would reset to the default (full) width whenever the user interacted with one of them (right-clicking a misspelled word, opening a toolbar menu, switching tabs, resizing a pane, etc.).

### Root cause

The visual editor applies the content-width padding through a single, document-global `<style id="pm-editor-padding-styles-id">` element whose rule targets the `.pm-editing-root-node` class -- a class present on the body node of *every* open visual editor. The element is shared, so the last writer wins across all editor instances.

`Editor.syncContentWidth()` computes the padding from `view.dom.clientWidth`. A hidden source tab has a measured width of 0, so the `parentWidth > maxContentWidth + 2*minPadding` test fails and it writes the *minimum* padding into the shared style, clobbering the visible editor's centered width. Layout/resize events fan out to hidden editors, which is why so many interactions trigger it. (Switching to the good tab and back, or toggling the outline, re-runs the sync while the editor has real width and restores it -- matching the comments on the issue.)

### Fix

The offending JS (`editor.resize()` / `setMaxContentWidth()`) is only ever invoked from the GWT side (`PanmirrorWidget`); there is no internal `ResizeObserver`/window listener in the editor. So GWT fully controls when the shared style is written.

This change guards `syncContentWidth()` and `resizeEditor()` in `PanmirrorWidget` so they no-op when the editor isn't actually visible (`getOffsetWidth() == 0`). Computing content-width padding at width 0 is always wrong, and since only the visible visual-editor tab has a nonzero width, the shared style now always reflects that one editor. `resizeEditor()` also re-asserts the content width on becoming visible, so a tab that was hidden during a content-width preference change picks up the current value when it is shown again.

This keeps the fix entirely within the RStudio (GWT) codebase; the visual editor source lives in a separate `quarto-dev/quarto` repository, so no upstream change is required.

### Verification

`ant javac` passes. Manual verification still needed: open two R Markdown documents in visual mode, set a content width, and confirm interactions (right-click, toolbar menus, tab switches, pane resize) no longer reset the width on either document.

title: flush completion cache when deleting a namespace colon
description:
## Summary

Fixes autocomplete not updating when deleting a colon to go from `pkg:::` to `pkg::`. The popup kept showing all objects (exported and unexported) instead of narrowing to only the exported ones.

## Root cause

The completion cache (`CompletionRequester`) is keyed on the token text *after* the `::`/`:::`, which is the empty string for both `pkg::` and `pkg:::`. The cache therefore cannot distinguish the `TYPE_NAMESPACE_ALL` (`:::`) context from `TYPE_NAMESPACE_EXPORTED` (`::`).

`RCompletionManager`'s backspace handler called `beginSuggest(false, ...)` (no cache flush), so deleting the trailing colon reused the stale all-objects result. The forward path (typing `:`) already works because `previewKeyPress` calls `invalidatePendingRequests()`, which flushes the cache.

## Fix

In the backspace handler, flush the completion cache when the deleted character is a colon, so the namespace context is re-evaluated server-side. This mirrors the existing forward-typing behavior.

## Testing

Added a Playwright regression test (`tools:::` -> Backspace -> `tools::` must narrow the completion list). Verified the test fails without the fix and passes with it, against a dev desktop build.

Fixes #17831.

title: surface main window when launching jobs from a detached source window
description:
### Summary

"Run Selection as Background Job" (and the related Source/Launcher job commands) appear to do nothing when invoked from a detached (popped-out) source window on Windows Desktop.

### Root cause

These commands are `windowMode="any"`, so their handlers run in the source window and fire a `CrossWindowEvent` (`JobRunSelectionEvent`, `JobRunScriptEvent`, and the `LauncherJob*` variants). The event is forwarded to the main window, whose `JobManager` shows a modal `JobLauncherDialog`. The events used the default `focusMode()` of `MODE_BACKGROUND`, so `EventBus` never brought the main window forward. On Windows Desktop the modal therefore rendered behind the detached source window, so the command looked like it silently did nothing. On macOS/Linux Desktop the OS/Electron surfaced the window anyway, which is why it worked there.

### Fix

Override `focusMode()` to return `MODE_FOCUS` on the four job-launch events, mirroring the existing `SendToConsoleEvent` precedent (commit 28a5788e7a, which did the same for the show-help / send-to-console commands). This brings the main window to the front before the dialog appears, giving Windows the same behavior macOS/Linux already have.

`MODE_AUXILIARY` was considered but rejected: it re-focuses the source window afterward, which would leave a *modal* dialog hidden behind it.

Because the fix lives on the event's `focusMode()`, it only affects the satellite-forwarding path; events fired from the main window are not forwarded and never consult `focusMode()`, so there is no behavior change in the common case.

### Testing

Manual verification required on Windows Desktop (cannot be reproduced on macOS). `cd src/gwt && ant javac` passes.

Addresses #18101.

title: strip --| cell-option lines from sql chunks before execution
description:
## Problem

Running a `{sql}` chunk interactively with the Quarto/knitr cell-option comment syntax fails on MySQL/MariaDB:

`````qmd
```{sql}
--| connection: con
SELECT 1;
```
`````

RStudio sent the option line `--| connection: con` to the database as part of the statement. MySQL/MariaDB require whitespace after `--` for a line comment, so they parse `--|` as SQL and error (1064). SQLite/Postgres tolerate `--|`, which is why the bug was invisible there.

## Root cause

Interactive SQL chunk execution parses the chunk in two independent steps in `SessionRmdNotebook.R`:

- `.rs.evaluateChunkOptions()` extracts the options and already picks the comment prefix per engine (`--` for sql, `//` for C-like, `#` otherwise), so the `connection` option parsed correctly.
- `.rs.extractChunkInnerCode()` extracts the body sent to the DB, but stripped option lines with a hardcoded `#|` pattern only. A `--|` (or `//|`) option line therefore survived into the query.

## Fix

Strip all comment prefixes that `.rs.evaluateChunkOptions()` recognizes:

```r
code <- gsub("(#|--|//)[|].*$", "", code)   # was: "#[|].*$"
```

This function is only used for alternate-engine chunks (sql, stan, Rcpp, js, bash, ...). Verified that `--|`/`//|` option lines are stripped while plain `-- comment` lines and the SQL concat operator `a || b` are left untouched.

## Testing

- Added a `--|` (SQL) test case to `test-notebook.R` alongside the existing `#|` (#11606) case.

Fixes #18093.

title: report source directory in .rs.trust.status result
description:
## Summary

`.rs.trust.status()` reports whether a directory is `"trusted"`, `"untrusted"`, or `"default"`, walking up the directory tree so that a directory can inherit its status from an ancestor. Previously the result gave no indication of *which* directory was responsible for the decision.

This change attaches a `source` attribute to `"trusted"` and `"untrusted"` results, identifying the directory that determined the status. When a directory inherits its status from an ancestor, `source` is that ancestor; when the directory itself is in a trust list, `source` is the directory itself. `"default"` results carry no `source` attribute.

```r
status <- .rs.trust.status("/path/to/project/subdir")
status                  # "trusted"
attr(status, "source")  # "/path/to/project"  (the trusted ancestor)
```

## Implementation

- `resolveTrustStatus()` gains an optional `std::string* pSource` out-param, populated with the matching ancestor's absolute path.
- `rs_trustStatus()` sets that path as a `source` attribute on the returned character vector.

Internal callers (`projectTrustStatus()`, `initializeTrustState()`) pass `nullptr` and are unaffected.

title: make C++ worktree builds practical (ccache BASEDIR + bootstrap --with-build-dir)
description:
## Summary

Developer-tooling changes that make C++ builds in a git worktree practical, so a worktree's first build doesn't recompile the whole tree from scratch.

## 1. Share ccache across checkouts/worktrees (`cmake/globals.cmake`)

The dev-build compiler-cache block already aimed to let git-worktree builds reuse cached objects, but in practice the cross-checkout hit rate is near zero: ccache hashes absolute source/include paths, which differ between checkouts, so nothing is reused across worktrees.

This threads two env vars through `env` in the compiler-launcher list (ccache-only, non-Windows):

- `CCACHE_BASEDIR` rewrites absolute paths under the source tree to build-dir-relative paths before hashing.
- `CCACHE_NOHASHDIR` stops ccache from folding the build dir into the hash.

With both set, the same source compiled from two different checkout roots produces the same hash, so a fresh worktree's first build reuses objects another checkout already compiled.

**Trade-off:** a cross-checkout cache hit reuses the object that first populated the cache, so embedded debug / `__FILE__` paths may point at the checkout that built it. Acceptable for development builds.

## 2. `bootstrap-worktree.sh --with-build-dir` (`scripts/bootstrap-worktree.sh`)

Adds an opt-in `--with-build-dir[=<dir>]` flag (default `<worktree>/build`; absolute or worktree-relative) that runs a **fresh** `cmake -S <worktree> -B <dir>` configure.

It deliberately configures fresh rather than copying the main checkout's `build/`: a CMake build tree bakes absolute paths into its cache, ninja depfiles, generated dev confs (`www-local-path`), and the compiled objects themselves, so a copied tree would build and serve the wrong checkout. Paired with the `CCACHE_BASEDIR` change above, the subsequent compile reuses cached objects, so a fresh configure stays cheap.

## Testing

- Verified the launcher is wired correctly in `CMakeCache.txt` and that CMake/Ninja compiles cleanly through the `env`-wrapped launcher.
- Confirmed the mechanism empirically: the same source compiled from two different checkout roots is a ccache **hit** with the change and a **miss** without it.
- `bash -n` on the bootstrap script passes; verified `--with-build-dir` resolves the path and configures correctly.

Developer-only tooling change; no associated issue or NEWS entry.

title: collapse duplicated browser-active cache in SessionEnvironment
description:
## Intent

Fixes #17492. Removes the file-local `s_browserActive` cache in `SessionEnvironment.cpp`, which duplicated the authoritative copy in `RSession.cpp` and was a latent desync class.

## Summary

`RSession.cpp` owns the authoritative browser state -- it is set/cleared synchronously from `RReadConsole` based on the prompt, and `r::session::isBrowseActive()` reads it directly. `SessionEnvironment.cpp` kept a derived `s_browserActive` that was only ever refreshed by assigning `r::session::isBrowseActive()` right before each use, so it could only ever go stale relative to the source of truth.

This removes that cache entirely and has every reader consult `r::session::isBrowseActive()` directly:

- `s_browserActive` declaration deleted.
- `rs_isBrowserActive()` returns `r::session::isBrowseActive()`.
- `setContextDepth`, `onConsolePrompt`, and `onBeforeExecute` consult `r::session::isBrowseActive()` instead of the cache. In `onConsolePrompt` the value is read once into a function-local `browserActive` and reused within the call (it cannot change mid-handler), which is a convenience local, not a persisted cache.

`isBrowseActive()` is a side-effect-free read of two statics, so reading it on demand is no more expensive than the old assign-then-read pattern.

## Testing

No behavior change: the cache was always assigned `isBrowseActive()` immediately before use, so a direct read is identical. The existing Playwright test `multi-line input at Browse[N]> preserves browser state` (debugger_extras.test.ts) already exercises the changed `rs_isBrowserActive()` path -- it submits a multi-line block at the `Browse[N]>` prompt, steps through a nested debug invocation, and asserts `.rs.isBrowserActive()` returns `TRUE` mid-block. That is the stepping-through-multi-line-paste case called out in the issue's acceptance criteria.

Note: the issue's acceptance mentions "BRAT tests" -- BRAT has since been migrated to Playwright (#17713), so the relevant coverage now lives under `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/debugger/`.

title: fix reformat-on-save for files outside the active project
description:
### Intent

Fixes #17774.

Reformat-on-save stopped working for R scripts opened outside of an RStudio project (or with no project open) in 2026.04/2026.05, even though the **Reformat Document** command still worked. The reporter's workflow -- edit a script, save, see it unchanged, then run Reformat Document and watch it format -- is the exact signature of this.

### Cause

The format-on-save path, `TextEditingTarget.maybeFormatOnUserInitiatedSave`, had a guard the Reformat Document command does not: it only formatted files **inside the active project**, and skipped formatting entirely when no project was open. That guard was added in #16747 ("only format files in current project"), which landed after the 2026.01 release branch -- which is why it worked in 2026.01 and regressed in 2026.04+.

The earlier Air fixes in this release (#17202 formatter selection, #18007 external-formatter air.toml discovery) did not touch this guard, so files outside a project stayed broken.

### Approach

Remove the project-membership guard. Format-on-save now mirrors Reformat Document: both rely on `withFormatContext()` to resolve the formatter (and any air.toml) for the document, which already handles non-project files via the `format_context` RPC fallback.

### Automated Tests

Added `air_formatting` case 14: with Air enabled and reformat-on-save on, a file written **outside** the active project is reformatted by Air on save. Updated the suite's now-stale `beforeAll` comment (which previously documented the removed guard) and the test-matrix header.

### QA Notes

- Open an R script that is **not** part of any RStudio project (no project open).
- Configure Air for format-on-save (built-in "Use Air", or external `air format`), with "Reformat documents on save" enabled.
- Make a change and save; the document should now be reformatted. Previously it was left unchanged while Reformat Document still worked.

### Documentation

N/A

title: detect package-library mutations by resolving call namespaces
description:
### Summary

The Packages pane refresh was triggered whenever console input merely *contained* a keyword like `remove` or `update`. The detection was a substring/keyword regex, so it fired on comments, strings, and identifiers such as `str_remove_all()`, as well as base R's `remove()` (object removal) and `update()` (model refit). Each false positive kicked off a full installed-package scan, which on a large library served over NFS could hang the console for minutes (the session entering uninterruptible `D` state) -- see #17758.

### Approach

Replace the keyword regex with a two-stage check:

1. **C++ pre-filter** (`containsCallSyntax`) -- a deliberately dumb regex that only asks "does this input contain a function call?". It carries no package knowledge, so there is no keyword list to keep in sync.
2. **Precise R check** (`.rs.isPackageManagementCall`) -- parses the input and, for each call, resolves its namespace against a strict per-namespace registry of library-mutating functions (`utils`, `renv`, `pak`, `pacman`, `remotes`, `devtools`, `BiocManager`). Namespace-qualified calls (`renv::update()`) use the literal namespace; bare calls resolve via a search-path walk.

The bare-call resolver **never reads the binding's value** (no `get()`, no mode matching) -- it only tests for the binding's presence and uses the providing environment's name. That keeps it from forcing a promise (`delayedAssign`) or re-invoking an active binding as a side effect, and it never scans the package library.

As a result, `base::remove()` / `stats::update()` are ignored because of what they resolve to, while genuine package operations (`install.packages()`, `remove.packages()`, `renv::update()`, ...) still refresh the pane.

### Testing

- C++ gtests (`SessionPackagesTest`) updated to cover the pre-filter; pass.
- New `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-packages.R` covers qualified/unqualified resolution, base-R disambiguation, comments/strings, multi-statement and nested calls, unparseable input, and the active-binding / promise side-effect-safety guarantees (45 expectations, all passing).

Fixes #17758.
