title: guard data viewer histogram computation against hist() failures
description:
When opening a data frame in the data viewer, RStudio computes a histogram for each numeric column (via `hist()` in `.rs.describeCols()`, `SessionDataViewer.R`) to power the column sparkline and brushing filter.

There are two related problems, both surfacing as `hist.default()` raising `stop("invalid number of 'breaks'")` (and other `stop()` paths):

1. **No error guard.** The histogram branch only wrapped the call in `suppressWarnings()`, which does not catch errors, so any `hist()` failure propagated and aborted the entire `describe` call -- breaking the whole data viewer rather than just the offending column.

2. **Collapsed integer breaks.** For whole-number columns spanning a small range we build `int_breaks <- seq(min - 0.5, max + 0.5, by = 1)` to draw one bar per integer. At very large magnitudes (abs value >= ~2^52, reachable since #17951 coerces integer columns to double) the unit step and 0.5 offsets fall below the floating-point resolution and the sequence collapses to a single value. `hist()` then treats that lone break as a scalar *bin count* -- which errors for large negative values (count < 1) and is meaningless for positive ones.

This wraps the histogram computation in `.rs.tryCatch()` (matching the sibling factor / character-summary branches: on failure the column's histogram fields are cleared and the error is logged), and drops the integer breaks when they collapse so we fall back to default binning. Includes a regression test for the large-magnitude case.

Reported (without a reproducible example) at https://forum.posit.co/t/new-histograms-in-golden-wattle-data-viewer-break/212784

Fixes #17990.

title: Disable manifest-check throttling when using the test manifest
description:
## Summary

When Posit Assistant is opted into the pre-release (test) manifest, manifest update checks now ignore the persisted `posit_assistant_update_check_interval_hours` throttle and behave as if the interval were 0 (re-fetch on each session/startup check).

The test manifest is an internal pre-release detail, so honoring the cross-session download throttle there meant developers could pick up stale manifest data after it changed. Treating the throttle window as 0 when the test manifest is in use keeps test-manifest sessions current.

## Changes

- `shouldFetchManifest` uses a throttle window of `0` when the test manifest is active, instead of reading `posit_assistant_update_check_interval_hours`. The "always due" path (`manifestCheckDue(..., 0)`) is already covered by existing throttle unit tests.
- Extracted the duplicated test-manifest opt-in check (command-line/session option OR user preference) into a shared `isUsingTestManifest()` helper, now used at all three sites.

This intentionally leaves the pre-existing per-session in-memory cache untouched, matching `posit_assistant_update_check_interval_hours = 0` semantics rather than forcing a fetch on every in-session check.

title: Preserve package-provided protocol.json on Posit Assistant install
description:
When RStudio downloads and extracts the Posit Assistant package, it writes a `protocol.json` recording the protocol version the install was built for. Newer Posit Assistant packages now ship their own `protocol.json` as part of the package.

RStudio now writes `protocol.json` only when the extracted package does not already contain one, so a package-provided file is preserved instead of being overwritten with RStudio's compiled-in protocol version. The write is extracted into `installation::writeProtocolVersionFileIfMissing()`, alongside the existing `getInstalledProtocolVersion()` reader, with unit tests covering both the missing-file and package-provided-file cases.

title: windows automation
description:
<!-- include an entry in NEWS.md if required -->

### Intent

GitHub issue: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-ide-automation/issues/4990

Adds full Windows Server 2025 x64 CI automation for RStudio Desktop e2e Playwright tests, and aligns the existing macOS 26 ARM64 CI to follow the same validated pattern. Previously, Windows had no PR-triggered or scheduled e2e coverage, and macOS lacked build-from-source, auto-resolved daily installers, and a unified PR orchestrator.

### What changed

#### Windows Server 2025 (new)

- **`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025.yml`** — reusable core workflow with two jobs:
  - `build`: compiles RStudio Desktop from source via `make-package.bat nozip quick`, uploads Electron app as artifact. Skipped when `build_from_source: false` or `rstudio_installer_url` is provided.
  - `e2e-desktop-windows`: two shards; installs built artifact or daily `.exe`; runs Playwright suite; posts merged results to PR via sticky comment.
- **`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-pr.yml`** — combined Windows + macOS PR orchestrator: fires on `src/**`, `e2e/**`, `cmake/**`, `package/**`; `build_from_source: true`; concurrency cancel-in-progress; one `detect-changes` job shared by both platforms.
- **`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025-scheduled.yml`** — Mon–Fri 03:00 UTC against latest daily build.
- **`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-windows-server-2025-seed.yml`** — Monday 04:00 UTC build-only run to prevent 7-day GitHub cache eviction.
- Auto-detect C++ changes: build job only runs when `src/**` or `dependencies/**` actually changed, skipping the ~90 min compile on e2e-only PRs.
- `mozilla-actions/sccache-action` (pinned SHA) with `SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED=true` for compiler caching — no AWS credentials needed.
- GWT output cache (`src/gwt/www|bin|extras`) with `actions/cache/restore` + `actions/cache/save` split (replaces deprecated `save-always: true`); build uses `nogwt` on cache hit. Cache key hashes `src/gwt/src/**` + `acesupport/**` + `lib/**` + `build.xml` + `conf/**` so non-Java GWT inputs (`.ui.xml`, `.css`, JS resources) invalidate the cache.
- rstudio-tools deps cache with same restore/save split.
- `winget install --disable-interactivity` to prevent interactive prompts on CI.
- `/Z7` debug info forced via `add_compile_options` for all targets including FetchContent deps (fixes sccache on MSVC).
- R bin path constructed from `R.home()` (fixes `$rBin` alias bug on Windows where `bin\x64` doesn't exist under rig-installed R).

#### Visual Studio 2026 transition (mid-PR rollout)

GitHub Actions began migrating the `windows-2025` runner image from VS 2022 to VS 2026 during this PR's lifetime ([actions/runner-images#14017](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14017), rollout June 8–15, 2026). Microsoft's guidance is that customers needing VS 2022 should switch to `windows-2022`; we stayed on `windows-2025` and patched the toolchain to support VS 2026 instead. Three coordinated fixes were required:

- **CMake** (`src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`): Boost / SOCI prebuilts are keyed by MSVC toolset version. The runner now reports `MSVC_TOOLSET_VERSION=145` (VS 2026) but only msvc143 prebuilts exist on S3. Added a fallback that uses the msvc143 directory when the current toolset's directory is absent — MSVC 14.x releases are binary-compatible so the link still works. Also bypassed `find_package(Boost)` in favor of an explicit `Boost_INCLUDE_DIRS` since CMake 4.x dropped `FindBoost.cmake` (CMP0167).
- **install-soci.R generator**: it defaulted its CMake generator to `Visual Studio 17 2022`, which fails on a VS-2026-only runner with `could not find any instance of Visual Studio`. The workflow now passes `CMAKE_GENERATOR=Visual Studio 18 2026` on the `Install build dependencies` step so install-soci.R builds against the available generator.
- **node-gyp** for Electron native rebuild: the version bundled by `@electron/rebuild@3.7.x` (which `electron-forge` pins) only recognizes VS 2017–2022, so `node-gyp rebuild` aborts with `unsupported version: 18`. Two layers fix this:
  - An npm `overrides` entry in `src/node/desktop/package.json` redirects `@electron/node-gyp` → `npm:node-gyp@^12` (which supports VS 2026). Covers the `@electron/rebuild` path.
  - A workflow step replaces npm's *bundled* node-gyp (inside `dependencies/common/node/<ver>/node_modules/npm/node_modules/node-gyp`) with an `--install-strategy=nested` install of upstream `node-gyp@^12`. Covers the lifecycle path that runs `node-gyp rebuild` literally from a shell, since npm's bundled node-gyp wins PATH resolution there.

These layers are independent — Electron uses one node-gyp invocation chain, the npm install lifecycle uses another, and both had to be redirected at VS-2026-aware node-gyp v12 to unblock the build.

#### macOS 26 ARM64 (aligned and improved)

- Aligned reusable workflow with Windows: `build_from_source` input, daily auto-resolve from `dailies.rstudio.com` JSON manifest, SHA-256 verification, installer cache keyed on filename.
- `detect-changes` job added to macOS PR workflow — skips ~60 min source build on e2e-only changes.
- Combined Windows and macOS PR workflows into a single orchestrator (`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-pr.yml`) with one `detect-changes` job shared by both platforms.
- `mozilla-actions/sccache-action` (pinned SHA) replacing manual sccache setup on macOS.
- GWT output cache (`package/osx/build-arm64/gwt/`) with restore/save split; build uses `--build-gwt=0` on cache hit. Cache key hashes the same broad set of GWT inputs as the Windows side (originally `*.java`-only, which silently served stale compiled GWT bundles when only non-Java GWT inputs changed — fixed by expanding the glob and bumping the key prefix to `v2` so existing stale entries don't get pulled via `restore-keys`).
- `actions/cache/restore` + `actions/cache/save` split throughout (replaces deprecated `save-always: true`) so caches are written even when later steps fail.
- `pull-requests: write` at top-level reusable workflow permissions + `GITHUB_TOKEN` explicitly passed to `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` — fixes "Requires authentication" in `workflow_call` context where job-level permissions are capped by the top-level declaration.
- `strategy.job-total` used for shard count instead of hardcoded value.
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in e2e-merge (skips browser binary downloads; only merge-reports needed).
- `NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL: error` and `NPM_CONFIG_AUDIT: 'false'` to suppress npm noise in build logs.
- e2e-merge skips when e2e jobs were cancelled; PR comment guarded to only post when there are actual test results.

#### Test fixes and stabilisation

- **`source_pane.actions.ts`** — `ensureVisualMode` ProseMirror `waitFor` timeout 15 s → 90 s; macOS 26 pandoc conversion of template documents with chunks/plots reliably exceeds the original 15 s ceiling.
- **`autocomplete.actions.ts`** — `getCompletionItems` default timeout 5 s → 15 s; macOS 26 ARM64 R response to Ctrl+Space can exceed 5 s under load.
- **`rmarkdown.test.ts`** — `beforeAll` `ensurePackages` extended to install `thematic` + `bslib`. The "Theming with bslib and thematic" RMarkdown template selected by the `rmd templates display` test would otherwise surface a non-modal "Package thematic required" notification banner that blocks panmirror from mounting; `installDepIfPrompted` only handles modal install dialogs, not the inline banner, so pre-installing the packages is the cleanest fix.
- **`markdown.test.ts`** + **`rnotebook.test.ts`** — extended the cross-origin `SecurityError` `test.fixme` guard to cover `darwin` CI in addition to `win32`. The underlying GWT preview-iframe bug isn't platform-specific; macOS 26 just exposes it intermittently.
- **`data_viewer.test.ts`** (`End scrolls to the last row of the current column (#17958)`) — `test.fixme` on `win32` CI. The bottom-edge assertion overshoots by ~24 px on Windows because `visibleBodyHeight` in `DataViewer.js` subtracts only the 10 px overlay scrollbar; an additional row-height/clientHeight delta on Windows Chromium/Electron isn't accounted for. The fix landed on main with #17961 but was developed on macOS overlay scrollbars; a Windows follow-up is needed to tune `visibleBodyHeight`. The fixme references the issue so it's straightforward to remove once the product side is patched.
- **`import_dataset.test.ts`** — extracted `awaitPreviewOrSkip` helper; `test.fixme` on Windows CI where the readr preview subprocess occasionally fails to start (known environment issue, not a product bug).
- **`python_completions.test.ts`** — `test.fixme` when popup doesn't appear on Windows CI (known reticulate/jedi initialisation issue).
- **`ignorefiles.test.ts`** — `split(/\r?\n/)` throughout to handle Windows CRLF line endings in `.gitignore` content.

#### e2e-deps action fix

- **`.github/actions/e2e-deps/action.yml`** — `npm ci` retry loop always exited 0 after 3 failures because `sleep 10` was the last command. Added explicit `exit 1` after the final failed attempt.

### Approach

All four new Windows workflow files follow the same build → artifact → e2e → post-results pattern validated by the existing macOS workflow. The reusable workflow accepts `build_from_source`, `rstudio_installer_url`, `r_version`, `project`, `grep`, `test_selector`, `test_ignore`, and `grep_invert` inputs so it can be called from PR triggers, scheduled runs, seed jobs, and `workflow_dispatch` with consistent behaviour.

### Automated Tests

This PR is the test infrastructure itself. All Playwright tests on both platforms pass on the final CI run. Jenkins (c++-unit-tests, gwt-unit-tests, build-package) and Snyk also pass. No additional unit tests are needed for workflow files.

### QA Notes

After merging, manually trigger the Windows seed workflow once to warm the sccache and rstudio-tools caches before the first PR run hits them cold:

`Actions → Cache Seed: E2E Playwright RStudio (Desktop, Windows Server 2025 x64, Open Source) → Run workflow`

The first seed run will take ~90 min (cold build). Subsequent PR runs on a warm cache should complete in ~20–30 min.

### Follow-up issues

Two test skips in this PR reference upstream product bugs and should be removed once those land:

- `data_viewer.test.ts:End scrolls to the last row (#17958)` on Windows — needs `visibleBodyHeight` in `src/cpp/session/resources/grid/DataViewer.js` to also subtract the Windows-specific scrollbar/row-height delta. The 10 px overlay-scrollbar subtraction from #17961 is insufficient on `windows-2025` Chromium.
- `markdown.test.ts:preview markdown file as HTML` and `rnotebook.test.ts:create new R Notebook and preview` on Windows + macOS CI — GWT raises a cross-origin `SecurityError` accessing the preview iframe. Needs a product fix in the preview/iframe wiring.

### Documentation

No user-facing or admin documentation needed. This is CI infrastructure only. Key design decisions (7z for MAX\_PATH, directory junction for CMake, winget for rig, weekly seed cadence, `/Z7` for sccache on MSVC, `split/save` cache pattern, VS 2026 toolchain fallbacks, node-gyp bundled override) are documented inline in the workflow files.

### Checklist

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [ ] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: auto-resolve conflicts under release-only dirs in merge-release-branch.sh
description:
merge-release-branch.sh exited for manual resolution on any unresolved conflict before its RELEASE_ONLY_DIRS reset pass could run, so a conflict under `src/node/desktop/src/assets/whats-new` (e.g. both-modified or both-added) aborted the merge even though the policy for those paths is unambiguous: main's version always wins.

A new resolution pass now runs before the generic unresolved-conflict check: any unmerged path under a release-only directory is restored to HEAD's content (or removed when not present in HEAD, covering delete/modify conflicts). `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` is used rather than `--ours` since the latter fails for conflict types where our stage is absent.

Verified in a scratch repository simulating UU, AA, and DU conflicts under whats-new (all auto-resolved to main's content, merge left staged) and a genuine conflict elsewhere (still aborts with exit 2).

Developer tooling change; found by code review (roborev job 546).

title: always show column count in data viewer status bar
description:
Follow-up to #17613: the status bar appended the column count only when `totalCols > 0`, so a genuinely zero-column object showed no count at all. The guard is removed; `totalCols == 0` can only mean "unknown" in the window between `resetGridState` and the bootstrap column fetch, and in that window `totalRows` is also 0, which blanks the bar via the existing early return -- so whenever the column-count line is reached, the value is a real count. A comment documents that invariant.

Also corrects the golden wattle release-notes example for #17613 to quote the implemented string ("Showing 1 to 18 of 100,000 entries, 500 total columns"); the previously documented wording ("Showing rows ... total rows") never matched the UI, which is asserted as-is by existing e2e tests.

Found by code review (roborev job 521).

Addresses #17613.

title: add regression tests for help arguments header rewrite
description:
The Help pane's `

Arguments

` rewrite (which attaches the `r-arguments-title` class used by R.css for argument-table alignment) has broken once before when newer R versions started emitting attributes on the header (fixed in 852f68f for #17622), and had no test coverage. The rewrite is moved verbatim from the help contents filter into `help::detail::addArgumentsHeaderClass()` -- following the existing `SessionLists` detail-namespace precedent for exposing file-local helpers to tests -- and exercised by four new gtests in `SessionHelpTests.cpp`: the bare header, attributed variants (including R 4.6's `id="_sec_arguments"`), the header embedded in surrounding page content, and negative cases that must pass through untouched. Behavior-preserving refactor; the regex is unchanged. All 337 rsession-scope tests pass, including the 4 new ones (`rstudio-tests --scope rsession`). Addresses #17622.

title: skip initialization steps when stale 'initialize' continuation is cancelled
description:
The `initialize` continuation only checked for errors, not cancellation. Stale continuations are cancelled by the pruning pass in `onBackgroundProcessing` (with a `{"cancelled": true}` result), but the callback body still ran: it sent an `initialized` notification and the old assistant's configuration through global state to whatever agent was currently running. A fast assistant switch (e.g. Copilot -> Posit) could therefore double-initialize the new agent and apply the previous assistant's configuration to it.

The callback now returns early when the response indicates cancellation, before any notifications are sent. `s_agentRuntimeStatus` is deliberately left untouched in this path: on a switch, the new agent's own startup sequence manages it, and writing `Unknown` here would clobber the live status.

Found by code review (roborev job 548). Requires manual verification (fast assistant switching); no automated test.

Addresses #17969.

title: correct golden wattle news entry for ai ignore-file augmentation
description:
The 2026.05.0 (golden wattle) release-notes entry for #17665 claimed `.claude` is added to a project's `.gitignore` and `svn:ignore`; it never was -- only the Posit Assistant state directories are. `.claude` is only handled by the `.Rbuildignore` augmentation (package projects), deliberately, since repositories often commit `.claude`.

Verified against the `origin/rel-golden-wattle` sources: `.positai` -> `.gitignore`/`svn:ignore` (existence-gated); `.positai` and `.claude` -> package `.Rbuildignore` (existence-gated). The entry is reworded to state exactly that.

Documentation-only change to the released notes; found by code review (roborev job 565).

title: add pin/sort controls, richer summaries, and help dialog to data viewer sidebar
description: --- A batch of polish for the data viewer's column summary sidebar: - **Pin and sort from the sidebar.** Each entry carries a pin icon and a sort icon mirroring the grid header's affordances. State syncs both ways (grid header, keyboard, status-bar clear-sort, and the sidebar icons all flow through the same paths), and `handleSortClick` no longer requires a rendered ``, so columns virtualized out of the grid window can still be sorted from the sidebar. - **Uniform footers.** Numeric columns show their actual data range as `[min, max]` (new `col_min`/`col_max` from `describeCols` -- the histogram breaks are `pretty()`-ed and may extend past the data, and the sparklines have no axis ticks). Factors show "N levels", characters "N unique", and every column shows its NA percentage, dimmed when zero. The interval's bracket/comma adornments are dimmed so the numbers read at full contrast. - **Categorical mini-plots.** Factor and character columns with at most 24 distinct values (`maxCategoryBars`) draw frequency sparklines in an alternate themeable color (`--grid-spark-categorical`) to cue a discrete x-axis: factors in level order (preserving ordinal structure), characters most frequent first. Above the cutoff the footer names the dominant value instead -- omitted for all-distinct, ID-like columns. Character counting costs a full `table()` hash, so it is gated on `rstudio.dataViewer.maxCategorizeRows` (default 1e6); factor counts are a cheap `tabulate()`. - **Help dialog.** A "?" in the sidebar header opens a small modal explaining the entry structure, with legend swatches bound to the same CSS variables the sparkline canvases read, so the legend can't drift from the actual colors. Activating it doesn't collapse the panel, and hovering it doesn't light the header's close glyph. ## Testing - New testthat cases cover the `col_min`/`col_max` range fields, category counts (level order, unused levels, NA exclusion), the exactly-24/25 bar-cutoff boundary, the >24 text fallback for both column types, Inf exclusion from the range, list columns of character/factor vectors, the character row-limit gate (and factor counts surviving it), and malformed `maxCategorizeRows` values (`rstudio-tests --scope r --filter dataviewer`: 182 passing). - New Playwright tests cover the sidebar pin/sort icons (two-way sync with the grid header, including row-order assertions), sorting a column whose header is virtualized out of the grid window, sidebar icon sync on the status-bar clear-sort and state-restore paths, the uniform footer, category bars vs. text fallback, and the help dialog open/Escape flow without panel collapse (full data-viewer suite: 44 passing).

title: Fill in missing French translations for GWT property files
description:
## Summary

A review of the GWT `_en` / `_fr` property file pairs surfaced 20 keys with no French translation. This resolves them in two ways, depending on the cause:

- **`UserPrefsAccessorConstants_fr.properties`**: Adds French translations for 16 strings, covering 8 newly added preferences (hierarchical section folding, inline notebook chunk execution, data viewer summary panel, durable file writes, system certificate store, Posit Assistant pre-release manifest, Posit Assistant update check interval, and the Air `air.toml` requirement). All 16 keys correspond to existing methods on the `Constants` interface.

- **`EditorsTextConstants_en.properties`**: Removes 4 orphaned keys (`checkTestPackageDependenciesError`, `checkTestPackageDependenciesMessage`, `checkTestPackageDependenciesCaption`, `installShinyTestDependenciesError`). These are not declared on the `Messages` interface and have no call sites — the `checkTestPackageDependencies` flow now delegates to `dependencyManager_.withTestPackage(...)`. Removing them brings the English bundle back in sync with French, which never defined them.

## Verification

- Re-ran a key diff across all 108 `_en`/`_fr` pairs under `src/gwt/src/`: no remaining keys lack a French counterpart.
- New French entries match the file's conventions (retained English comments, single apostrophes as required for a `Constants` interface, raw UTF-8 accents); no duplicate keys.
- Confirmed the removed keys are not referenced in downstream rstudio-pro code (no accessor call sites, not declared on the interface there either).

No NEWS.md entry: the added translations cover new/unreleased preferences, and the removed keys were dead.

title: use index-based access for duplicated names in object explorer
description:
## Intent

Fixes #17937.

The Object Explorer showed the first element's contents for every same-named element of a list. Expanding a node re-extracts the element via generated access code, and named elements used access-by-name (`x[["Passenger"]]`), which always retrieves the first match. Elements whose name is duplicated (or `NA`) are now accessed by index (`x[[2]]`), while still displaying their name. Uniquely named elements keep access-by-name. The same fix applies to named atomic vectors.

## Approach

In `SessionObjectExplorer.R`, the child-context construction shared by `inspectList` and `inspectDefault` is factored into `.rs.explorer.childContextForElement()`, which falls back to index-based access when the element's name does not uniquely identify it. Since the generated access code is also what the "extract code" action inserts, that code now correctly resolves to the clicked element as well.

## QA Notes

In the console:

```r
a <- list(list(Id = 1, Age = 12), list(Id = 2, Age = 22), list(Id = 3, Age = 33))
names(a) <- rep("Passenger", 3)
View(a)
```

Expanding each `Passenger` node should show its own `Id`/`Age` values (previously all three showed `1` / `12`).

## Automated Tests

- `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-object-explorer.R`: unit tests for the generated access strings (duplicated, unique, empty names; lists and atomic vectors), including a simulation of the client's re-extraction round trip.
- `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/object-explorer/object_explorer.test.ts`: drives `View()` on the reporter's list, expands the second and third `Passenger` nodes, and asserts each shows its own values. Verified to fail against the pre-fix build and pass with the fix.

## Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, I have added an entry to `NEWS.md`
- [x] My PR is targeting the correct branch

title: Populate Blue Plumbago what's-new page
description:
Populates the Blue Plumbago "What's New" page (`src/node/desktop/src/assets/whats-new/blue-plumbago/index.html`), shown to users on first launch of the release.

- The New Features section lists the user-facing additions drawn from `NEWS.md`.
- The Fixes section links to the online release notes for the full bug-fix list.

Fixes #17853.

title: show column count and close glyph in summary sidebar header
description:
## Summary

When the data viewer's Summary sidebar is open, its header strip repeated the word "Summary" directly below the toolbar's Summary toggle button, which already names (and latches for) the panel.

The header strip itself still earns its place -- it visually caps the panel in line with the grid's column-header row, hosts the shared column-summary fetch spinner, and acts as an in-panel close control -- so rather than removing it:

- The label now shows the column count (e.g. "12 columns"), or "50 of 5,000 columns" when column pagination means the sidebar lists only the current page.
- A right-aligned close glyph was added as a visual affordance. It is `aria-hidden` and has no handler of its own; clicks bubble to `#sidebarToggle`, which remains the panel's single accessible control with its existing `aria-label`/`aria-expanded` wiring.

No NEWS.md entry since the Summary sidebar is unreleased (2026.06.0).

## Testing

- `node --check` passes on `DataViewer.js`; the file remains ASCII-only (the glyph is written as a `\u00D7` escape).
- Ran the Summary sidebar e2e tests against the dev build: `npm run test:desktop-dev -- tests/panes/data-viewer/data_viewer.test.ts -g "Summary"` -- 2 passed ("dismissed summary sidebar stays dismissed when a column is added", "the in-grid Summary toggle still works after a data refresh").

title: Vary "Posit Assistant Not Installed" message based on a manifest flag
description:
Reads an optional `providers` array from the Posit Assistant manifest entry that matches this build's protocol version, and uses it to vary the copy shown in the "Posit Assistant Not Installed" view.

## What changed
- The manifest parser (`ChatIntegrity`) now also returns the `providers` identifiers advertised for the selected protocol entry, plus a small tested predicate over them.
- The session module surfaces a flag on the `chat_check_for_updates` result based on that array.
- When the flag is set, the chat pane appends a sentence to the open-source "Posit Assistant is powered by the Posit AI service…" description. The Workbench description (shown only for a pro license on the server) is left unchanged.
- When the array is absent — or the field is omitted by an older session — the view is unchanged, so the behavior is backward compatible.
- A malformed `providers` array is treated as empty, deterministically (no dependence on element order).

## Tests
- C++ unit tests in `ChatIntegrityTests.cpp` cover provider extraction from the selected protocol entry, absence, malformed input, and the predicate.

An end-to-end test is intentionally deferred and will be handled separately.

Addresses #17957.

title: add read-only permission allowlist to claude settings
description:
## Summary

Adds a `permissions.allow` list to the checked-in `.claude/settings.json`, so Claude Code no longer prompts for common read-only or test-loop commands in this repo.

The entries were derived by scanning recent session transcripts for frequently-prompted commands, keeping only those that are read-only or standard test/check invocations:

- `npm run test:desktop-dev` -- Playwright desktop tests against the dev build
- `./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests` -- C++ / R test runner
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` -- desktop checks and unit tests
- `gh search`, `gh run watch` -- read-only GitHub CLI queries

Deliberately excluded: anything mutating (`git push`, `gh pr create`, `gh issue edit`, ...), interpreters and package runners (`Rscript`, `node`, `npx`), and builds (`cmake --build`, `ant draft`). Commands Claude Code already auto-allows (read-only `git`/`gh` subcommands, `grep`, `ls`, etc.) are omitted as redundant.

No NEWS.md entry since this is a developer-tooling change with no user-facing impact.

title: restore data viewer end/ctrl+end scroll-to-bottom behavior
description:
End and Ctrl+End in the data viewer body now move to the last row of the *current* column, matching the pre-rewrite (DataTables) viewer, instead of jumping to the last column; Home likewise returns to the top of the current column. Header-mode Home/End still walk between column headers.

This also fixes the "doesn't quite reach the bottom" half of the report: `ensureActiveCellVisible` computed bottom-edge scrolls from the raw viewport `clientHeight`, but the sticky header both contributes to scroll content height and occludes the top of the viewport (and the custom horizontal scrollbar overlays the bottom 10px), so a jump to the last row landed a header-height (~25px) short, leaving the target row hidden below the fold. The bottom-edge math now uses the effective body-visible height, shared with the status bar via a new `visibleBodyHeight` helper.

The copy/paste half of #17958 was already fixed on main by #17804 (Ctrl+C no longer clobbers a multi-cell text selection); it just isn't in the 2026.05.0 release the reporter is on.

Includes an e2e regression test (verified to fail against the old bottom-edge math). Full data viewer spec passes (38/38, desktop-dev).

Fixes #17958.

title: add a clear-sort button to the data viewer status bar
description:
When a column sort is active, the "Sorted by: <column> (<direction>)" status at the right of the data viewer's info bar now includes a small X button that clears the sort, restoring the frame's natural row order.

Implementation notes:

- The sort status element is split into a text span plus a persistent `<button>`, so the button's click listener (wired once at `DOMContentLoaded`, like the sidebar toggle) survives info-bar updates; a `setSortStatus()` helper updates the text and toggles button visibility everywhere the status used to be written directly.
- `clearSort()` mirrors `handleSortClick`'s unsort path: it resets the sort state, clears the active cell, resets header arrows and `aria-sort`, re-fetches from the top, and saves state so the cleared sort persists.
- The button reuses the same inline-SVG X icon styling as the column filter's clear affordance.

Includes an e2e test covering: sort applied -> status text and button visible -> click -> natural order restored, status cleared, button hidden, header indicator and `aria-sort` reset.

No NEWS.md entry since the sort status bar is part of the unreleased data viewer rework.

Fixes #17959.

---

Also tags along an unrelated e2e-stability fix (45d2a49e06): `ScrollUtil.setScrollPositionOnLoad` polled the rmd preview frame's document without a try/catch, so a transiently cross-origin frame raised an uncaught `SecurityError` from the 50ms timer -- killing the scroll restore and (since #17956) failing whichever e2e test was running, as seen with `create new rmarkdown and knit to HTML` in [run #240](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/27429548185). A throw is now treated like the other not-ready cases and polling continues, matching the guarded versions of the same access in `RmdOutputFramePane`.

title: add data viewer filter coverage; fix factor restore and stale filter re-apply
description:
Following up on the report in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17806#issuecomment-4683276058 that "filter and sorting don't work" in the new data viewer: the mechanics check out on main, but our coverage of per-column filters turned out to be character-only. This PR fills in the missing coverage and fixes two real bugs it surfaced.

## Tests added

**testthat (`test-dataviewer.R`)** -- `.rs.applyTransform()` semantics:
- all four filter wire formats: `character|` (case-insensitive literal substring), `factor|<level index>`, `numeric|lo_hi` range and single-value equality (NA/Inf dropped), `boolean|` (NA rows dropped)
- malformed / empty filters are ignored rather than applied or errored
- global search matches data columns and row names
- column filter + global search + sort compose
- asc/desc sorting of character, factor (level order), logical, Date, and POSIXct columns

**Playwright (`column-filters.test.ts`)** -- the three previously untested filter widgets, asserting the server round-trip via the info bar's "filtered from" text:
- numeric: typed range, narrowing to equality, header label rendering, and clear
- factor: level click applies the filter and shows the level in the filter box
- factor display survives a column scrolling out of and back into the virtualized window
- boolean: value click and clear
- columns with no supported filter type (e.g. Date) render no filter widget, while neighbors still filter

## Bug fixes

**Factor filter restore.** The virtualization test failed against unfixed code: a restored `factor|<idx>` filter rendered a blank filter box while the filter remained active server-side (the same "invisible active filter" class of bug as #17830), because `createTextFilterBox` only restores `character|` values. `createFactorFilterUI` now maps the stored 1-based level index back to its level name. No NEWS entry: column virtualization postdates the 2026.05.0 release.

**Stale debounced filter re-apply** (caught by this PR's numeric test failing on CI). Clearing a column filter could silently re-apply it: the clear's own blur fires a native `change` commit on the dirty input, scheduling one last debounced apply that lands after the clear -- leaving the filter active server-side while the header shows "All". The race window is the 200ms filter debounce, so it reproduces deterministically when the dismiss and the clear click land close together (CI trace showed the cleared fetch at +0ms and the stale `numeric|7` re-apply at +31ms). `debounce()` now takes an optional `watch` getter, sampled when a call is scheduled and again when the timer fires; the pending call is dropped if the watched value changed in between. Column filters watch their own stored search value -- so a pending apply is discarded only when *that* filter was cleared or rewritten underneath it, while applies racing unrelated invalidations (a sort, the global search, another column's filter) still run. The global search debounce watches `cachedSearch` for the same race against `resetGridState`. Also reorders the arguments to `debounce(wait, watch, func)` so call sites end with the closure body.

## Testing

- `rstudio-tests --scope r --filter dataviewer`: 129 pass
- `npm run test:desktop-dev` for the full `tests/panes/data-viewer/` suite: 31 pass
- `column-filters.test.ts -g "numeric filter" --repeat-each=5`: 5 pass (this test failed both CI attempts before the debounce fix)

Addresses #17806.

title: evaluate notebook inline R code in the user's session
description:
Since the async notebook render from cache (#17309), R Notebook previews are rendered in a child R process. The child's global environment is empty, so inline R code referencing the user's objects (e.g. `` `r max(dfSamples$date_received)` ``) failed with "object not found" -- knitr evaluates inline expressions live at render time, even when chunk outputs come from the cache.

This PR evaluates inline R code in the user's R session before spawning the background render:

- `.rs.rnb.evaluateInlineChunks()` extracts inline expressions (using knitr's own `parse_inline` after stripping fenced code blocks), evaluates each through knitr's default `evaluate.inline` hook against the global environment, formats the result with the inline hook, and writes the outputs to a transport `.rds` file. Evaluation errors are captured per-expression.
- The child process (`SessionNotebookRender.R`) loads the transport file and installs an `evaluate.inline` knit hook that substitutes the precomputed outputs, re-signals captured errors (preserving the message and line attribution an in-session render would have produced), and falls back to normal evaluation on a cache miss.
- The document itself is never modified, so the source embedded in the `.nb.html` and error line numbers remain exact.
- A new preference, "Execute inline R code when previewing notebooks" (Global Options > R Markdown, default on), can disable the in-session evaluation for users who prefer that saving a notebook never runs inline code in their session.

Inline evaluation is re-done on every save/preview, matching the pre-#17309 semantics where the in-session render evaluated inline code live each time. The expensive, document-size-driven work (knit from cache, base64 embedding, pandoc) remains in the background process.

Fixes #17521.

Includes an e2e Playwright test (`notebook_inline_chunks.test.ts`) covering both paths: inline code referencing a global-environment object renders correctly in the background preview, and disabling the preference falls back to background evaluation.

title: run per-test e2e resets via auto fixture; capture client exceptions; pin test geometry
description:
Fixes #17954. Fixes #17955.

Follow-ups from validating #17953 -- the residual environment-pane flake turned out to be a deeper harness defect, and chasing it surfaced a product bug.

### Product fix (#17954)

`ImageFrame.replaceLocation` (Plots pane) dereferenced `el.contentWindow` unconditionally; during pane re-parenting (quadrant swaps, snap-to-minimize churn on short windows) it is null, and the read raised an uncaught TypeError shown to the user as an error dialog. Now reports not-ready, feeding the existing `onLoad` retry. Verified: `pane_layout.test.ts` goes from 15/16 to 16/16 at 1024x640.

### Harness fixes (#17955)

- **Per-test reset as an auto fixture.** The module-scope `test.beforeEach` only attached to the first spec file loaded per worker (Node module caching), so every later file ran without resets -- the actual mechanism behind the environment-pane first-test flake. Auto fixtures run for every test in every file. Verified: three files in one worker, resets fire for each file, all green at the geometry that previously reproduced the flake.
- **Uncaught client exceptions fail the test that raised them.** The automation agent wraps the uncaught-exception handler and records message + stack into `window.rstudio.errors`; the fixture drains it after every test (failing with the stack in the output; `PW_IGNORE_CLIENT_EXCEPTIONS=1` downgrades to warnings), and warns with contents for any leaked modal the reset dismisses. New harness self-test exercises the chain end-to-end via `errors.simulate()` (a real throw from a `$entry` context), including a `test.fail()`-inverted check that the fail-on-exception machinery actually fails tests.
- **Pinned window geometry: 1024x645 for local and CI.** macOS clamps windows to the visible frame, so CI was already running at its 1024x645 workArea while local ran 1400x900 -- geometry-sensitive bugs surfaced only on CI. 800x600 was evaluated and rejected (genuinely cramps layouts: data-viewer column tests, Import Dataset dialog; 7 failures).

### Verification

87 tests green locally at the pinned geometry in one run: `tests/harness`, `rnotebook` + `environment_pane` (the CI failure sequence, same worker), all of `tests/panes/layout`, and all of `tests/panes/data-viewer`. `ant javac` and the e2e typecheck pass.

title: clear pane maximize state in e2e resets; isolate per-spec data homes
description:
Fixes #17952.

Two fixes for the environment-pane e2e failures where `#rstudio_workbench_tab_environment` resolved as selected but stayed "not visible" for the rest of a CI run:

### `layout.reset()` now clears WindowFrame-level pane maximize

`PaneManager.endZoomIfActive` (backing `window.rstudio.layout.reset()`, which the per-test reset calls) only checked PaneManager's zoom tracking. A quadrant maximized through the WindowFrame state machine -- the pane-header min/max buttons, or `EnsureHeightEvent` escalating to MAXIMIZE when the requested height doesn't fit (the R Notebook preview on ~645px-tall CI displays) -- was invisible to it, leaving TabSet1 minimized with its real tab elements hidden. When no tracked zoom is active, the reset now restores any MAXIMIZE-state quadrant to NORMAL, which also restores its minimized sibling; HIDE/EXCLUSIVE pairs (the empty-source-pane layout) are left alone.

### Per-spec `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` in the desktop e2e fixture

All workers shared one data home, so the maximize persisted via client state (`data-home/pcs/windowlayoutstate.pper`) and every subsequent launch -- including fresh retry workers -- restored the broken layout at startup. Each launch now gets its own data home under its per-spec config root (still reused across deliberate quit-and-restart flows, so persistence tests keep working), and the seeded Posit Assistant build is symlinked into each per-spec data home. The uninstall flow deletes pai via `boost::filesystem::remove_all`, which removes the link without following it, so the shared seed survives.

### Tests

- New regression test in `tabs.test.ts`: maximizes TabSet2 via `maximizeTabSet2` (the same WindowState path the notebook preview takes), confirms the Environment tab is hidden, and verifies `layout.reset()` restores it. Passes against the dev build.
- `environment_pane.test.ts` passes locally when run after main's `rnotebook.test.ts` in the same worker (the CI failure sequence).
- `sandbox.test.ts` updated for (and verifying) the per-spec data home, including that the session writes `rstudio-desktop.json` there.
- `pane_location_persistence.test.ts` (config-root reuse across restart) passes.

title: restore the active source tab by document id, not tab index
description:
The Source pane persisted the active tab across reloads as a physical tab index (the in-session display position mapped through the `tabOrder_` permutation), but on restore the saved index was applied directly to the freshly built tab set, whose order comes from the persisted `relativeOrder` (falling back to creation time). Whenever the two orders diverge -- tabs drag-reordered during the session, or a document opened mid-session (new tabs are inserted immediately after the current tab but restored at the end, since they keep `relativeOrder == 0`) -- the wrong tab was selected after a reload or session restart.

This change persists the active document's ID instead (client state key `activeTabDocId`) and resolves it to a tab after the documents are restored:

- `Source.java`: the `IntStateValue` for the active tab becomes a `StringStateValue` holding the active document ID.
- `SourceColumnManager.initialSelect()` now takes a doc ID, restores the last active column, and selects the column/tab containing that document.
- `SourceColumn.initialSelect()` looks the document up by ID and selects its tab.

The in-session save/restore pair (`getPhysicalTabIndex()` / `setPhysicalTabIndex()`) is untouched; only the cross-reload persistence path changes. The previously saved `activeTab` integer is simply ignored (one-time, the active tab falls back to the first restored document).

Includes a Playwright regression test that opens documents so the physical order diverges from the restored order, reloads, and asserts the pre-reload active document is re-selected. Verified the test fails (selects the wrong tab, exactly as reported) against the unfixed build and passes with the fix.

Not included: the complementary `set_doc_order` change suggested in the issue (persisting tab order when a tab is inserted at a non-terminal position). That would make the restored *tab order* match the pre-reload physical order, but it adds an RPC to every document open and is a separate, cosmetic symptom; the wrong-active-tab bug is fully addressed by the ID-based persistence.

Fixes #17944.

title: keep summary sidebar state across data refreshes
description:
## Summary

In the Data Viewer, dismissing (or opening) the Summary sidebar and then changing the viewed object's column structure (e.g. `df$new <- 1`) inadvertently toggled the sidebar back to the `data_viewer_show_summary` preference default.

The structure-changed refresh re-bootstraps the grid. Because adding a column flips the server-side column fingerprint, the saved per-object UI state is discarded as incompatible -- and the bootstrap then fell through to re-applying the preference default for the sidebar, clobbering the user's live choice.

The fix resolves the URL/preference default only on the first bootstrap of the frame; later re-bootstraps (data refresh, column pagination) keep the live in-memory `sidebarVisible` value.

## Testing

Adds a Playwright regression test (`dismissed summary sidebar stays dismissed when a column is added`) that dismisses the sidebar via the toolbar toggle, adds a column from the console, and asserts the sidebar (and the toolbar latch) stays dismissed. Verified the test fails against the pre-fix code and passes with the fix.

Fixes #17942.

title: use air for formatting even without an air.toml
description:
## Summary

Addresses the confusion in #17748: enabling "Use Air for code formatting" together with "Reformat documents on save" silently did nothing unless the project contained an `air.toml`, with the requirement only visible in a tooltip.

With this change:

- **Air no longer requires an `air.toml`.** When none is found, the backend synthesizes one in the formatting staging directory from the effective editor indentation settings -- `use_spaces_for_tab` maps to `indent-style` and `num_spaces_for_tab` maps to `indent-width` (project-level settings are honored via the usual pref layering). `line-width` is left at Air's default, since `margin_column` only controls the editor's margin indicator. This matches Positron, where the Air LSP picks up editor settings when no `air.toml` exists.
- **The previous gating is available as an opt-in**: a new "Only use Air when an air.toml file is found" preference (Global Options > Code > Formatting, `air_formatter_require_toml`, default off).

## Bug fixes picked up along the way

- `.rs.air.defaultVersion` passed a multi-line `readLines()` result to `.rs.fromJSON`, which only parses the first element -- this broke Air autoinstall whenever the GitHub API response was pretty-printed.
- The `format_context` RPC reports a missing `air.toml` as an empty string, which the client treated as "present", defeating the require-toml gate.

## Tests

The `air_formatting` Playwright suite grows from 8 to 12 cases, covering the require-toml gate (manual reformat, save, and the original silent-no-op scenario) and the synthesized config (a project with `NumSpacesForTab: 4` produces 4-space-indented Air output without an `air.toml`; Air's own default of 2 makes the width a true discriminator). Also adds a `window.rstudio.project.airTomlPath()` automation bridge accessor so tests can wait for the client-side `air.toml` cache instead of sleeping.

All 12 cases pass locally in desktop-dev mode; `tsc`, `ant javac`, and the backend build are clean.

Fixes #17748.

title: reassemble utf-8 characters split across terminal output chunks
description:
Addresses #17941.

## Problem

PTY reads are arbitrary byte windows over the child process's UTF-8 stream, so an output chunk can end in the middle of a multi-byte character. When the terminal is connected over WebSockets (the default), each chunk was sent as a WebSocket text frame; websocketpp validates outgoing text frames and rejects payloads that are not valid UTF-8, and the returned error was discarded -- so the entire chunk (~1KB, including any valid ASCII coalesced into the same read) was silently dropped. Programs emitting non-ASCII output at volume (modern TUIs, R packages printing Unicode) hit this constantly, producing missing output, overprinting, and cursor desync.

The RPC fallback channel had a milder version of the same defect: each chunk was decoded independently, so a split character rendered as replacement characters at the chunk seam.

## Fix

- Add `string_utils::utf8IncompleteSuffixLength()`, which measures a truncated UTF-8 sequence at the end of a chunk (distinguishing it from genuinely invalid bytes).
- In `ConsoleProcess::enqueOutputEvent`, hold the truncated trailing sequence back (per terminal) and prepend it to the next chunk, so both channels -- and the saved output buffer used for scrollback replay -- always see whole characters.
- In the websocket branch, scrub any genuinely invalid UTF-8 (e.g. non-UTF-8 program output) with `?` instead of letting websocketpp reject the frame, and log `sendText` failures instead of discarding them.
- Drop (with a debug log) held-back bytes that can no longer be completed when the process exits.

## Testing

- New gtest coverage for `utf8IncompleteSuffixLength` (complete text, all truncation lengths for 2/3/4-byte sequences, invalid-but-not-truncated bytes) in `StringUtilsTests.cpp`; full `StringTest` suite passes locally.
- `rsession` builds cleanly.
- The minimal reproduction in the issue (a `U+2500` split across two PTY writes) should be verified manually against this build.

title: Assistant: interleave code and output in `executeCode`
description: ### Intent Up to this point, when the agent runs R code with `executeCode`, we run it all in one go, and then provide all of the output after. This can make it hard to tell which pieces of output came from which code. Instead, we can run the code expression by expression, and then interleave the code and its output in the Assistant UI: Scrolled down a bit: 2/2 of closing https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/issues/1496, the other PR is https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/1577. ### Approach This PR introduces two entry points that we make use of on the Positron side—silent code execution and a hook to see when evaluation of a given expression completes: > In **Positron**, this happens in three steps. Positron gives us the ability to silently execute code, and Ark gives us a entry point (`base::.ark_last_value`) to mark the boundaries between individual expressions. Thus, we: > > 1) Silently execute some code to set up handlers > 2) Execute the code written by the model; task callback fires per expression > 3) Silently execute teardown code ### Automated Tests Adds tests on the R side, but not the C++ side. Tests on the other side of the RPC boundary in https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/1577. ### Checklist - [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` - [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility) - [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list) - [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: update claude.md docs
description:
Documentation-only updates to the project CLAUDE.md files:

- Fix the documented `rstudio-tests` path: the script is generated into `build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests` (from `src/cpp/rstudio-tests.in`), not the repo root.

title: avoid querying github on every save with the air formatter
description:
Previously, `.rs.air.ensureAvailable()` was invoked before every call to Air (i.e. on every save with format-on-save enabled), and in the auto-installed Air case it queried the GitHub releases API every single time just to learn which already-installed version to use -- adding ~600ms (or much worse offline) to every save for a formatter that runs in 5-10ms.

This PR fixes that in two layers:

- **R**: `.rs.air.ensureAvailable()` now prefers the newest already-installed copy of Air under `~/.local/lib/air/` (via a new `.rs.air.installedVersions()` helper), so GitHub is only queried for the latest release when no copy is installed yet. An explicitly-requested `rstudio.air.version` still takes precedence.
- **C++**: a new `modules::air::executablePath()` caches the resolved executable path, so the format-on-save path normally invokes Air without calling back into R at all. The cache revalidates with an exists-check (recovering automatically if the binary is removed) and is invalidated when the `code_formatter` / `use_air_formatter` preferences change.

As discussed in the issue, changing the Air version in use (e.g. via the `rstudio.air.version` option, or by placing a new `air` on the `PATH`) mid-session may require a restart of RStudio to take effect.

Includes testthat tests covering the version discovery/sorting logic and verifying (via a `trace()` that errors if `.rs.air.defaultVersion()` is reached) that no GitHub query occurs when a copy of Air is already installed.

Fixes #17750.

title: use curl binary for air downloads when available
description:
## Summary

The automatic download of the Air formatter could fail on slow connections, because `download.file()` enforces R's `timeout` option (default 60 seconds) as an absolute cap on total download time -- a slow but actively progressing download is killed at the deadline.

This PR changes `SessionAir.R` to:

- Prefer the system `curl` binary for all Air downloads (release metadata and platform binaries). Curl is configured with `--speed-limit 1 --speed-time 60`, so it only aborts after 60 seconds of effective inactivity; an active download is never killed regardless of how long it takes. A nonzero exit raises an R error that includes curl's stderr. All flags used are available since curl 7.7 (2001), so any curl shipped on Windows 10+, macOS, or Linux qualifies.
- Fall back to `download.file()` when curl is not on the PATH, with the `timeout` option raised to `max(300, getOption("timeout"))` for the duration of the call, as requested in the issue.

## Testing

- Exercised the curl helper standalone via Rscript: release metadata download succeeds, a 404 raises an R error, and a real release asset (which redirects through `objects.githubusercontent.com`) downloads and extracts correctly.
- R linter test suite passes (79 PASS, 0 FAIL).
- Manual verification of the in-IDE download path is still advisable on a clean machine.

Addresses #17746.

title: Avoid blocking the Posit Assistant update check on agent stop
description:
## Problem

When an installed Posit Assistant is incompatible with the running RStudio (e.g. the installed `protocol.json` reports protocol `10.0` while RStudio requires `11.0`), opening RStudio with the Posit Assistant pane visible shows "Checking for Posit Assistant installation..." for a consistent ~10 seconds before the "Update Required" view appears. Other manifest-fetch outcomes (fresh install, a compatible update) transition almost instantly.

The delay occurs only when the Posit AI code-completions agent is also running.

## Root cause

The `chat_check_for_updates` RPC keeps the "Checking..." UI up until `onUpdateCheckComplete` finishes. In the unsupported / protocol-mismatch branch it called `stopAgentForUpdate()`, which synchronously waits for the completions agent process to exit.

That completion runs inline within a `ProcessSupervisor::poll()` (the manifest fetch result is delivered on the main thread), so the wait re-enters `poll()` — a no-op under the supervisor's re-entrancy guard — and never observes the agent's exit. `waitFor` therefore exhausts its full 100 × 100 ms (~10 s) budget every time before the RPC resolves.

## Change

- Add a non-blocking `assistant::requestAgentStop()` that terminates the agent and lets normal background polling reap it via `onExit`.
- Use it on the two update-check state-computation paths (`onUpdateCheckComplete` and `resolveWithoutManifestFetch`), which resolve the RPC and must not block the main thread.
- Keep the synchronous `stopAgentForUpdate()` for install and uninstall, which must wait for the agent to release its file handles before overwriting or deleting files on disk.
- Document the blocking/non-blocking contract (and the supervisor re-entrancy footgun) in `SessionAssistant.hpp`.

## Testing

Verified the `rsession` target compiles and links. No automated test is added: reproducing the deadlock requires a full session with a real agent process and the inline-poll manifest delivery, and the `chat_set_update_check_override` automation hook returns before `onUpdateCheckComplete`, so it cannot exercise this path. Manual verification: set `~/.local/share/rstudio/pai/bin/protocol.json` to an unsupported protocol with the Posit AI completions agent running, open RStudio with the Posit Assistant pane visible, and confirm the "Update Required" view now appears without the ~10 s pause.

Addresses #17931

title: Display the Assistant code-suggestions delay field
description: ## Summary In Global Options > Assistant, the numeric "Show code suggestions after keyboard idle (ms)" field was constructed and wired for show/hide but never added to the layout, so it never rendered. The AI completions delay could only be changed via the command palette or by editing preferences directly. This adds the field to the Code Suggestions settings and enforces its bounds now that it is user-editable. ## Changes - Add `nvwAssistantCompletionsDelay_` to the shared settings panel after the completions-trigger selector, and set its initial visibility from the current trigger value (the change handler does not fire until the value changes). Visibility is now maintained by a single `updateCompletionsDelayVisibility()` shared by the initial setup and the trigger selector's change handler. - Enforce the field's 10-5000 range now that it can be edited: - `validate()` rejects an out-of-range value while the field is shown. - The value is clamped at apply time, before `super.onApply()` persists it, so no out-of-range delay can be saved regardless of how the field was hidden (manual trigger) or detached (a different assistant selected). - Harden the shared `NumericValueWidget.validate()`: parse the range check as a long and treat `Integer.MAX_VALUE` as the maximum when none is set, so a digit string that overflows int is rejected with the range error instead of throwing or being silently dropped on apply. ## Tests Playwright coverage in `e2e/rstudio/tests/preferences/global_prefs_panels.test.ts`: - The field renders visible on open for automatic completions (initial layout-time path, no `selectOption`), showing its saved value. - Visibility follows the completions-trigger selector (shown for Automatically, hidden for Manually). - Out-of-range and int-overflowing entries are rejected on apply while the field is shown, including for the no-maximum update-check interval field. - Out-of-range and non-numeric entries are clamped back into range when the field is hidden. - An out-of-range value entered then hidden by switching assistants is clamped before it is persisted. ## Notes Introduced in #16844; discovered during review of #17926. Fixes #17929.

title: Set automation ready flag on re-join after page reload
description:
## Summary

The `--automation-agent` bridge sets `window.rstudio.ready` to `true` only from the `DeferredInitCompletedEvent` handler. That client event (`kDeferredInitCompleted`) is enqueued once per R session in `SessionMain::rSessionInitHook`, not once per client connect, so it does not re-fire on a re-join: a renderer reload that reconnects to a still-running R session which already finished its deferred init. `restoreDefaultPaneAndTabLayoutNoPrompt` is exactly that path -- it saves preferences and then calls `WindowEx.reload()`.

After such a reload `ready` stayed `false` indefinitely, because `ApplicationAutomation` listened for the event but never read the re-join signal. Any Playwright test whose `beforeEach` gates on `window.rstudio.ready` after a reload then timed out (observed in `pane_layout.test.ts`: the first test whose reset runs after a preceding test's `resetUILayout` reload).

## Change

In `registerReadinessHandlers`, after wiring the event handlers, set the ready flag immediately when `sessionInfo.deferred_init_completed` is already `true`. This mirrors how `Packages.java` already handles the re-join case. `initializeAgent` runs inside the post-`ClientInit` callback, so `sessionInfo` is populated at that point.

Fresh start and suspend/resume are unchanged: `deferred_init_completed` is still `false` at this point, so the new check is a no-op and the event handler does the work as before. The change is therefore confined to the re-join path and cannot affect the paths that already work.

Only the automation bridge (`--automation-agent`) is touched; there is no user-facing behavior change, so no NEWS entry.

## Verification

- `cd src/gwt && ant javac` passes.
- roborev review: no issues found.

title: use 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost for viewer pane urls
description:
On RStudio Desktop, the Viewer pane serves session temporary files (plain HTML files and htmlwidgets) directly from R's internal help server, via a URL of the form `http://localhost:<port>/session/<file>`. However, R's help server binds explicitly to the IPv4 loopback address (`Rhttpd.c` calls `startHTTPD("127.0.0.1", port)`), and R's own help URLs use `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...`.

On systems where `localhost` does not resolve to `127.0.0.1` (e.g. resolves only to `::1`, or loopback traffic is intercepted), the Viewer pane's iframe fails to connect and renders blank, while the Help pane continues to work since it is served in-process by the rsession. This change uses `127.0.0.1` directly, matching the URLs R itself generates.

Notes for reviewers:

- `isLocalURL()` in `SessionHelp.cpp` already checks the `127.0.0.1` prefix (before `localhost`), so `browseURL()` interception of help-server URLs is unaffected.
- `url_ports::mapUrlPorts()` is a passthrough in desktop mode, and this code path is desktop-only (`isUsingRHelpServer()` returns false in server mode).
- Also switched the function from `boost::format` to `fmt::format`.

Requires manual verification on a machine where `localhost` resolution is broken; I was unable to reproduce the original failure locally.

Addresses #17579.

title: fix shiny app window becoming unclosable and orphaned
description:
## Problem

With Run App > Run in Window, the Shiny app window could become impossible to close: clicking X grayed the window out (the app was stopped) but the window stayed open, never refreshed on subsequent runs, and could only be removed by quitting RStudio.

Root cause: when a page registers a `beforeunload` handler that prevents unload (e.g. `window.onbeforeunload = function() { return 'Your changes will be lost!'; }`, as the app in #17502 does), Chromium cancels the window close. A regular browser shows a "Leave site?" confirmation in this situation, but RStudio Desktop had no `will-prevent-unload` handler, so the close was cancelled silently -- every time, with no way to override it.

A second bug then orphaned the window permanently: `SatelliteWindow.closeEvent()` unregistered the window from `GwtCallback` during the close *attempt*, so once a close was cancelled, the still-live window could no longer make desktop callbacks. This is the `Received callback desktop_allow_navigation from unknown window` error in the reporter's logs, and why the window stayed gray and could not display a re-run app.

## Fix

- Handle `will-prevent-unload` in `DesktopBrowserWindow`: show a native "Leave page?" confirmation mirroring browser behavior, and force the close if the user chooses Leave. (Chromium does not expose the page's custom `beforeunload` message, so a generic message is the best we can do.) Strings are localized (en/fr).
- Unregister satellite windows from `GwtCallback` only on the `closed` event (window actually destroyed), so a cancelled close no longer orphans the window. This also fixes premature unregistration on the source-window close path when the user cancels an unsaved-changes prompt.
- `RSTUDIO_DESKTOP_IGNORE_BEFOREUNLOAD=1` skips the dialog and forces the close; the e2e harness sets it since automation cannot dismiss native modals.

## Tests

- New desktop unit tests for the `will-prevent-unload` choices (leave/stay/env bypass) and for unregister-only-on-destroy.
- New e2e suite `e2e/rstudio/tests/shiny/shiny-app-window-close.test.ts` (@desktop_only) covering: window closes when the app is stopped, when closed while running, and -- the regression -- when the app's iframe registers a close-preventing `beforeunload` handler. The third test fails without this fix.

Note: if the user chooses "Stay", the app will typically already have been stopped, since the satellite close notification (which stops the app) is sent before Chromium runs `beforeunload`. The window remains open and closable; reordering that is a deeper change to the satellite close protocol left out of scope here.

Fixes #17439.
Fixes #17502.

title: Make the Posit Assistant update check interval a preference
description: Follow-up on #17915, which introduced a hardcoded 24-hour throttle on how often the Posit Assistant downloads `manifest.json` to check for a new version. This makes that interval a user preference and changes the default to **two hours** instead of 24. ## What this does - Adds a `posit_assistant_update_check_interval_hours` integer preference (default 2). It replaces the hardcoded throttle window in `shouldFetchManifest()`. - `0` means "always check" — the manifest is fetched on every check, as it was before the throttle existed. Negative values are not accepted. - Surfaces the preference in two places: - The command palette (any titled preference appears there automatically). - Global Options > Assistant, at the end of the Chat section above the Code Suggestions heading, as a numeric field with a hover tooltip explaining the `0` behavior. ## Implementation notes - The hours-to-seconds conversion lives in a pure helper, `throttle::throttleSecondsFromHours()`, which clamps non-positive input to `0` and caps large values so the seconds count cannot overflow `int`. - The numeric field uses a zero minimum and digit-only input, and the pane's `validate()` rejects a negative value before save. The backend also clamps defensively, so an out-of-range value reaching the session is treated as "always check". - The tooltip string is added to `PrefsConstants` with English and French translations. ## Testing - Unit tests for `throttleSecondsFromHours()` cover the zero, negative, exact-maximum, and overflow boundaries, plus the zero-window "always due" path in `manifestCheckDue()`. - The Options pane field and tooltip were verified by compiling the GWT frontend; the rendered UI needs manual verification. Addresses #17915.

title: Trim manifest-fetch child to utils to cut R startup latency
description:
## What

Follow-up to #17891 / #17896. That work moved the Posit Assistant manifest download into an async `R --vanilla` subprocess to eliminate the Windows `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`. Spawning a fresh R process is now the dominant cost of the fetch: `--vanilla` still loads R's full default package set (`methods`/`stats`/`graphics`/`grDevices`/`datasets`), while the manifest download itself is tiny.

The generated download command only uses `download.file` (from `utils`) plus base builtins (`options`, `tempfile`, `readLines`, `cat`). This forces `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=utils` in the child's environment so it skips loading the rest. `utils` is the complete dependency set regardless of the user's `download.file.method` (the external `wget`/`curl` methods shell out; `libcurl`/`internal`/`wininet` live in base/utils).

## Changes

- `SessionChat.cpp` (`fetchManifestAsync`): pass an environment with `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=utils` to the manifest-download child via the existing `AsyncRProcess::start` environment overload. The child still inherits the parent process environment (proxy vars, `R_LIBS`, etc.); only the default-package list is overridden.

## Measurements

Local Linux, R 4.6.0, full download-command shape using a local `file://` source to isolate spawn cost from network time:

| | mean spawn (n=20) |
|---|---|
| default packages | 148.3 ms |
| `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=utils` | 55.8 ms |

About a 62% reduction in the per-fetch fixed cost. The absolute saving is expected to be larger on Windows, where the skipped package loads are antivirus-scanned. This trims the fixed spawn cost only; it does not change network/DNS/TLS time.

## Testing

- Full backend build (`ninja`) links cleanly.
- Verified end-to-end against `https://cdn.posit.co/posit-ai/manifest.json` with `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=utils`: `download.file` is available, only `utils`/`base`/`compiler` load, and the manifest is returned with exit status 0.

Addresses #17891.
