title: Spell-check headings in source mode (#17568)
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17568.

## Summary

In source mode, real-time spell check did not flag misspelled words inside Markdown, R Markdown, or Quarto headings. The same word in a paragraph was flagged correctly.

`TextFileType.getSpellCheckTokenPredicate()` only accepted tokens whose type matched `\btext\b` or `\bcomment\b`. The body of an ATX heading is tokenized in the `header` state with `defaultToken: "heading"` (see `markdown_highlight_rules.js:340`), and setext underlines produce `markup.heading.N` tokens. Neither matches the predicate, so heading text was filtered out before reaching the spell checker.

The general-purpose `getTokenPredicate()` ten lines above in the same file already handles headings via `reHeaderType_` (`\bheading\b`); the spell-check predicate just wasn't wired up the same way. This adds the heading branch to the spell-check predicate to match.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a `.md`, `.Rmd`, and `.qmd` file in source mode.
- [ ] Type `## weeird` and confirm a spell-check squiggle appears under `weeird`.
- [ ] Type `weeird` in a paragraph and confirm the existing squiggle still appears.
- [ ] Confirm a setext heading underline (`Heading\n=======`) also gets squiggles on misspellings.
- [ ] Confirm headings inside YAML/code chunks are unaffected (no spurious squiggles).
- [ ] Confirm non-Markdown file types (R, C++) still spell-check only comments.

title: Add Playwright workflow for RStudio Server on Ubuntu 24
description:
## Summary

Adds a new GitHub Actions workflow, `test-e2e-rstudio-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml`,
that runs the RStudio Playwright suite against an `rstudio-server` instance
installed on `ubuntu-24.04`. Mirrors the existing Desktop Ubuntu 24 workflow
where possible and diverges where Server requires it.

Server-specific differences from the Desktop variant:

- Resolves the installer from `.products.server.platforms."noble-amd64"` in
  the dailies manifest (vs `.products.electron`). Strips query parameters
  before deriving the local filename so presigned/CDN override URLs install
  cleanly.
- Drops `xvfb` -- Server is browser-driven; Playwright launches its own
  Chromium against `http://localhost:8787`.
- Enables and starts `rstudio-server` after install, runs
  `rstudio-server verify-installation`, and waits up to 60 s for the
  `/auth-sign-in` endpoint to respond before running tests.
- Generates a throwaway test user and password per run via `openssl rand`,
  masks both with `::add-mask::`, creates the user with `useradd` + `chpasswd`,
  and exports `PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_USER` / `PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_PASSWORD` for
  the Playwright fixture. No credentials are stored in the repo or in
  GitHub Secrets -- the user only exists for the life of the runner VM.
- Sets `PW_RSTUDIO_MODE=server`, `PW_RSTUDIO_EDITION=os`, and
  `PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:8787`.
- `timeout-minutes: 120` (matching the macOS 26 data point from the rollout).
- On failure, captures `journalctl -u rstudio-server` and `/var/log/rstudio`
  as artifacts for triage.

Inputs match the Desktop workflow with two changes: the `project` input
defaults to `server`, and `rstudio_extra_args` is dropped (Server has no
equivalent launch flags).

Part of the Playwright workflows rollout (item 15).

title: Audit log direct file downloads from Files pane
description:
## Intent

Addresses [rstudio-pro#9965](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/9965). Open-source counterpart to [rstudio-pro#10912](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/pull/10912), since the change spans open-source code in `src/cpp/session/modules/{SessionFiles,SessionWorkbench}.cpp` plus the GWT Files pane.

## Summary

- Emit a `session_file_download` audit event for user-initiated downloads from the Files pane:
  - `handleFilesRequest` (`/files/<path>`, files in `$HOME`).
  - `handleFileShow` (`/file_show?path=...`, files outside `$HOME`).
- Both handlers log only when the Files pane has signaled an explicit download (binary file click through `BrowserType`). HTML "Show in Browser", Ace-editor link clicks, HTML sub-resources, and other internal `/files/` consumers (`file.show()`, `browseURL`, Sweave, Viewer save-as) are not logged.
- The audit `data` field uses `module_context::createAliasedPath(filePath)` — consistent with the existing download audit calls in the export handlers (which log the raw form-field value); chosen over the raw form value so the resolved `index.html` is captured when a directory is requested, and so paths outside `$HOME` are recorded as absolute.

## Test plan

Run against a Workbench build (audit log is Pro-only). Set `audit-r-sessions=1` in `/etc/rstudio/rserver.conf` and restart `rstudio-server`. OSS builds have no audit-log consumer, so this is the only useful test environment.

**Should log 1 event each:**
- [ ] Click a `.zip` (or other binary) in `$HOME` from the Files pane → 1 event, `data = ~/path/to/file.zip`.
- [ ] Files pane → Go To Folder → `/tmp` → click a binary file → 1 event, `data = /tmp/foo.zip`.
- [ ] Browse to a `/files/<dir>/` containing an `index.html`; the resulting event references the resolved `index.html` path.
- [ ] More → Export... → Download (single file) → 1 event (regression check on existing `/export/` path).
- [ ] More → Export... → Download (multiple files) → 1 event per file.

**Should log 0 events:**
- [ ] HTML "Show in Browser" from Files pane (and the sub-resources of the loaded page).
- [ ] `utils::file.show("~/.Rprofile")`.
- [ ] `browseURL("file://~/some.html")` and the auto-preview after knitting a non-self-contained Rmd in a project.
- [ ] Sweave-compile a `.Rnw` to PDF; preview opens.
- [ ] Viewer → "Save As Web Page" to a path under `~`.
- [ ] Click an Ace-highlighted file URL in a source-code comment.

**Worth eyeballing:**
- [ ] Desktop build (if available): file clicks still open/download; Desktop URLs are `file://` and never go through the session, so 0 audit events regardless.

title: Decouple source-mode spell check from yaml-lint
description:
## Intent

Addresses #15711.

## Summary

Source-mode spell check stops working on Quarto and R Markdown documents when the bundled YAML diagnostics worker fails to respond (e.g. an outdated Quarto installation throwing during init). The lint pipeline made spell-check rendering conditional on yaml-lint resolving, so a hung worker silently suppressed spelling diagnostics for the rest of the session.

This branch decouples the two and tightens the spell-check render path against stale callbacks:

- `LintManager.performRLintServerRequest` now calls `showLint(context, lint)` immediately on R-lint completion. Yaml-lint still runs and merges into a second `showLint` pass when (or if) it returns; if it never returns, no harm.
- The yaml-lint callback skips its second `showLint` when the context's invalidation token is no longer current or the yaml result is empty.
- `showLint` allocates a fresh `finalLint` array and treats the caller's `lint` argument as read-only; spell-check items can no longer leak back into a subsequent yaml-merge pass.
- Each `showLint` invocation captures a generation counter; the async spell-check callback bails out if a later pass has run, or if the lint context has been invalidated by a document edit.

## Test plan

- [ ] Install Quarto 1.6.39 (the version that triggers the original report's `Deno is not defined` worker error). Open a `.qmd` document, type a misspelled word in source mode, and confirm the spelling squiggle appears.
- [ ] With a healthy Quarto install, confirm YAML diagnostics in `.qmd` and `.Rmd` front matter still render as before.
- [ ] In a `.Rmd` document, type quickly to trigger overlapping lint cycles; confirm no duplicate spelling markers and no stale lint persists across edits.
- [ ] Toggle Tools → Global Options → Code → Diagnostics → Show diagnostics for YAML on/off; confirm spell check works in both states.

title: show difftime values in the environment pane
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17556.

`difftime` objects (e.g. the result of `Sys.time() - Sys.time()`) showed an empty cell in the Environment pane. They fell through `valueAsStringImpl` to `NO_VALUE` because they carry attributes (so the atomic-no-attributes branch is skipped) and weren't in the date/time class list at line 134. POSIXct and Date already worked because they were in that list.

## Summary

- Add `"difftime"` to the inherits() class list in `valueAsStringImpl`. Length-1 difftime values now format via `format(val, usetz = TRUE)` (the `usetz` arg is a harmless no-op for `format.difftime`), producing e.g. `"1.5 hours"` or `"-9.5e-07 secs"`. Longer vectors get the `str()` summary, matching POSIXct/Date.
- Add a BRAT test that exercises the formatting path for both scalar `difftime` and `POSIXct` through `.rs.describeObject`.
- NEWS entry under 2026.05.0 "Golden Wattle".

## Test plan

- [ ] Build the session and run `./rstudio-tests --scope rsession --filter test-environment` (or run the new `date/time scalars are formatted in the environment pane` test in BRAT).
- [ ] In RStudio, run `dt <- Sys.time() - Sys.time()` and confirm the Environment pane shows the formatted value (e.g. `-9.5e-07 secs`) rather than an empty cell.
- [ ] Sanity check that `Sys.time()` and `Sys.Date()` values still display correctly (regression check).
- [ ] Try a multi-element difftime (`as.difftime(c(1, 5, 60), units = "secs")`) and confirm it gets a `str()`-style summary.

title: initialize r runtime dispatch before setup_Rmainloop
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17450.

The previous fix (#17452) deferred package hooks but did not address the root cause of the crash on Windows when `Rprofile.site` calls `update.packages()` (or `download.file()` in general). The `download.file` hook in `Hooks.R` is sourced inside `r::session::initialize()`, which runs from `RReadConsole` on the first prompt -- well after `setup_Rmainloop` has executed `Rprofile.site` -- so the hook is not in the failing call chain.

## Root cause

PR #17320 introduced runtime symbol dispatch (`r::runtime::initialize()`) that resolves R API symbols via `dlsym` / `GetProcAddress`. The dispatch entry points look like:

```cpp
SEXP findVarInFrame(SEXP envSEXP, SEXP nameSEXP) {
    return unboundToNull(s_findVarInFrame(envSEXP, nameSEXP));
}
```

The `s_*` function pointers are `nullptr` until `initialize()` runs. `initialize()` was called *after* `setup_Rmainloop`, but `setup_Rmainloop` is what sources `Rprofile.site` -- so any code reached from profile execution that dispatched through `r::runtime` / `r::sexp` would call through a null function pointer and crash with an access violation. This matches the `0x0` termination in the user's `rd_traceback`.

The user's repro (`utils::update.packages()` in `Rprofile.site`) reaches this path via:
- `download.file` -> libcurl
- libcurl -> `R_Busy(0)` / `REprintf(...)`
- `RBusy` / `RWriteConsoleEx` -> `rBusy` / `rConsoleWrite`
- ...callbacks that eventually exercise `r::sexp::findVar` / `getOption` / etc.

## Fix

Move `r::runtime::initialize()` ahead of `setup_Rmainloop()` on both Windows and POSIX. R.dll / libR is already loaded by this point (via `R_DefParams` / `getDLLVersion` on Windows; the process handle on POSIX), so `GetModuleHandle` / `dlopen(nullptr, ...)` succeed.

The one piece of state that previously required post-`setup_Rmainloop` timing was `R_UnboundValue`, which R sets in `InitMemory()` (called from `setup_Rmainloop`). Reading it earlier would capture a null/garbage value. Convert it to address-only resolution (`s_pUnboundValue`) and dereference lazily at use, mirroring the existing `s_pSaveAction` pattern. The address is stable; the value is read at call time, after `InitMemory` has populated it.

The failure branch uses `R_Suicide` rather than `Rf_error`: `Rf_error` longjmps to `R_ToplevelContext`, which is only populated inside `setup_Rmainloop`, so it would be unsafe at the new (earlier) call site.

## Audit of other R-resolved state

Confirmed no other globals in `RRuntime.cpp` need similar treatment:
- All `RS_IMPORT_FUNCTION_*` are function-pointer resolution (code, not data) -- safe pre-init.
- `SaveAction` is already address-based (`s_pSaveAction`).
- `R_NilValue` / `R_MissingArg` referenced inside fallback lambdas are R-linker-resolved globals; the lambdas are only invoked through the dispatch entry points (post-init R state), so the values are valid at call time.
- `INTEGER_OR_NULL` (`SessionEnvironment.cpp`) is a function pointer resolved during module init, well after `setup_Rmainloop` -- unaffected.

## Test plan

The bug only manifests when `Rprofile.site` (or `.Rprofile`) emits console output during startup, so a passing "normal startup" check is not sufficient evidence that the fix works -- the validating test is the original repro from #17450.

**Validates the fix:**
- [ ] On Windows, place the following in `Rprofile.site` and confirm RStudio starts cleanly:
  ```r
  utils::update.packages(ask = FALSE, type = "win.binary")
  ```

**Sanity checks (does the new init order break unrelated paths?):**
- [ ] Normal RStudio session startup on Windows
- [ ] Normal RStudio session startup on macOS
- [ ] Normal RStudio session startup on Linux

**Notes:**
- C++ unit tests (r-scope: 3301 pass, rsession-scope: 180 pass, locally on macOS) do not exercise `runEmbeddedR()` or `r::runtime::initialize()`, so they don't validate the new init order; they serve as a regression check on the surrounding code only.

title: add CMakePresets.json with cross-platform configuration
description:
## Summary

- Adds `CMakePresets.json` at the repo root with a cross-platform `default` preset and a Windows-specific `windows-x64` preset.
- On Windows, the `windows-x64` preset uses `architecture: { value: "x64", strategy: "external" }`, which causes CMake Tools (VSCode) and Visual Studio to source `vcvarsall.bat x64` automatically. This avoids a class of failures where the Ninja CMake cache pins the x86 `cl.exe` (`Hostx64\x86\cl.exe`) while the project compiles with `_WIN64` defined, causing `<atomic>` to reach for `_InterlockedCompareExchange128_nf` (which does not exist on 32-bit targets).
- The `default` preset matches the existing `cmake.generator: "Ninja"` and `build/` conventions already used in `.vscode/open-source/settings.json`.
- The `windows-x64` preset is `condition`-gated on `${hostSystemName}`, so on macOS/Linux only `Default` shows up and behavior is unchanged from the current kits + settings.json flow.
- Picked up automatically by CMake Tools (`cmake.useCMakePresets` defaults to `auto`) and by `cmake --preset` from the CLI. No `.vscode/settings.json` changes required.

## Test plan

- [ ] On Windows: `CMake: Delete Cache and Reconfigure`, then `CMake: Select Configure Preset` -> `Windows x64`. Verify `build/CMakeCache.txt` shows `Hostx64\x64\cl.exe`.
- [ ] On Windows: configure + build from VSCode succeeds without the `_InterlockedCompareExchange128_nf` error.
- [ ] On macOS/Linux: only `Default` shows in the CMake Tools picker. Configure + build behaves identically to the prior kits-based flow.
- [ ] `cmake --list-presets` shows both presets on Windows, only `default` on non-Windows.

title: disable @electron/node-gyp default clangcl toolset on windows
description:
## Intent

`@electron/node-gyp` defaults to selecting the ClangCL platform toolset when generating MSBuild projects for Electron native addons (so that the toolchain matches Electron's own clang-cl-built binaries). Most Windows developers don't have the Clang components of Visual Studio installed, so the default produces a confusing `MSB8020` ("ClangCL build tools cannot be found") failure during `npm install` in `src/node/desktop`.

This adds a project-level `.npmrc` that pins `clang=false`, restoring the standard MSVC v143 toolset for our `desktop`/`dock` native modules.

The `clang` flag only affects the Windows MSBuild generator. On macOS and Linux node-gyp uses the Make/Xcode/Ninja generators, which don't honor this flag, and `binding.gyp` doesn't reference the `clang` variable in any conditions, so this is a no-op on non-Windows platforms.

## Test plan

- [ ] On Windows with VS 2022 Community (no Clang components), `npm install` in `src/node/desktop` completes without `MSB8020` errors.
- [ ] On Windows, generated `build/desktop.vcxproj` contains `<PlatformToolset>v143</PlatformToolset>` (not `ClangCL`).
- [ ] On macOS, `npm install` in `src/node/desktop` still succeeds.
- [ ] On Linux, `npm install` in `src/node/desktop` still succeeds.

title: Add Playwright E2E workflow for Desktop on Windows Server 2025
description:
New GitHub Actions workflow that runs the Playwright E2E suite against RStudio Desktop
on the `windows-2025` runner. Mirrors the existing macOS 26 ARM64 and Ubuntu 24 siblings
so the matrix gains x64 Windows coverage.

Note on the runner choice: we'd prefer Windows 11 x64 to match what most users run, but
GitHub Actions doesn't host a Windows 11 x64 runner -- only `windows-11-arm` exists, and
RStudio Desktop has no ARM Windows build yet. `windows-2025` (Windows Server 2025) is the
closest available stand-in, sharing the same Windows NT 10.0 kernel family and Win32 API
surface as Windows 11. We'll switch to a Windows 11 x64 runner if and when GitHub adds one.

Uses native PowerShell throughout. Auto-resolves the latest daily Windows `.exe` from
`dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/latest/index.json` (override URL also accepted), verifies
SHA-256, silent-installs to `C:\Program Files\RStudio\rstudio.exe`, installs R via `rig`,
sets up R packages from `e2e/rstudio/DESCRIPTION` with caching, and runs `npx playwright test`
with the selected project / grep / test_selector inputs.

Default `timeout-minutes: 120`, matching the macOS 26 sibling.

title: avoid duplicate package state refresh on session startup
description:
## Summary

- The `Packages` presenter previously called `updatePackageState` once from its constructor and registered a `DeferredInitCompletedEvent` handler 2 seconds later. The 2-second delay was meant to ensure the handler was registered after R's deferred init had fired (so a fresh new session got a single refresh), but on slow filesystems the deferred init can take longer than 2 seconds, causing the refresh to run twice.
- Replaces the timer-based heuristic with an explicit signal: a new `deferred_init_completed` flag on `sessionInfo`. The flag is reset in `rInit` and set in `rSessionInitHook`, so it accurately reports whether R's deferred init hook has run for the current R session.
- The `Packages` constructor now registers its handler immediately and only fetches the initial package state itself when re-joining a session whose deferred init has already completed. For fresh starts, suspend/resume, and session restarts the event handler performs the single refresh when the event fires.

## Test plan

- [ ] Start a new R session on a slow filesystem and confirm the Packages pane refreshes only once.
- [ ] Open a second browser tab against an already-running session (re-join) and confirm the Packages pane populates without waiting on a deferred init event.
- [ ] Suspend and resume an R session (server mode) and confirm a single refresh happens after the resume completes.
- [ ] Restart the R session (Session > Restart R) and confirm the Packages pane refreshes once after restart.

title: Fix chat-user-skills afterAll wiping ~/.positai/ via relative-path unlink
description:
## Summary

The `chat-user-skills` test's `afterAll` ran `unlink(".positai", recursive = TRUE)` in R
with a relative path. Since R's cwd defaults to the user home directory when no project is
open, this wiped `~/.positai/` entirely -- including the auth store at
`~/.positai/store/data.json` -- on every test run, signing Posit AI out.

The fix creates a real RStudio project inside the suite sandbox so that:
- The project-level skill lands in `<project>/.positai/skills/` (correct)
- The user-level skill cleanup uses an absolute path (safe)
- The destructive relative-path unlink is removed entirely

Also extracts a shared `utils/project.ts` utility (`createAndOpenProject`,
`waitForSessionRestart`) from `chat-guardrails`, which already had this logic inline.

title: Fix rig install on macOS workflow to use .pkg installer
description:
## Summary

The macOS rig install step in `test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-26-arm64.yml` fetched `rig-macos-arm64-latest.tar.gz`, but rig doesn't ship a macOS tarball -- only a `.pkg` installer. Swapped to downloading the `.pkg` and installing via `sudo installer -pkg ... -target /`, matching what rig documents for macOS.

title: data viewer: add Reset View action to options menu
description:
## Summary

- Adds a "Reset View" item to the options dropdown next to the Refresh button in the data viewer toolbar.
- Selecting it wipes the persisted per-table view state (sort, filters, pinned columns, manual column widths, sidebar visibility) and re-bootstraps the grid so the table renders with defaults.
- The existing Refresh button is unchanged: it still re-fetches data and the round-trip through localStorage preserves view state. Reset View is the explicit opt-in way to start fresh.

## Implementation notes

- `DataViewer.js`: new `window.refreshAndReset` calls the existing `clearSavedState()` (drops the localStorage entry) before `bootstrap()`. `bootstrap()` -> `destroyGrid()` -> `resetGridState()` already clears in-memory state; with localStorage now empty, the subsequent `applySavedState` is a no-op and the grid renders with defaults.
- `DataTable.java`: `refreshAndReset()` mirrors `refreshData()`'s toolbar reset (clears the search widget text, unlatches the filter button) before invoking the JS-side method via a JSNI bridge that matches the pattern already used for `refreshData`/`applySearch`/etc.
- New `MenuItem` is added to `optionsMenu_` above the existing `showSummaryItem_`, with an `addSeparator()` between them. `Reset View` is a per-table action; `Show Summary panel by default` is a global user preference, so the separator marks the conceptual boundary.
- `Reset View` does not touch the `data_viewer_show_summary` user preference (deliberately) since that lives outside the per-table localStorage entry.
- New i18n key `optionsResetView` added in `DataViewerConstants.java` plus English and French properties files.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open the data viewer dropdown next to Refresh; menu reads `Reset View` then a separator then `Show Summary panel by default`.
- [ ] Apply a sort, a column filter, pin a column, drag a column wider; click `Reset View`; sort/filter/pin/width all revert to defaults and the data is re-fetched.
- [ ] Toggle the sidebar off via the sidebar button, click `Reset View`; sidebar reverts to its default visibility.
- [ ] Confirm the "Show Summary panel by default" preference is unchanged after `Reset View`.
- [ ] Confirm clicking the regular Refresh button still preserves view state across the refresh.
- [ ] Verify French locale shows `Réinitialiser la vue` for the menu item.

title: data viewer: show active sort in status bar
description:
## Summary

- Surface the active sort in the data viewer's status bar so users have a persistent reminder of how rows are ordered.
- New text reads `Sorted by: <colname> (ascending|descending)` and is shown only when a sort is active; nothing is shown when unsorted (current behavior).
- Placed on the right side of the status bar, with the existing `Showing X to Y of Z entries` text remaining on the left.

## Implementation notes

- `gridviewer.html`: `#rsGridData_info` now contains two child divs -- `#rsGridData_info_sort` (first in source) and `#rsGridData_info_text`.
- `DataViewer.css`: sort div is `float: right`; text div uses `overflow: hidden` so it forms a new BFC and sits to the left of the float instead of running underneath it. Added `box-sizing: border-box` on the parent so its `padding: 5px` doesn't push the contents past the 100% width.
- `DataViewer.js`: `updateInfoBar` writes to the two child divs separately. `destroyGrid` clears the children rather than setting the parent's `textContent`, which would otherwise delete the children and break the next render.

Single-column sort only -- the underlying sort model is single-column today (`order[0]` in the fetch params), so no multi-column rendering is needed.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a data frame in the data viewer; status bar shows only `Showing X to Y of Z entries`.
- [ ] Click a column header to sort ascending; status bar shows `Sorted by: <name> (ascending)` on the right.
- [ ] Click again to sort descending; right text updates to `(descending)`.
- [ ] Click a third time to clear the sort; right text disappears.
- [ ] Apply a filter that reduces rows; left text shows `(filtered from N total)` and the sort indicator continues to render alongside it.
- [ ] Apply a filter that returns zero rows; both texts behave sensibly (sort still shown when set).
- [ ] Resize the viewer narrow enough that the two texts would overlap; long column names get clipped on the right rather than wrapping under.

title: make data viewer grid a single tabstop
description:
## Summary

- Makes the data viewer grid a single tabstop per the [WAI-ARIA grid pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/). Previously, column headers and pin icons each had `tabindex=0`, so Tab from a body cell visually jumped backwards to the header row -- a WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) violation.
- Tab/Shift+Tab now leave the grid; arrow keys navigate within. From row 0, ArrowUp enters header mode at the same column; ArrowDown returns to the body. Left/Right/Home/End walk between headers.
- Header-mode actions are owned by the grid-level keydown handler: Enter/Space cycles sort, P toggles pin (replacing the per-th and per-pin-icon keydown handlers).
- Screen-reader support via `aria-activedescendant` on `#gridViewport` pointing at the active cell or header (each header has a stable id; the active td's id is re-applied in `buildRow` because rows are recreated on scroll).
- Mouse: clicking a header or pin icon now also focuses the viewport and sets that column as the active header, so subsequent keystrokes route through the grid.

## Notes

- The pin icon is now `aria-hidden` (decorative); pin state is conveyed by the header itself via the existing visual indicator. A follow-up could add a short aria-description on the header announcing the P shortcut and pinned state for AT users.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a data frame in the data viewer.
- [ ] Click a body cell, then Tab -- focus should leave the grid (e.g., to the sidebar toggle), not jump to the header row.
- [ ] Shift+Tab from a cell -- focus should leave the grid backwards (e.g., to the refresh dropdown).
- [ ] From any cell in row 0, press ArrowUp -- the column header outlines and announces.
- [ ] From a header, press Enter or Space -- the column sorts and the header outline persists.
- [ ] From a header, press P -- the column pins/unpins; outline tracks the column to its new position.
- [ ] From a header, ArrowDown -- focus returns to row 0 in that column.
- [ ] Left/Right/Home/End in header mode walk to adjacent / first / last columns.
- [ ] Click a header (sort) or pin icon (pin) with the mouse, then use arrow keys -- nav works without first Tab'ing back into the grid.
- [ ] With a screen reader, Tab into the grid, navigate with arrows, and confirm the active cell / header is announced.

title: data viewer: cache total table width for overscroll calc
description:
## Summary

Cache the total column width (`totalTableWidth`) in `autoSizeColumns` and
`applyResizeDelta`, and read it directly in `applyPinnedColumns` instead
of deriving content width from `table.offsetWidth - paddingRight`.

The derivation was unreliable: with the global `* { box-sizing: border-box }`
rule and the dynamic `paddingRight` we set for horizontal overscroll,
`table.offsetWidth` and the implicit content area diverge in ways that
depend on browser-specific table-layout decisions. Caching the column
sum makes the overscroll calculation a function of saved state rather
than live layout, so it stays consistent across pane resizes regardless
of how the browser reconciles the conflicting layout constraints.

No NEWS entry: this code shipped in #17382 (data viewer rewrite) and has
not been released.

## Test plan

- [ ] View a data frame whose columns extend past the pane width; resize the pane horizontally and verify column widths do not shift
- [ ] View a small data frame that fits the pane; verify no phantom right-padding/horizontal scrollbar appears
- [ ] Pin and unpin columns; verify pinned columns position correctly
- [ ] Manually resize a column via the resizer; verify the table grows/shrinks and pinned-column overscroll updates correctly
- [ ] Toggle the sidebar/filter UI; verify column layout stays stable

title: fix data viewer zebra striping flipping during virtual scroll
description:
## Intent

Fix a regression in the new data viewer where the zebra-striping pattern flips for any given data row as the user scrolls through a virtualized table.

The stripe rule was keyed off `tbody tr:nth-child(odd)`, but the virtualized `tbody` contains a leading spacer row plus only the visible window of data rows. A data row's DOM position is `(r - newStart) + 2`, so the parity for any given data-row index flips with `newStart` as the window slides during scroll.

## Changes

- `DataViewer.js` -- `buildRow` adds an `odd-row` class to data rows when the data-row index `r` is odd, so the stripe key follows the actual row index rather than DOM position.
- `DataViewer.css` -- stripe and hover-stripe rules switched from `:nth-child(odd)` to `tr.odd-row`. The spacer-row override no longer needs `:nth-child(odd)` variants, since spacer rows don't carry the new class.

No `NEWS.md` entry: the data viewer rewrite (#17382 / #17539) ships in the upcoming 2026.05.0 "Golden Wattle" release, so the bug was introduced in unreleased code.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a data frame larger than the viewport (e.g. `View(ggplot2::diamonds)`).
- [ ] Confirm rows alternate stripe/no-stripe consistently from row 0 onward.
- [ ] Scroll down a few full pages and confirm a given row's stripe state never changes as it scrolls in/out of view.
- [ ] Scroll back up and confirm the pattern remains stable.
- [ ] Confirm the row-number column (first column) remains unstriped.
- [ ] Confirm the spacer area at the top/bottom of the virtual scroll still shows the diagonal "loading" gradient and is not striped.
- [ ] Hover a row in both odd and even positions and confirm the hover background paints over the stripe correctly.

title: OS-PR for rstudio/rstudio-pro/pull/9462

title: fix data viewer active-cell outline lingering after focus leaves grid
description:
## Summary

- The data viewer's active-cell outline doubled as the keyboard focus indicator, but the CSS rule applied unconditionally whenever a cell carried the `.activeCell` class.
- After clicking a cell and Shift+Tab'ing out of the grid, the outline lingered, making it look like keyboard focus was in two places at once.
- Scoped the outline to `#gridViewport:focus-within td.activeCell` so it only paints while the grid (or one of its descendants, e.g. an inline filter popup) actually holds focus. The active-cell state is preserved, so the outline reappears at the same cell when focus returns.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a data frame in the data viewer.
- [ ] Click a cell -- verify the blue outline appears.
- [ ] Press Shift+Tab to move focus to the refresh button's dropdown -- verify the outline disappears.
- [ ] Tab back into the grid -- verify the outline reappears at the same cell.
- [ ] Use arrow keys to navigate -- verify the outline tracks the active cell as before.

title: Playwright: reuse local data home and extend debugger test
description:

- `e2e/rstudio/fixtures/desktop.fixture.ts`: stop overriding `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` so test runs share the host's Posit Assistant install and login. The other three RStudio config env vars stay sandboxed. title: rewrite data viewer frontend with vanilla JS
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17539.

## Summary

- Replace jQuery + DataTables + Scroller plugin with a custom vanilla JS grid implementation (~2600 lines replacing ~19600 lines of vendored code)
- Add column summary sidebar with sparkline histograms for numeric columns
- Add virtual scrolling with row caching and async prefetch
- Add sticky column headers and pinnable columns with reordering
- Add custom scrollbars positioned below the header and after pinned columns
- Add auto-sized column widths based on content measurement
- Bump default max display columns from 50 to 200
- Sort indicators and pin icons use mask-image for automatic dark theme support
- Fix latchable toolbar button border shift in themeStyles.css
- No backend or GWT protocol changes -- preserves full window.* API contract

## Test plan

- [ ] `View(mtcars)` -- verify row names display, sort, filter, column resize, sticky header
- [ ] `View(iris)` -- verify factor column filters, sidebar sparklines
- [ ] `View(ggplot2::diamonds)` -- verify virtual scrolling with 53,940 rows
- [ ] `View(as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(100000), nrow=100, ncol=1000)))` -- verify wide dataset with column pagination
- [ ] Pin a column -- verify it moves to the left and sticks during horizontal scroll
- [ ] Toggle sidebar -- verify column summaries with histograms
- [ ] Switch between light and dark themes -- verify all elements theme correctly
- [ ] Test filter UI: numeric range (histogram brush), factor dropdown, text search, boolean
- [ ] Test data import preview (Import Dataset dialog)
- [ ] Test nested viewer links -- click a data.frame or list cell
- [ ] Verify custom scrollbars appear/hide correctly, drag and track-click work

title: Fix uninformative error in `rstudio::sourceMarkers()` when `marker$type` is not a length-one vector
description:
#17527 corrected a bug to have the informative error `Invalid marker type` instead of the syntax error `missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed` when calling `rstudio::sourceMarkers()` with a marker that contains a non-`NULL` but zero-length type (e.g., `character(0)`).

This PR expands on the fix in #17527 , implementing suggestions by @gtritchie (see also #17534):
- Updating the condition `length(marker$type) == 0L` to `length(marker$type) != 1L` ensures that calling `rstudio::sourceMarkers()` with a marker that contains a `type` of length > 1L gives an informative error `Invalid marker type` instead of the syntax error `'length = 2' in coercion to 'logical(1)'`. A test for the informative error message in case of a marker that contains a `type` of length > 1L was added.
- Updating a hardcoded path in the test file that used Windows forward slash to use `file.path()` makes it more portable.
- Added a `NEWS` entry.

title: Add macOS 26 ARM64 Playwright workflow and rename to test-e2e-rstudio-* pattern
description:
## Summary
- Add `test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-26-arm64.yml` mirroring the Ubuntu 24 workflow with macOS-specific install steps (rig arm64 tarball, `.dmg` mount/copy/detach, `xattr -cr` to strip quarantine).
- Rename `playwright-desktop-os-ubuntu-24.yml` to `test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-ubuntu-24.yml`. Display name updated to `Test: E2E Playwright RStudio (Desktop, Ubuntu 24, Open Source)`.
- Update `e2e/rstudio/DESCRIPTION` reference to glob the new file pattern.
- Address PR-review findings: `curl -fLs` on rig install in both workflows so HTTP errors fail loudly. Validate `hdiutil` mount path before `cp` in the macOS workflow.

title: Add `test_selector` input to Ubuntu 24 Desktop Playwright GitHub Actions workflow
description: Adds a `test_selector` input to the GitHub Actions workflow so a manual run can target specific test files or directories without writing a `--grep` regex. Accepts space-separated paths/substrings (e.g. `autocomplete.test.ts`, `tests/panes/misc/`) and is appended as positional args to `npx playwright test`.

title: Show clear message when uninstalling Posit Assistant that is not installed
description:
## Intent

Refinement of [#17322](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17322).

When the user invokes Uninstall Posit Assistant while it is not installed, RStudio previously restarted silently. This branch surfaces a clear message ("Posit Assistant is not installed.") and skips the restart.

## Summary

- `chatUninstallPositAssistant` in `SessionChat.cpp` now distinguishes the env-var, system-level, and not-installed cases and delivers a targeted user-facing message in each. Messages are attached to the JSON-RPC error via `client_info` so the frontend can display them verbatim; `Error::getSummary()` would otherwise wrap the system errno text and obscure the description.
- `ChatPresenter.onError` reads `client_info` from the server error and falls back to `getUserMessage()` when absent.
- The cached install state (`s_updateState`, `s_positAssistantVersion`) is still cleared in the not-installed branch so a directory removed out-of-band does not leave stale in-memory state.

## Test plan

- [ ] With Posit Assistant not installed, invoke Uninstall Posit Assistant: dialog shows "Posit Assistant is not installed." and the IDE does not restart.
- [ ] With `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` set to an existing directory and no user-data install, invoke Uninstall: dialog shows the env-variable-install message.
- [ ] With a system-level install in `xdg::systemConfigDir()` and no user-data install, invoke Uninstall: dialog shows the administrator-install message.
- [ ] With a normal user-data install, invoke Uninstall: behaves as before (uninstall + restart).

title: Posit Assistant: ui/previewUrl JSON-RPC method
description:
## Intent

## Summary

- Validation lives in two pure helpers in `chat/ChatConstants.{hpp,cpp}` (`isValidPreviewUrlScheme`, `isValidPreviewUrlHeight`) with 15 new gtest cases. The handler delegates to the existing `module_context::viewer()`, which already handles server-mode port mapping and fires the `kViewerNavigate` client event -- no GWT changes needed.
- This PR is the RStudio side only; wiring a `previewUrl` method through `JsonRpcUIService` in Posit Assistant is tracked separately: https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/issues/1243

## Test plan

The full round trip won't work until the change in https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/issues/1243 lands and a new Posit Assistant build is installed. Until then:

- [ ] Confirm the 15 new `IsValidPreviewUrlScheme` / `IsValidPreviewUrlHeight` gtest cases pass under `./rstudio-tests --scope rsession`.
- [ ] With any build of Posit Assistant connected, confirm `ui/previewUrl` appears in the `protocol/getVersion` capabilities list.
- [ ] `rstudioapi::viewer("http://localhost:4321")` from the R console (against a running Shiny app) still navigates the Viewer pane correctly -- exercises the same `module_context::viewer()` path the new handler delegates to.
- [ ] With a Posit Assistant build that calls `ui/previewUrl`: send `{ "url": "http://localhost:4321" }` and confirm the Viewer pane navigates; send `{ "url": "http://localhost:4321", "height": -1 }` and confirm it maximizes.
- [ ] Same Posit Assistant build: send a malformed request (`{}`, `{ "url": "file:///tmp/x.html" }`, `{ "url": "HTTP://example.com" }`, `{ "url": "...", "height": "tall" }`, `{ "url": "...", "height": -5 }`) and verify rsession returns a JSON-RPC `Invalid params` error with a clear message in each case.

title: Fix Windows installer File Version mismatch
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17128.

## Summary

The Windows installer's **File Version** field on `setup.exe` shows an unrelated number (e.g. `5997.5.0.0` for the 2026.05 release) while **Product Version** correctly shows `2026.05.0.0`.

`VIProductVersion` in `package/win32/cmake/modules/NSIS.template.in` was using `CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MAJOR_NUMERIC`, which concatenates the major and minor components (e.g. `2026` + `05` = `202605`). Each component of `VIProductVersion` must fit in 16 bits (max 65535); `202605` overflows and is truncated to `5997`. Since no `VIAddVersionKey "FileVersion"` was set, NSIS used the truncated binary value as the displayed File Version.

`MAJOR_NUMERIC` was introduced in 2021 (commit `6dc06a46b95`) when `CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MAJOR` contained `%Y-%m` and NSIS rejected the dash. Today `MAJOR` is just the year (e.g. `2026`), so it fits in 16 bits and can be used directly.

## Changes

- `VIProductVersion` now uses `CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MAJOR` directly (year-only) so all four components stay within NSIS's 16-bit-per-component limit.
- Added an explicit `VIAddVersionKey FileVersion` so the displayed File Version is set deterministically rather than depending on NSIS's fallback.
- NEWS.md entry under `### Fixed`.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified locally with a test package build that File Version and Product Version on `setup.exe` now match.

title: add headless runner for standalone HTML test pages
description:
## Intent

The standalone HTML test pages under `src/gwt/test/` (`autoindent_test_cpp.html`, `autoindent_test_r.html`, `highlight_test_cpp.html`, `highlight_test_sql.html`) verify acesupport indent and highlight behavior by driving a real Ace editor in the browser, but they were never wired into any automated test run. As a result they had bit-rotted -- each page had at least one missing or stale `<script>` import that prevented the harness from running at all when opened directly.

This PR adds a small headless runner so these pages stay green automatically.

## Summary

- **New runner package** at `src/gwt/test/runner/` (Node + Playwright). On `npm ci`, Playwright's `postinstall` downloads its bundled chromium for the host OS, so the runner works on macOS/Linux/Windows without depending on a system Chrome.
- **`runner.mjs`** spins up an in-process HTTP server pointing at `src/gwt/`, navigates each test page in headless chromium, waits for the page to populate `#passed` / `#failed` spans, and aggregates per-page results. Captures uncaught page errors and 4xx responses so silent regressions (like the missing imports below) become visible.
- **`ant testpage`** target wires the runner into the build (chained from `ant test`). `ant unittest` is unchanged for fast iteration.
- **Page fixes uncovered while bringing the runner up:**
  - `autoindent_test_cpp.html` and `autoindent_test_r.html` were missing `yaml_highlight_rules.js` and `colors.js` imports that newer code in `utils.js` and `r_highlight_rules.js` depends on -- the pages errored out at script load.
  - `autoindent_test_r.html` referenced `tools/ace/build/src/keybinding-vim.js`, which doesn't exist; corrected to the in-tree `keybinding-vim.js` next to `ace-uncompressed.js`.
  - `highlight_test_cpp.html` referenced a deleted `background_highlighter.js`.
  - `highlight_test_cpp.html` and `highlight_test_sql.html` reported results by appending free-form text to the body. Normalized them to expose the same `#passed` / `#failed` contract the autoindent pages already use, giving the runner one shape to detect.
  - `autoindent_test_cpp.html` previously sourced ace from the gitignored `tools/rstudio-ace/` bundle; switched to the in-tree `ace-uncompressed.js` the other three pages already use, so the runner works in fresh worktrees without building the upstream Ace fork.
- **CLAUDE.md** updated to mention the new `ant testpage` and `ant test` chain.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd src/gwt && ant testpage` from a clean checkout: 596 / 596 pass across the 4 pages.
- [x] `npm ci` followed by `node runner.mjs` works directly (without ant) -- useful for tight iteration on a page.
- [x] `cd src/gwt && ant unittest` still passes 462 / 462 (untouched).
- [ ] Reviewer confirms `ant testpage` works on Linux and Windows (Playwright bundles its own chromium per-OS, so it should -- but worth a sanity pass).

## Notes

- Overlaps with #17516 (the C++ reindent fix), which separately adds the same `yaml_highlight_rules.js` + `colors.js` imports to `autoindent_test_cpp.html`. Whichever lands second will get a trivial 3-way merge -- the imports are byte-identical lines.
- The runner is deliberately minimal (~150 lines, no test framework on top of Playwright). Each page is the unit; pass/fail aggregation lives on the page side. If we want richer per-test-case reporting later, we can move to `@playwright/test` -- but for now this matches the existing in-page harnesses.

title: fix double-increment in spell-check suggestion loop
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17530.

## Summary

In `TextEditingTargetSpelling.injectContextMenuHandler()`, the loop that builds spelling-correction menu items advances `i` twice per iteration: once in the `for` header and once explicitly at the bottom of the loop body. With `MAX_SUGGESTIONS = 5`, this means only the suggestions at indices 0, 2, and 4 are added before the cap kicks in -- so the menu shows at most 3 items, and every other suggestion in the response is silently skipped.

The bug was introduced in #9161 (April 2021) when realtime spellchecking was migrated off Typo.js, so it has shipped in every release since.

The fix removes the redundant `i++` in the loop body.

## Test plan

- [ ] Right-click a misspelled word that has 5+ suggestions (e.g. a common typo) and confirm the context menu shows up to 5 distinct suggestions, in order, instead of every other one.
- [ ] Confirm that selecting any suggestion still applies the replacement and clears the spelling marker as before.
- [ ] Sanity-check the cap by right-clicking a word with many suggestions and confirming the menu does not exceed 5 items.

title: fix C++ reindent over-indenting after brace-less control flow body
description:
## Intent

Addresses #4402.

## Summary

- In C++ files, "Reindent lines" misindented the line following a brace-less control-flow body. For example, in
  ```cpp
  for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++)
    if (i == 4) {
      printf("in the loop");
    }
    printf("not in the loop");   // wrongly indented to match the `if`
  ```
  the trailing `printf` was placed at the `if`'s indent instead of the surrounding (`for`) context.
- The token walker in `cpp_code_model.js#getNextLineIndent` already had a `startValue !== ";"` fall-through for `for`/`while`/`do`/`try`, but (a) it didn't fall through on `}` (closed body) and (b) the analogous `if`/`else` rule had no fall-through at all, so it always returned the inner keyword's indent.
- Extended both rules to also fall through on `}`, mirroring the equivalent R-side fix from #7930 (commit `da52b5af39`). When the start token indicates we walked back from the end of a statement (either `;` or `}`), the body is complete, so the walker continues to find the surrounding context.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd src/gwt && ant unittest` passes (462/462).
- [x] `src/gwt/test/autoindent_test_cpp.html` passes 396/396 (added 4 new regression tests covering `for`+`if{}`, `for`+`while{}`, `if`+`if{}`, and `while`+`for`+`if{}`).
- [x] Manual repro from the issue indents correctly in C++ mode.
- [ ] Verify in Reviewer's local build that nothing else regresses (open a representative C++ file, run "Reindent lines" over a substantial selection).

## Notes

- The HTML test page was missing two `<script>` imports (`yaml_highlight_rules.js`, `colors.js`) that newer code in `utils.js` and `r_highlight_rules.js` depends on -- fixed alongside, otherwise the page can't run at all.
- Typing `{` directly after a closed brace-less control-flow body still shows the same surface symptom (handled separately by `getRowForOpenBraceIndent` for open-brace auto-outdent). That's a separate code path; the new tests skip the `open-brace` state via `open-brace-skip` and the issue at hand (Reindent Lines) is fully addressed by this change.

title: fix npe in spell-check marker invalidation
description:
## Summary

The predicate passed to `docDisplay_.removeMarkers` in `TextEditingTargetSpelling.invalidateAllWords()` guards `a != null` but then calls `a.text().toLowerCase()` without null-checking the result of `text()`. `AceAnnotation` is a `JavaScriptObject` overlay whose `text()` returns the raw `this.text` property, which can be `null` or `undefined` for annotations that don't carry one. When `invalidateAllWords()` runs and encounters such an annotation, the predicate blows up.

This surfaces in the server log as something like:

```
ERROR CLIENT EXCEPTION (rsession-...): (TypeError) : can't access property "toLowerCase",
  asNativeString__Ljava_lang_String$NativeString___devirtual$_0_g$(...) is undefined
  ...
  toLowerCase__Ljava_lang_String___devirtual$_0_g$
  ...
  test_84_g$
  ...
  removeIf_1_g$
  removeMarkersImpl_0_g$
```

The fix null-checks `a.text()` before lower-casing.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a project with documents that trigger spell-check; switch the dictionary language (Tools > Global Options > Spelling) and confirm the markers refresh without raising a `TypeError` in the server log.
- [ ] Exercise any code path that produces non-spellcheck Ace annotations (e.g. lint output, debug breakpoints) and then call something that invokes `invalidateAllWords` (toggling spell-check, dictionary change). Confirm no `toLowerCase` error appears.

- **OS**: `desktop` filters OS-only tags by `os.platform()`; `server` hardcodes `@windows_only|@macos_only` (server always targets Linux).

description:
## Summary

Adds a manually-triggered GitHub Actions workflow that runs RStudio Playwright Desktop tests on Ubuntu 24, plus a `DESCRIPTION` file listing R packages the tests rely on.

The workflow installs the latest noble-amd64 daily `.deb` (or a user-supplied URL) with SHA-256 verification, sets up R via [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig), installs R packages with `pak::local_install_dev_deps()` from [P3M](https://packagemanager.posit.co/) (precompiled Linux binaries), then runs Playwright under `xvfb` at 1920x1080. Test reports upload as artifacts on every run.

Triggers are `workflow_dispatch` + `workflow_call` only -- nothing runs automatically on commits or PRs. A future umbrella workflow can call this one when CI on PRs is wired up.

Inputs (all optional with sensible defaults):
- `rstudio_installer_url` -- override the auto-resolved latest daily (generic name so per-platform sibling workflows can share the same input shape)
- `r_version` -- rig spec, defaults to `release`
- `project` -- Playwright project, defaults to `desktop-os-linux`
- `grep` -- Playwright `--grep` filter

First runs are expected to be red because tests requiring Posit AI / Copilot credentials will fail without auth wired up. Follow-up PRs will add tags or skip guards based on what the first run surfaces.

title: preserve browser state across continuation prompts in the debugger
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17481. Two related debugger regressions introduced by #17288, both surfacing as "the debug UI doesn't appear when the debugger is activated":

1. **Top-level breakpoints** (e.g. via `debugSource()`) never showed the highlight or call stack at all.
2. **Multi-line input at the `Browse[N]>` prompt** could clear the captured browser context, freezing the debug UI for the rest of the session.

## Summary

### Top-level breakpoints (`isBrowseActive()` excluded `R_GlobalEnv`)

`isBrowseActive()` in `RSession.cpp` required the captured browser env to be `!= R_GlobalEnv`. For top-level debugging the script is evaluated in `globalenv()`, so the inject's `parent.frame()` correctly captures `R_GlobalEnv` — and the check then rejected the legitimate state. `onConsolePrompt` took its `if (*pContextDepth == 0 && !s_browserActive) return;` early-return path before firing `kContextDepthChanged`, so the client never saw the debug context.

The right invariant is "env was captured" (non-nil), not "env is non-globalenv". `R_GlobalEnv` is a perfectly valid captured env when debugging at the top level of a sourced script.

### Multi-line input at the Browse prompt

Continuation prompts (`+ `) share the `hist == 1` path with fresh REPL prompts in `RReadConsole`, so they were calling `setBrowserActive(false)` between every line of a multi-line expression at the Browse prompt. That cleared the captured `s_browserEnv` and stuck the cached `s_browserActive` (SessionEnvironment side) at `FALSE`, which in turn could prevent `onConsolePrompt` from firing a fresh `kContextDepthChanged` after the multi-line eval finished (the change-detection conditions all read equal because nothing had legitimately changed during the continuation detour).

A continuation prompt does not change which REPL we're in (browser or top-level), so the cached state from the prior fresh prompt should be preserved. We now detect continuation prompts via `getOption("continue")` and skip the `setAtTopLevelPrompt` / `setBrowserActive` updates in that case. This also tightens the `atTopLevelPrompt` semantics from #17352: continuation-while-in-browser now correctly reads as *not* at top level.

## Test plan

Manual:

- [ ] **Top-level**: open a script (e.g. `x <- 1; y <- 22; print(x + y)`), set a breakpoint on line 2, run `Source` (or `debugSource()`). Confirm the debug highlight appears at line 2 and the debugger toolbar is enabled. Pre-fix this never worked.
- [ ] **Function-level + multi-line paste**: `f <- function() { browser(); 1 + 1 }; f()`. At `Browse[1]>`, paste a multi-line `local({ … })` block. Confirm the highlight and call stack remain visible across the paste, and that `n` continues to step correctly.
- [ ] **`.rs.isBrowserActive()` parity**: at any Browse prompt (top-level or function-level), `.rs.isBrowserActive()` returns `TRUE`. Pre-fix it returned `FALSE` for top-level and could read `FALSE` mid-multi-line.

Automated coverage in `test-automation-debugger.R`:

- [ ] Multi-line paste at Browse prompt asserts `.rs.isBrowserActive()` is `TRUE` mid-eval and `.ace_executing-line` survives the paste.
- [ ] Top-level breakpoint via `sourceActiveDocument` asserts `.ace_executing-line` appears at the breakpoint line.

title: encode user-provided strings in data import preview/import code
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17510.

## Summary

`assembleDataImport()` and its helpers build R source code by string concatenation, then later pass that source through `eval(parse())`. Several inputs to that pipeline -- column names, column parse formats, character options, locale option values, and import URLs -- originate outside the session and were spliced in via hand-rolled `paste("\"", x, "\"", ...)` (or no escaping at all). Values that contained R-syntactically-significant characters (`"`, `\`, newlines, control chars) could either break parsing or, in the column-name and import-URL cases, inject a top-level call.

This PR routes every such value through `encodeString(x, quote = "\"")` before splicing, in `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionDataImportV2.R`:

- Column names (`columnDefinitionsReadR` branch).
- `format = "..."` strings for `col_date()` / `col_time()` / `col_datetime()` (the `levels = ...` factor branch is intentionally left alone -- it splices raw R code, not a string literal).
- `"character"` option-type branch (e.g. `na`, `delim`, `quote`, `comment`).
- `"locale"` option-type branch (character-typed `locale()` arguments such as `tz`, `encoding`).
- `cacheUrlName <- "<url>"`, `cacheVariableName <- "<dataName + ext>"`, and `cacheVariableName <- "<localFile>"` in `cacheCodeFromOptions`.

title: enable mathjax safe extension to block javascript: hrefs
description:
## Intent

Addresses an internal security report: MathJax 2.7.9 ships in RStudio without the `Safe` extension, so `\href{javascript:...}{...}` inside a `.Rmd` file produces a clickable anchor in the IDE's same-origin DOM. A user clicking that link runs attacker JavaScript in the session origin, which can then call any RPC the user is authorized to call (including code execution).

## Summary

- Add `Safe.js` to the IDE's MathJax extensions list (`MathJaxLoader.java`). Covers the visual editor and the source-mode inline math preview.
- Inject a `text/x-mathjax-config` block enabling Safe in `mathjax.html` (HTML preview) and `presentation/mathjax.html` (slide preview).
- Inject the same block in `MathjaxFilter::substitute` whenever the rmarkdown loader marker is rewritten, so rendered Rmd output served by the session also runs Safe. Refactored the existing Windows-desktop-only `kQtMathJaxConfigScript` injection so the two config blocks coexist cleanly.

The Viewer pane's iframe is unsandboxed for local URLs (`ViewerPane.java:454-456`), so HTML preview / presentation / rendered Rmd all share the IDE origin and need the same treatment as the IDE itself.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an `.Rmd` containing `$\href{javascript:alert(1)}{x}$` in the visual editor: rendered link's `href` should be empty (Safe strips it); clicking does nothing.
- [ ] Same payload with the source-mode inline math preview enabled.
- [ ] Knit the `.Rmd` to HTML and verify the rendered Viewer iframe is also neutralized.
- [ ] Render an `.Rpres` with the same payload and view in the Presentation pane.
- [ ] Sanity check: ordinary math (`$\frac{1}{2}$`, AMS environments, `\boxed`, etc.) still renders normally in all four contexts.

title: Trash-aware delete confirmation in the Files pane
description:
## Intent

Addresses #3780.

When the system-trash preference is enabled on RStudio Desktop, the Files pane now confirms with wording that matches what the backend will actually do, and a trash failure no longer silently falls back to a permanent delete.

## Changes

- **Trash-aware confirmation message.** When `Desktop.isDesktop() && delete_to_trash` is true, the prompt becomes "Are you sure you want to move `foo.R` to the Trash/Recycle Bin?" In all other cases (Server, Workbench, or Desktop with the pref off) the existing "permanently delete ... This cannot be undone" wording is preserved. The combined "Trash/Recycle Bin" phrasing matches the existing pref label. French translations updated.
- **No silent fallback to permanent delete.** `SessionFiles.cpp::deleteFile` previously fell back to `filePath.remove()` when `recycle_bin::sendTo()` failed. That would have destroyed the file the user expected to be recoverable, contradicting the new prompt. The error now propagates back to the client and the file stays on disk.
- **Friendlier error message on trash failure.** Instead of the raw "system error N (Operation not permitted)", users see the failing file's name and the underlying error, e.g.:

  > Could not move "foo.R" to the Trash/Recycle Bin.
  >
  > system error 1 (Operation not permitted)

  For multi-file deletes, the prefix becomes "One or more of the selected files could not be moved to the Trash/Recycle Bin." (the backend bails on the first failure, so we don't track which one).

## Test plan

- [x] `cd src/gwt && ant javac` passes
- [x] `cmake --build . --target rsession` passes
- [ ] Server build: confirm the dialog still says "permanently delete ... This cannot be undone"
- [ ] Desktop with `delete_to_trash` off: same as Server
- [ ] Desktop with `delete_to_trash` on, single-file delete: dialog says "move ... to the Trash/Recycle Bin?" and the file ends up in the system trash
- [ ] Desktop with `delete_to_trash` on, multi-file delete: dialog uses "the N selected files" phrasing
- [ ] Force a trash failure on each platform and confirm: error dialog names the file, includes the OS error, and the file remains on disk:
  - **macOS**: `touch /tmp/trashtest.R && chflags uchg /tmp/trashtest.R`, then delete from the Files pane. Cleanup: `chflags nouchg /tmp/trashtest.R && rm /tmp/trashtest.R`.
  - **Linux**: `mkdir /tmp/locked && touch /tmp/locked/test.R && chmod a-w /tmp/locked`, then delete `test.R` from the Files pane (the rename out of the locked directory fails). Cleanup: `chmod u+w /tmp/locked && rm /tmp/locked/test.R && rmdir /tmp/locked`.
  - **Windows**: `echo. > C:\Temp\trashtest.R && icacls C:\Temp\trashtest.R /deny "%USERNAME%:(D)"`, then delete from the Files pane (delete permission is denied on the file). Cleanup: `icacls C:\Temp\trashtest.R /remove:d "%USERNAME%" && del C:\Temp\trashtest.R`.

title: reduce package pane refresh overhead
description:
## Intent

Addresses rstudio/rstudio-pro#10771.

## Summary

Two changes that both cut work triggered by Packages pane refreshes, especially noticeable with large libraries or slow filesystems (e.g. NFS):

- **Scope the `install.packages()` hook before/after scan.** The hook used to diff `file.info()` across the entire library to identify which packages were installed or updated. It now scopes the scan to the requested packages plus their dependency closure (derived from the user's `dependencies` argument), which is an upper bound on what `install.packages` can touch. Also threads a single `available.packages()` lookup through to `recordPackageSource` so we don't fetch it twice.
- **Tighten the console-prompt package-command detection.** The previous `boost::algorithm::contains` check would fire on any input containing substrings like `install`, `update`, or `remove`. It now uses a compiled regex that requires an opening `(` after the identifier, eliminating false positives like `updates <- c(1, 2)` and `installed.packages()` while still catching base R, devtools/remotes, pak, pacman, and renv entry points.

Related OSS issue on the broader "slow with many installed packages" theme: #17392.

## Test plan

Manual verification done so far:
- [x] R parse check of `Tools.R`; `rsession` C++ build clean.
- [x] Helper-function behavior confirmed: `get("dependencies", envir = environment(), inherits = FALSE)` correctly resolves the default NA and explicit `TRUE` / character-vector / unrelated-arg cases after `formals(hook) <- formals(original)`.
- [x] Regex verified with 18 positive and 11 negative R expressions.

Still to do (tests to be added in follow-up commits on this branch):
- [ ] Automated test for the scoped `install.packages` hook (single-pkg install, multi-pkg install, `dependencies = FALSE`, `dependencies = TRUE`).
- [ ] Automated test for the tightened `onConsolePrompt` detection.
- [ ] End-to-end smoke test: install a package and confirm the Packages pane repopulates with correct state and `RemoteRepos` annotations.

title: preserve browser state across continuation prompts in the debugger
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17481. Two related debugger regressions introduced by #17288, both surfacing as "the debug UI doesn't appear when the debugger is activated":

1. **Top-level breakpoints** (e.g. via `debugSource()`) never showed the highlight or call stack at all.
2. **Multi-line input at the `Browse[N]>` prompt** could clear the captured browser context, freezing the debug UI for the rest of the session.

## Summary

### Top-level breakpoints (`isBrowseActive()` excluded `R_GlobalEnv`)

`isBrowseActive()` in `RSession.cpp` required the captured browser env to be `!= R_GlobalEnv`. For top-level debugging the script is evaluated in `globalenv()`, so the inject's `parent.frame()` correctly captures `R_GlobalEnv` — and the check then rejected the legitimate state. `onConsolePrompt` took its `if (*pContextDepth == 0 && !s_browserActive) return;` early-return path before firing `kContextDepthChanged`, so the client never saw the debug context.

The right invariant is "env was captured" (non-nil), not "env is non-globalenv". `R_GlobalEnv` is a perfectly valid captured env when debugging at the top level of a sourced script.

### Multi-line input at the Browse prompt

Continuation prompts (`+ `) share the `hist == 1` path with fresh REPL prompts in `RReadConsole`, so they were calling `setBrowserActive(false)` between every line of a multi-line expression at the Browse prompt. That cleared the captured `s_browserEnv` and stuck the cached `s_browserActive` (SessionEnvironment side) at `FALSE`, which in turn could prevent `onConsolePrompt` from firing a fresh `kContextDepthChanged` after the multi-line eval finished (the change-detection conditions all read equal because nothing had legitimately changed during the continuation detour).

A continuation prompt does not change which REPL we're in (browser or top-level), so the cached state from the prior fresh prompt should be preserved. We now detect continuation prompts via `getOption("continue")` and skip the `setAtTopLevelPrompt` / `setBrowserActive` updates in that case. This also tightens the `atTopLevelPrompt` semantics from #17352: continuation-while-in-browser now correctly reads as *not* at top level.

## Test plan

Manual:

- [ ] **Top-level**: open a script (e.g. `x <- 1; y <- 22; print(x + y)`), set a breakpoint on line 2, run `Source` (or `debugSource()`). Confirm the debug highlight appears at line 2 and the debugger toolbar is enabled. Pre-fix this never worked.
- [ ] **Function-level + multi-line paste**: `f <- function() { browser(); 1 + 1 }; f()`. At `Browse[1]>`, paste a multi-line `local({ … })` block. Confirm the highlight and call stack remain visible across the paste, and that `n` continues to step correctly.
- [ ] **`.rs.isBrowserActive()` parity**: at any Browse prompt (top-level or function-level), `.rs.isBrowserActive()` returns `TRUE`. Pre-fix it returned `FALSE` for top-level and could read `FALSE` mid-multi-line.

Automated coverage in `test-automation-debugger.R`:

- [ ] Multi-line paste at Browse prompt asserts `.rs.isBrowserActive()` is `TRUE` mid-eval and `.ace_executing-line` survives the paste.
- [ ] Top-level breakpoint via `sourceActiveDocument` asserts `.ace_executing-line` appears at the breakpoint line.

title: enable tcp keepalive on accepted connections
description:
### Intent

Partial mitigation for [rstudio/rstudio-pro#10805](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/10805) — `rserver` accumulates thousands of stuck proxied websocket connections in production, eventually OOMing.

### Approach

Enable `SO_KEEPALIVE` on accepted sockets in `AsyncServerImpl::handleAccept`. Without it, when a peer disappears without sending FIN/RST (e.g. browser tab hibernation, NAT timeout, laptop sleep, network change without graceful close), the half-open TCP socket on the server side lingers indefinitely. With keepalive on, the OS will probe the peer after the kernel-configured idle period (Linux default ~2h) and close the socket if it's truly gone.

This is one half of a two-part fix. The complementary change — an application-level idle timer in `SocketProxy` so we don't have to wait for the OS keepalive — will come as a follow-up. That follow-up will also need a config option for the timeout and so warrants separate review.

The change uses the non-throwing `error_code` overload of `set_option`, so it won't throw in the accept hot path. For non-TCP protocols (Unix domain sockets used by some internal listeners) the syscall either succeeds as a no-op or returns a benign error that we log at DEBUG level.

### Customer relevance

Customer reports `num active: 3704` connections frozen on a leaking pod (vs. 5–7 on a fresh pod). The frozen-but-high count is consistent with stuck websockets that have no path to closure: the server-side `SocketProxy::close()` only fires on a read/write error or session invalidation, and with no keepalive on, ghosted peers never produce a read/write error.

### Automated Tests

Not practically testable by unit tests — the change is observed only on connections whose peer has disappeared without sending FIN/RST.

### QA Notes

- Build and run rserver as usual.
- On Linux, on an accepted connection: `ss -tn -o state established '( sport = :8787 )'` and check the `keepalive` indicator in the timer column. With this change, TCP keepalive should be on for accepted client connections.
- Prior behavior: a hibernated browser tab leaves an idle ESTABLISHED connection on rserver indefinitely. New behavior: the connection is reaped when the kernel keepalive sequence completes (default ~2h on Linux).

### Documentation

NEWS.md entry added under "Fixed" (`Server: Enable TCP keepalive on accepted connections...`).

title: Disable GWT Super Dev Mode redirect hook in production desktop builds
description:
## Intent

Addresses #12235.

## Summary

The new window opened by Session > New Session takes ~4s longer to reach `dom-ready` than the first launch. The delay comes from the GWT bootstrap (`rstudio.nocache.js`): its Super Dev Mode redirect hook calls `sessionStorage.setItem` during startup, and in the spawned Electron child that call contends with the parent's Session Storage LevelDB lock for ~4s before timing out.

The redirect hook is only useful for the Super Dev Mode workflow, which has its own GWT module (`RStudioDesktopSuperDevMode`). Setting `devModeRedirectEnabled=false` on the production `RStudioDesktop` module makes the linker emit an empty fragment in place of `DevModeRedirectHook.js`, so the production bootstrap no longer touches `sessionStorage`.

## Verification

- Rebuilt `rstudio.nocache.js` against the `RStudioDesktop` module (`ant gwtc -Dgwt.main.module=org.rstudio.studio.RStudioDesktop`).
- `grep -c sessionStorage` on the resulting `rstudio.nocache.js` returns `0` (was `2` previously).
- Related dev-mode constants (`_gwt_dummy_`, `__gwtDevModeHook`, `Ignoring non-whitelisted`) are also absent from the output.

## Test plan

Note that this may be a non-determistic change depending on platform, phase of the moon, colour of your socks, etc. On my Mac dev machine, it was a consistent ~4 second improvement in startup time.

- [ ] Build a packaged desktop install (`make-package --install --arch=arm64 --build-dmg=0`) and confirm Session > New Session no longer pauses ~4s before the new window paints.
- [ ] Confirm `ant desktop` (Super Dev Mode against `RStudioDesktopSuperDevMode`) still works, since that module is unchanged.

title: Add deeper git clone before checkout.
description:

### Intent

title: fix TypeError on ace editor attach by lifting pref bind() out of varargs
description:
## Summary

Fixes a `(TypeError) : handler.execute is not a function` thrown from `Prefs.JsonValue.bind()` on the synchronous initial `handler.execute(getValue())` call when an `AceEditorWidget` attaches to the DOM.

## Cause

In `AceEditorWidget.attachImpl()`, two `pref.bind(new CommandWithArg<...> { ... })` calls were inlined as arguments to a long variadic `aceEventHandlers_.add(addEventListener(...), addEventListener(...), ..., bind(...), bind(...))` literal alongside many other `CommandWithArg`-bearing expressions. That shape — multiple `CommandWithArg`-bearing arguments mixed into a single varargs literal that also contains a `bind()` call — triggers a GWT compiler optimization quirk that produces a JS callsite where the handler object's `execute` method has been pruned/renamed away, causing a runtime `TypeError`.

The bug was introduced by #17012 (`Fix AceEditor subsystem lifecycle across detach/re-attach cycles`), which moved the pref bindings from `onLoad()` into the new `attachImpl()` method and changed `aceEventHandlers_` to use the variadic `HandlerRegistrations.add(HandlerRegistration...)` form.

## Fix

Lift the two `bind()` calls out of the varargs literal into their own `HandlerRegistration` local variables, and pass those locals into `aceEventHandlers_.add(...)` like any other registration. Each `bind()` call is now type-checked in isolation before its result becomes part of the variadic array, sidestepping the optimizer issue without changing semantics.

A code comment documents the rule (don't put `bind()` calls inline alongside other `CommandWithArg`-bearing arguments in a single varargs `add()` literal) for future contributors.

I scanned the rest of the repo for the same pattern; no other call sites are at risk. Other `bind()` usages either stand alone, sit in their own one-argument `add()`, or are the sole argument to a `new HandlerRegistrations(...)` constructor.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cd src/gwt && ant javac` — compiles cleanly
- [ ] `cd src/gwt && ant draft` — produces runnable JS
- [ ] Open RStudio Server in a browser, open a source file, confirm no `TypeError` is logged and tab-key behavior + scroll-speed pref both still drive the editor
- [ ] Toggle "Use Tab key to move focus" in Global Options and confirm the editor reflects the new value live

title: avoid hang when tab-completing inside [ on sparse matrices
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17440.

## Summary

Tab completion inside `x[, ...]` fell through to `.rs.getNames(x)` for S4 matrix-like objects (e.g. Matrix-package `dgCMatrix`), because `is.array()` returns `FALSE` for them. `.rs.getNamesImpl()` then called `vapply(x, ...)` to collect element labels, which coerces `x` to a list of length `prod(dim(x))` -- hundreds of millions of elements for a realistic sparse matrix -- and exhausts system memory.

Two fixes:

- Guard the label-collection `vapply` in `.rs.getNamesImpl()` with `is.list(object)` so non-list objects are never iterated element-wise. The label attribute pattern only makes sense for lists (data frames, labelled columns); iterating element-wise on anything else is at best wasted work and at worst catastrophic.
- Widen the dimnames branch in `.rs.getCompletionsSingleBracket()` to use `!is.null(dim(object))` instead of `is.array(object)`, so matrix-like S4 objects get proper column-name completion via `dimnames()`.

## Test plan

- [ ] With the reproducer from #17440 (30000 x 10000 `dgCMatrix`), press Tab inside `m[, cel]` and verify the session does not hang or blow up RAM
- [ ] Assign `colnames(m) <- c("cell1", "cell2", ...)` and verify Tab completion inside `m[, ce]` now offers matching column names
- [ ] For a regular base-R matrix with `dimnames`, confirm completion still offers row/column names as before
- [ ] For a data.frame, confirm column-name completion and labels still work

title: fix startup hang when _quarto.yml exists in large projects
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17176.

## Summary

- When a project contains `_quarto.yml`, RStudio calls `quarto inspect` on the project directory at startup to resolve the project type. This spawns a synchronous subprocess that scans the entire directory tree, causing the IDE to hang indefinitely for projects with large directories (e.g. `_targets/` or raw data folders with 1M+ files).
- Replace the `quarto inspect` call with direct YAML parsing: builtin types are used as-is, and custom extension types are resolved by reading the small `_extension.yml` file instead of scanning the whole project.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a Quarto project with a standard type (`website`, `book`, `manuscript`, `default`) and verify startup behavior is unchanged
- [ ] Open a Quarto project with a custom extension type (e.g. `type: posit-docs`) and verify the base type is correctly resolved
- [ ] Open a Quarto project with a large directory tree (e.g. containing `_targets/` with many files) and verify startup is no longer slow

title: Fix AceEditor subsystem lifecycle across detach/re-attach cycles
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17009.

## Summary

Pane layout changes trigger `BinarySplitLayoutPanel.setWidgets()`, which removes and re-adds child widgets — including `AceEditor` instances — to the DOM. The `AttachEvent` handler was tearing down 8 subsystems on detach but only restoring 3 on re-attach, permanently breaking code completion, diagnostics, link detection, background highlighting, and more.

- Give each subsystem an idempotent `attach()`/`detach()` pair
- Have `AceEditor` drive them from its `AttachEvent` handler
- Stop destroying state (nulling references) on detach so subsystems can restart

### Subsystems fixed

- **AceEditorMonitor** — DPI monitoring
- **AceEditorMixins** — Linux Desktop selection handler
- **AceBackgroundHighlighter** — chunk background highlighting
- **BackgroundTokenizer** — scope tree tokenization
- **DiagnosticsBackgroundPopup** — lint/diagnostics hover popups
- **AceEditorBackgroundLinkHighlighter** — clickable link detection
- **CompletionManager** hierarchy — code completion (Ctrl+Space, tab, auto-popup)
- **Keyboard handlers** — `updateKeyboardHandlers()` now called on re-attach (guarded by `fileType_ != null`)

## QA Notes

1. Open a source file, change pane layout, verify: code completion (Ctrl+Space), diagnostics popups, link highlighting (Cmd/Ctrl hover), keyboard shortcuts
2. Repeat layout changes multiple times — verify no degradation
3. Test with R Markdown in Visual mode — verify chunk editor shortcuts still work
4. Test Console editor — verify completion and shortcuts survive layout changes

title: preserve hard file limit when raising soft limit in rsession
description:
## Intent

Addresses review feedback on #17409 ([review](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/17409#pullrequestreview-4094290675)) that landed after the original PR was merged.

## Summary

- The single-argument `setResourceLimit(FilesLimit, newLimit)` overload sets **both** the soft and hard limits to `newLimit`. On systems where the hard limit is much higher than 4096 (common on Linux — e.g. 1048576), the merged change irreversibly lowered the hard limit. Since rsession runs as a non-root process, it cannot re-raise its hard limit afterward, and child processes inherit the lowered cap. Switch to the two-argument overload (`newLimit, hard`) so we only raise the soft limit and preserve the existing hard limit.
- Add a warning log when `getResourceLimit()` fails (was silently dropped), matching the pattern already used in `ServerMain.cpp`.

## Test plan

- [ ] rsession builds cleanly on Linux, macOS, and Windows
- [ ] On Linux, confirm the debug log message still appears when the soft limit is raised
- [ ] Confirm the hard limit is preserved (e.g. `prlimit -p \$(pgrep rsession) -n` shows hard limit unchanged)

title: raise open file descriptor limit in rsession startup
description:
## Intent

Addresses #16067.

## Summary

- Raise the `RLIMIT_NOFILE` soft limit to `min(4096, hard)` early in rsession startup, before the file monitor is initialized. This mirrors what rserver already does in `ServerMain.cpp`.

The default soft limit for desktop Linux sessions is typically 1024. On some systems (reported by multiple users on Tuxedo laptops with Ubuntu), this is too low — rsession's existing fd usage from R libraries, sockets, config files, etc. leaves insufficient headroom for `inotify_init()`, which fails with `EMFILE` (errno 24, "Too many open files") and disables project file monitoring.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify rsession builds cleanly on Linux, macOS, and Windows
- [ ] On Linux, confirm the debug log message appears when the limit is raised (`Raised open file limit from ... to ...`)
- [ ] Confirm project file monitoring works normally after the change
