title: Add support for partitioned cookies (CHIPS) on port-token cookie
description:
## Intent

Addresses issue 5 of https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17423.
Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17430.

Adds support for the `Partitioned` cookie attribute ([CHIPS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Privacy/Privacy_sandbox/Partitioned_cookies)) to all `SameSite=None; Secure` cookies. When RStudio Server is embedded in a cross-origin iframe (e.g., a portal or LMS) with `www-same-site=none`, browsers that enforce third-party cookie restrictions (or users who opt into blocking them) will reject these cookies unless they carry the `Partitioned` attribute — breaking sign-in, CSRF validation, and port-mapped content.

## Approach

- Added a `partitioned_` member to `core::http::Cookie` with getter/setter, emitting `; Partitioned` in the `Set-Cookie` header value.
- In `Response::addCookie()`, automatically set `Partitioned` on any cookie with `SameSite=None` and `Secure`. This covers all cookie-setting call sites (auth, CSRF, port-token, etc.) without requiring per-site opt-in.
- The legacy cookie copy (with `SameSite=Undefined`) explicitly clears `Partitioned`, since CHIPS requires `SameSite=None; Secure`.

## Automated Tests

No automated tests — this requires a cross-origin iframe environment with third-party cookie restrictions enabled to verify.

## QA Notes

See https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17423.

## Documentation

No documentation changes needed. This is an internal cookie attribute change that requires no user-facing configuration.

title: Add SHA-256 integrity verification for Posit Assistant package downloads
description: ### Intent Addresses posit-dev/assistant#1079 Adds SHA-256 integrity verification for Posit Assistant package downloads, ensuring that downloaded packages have not been corrupted or tampered with before installation. If the sha is missing from the manifest: If the sha is invalid: ### Approach - The manifest now includes an optional `sha256` field per protocol version entry. This hash is parsed during update checks and stored in `UpdateState`. - Before installing a downloaded package, the SHA-256 of the file is computed and compared against the expected hash from the manifest. - If the hash is missing from the manifest or does not match, installation is refused and the temporary file is cleaned up. - The manifest parsing (`getPackageInfoFromManifest`) and hash verification (`verifyPackageSha256`) logic is extracted into a separate `ChatIntegrity` module (`chat/ChatIntegrity.hpp/.cpp`) to enable unit testing. ### Automated Tests 15 unit tests added in `ChatIntegrityTests.cpp` covering: **`verifyPackageSha256`** (5 tests): - Matching hash succeeds - Case-insensitive hex comparison (uppercase hash) - Mismatched hash returns error - Non-existent file returns error - Binary content is handled correctly **`getPackageInfoFromManifest`** (10 tests): - Basic parsing with sha256 - Works without sha256 output param (nullptr default) - sha256 is empty when manifest omits it - Selects highest minor version within same major - Ignores different major versions - Errors when no compatible version found - Skips non-HTTPS URLs - Errors on missing "versions" field - Errors on invalid protocol version string - Errors on null output pointers ### QA Notes > Ensure you have updated the QA Notes in the original issue. ### Documentation No documentation changes needed — this is an internal integrity check with no user-facing configuration. ### Checklist - [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` - [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility) - [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list) - [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: deliver Posit Assistant auth token via HTTP-only cookie in server mode
description:
### Intent

Deliver the Posit Assistant auth token via an HTTP-only cookie instead of a URL query parameter in server mode, preventing credential leakage in browser history, server access logs, and the `Referer` header.

Addresses Issue 3 of rstudio/rstudio#17423.

### Approach

- Added `setChatBackendAuthToken()` to `ChatStaticFiles` so the static file handler has access to the current auth token.
- When serving `index.html` in server mode, the handler now sets an HTTP-only, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (`posit-assistant-auth`) containing the token.
- On the frontend (`ChatPresenter.java`), the auth token URL parameter is now only appended in Desktop mode (`Desktop.hasDesktopFrame()`). In server mode, the browser automatically sends the cookie with subsequent requests.
- The token is cleared from `ChatStaticFiles` when the backend stops, matching the existing cleanup in `clearChatBackendPort()`.

### Automated Tests

No automated tests added. This is a transport-layer change for an unreleased feature; manual QA covers verifying the cookie is set in server mode and the URL parameter is absent.

### QA Notes

1. **Server mode**: Open Posit Assistant, verify the chat iframe loads. Inspect the network tab — `index.html` response should include a `Set-Cookie: posit-assistant-auth=...` header with `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`. The iframe URL should **not** contain an `authToken` query parameter.
2. **Desktop mode**: Open Posit Assistant, verify the chat iframe loads. The iframe URL **should** contain the `authToken` query parameter (no cookie).
3. Verify chat functionality works end-to-end in both modes.

### Documentation

No documentation changes needed — this is an internal implementation detail.

title: Show web socket connection errors in Posit Assistant pane
description:
## Intent

Addresses issue 6 of #17423: no user-visible error on WebSocket connection failure.

When the Posit Assistant WebSocket connection fails or enters a silent reconnect loop, users see a dead chat pane with no explanation. This PR adds a notification bar that surfaces connection errors to the user.

## Approach

The assistant iframe tracks consecutive WebSocket reconnect failures and notifies the RStudio parent frame via `postMessage` (a browser-internal channel unaffected by network issues). RStudio shows a non-destructive notification bar with "Restart" and "Dismiss" buttons — the iframe stays alive so reconnection can still succeed. When the connection recovers, the assistant sends an `assistant-connected` message and the notification auto-dismisses.

**Assistant side** (posit-dev/assistant#1069):
- `websocket-backend.ts`: Tracks `reconnectFailures` counter. After 3 consecutive failures, sends `{ type: 'assistant-error', message }` to the parent frame. On reconnect, sends `{ type: 'assistant-connected' }` to dismiss the notification. Uses `window.location.origin` (not `*`) for `postMessage` target.
- `rstudioBackend.ts`: Overrides `handleAuthExpired()` to notify the parent on auth token expiry.

**RStudio side** (this PR):
- `ChatPane.java`: Listens for `assistant-error`, `assistant-warning`, and `assistant-connected` postMessages (with source + origin validation). Shows connection errors as a notification bar using the existing notification infrastructure. Hides on `assistant-connected` or restart.
- `ChatPresenter.java`: Observer callbacks `onIframeError()`, `onIframeWarning()`, `onIframeConnected()`. Error shows the notification bar; connected hides it; restart dismisses it before starting the restart flow.

**Interaction with existing crash handling:** When the backend process crashes, both `ChatBackendExitEvent` and the iframe's reconnect failure notification may fire. The crash handler calls `showCrashedMessage()` which replaces the iframe entirely, taking precedence over the notification bar. No conflict.

## QA Notes

**Repro (connection failure):**
1. Open chat, find the backend port: `ps aux | grep "dist/server/main.js"`
2. Block the port: `sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport <port> -d 127.0.0.1 -j REJECT`
3. Refresh the page and open the chat pane
4. After ~3 seconds, a notification bar should appear: "Unable to connect to Posit Assistant. Retrying..."
5. Unblock: `sudo iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp --dport <port> -d 127.0.0.1 -j REJECT`
6. Notification should auto-dismiss when connection recovers

**Verify no regression:**
- Normal startup: no notification should appear
- Backend crash (`kill <pid>`): existing crash handler should still show "Process Exited" with restart button

## Automated Tests

No automated tests — the notification requires simulating WebSocket connection failures which is not covered by existing test infrastructure.

## Documentation

No documentation changes needed — this is an internal UX improvement for error feedback.

title: Add support for www-frame-origin option to control CSP frame-ancestors
description:
## Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17423 (Issue 4).

When RStudio Server is embedded in a cross-origin iframe (e.g. portal deployments), the Posit Assistant chat pane fails to load because its CSP `frame-ancestors` directive is hardcoded to `'self'`. This PR forwards the existing `www-frame-origin` server option into the session so the chat pane's CSP respects the admin's configured framing policy.

## Approach

The server already has a `www-frame-origin` option that controls `X-Frame-Options` and CSP for the main GWT page. This change:

1. Adds a hidden `session-www-frame-origin` session option (schema + generated code) to receive the value from rserver.
2. Forwards the value from `ServerSessionManager` when launching sessions.
3. Uses the forwarded value in `ChatStaticFiles.cpp` to build the `frame-ancestors` directive, mapping the same keyword vocabulary (`none`, `same`, `any`, or a specific origin URL) to valid CSP syntax.

The server option is always authoritative — it overrides any `frame-ancestors` value from the bundled `csp.json`, so admin configuration cannot be silently ignored.

## Automated Tests

No automated tests added. The CSP construction logic operates on internal cached state that is not easily unit-testable without refactoring. The change was verified manually in an embedded iframe deployment.

## QA Notes

Configure `www-frame-origin` in `rserver.conf` and verify the chat pane loads correctly:
- `www-frame-origin=none` → chat pane should deny all framing (`frame-ancestors 'none'`)
- `www-frame-origin=same` (or unset) → chat pane allows same-origin framing (`frame-ancestors 'self'`)
- `www-frame-origin=any` → chat pane allows all origins (`frame-ancestors *`)
- `www-frame-origin=https://portal.example.com` → chat pane allows self + that origin

## Documentation

No documentation changes needed. The `www-frame-origin` option is already documented in the Admin Guide; this change makes the chat pane respect it consistently.

title: fix Connect Cloud republish failing with parse error
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17306.

## Summary

- Quote and escape the `appId` parameter in the R expression constructed for `rsconnect::deployApp()`, fixing Connect Cloud republish which uses UUID content IDs that cause R parse errors when inserted unquoted
- Add consistent spacing after commas in the generated R expression

## Details

The R command constructed in `SessionRSConnect.cpp` for deploying content inserted `appId` as a bare value (`appId = <value>`). This works for numeric IDs (Connect, ShinyApps.io) but fails for Connect Cloud, which uses UUID-style content IDs (e.g. `550e8400-e29b-41d4-a716-...`). Unquoted, R's parser chokes on UUID segments like `41d4` — `41` is parsed as a number and `d4` as an adjacent symbol with no operator between them, producing `Error: unexpected symbol`.

The `appId` was the only parameter in the `deployApp()` call not wrapped in single quotes. Now it is quoted and escaped like all other string parameters. Verified in the `rsconnect` package source that `appId` is never type-checked as numeric — it's used only in string comparisons against deployment records and in URL path construction, so passing it as a character string is safe for all publish targets.

title: fix Connect Cloud republish losing previously-used title
description:
Addresses #17306

## Intent

Fixes republishing to Connect Cloud when the title was changed from the default filename-based title.

## Summary

When republishing a document to Connect Cloud after changing its title on the first publish, the deploy dialog would:
- Briefly show the correct (previously-used) title
- Revert to the filename-based title
- Treat the republish as a new deployment rather than an update

**Root cause:** `setPreviousInfo()` fetches the app by its known ID, then routes the result through `onAppsReceived_` which compares `info.getName()` against the local deployment record name. The Connect Cloud content API doesn't return a `name` field in its response, so this comparison always fails, triggering `forgetPreviousDeployment()`.

**Fix:** When the app is successfully found by ID, call `showAppInfo()` directly instead of routing through the name-matching callback. The name comparison is only needed when searching a list of apps by name (the `getRSConnectAppList` path).

Also fixes `AppNameTextbox.setDetails()` which called `setTitle()` (sets the HTML tooltip attribute) instead of `setText()` (sets the visible text content).

## QA Notes

1. Publish a `.qmd` document (e.g. `yoyo.qmd`) to Connect Cloud, **changing** the title from the default to something else (e.g. "momo")
2. Republish — the dialog should show the previously-used title "momo" and republish as an update to the same content
3. Verify that the default case (publishing without changing the title, then republishing) still works

title: Suspected typo in `r-ldpath.in`
description:
At the least this would be unfortunate naming, but I believe this may actually be a typo.

### Intent

Without this change, it seems that `R_HOME` is not set when calling `$RHOME/etc/ldpaths` which means that the system path `/lib` (instead of `$R_HOME/lib`) gets included in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` when opening a terminal. On most systems this probably has no impact, but we install RStudio under Gentoo Prefix which breaks in this case.

### Approach

I don't pretend to understand the codebase, but the change is tiny, and not exported. It does fix the problem that I have experienced.

### Automated Tests

No additional tests. I did note that the real value of `$R_HOME` is prepended to what is returned by `$RHOME/etc/ldpaths` which I suspect is a workaround for the fact that the correct path to `$R_HOME/lib` was not returned. With this change that path is now duplicated.

### QA Notes

title: dismiss chat readline notification when console input is received
description:
## Intent

## Summary

- Added a new `kConsoleReadCompleted` client event, fired from `rConsoleRead()` whenever console input is received. - Fixed stale `atTopLevelPrompt` state in `processPendingExecution()`: code executed by the chat backend that called `readline()` left this flag as `false`, causing `reissueLastConsolePrompt()` to fire with `busy=true` and the notification to persist indefinitely.

## Test plan

title: fix C++ code completion when CXX_STD >= CXX20
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17159.

## Summary

- In R 4.4+, the default `CXX` variable embeds a standard flag (e.g. `-std=gnu++17`), so `R CMD SHLIB` output contains both the default and the package-requested standard (e.g. `-std=c++20`). This caused `extractStdArg()` to pick the wrong (first) flag, building the precompiled header with C++17 while the translation unit was parsed with C++20 -- producing a fatal PCH mismatch error.
- Fix by deduplicating `-std` flags after assembling compilation args, keeping only the last one (matching compiler "last flag wins" semantics).
- Add `USE_CXX20` / `USE_CXX23` env vars for packages using `SystemRequirements: C++20` or `C++23` in DESCRIPTION.
- Fix a latent bug in `SourceIndex.cpp` where the C vs C++ std flag filtering conditions were always true/false (no-op), so C-only std flags were never removed from C++ compilations.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an R package with `CXX_STD = CXX20` in `src/Makevars` and verify C++ code completion works
- [ ] Open an R package with `CXX_STD = CXX17` and verify code completion still works (regression check)
- [ ] Verify precompiled headers are built with the correct standard (check `clang_verbose` output)

title: suppress errors in get_help RPC handler
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17156.

## Summary

- Wrap the `get_help` RPC handler in a `tryCatch` so that errors during help retrieval (e.g. `tools:::httpd()` failing with "cannot open the connection") silently return no result rather than surfacing an error dialog

A previous fix (c826ce0d4d) added error suppression for the `getHelpColumn` code path specifically, but the same class of error can occur through any path that reaches `tools:::httpd()` — including `getHelpFunction`, `getHelpArgument`, `getHelpDataFrame`, etc.

**Note:** This fix is speculative. We haven't been able to reproduce the issue locally, but the error in the report (`Error in file(out, "wt") : cannot open the connection`) points to a failure inside R's help rendering system that we should be resilient to.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify autocomplete help tooltips still work normally
- [ ] Verify that if `tools:::httpd()` errors, the tooltip is simply not shown (no error dialog)

title: disable debugger during environment pane object inspection
description:
## Intent

Addresses #16987.

## Summary

- When stopped at a breakpoint inside an S3 method (e.g. `[[.some_class`), the Environment pane refresh calls `.rs.describeObject()`, which can dispatch to the same method via `str()`, re-triggering the breakpoint and creating infinite recursion.
- Add `.rs.withDebuggerDisabled()`, which temporarily sets `tracingState(FALSE)` and `debuggingState(FALSE)` to suppress both `trace()`-injected breakpoints and `debug()`-based stepping during evaluation.
- Wrap the dispatch-prone paths in `describeObject()` and `getObjectContents()` with this guard.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a new R script with the reproducer from #16987

- [ ] Verify the debugger stops at the breakpoint without freezing R
- [ ] Verify the Environment pane displays correctly while in the browser
- [ ] Verify stepping through and exiting the browser works normally
- [ ] Verify that breakpoints still work normally for functions that are *not* called during environment inspection

title: sync clamped editor width when margin column changes
description:
## Intent

## Summary

## Details

`syncEditorWidth()` was only called on ACE render-finished events, so changing the margin column preference updated the print margin position in ACE but never triggered a recalculation of the editor's `maxWidth`. description:
## Intent

Addresses #17369.

## Summary

In packaged builds, the What's New iframe content opened in the system browser instead of rendering inside the dialog. The universal build (`--arch=x86_64,arm64`) is unchanged.

title: use GetModuleHandle for R.dll symbol resolution on Windows
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17341.

## Summary

- The runtime dispatch layer (`r::runtime::initialize()`) used `LoadLibraryEx("R.dll")` on Windows to obtain a handle for symbol resolution. This fails when R.dll is not on the DLL search path, which can happen when launching from Electron.
- Since R.dll is already loaded into the process by the time `initialize()` runs (after `setup_Rmainloop()`), use `GetModuleHandle("R.dll")` instead. This mirrors the POSIX approach of using `dlopen(NULL)` to resolve symbols from the already-loaded process image.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify RStudio Desktop starts successfully on Windows with a standard R installation
- [ ] Verify runtime dispatch functions (closure accessors, findVar, etc.) work correctly after startup

title: avoid crash when environment pane inspects S4 objects with broken packages
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17353.

## Summary

- When the Environment pane calls `.rs.describeObject()` on S4 objects whose defining package isn't loaded, operations like `length()`, `is()`, and `str()` trigger S4 method dispatch, which calls `.requirePackage()` to load the namespace and its native DLL. If the DLL is broken (e.g. missing entry point), Windows terminates the process with `STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND` (`0xC0000139`) before R's `tryCatch` can intervene.
- Added an early check in `.rs.describeObject()` that detects S4 objects with unloaded package namespaces using only safe attribute reads (`isS4()`, `class()`, `attr()`, `isNamespaceLoaded()`), and returns a minimal description that avoids all S4-dispatching operations.
- Affected objects are displayed as `Formal class 'Foo' [package "bar" not loaded]` with deferred contents.

## Test plan

description:
## Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17350.

## Summary

- The `isAtTopLevel()` replacement for `globalContext().nextcontext()` in f016ddbe returns false during continuation prompts (`+ ` != `> `), causing the notebook queue to defer indefinitely instead of sending the next line of a multiline expression.
- Skip the deferral guard in `NotebookQueue::process()` when in continuation mode, since R is waiting for input, not executing code.
- Add automation test for multiline chunk execution with both incomplete-expression (`1 +\n2`) and open-paren (`sum(1,\n2)`) cases.

- [ ] Verify chunks with errors still halt as expected

title: add r-max-connections session option
description:
## Intent

Adds an `r-max-connections` setting for `rsession.conf`, allowing administrators to configure the maximum number of R connections.

## Summary

- Wires the option through `ROptions` → `runEmbeddedR` → `structRstart.nconnections`
- Uses runtime detection: the `structRstart` is zero-initialized before `R_DefParams`; R >= 4.4.0 populates `nconnections = 128`, older R leaves it as `0`. This distinguishes support without version string parsing.
- On Windows, adds the `nconnections` field to the custom `RStartup` struct (occupies alignment padding on 64-bit, no offset shift)
- Logs a warning if the option is configured but the running R version doesn't support it

## Test plan

title: Replace R-internal locale2charset() with core::system::currentCharset()
description:
## Summary

R's `locale2charset()` is declared in `Defn.h` (an internal header, not part of the public API) and is being removed in the next R release. RStudio accessed it via `extern "C"` forward declarations from three session files.

All call sites only called `locale2charset(nullptr)` to get the charset name for the current `LC_CTYPE` locale. This PR replaces those calls with a new cross-platform utility function `core::system::currentCharset()`.

## Implementation

### POSIX (Linux, macOS)
- Uses `nl_langinfo(CODESET)` from `<langinfo.h>`
- Handles macOS quirk where `CODESET` returns `""` for UTF-8 locales
- Normalizes glibc's `ANSI_X3.4-1968` to `ASCII`

### Windows
- Parses the codepage from `setlocale(LC_CTYPE, NULL)`
- Detects UTF-8 variants (`utf-8`, `utf8`, codepage 65001)
- Returns `CPnnn` format for numeric codepages (iconv accepts these directly)

### Differences from R's locale2charset
- Does not replicate R's codepage 1252 → `ISO8859-1` mapping (CP1252 is a superset of ISO-8859-1, and `iconv` accepts `CP1252` directly)
- Does not include the large locale-name-to-charset lookup table (unnecessary since we only query the current locale, not arbitrary locale strings)

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `core/include/core/system/Locale.hpp` | New header |
| `core/system/Locale.cpp` | New implementation |
| `core/CMakeLists.txt` | Added `Locale.cpp` |
| `session/SessionClientInit.cpp` | Replaced `locale2charset` usage |
| `session/SessionContentUrls.cpp` | Replaced `locale2charset` usage |
| `session/modules/SessionSource.cpp` | Replaced `locale2charset` usage |

description:
## Intent

Addresses #17333.

## Summary

- The publishing wizard crashes with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" when publishing Quarto documents with Quarto v1.9. Quarto v1.9 now returns project metadata for standalone `.qmd` files, causing `_quarto.yml` (and potentially other non-existent resources) to be added to the deployment file list. `file.info()` returns `NA` sizes for these missing files, which propagates through `sum()` and crashes the `if` condition in `rsconnectDeployList`.

- Add a regression test that stubs `quartoFileProject` to return a non-existent resource and verifies `docDeployList` returns a valid `totalSize`.

title: replace compile-time R_VERSION checks with runtime symbol dispatch
description:
## Intent

Replace compile-time `R_VERSION` checks with runtime `dlsym`-based dispatch so that
the version of R used at compile time need not match the version loaded at runtime.

## Summary

- Add `RRuntime.hpp` / `RRuntime.cpp`: a dispatch layer that imports R API symbols via
  `dlsym` at startup and routes calls to the best available implementation
- Import symbols at runtime: `FORMALS`, `BODY`, `CLOENV`, `R_ClosureFormals`,
  `R_ClosureBody`, `R_ClosureEnv`, `R_ParentEnv`, `R_getVarEx`, `R_GetBindingType`,
  `R_DelayedBindingExpression`, `R_findVarLocInFrame`, `PRCODE`, `PRENV`, `PRVALUE`,
  `Rf_findVarInFrame`, `Rf_findVar`, `R_UnboundValue`
- Replace all `#if R_VERSION` blocks in `RSexp.cpp` with `r::runtime::` calls
- Replace `R_UnboundValue` with `nullptr` across the codebase (imported once in
  `RRuntime.cpp`, converted at the `findVar`/`findVarInFrame` boundary)
- Replace `R_TrueValue` / `R_FalseValue` (non-API globals) with `Rf_ScalarLogical`
- Replace `R_Visible` (non-API global) with `withVisible()` in `RSessionState.cpp`
- Replace `R_NamespaceRegistry` with an R helper `.rs.getNamespace()`
- Replace `R_NaReal` with `NA_REAL`
- Consolidate SEXPREC struct definitions into `RSexpInternal.hpp`
- Rewrite `r-api-report` script in R (replaces fragile bash/curl with git clone)

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify RStudio starts and basic functionality works with R 4.4, 4.5, and 4.6
- [ ] Verify environment pane correctly displays bindings (active, promise, normal)
- [ ] Verify variable lookup (`findVar`, `findVarInFrame`) works in console and completions

title: Fix notebook preview-on-save BRAT test
description:
## Intent

Addresses #15925.

## Summary

Fixes the "saving a notebook with preview on save does not call source()" BRAT test and re-enables it in CI.

The test targeted `#rstudio_cb_source_on_save`, which resolves to the outer GWT `CheckBox` wrapper (`<span>`), not the inner `<input>` element. The `.checked` property is undefined on `<span>` elements, causing `dom.isChecked()` to return a zero-length value. The test also used a fragile `js.querySelector` + `clickElement` toggle that never verified the resulting checkbox state, and relied on a fixed `Sys.sleep(2)` to wait for notebook output.

Changes:
- Target `#rstudio_cb_source_on_save input` to reach the actual checkbox input, matching the pattern used by other BRAT checkbox tests (e.g. `test-automation-projects.R`)
- Replace `js.querySelector` + `clickElement` with idempotent `dom.setChecked(..., checked = TRUE)`
- Replace `Sys.sleep(2)` with `.rs.waitUntil()` polling for `.nb.html` existence
- Remove `skip_on_ci()`

title: fix notebook "preview on save" calling source() instead of rendering
description:
## Intent

Addresses #15925, #17293.

## Summary

- **Fix source-on-save regression for notebooks**: The source-on-save handler in `TextEditingTarget` didn't match the `XT_RMARKDOWN_NOTEBOOK` extended type (introduced in 2020), so notebooks fell through to `executeRSourceCommand()` which called `source()` on the `.Rmd` file. This regressed in 9edcff42 (2021-06-23) when the Quarto render-on-save support was added with an exact `== XT_RMARKDOWN_DOCUMENT` check instead of the previous `startsWith(XT_RMARKDOWN_PREFIX)`.

- **Notebooks no longer do a full knit on save**: Even if the extended type had matched, notebooks would have called `renderRmd()` (full knit, re-executes all chunks). Notebooks now correctly skip `renderRmd()` and rely on `NotebookHtmlRenderer` which assembles the `.nb.html` from the chunk output cache.

- **NotebookHtmlRenderer respects "Preview on Save"**: The `.nb.html` cache-based assembly on save now checks the `sourceOnSave` property, so unchecking "Preview on Save" actually prevents on-save work.

- **Skip redundant .nb.html generation**: `createNotebookFromCache` now short-circuits when the `.nb.html` is already up-to-date relative to the chunk definitions cache, avoiding an unnecessary `rmarkdown::render` / pandoc invocation that blocks the R session.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an `.Rmd` notebook (`output: html_notebook`) with prose content
- [ ] Enable "Preview on Save", save the document — verify no `source()` error in console
- [ ] Disable "Preview on Save", save the document — verify no rendering work occurs
- [ ] Execute a chunk, save with "Preview on Save" enabled — verify `.nb.html` is updated
- [ ] Save again without changes — verify no pandoc stall (short-circuit)

title: Allow install.packages/download.packages to read ~/.netrc
description:
## Problem

`install.packages()` and `download.packages()` were being blocked by the agent guardrails when they attempted to read `~/.netrc` for HTTP authentication during package downloads.

The error:
```
Error: One or more agent file operations were blocked.
- Action: readLines()
- Path:   ~/.netrc
- Reason: File may contain secret keys or credentials.
```

## Root Cause

The trusted-caller check in `chat.isCalledFromPackageImpl` grants trusted status to any non-base package namespace on the call stack. However, `utils` is a base package, so `install.packages` and `download.packages` were not recognized as trusted, causing the `~/.netrc` deny pattern to fire.

## Fix

Introduce `chat.safeFunctions`: a list of specific base-package functions captured **before** hook injection. `isCalledFromPackageImpl` now checks for these via `identical()` and treats them as trusted callers, bypassing the credential-path deny-pattern check.

The identity check keeps the allowlist precise — only these two named functions gain the exemption, not all of `utils`.

title: r api compliance for r-devel
description:
## Intent

Addresses R API compliance issues for compatibility with R-devel (R 4.6.0).

## Summary

### Binding API refactor

- Remove `r::sexp::Variable` typedef; `listEnvironment` now returns variable names only
- Add `r::sexp::BindingType` enum and `getBindingType()` using `R_GetBindingType` on R >= 4.6.0, with `TYPEOF`/`PRVALUE` fallback on older R
- Add `r::sexp::getBindingIdentity()` for change detection: returns the value for normal bindings (`R_getVarEx`), the expression for promises (`R_DelayedBindingExpression` / `PRCODE`), or `R_NilValue` for active/missing/unbound
- Rewrite `EnvironmentMonitor` change detection using `BindingSnapshot` (name + type + opaque identity token) instead of raw SEXP pointer comparison
- Add `RFunction::addQuotedParam()` for passing expressions to R without evaluation
- Add `.rs.promiseExprDescription()` R function; refactor `.rs.promiseDescription()` to delegate to it
- Switch `.rs.describeObject` to `(name, env)` parameter ordering
- Avoid forcing promises in SessionChat context collection via `getBindingType` filtering

### Environment API cleanup

- Add `r::sexp::getParentEnv()` using `R_ParentEnv` on R >= 4.5.0, falling back to `sxpinfo::getEnclos`
- Use API-compliant `findVarInFrame` wrapper in `findNamespace` and `hasActiveBindingImpl`
- Consolidate internal struct access into `sxpinfo` namespace with TODO markers; remove unused `getExtra`, `setExtra`, `getGp`
- Remove `hasExternalPointer` / `rs_hasExternalPointer` and deprecate `check_null_external_pointers` preference
- Remove `rs_getRefCount` / `rs_setRefCount` (`NAMED` / `SET_NAMED`) and `rs_objectAttributes` (`ATTRIB()`)

### Object size and ALTREP

- Replace `sxpinfo::getAttrib` with `base::attributes()` + `base::as.pairlist()` for ALTREP class inspection
- Fix LGLSXP double-counting bug in `obj_size_attrib`

### Other fixes

- Use `Rf_eval` instead of `PRVALUE` in DataViewer for promise forcing
- Use `execFileSync` with argument array instead of `execSync` with shell string for R version detection (fixes shell injection risk)
- Use component-wise version comparison instead of flattened integer
- Add R version warning for R newer than maximum supported version
- Remove active binding debug check from `findVar` that leaked error messages
- Fix `base:::sort` → `base::sort` in `SessionFiles`
- Add `r-api-report.sh` script for tracking non-public API symbol usage
- Pass `quiet = TRUE` to `download.file` / `download.packages` in tests

## Testing

- Manual testing of environment pane: variable creation, promise display, promise forcing, active bindings
- Desktop verification: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`

title: fix chromium startup failures in automation tests on linux
description:
## Intent

Fix automation tests failing to start Chromium on Linux due to X11 authentication
errors and snap wrapper script issues.

## Summary

- **Skip shell script wrappers**: `chromium-browser` on Ubuntu is a shell script
  that delegates to snap. This breaks `processx` process tracking because the
  wrapper exits while the actual browser runs as a separate process. Browser
  detection now identifies and skips wrapper scripts, preferring direct executables.

- **X11 authentication**: Extract display setup into `.rs.automation.initializeX11()`,
  which discovers both `DISPLAY` and `XAUTHORITY`. On GNOME/Wayland systems, it
  finds the Mutter Xwayland auth file in `/run/user/<uid>/`. Without `XAUTHORITY`,
  Chromium fails with "Authorization required, but no authorization protocol
  specified".

- **Explicit environment passing**: Pass the environment directly to `processx`
  via the `env` parameter instead of relying on `withr::with_envvar`, ensuring
  snap-launched browsers inherit the correct environment.

- **Linux flags**: Restore `--disable-dev-shm-usage` (needed in Docker where
  `/dev/shm` is limited) and add `--no-sandbox` for containerized environments.

- **Better error reporting**: Capture stderr/stdout when the browser process fails
  to start, and log process exit during the debug server wait loop.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified Chromium starts successfully on GNOME/Wayland (Xwayland) with snap Chromium
- [ ] Verify on systems with native X11 and non-snap Chromium
- [ ] Verify on systems with Google Chrome installed
- [ ] Verify in Docker/container environments

title: Fix theme changes not propagating to satellite windows
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17220.

## Summary

- Replace the `editorTheme()` pref binding in `SatelliteWindow` with a `UserState.theme()` binding so that `ThemeChangedEvent` fires after the authoritative theme value has been updated

The preferences dialog dispatches `UserPrefsChangedEvent` to satellites synchronously before `state_.writeState()` completes. The `editorTheme()` pref binding fired `ThemeChangedEvent` immediately, but `UserState.theme()` still held the previous value at that point, so `RStudioThemes.initializeThemes()` read stale state and satellite CSS classes were never updated to reflect the new theme.

Binding to `UserState.theme()` instead ensures `ThemeChangedEvent` fires once the theme value is current. The `globalTheme()` binding is kept separately for UI chrome changes.

This affects all satellite windows (chat, source, chunks, etc.), not just the Posit Assistant.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a source satellite window (pop out a source tab); change editor theme in Global Options > Appearance; verify the satellite updates
- [ ] Open the Posit Assistant in a satellite window; change editor theme; verify the satellite updates
- [ ] Verify theme changes still apply correctly in the main window
- [ ] BRAT automation test to follow in a separate PR

title: Fix theme propagation in popped-out chat satellite window
description:
## Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17220.

## Summary

- Override `onThemeChanged()` in `ChatSatelliteWindow` to clear the `ThemeColorExtractor` cache and re-inject CSS theme variables into the chat iframe when the editor theme changes
- This mirrors the existing handler in `ChatPane`, which calls `injectThemeVariables()` directly to ensure CSS variables are updated

## Background

When the chat pane is popped out into a satellite window, changing the editor theme did not update the chat iframe's theming. The satellite window relied on `RStudioThemedFrame`'s built-in theme handler, which goes through `addThemesStyle()` but does not clear the `ThemeColorExtractor` color cache first. `ChatPane` (main window) has its own explicit handler that clears the cache and calls `injectThemeVariables()` directly, which is why theming worked correctly in the main pane.

## Test plan

- Start RStudio Desktop with default layout and theme (Textmate)
- Show the sidebar and pop out the Posit Assistant into a separate window
- Tools > Global Options > Appearance: Choose a different editor theme (e.g. "Cobalt") and click OK

title: Fix chat showing in both satellite and main window on Chrome
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17221.

## Summary

- Replace deferred `returnChatToMain()` in `onSatelliteClosed()` with `WindowCloseMonitor.monitorSatelliteClosure()`, which polls the satellite window for up to 5 seconds to distinguish a real close from Chrome's reload-based reactivation
- This prevents the spurious `SatelliteClosedEvent` (fired by the old content's unload handler during Chrome's `window.open()` reload) from returning chat to the main pane while the satellite is still open

## Details

On Chrome, `SatelliteManager.openSatellite()` navigates the existing satellite window via `window.open(url, name)` instead of calling `callNotifyReactivated()` in-place. The old content's unload handler fires `notifyRStudioSatelliteClosed()`, which triggers `returnChatToMain()` — causing chat to appear in both the satellite and main window after "Session > Restart R" or session suspend/resume.

`WindowCloseMonitor.monitorSatelliteClosure()` polls `window.isClosed()` at 250ms intervals. On Chrome's reload path the window object stays open, so polling correctly identifies it as a reload (no-op). For a real user close, the window is gone and `onClosed` fires as expected. This is the same pattern used by `SourceWindowManager`, `ShinyApplication`, and `PlumberAPI`.

The existing `windowsClosing_` / `LastChanceSaveEvent` guard for Cmd+Q remains effective — the first poll at 250ms gives more time than the previous one-tick defer for `LastChanceSaveEvent` to set the flag.

## Test plan

- [ ] **Chrome — Restart R**: Pop out chat → Session > Restart R → chat stays only in satellite, sidebar stays hidden
- [ ] **Chrome — Session suspend/resume**: Pop out chat → wait for suspend → on resume, chat stays only in satellite
- [ ] **Chrome — Return to main**: After restart/resume, click "Return to main window" → moves chat back correctly
- [ ] **Chrome — Pop out again**: After returning to main, click "Pop out" → opens satellite without flashing
- [ ] **Chrome — Real close**: Pop out chat → close satellite window (X button) → chat returns to main pane
- [ ] **Chrome — Quit**: Pop out chat → Cmd+Q → clean shutdown, no errors
- [ ] **Firefox/Safari**: Repeat above steps — behavior unchanged (these browsers use the non-Chrome reactivation path)

title: Fix chat WebSocket URL for subpath reverse proxy deployments
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17249.

## Summary

- Prepend `session-root-path` to the chat WebSocket URL in `buildWebSocketUrl()` when RStudio Server is behind a subpath reverse proxy (e.g., `/rstudio/`)
- Without this, the WebSocket URL is `/p/{hash}/ai-chat/ws` instead of `/rstudio/p/{hash}/ai-chat/ws`, which bypasses the proxy's location block and omits cookies scoped to the subpath

## Details

`buildWebSocketUrl()` already prepends the `RS_SESSION_URL` env var for Workbench session prefixes, but did not account for the `session-root-path` option. In open-source RStudio Server, `RS_SESSION_URL` is always empty, so subpath deployments produced WebSocket URLs without the root path prefix.

Other port-mapped features (Shiny, Viewer, Plumber) are unaffected because they return relative URLs that the browser resolves against the current page. The chat code constructs an absolute path, so it needs the root path explicitly.

The fix reads `options().rootPath()` and prepends it when set to something other than the default `/`. The `www-root-path` server option passes this to the session automatically via `--session-root-path`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Root-level proxy: chat WebSocket connects at `/p/{hash}/ai-chat/ws`
- [ ] Subpath proxy (`/rstudio/`): chat WebSocket connects at `/rstudio/p/{hash}/ai-chat/ws`
- [ ] Desktop mode: unaffected (code is inside `#ifdef RSTUDIO_SERVER`)
- [ ] Shiny/Viewer/Terminal: still work through subpath proxy
- [ ] Session suspend/resume: chat reconnects

title: Update getCompletionsInheritDotParams to handle comma-combined arguments and cross-package sourcing.
description: #17243 ### Intent This PR resolves the 2 issues identified in #17243: 1. Comma-combined arguments (e.g. "n, prop") are presented as a single argument, but should be separated. 2. title: Suppress macOS menu rebuild warnings by updating MenuItems in-place
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17166.

## Summary

- Update `enabled`, `checked`, and `label` in-place on live Electron `MenuItem` objects instead of triggering full menu rebuilds (`Menu.buildFromTemplate` + `Menu.setApplicationMenu`) via debounced `updateMenus()` calls
- Full rebuilds are still used for `visible` and `accelerator` changes, which cannot be applied in-place
- Extract the modal-whitelisted roles into a shared `MODAL_ENABLED_ROLES` constant, and drop the dead `'redo'` entry (redoDummy has no role assigned)
- Add 8 new unit tests covering in-place updates, modal safety, and whitelisted role edge cases

The primary motivation is suppressing macOS AppKit warnings (`representedObject is not a WeakPtrToElectronMenuModelAsNSObject`) caused by calling `setApplicationMenu()` while old menu references still exist. Since `setCommandEnabled` fires on every focus/selection change, this was causing dozens of rebuilds per second. The optimization benefits all platforms.

Some warnings will still occur from visibility and shortcut changes, which require full rebuilds. Eliminating those would require Electron-level changes.

## Test plan

### Automated
- [ ] `cd src/node/desktop && npm test` — all 340 tests pass
- [ ] `cd src/node/desktop && npm run lint` — clean

### Manual — macOS (primary: warning suppression)
- [ ] Run RStudio from the terminal, observe significantly fewer `representedObject is not a WeakPtrToElectronMenuModelAsNSObject` warnings during normal use
- [ ] **Enabled/disabled states**: Open a source file, click in the editor, then click in the console — verify menu items like Edit > Undo, Code > Comment/Uncomment Lines toggle enabled/disabled as focus changes
- [ ] **Checkmarks**: Toggle View > Show Toolbar, View > Show Status Bar — verify checkmarks update immediately
- [ ] **Dynamic labels**: Open the Build pane with an R package project, verify Build menu shows the correct project-specific labels (e.g., "Install Package" vs "Build All")
- [ ] **Modal dialog**: Open Tools > Global Options, then switch tabs or click around in the editor behind it — verify menu items stay disabled while the dialog is open, and restore to correct state after closing
- [ ] **Cut/Copy/Paste in modal**: While a modal dialog (e.g., Global Options) is open, verify Edit > Cut, Copy, Paste remain enabled and functional in text fields within the dialog

### Manual — Windows and Linux (regression check)

title: Fix Posit Assistant broken after session restart
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17233.

## Summary

After a session restart (e.g. "Install Package" / Cmd+Shift+B), the Posit Assistant chat pane could become dimmed with a stuck suspend overlay, or show "Timeout waiting for backend to start" errors. Four related fixes:

- **Remove suspend overlay when showing HTML content** (`ChatPane.updateFrameContent`). Error messages and status views go through `updateFrameContent()` which never cleared the overlay, leaving content hidden behind the dim layer.
- **Guard SUSPEND handler** — only add the overlay when the chat UI was actually loaded (`cachedUrl_ != null`). Dimming an uninitialized pane creates problems on resume.
- **Guard RESUME handler** — reset stale `initializing_` flag and skip polling when the backend was never started. If startup was in-flight pre-suspend, re-trigger `initializeChat()` so the user isn't stranded on a "Starting..." screen.
- **Add poll generation counter** to prevent stale `pollForBackendUrl` callbacks from racing across suspend/resume boundaries. Each suspend and resume increments the generation; callbacks from a prior generation are discarded.

## Test plan

BRAT automation tests will be provided in a separate change. Manual verification:

- [ ] Start RStudio with sidebar hidden → open a package project → run "Install Package" (Cmd+Shift+B) → after session restart, show sidebar → pane is not dimmed, shows correct UI
- [ ] Show chat pane, then hide it → run "Install Package" → session restart → show sidebar → pane is not dimmed, chat resumes
- [ ] Show chat pane with active conversation → trigger session restart (`.rs.restartR()`) → overlay appears during suspend, chat resumes with conversation intact
- [ ] Start with chat running → trigger restart → switch provider away from Posit before resume completes → shows "not enabled", no dimmed overlay
- [ ] Pop out chat to satellite window → trigger suspend/resume → no stuck overlay or blank pane

title: Show error details and retry button when manifest download fails
description: ## Intent Addresses #17227. ## Summary - Show the actual error message from failed manifest downloads in the Chat pane instead of a generic message - Add a Retry button so users can retry without restarting RStudio - Remove unused update check throttling code (was disabled during development, not being re-enabled) ## Follow-up fixes - Check `readParam` return value in `chatCheckForUpdates` so a malformed parameter returns an error instead of silently defaulting - Use `data-*` attributes to pass i18n labels to JS instead of interpolating into JS string literals - Add `.catch()` handler on the clipboard API promise so the user gets feedback if copy fails - Route clipboard copy-failure text through i18n constants (`chatCopyFailed`) - Reset stale state flags in `checkForUpdatesOnStartup` to match the pattern in `doUpdateCheck()` - Fix low contrast on error detail block in dark themes by using theme-aware CSS variables - Add `initializing_` re-entry guard on retry-manifest to prevent concurrent RPCs from double-clicks - Disable retry button on click for immediate visual feedback ## Screenshots ### Before ### After (this fix) ## Test Plan ### Setup: Force manifest download failure Block network access to `www.rstudio.org` by adding a hosts file entry. This requires administrator/root privileges. **Mac / Linux:** ```bash sudo sh -c 'echo "127.0.0.1 www.rstudio.org" >> /etc/hosts' ``` **Windows** (run Command Prompt or PowerShell as Administrator): ```cmd echo 127.0.0.1 www.rstudio.org >> C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts ``` ### Test cases - [ ] **Error displays correctly:** With the host blocked, open the Chat pane. Verify it shows a "Connection Error" heading, a user-friendly message, the specific error in a monospace block, and a Retry button. - [ ] **Error detail readable in dark theme:** Switch to a dark editor theme and verify the error detail block has proper text contrast. - [ ] **Retry succeeds after recovery:** Remove the hosts entry (see cleanup below), click Retry. Verify chat initializes normally. - [ ] **Retry fails gracefully:** With the host still blocked, click Retry. Verify the error view refreshes with a new error message and does not stack or break. - [ ] **Double-click retry:** Click Retry rapidly. Verify only one RPC is sent (no duplicate callbacks or errors). - [ ] **Satellite window:** Pop out the Chat pane to a satellite window, trigger the error, and verify the Retry button works there too. ### Cleanup: Restore network access **Mac:** ```bash sudo sed -i '' '/127.0.0.1 www.rstudio.org/d' /etc/hosts ``` **Linux:** ```bash sudo sed -i'' '/127.0.0.1 www.rstudio.org/d' /etc/hosts ``` **Windows** (run as Administrator): Open `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts` in a text editor and remove the `127.0.0.1 www.rstudio.org` line. On all platforms, you may need to flush the DNS cache afterward: - **Mac:** `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder` - **Linux:** `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` (or restart `nscd`/`dnsmasq`) - **Windows:** `ipconfig /flushdns`

- Only uses `devtools::test()` when devtools is available and enabled in the project config (`useDevtools()` check).
- Files not matching the `test-<name>.R` pattern preserve existing `testthat::test_file()` behavior.
- Fix condition annotation grouping: when a warning or error prefix was found mid-output (e.g. a deferred "Warning message:" at the end of accumulated build output), the group markers were inserted at position 0, wrapping all preceding text in the condition group. Now inserts the group start marker at the match position so only the condition text is grouped.

## Test plan

title: Fix chat restarting when Global Options dismissed without changes

title: Include auto-completion for dot params when tagged with @inheritDotParams
description: ### Intent Addresses #16069 This PR results in Rstudio autocompletion expanding dot params when the function is tagged with roxygen `@inheritDotParams`. For example, this is what it now looks like for `ggplot2::scale_color_grey` which inherits dot params from `ggplot2::discrete_scale`: ### Approach Add a method to SessionRCompletions that: 1. Retrieves the help documentation for the function. 2. Checks if `...` exists with the precise formatting associated with `@inheritDotParams`. (Since we can't test for the presence of the roxygen tag directly we have to test for its result: Dot params with the text "arguments passed to" and children items with `\code`. 3. If (2) is true, the referenced function's formals are added to the autocompletions, except where a local one already exists, or if that function has `...`. Since the goal of this is to help with simple wrappers, I decided to force it to be shallow -- it does not recurse. Note: This PR was developed in concert with Claude. ### Automated Tests Tests for this capability are in a new `test-completions-inherit-dot-params.R` file. ```r > testthat::test_dir("src/cpp/tests/testthat", filter = "completion") ✔ | F W S OK | Context ✔ | 31 | auto-completion ✔ | 26 | inheritDotParams completions ══ Results ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ [ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 57 ] ``` _Note: Since `rstudio` is not a typical R package that can leverage tools like `devtools::load_all()`, I ran the test locally by updating the `SessionRCompletions.R` file in my local RStudio installation._ ### QA Notes #### Steps to Test Manually: Load RStudio with the updated `SessionRCompletions.R` file in `src/cpp/session/modules`. Test autocompletion on a function that uses `@inheritDotParams`, such as `ggplot2::scale_color_grey` (which uses `@inheritDotParams discrete_scale -expand -position -scale_name -palette -fallback.palette`). 1. In the console, type `ggplot2::scale_color_grey(` and press tab. You should see all the the formals of `scale_color_grey` (including `...`) AND the inherited formals from `discrete_scale`, labeled as such. You You should NOT see the excluded items from `discrete_scale` in the list above, e.g. `expand`, `position`, etc. 2. Test without package name prefix, by loading `ggplot2` (e.g. running `library(ggplot2)`) and then typing `scale_color_grey(` and pressing tab to trigger auto-complete. You should now see the same thing as before but rhs do not have the package name. 3. Test with a partial token for inherited args, for example, by typing `scale_color_grey(br`. Autocomplete (either by waiting or pressing tab) should show `breaks` which comes from `discrete_scale` and not from scale_color_grey's formals. 5. Test with a partial token for standard formals, for example, by typing `scale_color_grey(st` and you should see `start`. 6. Test on a function that has dots but not `@inheritDotParams`, such as by typing `scale_alpha` and triggering autocomplete via tab. That should show the formals for scale_alpha as normal, including the dots. #### Testing Results with screenshots All tests above pass 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. #### Risks and Other Considerations ##### Performance Performing this completion analysis requires an extra call to `utils::help` (via `.rs.makeHelpCall`) and `utils:::.getHelpFile`. The worst I have seen running `.rs.getCompletionsFunction` on `ggplot2::scale_color_grey` for the first time, it took 1.77s, presumably to load all the help for ggplot2. But afterwards, that is cached and the calls were instantaneous. In that case, however, RStudio felt especially laggy so there may have been other issues with my computer. In subsequent runs, where RStudio did not feel laggy, the pre-cached time was 0.02-0.06s, so I believe this is low risk. ##### Changing existing behavior of `@inheritDotParams` The approach for this PR takes advantage of the existing `@inheritDotParams`. This means a forced change in behavior for those that had opted in to what `@inheritDotParams`. This will not cause any errors, but may clutter autocomplete for those functions where not intended. Furthermore, I believe this has been viewed as a limitation of inheritDotParams not the design, and so I think this is a low risk change. ##### Auto-complete is based documentation not the installed version If a developer uses `@inheritDotParams` with an external package, the help documentation will be based on the version used when the documentation was built, not the one that the end user has currently installed. This is already a limitation of `@inheritDotParams` and is why using it with functions from external packages should only be done with caution. This new functionality continues that same approach, assuming the documentation is the state of truth. #### TBD: Update original issue > Ensure you have updated the QA Notes in the original issue. TBD ### Documentation > Specify which documentation has been added or modified and why (User Guide? Admin Guide?). If no documentation was added for a new feature, indicate why. If documentation was added in a separate PR, link the PR here. I don't believe this requires any RStudio documentation updates, but requires updating roxygen documentation for `@inheritDotParams`. ### Checklist - [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` - [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility) - [x] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list) - [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: Add pop-out satellite window for Posit Assistant chat pane
description: ## Intent Addresses #16937. ## Summary Adds the ability to pop the Posit Assistant (chat) pane out into a separate satellite window, allowing users to take advantage of multiple monitors. This follows the same satellite window pattern used by the Source Editor pop-out. ### New commands - **Pop Out Posit Assistant** — opens the chat pane in a separate window, replacing the chat content with a placeholder showing "Bring to Front" and "Return Here" buttons - **Return Posit Assistant to Main Window** — closes the satellite and restores the chat content to the main window pane - **Activate Chat** — brings the satellite window to the front when chat is popped out ### How it works - `ChatPresenter` remains the singleton owner of backend lifecycle in the main window. The satellite window displays the chat UI in an `RStudioThemedFrame` but never manages the backend. - When popped out, the main window ChatPane shows a placeholder with action buttons. The satellite toolbar has a "Return to Main Window" button. - Cross-window communication uses `CrossWindowEvent` (`ChatReturnToMainEvent`, `ChatSatelliteActionEvent`) routed through `$wnd.opener`. - Pop-out state and window geometry are persisted via `ClientState` (project-persistent scope), so the satellite automatically reopens after RStudio restart or session resume. - The sidebar auto-hides when chat is popped out (unless there are additional tabs in the Sidebar) and restores when chat returns. ### New files - `ChatSatellite.java` — satellite application entry point - `ChatSatelliteWindow.java` — satellite window with themed frame and toolbar - `ChatSatelliteView.java` — satellite view interface - `ChatSatelliteParams.java` — JavaScriptObject overlay for passing chat URL/auth to the satellite - `ChatReturnToMainEvent.java` — cross-window event (satellite → main) - `ChatSatelliteActionEvent.java` — cross-window event for button actions from the placeholder ### Edge cases handled - Backend crash while popped out closes the satellite and shows error UI in the main pane - Chat provider change while popped out closes the satellite - Session suspend keeps the satellite open; resume restores it - Sidebar hidden at startup with chat popped out correctly restores the satellite - Pop-out button only appears when the chat backend is ready ### Known Issues On Linux with Wayland, window positioning requests are generally ignored so layout of multiple windows won't be preserved on restart. This is a Wayland thing. ### Screenshots Arrow pointing at the pop-out / pop-in widgets. Note this button is on the "native" toolbar in the chat pane, which was previously hidden. There was talk of implementing the chat toolbar in the "native" toolbar as well but we don't currently plan to do that. ## Test plan - [ ] Pop out: click toolbar button → satellite opens, main shows placeholder - [ ] Return: click "Return to Main Window" in satellite → satellite closes, chat restores in main - [ ] Close satellite via window close button → chat restores in main - [ ] "Bring to Front" button raises satellite window - [ ] Restart persistence: pop out, restart RStudio → satellite auto-reopens - [ ] Session suspend/resume with satellite open - [ ] Theme change propagates to satellite window - [ ] Backend crash while popped out → satellite closes, error shown in main - [ ] Provider change while popped out → satellite closes - [ ] Test in both desktop (Electron) and server (browser) modes - [ ] Automated tests (BRAT) will be added in a separate PR

title: fix air formatting when 'use air' preference is not set
description:
## Intent

Addresses #16721.

## Summary

- The format-on-save path (`maybeFormatOnUserInitiatedSave`) bypassed the `useAirFormatter` preference entirely, unconditionally sending a format request to the backend. The backend's `formatDocumentImpl()` treated `codeFormatter="none"` (the default) as "use Air" without checking the `useAirFormatter` preference. This caused Air formatting on save even when "Use Air for code formatting" was unchecked.

- Additionally, `useBuiltinFormatter()` had inverted logic (`return hasAirToml` instead of `return !hasAirToml`), which prevented Air from being used for manual reformat/reformat-selection even when it was enabled.

## Changes

- **`TextEditingTarget.java` — `useBuiltinFormatter()`**: Invert the return value so that when `useAirFormatter` is true and `air.toml` exists, the server-side Air formatter is used instead of the built-in formatter.
- **`TextEditingTarget.java` — `maybeFormatOnUserInitiatedSave()`**: Gate on `useBuiltinFormatter()` so format-on-save only calls the server when an external formatter (Air/styler/external) is actually configured.
- **`SessionSource.cpp` — `formatDocumentImpl()`**: Add a `useAirFormatter` check as a backend safety net when `codeFormatter` is `"none"`.

## Test plan

- [ ] With `useAirFormatter` **unchecked** and `reformatOnSave` enabled, saving an R file should **not** apply Air formatting
- [ ] With `useAirFormatter` **checked**, `air.toml` present, and `reformatOnSave` enabled, saving an R file **should** apply Air formatting
- [ ] Manual reformat (Ctrl+Shift+A) with `useAirFormatter` checked and `air.toml` present should use Air (not the built-in formatter)
- [ ] Manual reformat with `useAirFormatter` unchecked should use the built-in formatter
- [ ] Styler and external formatter paths remain unaffected

title: Add libgit2 for gitignore-aware file monitoring
description:
## Summary

- Integrates libgit2 to respect `.gitignore` rules when filtering the project file monitor, so that gitignored files (build artifacts, vendor directories, generated output, etc.) are automatically excluded from code search indexing and other file-monitor subscribers
- Adds a `file_monitor_use_gitignore` user preference (default: `true`) that can be toggled per-project via Project Options > Code Editing > Indexing
- Adds private project-specific preferences support: per-user prefs stored in `.Rproj.user/<ctx>/rstudio-prefs.json`, with a schema-driven allowlist (`"private": true`) and bulk read/write through the existing project options RPC
- Adds save/restore macros for global CMake settings to prevent FetchContent dependencies from polluting the parent project's cache variables (e.g. `CMAKE_C_STANDARD`, `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS`)
- Refactors `PrefLayer::loadPrefsFromFile` to use an output parameter instead of writing directly to `cache_`, fixing a corruption bug in `onPrefsFileChanged` error paths
- Fixes `mergePrefs()` to use `json::Value::clone()` instead of destructive move assignment, which was nullifying values in source caches
- Existing hardcoded ignore patterns are preserved as a first-pass filter; gitignore checking runs after them
- Non-git projects are handled gracefully (no-op)
- The Files pane is unaffected (it uses a separate monitor)

## Intent

Addresses #16879.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open RStudio with a git project that has a `.gitignore`
- [ ] Verify that gitignored files (e.g. build artifacts) do not appear in Go to File/Function results
- [ ] Verify that non-gitignored files still appear in search
- [ ] Verify that a non-git project still works (graceful no-op)
- [ ] Open Project Options > Code Editing > verify "Respect .gitignore when indexing files" checkbox appears and reflects saved state
- [ ] Uncheck the checkbox, click OK, verify `.Rproj.user/<ctx>/rstudio-prefs.json` contains `{"file_monitor_use_gitignore": false}`
- [ ] Reopen the dialog, verify the checkbox reflects the saved value
- [ ] Build on Windows and Linux to verify cross-platform compilation

title: Improve code search indexing performance for large projects
description:
## Summary

- Adds an `unordered_map`-based path lookup cache to the `EntryTree`, replacing O(n) sibling/leaf scans with O(1) lookups for insert, find, and remove operations
- Introduces a directory-level ignored-dir cache (`s_ignoredDirCache`) to avoid repeated filesystem checks during indexing
- Extracts `isIgnoredDirectory()` helper to consolidate directory-ignore logic into a single function
- Increases incremental indexing batch size and scheduler intervals for better throughput
- Ignores `__pycache__` directories in the file monitor and fixes the `virtualenv` filter list
- Falls back to root-level search instead of bailing out when a parent node isn't yet indexed

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `node_modules`, `packrat`, `renv`, cmake build, `revdep`, `__pycache__`, and `venv` directories are excluded from code search results
- [ ] Verify file changes (add/remove/modify) are still reflected in search results after indexing completes
- [ ] Verify code search works correctly in small projects with no special directories

title: fix multiple bugs in R parser diagnostics
description:
## Summary

- Fix `closesArgumentList()` checking `RToken::RBRACE` instead of `RToken::RBRACKET` for single-bracket argument lists (e.g. `x[1]`)
- Fix glue string validation handling escaped quotes incorrectly in embedded strings — the escape character was consumed but then the delimiter check re-matched the same character
- Fix static `symbolRanges` leaking symbol definitions across independent parse operations by making it a per-node member instead of a process-wide static singleton
- Fix `isSymbolDefinedButNotUsed()` only handling the single-definition/single-reference case; generalize to correctly handle multiple definitions by checking whether every reference position coincides with a definition position
- Fix parent assignment (`<<-`) handler walking `getReferencedSymbols()` instead of `getDefinedSymbols()` when searching parent scopes for existing definitions
- Fix native pipe `|>` placeholder detection — was checking unnamed arguments for `_`, but the native pipe placeholder is only valid as the value of a named argument (e.g. `f(x = _)`)
- Fix `handleElseToken()` not detecting stray `else` tokens without a matching `if`, and not popping function expression states during the control-flow unwind
- Fix glue `.open`/`.close` delimiter unescaping silently ignoring errors from `jsonLiteralUnescape()`

Adds tests for each fix in `SessionDiagnosticsTests.cpp`.

## Test plan

- [x] All `DiagnosticsTest.*` tests pass (6 tests including new ones)
- [ ] Verify R parser diagnostics still work correctly in the IDE (open an R file, check that lint markers appear as expected)

title: Fix YAML comment preservation in YamlTree
description:
## Intent

Addresses #14882.

## Summary

- `YamlTree` treated YAML comment lines (starting with `#`) as multi-line value continuations, causing them to be dropped or displaced when YAML front matter was round-tripped
- Comments are now recognized as standalone tree nodes that preserve their position during serialization, without polluting the key map
- Adds `YamlTreeTests` with 9 test cases covering root-level comments, indented comments, comments with colons, and the `RmdEditorOptions.set()` integration path

## Motivation

When toggling **Chunk Output in Console** on an R Markdown file, RStudio modifies the YAML header to add `editor_options: chunk_output_type: console`. This round-trips the YAML through `YamlTree`, which was silently dropping or displacing any `#` comment lines in the front matter.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an `.Rmd` file with comments in the YAML header, toggle "Chunk Output in Console", and verify comments are preserved in their original positions

title: Show Chat pane notification when readline blocks during AI code execution
description: ## Intent When Posit Assistant executes R code that calls `readline()`, R blocks waiting for user input in the Console. title: Bind terminal websocket to loopback in non-standalone mode
description:
## Intent

Harden the terminal websocket server against unauthorized network access.

## Summary

- Bind the terminal websocket (`SessionConsoleProcessSocket`) to loopback (`127.0.0.1` / `::1`) in non-standalone mode instead of all interfaces (`tcp::v4()` / `tcp::v6()`)
- In non-standalone mode the rserver proxy handles external connections and authenticates them; the rsession websocket server should not be directly reachable from the network
- Add a websocket validate handler that rejects connections during the upgrade handshake if the URL is malformed or the terminal handle is not registered, preventing unauthorized clients from establishing connections
- In desktop mode, validate the Origin header and reject connections from non-loopback origins to prevent cross-site websocket hijacking (CSWSH)

title: Expand chat guardrails for file access permissions
description:
## Intent

Expand the AI chat guardrails to permit file operations in additional
standard R directories, deny reads on more credential files, and add
trusted caller detection for package code.

## Summary

**Expanded edit allowlist:**
- Allow edits within R library paths (`.libPaths()`) so AI-generated code can install packages
- Allow edits within R user directories (data, config, cache via `tools::R_user_dir()`) to support renv cache, package configs, and other R tooling

**Expanded deny-read patterns (defense-in-depth):**
- Container/cloud: `.docker`, `.kube`, `.config/gcloud`, `.azure`
- Crypto/keys: `.gnupg`
- Package registries: `.pypirc`, `.gem/credentials`
- Databases: `.pgpass`, `.my.cnf`, `.mylogin.cnf`
- Git/CLI tokens: `.git-credentials`, `.config/gh/hosts.yml`, `.huggingface/token`
- R config files: `.Renviron`, `.Rprofile`

**Trusted caller detection:**
- Walk the call stack to detect whether a file read originates from a non-base package namespace
- When it does, skip the deny-pattern check so that package code (e.g. usethis, credentials) can legitimately access credential files
- Base and recommended packages are excluded from the trusted set since the agent could call them directly

**Path normalization improvements:**
- Replace R's `normalizePath()` with a C++ implementation using Boost's `weakly_canonical` + `lexically_normal`, which properly resolves symlinks and removes `.`/`..` components even for non-existing path tails
- Guard `isPathWithin` against empty, root, and bare Windows drive root directories

**Testing:**
- Add comprehensive unit tests for deny patterns, path containment, normalization, edit/read allowlists, and trusted caller detection
- Disable ANSI escape codes in CI test runner

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify AI-generated code can call `install.packages()` without being blocked
- [ ] Verify AI-generated code can write to renv cache directories
- [ ] Verify reads of newly-denied credential files are blocked
- [ ] Verify package code (e.g. usethis) can still access `.Renviron`/`.Rprofile`
- [ ] Verify existing guardrail behavior is unchanged for project/working/temp directories
- [ ] Unit tests pass (`test-chat-guardrails.R`)

title: Fix pane layout not persisting when moving tabs out of sidebar
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17177.

## Summary

- Fix a race condition where pane layout changes involving the sidebar (visibility, location, or column count) were not persisted to `rstudio-prefs.json`
- Add BRAT tests verifying that moving Posit Assistant from sidebar to TabSet1 persists across a UI reload

## Details

When sidebar visibility changed (e.g. moving the last tab out of the sidebar), `setGlobalValue` was deferred via `Scheduler.get().scheduleDeferred()` to avoid a `getOffsetWidth()==0` layout bug. But `doSaveChanges()` ran synchronously before the deferred command executed, serializing the stale config.

The fix writes the new config immediately without firing events (so `doSaveChanges()` serializes the correct value), then fires `ValueChangeEvent` in the deferred command after the browser renders.

## Test plan

- [ ] Move Posit Assistant from sidebar to TabSet1 via Pane Layout prefs, click OK, restart — verify it stays in TabSet1
- [ ] Same test but with sidebar initially visible
- [ ] Move tabs between TabSet1/TabSet2 (no sidebar change) — verify still persists (regression)
- [ ] Toggle sidebar location (left → right) — verify persists across restart
- [ ] Add/remove source columns — verify layout persists
- [ ] `cd src/gwt && ant javac` builds cleanly

title: Respect user-configured R download method for Posit AI package downloads
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17052.

## Summary

- Remove hardcoded `method = "libcurl"` from the manifest and package `download.file()` calls in `SessionChat.cpp`, so R uses whatever download method the user/admin has configured via `options(download.file.method)` and `options(download.file.extra)`.
- Set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` from `--posit-assistant-ssl-certificates-file` in `startChatBackend()`, mirroring what `SessionAssistant.cpp` already does for Copilot/NES.

PR #17059 fixed proxy support for the Node.js chat backend (`fetch()` calls) by setting `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`. However, the R-side manifest and package downloads still failed behind SSL-intercepting proxies because `download.file(method = "libcurl")` was hardcoded, overriding any user/admin R configuration.

Corporate proxy environments typically configure R with `options(download.file.method = "curl")` and `options(download.file.extra = "--cacert /path/to/proxy-ca.pem")`. With the hardcoded `"libcurl"`, this configuration was ignored.

## Test plan

See https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/17059 for more detailed testing instructions. This new change adds an additional requirement, putting following in ~/.Rprofile:

```R
options(
   download.file.method = "curl",
   download.file.extra = paste(
      "-L -f --cacert",
      "/Users/username-here/.mitmproxy/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem"
   )
)
```

- [ ] **Proxy test**: Configure mitmproxy (`mitmdump -p 8888`), set `https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:8888` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=~/.mitmproxy/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem` in `~/.Renviron`, set `options(download.file.method = "curl", download.file.extra = "-L -f --cacert ~/.mitmproxy/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem")` in `~/.Rprofile`. Verify manifest and package download succeed through the proxy.
- [ ] **Regression test**: Remove all proxy configuration. Verify Posit Assistant downloads work normally with no proxy.
- [ ] **Windows test**: Verify default `"wininet"` method works (uses Windows certificate store).

title: Enable proxy support for Posit Assistant chat backend
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17052.

## Summary

- Set `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` in the chat backend's Node.js process environment so that `fetch()` routes through `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` when those variables are present (e.g. via `~/.Renviron`).
- This is an official Node.js 22.21+ feature ([nodejs/node#57165](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/57165)) that installs an `EnvHttpProxyAgent` as the global dispatcher at startup. RStudio ships Node.js 22.22.0, which supports it.
- When no proxy env vars are set, the flag has no effect.
- Includes `TEST-PROXY.md` with manual testing instructions using mitmproxy.

## Testing Proxy Support for Posit Assistant

Note: you should also test NES and Copilot as I've applied the same fix to that scenario.

Verifies that the `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` change in `SessionChat.cpp` causes
the chat backend's `fetch()` calls to route through `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`.


### 1. Quick smoke test (no proxy software needed)

Set the proxy to a port where nothing is listening. If `fetch()` respects the
proxy, it fails with a connection-refused error; if it ignores the proxy, it
connects directly.

Add to `~/.Renviron`:

```
https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:9999
```

Restart RStudio, open Posit Assistant, and attempt to sign in. The chat backend
stderr logs should show a connection error referencing `127.0.0.1:9999`,
confirming `fetch()` is routing through the proxy.

To confirm it's specifically `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` causing this, temporarily
comment out the `setenv` line in `SessionChat.cpp`, rebuild, and repeat -- the
sign-in should bypass the broken proxy and attempt a direct connection instead.

Remove the `~/.Renviron` line when done.


### 2. Full positive test with mitmproxy

Verifies end-to-end: sign-in and chat complete through a real proxy.

#### Setup

```bash
brew install mitmproxy
```

Run it once to generate its CA certificate, then start it:

```bash
mitmdump -p 8888
```

The CA cert is created at `~/.mitmproxy/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem` on first run.
Node.js needs to trust it for HTTPS interception. Add both lines to
`~/.Renviron`:

```
https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:8888
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/Users/gary/.mitmproxy/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem
```

`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is already picked up by the chat backend --
`SessionAssistant.cpp` passes it through to the Node.js environment.

#### Verify

Restart RStudio, open the chat pane, and sign in. In the `mitmdump` terminal
you should see CONNECT requests to `login.posit.cloud` and then
`gateway.posit.ai` once you send a message.


### 3. Regression check (no proxy)

Remove both lines from `~/.Renviron`, restart RStudio, and verify Posit
Assistant works normally with no proxy configured. `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`
should have no effect when no proxy env vars are set.

title: Suppress 'R Session Disconnected' dialog on Desktop and during restart
description:
## Summary

The `onClientDisconnected` handler in `Application.java` was showing the "R Session Disconnected" popup unconditionally. This is wrong in two cases:

1. **On Desktop**, where the dialog should never appear (Desktop has its own session recovery mechanism triggered by process exit).
2. **During a deliberate restart**, where in-flight RPC requests may return `INVALID_CLIENT_ID` as the session resets, spuriously triggering the disconnect event.

## Fix

Add guards for both cases in `onClientDisconnected()`:
- `Desktop.isDesktop()` check, mirroring the existing pattern in `onQuit()`
- `pApplicationQuit_.get().isSuspendingAndRestarting()` check, using the existing accessor on `ApplicationQuit`

## Testing

- On Desktop, verify the "R Session Disconnected" dialog no longer appears during restart
- On Server, verify the dialog no longer appears during a deliberate restart
- On Server, verify the dialog still appears for genuine disconnections (e.g. network loss)
