title: Suppress new frame prompt during AI code evaluation
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17162.

## Summary

- When `par(ask = TRUE)` is set, R prompts "Hit <Return> to see next plot:" via `GD_NewFrameConfirm()`. This blocks AI-generated code execution waiting for interactive input.
- Adds a `SuppressNewFrameConfirmScope` RAII class (in `RGraphics.hpp`) with a static int counter that tracks nested suppression scopes.
- Constructs a scope instance in `executeCodeImpl()` before the expression evaluation loop, so the counter is active during AI code evaluation and automatically decremented when the scope exits.
- Checks `SuppressNewFrameConfirmScope::isActive()` in `GD_NewFrameConfirm()` to return `TRUE` (skip the prompt) while the AI assistant is evaluating code.

## Test plan

- [ ] Set `par(ask = TRUE)`, then ask the AI assistant to generate multiple plots — it should not block on the "Hit <Return>" prompt
- [ ] Verify that `par(ask = TRUE)` still works normally when plotting from the R console

title: Fix NES gutter icon persisting across file close/open cycles
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17108.

## Summary

- Invalidate in-flight async RPC request IDs (`requestId_`, `nesId_`) in `onDismiss()` so that stale completion callbacks are rejected when they arrive after a file is closed
- Add a `dismissed_` guard flag checked at key async entry points (`showEditSuggestionImpl`, `requestNextEditSuggestions`, `suggestionTimer_`) to prevent any suggestion rendering or request scheduling on a dismissed editor

The root cause is a race condition specific to the Copilot NES fallback path: when a regular completion request is in-flight at the time a file is closed, the response callback can pass the staleness check (since `onDismiss()` did not previously invalidate the request IDs), then reschedule `nesTimer_` via the empty-result fallback, ultimately rendering a stale NES gutter icon.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a file, trigger an NES suggestion with Copilot, accept it, then close the file without saving
- [ ] Open a new file and verify no stale NES gutter icon appears
- [ ] Verify NES suggestions still work normally after the fix (accept, dismiss, auto-trigger)

title: Fix theme color computation race condition on first launch
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17151.

## Summary

- Replace speculative animation-frame and timer-based theme color sampling with `onload` handlers on the Ace theme CSS and server font CSS `<link>` elements
- Theme colors are now (re)computed once the stylesheet has actually been fetched and parsed, rather than after an arbitrary delay
- `EditorThemeChangedEvent` and desktop frame color synchronization are now also driven by the CSS load handler, replacing the previous fixed 100ms `Timer`
- Adds `onerror` handlers that log a warning and fire fallback events if CSS fails to load
- Clears stale `onload`/`onerror` handlers when replacing existing link elements
- Restricts load handlers to the main document to avoid duplicate events from iframes and satellite windows

## Background

On first launch with an empty browser cache, the `.rstheme` CSS file may not finish loading within the ~48ms window provided by three animation frames. When this happens, `onComputeThemeColors()` samples default/incorrect colors from `getComputedStyles()`, causing the IDE to appear unthemed.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify theme loads correctly on first launch (Desktop and Server)
- [ ] Verify switching themes in Global Options applies immediately
- [ ] Verify chat pane picks up correct theme colors
- [ ] Verify no regressions with light/dark theme toggle

title: Block unsupported Posit AI versions, protocols, and manifest failures
description: Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17145 ## Summary - Add support for an `unsupported` field in the Posit AI manifest.json that allows blocking specific package versions, protocol versions, and setting a minimum required package version - Block Posit AI entirely (Chat pane and NES language server) when the manifest cannot be downloaded - Gate the NES language server on the same unsupported-version/protocol checks as the Chat pane ## Manifest `unsupported` field The manifest.json now supports an optional `unsupported` object: ```json { "unsupported": { "minimumPackageVersion": "1.3.0", "packageVersions": ["0.0.0"], "protocols": ["8.0"] } } ``` All three sub-fields are optional and evaluated independently: | Field | Effect | |-------|--------| | `minimumPackageVersion` | Any installed version below this semver is blocked | | `packageVersions` | Exact-match blocklist of specific package versions | | `protocols` | Blocklist of RStudio protocol versions | When a condition matches: - The Chat pane shows a blocking message (unsupported version or unsupported protocol) — the user can no longer dismiss or ignore a required update - The NES language server is stopped (or prevented from starting) via a new `isPositAiUnsupported()` check in `SessionAssistant.cpp` - If an update is available for a blocked version, the user is prompted to update; if not, they are told to update RStudio ## Manifest download failure Previously, if the manifest failed to download (network error, HTTP failure, or debug manifest misconfiguration), the update check silently returned and Posit AI loaded normally. Now: - A `manifestUnavailable` flag is set in `UpdateState` and returned to the frontend via the `chatCheckForUpdates` RPC - Both the Chat pane and the NES language server are blocked - The Chat pane shows: "Unable to verify Posit AI compatibility. Please check your network connection and restart RStudio." - The flag is cleared on the next successful manifest download ## Debug manifest (`RSTUDIO_CHAT_DEBUG_MANIFEST`) In debug builds, all error paths for `RSTUDIO_CHAT_DEBUG_MANIFEST` now return hard errors instead of silently falling through to HTTP: - Path doesn't end with `manifest.json` → `invalid_argument` error - File doesn't exist → `no_such_file_or_directory` error ## NES language server gating `SessionAssistant.cpp` now calls `chat::isPositAiUnsupported()` before starting the Posit AI agent. This function returns `true` when any of these conditions hold: - Installed package version is unsupported - RStudio protocol version is unsupported - Manifest was unavailable ## UI Examples ### Protocol not supported ### Current version too old, no update available ### Current version too old, update available (note no "Ignore" option) ### Unable to download the manifest.json ## Test plan - [ ] Set `RSTUDIO_CHAT_DEBUG_MANIFEST` to a non-existent path → Chat pane shows "Unable to verify" message, NES completions don't work - [ ] Set `RSTUDIO_CHAT_DEBUG_MANIFEST` to a path not ending in `manifest.json` → same blocked behavior - [ ] Point to a valid manifest with no `unsupported` field → Chat and NES work normally - [ ] Point to a manifest with `"protocols": [""]` → Chat shows protocol unsupported message, NES stopped - [ ] Point to a manifest with `"packageVersions": [""]` → Chat shows version unsupported, NES stopped - [ ] Point to a manifest with `"minimumPackageVersion"` above installed version → same blocked behavior - [ ] Point to a manifest blocking the installed version but with an update available → user is prompted to update (cannot dismiss) - [ ] Unset env var and disconnect network → verify manifest-unavailable blocking on HTTP failure - [ ] Fix path / restore network and restart → verify recovery works

title: Suppress INVALID_CLIENT_ID disconnect during R session restart
description:
## Summary

During a deliberate restart, in-flight RPC requests (e.g. the event polling request from `RemoteServerEventListener`) may return `INVALID_CLIENT_ID` after the R session resets. Previously this triggered `disconnect()` and fired `ClientDisconnectedEvent`, which:

1. Set the `disconnected_` flag, silently breaking the ping loop in `waitForSessionRestart` that detects when the new session is ready.
2. Showed the "R Session Disconnected" dialog (a separate bug addressed in #17139 / #17140).

## Fix

Track restart state in `RemoteServer` by subscribing to `RestartStatusEvent`. When a restart is in progress, suppress the `disconnect()` call and `ClientDisconnectedEvent` for `INVALID_CLIENT_ID` errors, since they are expected and transient.

This is a root-cause fix that complements the handler-level guards in #17139 / #17140.

## Testing

- Restart R session and verify no spurious disconnect events are fired
- Verify `waitForSessionRestart` ping loop continues operating through the restart window
- Verify genuine `INVALID_CLIENT_ID` errors (outside of restart) still trigger disconnect as before

title: Suppress 'R Session Disconnected' dialog on Desktop

## Testing

- Verify the "R Session Disconnected" dialog no longer appears
- On Server, verify the dialog still appears for genuine disconnections

title: Ignore mouse events on splash screen to avoid Electron teardown crash
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17135.

## Summary

- Call `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` on the splash screen BrowserWindow to prevent Chromium from processing mouse events, avoiding the hit test code path that crashes during window teardown

Electron 39.7.0 introduced a regression where hit tests on transparent frameless windows during teardown dereference freed memory. On Windows this causes a startup crash when the mouse pointer is over the splash screen while it closes. The upstream fix is [electron/electron#49929](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/49929) but hasn't shipped in a release yet.

This temporarily disables click-to-dismiss and keypress-to-dismiss on the splash screen. The event handlers in `splash.html` are retained so they can be re-enabled once the Electron fix is available.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm no crash occurs
- [ ] Confirm splash screen displays and auto-closes after main window loads

title: Fix FilePath::openForRead reporting "not found" for permission errors
description:
## Intent

Fix `FilePath::openForRead` to report the actual errno (e.g. `EACCES`) instead of always assuming `no_such_file_or_directory` when `std::ifstream` fails to open a file on non-Windows platforms.

## Summary

- Clear `errno` before calling `std::ifstream::open` so we get a reliable error code
- When the stream fails to open, use the actual `errno` value to construct the system error instead of hardcoding `no_such_file_or_directory`
- Windows codepath is unchanged (it uses a separate `file_descriptor_source` path)

## Motivation

When Posit Assistant's `read` tool tries to read a file with mode 000, it gets "File not found" instead of "Permission denied". The distinction matters because "permission denied" signals to the model that the file exists but is inaccessible, whereas "not found" suggests it should keep looking or try alternative paths.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reproduce: create a file with `chmod 000`, use Posit Assistant's `read` tool to read it, confirm the error now says "Permission denied" instead of "File not found"
- [ ] Verify normal file-not-found errors still report correctly

> [!WARNING]
> This change has not been compiled or tested locally due to build environment issues.

Note that this is specifically designed to prevent accidental mis-use; not as a
real security sandbox.

## Summary

- Adds infrastructure for injecting preflight hooks into base R functions
  (`addPreflightHook`, `addPreflightHooks`, `restoreBindings`)
- Validates file edit and read operations against an allowlist of directories
  (project dir, temp dir) before the real implementation executes
- Hooks cover file CRUD (`file.create`, `file.remove`, `file.rename`, `unlink`,
  etc.), I/O (`writeLines`, `cat`, `readBin`, `writeBin`, etc.), serialization
  (`save`, `saveRDS`, `dput`, `dump`), and filesystem metadata (`dir.create`,
  `Sys.chmod`, `Sys.setFileTime`)
- Hooks are injected in `chat.safeEval` and restored on exit

- [ ] Verify code assistant can write files within `tempdir()`
- [ ] Verify code assistant is blocked from writing files outside allowed directories

title: Fix Cmd+W in secondary windows also closing source tab in main window
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17115.

## Summary

On macOS, pressing Cmd+W in a secondary window (e.g. Shiny app running in a window, popped-out Help pane) would close the secondary window **and** close a source tab in the main window. This regression began with the Electron 38.7.0 update (#16665), which changed how macOS application menu accelerators interact with child windows.

The root cause: Electron's `Menu.setApplicationMenu()` registers accelerators globally on macOS. When Cmd+W was pressed in a secondary window, the `before-input-event` handler correctly closed the secondary window, but the global `closeSourceDoc` accelerator also fired and routed the command to the main window. `BrowserWindow.removeMenu()` (called via `ensureNoMenu()`) is a no-op on macOS since the application menu is application-wide.

The fix:

- Call `event.preventDefault()` in the `before-input-event` handler when intercepting Cmd+W. Per the Electron docs, this suppresses both page key events and menu shortcuts.
- In `GwtWindow.onCloseWindowShortcut()`, explicitly invoke `closeSourceDoc` (with `$RStudio.last_focused_window` routing) instead of relying on the now-suppressed menu accelerator.

## Test plan

- [ ] macOS: Open a Shiny app in a window, press Cmd+W — only the Shiny window closes, source tabs in main window are unaffected
- [ ] macOS: Pop out the Help pane, press Cmd+W — only the Help window closes
- [ ] macOS: With a source tab focused in the main window, press Cmd+W — the source tab closes as expected
- [ ] macOS: Open a separate source window (pop out a source tab), press Cmd+W — closes a source tab in that window, not in the main window
- [ ] macOS: Other shortcuts (Cmd+N, Cmd+O, etc.) still work from secondary windows and route to the main window
- [ ] Windows/Linux: No behavioral changes (the fix is macOS-only)

title: add support for parsing ISO 8601 dates with zones
description:
### Intent

The current datetime functions only support ISO 8601:2004, but the ISO 8601:2019 Extended format is more common on the modern Internet -- in particular, JavaScript's `Date.prototype.toISOString()` returns it. Furthermore, the current functions ignore timezone information even if it's provided. 

This new function, `parseUtcTimeFromIsoString`, supports both ISO 8601:2004 and ISO 8601:2019, in both Basic and Extended formats, and applies timezone conversions if time zones are supplied.

### Approach

Boost's `from_iso_string` and `time_from_string` functions only support one format each, and neither of them is 8601:2019 Extended. This function identifies which format the input uses and translates to one of the formats that Boost's parsers support.

Boost's `posix_time` functions ignore time zone information if it's present, so I had to write something to parse and apply them by hand.

### Automated Tests

This PR includes unit tests.

title: Fix blurry inline notebook plots on HiDPI displays
description:
## Intent

Addresses #16838.

## Summary

- Fixes a regression where inline notebook/Quarto plots rendered with custom figure dimensions (`fig-width`, `fig-height`, `fig-asp`) were blurry on HiDPI/Retina displays
- The device pixel ratio was only being applied to DPI when using automatic (pixel-based) sizing, not when using manual (inch-based) sizing
- Moves the `dpi * pixelRatio` scaling outside the `units == "px"` conditional so it applies to both sizing modes

## Details

Commit `98bc0203b5` ("support custom DPI in chunk plots") refactored `NotebookPlots.R` and inadvertently moved the DPI pixel-ratio scaling inside a conditional block that only executes for automatic sizing. Previously, DPI was unconditionally scaled via `res = 96 * pixelRatio`.

When a user specifies custom figure dimensions, the sizing mode is set to `PlotSizeManual` with `units = "in"`, which skipped the pixel ratio multiplication on DPI. This produced images at 96 DPI instead of 192 DPI on 2x Retina displays (e.g., 672x480 instead of 1344x960 for a 7x5 inch plot).

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a Quarto or R Notebook document on a HiDPI/Retina display
- [ ] Run a chunk with default figure settings — verify the plot is crisp
- [ ] Run a chunk with custom `fig-width`/`fig-height` — verify the plot is equally crisp

description:
## Intent

## Summary

- Adds handling for the ANSI CSI `K` (Erase in Line) escape sequence in `VirtualConsole`, supporting all three modes: erase to end of line (0/default), erase from beginning of line to cursor (1), and erase entire line (2).

title: Add capability negotiation to protocol handshake
description:
## Intent

Add capability negotiation to the `protocol/getVersion` handshake between rsession and the databot backend.

## Summary

- Define the list of JSON-RPC methods RStudio handles in `ChatConstants.cpp` (`rstudioCapabilities()`)
- Define the baseline peer capabilities assumed for protocol 8.0 (`baselinePeerCapabilities()`)
- Extend `handleGetProtocolVersion()` to read an optional `capabilities` array from the request and include RStudio's capabilities in the response
- Add `peerHasCapability()` query function for runtime checks
- Guard `requestBackendShutdown()` and `sendStreamingOutput()` with capability checks

Both sides exchange capability lists during the handshake. When a peer omits the field (older build), the baseline set for protocol 8.0 is assumed. This is additive within the current protocol version — no version bump needed.

Companion PR: https://github.com/posit-dev/databot/pull/604

## Test plan

- [ ] New RStudio + new databot: verify capabilities appear in handshake logs, `lifecycle/requestShutdown` sent only when peer advertises it
- [ ] New RStudio + old databot (no capabilities in request): verify baseline assumed, all notifications sent as before
- [ ] Old RStudio + new databot (no capabilities in response): verify databot assumes baseline

title: Make the "Session Suspended" view in Posit Assistant less distracting
description:
Addresses rstudio/rstudio#17017. Getting some mileage on PA during R package development today, this stuck out to me again. 

The simplest approach--an overlay on top of the iframe--results in a flicker of the PA homepage when `loadUrl()` navigates the iframe to a new URL.

Instead, on resume we create a second hidden iframe (`visibility: hidden`) and load the new URL into it. The old iframe stays untouched and visible through the overlay. Once the new iframe's React app has rendered (load event + 350ms), we flip it to visible, remove the old iframe, and remove the overlay:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c37b73e6-7d7e-42eb-bb58-df82935987c9

title: Add Claude hook to guard auto-generated files
description:
## Summary

- Adds a Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook in `.claude/settings.json` that blocks direct edits to auto-generated files, directing to the correct schema and regeneration script instead
- Guards 24 generated files across three codegen pipelines: `generate-prefs.R`, `generate-options.R`, and the GWT `ant` build

## Details

When Claude attempts to edit a generated file, the hook blocks the edit and displays an actionable message indicating which source file to edit and which script to run:

| Pipeline | Guarded Files | Redirect |
|----------|--------------|----------|
| `scripts/generate-prefs.R` | `UserPrefValues`, `UserStateValues`, `UserPrefsAccessor*`, `UserStateAccessor*`, `SessionUserPrefValues.R` | Edit schema in `src/cpp/session/resources/schema/` |
| `scripts/generate-options.R` | `ServerOptions.gen.hpp`, `SessionOptions.gen.hpp` | Edit `server-options.json` or `session-options.json` |
| GWT `ant` build | `CmdConstants*`, `MenuConstants*`, `Commands.cmd.xml.MD5` | Edit `Commands.cmd.xml` |

## Notes

- Requires `jq` and `grep` (available in any Unix shell or WSL)
- On native Windows without WSL, the hook fails with a non-blocking exit code, so normal editing is unaffected — the guard is simply inactive

## Test plan

- [x] Verify Claude blocks edits to `UserPrefValues.cpp` with the correct message
- [x] Verify Claude blocks edits to `ServerOptions.gen.hpp` with the correct message
- [x] Verify Claude blocks edits to `CmdConstants.java` with the correct message
- [x] Verify Claude can still edit non-generated files normally

title: Add workspace/editFileContent JSON-RPC handler
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17033

## Summary

- Add `workspace/editFileContent` RPC method so databot's `edit` tool routes file edits through rsession instead of performing read-modify-write on disk directly
- When the file is open in the editor, builds precise `replace_ranges` events so edits appear with working undo and dirty buffers are handled correctly
- When the file is not open, reads from disk with LF normalization, applies the replacement, and writes back preserving original line endings
- Supports `replaceAll` flag for multi-occurrence replacement, with ambiguity detection when disabled
- Handles untitled (unsaved) documents via the existing `untitled:<docId>` URI scheme

title: Fix Windows HOME for assistant and chat backend processes
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17056.

## Summary

- On Windows, R sets `HOME` to the user's Documents directory instead of `%USERPROFILE%`. The assistant and chat backend child processes inherited this incorrect `HOME`, causing tools like `git` to fail to find `~/.gitconfig` and other user config files.
- Call `setHomeToUserProfile()` when building the child process environment in both `SessionAssistant.cpp` and `SessionChat.cpp`, matching the existing pattern used by `SessionGit`, `SessionSVN`, and `SessionWorkbench`.

## Test plan

- [ ] On Windows, open Posit Assistant and ask it to run a git command (e.g. `git log --oneline -3`) — verify it finds `~/.gitconfig` and completes successfully
- [ ] Verify R code execution from the assistant is unaffected (R's own `HOME` is unchanged)

title: Use periodic scanning for monitored scratch directory on Windows
description:
## Intent

Addresses #15609 (at least for this scenario)

## Summary

On Windows, `initializeMonitoredUserScratchDir()` now uses periodic polling (every 3 seconds, idle-only) instead of native file monitoring (`ReadDirectoryChangesW`). This avoids `IRP_MJ_DIRECTORY_CONTROL` operations that enterprise endpoint security software can intercept synchronously, adding seconds to startup time.

The scanning code path (`scanForMonitoredPathChanges`) already existed as the error-recovery fallback when native monitoring fails. This change makes Windows use it from the start. `monitoredPathTree` now reports scan errors so that `scanForMonitoredPathChanges` can skip a cycle on failure instead of generating spurious events.

The directory is question is the user scratch directory: `%localappdata%\rstudio\monitored` (technically directories IN that directory are monitored).

Non-Windows platforms are unchanged.

## Test plan

Three features depend on the monitored scratch directory: Connection History, Lists/MRU, and Snippets.

**Startup performance (primary goal)**
- [ ] Windows with endpoint security: Launch RStudio on a Windows machine with enterprise endpoint security software (e.g., CrowdStrike, Carbon Black, Symantec). Measure startup time before and after the change. Expect a measurable improvement (seconds shaved off).
- [ ] Windows without endpoint security: Launch RStudio on a clean Windows machine. Verify startup time is not regressed.

**Connection history**
- [ ] Open RStudio on Windows, open the Connections pane, create a new database connection, disconnect, verify it appears in the connection history.
- [ ] Open a second RStudio session, make a connection change there, verify the first session picks up the change within ~3-6 seconds.

**Lists / MRU**
- [ ] Open several files to populate the MRU file list, verify the "Recent Files" menu updates correctly.
- [ ] Open a second session, open different files there, switch back to the first session — the MRU list should sync within ~3-6 seconds.

**Snippets**
- [ ] Go to Tools > Edit Snippets, add or modify a custom snippet, save and verify the snippet is available in autocomplete.
- [ ] In a second session, modify snippets and verify the first session picks up changes within ~3-6 seconds.

**Latency acceptability**
- [ ] Verify changes to monitored scratch files are detected within 3-6 seconds when idle. This is a slight regression from native monitoring (near-instant) but acceptable for this low-traffic directory.
- [ ] Verify that during active typing/execution, changes still get picked up once the session goes idle.

**Non-Windows regression**
- [ ] On macOS and Linux, verify Connection History, Lists, and Snippets still work as before (native file monitoring path is unchanged).

**Edge cases**
- [ ] Empty scratch directory: Start RStudio fresh (no prior state). Verify the scanner doesn't error on an empty tree.
- [ ] Session suspend/resume: Suspend and resume on Windows. Verify the periodic scanner continues working.

title: Fix writeFileContent to sync editor buffer and disk
description:
## Intent

Partially addresses #16951.

## Summary

- Fix the `replace_ranges` range calculation in `handleWriteFileContent()` to use the old editor buffer dimensions instead of the new content dimensions, preventing incorrect replacement bounds when the document changes size.
- For file-backed documents open in the editor, call `saveDocumentToDisk()` after updating the buffer so the file on disk matches and the dirty flag is cleared.
- For untitled documents, persist to the source database as dirty without attempting a disk write.
- On disk write failure, mark the document dirty and return an error so the user sees the new content and can save manually.

## Test plan

- [ ] Create an untitled buffer, use chat LLM to rewrite it. Verify editor shows new content with dirty indicator.
- [ ] Have the LLM write to a file not open in the editor. Verify file on disk has new content.
- [ ] Test with files where new content has more/fewer lines than old content. Verify no leftover old content at end of buffer.

title: Fix file type icons not showing on Linux
description: ## Intent Addresses #14626. ## Summary On Ubuntu 24.04 (and likely other distros), `.Rproj`, `.Rmd`, `.qmd`, and other RStudio-specific file types show generic/blank icons in the file manager. The root cause is twofold: 1. **Only 2 of 9 R-specific MIME type icons were installed** — the CMake rules only installed `application-x-r-data` (.RData) and `application-x-r-project` (.Rproj), missing 7 other types. 2. **The DEB/RPM postinst scripts didn't refresh the icon or MIME caches** after installation, so even installed icons weren't picked up. 3. **Ubuntu's Yaru icon theme doesn't fall back to hicolor** for MIME type icons ([GNOME/nautilus#2190](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/nautilus/-/issues/2190)), so icons in hicolor alone are invisible to Nautilus. ## Changes - **Install all R-specific MIME type icons** (`CMakeLists.txt`): Added install rules for `text-x-r-source` (.R), `text-x-r-doc` (.Rd), `text-x-r-sweave` (.Rnw/.Rtex), `text-x-quarto-markdown` (.qmd), `text-x-r-markdown` (.Rmd), `text-x-r-html` (.Rhtml), and `text-x-r-presentation` (.Rpres) across all 5 icon sizes. Generic icons (CSS, HTML, JS, markdown, TeX) are intentionally skipped to avoid overriding system-wide icon themes. - **Create missing 48x48 icon**: `text-x-r-presentation.png` was missing from the 48x48 directory (present at all other sizes). Scaled from the 64x64 version. - **Add explicit `` elements to MIME definitions** (`rstudio.xml`): Rather than relying on auto-derivation of icon names from MIME types, explicitly specify the icon name for each type. - **Refresh MIME and icon caches in packaging scripts**: Added `update-mime-database` and `gtk-update-icon-cache` calls (with `command -v` guards) to DEB and RPM post-install and post-remove scripts. - **Work around Ubuntu/Yaru icon theme bug** (DEB only): The postinst creates symlinks from installed Yaru theme directories to our hicolor icons, and the postrm cleans them up. This ensures Nautilus finds the icons regardless of the Yaru fallback bug. ## Before / After ## Test plan - [x] Build DEB package on Ubuntu 24.04 - [x] Install with `sudo dpkg -i rstudio-*.deb` - [x] Verify `xdg-mime query filetype test.Rproj` returns `application/x-r-project` - [x] Confirm file manager shows RStudio icons for `.Rproj`, `.Rmd`, `.qmd`, `.R`, `.Rd`, `.RData` files - [ ] Verify RPM install on Fedora refreshes caches correctly - [ ] Uninstall and verify icons revert to generic

title: Fix invisible return value visibility detection in chat code execution
description:
## Intent

Addresses rstudio/rstudio#17044.

Note: submitting on behalf of @gadenbuie (author of the fix).

## Summary

- Fix a bug where R's invisible return values (e.g. from `x <- 1:10`, `library(tidyverse)`, `invisible(NULL)`) were being printed in the Posit Assistant chat pane and R console during tool-call code execution.
- The root cause: when calling `.rs.chat.safeEval(exprSEXP)`, R evaluates `exprSEXP` during argument passing, which destroys visibility information. By wrapping the expression in `quote()` before passing it (`Rf_lang2(Rf_install("quote"), exprSEXP)`), the expression is passed unevaluated and `.rs.chat.safeEval()` can correctly detect visibility.

## Test plan

- [ ] In Posit Assistant, ask it to run `x <- 1:10` — the assignment should execute silently (no printed output in console or chat pane)
- [ ] Run `library(tidyverse)` — should not print the search path in the chat pane
- [ ] Run `1:10` (a visible expression) — should still print the result
- [ ] Run `invisible(NULL)` — should produce no printed output

title: Block user code execution during chat and fix busy state
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17023.

## Summary

- Block user code execution in the R console while the Chat feature is executing R code, preventing conflicts from concurrent R usage
- Expose `console_input::setExecuting()` so the chat module can signal busy state during direct R code execution
- Fix R session remaining stuck in "busy" state after chat code execution completes, which caused a spurious "The R session is currently busy" warning on quit
  - Root cause: chat executes R code directly via `r::exec::RFunction`, bypassing R's REPL loop whose `rBusy(false)` callback normally sends the `kBusy(false)` client event. The `kBusy(false)` event was never sent, leaving `WorkbenchContext.isServerBusy_` permanently true.
- Set Shell view to busy on `BusyEvent` so the console input is disabled while chat code runs

## Test plan

- [ ] Start a chat conversation that executes R code that takes a while (e.g., ask it to print 1 through 30, pausing 1 second after each number)
- [ ] Verify the R console shows as busy while chat code executes
- [ ] Verify user cannot submit code in the console while chat is executing
- [ ] After chat finishes, verify the console returns to the normal prompt state
- [ ] After chat finishes, verify quitting RStudio does **not** show "The R session is currently busy" warning
- [ ] Verify normal R console execution still works correctly (busy/not-busy transitions)
- [ ] Confirm that clicking the Stop button in console while chat code is executing stops the code (it will show up as an error on the chat side)

title: Save dirty editors before read/write tool operations
description:
## Summary

- When Posit AI's `read` tool targets a file that is open in RStudio's editor with unsaved changes (dirty), the file is now saved to disk before the tool operates on it
- The `write` tool now correctly replaces the entire document not just a subset
- `write` will ensure the modifications are reflected both in the editor (if file is open) and in the backing file (i.e. the file will be saved with the changes)
- Adds a `save_document` editor command event so the backend can trigger a frontend save, keeping the editor's dirty indicator in sync

## Intent

Addresses #16951 (for read and write tools; edit tool will be handled in a separate PR).

## QA Notes

1. Open a file in RStudio's editor and make unsaved changes (so the tab shows a dirty indicator)
2. Ask Posit Assistant to read the file — verify the file is saved first and the dirty indicator clears
3. Ask Posit Assistant to write/overwrite the file — verify the file is saved before the write occurs and the dirty indicator clears
<del>4. Verify untitled documents still work correctly with both read and write tools</del> - this is currently broken in general for the read and write tools: https://github.com/posit-dev/databot/issues/547
5. Verify files not open in the editor are read/written normally

## Test plan

- [ ] Dirty file-backed document is saved before read tool returns content
- [ ] Dirty file-backed document is correctly updated and saved when `write` is completed
- [ ] Frontend dirty indicator clears after backend-triggered save
- [ ] Files not open in the editor are unaffected

title: Improve Posit Assistant update error messages on Windows

## Intent

When updating Posit Assistant on Windows with multiple RStudio instances running, file locks on backend executables cause the update to fail. Previously all update errors showed the unhelpful generic message "Update failed: Error occurred while executing method". Now:

| Download error | "Download failed: [specific error]" |

title: Fix duplicate chunk toolbar when pressing Enter at end of document
description:
## Intent

Addresses #16995.

## Summary

- When a code chunk is defined at the bottom of an R Markdown document, pressing Enter after the chunk header (e.g. `` ```{r} ``) could cause the chunk toolbar to be duplicated on the newly created line.
- Ace's line widget manager shifts widgets down when a newline is inserted on their row, unless the widget has a `column` property set. Without it, the widget is displaced, and `PinnedLineWidget`'s anchor-based repositioning fails to correct it at the end of the document (because the end anchor is clamped to the last row, so anchors don't move and the shift goes undetected).
- Set `column = 0` on all pinned line widgets so Ace only shifts them when content is inserted before column 0, leaving repositioning to the existing anchor mechanism.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an R Markdown document and create a code chunk at the bottom of the document by typing `` ```{r} `` and pressing Enter. Verify only one chunk toolbar appears.
- [ ] Verify that creating chunks in the middle of a document still works correctly.
- [ ] Verify that MathJax previews and inline image previews still render and pin correctly after edits around them.

title: Avoid unnecessary widget detach/reattach on Pane Layout changes
description:
## Summary

- Avoid unnecessary `onUnload`/`onLoad` lifecycle events on all tab widgets when Sidebar visibility is toggled
- Avoid unnecessary `onUnload`/`onLoad` lifecycle events on all tab widgets when Pane Layout preferences are applied, by removing explicit `clear()` calls that defeated the existing `areTabsIdentical()` optimization in `WorkbenchTabPanel.setTabs()`
- Fix broken `PaneConfig.isEqualTo()` JSNI method (referenced wrong JS property `this.panes` instead of `quadrants`, and omitted several fields) and add early-return when config content is unchanged
- Add `clearing_` flag protection to `WorkbenchTabPanel.setTabs()` to prevent spurious selection events during tab panel rebuilds

## Intent

When the user opens Global Options > Pane Layout and clicks OK, or toggles the visibility of the Sidebar, all widgets in all tab panels were being detached and reattached — even tabs that didn't move. This triggered unnecessary `onUnload`/`onLoad` lifecycle events on every widget (Help, Plots, Files, etc.), causing state loss and performance issues.

## Changes

- **PaneManager.java**: Removed 3 explicit `clear()` calls before `populateTabPanel()` — `setTabs()` already handles unchanged tabs via `areTabsIdentical()` and GWT auto-reparents widgets that move between panels. Added early-return when config is identical.
- **WorkbenchTabPanel.java**: Wrapped `tabPanel_.clear()`/`tabs_.clear()` in `setTabs()` with `clearing_` flag to match existing protection in the standalone `clear()` method.
- **PaneConfig.java**: Replaced broken JSNI `isEqualTo()` with Java implementation comparing all fields (quadrants, tabsets, sidebar, console positions, etc.).
- **HelpPane.java**: Removed debug logging (`Debug.logToConsole` in `onLoad()`) and unused import.

title: Fix AceEditor command dispatch in Visual mode code chunks
description:
## Intent

Addresses #17007.

## Summary

- `AceEditor` registers its event bus listeners (including the `AceEditorCommandEvent` handler used by `AceEditorCommandDispatcher`) in response to GWT's `AttachEvent`. In Visual mode, code chunk editors have their DOM elements managed by Panmirror rather than GWT's widget hierarchy, so `AttachEvent` never fires and the command handlers are never registered.
- Call `registerEditorEventListeners()` in the constructor so that listeners are registered eagerly, regardless of how the editor is attached to the DOM.
- Make `registerEditorEventListeners()` idempotent (clears existing registrations before re-registering) so it is safe to call from both the constructor and the attach handler. The attach handler call is still needed because pane layout changes can trigger widget detach/re-attach cycles via `BinarySplitLayoutPanel.setWidgets()`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an R Markdown or Quarto document in Visual mode
- [ ] Click into a code chunk
- [ ] Verify that AceEditor keyboard shortcuts work (e.g. insert assignment operator, insert pipe operator, move lines up/down, yank/paste)
- [ ] Switch to Source mode and verify the same shortcuts still work
- [ ] Verify no regressions with the Console editor

description:

Since `.rs.valueContentsImpl()` unconditionally removes the first line of `str()` output expecting it to be the header, the first list element was silently dropped in the Environment pane.
- Fix detects whether the header is actually present by checking if the first line is indented (a data line) vs unindented (a header line), and only removes it when it's a real header.

title: Fix AceEditorCommandDispatcher shortcuts broken by handler leak fix
description:
## Intent

Addresses #16973.

## Summary

Two issues were causing keyboard shortcuts dispatched via `AceEditorCommandDispatcher` (insert pipe operator, insert assignment operator, yank region, etc.) to fail:

1. **Primary issue**: The handler leak fix (25bfce44c4) added the `AceEditorCommandEvent` EventBus handler to `editorEventListeners_`. However, `updateKeyboardHandlers()` clears this entire list whenever keyboard handlers are refreshed (on file type set, vim/emacs toggle). After the first refresh, the `AceEditorCommandEvent` handler was removed and never re-registered, silently breaking all `AceEditorCommandDispatcher` commands.

   Fix: Introduce a separate `keyboardHandlers_` list for the Ace-native handlers managed by `updateKeyboardHandlers()`, so lifetime editor event handlers (`AceEditorCommandEvent`, `EditEvent`, `colorPreview`) survive keyboard handler refreshes.

2. **Secondary issue**: The capturing keydown handler for ghost text suggestions checked whether the typed key matched the start of the suggestion text without checking for modifier keys. This could cause shortcuts like Ctrl+Shift+M to be intercepted when ghost text happened to start with the same letter.

   Fix: Skip ghost text prefix matching when Ctrl, Alt, or Meta is held.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a source file and verify Ctrl+Shift+M (insert pipe operator) works
- [ ] Verify Alt+- (insert assignment operator) works
- [ ] Verify other AceEditorCommandDispatcher commands work (move lines up/down, block indent/outdent, etc.)
- [ ] Toggle vim mode on/off, then verify shortcuts still work
- [ ] Verify shortcuts work both with and without ghost text suggestions visible
- [ ] Verify ghost text prefix matching still works for normal typing (no modifiers)

title: fix console warning box including excess content
description:
## Summary

- Adds `console_output::write()` and `writeLine()` helper functions that print messages to the console with appropriate ANSI escape annotations and reset the pending output type afterwards
- Updates the Rtools warning and R version change warning to use the new API

## Intent

Addresses #16885.

## Details

When warning messages were printed via `REprintf` (like the Rtools warning), they would trigger the warning annotation system because the output matched the warning prefix regex. This caused all subsequent console output to be incorrectly included in the warning box until R became idle.

The new `console_output::write()` function:
1. Wraps the message with ANSI group markers (if annotation is enabled)
2. Prints to the appropriate stream (stdout/stderr)

title: Fix Packages pane checkboxes for renv projects with shared cache
description:
## Intent

Addresses #16842.

## Summary

When renv uses a shared cache, packages in the project library are symlinks pointing to packages in the cache. The Packages pane was not correctly identifying loaded/attached packages because path comparisons failed when comparing the symlink path with the resolved cache path.

This fix uses `normalizePath()` to resolve symlinks before comparing paths in three places:

- **`listInstalledPackages`**: when checking if a package is loaded (fixes initial checkbox state)
- **`is_package_attached`**: when checking if a specific package is attached  
- **`reportPackageStatus`**: when sending package status change events (fixes dynamic checkbox updates)

title: Fix column collapse when changing layout in Pane Layout Preferences
description:
## Summary
- Fix bug where adding source columns via Pane Layout Preferences caused all columns to collapse to zero width when the sidebar was visible
- Fix bug where toggling sidebar visibility from hidden to visible via Pane Layout Preferences caused the sidebar and right column to collapse to zero width

Addresses #16845

## Root Cause
When layout changes (adding columns or toggling sidebar visibility) are applied via the Preferences dialog, the `userPrefs.panes()` ValueChangeHandler in PaneManager executes before the browser completes rendering the new layout. This causes `getOffsetWidth()` to return 0, triggering resize logic that collapses columns.

Additionally, when showing a hidden sidebar, calling `refreshSidebar()` caused a redundant destroy/recreate cycle that broke the layout.

## Fix
- Defer `setGlobalValue()` when column count, sidebar visibility, or sidebar location changes, giving the browser time to render
- Only call `clearSidebarCache()` and `refreshSidebar()` when the sidebar was already visible (not when transitioning from hidden to visible)
- Add element ID for the Add Column button to support automation testing

## QA Notes
1. Start RStudio in default layout (sidebar hidden)
2. Go to Tools > Global Options > Pane Layout
3. Click "Add Column" button
4. Click OK
5. Verify all columns (Source, Console, TabSet) have reasonable widths (not collapsed)

6. Reset layout, then:
7. Go to Pane Layout Preferences
8. Check "Sidebar Visible" checkbox
9. Click OK
10. Verify sidebar appears with proper width and all other columns are not collapsed
11. Test with sidebar visible on right side as well

title: Send incremental R session variable changes to AI assistant
description:
## Intent

Implements LSP-style session notifications to send incremental R session variable changes to the AI assistant, rather than sending the full variable context with every completion request.

## Summary

- Add `session/didCreate` notification when Posit AI agent initializes (includes sessionId and languageId)
- Add `session/didDestroy` notification when agent stops
- Add `session/didChangeVariables` notification when variables are created, modified, or deleted
- Classify variable changes as create/modify/delete based on EnvironmentMonitor diff analysis
- Add `onEnvironmentVariablesChanged` signal to SessionModuleContext for cross-module communication
- Currently enabled only for Posit AI via `supportsSessionNotifications()` check

## Notification Format

```json
// session/didCreate
{ "sessionId": "uuid", "languageId": "r" }

// session/didChangeVariables
{
  "sessionId": "uuid",
  "variables": [
    { "name": "df", "type": "data.frame", "action": "create", "children": [...] },
    { "name": "x", "type": "numeric", "action": "modify" },
    { "name": "old_var", "type": "", "action": "delete" }
  ],
  "reset": false  // true when environment is cleared
}
```

## Test Plan

title: Fix RStudio Chat WebSocket connection for remote access
description:
Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16933

## Summary

- Return relative WebSocket paths in server mode instead of absolute URLs
- This ensures the WebSocket connection uses the same hostname as the page, guaranteeing the `port-token` cookie is sent with the upgrade request

## Problem

RStudio Chat works when accessing RStudio Server via `localhost:8787` but fails when accessed via IP address from a remote machine. The root cause is a cookie domain scoping issue where the `port-token` cookie is not sent with WebSocket requests when the hostname differs.

## Solution

Changed `buildWebSocketUrl()` to return a relative path (e.g., `/p/xxxxxxxx/ai-chat`) instead of an absolute URL in server mode. The client then constructs the full WebSocket URL using `window.location`, ensuring the hostname matches and the cookie is sent.

## Test plan

- [ ] Access RStudio Server via localhost - verify Chat works
- [ ] Access RStudio Server via IP address - verify Chat works
- [ ] Access RStudio Server via domain name with HTTPS - verify Chat works
- [ ] Test RStudio Desktop - verify no regression

**Note:** Requires corresponding change in Posit AI client.

title: Improve ghost text rendering with synthetic token support
description:
## Motivation

The ghost text and edit suggestion system had grown organically with separate state tracking for different suggestion types (inline completions vs NES). This led to:

- **Duplicate state**: `activeCompletion_` and `nesCompletion_` tracked similar information separately
- **Anchor management complexity**: Suggestion anchors were instance variables separate from the suggestion state they tracked
- **Inconsistent naming**: Methods like `applyNesSuggestion` handled both NES and ghost text cases
- **Subtle bugs**: The prefix-matching logic for ghost text was incorrectly applied to NES suggestions, and anchor divergence caused acceptance bugs

This refactoring consolidates the suggestion state into a single `EditSuggestion` class, moves anchors into that class, and clarifies the code paths for different suggestion types.

## Summary

- Consolidate `nesCompletion_` and `activeCompletion_` into single `editSuggestion_` field with unified `EditSuggestion` class
- Move suggestion anchors (`startAnchor`, `endAnchor`) into `EditSuggestion` class with `detachAnchors()` method
- Rename methods for clarity: `applyNesSuggestion` → `acceptEditSuggestion`, `clearNesVisuals` → `clearSuggestionVisuals`, `doesChangeIntersectNesSuggestion` → `doesChangeIntersectSuggestion`
- Fix ghost text acceptance after typing prefix matches: use `startAnchor` for both range endpoints since ghost text is a pure insertion (not a replacement)
- Fix NES suggestion dismissal: restrict prefix-matching logic to ghost text only, so NES suggestions properly dismiss when typing at the end of the range
- Implement synthetic token API for custom ghost text rendering that persists across re-tokenization and document edits
- Add coordinate conversion overrides so cursor position is computed correctly with synthetic tokens present

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify ghost text appears correctly at cursor position
- [ ] Verify typing a prefix match updates ghost text and acceptance works correctly
- [ ] Verify cursor positioning is correct when clicking near ghost text
- [ ] Verify NES insertion previews render correctly
- [ ] Verify NES suggestions dismiss when typing at the end of the completion range
- [ ] Verify cleanup works correctly when dismissing suggestions

title: Fix stale error messages on interrupted code execution
description:
## Problem

When code execution is interrupted (e.g., by clicking Stop during `Sys.sleep(60)`), the tool was returning stale error messages from previous R session activity instead of cleanly reporting the interruption.

## Solution

Use `tryCatch(..., error = identity, interrupt = identity)` at the R level to capture errors and interrupts as condition objects. The C++ code then inspects the class of the returned object using `Rf_inherits()` to determine what happened:

- **Interrupt**: Treated as a regular error with message "Execution interrupted"
- **Error**: Message extracted using `conditionMessage()`
- **Success**: Normal `withVisible()` result with `$value` and `$visible`

## Changes

- Added `.rs.chat.safeEval()` helper function in SessionChat.R
- Modified expression evaluation loop in SessionChat.cpp to use the new helper
- Interrupts are now treated as regular errors (displayed but don't cancel the response)

## Benefits

1. Error messages are always fresh, extracted directly from condition objects
2. No reliance on stale console output buffers
3. Clean distinction between interrupts, errors, and successful evaluation

title: Avoid logging errors for non-existent directories in findProgramOnPath on Windows
description:
## Fix excessive error logging in Windows findProgramOnPath

Addresses #16839

### Summary

On Windows, when the PATH environment variable contains non-existent directories (e.g., `/usr/bin`, RStudio logs hundreds of spurious "system error 2" (file not found) errors during session startup and ongoing use.

### Problem

The `findProgramOnPath` function in `Win32System.cpp` calls `FilePath(path).completeChildPath(program + ext)` on every PATH entry without first checking if the directory exists. The `completeChildPath` method logs an error when the parent path doesn't exist, resulting in log spam like:

```
ERROR system error 2 (The system cannot find the file specified); OCCURRED AT: ...
```

In testing, a single `/usr/bin` entry in PATH generated 656+ error log entries during normal RStudio usage.

### Root Cause

This issue has existed since `findProgramOnPath` was added in July 2021 (commit 2817de9f13). The POSIX implementation correctly uses `open()` to check directory existence before proceeding, but the Windows implementation lacked an equivalent check.

### Solution

Add a directory existence check before calling `completeChildPath`, matching the POSIX implementation's approach:

This change:
- Skips non-existent PATH directories early, avoiding unnecessary filesystem operations
- Prevents spurious error logging from `completeChildPath`
- Creates the `FilePath` object once and reuses it (minor optimization)
- Matches the defensive approach used in the POSIX implementation

### Testing

- Build on Windows and verify no compilation errors
- Set PATH to include a non-existent directory like `/usr/bin`
- Start RStudio and open a session
- Verify rsession log contains no "system error 2" entries for the non-existent path
- Verify that programs in valid PATH directories (e.g., quarto, git) are still found correctly

### Impact

- **Log cleanliness**: Eliminates hundreds of spurious error entries

title: Fix Copilot sign-in button not appearing when selecting GitHub Copilot
description:
## Summary
- Fixes issue where selecting "GitHub Copilot" from the Assistant dropdown didn't show the sign-in button immediately
- Users previously had to apply settings, close, and reopen the dialog to see the correct status
- Also adds immediate disable behavior when switching away from Copilot (matching old checkbox behavior)

## Root Cause
PR #16823 replaced the "Enable GitHub Copilot" checkbox with a dropdown selector but removed the eager-save behavior. The old checkbox handler called `prefs_.writeUserPrefs()` before `refresh()`, which allowed the backend to start/stop the Copilot agent immediately. Without this, the backend didn't know about preference changes until Apply was clicked.

## Solution
Restore the eager-save behavior from the old checkbox implementation:

- **When selecting Copilot**: If not already enabled, verify installation and eagerly save preferences, then refresh status to show correct sign-in state
- **When selecting None or Posit AI**: If Copilot was enabled, eagerly save preferences to stop the agent immediately

## Test plan
- [ ] New user: Select "GitHub Copilot" from dropdown → Sign In button appears immediately
- [ ] Existing signed-in user: Open preferences → Sign Out button appears correctly
- [ ] Copilot enabled → Select None → Agent stops immediately
- [ ] Copilot enabled → Select Posit AI → Agent stops immediately
- [ ] None → Copilot → None → Copilot → Works correctly through multiple toggles

Addresses #16831

title: Add Posit AI feature flag
description:
## Intent

This accomplishes two things:

- added a feature flag to control whether Posit Assistant features are shown in the UI (defaults to OFF for Server Pro, on for open-source and Desktop Pro)
- don't show Posit AI in the list of assistant choices if it is hidden via feature flag or the existing setting

## Summary

Add a new `allow-posit-assistant` admin setting to control availability of the Posit AI assistant feature in RStudio Pro.

**Behavior:**
- **Open-source**: The `allow-posit-assistant` setting is ignored (always treated as `true`). Feature availability is controlled only by the user's `pai` preference.
- **RStudio Desktop Pro**: Same as open-source - setting is ignored.
- **RStudio Server Pro**: The feature is hidden by default. Admins must set `allow-posit-assistant=true` in the session configuration to make the feature available. Users must also enable the `pai` preference.

This follows the same pattern as other "allow" options (e.g., `allow-shell`, `allow-vcs`) using the `allowOverlay()` mechanism.

## Changes

### C++ (Session)

- **session-options.json**: Added `allow-posit-assistant` option with `defaultValue: false`
- **SessionOptions.gen.hpp**: Auto-generated accessor `allowPositAssistant()` with `|| allowOverlay()` pattern
- **SessionChat.cpp**: Added `isPaiEnabled()` helper function; updated 4 permission checks to use it
- **SessionClientInit.cpp**: Exposed `allow_posit_assistant` to the client via SessionInfo

### Java (GWT Client)

- **PaiUtil.java** (new): Static utility class with `isPaiEnabled(SessionInfo, UserPrefs)` helper
- **SessionInfo.java**: Added `getAllowPositAssistant()` accessor
- **PaneManager.java**: Updated 4 checks to use `PaiUtil.isPaiEnabled()`
- **PaneLayoutPreferencesPane.java**: Added Session injection; updated Chat pane visibility check
- **AboutDialog.java**: Updated Posit Assistant version fetch check
- **AssistantPreferencesPane.java**: Conditionally include Posit AI in assistant selector dropdown
- **ProjectAssistantPreferencesPane.java**: Same conditional logic for project-level preferences

## Helper Functions

Created centralized helper functions to simplify future removal of the temporary `pai` preference:

**C++ (`SessionChat.cpp`):**
```cpp
bool isPaiEnabled()
{
   return options().allowPositAssistant() && prefs::userPrefs().pai();
}
```

**Java (`PaiUtil.java`):**
```java
public static boolean isPaiEnabled(SessionInfo sessionInfo, UserPrefs userPrefs)
{
   return sessionInfo.getAllowPositAssistant() && userPrefs.pai().getGlobalValue();
}
```

## Configuration

In RStudio Server Pro, admins can enable the feature by adding to `rsession.conf`:
```
allow-posit-assistant=true
```

## Test Plan

- [ ] Open-source build: Verify `allow-posit-assistant` setting has no effect (feature controlled only by `pai` preference)
- [ ] Desktop Pro build: Verify `allow-posit-assistant` setting has no effect (feature controlled only by `pai` preference)
- [ ] Server Pro build with default config: Verify Posit AI is hidden even if `pai=TRUE`
- [ ] Server Pro build with `allow-posit-assistant=true`: Verify Posit AI appears when `pai=TRUE`
- [ ] Verify Chat pane visibility respects the combined check
- [ ] Verify Assistant preferences pane only shows Posit AI option when enabled
- [ ] Verify Project Assistant preferences pane only shows Posit AI option when enabled
- [ ] Verify About dialog only fetches Posit Assistant version when enabled

title: Fix deprecated macOS API usage in Keychain handling
description:
For years we've been getting the following warnings when building RStudio on macOS:

```
[184/668] Building CXX object src/cpp/core/CMakeFiles/rstudio-core.dir/http/Keychain.mm.o
/Users/gary/chat/rstudio/src/cpp/core/http/Keychain.mm:38:13: warning: 'SecKeychainOpen' is deprecated: first deprecated in macOS 10.10 - SecKeychain is deprecated [-Wdeprecated-declarations]
   38 |    status = SecKeychainOpen(kRootCertsKeychainPath, &rootCertsKeychain);
      |             ^
/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/Security.framework/Headers/SecKeychain.h:294:10: note: 'SecKeychainOpen' has been explicitly marked deprecated here
  294 | OSStatus SecKeychainOpen(const char *pathName, SecKeychainRef * __nonnull CF_RETURNS_RETAINED keychain)
      |          ^
/Users/gary/chat/rstudio/src/cpp/core/http/Keychain.mm:47:4: warning: 'SecKeychainCopySearchList' is deprecated: first deprecated in macOS 10.10 - SecKeychain is deprecated [-Wdeprecated-declarations]
   47 |    SecKeychainCopySearchList(&currentSearchList);
      |    ^
/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/Security.framework/Headers/SecKeychain.h:404:10: note: 'SecKeychainCopySearchList' has been explicitly marked deprecated here
  404 | OSStatus SecKeychainCopySearchList(CFArrayRef * __nonnull CF_RETURNS_RETAINED searchList)
      |          ^
```

# Replace deprecated macOS Keychain APIs

## Summary

Replace deprecated `SecKeychainOpen` and `SecKeychainCopySearchList` APIs with modern equivalents to eliminate compiler warnings on macOS. These APIs were deprecated in macOS 10.10.

## Changes

- Replace `SecKeychainOpen` + `SecKeychainCopySearchList` with `SecTrustCopyAnchorCertificates()` to retrieve system root certificates
- Use `SecItemCopyMatching` without a custom search list for user/system keychain certificates
- Add deduplication to handle certificates that may appear in both sources
- Add null checks for defensive coding
- Extract certificate data copying into a helper function to reduce duplication

## Why This Approach

The old code manually opened the SystemRootCertificates keychain and added it to the search list. The modern approach is:

1. `SecTrustCopyAnchorCertificates()` - directly retrieves trusted root certificates (available since macOS 10.3, not deprecated)
2. `SecItemCopyMatching` - retrieves certificates from user/system keychains using default search behavior

This achieves the same result without deprecated APIs.

## Testing

Verify HTTPS connectivity works correctly:
- Package installation from CRAN/GitHub over HTTPS
- Any feature that makes HTTPS requests to external servers
- If using internal CAs, verify connections to internal HTTPS servers

## Risk Assessment

**Low risk**:
- Uses stable, non-deprecated APIs that have been available for 20+ years
- Functionally equivalent to the old implementation
- Deduplication ensures no change in certificate set returned
- Includes defensive null checks

title: Fix intermittent mouse selection failure in source editor
description:
## Summary

- Adds automatic detection and recovery for corrupt Ace mouse handler state
- When an uncaught JavaScript exception occurs during mouse event handling, the MouseHandler can be left in an inconsistent state where mouse selection stops working for that editor tab
- Recovery is triggered when tabs are activated, so switching away and back to an affected tab will restore functionality

Addresses #13436

## Details

The root cause analysis suggests that Ace's MouseHandler can get stuck in a corrupt state when:
- An exception occurs during `onCaptureEnd` before cleanup code runs
- The `inVirtualSelectionMode` flag gets stuck `true` in multi-select scenarios
- The `state` property remains at a non-empty value like `"select"` or `"drag"`

This PR adds two methods to `AceEditorNative`:
- `isMouseHandlerStateCorrupt()` - detects suspicious state combinations (e.g., non-empty state when mouse is not pressed)
- `resetMouseHandlerState()` - resets all relevant state variables to their default values

The check runs in `AceEditorWidget.onActivate()`, so whenever a user switches to a tab with corrupt state, it will be automatically recovered.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify normal mouse selection still works correctly
- [ ] Verify multi-cursor selection (Alt+click) still works
- [ ] Verify drag-and-drop text still works (if enabled)
- [ ] If the bug can be reproduced, verify that switching tabs recovers the editor

title: Add punctuation color extraction with fallback logic
description:
Followup to https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/16812.

## Fix brace visibility in chat UI code blocks with dark themes

### Problem

Braces (`{` and `}`) are very hard to see in the chat UI code blocks when using dark RStudio themes like Dracula, Tomorrow Night, and others.

### Root Cause

The `ThemeColorExtractor` extracts `--rstudio-syntax-punctuation` from the `.ace_punctuation` CSS class, but most dark themes don't define this class. When the class is undefined, `getComputedStyle()` on a hidden element returns an inherited/default color that may have low contrast against dark backgrounds.

Meanwhile, braces in ACE are actually styled by `.ace_keyword.ace_operator`, not `.ace_punctuation`. The chat UI's syntax highlighter (Shiki) tokenizes braces as `punctuation.bracket` and maps them to `--rstudio-syntax-punctuation`, which was extracting the wrong color.

### Solution

Added a new `extractPunctuationColor()` method with a proper fallback chain:

1. First tries `.ace_paren.ace_keyword.ace_operator` (exact match for how ACE tokenizes braces)
2. Then tries `.ace_keyword.ace_operator` (what themes actually define for operators)
3. Then tries `.ace_punctuation` (for themes like Monokai that do define it)
4. Falls back to foreground color

This ensures braces in chat code blocks use the same visible colors as operators in the ACE editor.

### Expected Results by Theme

| Theme | Brace Color | Source |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| Monokai | Gray (#AAAAAA) | `.ace_keyword.ace_operator` |
| Dracula | Pink (#ff79c6) | `.ace_keyword.ace_operator` |
| Tomorrow Night | Teal (#8ABEB7) | `.ace_keyword.ace_operator` |

### Testing

1. Build RStudio with `ant draft` or full build
2. Run RStudio and select a dark theme (Dracula, Tomorrow Night, Monokai, etc.)
3. Open the chat pane
4. Send a message that generates code containing braces (e.g., ask for a function definition)
5. Verify braces are visible with good contrast in the code block
6. Test switching between different dark themes while the chat pane is open

title: Sync code theme colors with chat
description:
## Summary

Adds syntax highlighting color extraction to `ThemeColorExtractor` so that the Posit Assistant chat UI can display code blocks with colors that match the RStudio editor theme.

Previously, only UI colors (background, foreground, borders) were synced to the chat iframe. Code blocks in the chat used fixed Prism themes that didn't match RStudio's editor, causing visual inconsistency and poor readability—especially with dark themes where contrast was often too low.

## Changes

- Extract 12 syntax highlighting colors from the current Ace editor theme:
  - **Core tokens**: keyword, string, comment, number, function, operator
  - **Extended tokens**: variable, punctuation, constant, class-name, tag, attr-name
- Add new CSS variables (`--rstudio-syntax-*`) that are injected into the chat iframe
- Add fallback values for all syntax colors in case extraction fails

## Implementation Details

The extraction follows the existing pattern from `PanmirrorThemeCreator.java`, using `DomUtils.extractCssValue()` to sample colors from Ace CSS classes like `ace_keyword`, `ace_string`, etc.

title: Implement macOS font enumeration and remove node-system-fonts dependency
description:
Prerequisite work for updating electron (#16802).

## Summary

Replace the `node-system-fonts` npm package with a native CoreText implementation for enumerating fonts on macOS. This eliminates a native dependency that had compatibility issues and reduces the overall dependency footprint.

- Implement native macOS font enumeration using CoreText APIs in `desktop.cc`
- Remove `node-system-fonts` package dependency
- Maintain identical behavior to the previous implementation

## Background

The [node-system-fonts](https://github.com/jgilsaa/node-system-fonts) package is a native Node.js addon that wraps platform-specific font APIs. It seems abandoned (no updates in 6 years) and is no longer compatible with newer node.js releases used by latest Electron. So we need a different way to accomplish this on macOS.

## Implementation Details

### macOS (`desktop.cc`)

The new `macOSListFonts()` function uses CoreText APIs to enumerate system fonts:

- Uses `CTFontCollectionCreateFromAvailableFonts()` to get all available fonts
- Iterates through font descriptors to extract font information
- Returns **PostScript names** (e.g., "Menlo-Regular") for monospace fonts (used in the font picker)
- Returns **family names** (e.g., "Lucida Grande") for proportional fonts (used for UI font availability checking)

The implementation matches the previous `node-system-fonts` behavior:
- Filters out hidden fonts (starting with `.`)
- Filters out vertically-oriented fonts (starting with `@`)
- Filters out symbol/ornament fonts (like Wingdings)
- Filters out italic font variants (matched old behavior where the matching algorithm penalized italic mismatches)

### Windows

No changes - continues to use the existing `win32ListMonospaceFonts()` implementation.

### Linux

No changes - continues to use `fc-list` via fontconfig.

## Files Changed

- **binding.gyp**: Add CoreText framework linking for macOS
- **package.json**: Remove `node-system-fonts` dependency
- **desktop.cc**: Add `macOSListFonts()` native function
- **desktop.node.d.ts**: Add TypeScript declaration for new function
- **gwt-callback.ts**: Use new native function on macOS, refactor platform-specific code paths

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify monospace font list in Preferences > Appearance matches previous behavior on macOS
- [ ] Verify proportional font detection works (UI uses correct system font)
- [ ] Verify font enumeration still works on Windows
- [ ] Verify font enumeration still works on Linux
- [ ] Build succeeds on all platforms

title: Prevent child processes from inheriting parent-side handles in Win32ChildProcess
description:
### Intent

Addresses #16799

### Summary

Fixes a Windows-only bug where switching RMarkdown or Quarto documents into Visual Mode would show an infinite spinner and never complete. The issue was introduced in #16727 (commit d03d216b27514da3e5f7b23f1c06cba87970a549).

### Root Cause

The problematic commit increased pipe buffer sizes by passing `SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES` with `bInheritHandle = TRUE` to `CreatePipe()`. This made **both** ends of each pipe inheritable by child processes, not just the child-side handles.

Before:
- `CreatePipe(..., nullptr, 0)` created non-inheritable handles by default
- Only child-side handles (stdin read, stdout/stderr write) were explicitly made inheritable via `SetHandleInformation`

After the change:
- `CreatePipe(..., &sa, 256 * 1024)` with `sa.bInheritHandle = TRUE` made **both** ends inheritable
- Child processes inherited parent-side handles (stdin write, stdout/stderr read)
- Pipes never properly closed because child processes held copies of parent handles
- Panmirror hung during initialization waiting for input that never completed

### The Fix

After creating each pipe with the increased buffer size, explicitly set the parent-side handles to non-inheritable:

- `pImpl_->hStdInWrite` - parent writes to child's stdin
- `pImpl_->hStdOutRead` - parent reads from child's stdout
- `pImpl_->hStdErrRead` - parent reads from child's stderr

This restores the correct handle inheritance behavior while maintaining the increased 256KB buffer size that prevents pipe saturation.

### Testing

1. Create a new RMarkdown or Quarto document in RStudio on Windows
2. Click the "Visual" button to switch to Visual Mode
3. Verify that Visual Mode loads successfully without an infinite spinner
4. Verify that Visual Mode functionality works correctly (editing, saving, etc.)

### Files Changed

- `src/cpp/core/system/Win32ChildProcess.cpp` - Added `SetHandleInformation` calls to clear `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` on parent-side pipe handles

title: Added a cache around ssl contexts
description:
This will significantly speed up https client requests made by the rsession. Currently, for each request we search the default CA registry and load up all of the certs.

### Intent

Addresses: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/9770

### Approach

The SSL context takes the "verify T/F" flag and an optional custom CA. When not using custom CA's, there can only be two of them so there's no need for cache management and as far as I can tell, RStudio never uses custom CA's for it's client requests.

So for RStudio there will only be one ssl context that's cached. For any downstream dependencies that use lots of custom CAs, you'll need to use removeCertFromCache when that custom CA is no longer needed (or periodically use the api to clear the cache). 

(Note: workbench has a companion PR to remove the sesison-ssl-cert)

### Automated Tests

No behavior should change. This will be well covered by automation.

title: Fix issue with opening files via double-clicking in file explorer when RStudio has secondary windows open
description:
### Intent

Addresses #16740

### Approach

When a secondary window (viewer or plot zoom) is open and a user double-clicks a file that RStudio is registered to open from the OS file explorer, the file would incorrectly attempt to open in the satellite window, which was a no-op.

The `openFile` function in `desktop-bridge.ts` used `webContents.getAllWebContents()` which returns windows in an **undefined order**. The code then iterated through all windows and selected the first one with `desktopHooks`, which could be a satellite window rather than the main window.

Similarly, `args-manager.ts` used `webContents.getAllWebContents()[0]` to determine which window to activate, which was also non-deterministic.

Ensure files always open in the main window by using the stored reference to the main window (`gwtCallback.mainWindow`) instead of iterating through all web contents.

### Automated Tests

None

### QA Notes

1. Open RStudio
2. Knit an Rmd file to HTML and leave the viewer window open (or open a plot zoom window)
3. Navigate to file explorer and double-click a different Rmd file
4. Verify the main IDE window receives focus and the file opens in a new tab
5. Repeat test on Windows and Linux

Note that this issue and fix isn't specific to Rmd files, but for any file types that RStudio is registered to open.

title: Fix child process exit
description:
### Intent

> Describe briefly what problem this pull request resolves, or what new feature it introduces. Include screenshots of any new or altered UI. Link to any Github issues that are related. 

When the PAM login failed in the child process, it was shutting down the child using ::exit() , which causes atexit hooks to run, which includes C++ destructors for static objects. ::_exit() is what you're SUPPOSED to use in that context, which just kills the process right-here-right-now.

Presumably, one of those static destructors was modifying a file descriptor that the parent process depended on, making the event loop's internals fall into an inconsistent state.

### Approach

> Describe the approach taken and the tradeoffs involved if non-obvious; add an overview of the solution if it's complicated.

When PAM session initialization failed in a forked child process (before exec), rserver-launcher would enter an unresponsive state and stop processing new session launch requests. This required manually restarting rserver-launcher to recover.

The issue manifested as:
- PAM errors logged successfully (e.g., "pam_open_session failed: Cannot make/remove an entry
 for the specified session")
- Child process exiting
- But `onSessionExit` callback never being called in parent
- rserver-launcher appearing to run normally but not responding to new launch requests


After fork (but before exec), calling `exit()` is dangerous because:
- Running destructors can modify shared state (like file descriptors) that the parent process
 depends on
- This can corrupt the parent's event loop state, causing it to become unresponsive
- The behavior is non-deterministic depending on what static destructors do

title: Added mousewheel scrolling for feature tabs when pane is too narrow to show them all
description:
Addresses #16734

## Summary

Implement horizontal scrolling for tabs in ModuleTabLayoutPanel (used by TabSet1, TabSet2, Console, and Sidebar panes) when there are more tabs than can fit in the available horizontal space.

Previously, when many tabs were open in these panes, tabs would either overflow or be hidden with no way to access them. This change adds mousewheel scrolling support similar to the existing implementation in DocTabLayoutPanel (source editor tabs).

Also, if a pane is selected via a command (View / Show History and so on) its tab will be scrolled into view, if currently hidden.

Ideally, test with both an actual mouse wheel, and with trackpad gesture (two finger swipe up/down, for example).

## Changes

### New Scrolling Infrastructure

- **`onLoad()`**: Sets up the scroll container with `overflow-x: hidden` on the tab bar parent and registers wheel event listeners
- **`getTabBarElement()`**: Helper to find the `gwt-TabLayoutPanelTabs` element in the DOM
- **`WheelEventListener`**: Handles mousewheel/wheel events to scroll tabs horizontally (100px per scroll event)

### Dynamic Tab Bar Width

- **`updateTabBarWidth()`**: Calculates and sets the tab bar width based on actual tab content plus button area (55px for min/max buttons)
- **`getTabsContentWidth()`**: Measures total width of all tab elements
- **`getMaxScroll()`**: Calculates maximum scroll position to prevent over-scrolling

### Scroll Animation

- **`scrollBy()`**: Scrolls relative to current position
- **`scrollTo()`**: Scrolls to absolute position with bounds checking
- **`animateScrollTo()`**: Smooth 200ms animation for scroll transitions
- **`reducedMotion()`**: Respects user's reduced motion preference

### Tab Visibility Management

- **`ensureSelectedTabIsVisible()`**: Automatically scrolls to show the selected tab when it's outside the visible viewport
- **`selectTab()` override**: Cancels ongoing animations and uses `scheduleFinally()` to ensure scroll adjustment happens after CSS layout changes settle
- **`remove()` override**: Updates tab bar width and ensures selected tab visibility after tab removal
- **`onResize()` override**: Recalculates tab bar width and tab visibility on resize

### Position Calculation

- Uses `DomUtils.getRelativePosition()` for accurate tab positioning relative to the scroll container (matching the proven pattern from DocTabLayoutPanel)

## Technical Details

- Follows the same patterns established in `DocTabLayoutPanel.java` for consistency
- Tab bar parent uses `overflow-x: hidden` to enable scrolling via `scrollLeft` without showing scrollbars
- Animation is cancellable to prevent timing conflicts when rapidly switching tabs
- `scheduleFinally()` ensures scroll adjustments happen after browser layout reflow from CSS class changes
