title: Fix inconsistencies/bugs in desktop logging
description:
## Summary

Fixes critical bugs in the Electron desktop app's logging level handling where:
1. `--log-level=WARN` would incorrectly cause rsession to use DEBUG level instead of WARN
2. Environment variables with C++ level names (e.g., `RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING`) would break Winston logging
3. `--log-level=TRACE` couldn't actually set TRACE level for rsession
4. Syslog mode (Linux) would break with WARN/WARNING due to different level naming
5. `logWarning()` silently dropped all warning messages in syslog mode (Linux)

## Problems

### Bug #1: `--log-level=WARN` Results in DEBUG Level (Critical)

When users passed `--log-level=WARN` to the Electron desktop app:

1. Electron's `parseCommandLineLogLevel()` converted `"WARN"` → `"warn"` (Winston log level)
2. When launching rsession in `session-launcher.ts`, it simply uppercased: `"warn"` → `"WARN"`
3. rsession's C++ code (`Logger.cpp:logLevelFromStr()`) expects `"WARNING"` not `"WARN"`
4. Since "WARN" didn't match any case, it fell through to default: `LogLevel::DEBUG`
5. **Result**: User asked for WARN level but got DEBUG level instead

### Bug #2: Environment Variables Break Winston Logging

When users set environment variables using C++ level names:
- `RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING` or `RS_LOG_LEVEL=TRACE` would be passed directly to Winston
- Winston uses npm levels (`warn`, not `warning`; no `trace` level exists)
- Winston would receive an unrecognized level, causing undefined logging behavior
- **Result**: Logging could be completely suppressed or behave incorrectly

### Bug #3: TRACE Level Doesn't Work

- Help text advertised `--log-level=TRACE`
- But the implementation mapped TRACE → `'debug'` everywhere
- rsession would receive `RS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`, never `TRACE`
- **Result**: No way to actually enable TRACE level in rsession via command-line

### Bug #4: Inconsistent Naming - `ERR` vs `ERROR`

- Help text advertised `--log-level=ERR|WARN|INFO|DEBUG`
- But environment variables use: `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`, `DEBUG`, `TRACE`
- Users trying `--log-level=ERROR` would fail (fell back to default)
- `--log-level=ERR` worked only due to internal conversion, causing confusion

### Bug #5: Syslog Mode Breaks with WARN/WARNING (Linux-specific)

When `--logger-type=syslog` on Linux:
- Winston npm levels use `'warn'` (error, **warn**, info, debug)
- Winston syslog levels use `'warning'` (error, **warning**, info, debug)
- Normalization would always convert to `'warn'`, but syslog expects `'warning'`
- Winston would have an invalid level name for the active level system
- **Result**: Log filtering would break, messages could be dropped or logged incorrectly

### Bug #6: `logWarning()` Silently Drops Messages in Syslog Mode (Linux-specific)

When `--logger-type=syslog` on Linux:
- `WinstonLogger.logWarning()` calls `this.log('warn', message)`
- The logger's level set is configured with syslog levels (`winston.config.syslog.levels`)
- Syslog levels only define `'warning'`, not `'warn'`
- Winston filters out messages with unrecognized levels
- **Result**: All warning messages were silently dropped when using syslog mode

## Solution

### Architecture

The solution properly handles four different logging level formats:

1. **User Input**: Accepts both abbreviated (`ERR`, `WARN`) and full names (`ERROR`, `WARNING`, `TRACE`)
2. **Electron/Winston (npm levels)**: Uses npm levels: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `http`, `verbose`, `silly`
3. **Electron/Winston (syslog levels)**: Uses syslog levels: `error`, `warning`, `info`, `debug` (note: `warning` not `warn`)
4. **rsession (C++)**: Uses custom levels: `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`, `DEBUG`, `TRACE`

The key insight is that Winston has two different level systems depending on the transport, and normalization must be aware of which system is active.

### Key Functions

#### 1. `parseCommandLineLogLevel()` - Command-line Parsing

**File**: `src/node/desktop/src/core/logger.ts` (lines 120-138)

Converts user-friendly command-line arguments to internal log levels:
- Accepts both `ERR`/`ERROR`, `WARN`/`WARNING`
- Returns internal level: `'error'`, `'warn'`, `'info'`, `'debug'`, `'trace'`
- `'trace'` is preserved (not mapped to `'debug'` yet)

```typescript
export function parseCommandLineLogLevel(level: string, defaultLevel: string): string {
  level = level.toUpperCase();
  switch (level) {
    case 'ERR':
    case 'ERROR':
      return 'error';
    case 'WARN':
    case 'WARNING':
      return 'warn';
    case 'INFO':
      return 'info';
    case 'DEBUG':
      return 'debug';
    case 'TRACE':
      return 'trace';  // Preserved for rsession
    default:
      return defaultLevel;
  }
}
```

#### 2. `levelToCppLevel()` - C++ Conversion

**File**: `src/node/desktop/src/core/logger.ts` (lines 140-158)

Converts internal log levels to C++ Logger levels for rsession:
- `'warn'` → `'WARNING'` (KEY FIX!)
- `'trace'` → `'TRACE'` (KEY FIX!)
- Handles all Winston and internal levels

```typescript
export function levelToCppLevel(level: string): string {
  switch (level.toLowerCase()) {
    case 'error':
      return 'ERROR';
    case 'warn':
      return 'WARNING';
    case 'info':
      return 'INFO';
    case 'debug':
      return 'DEBUG';
    case 'trace':
      return 'TRACE';  // Now properly passes TRACE to rsession!
    // ... other cases
  }
}
```

### Implementation Changes

#### 1. Updated `winston-logger.ts`

**File**: `src/node/desktop/src/core/winston-logger.ts` (lines 23, 36-77, 122-142, 148-157)

**Changes**:
- Removed unused `normalizeToWinstonLevel` import (line 23)
- Added `usingSyslog` flag to track if syslog mode is active
- Added `normalizeLevel()` method that handles both npm and syslog levels
- Check logger type before normalizing (constructor)
- Normalize log level in `setLogLevel()` method
- **KEY FIX (Bug #5)**: Returns `'warning'` for syslog mode, `'warn'` for npm levels
- **KEY FIX (Bug #6)**: `log()` method now normalizes level before passing to Winston
- Handles environment variables with C++ names (e.g., `RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING`)

```typescript
constructor(logOptions: LogOptions) {
  const level = this.readLogLevelOverride(logOptions.getLogLevel());
  const loggerType = logOptions.getLoggerType();
  const useSyslog = loggerType === 'syslog' && process.platform === 'linux';

  // Normalize to Winston-compatible level
  // Syslog uses 'warning', npm levels use 'warn'
  const winstonLevel = this.normalizeLevel(level, useSyslog);

  this.logger = winston.createLogger({
    level: winstonLevel,
    // ...
  });

  if (useSyslog) {
    // ... create syslog transport
    this.logger.levels = winston.config.syslog.levels;
    this.usingSyslog = true;
  }
}

normalizeLevel(level: string, useSyslog: boolean): string {
  const normalized = level.toLowerCase();

  if (normalized === 'err') return 'error';

  // WARN/WARNING - depends on whether we're using syslog
  if (normalized === 'warn' || normalized === 'warning') {
    return useSyslog ? 'warning' : 'warn';  // KEY FIX!
  }

  if (normalized === 'trace') return 'debug';

  // Pass through everything else
  return normalized;
}

setLogLevel(level: string): void {
  this.logger.level = this.normalizeLevel(level, this.usingSyslog);
}

log(level: string, message: string): void {
  // Normalize level for the active logger type (syslog uses 'warning', npm uses 'warn')
  const normalizedLevel = this.normalizeLevel(level, this.usingSyslog);
  this.logger.log(normalizedLevel, message);
}
```

This ensures that when `logWarning()` calls `this.log('warn', message)`, the level gets normalized to `'warning'` in syslog mode before Winston sees it.

#### 2. Updated `session-launcher.ts`

**File**: `src/node/desktop/src/main/session-launcher.ts` (lines 24, 114)

**Changes**:
- Import `levelToCppLevel` function
- Use conversion function instead of naive `.toUpperCase()`

```typescript
// Before:
env['RS_LOG_LEVEL'] = env['RS_LOG_LEVEL'] ?? rsessionOptions.getLogLevel().toUpperCase();

// After:
env['RS_LOG_LEVEL'] = env['RS_LOG_LEVEL'] ?? levelToCppLevel(rsessionOptions.getLogLevel());
```

#### 3. Updated Help Text

**File**: `src/node/desktop/src/main/args-manager.ts` (line 84)

Changed:
```
--log-level=ERR|WARN|INFO|DEBUG
```

To:
```
--log-level=ERROR|WARNING|INFO|DEBUG|TRACE
```

#### 4. Enhanced Tests

**File**: `src/node/desktop/test/unit/core/logger.test.ts`

Added comprehensive test coverage (2 test suites, 330 total tests passing):

1. **parseCommandLineLogLevel** tests:
   - Abbreviated forms (ERR, WARN)
   - Full names (ERROR, WARNING)
   - TRACE support
   - Case insensitivity

2. **levelToCppLevel** tests (new):
   - All level conversions
   - TRACE → TRACE conversion
   - Case insensitivity

Note: `WinstonLogger.normalizeLevel()` is an instance method tested through the existing WinstonLogger test suite.

#### 5. Updated Documentation

**File**: `logging.md` in rstudio-memory-bank

- Updated command-line options
- Added backwards compatibility note
- Updated environment variable table
- Added technical details about three-layer conversion

## Complete Flow

### Example 1: `--log-level=WARN`

```
User: --log-level=WARN
  ↓
parseCommandLineLogLevel('WARN') → 'warn'
  ↓
WinstonLogger.normalizeLevel('warn', useSyslog=false) → 'warn'
Winston uses 'warn' level ✅
  ↓
session-launcher: levelToCppLevel('warn') → 'WARNING'
  ↓
RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING passed to rsession ✅
```

### Example 2: `RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING` (environment variable)

```
User: RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING
  ↓
WinstonLogger.normalizeLevel('WARNING', useSyslog=false) → 'warn'
Winston uses 'warn' level ✅
  ↓
Environment variable already set, passed to rsession as-is
RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING received by rsession ✅
```

### Example 3: `--log-level=TRACE`

```
User: --log-level=TRACE
  ↓
parseCommandLineLogLevel('TRACE') → 'trace'
  ↓
WinstonLogger.normalizeLevel('trace', useSyslog=false) → 'debug'
Winston uses 'debug' level ✅ (closest available)
  ↓
session-launcher: levelToCppLevel('trace') → 'TRACE'
  ↓
RS_LOG_LEVEL=TRACE passed to rsession ✅
```

## Backwards Compatibility

✅ **Fully backwards compatible** - no breaking changes:

| User Input | Winston Level (npm) | Winston Level (syslog) | C++ Level (rsession) | Works? |
|------------|---------------------|------------------------|----------------------|---------|
| `--log-level=ERR` | `error` | `error` | `ERROR` | ✅ Yes |
| `--log-level=ERROR` | `error` | `error` | `ERROR` | ✅ Yes (new) |
| `--log-level=WARN` | `warn` | `warning` | `WARNING` | ✅ Fixed! |
| `--log-level=WARNING` | `warn` | `warning` | `WARNING` | ✅ Yes (new) |
| `--log-level=TRACE` | `debug` | `debug` | `TRACE` | ✅ Fixed! |
| `RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING` | `warn` | `warning` | `WARNING` | ✅ Fixed! |
| Config: `log-level=http` | `http` | `http` | `DEBUG` | ✅ Yes |

## Testing

### Unit Tests
- ✅ All 330 tests pass (added 1 new test suite)
- ✅ `parseCommandLineLogLevel` tests updated
- ✅ New `levelToCppLevel` test suite
- ✅ Existing `WinstonLogger` tests continue to pass (test normalizeLevel() instance method)
- ✅ Tests cover abbreviated forms, full names, TRACE, env vars, and Winston levels

### Manual Testing Recommended
1. Test `--log-level=WARNING` produces WARNING level in rsession
2. Test `--log-level=WARN` produces WARNING level in rsession (backwards compat)
3. Test `--log-level=ERROR` and `--log-level=ERR` both work
4. Test `--log-level=TRACE` sets TRACE in rsession, DEBUG in Winston
5. Test `RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING` works correctly for both Winston and rsession
6. Test config file with `log-level=http` still works
7. **Test syslog mode (Linux only)**: `--log-level=WARN --logger-type=syslog` uses 'warning' level
8. Verify rsession log files show expected log levels

### Verification Commands

```bash
# Test WARN mapping
RStudio --log-level=WARN --log-dir=./tmp &
# Check rdesktop.log shows: RS_LOG_LEVEL: WARNING

# Test environment variable
RS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING RStudio --log-dir=./tmp &
# Check rdesktop.log shows Winston using 'warn', rsession gets 'WARNING'

# Test TRACE support
RStudio --log-level=TRACE --log-dir=./tmp &
# Check rdesktop.log shows: RS_LOG_LEVEL: TRACE

# Test syslog mode (Linux only)
RStudio --log-level=WARN --logger-type=syslog &
# Check /var/log/syslog shows messages logged with 'warning' level
# Verify Winston doesn't error with invalid level
```

## Risk Assessment

**Low Risk**:
- Clear separation of concerns between three level formats
- Well-tested code area (330 passing tests, 1 new test suite)
- Backwards compatible
- Fixes critical bugs where users unknowingly got wrong log level

**No Breaking Changes**:
- Existing workflows continue to work
- Users benefit from bug fixes automatically
- Config files with Winston levels (http, verbose, silly) still work
- No changes to other environment variables

## Files Modified

1. `src/node/desktop/src/core/logger.ts` - Fixed parseCommandLineLogLevel(), added levelToCppLevel()
2. `src/node/desktop/src/core/winston-logger.ts` - Added normalizeLevel() instance method, normalize levels in log() method, removed unused import
3. `src/node/desktop/src/main/args-manager.ts` - Updated help text
4. `src/node/desktop/src/main/session-launcher.ts` - Use levelToCppLevel()
5. `src/node/desktop/test/unit/core/logger.test.ts` - Enhanced tests with 1 new test suite
6. Documentation updated in logging.md

## Related Issues

This fix resolves inconsistencies between:
- User-friendly command-line arguments (ERR, WARN, ERROR, WARNING, TRACE)
- Winston logger levels:
  - npm levels: error, **warn**, info, debug, http, verbose, silly
  - syslog levels: error, **warning**, info, debug (Linux only)
- Environment variables passed to rsession (C++ levels: ERROR, WARNING, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE)
- Config file formats (supports both Winston and C++ level names)

The solution provides a clean architecture that handles:
1. **Input Layer**: Accept flexible user input (abbreviated and full names)
2. **Winston Layer**: Normalize to Winston levels (npm or syslog) for Electron logging
3. **C++ Layer**: Convert to C++ Logger levels for rsession

**Key Insights**:
1. Winston uses different level names depending on the transport:
   - Default/file/stderr transports: Use npm levels (`warn`)
   - Syslog transport (Linux): Uses syslog levels (`warning`)
   - The `WinstonLogger.normalizeLevel()` method is logger-type-aware

2. Level normalization must happen at the message dispatch point:
   - The `WinstonLogger.log()` method normalizes every log call
   - This ensures `logWarning()` → `log('warn', ...)` → normalized to `'warning'` in syslog mode
   - Prevents silent message filtering by Winston when level doesn't match active level set

This approach ensures both logging systems work correctly while maintaining full backwards compatibility and supporting all valid Winston log levels from config files.

title: Don't automatically add Presentations tab to tabset2
description:
### Intent

Addresses #16733

### Problem

When TabSet2 has NO tabs assigned in the pane layout UI and the user minimizes the TabSet2 region, it incorrectly displays a "Presentation" tab. When TabSet2 is not minimized, it correctly shows a blank area as expected.

### Root Cause

The validation code in `PaneConfig.validateAndAutoCorrect()` was forcibly adding "Presentations" back to TabSet2 whenever it wasn't found in either TabSet1 or TabSet2:

```java
// if we don't have Presentation2 then provide it
if (!hasPresentation2(ts1) && !hasPresentation2(ts2))
{
   ts2.set(ts2.length(), PaneManager.PRESENTATIONS_PANE);
}
```

This code was added in September 2021 as an upgrade safety mechanism to ensure users upgrading from pre-Quarto versions would automatically get the new "Presentations" tab. However, it conflicts with RStudio's policy (since v1.4) that TabSets can be empty, and it cannot distinguish between:

- "User has old config from before Presentations existed" (should add)
- "User explicitly removed Presentations" (should NOT add)

Additionally, both the legacy "Presentation" tab and the newer "Presentations" tab display as "Presentation" (singular) to users, which is why the bug report mentioned seeing "Presentation" appear.

### Solution

Remove the auto-add code that forces "Presentations" to always be present. This aligns with RStudio 1.4+ policy allowing empty TabSets and respects user preferences.

**Changes:**
- Removed lines 271-275 in `PaneConfig.java` that auto-added "Presentations" to TabSet2
- Removed the now-unused `hasPresentation2()` helper method

### Risk Assessment

**Low Risk** - This change:
- Only affects users who explicitly remove all tabs from TabSet2
- Default configuration still includes Presentations in TabSet2 for new users
- Users with Presentations already in their config are unaffected
- Fixes the reported bug where TabSet2 cannot be empty
- The auto-add code was a temporary upgrade helper from 2021 that has outlived its usefulness

**Minimal upgrade impact:**
- Users upgrading from very old versions (pre-Sept 2021) won't automatically get Presentations tab
- However, Presentations is only useful when Quarto is enabled anyway
- Users can easily add it via Global Options → Pane Layout if needed

### Testing

**Manual test to verify the fix:**

1. Open Global Options → Pane Layout
2. Remove all tabs from TabSet2 (move them to other locations)
3. Click OK and observe TabSet2 minimizes (correct behavior)
4. Restart RStudio
5. **Expected:** TabSet2 remains empty with no "Presentation" tab appearing
6. **Before fix:** "Presentation" tab would incorrectly appear in minimized TabSet2

**Additional testing:**
- Verify first-time users still get default tabs including Presentations
- Verify empty TabSet1 also works correctly
- Verify users with existing Presentations tab keep it

title: apply formatting edits to document before save
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16714.

### Approach

- Introduces https://github.com/cubicdaiya/dtl as a tool for computing diffs / edits.
- Rather than apply the formatter to the document directly on disk, apply the formatter to a separate temporary file.
- Compute a set of edits that can be used to transform from the original document to the formatted document.
- Send those edits back to the client, and have it apply those edits in the buffer before the actual save.

In theory, we should be launching, using, and managing `air` as an LSP process, but this felt more straightforward, and should also work with any other external formatter.

The main benefit of performing formatting in this way is that it keeps the undo stack clean when formatting on save.

description:
# Add runtime/executeCode handler for code execution

## Summary

This PR implements the `runtime/executeCode` JSON-RPC request handler in rsession, allowing the backend to execute R code in the user's R session with full console integration and output capture.

## Features

### Code Execution
- Executes R code in `globalenv()` so variables persist across executions
- Uses the `evaluate` package for robust output capture
- Continues through errors (`stop_on_error = 0`) to capture partial results
- Returns structured response with output, errors, plots, and execution time

### Console Integration
- Code appears in RStudio Console with proper prompts (`>` and `+`)
- Output displayed via `consoleWriteOutput()` and `consoleWriteError()`
- User sees execution as if they typed it themselves

### Plot Capture
- When `capturePlot: true`, captures plots as base64-encoded PNG
- Default size: 7x7 inches at 96 DPI (672x672 pixels)
- Customizable via R options: `repr.plot.width`, `repr.plot.height`
- Uses base64enc or jsonlite for encoding

### Cancellation Support
- `runtime/cancelExecution` notification to interrupt running code
- Tracks executions by `trackingId` for targeted cancellation
- Supports pre-cancellation of queued requests
- Thread-safe state management with mutex protection

## Notes

- Timeout option is passed through but not enforced (to avoid interrupting legitimate long-running code)
- Only R language supported currently; Python support can be added later
- The `evaluate` package is required (already a knitr dependency)

# PR: Implement runtime/getDetailedEnvironmentContext handler

## Summary

Implements the `runtime/getDetailedEnvironmentContext` JSON-RPC request handler in rsession's SessionChat module. This handler responds to requests from the databot backend with session information, platform metadata, and placeholders for future context features.

## Changes

### RStudio (SessionChat.cpp)

**New handler function** (`src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp:256-290`):
- `handleGetDetailedEnvironmentContext()` - Returns detailed environment context to the databot backend

**Response structure**:
```json
{
  "files": [],
  "session": {
    "language": "R",
    "version": "4.3.0",
    "mode": "console",
    "sessionId": "abc123def456",
    "variables": []

    "hasPlots": false,
    "platformVersion": "2024.12.0",

}
```

title: Add suspension blocking for chat backend in SessionChat module
description:
# Implement `chat/setBusyStatus` Handler in rsession

## Summary

Implements handling of the `chat/setBusyStatus` JSON-RPC notification from the chat backend to prevent rsession from suspending while the backend is processing requests. This ensures that session suspension (which would kill the chat backend process) does not occur during active chat operations.

## Implementation Details

### Architecture

The implementation follows the established pattern used by other rsession modules (jobs, connections, etc.):

1. **Chat Backend → rsession**: Backend sends `chat/setBusyStatus` notification with `{ busy: true/false }`
2. **SessionChat.cpp**: Notification handler updates internal `s_chatBusy` flag
3. **SessionChat.hpp**: Exports `isSuspendable()` function that returns `!s_chatBusy`
4. **SessionConsoleInput.cpp**: `canSuspend()` function calls `modules::chat::isSuspendable()` to check if chat backend is busy
5. **Result**: When chat backend is busy, `canSuspend()` returns `false`, blocking suspension and showing user notification

**Critical point**: The actual suspension blocking happens in `canSuspend()` via the `isSuspendable()` check, NOT directly in the notification handler. This matches the established pattern for all other blocking conditions.

### Changes

**src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.hpp**
- Added `isSuspendable()` function declaration to expose busy state to suspension system
- Returns `true` when session can suspend (chat backend is idle)

**src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp**
- Added `s_chatBusy` static boolean flag to track current busy status from chat backend (line 93)
- Implemented `handleSetBusyStatus()` notification handler (lines 382-397)
  - Parses `busy` boolean from JSON-RPC params
  - Updates `s_chatBusy` flag
  - Logs status changes using chat-specific `DLOG` macro
- Implemented `isSuspendable()` function (lines 1107-1111)
  - Returns `!s_chatBusy` to indicate if suspension is safe
  - Follows same naming and semantics as other modules
- Registered notification handler in `initialize()` (line 1138)
- Added cleanup in `onBackendExit()` (lines 717-722)
  - Clears `s_chatBusy` flag to prevent stuck suspension blocking if backend crashes
  - Logs cleanup action for debugging
- Added cleanup in `onShutdown()` (lines 1077-1081)
  - Ensures clean state during rsession shutdown

**src/cpp/session/SessionConsoleInput.cpp**
- Added `#include "modules/SessionChat.hpp"` (line 26) using relative path pattern
- Added suspension check in `canSuspend()` function (line 136)
  - Calls `modules::chat::isSuspendable()` to check chat backend busy state
  - Uses `checkBlockingOp()` to both block suspension AND track reason for user notification
  - User-visible message: "Chat is processing a request"
  - Integrates with existing suspension decision framework

### Behavior

**When Chat Backend is Busy:**
- rsession **cannot suspend** (automatic or signal-based)
- If suspension is attempted, user sees notification: "Session suspension is blocked by: Chat is processing a request"
- Debug logs show: "Chat backend busy status: busy"

**When Chat Backend is Idle:**
- rsession **can suspend** (if no other blocking conditions exist)
- Normal suspension behavior resumes
- Debug logs show: "Chat backend busy status: idle"

**When Chat Backend Process Exits:**
- Busy state is automatically cleared in `onBackendExit()`
- Suspension is no longer blocked (unless other conditions exist)
- Debug logs show: "Cleared chat backend busy state on process exit"
- No risk of "stuck busy" state beyond backend process lifetime

### Thread Safety

- All JSON-RPC notifications processed on main thread (`callbacksRequireMainThread = true`)
- No synchronization needed for `s_chatBusy` variable
- `suspend::checkBlockingOp()` is thread-safe internally

### Testing

**Build Status**: ✅ Successfully compiled with no errors or warnings (except expected linker warnings for library versions)

**Recommended Manual Testing:**
1. Send a chat message during active session
2. Verify suspension is blocked while backend processes request
3. Verify suspension allowed after request completes
4. Test crash recovery by killing backend process during operation
5. Verify busy state is cleared and suspension no longer blocked

## Integration

This implementation works alongside existing suspension blocking conditions:
- Child processes in terminals
- Active background jobs
- Incomplete R commands
- Database connections
- External pointers

The chat backend manages its own busy state using a reference counting system that sends:
- `{ busy: true }` on 0→1 transition (first operation starts)
- `{ busy: false }` on 1→0 transition (last operation completes)

## Files Modified

- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.hpp` - Added public API
- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp` - Core implementation
- `src/cpp/session/SessionConsoleInput.cpp` - Suspension integration

title: Implement sidebar toggle functionality to preserve column widths
description:
# Fix sidebar toggle reverting column widths to previous state

Addresses #16676

## Summary

When users resized columns with the sidebar visible, then hid and showed the sidebar, column widths would revert to an older saved state instead of preserving the most recent widths. This PR fixes that issue by preserving column widths across sidebar visibility toggles.

## Changes

### Root Cause

The main split panel uses async state persistence to save/restore column widths. When toggling sidebar visibility:

1. User resizes columns → widths saved asynchronously to persistent storage
2. User toggles sidebar → panel reinitializes, creating a new state handler
3. New state handler reads from persistent storage before the previous save completes
4. Result: stale/older widths are restored instead of current widths

### Solution

Modified `MainSplitPanel.java` to preserve column widths directly in memory during sidebar toggles:

- **On hide sidebar**: Capture current widths (including sidebar) and store in memory
- **On show sidebar**: Restore widths from memory, bypassing async state persistence
- Added `isTogglingSidebar_` flag to skip normal state restoration during toggles
- Added `widthsBeforeHidingSidebar_` array to store widths between hide/show operations

### Implementation Details

**Key changes in `MainSplitPanel.java`:**

1. Added fields:
   - `isTogglingSidebar_`: Flag to detect sidebar toggle operations
   - `widthsBeforeHidingSidebar_`: Stores column widths when sidebar is hidden
   - `savedSidebarLocation_`: Stores sidebar location when hidden (for validation on restore)

2. Modified `removeSidebarWidget()`:
   - Captures current widths before hiding sidebar
   - Saves sidebar location for validation
   - Sets toggle flag to skip state restoration

3. Modified `setSidebarWidget()`:
   - Validates sidebar location matches saved location before restoring
   - Restores widths from saved state only if location matches
   - Discards saved widths if location changed (prevents width corruption)
   - Clears saved state after restoration

4. Modified `onInit()`:
   - **Removed `sidebarVisibilityChanged` logic** that incorrectly triggered on left widget changes
   - **Changed to strict column count equality check** (prevents ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
   - Skips state restoration when `isTogglingSidebar_` is true
   - Prevents conflict between state persistence and direct width preservation

5. Added helper methods:
   - `captureColumnWidths()`: Captures current widget widths
   - `restoreColumnWidths()`: Restores widgets to specified widths

## Verification

1. Open RStudio with sidebar visible
2. Resize columns by dragging splitters
3. Hide the sidebar (View → Panes → Hide Sidebar)
4. Show the sidebar again (View → Panes → Show Sidebar)
5. **Expected**: Column widths match step 2
6. **Before fix**: Column widths reverted to older saved state

** Edge case (no corruption on location change):**

1. Resize columns with sidebar on right
2. Change sidebar location to left (View → Panes → Sidebar Location)
3. **Expected**: Default layout, no width corruption
4. **Before fix**: Console width applied to right pane, right width to sidebar (corrupted)

title: Enhance WebSocket URL construction and cache control in Chat module
description:
# Fix Chat UI Loading and WebSocket Connection Issues in RStudio Server

## Summary

Fixes two critical issues preventing the Chat pane from working correctly in RStudio Server:

1. **WebSocket URL construction** now preserves session paths, enabling multi-user deployments
2. **Aggressive browser caching** is prevented through strengthened HTTP headers and cache-busting query parameters

## Problem

The Chat pane was experiencing two issues in RStudio Server mode:

### 1. WebSocket URL Missing Session Path
The WebSocket URL construction in `buildWebSocketUrl()` was using `parsedBase.host()` which only extracted the hostname and port, discarding the path component. This worked in single-user mode (`http://localhost:8787/`) but would fail in multi-user mode with session paths (`http://localhost:8787/s/abc123/`).

**Before:**
```cpp
std::string wsUrl = wsScheme + "://" + parsedBase.host() + portmappedPath + "/ai-chat";
// Result: ws://localhost:8787/p/58fab3e4/ai-chat (missing /s/abc123/)
```

### 2. Browser Caching Issues
Chrome was aggressively caching the Chat UI despite `Cache-Control: no-cache` headers, causing stale UI to load. This was particularly problematic during development and updates.

## Changes

### SessionChat.cpp

#### WebSocket URL Construction (lines 551-588)
- **Changed**: Preserve full path from `activeClientUrl()` instead of extracting only host
- **Method**: Strip scheme prefix (`http://`/`https://`) and replace with WebSocket scheme (`ws://`/`wss://`)
- **Impact**: WebSocket URLs now correctly include session paths for multi-user deployments
- **Example**: `http://localhost:8787/s/abc123/` → `ws://localhost:8787/s/abc123/p/58fab3e4/ai-chat`

#### Cache Headers (lines 951-961)
- **Added**: `Pragma: no-cache` header for HTTP/1.0 compatibility
- **Added**: `Expires: 0` header for proxy cache control
- **Enhanced**: `Cache-Control` header with `max-age=0`
- **Impact**: Comprehensive cache prevention across all browsers and proxies

### ChatPresenter.java

#### Timestamp Cache Busting (line 177-178)
- **Added**: Millisecond timestamp query parameter (`&_t=`) to iframe URL
- **Impact**: Forces browser to treat each Chat pane load as a unique URL, preventing iframe-level caching

## Testing

### Verified Scenarios
- ✅ **RStudio Desktop**: Chat pane loads and connects via WebSocket
- ✅ **RStudio Server (single-user mode)**: Chat pane loads correctly
- ✅ **RStudio Server (multi-user mode with session paths)**: WebSocket routing works correctly
- ✅ **Chrome caching**: Fresh UI loads on every restart, no stale cached content
- ✅ **Safari/Firefox**: Works correctly across all major browsers

### Test Plan
1. Deploy updated RStudio Server in multi-user configuration
2. Open Chat pane from different user sessions
3. Verify WebSocket connects successfully (check logs for correct URL format)
4. Update Chat UI bundle and verify new version loads immediately
5. Test in Chrome, Safari, and Firefox

## Technical Details

### WebSocket URL Routing in Server Mode

The WebSocket proxy in rserver routes requests like:
```
wss://hostname/s/session-id/p/obfuscated-port/ai-chat/ws
→ http://127.0.0.1:actual-port/ai-chat/ws
```

The session path (`/s/session-id/`) **must be preserved** between the hostname and portmapped path for routing to work. The previous implementation using `parsedBase.host()` would construct:
```
wss://hostname/p/obfuscated-port/ai-chat/ws  ❌ Missing session path
```

### Alignment with Terminal Implementation

This change aligns the Chat WebSocket URL construction with how Terminal WebSockets are handled (see `TerminalSessionSocket.java`), which also preserves the full URL path when constructing WebSocket URLs for Server mode.

## Files Changed

- `src/cpp/session/modules/SessionChat.cpp` - WebSocket URL construction and cache headers
- `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/chat/ChatPresenter.java` - Cache-busting timestamp

## Related Issues

This fix addresses WebSocket connection failures in multi-user RStudio Server deployments and resolves stale UI caching issues reported during Chat feature development.

title: Begin implementing RuntimeService support in rsession
description:
# Add RuntimeService JSON-RPC Request/Response Infrastructure to rsession

## Summary

This PR implements the rsession side of the RuntimeService JSON-RPC API. It adds full bidirectional request/response communication capability between rsession and the backend, starting with the `runtime/getActiveSession` method.

**Key Additions:**
- Complete JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response infrastructure with proper error handling
- Implementation of `runtime/getActiveSession` handler returning real session data
- Configurable logging system with two environment variables for debugging
- Synchronous message processing architecture to handle ProcessOperations lifetime correctly

## Background

The backend communicates with rsession via JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout. Previously, SessionChat only handled notifications (one-way messages from backend to rsession). This PR adds support for requests (two-way messages requiring responses from rsession).

The initial use case is `runtime/getActiveSession`, which is called to understand the current execution context (language, version, sessionId, mode). Without this implementation, the backend would timeout waiting for responses, blocking basic functionality.

## Changes

### JSON-RPC Request/Response Infrastructure

**New Functions:**
- `sendJsonRpcResponse()`: Sends success responses with Content-Length framing and error handling
- `sendJsonRpcError()`: Sends JSON-RPC 2.0 error responses (e.g., -32601 for "Method not found")
- `handleRequest()`: Dispatches requests to appropriate handlers based on method name
- `handleGetActiveSession()`: Implements `runtime/getActiveSession` method

**Architecture Changes:**
- Modified `processBackendMessage()` to distinguish requests from notifications per JSON-RPC 2.0 spec:
  - **Request**: `id` field is present (value can be string, number, or null)
  - **Notification**: `id` field is absent entirely
- Changed to synchronous processing model: messages processed immediately in `onBackendStdout()` while `ProcessOperations&` reference is valid
- Removed deferred message queue (`s_pendingResponses`) to avoid dangling reference bugs

**Compliance with JSON-RPC 2.0:**
- Flexible request ID handling (supports string, number, or null)
- Error responses with standard error codes (-32601 for unknown methods)
- Proper Content-Length framing for all messages
- Correct request vs notification detection based on field presence, not value

### runtime/getActiveSession Implementation

Returns real session information:
```cpp
{
  "language": "R",                              // Currently hardcoded (Python detection TODO)
  "version": module_context::rVersion(),        // Actual R version (e.g., "4.3.2")
  "sessionId": module_context::activeSession().id(),  // Real session ID
  "mode": "console"                             // Currently hardcoded
}
```

### Logging Enhancements

#### Two Environment Variables:

**1. CHAT_LOG_LEVEL** (controls rsession verbosity):
- `0`: No console output (default)
- `1`: rsession logs only (no JSON-RPC message bodies)
- `2`: rsession logs + JSON-RPC bodies for all messages except `logger/log` (formatted version shown instead)
- `3`: rsession logs + JSON-RPC bodies for ALL messages including `logger/log` (for debugging logging mechanism)

**2. CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL** (filters backend logs by severity):
- Valid values: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal` (case-insensitive)
- Default: `error` (only show error and fatal logs from backend)
- Example: `CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL=info` shows info, warn, error, and fatal logs

#### Log Level Handling:

Added `getLogLevelPriority()` function with conservative filtering:
- Known levels: `trace` (0), `debug` (1), `info` (2), `warn` (3), `error` (4), `fatal` (5)
- **Unknown levels**: priority 999 (treated as highest severity to ensure critical messages never filtered)

Updated `handleLoggerLog()` to:
- Apply level filtering based on `CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL`
- Include level in formatted output
- Route `fatal` logs to `ELOG` (not `DLOG`)
- Route unknown levels to `ELOG` (conservative approach for potentially critical issues)

Added `shouldLogBackendMessage()` to eliminate duplicate output:
- At level 2: Hide raw JSON for `logger/log` notifications (formatted version sufficient)
- At level 3+: Show raw JSON for all messages including `logger/log` (for debugging logging itself)

## Technical Details

### ProcessOperations Lifetime Management

The original implementation attempted to store a `ProcessOperations` reference globally to send responses later. This caused dangling reference bugs because `ProcessOperations` is an abstract class passed as a reference parameter.

**Solution**: Changed to synchronous processing. Messages are parsed and processed immediately in `onBackendStdout()` while the `ProcessOperations&` reference is valid. This is safe because `callbacksRequireMainThread=true` ensures we're already on the main thread.

### Error Handling

All `writeToStdin()` calls now check for errors and log failures via `ELOG`. Unknown request methods receive proper JSON-RPC error responses instead of being silently ignored.

### Removed Code

- Removed `s_pendingResponses` queue (no longer needed with synchronous processing)
- Removed `processPendingMessages()` function (no longer needed)
- Cleaned up `onBackendProcessing()` and `onBackgroundExit()` to remove references to message queue

## Testing

### Manual Testing

Set environment variables and observe logging:

```bash
# Minimal logging (errors only from backend)
CHAT_LOG_LEVEL=1 CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL=error ./rsession

# Verbose logging for debugging (show all backend logs, raw JSON for non-logger messages)
CHAT_LOG_LEVEL=2 CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL=trace ./rsession

# Maximum verbosity (show everything including logger/log raw JSON)
CHAT_LOG_LEVEL=3 CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL=trace ./rsession

# Only show critical backend failures
CHAT_LOG_LEVEL=1 CHAT_BACKEND_MIN_LEVEL=fatal ./rsession
```

### Verification

With backend running:
- Send `runtime/getActiveSession` request → Verify response received with correct session data
- Send unknown method request → Verify error -32601 response returned
- Send request with `{"id": null}` → Verify response sent with `"id": null`
- Check backend logs filtered correctly by level
- Verify fatal logs always visible regardless of filter setting
- Confirm no duplicate output for logger/log messages

## Future Work

- **Python REPL detection**: Currently `language` is hardcoded to "R"
- **Additional RuntimeService methods**: `getWorkingDirectory`, `executeCode`, etc.
- **Mode detection**: Currently `mode` is hardcoded to "console"
- **Request timeouts**: Add timeout handling for request/response pattern (similar to SessionCopilot.cpp)

## Related Issues

Unblocks basic functionality by implementing the first RuntimeService API method that the backend requires to understand the execution context.

title: Additional fixes to rpostback askpass
description:
Addresses #16656

## Summary

Fixes a regression introduced in #16636 where the `rpostback askpass` the entered passphrase would not be captured.

## Root Cause

PR #16636 converted the RSA encryption from synchronous to asynchronous by having the JavaScript `window.encrypt()` function return a Promise with an object containing the encrypted data and algorithm:

```javascript
{ ct: "<base64-ciphertext>", alg: "RSA-OAEP" }
```

The Java/GWT code was updated to handle the Promise by calling `.then()`:

```java
$wnd.encrypt(value, exponent, modulo).then(callback.onSuccess, callback.onFailure);
```

This introduced three bugs:

### Bug 1: Callback Binding Issue (Modal Not Closing)

Fixed in a previous PR: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/16669

### Bug 2: Data Format Issue in Success Callback (Passphrase Not Captured)

Even with proper callback binding, the JavaScript object `{ct: "...", alg: "..."}` was being passed directly to a Java method expecting a String parameter:

```java
void onSuccess(String encryptedData);
```

When GWT converts a JavaScript object to a Java String, it produces `"[object Object]"` instead of the actual encrypted data. This corrupted value was sent to the server, causing decryption to fail and the passphrase to be lost.

### Bug 3: Data Format Issue in Error Callback

Similarly, the error callback had a type mismatch. JavaScript Error objects (with properties like `message`, `name`, `stack`) were being passed directly to a Java method expecting a `ServerError` interface:

```java
void onFailure(ServerError error);
```

The `ServerError` interface requires methods like `getCode()`, `getMessage()`, `getCause()`, etc., which JavaScript Error objects don't have. This would cause the error callback to fail if encryption ever encountered an error.

## Solution

The fix addresses all three issues by properly wrapping the callbacks using GWT's JSNI syntax and converting JavaScript data types to the expected Java types.


A helper method `createEncryptionError()` was added to create a `ServerError` implementation from an error message.


This ensures:
1. The Java callback methods are invoked with the correct context (previously fixed)
2. The encrypted data is extracted from the JavaScript object and formatted as `$RSA-OAEP$<ciphertext>`, which is the format expected by the server-side decryption code (fixes Bug 2: passphrase capture)
3. JavaScript errors are properly converted to `ServerError` objects that the Java code expects (fixes Bug 3: error handling)

## Testing

1. Start RStudio Server
2. Open a terminal in RStudio
3. Run: `/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/rpostback askpass "Enter test passphrase"`
4. A modal dialog should appear
5. Enter a passphrase and click OK
6. The dialog should close immediately
7. The passphrase should appear in the terminal output

Alternatively, trigger the askpass dialog through a git operation requiring authentication (e.g., `git push` to a repository with SSH key passphrase protection).

title: Fix `rpostback askpass`
description:
### Intent

Addresses #16656

(rpostback askpass modal not closing)

### Summary

Fixes a regression introduced in #16636 where the `rpostback askpass` modal dialog would not close when clicking OK, and the entered passphrase would not be captured.

Fixes #16656

### Root Cause

PR #16636 converted the RSA encryption from synchronous to asynchronous by having the JavaScript `window.encrypt()` function return a Promise. The Java/GWT code was updated to handle this by calling `.then()` on the Promise:

```java
$wnd.encrypt(value, exponent, modulo).then(callback.onSuccess, callback.onFailure);
```

However, this approach doesn't work correctly in GWT's JavaScript interop. When Java method references are passed directly to JavaScript code as callbacks, they lose their proper binding context. As a result:

1. The Promise resolves successfully in JavaScript
2. The `.then()` handler attempts to call `callback.onSuccess`
3. The callback fails to execute due to improper binding
4. The Java code never receives notification that encryption completed
5. The modal dialog never closes

No errors were logged because from JavaScript's perspective, the Promise resolved successfully. From Java's perspective, it was simply waiting for a callback that never came.

### Solution

Wrap the callback method invocations using GWT's JSNI (JavaScript Native Interface) syntax, which properly binds the Java methods when calling them from JavaScript:

```java
$wnd.encrypt(value, exponent, modulo).then(
   function(data) { callback.@org.rstudio.studio.client.common.crypto.RSAEncrypt.ResponseCallback::onSuccess(Ljava/lang/String;)(data); },
   function(error) { callback.@org.rstudio.studio.client.common.crypto.RSAEncrypt.ResponseCallback::onFailure(Lorg/rstudio/studio/client/server/ServerError;)(error); }
);
```

This ensures that when the Promise resolves or rejects, the Java callback methods are invoked with the correct context.

### Testing

1. Start RStudio Server
2. Open a terminal in RStudio
3. Run: `/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/rpostback askpass "Enter test passphrase"`
4. A modal dialog should appear
5. Enter a passphrase and click OK
6. The dialog should close immediately
7. The passphrase should appear in the terminal output

Alternatively, trigger the askpass dialog through a git operation requiring authentication (e.g., `git push` to a repository with SSH key passphrase protection).

### Files Changed

- `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/common/crypto/RSAEncrypt.java`

title: Implement JSON-RPC over stdio for Chat Backend Communication
description:
## Summary

Implements JSON-RPC over stdio protocol in SessionChat.cpp to communicate with the databot backend, following the proven patterns from SessionCopilot.cpp. This enables the backend to send logging notifications to RStudio's logging system, with infrastructure in place for future Request/Response and Events patterns.

## Background

The Chat pane's databot backend (Node.js) is launched with the --json flag, which enables JSON-RPC over stdio mode. Previously, SessionChat.cpp only logged stdout/stderr as plain text. This PR implements proper JSON-RPC message parsing and routing, starting with support for logging notifications from the backend.

##  Changes

Core Infrastructure (SessionChat.cpp)

Message Parsing:
- Added s_backendOutputBuffer for accumulating partial messages
- Added s_pendingResponses queue for parsed JSON-RPC messages
- Added case-insensitive Content-Length header regex (follows HTTP spec)
- Added s_notificationHandlers map for method routing

Notification Handling:
- registerNotificationHandler() - Register handlers for notification methods
- handleNotification() - Dispatch notifications to registered handlers
- processBackendMessage() - Route incoming messages (notifications vs responses)
- handleLoggerLog() - Handle logger/log notifications with direct level mapping:
    - trace → TLOG
    - debug → DLOG
    - info → ILOG
    - warn → WLOG
    - error → ELOG
- processPendingMessages() - Process queued messages
- onBackgroundProcessing() - Main-thread callback for safe message processing

Content-Length Message Parser:
- Replaced simple stdout logging with proper JSON-RPC message parser
- Parses Content-Length headers (case-insensitive per HTTP spec)
- Try to handle malformed message by only looking for Content-Length in complete header blocks
- Handles multiple messages in single read
- Buffers partial messages until complete
- Extracts body based on byte count (UTF-8 safe)
- Verbose logging at chatLogLevel >= 2

Thread Safety:
- Messages queued in onBackendStdout() on stdout thread
- Processing deferred to onBackgroundProcessing() on main thread
- Follows SessionCopilot pattern: separation of buffering from processing
- Infrastructure ready for future timeout handling

State Cleanup:
- Clear buffers on backend exit
- Clear buffers on shutdown

Design Decisions

1. Minimal Implementation Scope

- Only implements notification (fire-and-forget) pattern for current logging use case
- Request/Response and Events infrastructure deferred to future PR
- Keeps this PR focused and reviewable

2. Case-Insensitive Header Matching

boost::regex s_contentLengthRegex("Content-Length:\\s*(\\d+)", boost::regex::icase);
- Follows HTTP/JSON-RPC spec (headers are case-insensitive)
- Backend's connection.ts uses /i flag
- Prevents silent failure if backend emits different casing

3. Background Processing Pattern

- Follows SessionCopilot architecture: onStdout buffers, background processor handles
- Ensures main-thread execution for handlers
- callbacksRequireMainThread = true provides thread-safety guarantee
- No mutex needed (verified against SessionCopilot pattern)

## Testing

1. Set log level (optional):
  export CHAT_LOG_LEVEL=2  # 0=off, 1=errors, 2=verbose
2. Launch RStudio and start Chat backend
3. Verify backend logs appear in rsession logs with [databot] prefix
4. Check level mapping:
    - Backend logger.trace() → RStudio TLOG
    - Backend logger.debug() → RStudio DLOG
    - Backend logger.info() → RStudio ILOG
    - Backend logger.warn() → RStudio WLOG
    - Backend logger.error() → RStudio ELOG
5. Verbose mode (CHAT_LOG_LEVEL=2):
    - Should see "Received message from backend: {...}" for each JSON-RPC message

## Architecture

Message Flow
```
  Backend (Node.js)                    RStudio Session (C++)
        |                                     |
        | --[stdout]-->                       |
        | Content-Length: 123\r\n\r\n         |
        | {"jsonrpc":"2.0",...}               |
        |                                     |
        |                  [onBackendStdout - Any Thread]
        |                  - Accumulate in buffer
        |                  - Parse Content-Length header
        |                  - Extract message body (byte-based)
        |                  - Parse JSON
        |                  - Queue in s_pendingResponses
        |                                     |
        |              [onBackgroundProcessing - Main Thread]
        |                  - processPendingMessages()
        |                  - processBackendMessage()
        |                  - handleNotification()
        |                  - handleLoggerLog()
        |                  - DLOG/WLOG/ELOG/etc.
```
##  Thread Safety

  - callbacksRequireMainThread = true ensures callbacks run on main thread
  - poll() skips callbacks when not on main thread (PosixChildProcess.cpp:1063)
  - Background processor provides explicit main-thread execution
  - Matches SessionCopilot's battle-tested pattern (no mutex needed)

title: Add support for RSA-OAEP in encrypted credentials
description:
### Intent

Addresses rstudio/rstudio-pro#6675

RSA with PKCS#1 1.5 padding was deprecated in 2020 and prohibited from use in FIPS contexts in 2023. This PR adds support for a newer padding algorithm, OAEP.

### Approach

Because the `rsa.js` we use for client-side encryption doesn't support OAEP, I opted to use WebCrypto instead of implementing OAEP myself.

I had seriously considered implementing it myself, and I had actually gotten started, because WebCrypto is only available in "secure" contexts. However, as the code started getting awkward, I had second thoughts. When we discussed this recently, we had agreed that it would probably be acceptable to try to use WebCrypto and then fall back to `rsa.js` if it's not available.

To accommodate the fallback, I took a hint from the format used by `crypt()` and used `$algo$payload` as the syntax to mark the method used for encrypting the payload.

### Automated Tests

I added some unit tests to validate the server-side RSA implementation.

The existing tests should be able to validate the client-side implementation, but since we don't run them over HTTPS or from `localhost` normally it's not going to exercise the codepath in CI. We might want to think about how to address this.

### QA Notes

> Ensure you have updated the QA Notes in the original issue.

Done.

News is included in this PR.

title: Add LoongArch64 Support for RStudio
description:
## Add LoongArch64 Support for RStudio

This PR adds support for the LoongArch64 architecture by defining the appropriate architecture identifier for Quarto integration.

### Changes Made

1. **Architecture Definition**: Added `kQuartoArch "loongarch64"` definition for LoongArch64 platforms in the session options configuration, aligning with the existing architecture definitions for other platforms.

2. **Conditional Compilation**: Extended the preprocessor directives to properly recognize `__loongarch64` and assign the correct Quarto architecture directory name.

### Technical Details

The change follows the existing pattern used for other architectures:
- Uses `__loongarch64` macro for detection
- Assigns `"loongarch64"` as the architecture identifier
- Maintains consistency with Quarto's expected architecture naming conventions

```cpp
#if defined(_WIN32)
# define kQuartoArch "x86_64"
#elif defined(__aarch64__)
# define kQuartoArch "aarch64"
#elif defined(__amd64__)
# define kQuartoArch "x86_64"
#elif defined(__loongarch64) // Add LoongArch64 support
# define kQuartoArch "loongarch64" // Or "loong64", check what Quarto expects
#else
# error "unknown or unsupported platform architecture"
#endif
```

This enables RStudio to properly locate and utilize Quarto binaries and tools on LoongArch64 systems, ensuring full functionality of Quarto-related features including document rendering and project management.

### Important Note

While the RStudio desktop application build is currently not successful due to Electron not yet supporting LoongArch64, the server version can run properly by relying on the local Node.js runtime through the serve version.

### Testing

Verified that the build completes successfully on LoongArch64 systems and that Quarto integration functions correctly within the RStudio environment.

Fixes architecture support for LoongArch64-based systems running RStudio.

title: Fix issue with zooming and unzooming panes when no source documents are open
description:
### Intent

Addresses #16583

### Approach

Gory details follow:

#### Root Cause
The issue was caused by an asynchronous event handler that automatically transfers zoom to windows requesting visibility, combined with the Source window becoming visible during the zoom process.

#### The Sequence
1. User zooms Environment pane
2. `fullyMaximizeWindow(TabSet1, Environment)` is called
3. Correctly sets `maximizedWindow_ = TabSet1`, `maximizedTab_ = Environment`
4. Sets all panes to NORMAL state (required for proper EXCLUSIVE transition)
5. Sets TabSet1 to EXCLUSIVE state
6. Method completes and returns
7. Asynchronously, a `WindowEnsureVisibleEvent` fires for the Source window
8. The event handler sees:
   - `maximizedWindow_ != null` (TabSet1)
   - Source window is different from TabSet1
   - Interprets this as "user wants to transfer zoom to Source"
9. Calls `fullyMaximizeWindow(Source, Environment)`
10. This overwrites the correct zoom state with wrong values:
   - `maximizedWindow_ = Source`
   - `maximizedTab_ = Source`

#### Why This Happens
The `WindowEnsureVisibleEvent` handler at PaneManager.java:473 includes logic to automatically transfer zoom when a different window requests visibility:

```java
if (maximizedWindow_ != null && !maximizedWindow_.equals(window))
{
   fullyMaximizeWindow(window, lastSelectedTab_);  // Auto transfer!
   return;
}
```

This feature is intentional - it allows users to click on a minimized pane while zoomed and have the zoom transfer to that pane. However, it has an unintended side effect when empty Source windows request visibility during normal zoom operations.

### Automated Tests

Added a test for zooming/unzooming environment pane with no source document opened.

### QA Notes

Test as described. Try a variety of panes.

NOTE: the empty source document will still be created; it was too risky to try and mess with that

### Documentation

NA

title: fix issue with electron unit tests failing to run on Linux after upgrading Electron
description:
### Intent

Electron unit tests were failing to run on Linux, giving error:

```
ERROR: Unexpected module status 0. Cannot require() ES Module /tmp/jenkins-e148c0d3/workspace/IDE/OS-Builds/Platforms/linux-pipeline/rel-cucumberleaf-sunflower/src/node/desktop/node_modules/chai/chai.js because it is not yet fully loaded. This may be caused by a race condition if the module is simultaneously dynamically import()-ed via Promise.all(). Try await-ing the import() sequentially in a loop instead. (from /tmp/jenkins-e148c0d3/workspace/IDE/OS-Builds/Platforms/linux-pipeline/rel-cucumberleaf-sunflower/src/node/desktop/test/unit/core/array-utils.test.ts)
```

### Approach

Bump version of `mocha` package to match what's in `main`. This is only used for running unit tests so low risk.

The `.ncurc.json` file is copied over from `main` as well; this is only used by the `ncu` utility which I run manually to see what packages can be updated. The `@vercel/webpack-asset-relocator-loader` package must remain locked at the current version due to compatability issues with electron-forge.

title: don't show gutter icons for spelling mistakes
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/14510.

### Approach

When displaying lint in a document, we need to decide if we want to (1) display it within the gutter, (2) display it with an inline marker (e.g. underline some text), or (3) both.

Currently, spell issues display only with inline markers; however, syntax errors display with both. However, we were collecting both of these together as "annotations" and so were occasionally incorrectly displaying (or updating) spellcheck errors as gutter annotations.

This PR tries to resolve this by tracking "gutter" annotations and "inline" annotations separately, where "gutter" annotations display in _both_ the gutter and via an inline marker, while "inline" annotations display _only_ via an inline marker.

### Automated Tests

N/A

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/14510. In particular, you shouldn't ever see gutter icons for spelling mistakes.

description:

### Approach

This might come up randomly for our customers in 2025.05 and 2025.09 - Boost 1.87... if something the process does before initializing the http server gets a ERANGE error, that process throws this unexpected exception.

I tested this code and if you set errno = 34 -  it gets that error.  So setting it to 0 should avoid the problem.

title: support completions for pipe placeholder
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16415.

### Approach

Previously, the pipe parsing logic assumed completions would only be relevant within parentheses, e.g. as in

```R
mtcars %>%
    mutate(|)
```

However, new versions of R have introduced the base pipe operator `|>`, as well as `_` as a placeholder for the piped-in object. This means that code like this is valid:

```R
mtcars |> _$
```

where `_` refers to `mtcars`, and the expression here exists outside of any parentheses. This PR relaxes the logic uses to find the root of a pipe expression so that this can be handled.

### Automated Tests

A test is included.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16415.

description:
### Intent

One change is that the optional environment variable used to have RStudio use a different installation of the copilot-language-server has changed from `RSTUDIO_COPILOT_FOLDER` to `RSTUDIO_COPILOT_JS_FOLDER`. This avoids backwards compability issues if running a mixture of RStudio versions and using a customer Copilot installation. The `RSTUDIO_COPILOT_JS_FOLDER` must point to the directory containing the extracted contents of the Copilot Language Server Javascript distribution (e.g. [copilot-language-server-js-1.364.0.zip](https://github.com/github/copilot-language-server-release/releases/download/1.364.0/copilot-language-server-js-1.364.0.zip)). One other change is that on macOS we now bundle both x86_64 and arm64 node.js with the macOS RStudio, so on Apple Silicon machines copilot will no longer be running via Rosetta (as it was before we switched to the binaries in 2025.05). ### Automated Tests No new tests. Existing tests should continue working. ### QA Notes Things to check (beyond confirming that Copilot completions continue to work): - node.js is being installed with RStudio again, and on macOS, both Intel and ARM64 node.js are installed (details on expected location in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/16378) - on macOS, confirm that the arm version of node.js being used, and check that x86_64 is used, instead, on an Intel Mac - copilot-language-server Javascript distribution being installed with RStudio, instead of the binary distribution The Javascript copilot distro is cross platform (same bits for Mac, Windows, and Linux), and should look like this (details could change with new releases, but `language-server.js` should not change). ### Documentation Updated NEWS

title: fix unreliable use of errno
description:
### Intent

The way we're using `errno` in `AsyncChildProcess::poll()` isn't reliable, as we're calling other functions between the `::waitpid` call and checking the content of `errno` and it's possible for one of those other functions to modify it.

This doesn't fix any known issues, but it's wrong and I suspect it's causing the wrong error message to be logged, which certainly doesn't help with troubleshooting.

### Approach

This PR copies `errno` into a local variable immediately after the `::waitpid` call returns.

### Automated Tests

There's no consistent way to test this kind of behavior because the functions in question don't normally fail. This function is pretty heavily used, though, so the standard autotests will exercise it for regression testing.

title: let dirty flag be 'sticky' across background saves
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/15963.

### Approach

Allow the dirty flag on a document to be 'sticky' across background saves.

Note that a background save might be triggered not by changes in the in-editor buffer, but instead by changes in document properties -- for example, the chunk outputs associated with an R Markdown document. In this scenario, the save might be performed with no document changes, but this does not imply that the document on-disk will now be in-sync with our source database.

With this change, once a document is 'dirty', it will remain dirty until the user explicitly saves the document, which would tell RStudio to write the document's contents out to disk. This will cause us to incorrectly consider a document as 'dirty' after e.g. inserting a character, waiting for autosave, deleting a character, and then waiting for autosave again, but this seems better than the alternative.

This PR also changes some of the sequencing around when a document's dirty state is changed. In particular, we now only mark a document as "clean" following a successful save, whereas previously we were marking a document's dirty flag prior to the (successful or failed) save attempt.

title: fix issue with creating new folder in Choose Directory dialog
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16326.

### Approach

When the file/folder list widget was virtualized to handle huge file lists via https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/15666 the scenario of creating a new folder via the "New Folder" button in the web-based file dialogs was not updated to reflect this, leading to a reference to an `undefined` object. This includes "Choose Directory" and "Save File".

The code was trying to scroll the last item in the list into view in a way that relied on the old non-virtualized implementation; now it uses a method that knows about this change.

- Removes direct DOM manipulation that was incompatible with virtualized lists
- Uses the proper API (selectRow) that handles virtualized scrolling internally

### Automated Tests

QA is looking into that.

### QA Notes

The modified code is only invoked after using the "New Folder" button in the web-based file dialogs. It is called in response to confirmation that the folder has been created.

title: Cleanup GWT string resources
description:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> When merging this to pro, will need to check on these pro-specific changes:
> 
> LauncherSessionStatusLauncherSessionStatusUiBinderImplGenMessages_en.properties
> returnToWorkbenchHome=Return to Posit Workbench Home
> serverHomeText=Posit Workbench
> 
> CmdConstants_en.properties
> showAboutDialogLabel = About RStudio Pro...
> showAboutDialogMenuLabel = A_bout RStudio Pro

### Intent

- Eliminate redundant copies of the English strings (they existed up to four times each, often out of sync)
- Catch up on localizing strings into French
- Delete orphaned string entries in the properties files
- Fix incorrect use of `''` instead of `'` in properties files (see README.md for details on the scheme for this)
- Added a README.md (gwt/tools/locdiff/README.md) that describes the localization scheme (was actually for giving Claude Code context, but useful to keep around for future exercises of this sort)
- Got rid of `locdiff` tool; it made some bad assumptions (i.e. that all new strings were in the English properties files, which was definitely not the case) and after this change should be much easier to track string changes moving forward

### Approach

HUGE change. Mostly done via python scripts, in multiple passes, with lots of spot-checking along the way.

- Got rid of `@DefaultMessage()` in the .java files; the English string values now MUST be entered in the associated `*_en.properties` file (or GWT will fail to build), making this file the sole authority on English strings.
- Got rid of `@Key` in cases where it was the same as the method name (almost all cases).
- Scanned for orphaned and missing keys in the French files, and keys in the English files that weren't in the associated Java file, and fixed it all up (adding French translations to those that were missing)

Entries in the Java files for strings goes from:

```java
    /**
     * Translated "Documentation not found.".
     *
     * @return translated "Documentation not found."
     */
    @DefaultMessage("Documentation not found.")
    @Key("noDocumentation")
    String noDocumentation();

    /**
     * Translated "Package not found.".
     *
     * @return translated "Package not found."
     */
    @DefaultMessage("Package not found")
    @Key("noPackage")
    String noPackage();
```

to this:

```java
    String noDocumentation();
    String noPackage();
```

### Automated Tests

Ran existing GWT unit tests, and BRAT tests, and did some adhoc poking around the UI.

### QA Notes

This will mainly be tested by the full automation (when it assumes certain UI strings), and by general usage.

### Documentation

NA

title: allow access to authenticated repos from background jobs
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16278.

### Approach

This PR takes the machinery used to install the various R hooks we use to enable access to authenticated repositories, and ensures they're also made available to background jobs. Note that most of the code changes within are just re-organization; e.g. moving code to Tools.R as that file is normally sourced in so-called "augmented" child R processes.

The main code addition here is an R implementation of base64 encoding and decoding. The implementation here was adapted from `renv`, and has been thoroughly exercised and tested there.

### Automated Tests

TODO

### QA Notes

First, make sure you have the requisite credentials for solo.packagemanager.posit.co in your user `.netrc` file. Then,
test that the following script can successfully install packages, when run as a background job:

```R
options(repos = c(PPM = "https://solo.packagemanager.posit.co/cran-auth/latest"))
install.packages("renv")
```

title: defer setting height on chunk output
description:
### Intent

Speculatively addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16157.

### Approach

We have some code that tries to manually resize the chunk output widget after code execution has finished. My hypothesis is that, in some rare cases, the chunk output finished event might be received before we have finished rendering all error text into the chunk output widget, thereby causing us to resize the widget before we know the actual intended size.

As a band-aid, defer sync-ing the height after execution has finished, to give other machinery a chance to finish updating the chunk output.

title: fix: avoid hardcoding path to `xdg-open`
description:
### Intent

Makes the `viewer` RStudio API function work in Linux environments where `xdg-open` is found under a non-default location like e.g. in [Distrobox](https://distrobox.it)es (cf. https://github.com/89luca89/distrobox/issues/645#issuecomment-1462560668 and https://github.com/89luca89/distrobox/commit/e15cec7e3264878075ad8ee6161a06f7a53b6749). Also relevant for [`rstudioapi::viewer()`](https://rstudio.github.io/rstudioapi/reference/viewer.html) which calls the RStudio API function under the hood.

### Approach

Simply avoid hardcoding the path and instead expect `xdg-open` to be on `PATH` on Linux (which is usually the case).

title: use did-finish-load instead of ready-to-show at Electron startup
description:
### Intent

Addresses #16191 

### Approach

Per https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/40273 (and numerous other issues over the years) it appears Electron's `ready-to-show` message is not always fired, and we rely on that message to (1) show the main window and (2) hide the splash screen.

A common suggestion was to use `did-finish-load`, instead, so giving that a try.

### Automated Tests

None.

### QA Notes

I have never been able to repro this. It seems to be very machine and operating-system dependent.

So, if you are also unable to repro, at least do basic startup testing to ensure the main window appears and the splash screen goes away, even if you change focus to other windows (e.g. Alt+Tab on Windows) while RStudio is starting up.

Could also ask the person who opened the issue to try a daily build and see if it solves it, etc.

title: Fix segfault with use-after-free of Error object
description:
### Intent

> Describe briefly what problem this pull request resolves, or what new feature it introduces. Include screenshots of any new or altered UI. Link to any Github issues that are related. 

Fixes #16169.

### Approach

> Describe the approach taken and the tradeoffs involved if non-obvious; add an overview of the solution if it's complicated.

Debugging `rsession` revealed the issue:

```
Thread 1 "rsession" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x0000aaaae8eaa420 in rstudio::core::Error::operator= (this=0xffffcf743650) at /workspace/rstudio-pro/src/cpp/shared_core/include/shared_core/Error.hpp:178
178 class Error : public virtual ErrorLock
```

Which happened in the following code:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/blob/7ec3029abb4f14a72796757db86a4a37692f0c8d/src/cpp/session/modules/SessionDependencies.cpp#L629-L638

If the lambda is called after the `installDependencies` script returns, the local Error object we are capturing by reference will be destroyed by the time we attempt to reassign it inside the lambda.

Let's just not capture any variables and create a new Error object to use inside the lambda.

title: Update open file maximum with child processes
description:
* Switch to using the soft limit when closing file descriptors in a child process.
* Establish a reasonable upper limit of maximum files when closing file descriptors in a child process.

In recent Linux/Docker systems the hard limit for open files is set to nearly 1 billion. This causes issues with our slow close fallback mechanism which tries to brute-force close every file descriptor up to that limit. The limit of 1M included in this change was taken from an Ubuntu 22.04 system.

title: check for npm packages during precommit
description:
### Intent

Linting for the Desktop code was recently added, but the pre-commit hook fails if there are files modified in `src/node/desktop` but the dependencies haven't been installed because `prettier` and `eslint` aren't present.

Since these files can be modified in merge commits by people not working on Desktop, this results in people using `--no-verify`, which also bypasses the detect-secrets check.

### Approach

The detect-secrets check looks to see if `detect-secrets` is installed before running it. If it isn't installed, the hook outputs a non-error informational message.

This PR follows that precedent by checking for `prettier` and `eslint` before running the JS lint checks. If they aren't installed, it outputs an informational message directing the user to run `npm install` in the appropriate path.

When RStudio is executing a chunk, it will buffer any input submitted as part of that chunk execution, as per

The intention here is to collect all chunk input into a single "block" of command line history, so that it can all be recalled at once.

Unfortunately, it appears that RStudio was not sending a "chunk finished" event when an error occurred that halted chunk execution. This PR alleviates that.

title: Tell Copilot about source files loaded in the IDE before Copilot has started up
description:
### Intent

Addresses #15895

### Approach

When Copilot starts up tell the front-end UI to register any open documents with Copilot (one time). This ultimately uses the same code as the "project file indexing" feature.

This will typically be files that were left opened when the session closed, and thus get reloaded early in startup before Copilot has started up.

### Automated Tests

None

### QA Notes

- Add `RS_LOG_LEVEL=3` to ~/.Renviron
- Ensure signed in to Copilot in RStudio
- open some source files in the IDE (no project)
	- for my example I opened `a.R` and `hello.R`
- Close RStudio and then restart
- Examine Copilot logging output and make sure you see the following for previously opened files at startup

```
[indexFile]: Indexing document: ~/aaa/aaa/a.R
[indexFile]: Indexing document: ~/aaa/ppp/R/hello.R

REQUEST
----------------
Content-Length: 204
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"textDocument/didOpen","params":{"textDocument":{"uri":"file:///Users/gary/aaa/aaa/a.R","languageId":"r","version":0,"text":"...contents of file..."}}}
----------------

REQUEST
----------------
Content-Length: 622
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"textDocument/didOpen","params":{"textDocument":{"uri":"file:///Users/gary/aaa/ppp/R/hello.R","languageId":"r","version":0,"text":"...contents of file..."}}}
----------------
```

A second test case is to ensure project indexing is still working:

- open an RStudio project
- enable "Index project files with GitHub Copilot" in Global Options / Copilot
- open some files that are part of the project (and some that are not, if you want), then exit RStudio
- restart RStudio
- you should see every file in the project get indexed, then the opened files will get indexed
- there is some duplicated effort here; files that are part of the project AND previously left open will get registered twice; could do some work to eliminate this if we think it's worth it

title: Notify copilot about completion acceptance
description:
### Intent

Addresses #15903, and also puts back the change for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/15900 (which I accidentally stomped when I reverted the Visual Mode copilot change).

### Approach

See https://github.com/github/copilot-language-server-release?tab=readme-ov-file#inline-completions for gory details.

- when user accepts entire completion (tab key), invoke `workspace/executeCommand` with the completion command that was received with the completion
- when user accepts part of the completion (word-by-word via Cmd+Right Arrow), invoke `textDocument/didPartiallyAcceptCompletion` with the original completion plus the length of text accepted so far
- when a completion suggestion is shown, invoke `textDocument/didShowCompletion` (this is the part that was unintentionally removed)

### Automated Tests

None

### QA Notes

Enable logging via `COPILOT_LOG_LEVEL=3` in ~./Renviron, and check that the above messages are being sent and follow the format shown in https://github.com/github/copilot-language-server-release?tab=readme-ov-file#inline-completions.

There is no user-visible impact of these, it's all for Copilot's use server-side (metrics, training, whatever it does with it).

title: stop using maxFactors
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/14113.

### Approach

In older version of R (< 4.0.0), `stringsAsFactors = TRUE` was the default, and so data sets whose columns were logically character vectors were still read in as though they were factors. In practice, this meant you had character columns with a large number of unique "factors", even though it wasn't really intended to be used as a factor.

We tried to catch these scenarios by checking for factors which had more levels than might be typical, and treat those as though they were character vectors. Now that the default has changed, we can assume any existing factors are more intentional, and avoid "guessing" if they might have been intended to be character vectors.
