description: Fix for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/444, to disable verbose output while setting registry keys in windows for odbc installers but also add support for a `odbc.installer.verbose` option in case users need to troubleshoot.

title: Ignore errors in first regedit attempt in windows since it's expected to fail
description: Fix for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/443

title: Prevent intermitent failure from interproc odbcinst.ini flush
description: Potential fix for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/442, I haven't been able to reproduce this and the original repro is intermittent. We do write the odbcinst.ini file form a separate process as the last step while installing a driver and we immediately query to verify the installation so it's possible that the flush has not completed, planning to try this fix to see if we can be able to avoid this issue.

title: Fix odbc installer uninstall in linux due to case sensitivity
description: Fix for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/458, need to match case sensitivity in linux to uninstall odbc drivers correctly.

title: Support installing odbc drivers with existing drivers with same name
description: Fix for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/445, in some platforms, some drivers are already installed with the same name as potential drivers installed by RStudio. Only in these cases, a `with RStudio` is appended to the driver:

title: Fix odbc installer unnecessary warning
description: Fix for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/462, a warning is printed when it shouldn't.

title: fix handling of Shift+Tab keypress
description:
This PR fixes an issue where attempts to use <kbd>Shift + Tab</kbd> to shift focus to the previous element could fail. This was because the `insertSnippet` command was being handled within `AceEditorCommandDispatcher`, and since the `ShortcutManager` saw that the keypress had been dispatched to a command, it stopped propagation of the event and prevented the browser default behavior.

This PR also works around a Qt bug whereby its attempts to dispatch `Qt::Key_Backtab` events to Chromium would fail; we accommodate this by manually translating these back to regular shift-tabs.

Closes #2991.

title: mark UTF-8 encoding when extracting params
description:
This PR ensures that we re-mark the encoding of the document contents before passing it down to `knitr::knit_params()`. This fixes issues that occur when the document params cannot be represented in the current encoding.

(Some additional work is required in `knitr` to ensure arbitrary UTF-8 content can be handled on Windows)

title: Implement job cancellation
description:
This change makes it possible to abort (or interrupt) jobs in the Jobs pane.

When a job registers itself via `addJob`, it can supply a list of actions that can be performed on the job. If one of these actions has the special name `stop`, then the job is considered cancellable. 

A cancellable job gets a stop button next to its progress bar that can be used to request a stop.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/41566820-1a6808c4-7312-11e8-98cd-cc8784b30c60.png)

The job that represents R scripts now includes a `stop` action, so it gets the new cancellation treatment.

title: ensure RStudio exits after last window closed
description: This PR ensures that a close of a secondary window, if it is the final RStudio window opened, also quits the application.

title: ensure startup files have trailing newline (closes #3029)
description: Small enhancement that helps avoid the somewhat surprising behavior wherein a missing trailing newline in an R startup file can cause the final R expression in that file to be lost.

title: don't process file changes in packrat dir (#1864)
description: This PR fixes an issue where attempts to install R packages in a Packrat project could be very slow, due to the file monitor attempting to process file changes detected in the `packrat` folder. (This is especially true with the `BH` package which contains over 10,000 header files!)

title: Fix to package repos and support parsing inis with headers
description:
`.rs.readIniFile()` was missing to support nested structures to be properly called an `ini` file parser; while this feature is not required by the package management feature, better add support for this now that this is being heavily tested in case `.rs.readIniFile()` gets reused in the future.

Also fixing a repos preferences issue with reprex:
- Set `repos.conf`
- Clear user settings
- Restart session
- From preferences UI, remove secondary repos and revert to RStudio CDN
- Apply changes

Actual: Changes don't take effect until next session restart.
Expected: Changes to take effect.

title: Add support for header comments in odbcinst.ini
description: Fix for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/446.

title: Support package manager admins setting preferences
description:
While https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/2754 added support to set CRAN settings from the preferences pane or with admin settings like `r-cran-repos` and `repos.conf`, it was lacking support for use cases where admin settings are applied and also preferences need to be changed.

The behavior of this PR was to show inconsistent settings in the UI when the admin settings where set, usually, displaying the default CRAN repo or the user selection (which was made consistent with https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/2891 but was not showing what the final CRAN setting was).

This PR makes the system defaults visible by showing them in the preferences pane.
This PR also fixes one regression:
- Ability to change order in secondary CRAN repos from the UI

and a bug fix:
- Allow admins to change CRAN defaults after user logs in for the first time by setting `repos.conf`, etc. The problem here was that there are more places that use the user settings to set the CRAN repos, rather to chase all the places that might change this setting, we are adding a new `changed` user setting that is set only when an operation triggers from the UI.

title: ensure dialogs created by R shown on top
description:
This PR attaches a Windows event handler, listening for dialogs created by the `rsession` process. When such a dialog is created, we ensure that window is activated and brought to the front.

Fixes #2901. One thing worth discussing is whether we need to be more careful about which dialogs that R might create need to be brought to the front; I think it's okay to assume that all dialogs created from R are modal and require immediate user attention but perhaps I'm missing some cases where that might not be true (download dialogs?)

title: Allow deletion of secondary repos to fix #2860
description: Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2860

title: Feature/custom-themes
description:
Adds the theme conversion functionality for the user extensible theme feature. Note that `.rs.api.addTheme`, `.rs.api.removeTheme`, and `.rs.api.applyTheme` are partially implemented but not finished yet (they will be finished in a later PR). Additionally the UI updates will also be added in a later PR.

`.rs.api.convertTheme` takes a tmTheme file location, converts it from a tmTheme to an ACE CSS theme, and then modifies the ACE CSS into an rstudio compatible theme. It optionally saves a copy of the `.rstheme` file at a user specified location. When the other api methods are implemented and working correctly, it will also optionally add the theme to RStudio, either for a single user or globally, and if it adds the theme it may also optionally apply the theme to RStudio immediately.

title: Support multiple statements in SQL preview
description: Dependent on https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/2720 to consider this independently. DBI does not support executing multiple statements, see https://github.com/r-dbi/RPostgres/issues/138, but we can consider splitting them ourselves to enable more useful SQL script and modify also the default script that is created:

title: Upgrade embedded Pandoc to 2.2
description:
This change picks up Pandoc 2.2, which contains a number of important fixes to PowerPoint conversion.

It also updates our Pandoc installation scripts to use the folder layout from the official Pandoc releases, so that it's easier to upgrade to new releases (now that Pandoc is shipping static binaries we no longer need to rebuild or repackage). 

Closes #2714.

title: Save document when running test file to fix #2691
description: Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2691

title: Support for additional testthat file detection patterns
Attempt to parse package from testthat file
description: While testing a single `testthat` file under a project, `testthat::test_file()` works but the UI entry in the file does not. Previous testing of this feature was performed outside a project where one is expected to manually include the library, this fix parses the project only for `testthat` files and fixes an old merge conflict.

title: Add API for displaying job progress
description:
This change adds an API to RStudio for displaying progress and output from ongoing jobs. 

When a job is running, its progress is displayed in the Console pane.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/39071073-95e3c7a0-449a-11e8-9d18-22a8c18bf4ba.png)

It's possible for multiple jobs to run at once. When this happens, the Console pane summarizes the progress of all of the jobs. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/39071172-ee3eb0f4-449a-11e8-9117-f59a4e602f45.png)

It is also possible for jobs to emit more detailed information, including:

- their current status (e.g. "Pending", or "20kb/s")
- a stream of output
- their current state (running, failed, finished, etc.)

This additional information is shown in a new Jobs pane, which lists all of the running jobs (if any).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/39071343-88a6adc2-449b-11e8-8053-3cb3a4e4974e.png)

An individual job can be selected to examine that job's output and progress.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/39071544-54d62512-449c-11e8-8a31-8a14bbe0fda2.png)

There are still a few work items left; namely, support for grouped jobs, support for job callbacks (cancellation, help, etc.), and support for jobs which outlive the R session, but all will extend the framework introduced here.

title: Support changing d3 themes in notebooks
description: Themes can also change in notebooks in which case we need to notify all the frames of the theme update for all D3 renderings to update correctly.

title: associate rstudio API dialog requests with active window
description: This PR ensures that the file dialog APIs launched through `rstudioapi` are associated with the window that is currently focused, rather than the 'owner' of the GWT callbacks. This ensures that e.g. Shiny applications which open file dialogs will show the file dialog above the Shiny window, rather than the main window.

Not sure we want to implement our own 'download manager' in RStudio but at least this leaves the door open if we do?

This provides an escape hatch for users being hit bit slowness when RStudio's clipboard monitoring enabled, as per https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2068.

One can launch RStudio with something like:

```
RSTUDIO_NO_CLIPBOARD_MONITORING=1 rstudio
```

to activate this feature (pending extra UI for toggling this).

title: clamp htmlwidget height; tweak propagation of wheel events
description:
Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2174.

Note that this does tweak the scroll behavior for HTML widgets in Notebooks: widgets no longer unilaterally propagate wheel events; rather, they only propagate them when they have reached their scroll bounds and cannot be scrolled anymore.

(I initially wanted to test this by looking at e.g. the height of the iframe, but that was always reported as 0 -- or perhaps I'm misunderstanding some interplay between how an iframe's scroll position is reported)

Fixes #2541.

This PR also removes the 'GWTCallbackOwner' class as I felt that made the code harder to understand / read. We know the owner must be a GWT window, so let's just give it a GWT window.

Download: https://dev.mysql.com/get/Downloads/Connector-ODBC/5.3/ File: mysql-connector-odbc-5.3.10-macos10.13-x86-64bit.tar.gz Library: libmyodbc5a.so Warning: MySQL requires iODBC which can be downloaded from iodbc.org MD5: 698d85034830e59e0a311d268c6e7cbb ``` When the "New Connection" dialog opens, once per session, it will retrieve `connections-installer` and unpack the installers to `.rstudio/odbc/installers`, the installers will be read from this directory and presented in the dialog as follows, the example bundle contains only the MySQL driver with support for OS X: Notice that if the dialog fails to reach out to update the installer definitions, it will present this warning: When a user clicks an ODBC installer, it will prompt to install the `odbc` package if not installed, followed by a pre-install page: Then installation starts in the next page: and the driver is available as expected, if a connection snippet is provided, it will be shown otherwise the generic connection is presented: Notice that an `uninstall` button has been added, which will remove the driver with the following prompt when clicked: Finally, when the driver version inside the DCF changes, say to `Version: 5.4` in the example above, a warning is presented to the user to recommend uninstalling/reinstalling the driver:

title: Add harness for testing RPCs; move ad-hoc testthat tests
description:
This small change makes it possible to invoke session RPCs from tests, making it possible to write tests which invoke code in the R session in very much the same way that a client would. (It may also be helpful for ad-hoc use during development.) After the change, you can call:

    .rs.invokeRpc("name_of_rpc", arg1, arg2, ...)

The method returns the result of the RPC, and raises an R error if the RPC fails.

The invocation does not occur over the network; instead, it takes advantage of all of the R / JSON marshaling code that already exists to (a) convert the arguments into JSON, (b) synthesize a request with that JSON, (c) invoke the registered handler, and (d) marshal the resultant JSON back to R. 

As a proof of concept, some environment tests which add, list, and remove objects using RPCs are have been added. 

Finally, a couple of ad-hoc testthat tests from a few years back have been brought into the new framework.

title: Fix issue with persistent scrollbars on macOS
description:
This change fixes #1953, in which auto-hide scrollbars don't actually auto-hide on macOS (they are always visible).

The actual issue is fairly deep inside Chromium. Overlay scrollbars are painted on a second painting pass so that they're painted on top of other UI. However, this second pass does not occur when using the compositor, because the compositor defines a separate layer for scrollbar painting. Unfortunately the alpha animation that shows and hides the scrollbar is only painted during this 2nd pass, so using the compositor causes the animation to run but not paint, with the result that the scrollbar gets stuck in the fully opaque state.

The fix here is more of a workaround. Chromium has a preference which allows you to choose whether you'd prefer better text rendering (LCD text subpixel rendering/antialiasing) or using the compositor, which can be faster. The default is to use the faster but less accurate compositor. Switching the default to prefer better text rendering has the side effect of keeping us out of the problematic compositor codepath.

title: Fix opening project file in osx to fix #2203, #2205 and fix #2238
description: Fixes for #2203, #2205 and #2238. Project code assumes the last argument is the project name; therefore, this fix avoids appending more arguments at the very end. Somewhat related to https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/4350d5ea81c64b9d3f35d6a1deb9f42ee1f5012b but hard to catch since the relationship to the position was non-trivial.

title: ensure errno loaded from msvcrt when checking iconv success
description:
This should fix #2315.

---

Some background: it looks like `Riconv.dll` imports `msvcrt.dll`, and uses `_errno` from there. On the other hand, `rsession` is getting it from a different runtime altogether: `api-ms-win-crt-runtime-l1-1-0.dll`, which I believe is required for applications built with MSVC 2015 + Qt.

One alternative way of approaching this would be to attempt to link directly with `msvcrt.dll`, but I'm not sure if this would work with MSVC + Qt (although this may be worth exploring if we're not a fan of this solution).

We might want to wrap this up into something cleaner, and make it clear that when calling R APIs that set `errno` we need to explicitly grab it from `msvcrt.dll`.

title: import + patch sh highlight rules for heredocs
description: Fixes #2398.

title: Expose R session to testthat
description:
This change was made in order to support testing on a new 1.2 feature. It makes it possible to run tests against the R session executable, `rsession`, using the R package testthat.

The new tests complement the existing C++ unit tests (written in Catch). They are most useful for the following:

- Testing the .R code which supports the various session modules.
- Testing the R session from outside, as a black box in real-world conditions.
- Writing test scripts in R.

To make this possible, the R session gains a new parameter, `--run-script`. This new parameter causes the R session to behave very much like R does with `-e`; that is, it starts up normally, runs the R code given, and exits. In this mode, it also outputs to stdout rather than emitting console events. 

After this change, the R unit tests are run as part of `rstudio-tests`. You can also run just the R unit tests as follows:

    ./rstudio-tests --scope r

Future improvements may include:

- The ability to test session RPCs directly (w/o going over http)
- Integration with the build system to run tests as part of the build

The change is much smaller than it looks; most of the delta here is just a refactor of a large file (`RSession.cpp`) that would have otherwise been pushed pass the 2K line mark with this change.

description:

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2126.

Reported upstream at https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-66207 (was able to reproduce using the Qt 'minimal' example)

title: zoom without reloading RStudio UI
description: Does what it says on the tin -- makes it possible to zoom / unzoom the IDE on all platforms, without needing a reload of the whole UI.

title: Add a few additional db icons
improve Viewer performance w/large datasets
description:
This PR should vastly improve the data viewer performance when attempting to view large datasets (>10M rows). We avoid accidentally synthesizing a character vector equal to the number of rows of the dataset, when the row names are stored in a so-called compact representation.

I believe this will close #1705. While this does fix one kind of data viewer slowness, I unfortunately don't think it'll fix the issue seen by users when attempting to View datasets when their home directory lives on a network drive (that is still a separate issue).

title: Improvements to GWT build & test
description:
This change makes a number of improvements to the GWT build process.

- **GWT, GIN, and other libraries can now be stored outside the source tree**. Formerly, these libraries were presumed to exist at a hardcoded location inside the source tree. This change allows us to cache them in the Docker build containers, resulting in faster, less network-reliant builds.

- **Build output can now be placed in the binary directory**. Formerly, build output only went to the source directory. Using the binary directory prepares us for an upcoming change in which builds will happen outside the source tree.

- **Unit tests are run as part the build process**, using a unit test script generated at compile time with the appropriate folders.

None of these changes disturb the workflow we already use; the default directories are the same as they've always been, so local development workflow is unchanged.

title: resolve aliased vcs paths from client
description: This PR fixes an issue where users who have e.g. Git or SVN binaries installed into a sub-directory of home (which is somewhat common for portable Git installations on Windows) would find that their binaries were not properly detected / used. This would manifest as e.g. the Git tab not showing up, despite having pointed RStudio to an existing git executable.

title: Don't suspend sessions with external pointers (fixes #1696)
description:
This change prevents sessions from suspending when they have active external pointer objects.

This more or less duplicates some existing R code which looked for the opposite case (`NULL` external pointers). This has been rewritten in C for efficiency, and updated to search inside environments as well as S4 objects.

title: handle autocompletion of C++Object
description: Closes #1654.

title: Fix retina icon while republishing rsconnect plot to fix #1585
description: See https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1585

title: Add community forum link
description:
This change adds a link to the [RStudio Community Forum](https://community.rstudio.com/c/rstudio-ide) to the IDE's help menu.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/31566502-c60f67f0-b01f-11e7-905b-6a7cb1dd9158.png)

In RStudio Open Source, this link replaces the link to RStudio Support; in Pro, both links are shown. 

Practically speaking, very little peer-to-peer support occurs on the "support forum"; most questions take a long time to appear (~1 day), and have no responses or only a single response from the IDE team. In contrast, the community forum (though new) is much more user-friendly and has more active peer support. The downside, of course, is that it doesn't have the long tail of searchable content, so there's undoubtedly a tradeoff here.

title: fork python highlight rules
description: This PR forks Ace's Python highlight rules, in preparation for future improved editor support. We also implement a bit of extra highlighting, to better match how we highlight in R modes. (e.g. we now highlight brackets and `.`)

title: avoid querying clipboard while modal active
description: This should fix #1587.

title: Discard old data import assemble responses
description: It is possible that a response will come out of order in the data import dialog while assembling preview, for instance, as report by @jennybc: and a request log showing: Fix is to discard old assemble responses coming into this dialog.

title: Implement search for connections (closes #1549)
description:
This change adds a search bar to the Connections tab that, when connected, makes it possible to search for object in the connection by name.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/31422916-f20f3928-ae05-11e7-8968-0ea0da3ae73e.png)

Some notes:

- The search is currently fully local; that is, it does not query the server for matching objects. This allows very fast, as-you-type filtering, and avoids network calls and expensive queries. However, it might not be what users expect in all cases. We'll need to add something to the connections contract if we want to implement driver-backed queries.

- GWT's `CellTree` doesn't have a way to hide or show nodes; and opening and closing them as the user types results in some pretty unpleasant side effects. So the approach taken here is somewhat backhanded; we mark search matches in the DOM with a CSS class when the tree is rendered, and then make a second render pass of our own to hide the elements that don't match.

title: Change "build and reload" to "install and restart"
description: Change the title of the Build and Reload command, as suggested by Hadley. Also cleans up some invalid XML in this file.

title: Ensure tables refreshed on connected state
description:
This change fixes a bug in which the list of tables in the Connections pane is sometimes not fetched when initially connected. The fix is in two parts:

1. If we have a connection and enter the connected state, refresh the list of objects.

2. Because of this change (and some other codepaths around connection state changes), it is possible in some circumstances that two or more requests will be made for the list of tables concurrently. This can be an expensive call for some large databases, so if a request for the object list is made while we are currently waiting for one to return, we now stack the requests and fulfill both with the single pending RPC.

title: Fix code margin overlapping chunk under 'chaos' editor theme
description: THe chaos theme uses `border 1px` instead of `width 1px` like the other themes for their code margin, not entirely sure why this theme behaves in this way but seems safe enough to reduce the width to make it render similar to the other themes, with this change:

title: patch 'selectDirectory()' for rstudioapi 0.7
description:
This PR fixes an issue in rstudioapi 0.7 (which unfortunately just hit CRAN) wherein we accidentally delegated `selectDirectory()` to `selectFile()` instead.

This PR allows us to fix the issue on the RStudio side without necessitating a patch release of the `rstudioapi` package. (@jjallaire, let me know if you'd prefer if we just submit a patch release instead)

title: Avoid dark scrollbars on non-osx systems under popups
description: Two issues, 1) On windows: The problem here is that `useScrollbars()` was setting the scrollbars CSS when it was only intended for dark themes. However, since... 2) While changing between dark and light themes scrollbars don't change and require an rstudio restart. The fix for (1) and (2) is to rather make scrollbars dynamic based on `rstudio-dark-theme` CSS property. This works for the most part, except for a Safari bug (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3485365/how-can-i-force-webkit-to-redraw-repaint-to-propagate-style-changes) which prevents scrollbars from changing colors based on CSS changes. The workaround is to set a parent div to `display: none` and then `display: auto`. However, I'm hesitant to implement this workaround since it could cause unintended consequences. Instead, whenswitching themes, you might have to tab to a different pane and then tab back for the effect to take change.

title: vim extension: open adjacent files on filesystem
description:
This PR adds a small extension to our Vim integration that allows `]f` to open the next file on the filesystem, and `[f` to open the previous file on the filesystem (relative to the currently active open file). (Inspired by [vim-unimpaired](https://github.com/tpope/vim-unimpaired))

Users who want to use these commands outside of Vim mode can do so by rebinding them to separate shortcut keys.

title: fix 'Export to Image' for macOS desktop
description:
This PR fixes an issue where 'Export to Image' would fail on macOS when attempting to export Viewer content (e.g. HTML widgets).

It looks like newer versions of WebKit no longer return an `NSBitmapImageRep` as the first element of the possible image representations here -- rather, it returns an `NSCGImageSnapshotRep`, which AFAICS is not a publicly exported type. However, we can still get the bitmap image data through a separate set of APIs, which I believe should be backwards-compatible with older WebKit as well.

This may be a candidate for the patch release, since the current release of RStudio is affected by this as well.

title: Avoid incorrect connections in new connections list
description:
When a custom `script.R` connection is added, other connections using shiny connections get the incorrect packages, for instance, `sparklyr` connections stop rendering.

The issue triggers while comparing under a filter...

```
Filter(
  function(e) e$package == "sparklyr" & e$name == "Spark",
  list(
    list(package = NULL, name = "Test"),
    list(package = "sparklyr", name = "Livy"),
    list(package = "sparklyr", name = "Spark")))
```

returns "Livy" while "Spark" would be expected.

This is caused by a package being NULL, which mekes `package = NULL` becomes `logical(0)`, since Filter is implemented as:

```
ind <- as.logical(unlist(lapply(x, f)))
  x[which(ind)]
```

The `logical(0)` is omitted from `unlist` and the incorrect filter is returned.

title: Add Ubuntu Xenial builds
description:
This change has three distinct parts:

### Support for newer Debian-based Linux systems

It's not straightforward to install RStudio on systems based on Debian Stretch and Ubuntu Xenial, due to the introduction of new, incompatible system libraries on these distributions. This change adds a server build; when we're able to resolve dependencies in Qt we'll add a desktop build as well.

### Docker compilation tool for developers

There's a new `docker-compile.sh` tool included here that's designed to make it easy for developers to simulate the builds that occur in the lab on their local machines, without installing Jenkins (or really any local software other than Docker itself).  

### Improved Qt caching behavior

Formerly, Qt was downloaded every time we built RStudio in a container. We now download Qt and install it to `/opt` as part of the container's build process, so it can be cached.

title: Add connections pane support for structured object types
description:
Prior to this change, the connections pane supported only tables. After the change, it supports a hierarchy of objects, as supplied by the connection itself. The goal is to make it possible to navigate large databases by allowing users to drill down to specific objects as they do in traditional DBMS software.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/470418/24419668/c6e16f74-13a4-11e7-9e99-24f0586b3408.png)

There are three main changes which support this feature:

1. A connection now emits its object hierarchy when initialized, and the hierarchy is stored along with the connection. See the new `listObjectTypes` method on the connection observer, and the new `object_types` member of the persisted connection.

2. When specifying an object to interact with (e.g. preview), a fully qualified specifier is now necessary (not just a string with the object's name). This specifier is an array of names and types giving the parents of the object; for instance, a table `humanresources.employee` might be specified as `[{name = "humanresources", type = "schema"}, {name = "employee", type = "table" }]`. These become the arguments to the functions supplied by the connection, and are opaque to RStudio.

3. The object browser is now capable of showing several levels of nested objects; each object has its own child object provider which knows how to list its children (using the stack of specifiers mentioned above). 

There are pull requests into both the ODBC and SparklyR packages which use this new contract:

https://github.com/rstats-db/odbc/pull/42

https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/pull/580

title: guard against incompatible R versions on restore
description:
NOTE: not quite ready for merge; likely needs some tweaking re: how the message is reported to the user.

This PR fixes an issue where R could crash on startup when attempting to restore an workspace associated with a different version of R than the currently active version of R.

The fix is mostly straightforward -- on suspend, we now write the R version to a file; on restore, we validate against that version, and abort the restore if either the major or minor versions differ.

This should hopefully reduce some headaches that we might see with the introduction of R 3.4.0.

Right now, the error message is just plainly reported to the console:

![screen shot 2017-03-22 at 12 49 02 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/24217741/1816069e-0efe-11e7-9fdb-485d775326f6.png)

but we might want to tweak this (e.g. just change the error message, or provide a modal dialog information the user, or otherwise)

title: improve RStudio's ability to recover crashed sessions
description:
This PR allows us to check whether a link-based lockfile is orphaned; that is, generated by an `rsession` process that no longer exists. (This typically occurs when an `rsession` process crashes, and hence is unable to clean up the lockfile on exit.)

We accomplish this by writing the process ID of the active R session to the generated lockfile, and allowing other processes to check the PID in that lockfile when determining whether the lockfile is active or stale / orphaned.

This PR should ensure that users who see their R session crash are able to promptly reconnect to the previous session, and in particular should fix bogus 'File not found' errors that can pop up during file autosave when this underlying 'session disconnect' has occurred.

Currently, the PR is relatively conservative about the process id check -- in theory, since we don't check whether the existing process is an RStudio process of some kind, it's possible that another non-RStudio process could be generated with the same PID as seen in the lockfile, and we would then fail to detect that as orphaned. In practice, this should almost never occur.

title: support setting sql connection with knitr options
description:
SQL chunks support referencing connection by object and name, as in ` ```{r options=db}` or ` ```{r options="db"}`. However, we currently only support setting this through `knitr::opts_chunk$set` as `knitr::opts_chunk$set(connection="db")`. The cause, I believe, is that we internally serialize the options when we prepare the setup chunk and when running the data chunk, the `connection` is no longer a default.

Repro:

    ```{r setup}
    library(DBI)
    db <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), dbname = "sql.sqlite")
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(connection = db)
    ```

    ```{sql}
    SELECT 1
    ````

Instead of failing, this fix checks the cached version of the options `.rs.knitr.chunkOptions` before failing.

title: Make bringtotop unsupported in Windows
description:
Since `bringToTop` crashed in windows, this change marks this function as unsupported.

Some context: This is a `NULL` pointer dereference while running in `RGui` mode (https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/17e4dd5b60a3a148aa0664f01590acafb104ab4a/src/include/R_ext/RStartup.h#L53), in which `RConsole` is set to `NULL` but never initialized (https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/af7f52f70101960861e5d995d3a4bec010bc89e6/src/gnuwin32/rui.c#L50) Since there is no RGui in Linux, we don't have this crash outside Windows.

The commit that introduced this: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/7f71b9727725d9812eec10dacb87601f085272cc

We could, potentially, revert the change above which would fix this issue and the `utils::timestamp` crash; however, that would be a risky change since other features might depend on running on `RGui` mode in Windows.

@jcheng5 out of curiosity, do you remember why it's important to run `RGui` in Windows?

title: Fix YAML header mangling in backtick expressions
description:
This change fixes an oft-reported bug that arises when the YAML header contains something like this:

    date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%d %B, %Y')`"

When this gets round-tripped through the YAML package, the package decides to convert it into a single-quote string, and to escape the single quotes inside it. This doesn't go well, and leaves something like this:

    date: '`r format(Sys.time(), ''%d %B, %Y'')`'

Because the YAML package only does this for backtick expressions, this change works around the problem: it replaces backtick expressions with placeholder strings, and then puts them back after the conversion to YAML is complete.

title: fix regression in data viewer from f7794e by making column sortable
description: Run `View(mtcars)`, sort by column, click on top-left cell to clear formatting, observe it no longer works. Updated also support article form "right-top cell" to "left-top cell".

title: validate target path for new packages
description: This PR implements a bit of extra validation for the path chosen in new R package projects. The goal here is to avoid dismissing the 'New Package' dialog when an invalid path has been chosen.

title: suppress synthesized mouse events on modifier keys
description:
The issue here is a bit fiddly, so I'll try to explain what's going on...

With Safari WebKit, when a modifier key is pressed, the mouse cursor position is updated (the cursor is shown) and associated mouse events are emitted. This can cause a problem while typing in a textbox that has an associated completion list popup (e.g. Find in Files, C++ autocompletion popups) -- if the mouse cursor happens to lie over the generated popup, pressing a modifier key effectively moves focus to that menu item. (You can imagine trying to type a capital letter, and then seeing the mouse suddenly appear and set the selection / steal focus away from where you are typing.)

This PR attempts to resolve that issue by attempting to detect those synthesized events, and suppress them. If the last event was a key event (the user was typing), and the current event is a mouseover or mouseout with an associated modifier key (detecting a synthesized mouse event), then we eat that event, and any other future non-mousemove events for that short session.

title: Fix connections toolbar not refreshing in connection view
description: The connections toolbar is not being refreshed when the active list of connections changes and the user is viewing the active connection. With this fix we recreate the toolbar whenever the connection list changes, usually while connecting or disconnecting from connections.

title: Implement readline-like "reverse-i-search" for R console
description:
This change implements reverse incremental searching at the R console, a common request made by users who are used to this feature in bash and other Unix shells. 

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/470418/22674784/b1bac15c-ec96-11e6-909f-8873a59f2a23.png)

The reverse incremental mode differs from the existing Cmd+Up behavior in that it doesn't self-dismiss once you add characters; instead, it stays up and filters in real time as you type. Just as in bash, it's toggled by pressing Ctrl+R (the existing Cmd+Up behavior has not changed).

title: Allow F2 to open data frames
description: This change implements a suggestion to allow F2 to open data frames in addition to functions. It is designed for use in traditional R scripts wherein the data is present in the global environment, and invokes `View()` on the data if found (just like clicking on it in the Environment pane).

title: tweaks around sizing of inline chunk popups

description:
This PR resolves an issue where the chunk header parser (and hence the dialog for editing that chunk) would fail for chunk headers of the form:

    ```{r message=TRUE}

![screen shot 2016-11-02 at 3 03 43 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/19949195/9bec6774-a10d-11e6-9a96-66093b25acd6.png)

In such a case, we incorrectly parse the first option as the label, as we had expected to see a `,` separating the engine + (optional) label and the chunk option list.

title: Enable display of diagnostics when publishing
description:
This change adds a new UI pref that turns on a diagnostic mode for publishing.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/470418/19951660/d2ed347e-a11c-11e6-8f19-b157bda94764.png)

When enabled, lots of additional information is emitted to the Deploy tab, including:

- the full text of the `deployApp` command submitted on the user's behalf
- the user's `sessionInfo()`
- all the JSON messages sent and received from the server
- a full stack trace for any locally occurring errors

As part of this change, I've done some shallow refactoring on the publish RPC. It has so many parameters that we have to modify our function templates every time we add one. I've split the major groupings of parameters into objects.

title: don't save + restore workspace for 'install.packages'
description:
This PR seeks to resolve a loop that can occur when attempting to install a package that is currently loaded.

The overarching issue -- when RStudio restarts the session when installing a package, it also saves and restores the global environment. However, certain objects can force the load of a package namespace -- if the namespace of the package which we want to install is inadvertently loaded while restoring the global environment, then RStudio will present us with the same prompt again.

![install-loop](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/19951602/5cf5efa4-a11c-11e6-81bb-2a1e6abdff12.gif)

This PR seeks to resolve the issue by passing along the `saveWorkspace` argument through the regular `save` call. Previously, this argument was ignored (from the comments before it appears this was intentional, although I don't know why exactly); so the change here just makes sure that we respect this option in the regular `save` code path.

One major change with this PR is that we now actually discard the global environment when restarting for a package installation -- we could also defer restoration of the global environment instead until after the `install.packages()` command has run to completion.

title: evaluate notebook condition handler code in base namespace
description:
This PR resolves an infinite loop error that occurs when executing a notebook chunk if the user has defined a custom function called `c` in the global environment.

The overarching issue -- `evaluateStringUnsafe` evaluates its code in the global environment by default; hence, symbols will be resolved from there as well. This implies that any user-defined functions or symbols in the global environment that mask those in `base` will be picked up instead (note that in some occasions this behavior might actually be desired, but that isn't the case here).

The change here ensures that we evaluate the handler-attaching code directly in the base namespace.

title: Address race conditions in source database
description:
The underlying issue addressed by this change is that the persistent (`per`) directory of the source database can be read and written to, without guards, by multiple RStudio sessions. When running in multiple session mode this isn't a problem since each session gets its own persistent directory.

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/3dff46a66359df96a01e247a4a8a99c26cc1a5e2/src/cpp/session/SessionSourceDatabaseSupervisor.cpp#L71-L82

In desktop mode however there exists only a single persistent directory, even though multiple sessions can exist. This creates the potential for timing-related errors.

This change does two things to mitigate the problem:

**Use a stable folder for the source database**. Prior to this change, the source database got a unique ID on every session start. This meant that on restart or suspend/resume, the whole source database was pushed into the persistent directory on the way down, and rehydrated from the persistent directory on the way up, into a fresh directory with a new ID. 

After the change, the name of the source database folder is stable through suspend/resume. The folder therefore just stays in place until the session is actually terminated (quit). Since sessions no longer read or write from the persistent folder during the ordinary course of operations, it's not necessary to guard access to that folder with concurrency primitives.

In order to distinguish source database folders which represent suspended (or restarting) sessions from those which represent crashed sessions, a `suspend_file` is written to the folder prior to suspending and removed when resuming. Folders containing these files aren't treated as crashed sessions when looking for an orphan session to adopt.

**Add a launcher token to the session.** There can be multiple desktop sessions running at once, so when a session is resumed, it needs to know which source database to reattach to. This information is supplied from the session launcher by generating a random "launcher token" and supplying it to the session when it (re)starts. 

The launcher token functions more or less identically to the session ID in multisession mode. It represents an instance of a session launcher (for instance, an instance of rstudio.exe). In fact, the analog is close enough that it can be used as a drop-in replacement for the active session ID in most places, and replaces the "virtual session ID" used previously. 

For consistency, we also use a launcher token in server mode. An entire server can use a single launcher token; in single session mode, the context ID already scopes the source database, and in multisession mode, the session ID replaces the launcher token as the identifier for the database.

Some caveats:

1. No attempt is made to ensure that launcher tokens are unique. The odds of this being a problem are vanishingly small as the set of active launchers is bounded by the number of open RStudio windows (and therefore the odds of a collision are infinitesimal), but we could guard against this if we think it's worth the additional complexity.

2. If for some reason a session suspends but is unable to resume, that session's source database will be permanently orphaned. Again, this seems very unlikely, but if we wanted to guard against it we could so by using a lock file owned by the session launcher.

3. As there are no concurrency guards on the persistent directory, it is still possible for there to be write conflicts here in pathological conditions, but as writes only happen on session quit, the worst case is that the next new session launch doesn't have any open documents (significantly more benign than having a current session lose its documents!). Again, we could guard against this with a lockfile if we felt it necessary.

4. Now that source database folders are stable, we could probably dispense with the per-session persistent folders used in multisession mode with some small amount of additional effort.

title: Avoid nested restarts to prevent crashes during restart
description: Multiple subsequent restarts crash the IDE. While I spent some time trying to narrow this down, the code in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/master/src/cpp/r/session/RSession.cpp#L1598-L1654 does not seem safe to reentrancy to me. The fact that we are saving the session state and allowing another overlapping restart seems dangerous enough to be blocked. Thoughts? Can anyone think of a case where a user would actually be interested in restarting during a restart that currently works as expected?

title: fix escaping of shell characters
description:
This PR resolves an issue where elements were incorrectly escaped when passed to shell commands on POSIX systems.

One way to reproduce this -- in a Git project, attempt to stage a file with the name `$$$.R`. This fails because the filename is 'escaped' as `$1$1$1.R`, and an attempt to commit that file fails. The issue here is that we attempted to perform regex substitution without actually specifying a capture group in the regular expression used.

I think this is a candidate for v1.0-patch but let me know what you think.

title: allow customization of home, scratch directories
description:
This PR allows users to customize the default home directory, alongside the RStudio 'scratch' directory, using options passed to `rsession.conf`. This should be useful for RStudio Server users with limited space in their home directories, who instead want to tell RStudio to use + write configuration / state to a separate directory.

We likely want to tweak this PR a bit if we end up taking it, e.g.
1. We might want to allow 'templates' for the path; e.g. allow users to provide something like `/usr/local/rstudio/rstudio-$USER-$PID/`, and expand those shell variables (so one global config file can serve + separate for multiple users),
2. We might also want to allow users to set this with an environment variable.

Thoughts, @jjallaire @jmcphers?

title: report R launch errors
description:
This PR modifies some of the R startup error reporting such that non-zero exit statuses are now reported to the user. (Note that processes that run to completion, but return a non-zero exit status, return a `Success()` error object -- hence they are often not reported as one might expect).

The overall goal is to ensure that initialization errors are better reported to users.

title: Always use advisory locks for notebook path map on Windows
description:
This change resolves a problem that breaks the notebook path/ID cache on Windows. We use a lockfile-based mutex to ensure that two RStudio sessions do not both try to update the cache at the same time. The problem is that on Windows, link-based file locks aren't supported (even though they're the default):

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/5aebf29369ba3bc6c1e031fb4a1a569ad33db9a4/src/cpp/core/file_lock/LinkBasedFileLock.cpp#L246

...so we never acquire the lock and never update the cache. For the most part there's enough resiliency in the system that it works anyway, but without the mappings notebooks with identical filenames (but in different directories) can experience crosstalk.

@kevinushey Would you be willing to review this? I was tempted to just make the default lock type `LOCKTYPE_ADVISORY` on Windows everywhere, but that's obviously a larger change, and I suspect there's some reason this isn't already the case.

title: Default to advisory-based locks on Windows
description: `FileLock::createDefault()` currently returns an unusable lock on Windows since link-based locks are the default, but don't work on Windows filesystems. This change makes advisory locks the default on Windows.

title: refactor output handlers (readability / debugging)
Add notebook chunk output gallery
description:
This isn't ready for merge (pending UX tweaks and other fine-tuning), but it's close enough to its final form for code review.

This is primarily a UX change; there are only a couple of server-side changes involved. They are as follows.
1. **Add support for arbitrary chunk output metadata**. The metadata is used to store properties about the outputs such as their class and dimension for display in the gallery. The implementation is an untyped JSON object stored with each output, persisted in the cache as a `.metadata` file, stored in the `.nb.html` file, and hydrated with the rest of the cache data. 
2. **Implement support for hydrating `.rdf` files**. These were not previously stored in the `.nb.html` file. They are now stored there in base64 form, and deserialized back into the cache when it's hydrated from a `.nb.html` file. 

On the UX side, this is a refactor of the `ChunkOutputWidget`, which was formerly responsible for both receiving data and presenting it. There are now two strategies for presenting output (represented by the `ChunkOutputPresenter` interface): the `ChunkOutputStream` lays out content linearly (a straightforward port of the existing code), and the `ChunkOutputGallery` lays it out in gallery pages. The `ChunkOutputWidget` is responsible for selecting the appropriate presentation model, and routing data to the current presentation model. This makes it relatively easy to adjust the choice of presentation model if e.g. we decide later that we're switching to gallery view too aggressively. 

The new `ChunkOutputGallery` presenter contains a sequence of `ChunkOutputPage` objects, which are responsible for supplying their own thumbnails and content. Each type of content has its own output page class.

title: refactor output source implementations; preserve generated HTML
description:
This PR does two main things:
1. It refactors the `outputSource` implementation into a family of functions, each handling a different form of output;
2. It explicitly preserves HTML output, to help ensure that manually generated HTML that contains four spaces is not interpreted as a Markdown code block.

Note that four consecutive spaces within HTML output, even not at the start of the line, will be interpreted by pandoc as markdown code and so we need to be somewhat aggressive in protecting HTML here.

title: implement stan chunk execution for notebook
description:
This PR implements execution of `stan` code chunks (using `rstan`).

We handle execution in a similar way to `knitr:::eng_stan` (which effectively forwards arguments down to `rstan::stan_model`).

title: implement 'stan' chunk execution
description: This PR is a slightly trimmed down version of https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/708; in particular the client-side chunk parsing work is left out (to be more fully packaged in a separate PR). This PR should just have the guts of `stan` execution as-is from the previous PR.

title: implement client-side parser for Rmd chunk headers
description:
This PR implements a more comprehensive chunk header parser, effectively splitting options into key-value pairs. For example, we can parse e.g.

``````
```{r hello, echo = TRUE, fig.width=4, opts=list(a = 1)}
``````

would be parsed as

```
engine: "r"
label: "hello"
echo: TRUE
fig.width: 4
opts: list(a = 1)
```

Note that we don't attempt to parse the chunk 'values' as they can be arbitrary R code; we just split them into key-value components.

---

We should hold this for after the weekend + a bit of extra review since this is code that will be running quite often (basically, any time the document mutates and we need to re-detect whether a chunk is executable, etc.)

title: Move notebook execution to server
description:
This change moves notebook execution from the client to the server, and makes a variety of related improvements in the notebook code execution experience. 

Prior to the change, chunk queue management took place locally in `TextEditingTargetNotebook`. After it, queue management is much more distributed. Here's a rough overview:
1. There are three levels of queue objects: a document (`NotebookDocQueue`) is composed of chunks (`NotebookQueueUnit`), which are composed of ranges (`NotebookExecRange`). These objects are stateful, can be wholly represented as plain JavaScript objects, and have synchronized representations on both the client and server. When a notebook is executed, the client constructs the JavaScript objects representing the work and passes them to the server; the server is able at any time (for instance, on reload) to serialize the objects and return them to the client. 
2. On the client, the queue state and processing has been moved out of `TextEditingTargetNotebook` and into `NotebookQueueState`. The actual queue processing occurs on the server in `NotebookQueue`.
3. The `NotebookQueue` contains an object that exists as long as notebook chunks are running (and is shut down when they're not). This object maintains a thread which is used to submit console input on the user's behalf via a local HTTP request from the session to the session. 
4. Formerly, all a chunk's code was sent at once, and many systems used the console prompt as a signal that the chunk was finished executing. We now send the code line by line, with a prompt occurring after each line. This gives us finer-grained control, but requires a different connect/disconnect model; there's a new class `NotebookCapture` from which the capturing modules inherit, and they disconnect explicitly when instructed by their host. 

There's also some light refactoring of the alternate engine work here (cc @kevinushey); since it must now be driven by the server rather than an RPC I've moved it into its own translation unit. 

NOTE: Ready for initial review but not quite ready for merge (I'd like to have a little more test coverage first).

This PR displays a warning bar, rather than a prompt, when saving a Notebook file if the `rmarkdown` package is not present. (This change is made because if a user is editing a Notebook `.Rmd` file without internet access, the repeated on save prompts will be disruptive / annoying; the warning bar is less intrusive)

title: save html widgets as 'knitr' figures; display as 'viewer' in IDE
description:
This PR implements a simple `regex_filter` that allows us to save HTML widgets in their 'embedded' representation, while later showing them with their 'standalone' representation when loaded in the IDE. Just to set the stage, when an HTML widget is saved, it goes through `htmlwidgets:::toHTML(x, standalone)`, where the `standalone` parameter is used to state whether the widget should be shown standalone or not. When called through `knitr::knit_print` (as in `render`), standalone is set to `FALSE`. The main difference between these two representations is whether their sizing policy is also included in the HTML output: the 'embedded' representation might look like ``` html
``` while the 'standalone' representation might look like ``` html
``` Since we can recover the 'embedded' representation from the 'standalone' representation (but not the other way around), we save a modified version of the standalone representation, and use a server-side filter to recover the original standalone representation when displaying in the IDE. Note that this is not quite finished -- we need to ensure we aren't duplicating the `htmlwidget_container` IDs when generating a preview; likely this needs a separate filter. As an aside, in a perfect world, it seems like we would _always_ write the same representation for embedded vs. standalone widgets, e.g. ``` html
``` and use some global JS flag to denote which sizing policy should be applied (if any).

title: remove usage of '.rs.routines' object
description:
This PR removes the `.rs.routines` stuff I added a while ago, and instead just uses a `.rs.Call` method which delegates to `.Call` with the `PACKAGE =` argument set appropriately.

Was prompted to do this as I was bumping into more of the weird `.rs.routines` call errors when attempting to run `profvis` that seemed to be caused by a stale `.rs.routines` object.

title: implement base64 encoder/decoder
description:
I noticed that the Boost base64 encoder / decoder was actually surprisingly slow on larger strings (something that might come up more often with the notebook work) -- this PR implements a less featureful but much faster base64 encoder / decoder.

This is definitely something we shouldn't do / accept lightly, so feel free to close this if we'd rather not take the risk, but this implementation is ~10x faster on strings of ~1,000,000 bytes (and we could certainly expect some base64 encoded images of that size).

title: ignore '.', '_' when filtering completion results
description:
This PR augments the autocompletion system (client side) to ignore `_` and `.` when filtering matches.

This should enable something like the following:
1. The user wants to write `large.variable.name`,
2. The user writes `lar`, and requests completions (either manually or automatically),

title: ignore '.', '_' when filtering completion results
description: This is a much simpler version of the previous PR. I realized we can accomplish our goal simply by munging the query token; ie, we don't need all of the special logic attached to `isSubsequence` and friends.

title: Implement native notebook output and improve chunk execution model
description:
Prior to this change, notebook chunks, when run as a unit, were rendered by the rmarkdown package into a frame. When run line-by-line, they were rendered to a mini-console beneath the chunk. 

This change unifies (and simplifies) the execution model, and removes the rmarkdown package dependency. After the change, all code executed from a notebook chunk works the same way. 

Rough outline:
1. Prior to executing code from a chunk, a chunk execution context (`ChunkExecContext`) is established. This context is responsible for temporarily consuming output (console events, plots, and HTML widgets) while code from the chunk is executed. 
2. During chunk execution, output is streamed to the client as it's generated. It is simultaneously written to a series of ordered files in the notebook cache file. Each output operation either appends to an existing file or adds a new file.
3. When the chunk is finished rendering, the execution context cleans up its event handlers and output capture mechanisms.
4. To replay the chunk and re-create the output, the files are read back in order and sent to the client as a single unit.

The change is large, but looks slightly larger than it is since it includes some refactoring of what was formerly a somewhat monolithic session module handling all notebook-related RPCs and I/O.

title: Fixes for 'Rename in File'
description:
This PR fixes a couple of issues with the `Rename in File` action:
- occasionally failed when executed from a menu, as the underlying editor lost focus;
- failed when only one instance of the desired token was found (the 'refactoring mode' was exited over-aggressively),
- enabled refactoring of strings

Will double-check with @dfalty to confirm that this fixes the issues he discovered.

title: handle unnamed sections, sub-sections in R
description:
This PR implements a couple things:
1. It allows empty section headers, e.g. `#####` -- this was a regression from v0.98 and it looks like it's bugged quite a few users,
2. It enables folding for sub-sections (ie, sections within a function body).

I've confirmed that this works in R, Rmd, Rhtml and C++ modes, but let's leave this for a bit before merging.

title: re-write formula skipper
description:
This PR re-writes the formula skipper, fixing many issues that occurred when attempting to skip formulas when parsing an R expression.

The formula skipper is effectively a mini R parser, that parses to the end of a statement, and keeps track of whether a `~` operator was encountered within that statement.

title: only provide directories for package completions
description: Currently, the autocompletion system for packages (e.g. in `library()` calls) works by listing all _files_ within the library paths; this PR tidied up the logic a bit to exclude any files, or lock directories, that may have snuck in.

title: provide top-level file completions in unmonitored dir
description:
Previously, we relied on the file monitor always for providing file
completions when within a monitored project. However, certain files /
folders will be excluded from the file monitor; we still want to produce
(top-level, non-recursive) completions within that directory, so we make
sure that we take the union of what the file monitor gives us, alongside
a simple 'list.files()' listing.

Ultimately, this fixes a bug where file completions within the `packrat` directory of a packrat-managed project failed.

title: avoid firing active bindings in completion system
description: This PR ensures that we don't execute `foo$bar` in determining the type of an object, if the object is an active binding.

title: fix to data import column selection and parameter escaping
description:
Fixing 3 data import issues that we are hitting in the daily build:
- Missing to escape a couple characters (quotes and backslashes) for the comments parameter.
- Including "only" a column not working: The problem is that while refactoring code we stopped assigning a value to `dataImportOptions$columnsOnly`.
- Switching columns in XLS not working: Another refactoring issue caused by trying to clean code to use `any` + `hasAssignedType` without mapping into a vector first.

title: [emacs] C-f no longer opens find with Emacs mode
description: `C-f` is normally used to move the cursor forward; however, it was shadowed by our binding for the find-replace dialog. This PR ensures that `Ctrl+F` is only active when emacs mode is off.

title: [diagnostics] '{' can't form argument lists
description: This PR fixes a couple of issues when parsing after a function call.

title: prevent warnings from leaking when accessing refClass elements
description:
This fixes an issue where warnings are emitted when getting `$` completions on reference classes, e.g.

``` R
RC <- setRefClass("RC")
rc <- RC$new()
rc$<TAB>
```

Note that the issue is caused by attempting to evaluate e.g. `rc$.objectPackage` to get the object type; I believe this is a relatively recent change in R (hence why we hadn't seen it until now)

title: improve PopupPositioner horizontal overflow computation
description:
This PR improves the `PopupPositioner` horizontal overflow logic.

Previously, if we detected that the popup was going to overflow horizontally (to the right), we instead attempted to position the popup at the left corner of the rectangle (without checking the overflow in that case). This behaviour is bogus however and leads to left-overflow in cases with e.g. a data.frame having very long names, or overly long file paths.

This PR fixes that by instead just nudging the popup left to avoid overflow as much as possible, without overflowing left.

title: Remap Show All Panes on Windows
description:
@kevinushey discovered that [Windows takes _Ctrl+Shift+0_ for itself](http://www.eightforums.com/general-support/22552-cant-use-ctrl-shift-0-windows-has.html) on Windows 8 and newer. It is possible to disable this behavior so the binding is open for application use, but I don't think we can realistically expect users to figure this out.

This change remaps the command to _Ctrl+Alt+Shift+0_ on Windows (and leaves other platforms alone). This isn't terribly ergonomic but the other key combos we tried were somewhat nonsensical or already taken (eg. _Ctrl+Shift+-_ is unbound in RStudio but Chrome takes it for zooming).

title: fix for first file open after desktop launch
description:
This PR fixes an issue on OS X where the first attempt to open a file (by e.g. double-clicking it in the Finder, or on the Desktop) would not open that file in an already open RStudio instance.

If I understand correctly, the bug manifests in this way:
1. RStudio is launched (e.g. from Spotlight). The `openFile_` field in the `AppDelegate` is left `nil` and unset.
2. A user attempts to open e.g. an `.R` file, by double-clicking.
3. The `application` instance method is called, with that file -- however, because the `openFile_` field has not yet been set, we instead just set that field and do nothing (expecting that soon-to-come initialization logic would take care of it).

This PR fixes the issue by ensuring that the `openFile_` assignment can only happen on initialization (by using an `initialized_` member variable to track whether RStudio initialization finished successfully).

title: fix various warnings when compiling in Xcode
description:
This PR handles various warnings given by Xcode when compiling on El Capitan.

Not needed for this release, but I am marginally hopeful that we might get logged warnings on users who cut / copy / paste actions do not work. (On the other hand, those also may be manifestations of the bizarre focus issue we've heard some rumblings about...)

title: add (debug) command to show toke information
description:
NOTE: don't merge for this release.

---

This PR allows us to toggle token information on mouse over (similar to that in the Ace kitchen sink) for diagnosing tokenization errors (as needed).

title: [WIP] use directories for atomic file locking
description:
Probably not quite ready for merge, but ready for review.

---

This PR moves away from advisory-based locks (as used with `boost::filesystem::file_lock`) and instead implements a locking mechanism using directory creation + the so-called 'dead-mans switch'.

In this scheme, the lockfile unit is a directory, and the lock is considered active if:
1. It exists, and
2. The file is less than 30 seconds old.

We implement (as @jmcphers called it) the 'dead-mans switch', where a separate thread keeps track of, and 'marks', all active locks. Every 20 seconds, the thread updates the last modified time of the active locks, guaranteeing that any active locks remain 'alive' while they are locked.

title: turn off 'Ctrl + F -> Find' binding when in Emacs mode
description:
This PR disables the `Ctrl + F` binding used for 'Find' when Emacs keybindings are enabled.

We also remove some (what I believe are) unnecessary handlers attached to the Ace editor. If I understand correctly, the key event shouldn't actually even reach the Ace editor if we handle it at the top level with an RStudio command... but correct me if I'm wrong / missing something.

title: Only use libcurl when R SVN >= 69197
description:
This PR prevents the use of the libcurl method when we aren't running against recent (as of now only in dev versions) SVN revisions of R. This is to workaround the fact that in the original implementation of libcurl in R 3.2 HTTP 404 status results actually downloaded the 404 HTML page and treated the request as if it was successful.

This PR also adds two command line flags for the curl method:
- The "-L" flag (to tell it to follow redirects)
- The "-f" flag (to tell it to fail silently, R will take care of reporting failures)

@kevinushey Could you review and merge if this looks okay?

title: further refine pane zoom behaviour
description: @jjallaire, the implementation here feels fairly clunky but I can't think of a much better way of sharing this much state across the different elements in the IDE. Let me know if you can think of a cleaner way... This PR ensures that the currently selected layout state is zoomed when opening the layout dropdown, e.g. This is done in the following way: 1) The `PaneManager` maintains the currently zoomed 'tab' (or none, if no tab is zoomed), 2) An event is used to communicate the currently zoomed tab (requesters can fire that event, the pane manager will supply the currently zoomed tab), 3) When opening the popup menu, each item then asks the pane manager if it's the currently zoomed tab, and uses that to select its 'checked' status. Also -- let's not merge right away (I'll try to bring in other timing related fixes for zoom; you might have noticed that 'sometimes' zooming the 'help' Pane does not actually fully zoom it, for example)

title: fix cross-window passage of JS objects
description:
This PR fixes an issue where JavaScript objects containing arrays would not be properly serialized by GWT -- primarily due to the fact that those arrays inherited from the Array prototype belonging to a separate window.

The fix is to re-generate all objects and arrays, ensuring that the current window is used.

As an example, this fixes an issue where breakpoint arrays serialized from a satellite window would be serialized as objects -- e.g. instead of

``` js
{
    "0": { ... },
    "1": { ... },
    ...
}
```

we get (as expected)

``` js
[
    { ... },
    { ... },
    ...
]
```

@jjallaire, @jmcphers, can you please review this very carefully? This routine gets called whenever events need to cross window boundaries so it's very important that we get it right.

title: custom bindings should mask original AppCommand bindings
description:
This PR adds a mechanism for ensuring that AppCommands that have a custom binding are not executed from their original binding.

This ensures that, for example, when re-binding `Ctrl-P` away from 'jumpToMatching', it can instead fall back to 'move cursor up'.

This makes it easier to control how commenting works for 'double-sided' comments and also makes it a bit easier to handle what happens when considering commenting a line containing only whitespace.

2) Using the above, enables `<!-- -->` comments for Markdown modes.

As is tradition, a GIF showing this in action in an R Markdown document. Note that lines containing only whitespace within a selection are commented when within R mode, but not when within Markdown mode. (This seems like the most natural behaviour to me)

title: Improved autocompletions support for R
description:
This PR adds context and scope, specific completions for source documents.

![screen shot 2014-10-30 at 1 48 26 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/4851879/2da9b1ba-6076-11e4-8461-4dcba246a1cb.png)

A summation of the features in this branch:
- Function autocompletions automatically insert closing parens when appropriate -- for example, `rno|` would complete to `rnorm(|)`, while `debug(rno|)` would auto-complete to `debug(rnom|)`. (Certain function calls, ie, those potentially expecting functions as symbols, turn this behaviour off.)
- Auto-completions work for generic objects -- for example,

``` R
x <- ""
attr(x, "foo") <- function(alpha, beta) {}
attr(x, "foo")(|
```

provides auto-completion results for the parameters `alpha` and `beta`. This is particularly useful for e.g. `list`s and `environment`s containing functions, and also for e.g. `S4` accessor methods.
- Auto-completions understand arrays

For example,

``` R
m <- matrix(1:4, nrow = 2)
rownames(m) <- c("alpha", "beta")
m[al|
```

produces the completion `"alpha"` (which is automatically quoted after selection).
- Auto-completion understands 'chains' and dplyr

For example, in

``` R
mtcars %>% dplyr::select(|
```

auto-completion results are returned for 1) variables within `mtcars`, and also for function arguments in `select` (dropping the first argument).

As an added goodie, auto-completion also functions for the `join`s, so for example:

``` R
inner_join(foo, bar, by = c(|
```

provides completions for variables in `foo` when on the left side of an `=`, and `bar` when on the right side of an `=`.
- Auto-completion has a (basic) understanding of R6

E.g.

``` R
library(R6)
example(R6)
q$|
```

produces completions for the methods on the `q` (`Queue`) object generated in the example. More complex completions, e.g. when defining an R6 class, will be later handled with custom completion hooks.
- Context-specific variables are added to completions when appropriate

By scanning the source document (ie: not touching R), we provide completions for:
1. Any variables assigned in the current, or parent, scopes, and
2. All functions (and their arguments!) available in the top-level scope.

title: fix indentation following a ','; align =
description:
```
This commit fixes indentation following a ',', and also provides a
feature whereby multiple assignments following a ',' can be
automatically outdented and aligned.

For the first case, we now indent following a comma when appropriate,
e.g.

    int x = 1,

        ^

and in the second, we automatically align '=', e.g.

    int x = 1,
      y =
        ^~|

by adjusting the line's indent such that the '=' align.
```

title: Include function arguments in scope in auto-completion results
description:
This PR brings something that will make @jcheng5 very happy -- when attempting to retrieve autocompletion results in R modes, we look at all functions within the current scope, and also include function names and arguments within that scope in the completion list.

![screen shot 2014-10-29 at 10 18 14 am](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/4830705/aded3a50-5f8f-11e4-8bbd-8d0fe1b99b22.png)

There are still some TODO bits before merge, but I think this can be reviewed now.
1. I think there is some extra work needed to respecting an 'implicit' completion; e.g. when there is a single completion made from just functions in the scope, then the completion is automatically filled but we still get a pop-up.
2. This only works for declared functions (e.g. `x <- function(x, y) { ... }`; I could see people wanting the scope tree expanded to include e.g. `shiny`-specific things, which currently do not enter the scope tree). Maybe for another PR?

title: Add support for multi-line autocompletion in R scripts
description:
This allows us to get multiline autocompletion results with e.g. the context:

```
install.packages(
    |
```

I've implemented so that multiline autocompletion results can only be triggered with CTRL + SPACE (not with TAB) because it would be annoying for users who want to manually indent the current line in other contexts.

The basic way this PR works: instead of just passing the current line to the autocompletion generator, we look back and grab content until we have enough information to get an appropriate autocompletion. This is done by checking the balance of `(` and `)`; once we have more `(` than we do `)` we stop.

Multi-line strings, e.g.

```
"
This is some text with (
unbalanced parens
"
```

will probably confuse it, however.

description:
This change adds a dialog that shows a set of templates when New R Markdown ... is invoked.

The templates are expressed in a JSON data structure. Today the JSON data is hard-coded in `RmdTemplateData`, with the the goal of eventually getting this data from the server when we support user-created templates. The data is exposed via JSNI and used to create appropriate widgets for each template, format, and option.

To render the options to YAML, they're converted to a JavaScript object and passed to the server, which converts them to a structured data frame, hands them to R, and has the YAML package convert to text. The data is opaque to the server, so it's possible to change the options and their representations arbitrarily without server-side involvement.

title: Speed up Mac builds by avoiding double-compile of GWT
description:
### Intent

Our official Mac build (via `make-package`) builds the GWT subproject twice. GWT doesn't do incremental builds, so takes nearly as long the second time as the first.

On my Core i9 MBP, the GWT build alone takes 10 minutes, so given we have a single Mac builder, and an increasing number of branches competing for its services, shaving that amount of time (relatively) off the builds would be nice.

`make-package` for Mac currently does these steps:

1. `cmake generate` for Intel
2. `cmake build all` against that (includes GWT)
3. `cmake generate` and `build` for M1 (doesn't include GWT)
4. `cmake build install` back in the Intel directory (once again builds GWT)
5. bundling up of that produced install image into a DMG 

### Approach

If doing a package build, skip step #2 above. Generate the project tree for Intel but don't build it. Then step #4 will do the full build, including GWT.

I did package builds on my Intel Mac and my ARM Mac and everything appears to be fine. Always possible there's something slightly different on the official builder, but only one way to find that out.

### Automated Tests

No tests. Purely a build-time thing.

### QA Notes

Assuming the builds don't break, confirm the resulting Mac desktop builds "work" on both Intel and ARM. Routine usage, nothing special.

### Intent

Lay the groundwork for storing session information in a database. This has the potential to resolve a number of bugs and pain points around session management.

### Approach

I've encapsulated the on disk session metadata storage to limit the knowledge that calling classes have about how the session metadata is stored. An interface and factory have been created so that in the future switching to other storage options will be opaque to the callers.

description:
NOTE: this is targeting the Ghost Orchid patch.
