title: Support building Mac Electron Desktop via make-package
description:
### Intent

Step towards building the Electron-based desktop application on Mac and producing the DMG; this change enables building it entirely via `make-package` on Mac (Intel-only at the moment).

No changes made to Jenkinsfiles, and the intent of this change is to be a no-op for our current builds.

### Approach

#### Usage

To build a redistributable Electron desktop DMG on Mac:

```
cd rstudio/package/osx
./make-package clean --rstudio-target=Electron
```

A DMG will be produced: `src/node/desktop/out/make/RStudio-0.0.1-x64.dmg`.

#### How it works

First, build is configured with `-DRSTUDIO_TARGET=Electron` causing all the same things to be built as Qt desktop (rsession, GWT, various support things), MINUS the Qt desktop itself. The Electron app itself is not built during this phase.

After building, cmake is run again with the `install` target. This was already being done in the existing Mac build. In the Electron case, it lays out the structure for all the non-Electron bits needed in the app image.

Finally, `yarn make` is executed. This builds and packages the Electron app itself. A node script (`import-resources.ts`) is invoked by the electron-forge postPackage hook (see `forge.config.js`) and it copies the files from the cmake-generated install, into the Electron application. Then a DMG is produced (as part of the `yarn make` step).

A downside of this is an extra step (`yarn make`) is needed beyond running the cmake build. I will look at whether I can hook the `yarn make` step as a final step in the cmake `install` target so it is only necessary to run a single build step.

#### Next steps

- entitlements and notarization
- plumbing for versioning instead of current hardcoded 0.0.1
- support building native M1 version
- Linux and Windows (most of this work is reusable for those, but some additional script plumbing is required)
- (eventually) Jenkinsfile tweaks to actually build, run tests, and publish

### Automated Tests

Purely build-time.

### QA Notes

None.

title: Fix code execution via selection in indented visual chunks
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/9108.

### Approach

Code execution in the visual editor works by mapping the selection into the source editor and then executing the code there. For indented chunks, however, this mapping doesn't work correctly because the chunk in the visual editor's content is missing the leading spaces in the source editor. 

The fix is to examine the chunk's preamble (the line typically beginning with three backticks) to see if it's indented; if it is, we use the indent level to correct the mapping back to the source editor.

title: Implement collapse state for visual chunks
description:
### Intent

This change makes code chunks in visual mode collapsible/foldable. It adds a small arrow to visual mode chunks which can be used to fold them away:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/134059542-22d102d2-d293-4f96-b892-09045e77caac.png)

When folded away, a one-line summary of the chunk appears in its place, including its label (if any), length, and execution engine.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/134059614-9ccef9d7-699f-406a-abb9-d5e9dbbf453d.png)

There are also a couple of new visual editor commands, "Expand All Chunks" and "Collapse All Chunks", which do exactly what you'd expect.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/134060227-36704b4f-32f3-4847-9d4b-dfbd8b29050b.png)

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8613. 

### Approach

- Most work is in the editor host (GWT side) as that's where we decorate the editor and manage state.
- Nothing is removed from the DOM; the vertical content is just hidden by restricting its height. The editor is still present and will unfold when focused.
- The set of chunks that are collapsed are preserved in a document property, so will remain collapsed across sessions. Chunks are identified by position, which changes frequently as the document is edited, so to avoid RPC noise this information is both aggregated and debounced to 1s. 

### Automated Tests

N/A, visual editor isn't covered by automation yet. 

### QA Notes

- Test new commands
- Test that collapsed chunks remain collapsed after close/reopen
- Test UI visibility and usability in dark mode
- Test expansion/collapse of a chunk that is actively executing
- Test that find results inside a collapsed chunk cause it to expand (so you can see results)
- Test summary accuracy with various kinds (languages) of chunks

title: additional work on fold commands for visual mode
description:
@jmcphers This hooks up all of the standard editor commands for chunk folding to visual mode. It also allows the folded editor to accept focus (and shows the fold widget on focus).

There are three things we need for final polish:

1) We need to show the focus state in some suitably subtle fashion. You'll note that when arrowing down the cursor is at the beginning of the chunk (which to me seems like a good focus indicator) however if you arrow up or click in the middle the cursor isn't there (and may be invisible). I tried for a couple of hours to make it jump to the beginning in collapsed mode but there are too many overlapping sync operations (and flags/triggers) so I couldn't get this to work. I'd suggest that we hide the cursor entirely (esp. b/c it's read only) and do some sort of border treatment. At that point I think that clicking on it could expand it (and arrowing through it would not).

2) Sometimes unnamed R chunks show up as "R" and sometimes they show up as "unnamed-chunk-1" (I think the former is preferable for unnamed chunks)

3) We need to enable click to expand for the widget at right (or alternatively could have any click at all expand it). Note that the mouse cursor should also change state for this (currently its always the ibeam).

title: Fix wrapping for RStudio Workbench in About
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/2860.

### Approach

The reason this happens is that the CSS box that contains the product name has a fixed size; the position of the RStudio logo is also fixed. This makes it somewhat difficult to accommodate all the different product names and keep the name/logo centered. So I've make a somewhat larger change that uses Flexbox to lay these all out. Now the logo can move to help center the larger Workbench product name.

Server:

title: ensure we use a pre element when computing console width
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8696.

### Approach

We normally only apply our fonts to `<pre>` elements, as per https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/bugfix/font-size-computation-custom-fonts/src/cpp/session/resources/themes/css/fonts.css. However, when computing the Console width, we were doing so with a `<div>` element, which wouldn't have the custom font applied.

Because we were computing the width using a different font from the actual Console font, it's possible for text to overflow if the user has configured RStudio to use a font that is wider than the default font. This is most common on Windows, where the default font (Calibri) is somewhat more narrow.

### Automated Tests

N/A

title: properly handle UNC paths with git on Windows
description:
### Intent

### Approach

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/b80b77cf161c01e3a24cda3104f0d743fe3f689a/src/cpp/session/modules/SessionReticulate.R#L1859-L1863

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/b80b77cf161c01e3a24cda3104f0d743fe3f689a/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/environment/EnvironmentPresenter.java#L258-L271

whereas R uses separate "object added" and "object removed" events. If we see that an R-related update path is being used while Python is active in the Environment pane, then we can drop the change request.

title: support build vs. release configurations for desktop
description:
### Intent

Allow for the notion of different build types within our Typescript sources, in a simple (if somewhat hacky) way.

### Approach

`src/config` is now a symlink, which can be used to point either at `../config/development` or `../config/release`. The implementations within are just simple `enum`s, which indicate the "Current" build type, which can then be tested and used as appropriate.

The commands `yarn use-dev` and `yarn use-release` are shortcuts for updating that symlink.

I haven't verified this, but I believe this should suffice since these `enum`s and their tests will be constant expressions at build time, so any unused branches should be eliminated.

I took this approach for a couple of reasons:

`tsc` supports the notion of multiple projects; e.g. as in:

```
$ tsc --help | grep -- '--project'
 -p FILE OR DIRECTORY, --project FILE OR DIRECTORY  Compile the project given the path to its configuration file, or to a folder with a 'tsconfig.json'.
```

so, in theory, we could have separate `tsconfig.json` files ... but as far as I can see, there isn't a way to pass this configuration information down to `mocha` for unit testing. (I tried, but hit a number of landmines / road blocks in the process.)

We could also consider a separate CMake configuration step (and we might need this in the future), but I was worried this would complicate development work and I didn't want to bring CMake into the development pipeline unless absolutely necessary.

### Automated Tests

Included as part of the PR.

title: Make local jobs replayable
description:
### Intent

This change adds a Replay button to local background jobs, which can be used to restart the job without walking through all of the dialogs required to set it up the first time. It works on Shiny background jobs, too.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/119202933-b7db1f00-ba46-11eb-8ecb-d58449643a1a.png)

The layout of the job progress widget has also been improved. It uses Flexbox now, which prevents the elapsed timer from being cut off (something that happened a lot with the previous fixed-percentage table layout).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/119202794-6cc10c00-ba46-11eb-9027-2fb70215966b.png)

Addresses #5548.

### Approach

This mechanism uses the extensible "job actions" metaphor; script jobs now have a "replay" action which can be used to restart the job. This action replaces the previous run rather than creating a new one, so it's more like a restart than a new job with the same settings. 

### Automated Tests

Unit tests have been added to test the new Replay feature, and I have added unit tests for script jobs, which were not formerly covered.

### QA Notes

Not much risk to other code areas, but worth sanity checking adjacent background job features. It is worth noting that the jobs' definitions refer to input files by name, not contents, so if you replay a script job, it will re-run the file as it exists at that point in time (not as it existed during the previous run).

title: Bugfix/busy session async
description:
There are still some TODO comments here that I'm going to go over with Jonathan. Any feedback on how to make this better is much appreciated :) 

### Intent

Supports new configuration options to allow immediate or delayed async rpc and handling of selected operations offline - so they run even when the main thread is busy. 

### Approach

There are four new configuration options to rsession.conf:

    # settings to keep connectivity alive
    session-async-rpc-enabled=1
    session-async-rpc-timeout-ms=0

    # settings to process requests offline
    session-handle-offline-enabled=1
    session-handle-offline-timeout-ms=500

When either timeout-ms option is 0, the HttpConnection main request thread is used to convert all rpc requests to async or handle requests offline immediately. When it is non zero, the new OfflineService polling thread will do so if it wakes up and sees that the R session is currently executing, and the request was received longer than the specified timeout.

Periodically, offline service emits memory changed events in this same loop since those are only dispatched from the main thread.

An isMainThread check is added to key methods in r::exec so that the system logs and error and avoids stack corruption if an offline operation tries to use R. The app changes required include isWebsiteProject() - checking if R markdown is installed and findProgram(..) that calls R's Sys.which. There are TODOs in the code about how improving my solution to these problems.

The async-rpc requests are disabled from client_init until the first get_events request is made since the client only expects regular responses during setup.

Added a true/false user preference "Session protocol debug". When true, it logs debug messages to the file ~/.local/share/rstudio/log/rsession-(user).log for requests received and events sent from the rsession process. 

### Automated Tests

TBD: I would like to script up some tests that will kick off a system("sleep 60"), then verify that some operations can still proceed, and that we can queue up lots of console input messages, then interrupt the sleep.  It would be great to run these tests against a variety of configurations. We can also setup a mode to run all of the automated tests with various configuration options so that we can get more complete coverage of these new code paths.

Add a test in which R code updates the system PATH to include an executable checked by the rsession's findProgramOnPath.

### QA Notes

The defaults should not change any behavior right now as these options are disabled by default. 

Enabling and setting either or both of the timeout-ms values to 0 will ensure all requests are handled offline immediately if they are offlineable. If not, they are converted to async. With timeout-ms > 0, the request flow will only be altered if the R main thread is kept occupied for longer than the timeout-ms value. In other words, you will only see async rpcs used, or requests handled offline intermittently.

Also notice that when handle-offline is enabled, memory changed events should continue to be delivered even if R is busy.

There are two utilities in the code that have been changed to support "offline" requests: rmarkdownAvailable() and findProgramOnPath(). The rmarkdownAvailable() flag is now cached at startup. The findProgramOnPath() now uses the rsession's path env var which on Windows might drift out of sync if R makes changes to the PATH on the fly. 

For testing, there are three main types of code that can hang up R's main thread:

1) A call that blocks but still calls the "polledEventHandler" like this one:

> Sys.sleep(60)

This has always been interruptible, even before this fix

2) A call that blocks in a system call and does not call R's polledEventHandler.

> system("sleep 60")

This type is interruptible only with the busy session fix

3) A call that busy loops in C/C++ code - see Kevin's simple C++ code with a hang function in a comment on this issue:

   https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8865

This type is not interruptible even with the busy session fix, but you should reliably be able to abort the session. 

Another helpful thing to do during testing is to look at the Help -> Diagnostics -> Request log after running one of the busy loops above.  With the fix, there will typically be only one get_events request outstanding.  Each time you hit "enter" in the R console, rather than using up a new browser connection, you'll see an async reply after 200 ms. Later an event is delivered that contains the response.  Before the fix, each "enter" would hold onto another connection until the browser hits its limit of connections to the same server and stops sending more requests to the server (chrome allows 6, Firefox 8). At that point, nothing could be interrupted or aborted until the busy thread completed.

title: Bugfix/rstan duplicate save
description:
### Intent

Completion managers that extend the `CompletionManagerBase` class have duplicated handlers that fire twice for every one event they're registered for. This was noticed in #9106 specifically for `.stan` files when saving, but it's been occurring for all file types that use `CompletionManagerBase`, including:
- Markdown files
- Python files
- SQL files
- Stan files

### Approach

The handlers need to be registered after the completion manager objects are fully instantiated. Completion mangers now take a factory-ish approach using a "funstructor" `create()` method in place of the, now private, constructor to:
1. create the object
2. register the handlers
3. return the created object.

### Automated Tests

Probably not needed

### QA Notes

#9106 describes how to check the autosave handler for `.stan` files. Saves (and autosaves) should increment `count` by one. Clicking inside the editor of a `.stan` file for the first time should also trigger a single `OnFocus` event

title: place python on the PATH for new terminal sessions
description:
### Intent

Users can configure the version of Python to be used by RStudio and reticulate in a couple ways:

- By explicitly setting the `RETICULATE_PYTHON` environment variable;
- Via the UI, with global / project-specific options.

However, none of these configured versions of Python would propagate as the "default" to the terminal. This PR tries to make that happen.

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/9188.

### Approach

Making this work was a bit tricky, because ultimately we want to change the terminal process's `PATH` _after_ it has finished initializing (e.g. running profile startup scripts). The solution I landed on was to run `bash` as an interactive non-login shell, but then do all the things that a login shell would normally do -- that is, sourcing of `/etc/profile` and `~/.bash_profile`.

Note that the PR, in its current state, only works for the default Bash shell. Will need to confer with @gtritchie if this approach would be workable for other shells as well.

### Automated Tests

None yet.

### QA Notes

To test, try the following:

1. Using the RStudio Global Options dialog, tell RStudio to use a particular copy of Python.
2. Launch a new terminal in RStudio.
3. Run `which python`. Check that it matches the RStudio-configured version of Python.
4. Run `echo $RETICULATE_PYTHON`. Check that it matches the RStudio-configured version of Python.

We should also test that this behavior can be opted-out / disable via the associated option in Tools -> Global Options... -> Terminal.

@gtritchie also note:

> This feature must be tested on both Mac and Windows desktops, and with all available shell types (on Windows they’ll need to install a WSL flavor from Store so it’s available to test). Testing on Linux would be nice, too, but suspect Mac provides sufficient coverage

So this does require a bit of smoke-testing on all of the different flavors of bash we use on different operating systems.

title: Remove Typo.js from realtime spellchecking
description:
NOTE: This is just an early preview, it's not ready for final review yet. I just wanted to open the PR a little early so people could get eyes on it. I want to do another half day or so of extensive testing and finishing up some side features.

### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/9145

Typo.js just isn't up to the task for our enterprise uses. After looking at two spellchecking issues in the past two weeks for things that have come up due to our international requirements (Typo.js just cannot handle Korean, it chokes on larger dictionaries, etc) and expanding feature set (it's flaky interacting with Visual Mode) I decided to take some time and just rip it out entirely. The overhead that dealing with it has caused is just not worth it. Looking at the Typo.js repo it seems dead in the water and people have stale branches trying to fix some of these issues that the maintainer hasn't looked at. It hurts to delete some of my favorite code that I've written here (that prefetcher is 🔥 ) but I think we're all better off without Typo.js.

### Approach

All realtime requests are now just routed through the backend Hunspell checker. The one thing that I'm not entirely sold on the approach of so far is caching the responses on the client in a Hash to avoid subsequent server requests. This may need some periodic garbage collection if someone is working on a large document for hours at a time. Some sort of FIFO cleaning might be worth looking into.

Due to this change many calls look more complex due to them being routed through the server but I've tried to minimize that impact as much as possible. Overall performance of the spellchecking feels snappier already.

### Automated Tests

We do not currently have the infrastructure to automate testing the realtime spellchecking.

### QA Notes

Verify that realtime spellchecking works normally. There should be no recognizable changes.

title: build both x86_64 and arm64 rsession components on macOS
description:
### Intent

This PR seeks to make it possible to use a single copy of RStudio with both x86_64 and arm64 builds of R on macOS.

### Approach

Roughly:

1. Produce a full build of RStudio for x86_64,
2. Produce an `rsession` build for arm64,
3. Copy that `rsession` (and its library dependencies) into the built tree for x86_64,
4. Build RStudio as a package with both binaries,
5. When RStudio is launched, choose the appropriate `rsession` based on the architecture of the underlying R library.

Note: I chose this approach over the "universal binary" approach as it's much easier to adapt our build scripts in this case. In particular, we depend on Homebrew for some libraries and Homebrew does not provide universal binaries or libraries in any case.

This also only effects package builds; developer builds will remain single-architecture. (This is mainly because I found getting CMake to build the same sub-directory in the same project with different compilers / compiler flags is rather challenging.)

The implementation here is also designed such that regular package builds on x86_64 should produce the exact same builds as we had before; any arm64 components should only be activated if we detect that the running machine is itself running on arm64.

### Automated Tests

None required.

### QA Notes

None required specifically for this PR, but smoke-testing on M1 macOS machines will be warranted.

title: Add rstudioapi support for command callbacks
description:
### Intent

This change makes it possible for RStudio add-ins and other API consumers to run arbitrary R code when an RStudio command is executed, supporting a variety of extensibility scenarios. Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/1846. 

### Approach

This change implements only the RStudio side of the work; it adds command callbacks that function very similarly to the chunk callbacks already implemented in the API. There are two types of command callbacks supported:

1. A callback for a specific command, which will be executed when that specific command is invoked via any means (keyboard shortcut, menu, palette, etc.).
2. A callback for all commands (a "command stream" callback), which will be invoked when *any* command is executed. This callback will be given the ID of the command that was executed. 

A little extra work is done here to synchronize the list of commands that have active callbacks with the client and the server. This allows the client to notify the server of a command execution only when strictly necessary; otherwise, we would have to fire an RPC with every command execution.

### Automated Tests

Unit tests covering registration, deregistration, and invocation of both types of callbacks discussed above are included.

### QA Notes

This will ultimately have rstudioapi wrappers, but can be tested today using the following raw API methods (rstudioapi wrappers will arrive in a separate PR to the rstudoapi package).

```r
# Register a callback for a specific command
handle <- .rs.api.registerCommandCallback("commandId", function() { ... })

# Register a callback for all commands
handle <- .rs.api.registerCommandCallback("*", function(commandId) { ... })

# Unregister callback
.rs.api.unregisterCommandCallback(handle)
```

title: avoid rearranging console input when fixing newlines
description:
### Intent

Unfortunately, 1.4 has a pretty ugly regression -- lines can be submitted out-of-order in some cases, if the user quickly submits multiple pieces of console input while the R console is busy. See https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8837 for details.

This PR seeks to rectify that.

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8837.

### Approach

When fixing up console input, we now:

1. Take the next console item at the front of the deque,
2. Create a vector of pending console items,
3. Replay those onto the front of the deque

thereby preserving the order of input in the console input queue even after splitting.

### Automated Tests

Tracked in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-ide-automation/issues/159.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8837. A simple way to test is with this script -- try executing the following line-by-line quickly, by pressing Ctrl + Enter a number of times:

```
#1.
Sys.sleep(1)

#2.
Sys.sleep(2)

#3.
Sys.sleep(3)
```

After execution, you should see:

```
> #1.
> Sys.sleep(1)
> #2.
> Sys.sleep(2)
> #3.
> Sys.sleep(3)
```

in the console history. If you're running a version of 1.4 with this bug, you will see:

```
> #1.
> Sys.sleep(1)
> #3.
Sys.sleep(3)
> #2.
> Sys.sleep(2)
```

instead.

title: Show memory usage details in Environment Pane
description:
### Intent

This change adds a small feature that makes it possible to see your current memory consumption in the Environment Pane. This is a feature frequently requested by users that run R in memory constrained environments, especially with RStudio Server. 

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/4033.

### Approach

RStudio's Environment Pane now includes the following memory usage widget:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/106518278-7d954400-648e-11eb-85f1-28959a6937c0.png)

This small bit of UI is placed here so that the buttons follow the workflow "import data into memory", "data currently in memory", "remove data from memory". It conveys two important values:

- The total amount of used/available memory (pie chart)
- The total memory used by the R session (MiB value)

The pie chart also has color coding for usage thresholds; it turns yellow and orange when usage approaches the limit, and bright red when very little memory is remaining. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/106518562-eda3ca00-648e-11eb-82ae-deaa316c9dfa.png)

Hovering over the values provides a little more detail. There's also a new Memory Usage Report which breaks down the amount of memory currently used by R (obtained from a `gc()` call), the IDE, and the system itself.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/106518704-2479e000-648f-11eb-9438-eda3b15f0f18.png)


While this feature is primarily of interest to RStudio Server users, it works on all platforms. This is done by using platform-specific implementations of a few functions that measure memory statistics. Backends have been implemented for Windows, macOS, and Linux (both `/proc/meminfo` and `cgroups` are supported).

It could be a little annoying to have a number in the Environment Pane that changes constantly as you work, so it's possible to turn this feature off if you don't like it. (We might consider turning it off by default on RStudio Desktop where memory is rarely top of mind.) This is done via a preference you can toggle from the menu.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/106518875-57bc6f00-648f-11eb-9cfc-2756fb8a846e.png)

Finally, memory usage is updated frequently: any time you enter an R command, and in the background while the session runs, every 10 seconds by default. This allows the memory usage indicator to show changes in usage that result from allocations in background jobs and other system processes. There is a new advanced option (accessible only via the Palette) which can be used to adjust the interval at which statistics are refreshed.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/106518766-39567380-648f-11eb-8015-403c892320b2.png)

This can be set to 0 to disable periodic refresh entirely.

### Automated Tests

This change includes unit tests that test both basic resource usage metrics and the memory report RPC.

### QA Notes

Lots of cross-platform testing is needed here since measuring memory usage is very OS-specific. On Linux in particular, the primary motivator for this change is for Kubernetes/Slurm environments, where memory usage is often constrained with cgroups.

This change is almost entirely additive; it doesn't touch much existing code, so risk to other areas is minimal. Probably the most relevant change is that the server is now trickling memory usage updates every 10 seconds to the client; formerly the client would often go a long time (minutes or longer) without updates from the server. Make sure things like session suspend and idle timeouts are still working with the increased traffic.

description:
### Intent

### Approach

Technically we could have just added this to our growing hard-coded whitelist, but this change adds a little more flexibility. The list of files we always show and extensions we always show is now configurable (only via config files). This makes it possible for users or administrators to force specific files to show up in the Files pane. 

It is also now possible via configuration to make the Files pane just show all hidden files or none of them by using empty option values. In this way, it addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/3221.

Of course we could have gone even further and added additional prefs/UI to make such configuration possible by ordinary users, but wanted to keep this scoped for Juliet Rose.

### Automated Tests

### QA Notes

{
  "always_shown_extensions": [],
  "always_shown_files": []
}

title: fix issue with debugger hang when using do.call()
description:
### Intent

Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/5158.

Normally, deparsing a call is cheap, as the only things embedded in a call object are symbols, calls, and literals. However, some calls (notably, those generated when a function is invoked via `do.call()`), will be very expensive to deparse, as deparsing those implies also deparsing the objects embedded in those calls.

Similarly, the "expression" associated with the promise of such a call might not actually be an expression, as `do.call()` can force early evaluation of its arguments -- and so R generated a promise mapping to an already-evaluated expression; that is, the expression is just the requested value itself.

### Approach

Detect and handle both of these cases when opening the debugger.

### Automated Tests

Unit tests included.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/5158. Fix has some risk as it touches the code used for formatting things for display in the debugger + environment pane.

title: Always report startup configuration related errors to stderr, even if not connected to a terminal
description:
### Intent

When installing on CentOS, configuration related error messages do not display during the installation. This is because stderr (where we log this information) is not connected to a terminal, so it is only logged to syslog. However, if we force write these to stderr, they will properly show up.

### Approach

For these startup related errors, forcefully log them to both stderr and syslog even if stderr is not connected to a terminal. This ensures that the output can be seen by a user when starting the process via the installation.

For other code paths that report errors after startup (or daemonization), do not forcefully log to stderr - we want to make sure we aren't writing to a buffer that is never going to be read from (which could cause a hang).

(Also includes some code that should have been merged back to OS but was forgotten - the ostream and operator changes in ProgramOptions).

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/2214

### QA Notes

See https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/2214

title: Improve sorting in the Command Palette
description:
### Intent

This change addresses some shortcomings in the way commands are sorted in the Palette. In particular, they currently aren't sorted at _all_, under the presumption that you'll search for what you want. However, this isn't very efficient and doesn't provide new users with a very good experience. This PR makes two improvements:

#### Add an MRU

The command palette now has an MRU; commands executed from the palette will appear in a new section at the top of the palette. This gives recently executed commands priority in searches, reducing the number of characters needed to match them. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/102666292-664b0300-413b-11eb-8e13-3abefc9420b2.png)

The MRU can be toggled on/off and (like the file and project MRUs) cleared, but these are considered power user features and both are available only via the palette itself. 

#### Front-load useful commands

The commands that appear "above the fold" when the palette is first open is now a hand-selected group of ~16 commands that are useful in day to day work.

Fixes #7567
Fixes #7956

### Approach

The MRU uses the same mechanism we use for every other MRU in the product: a file on disk containing a newline-delimited set of strings. Each palette entry has a "scope" which represents its source (e.g. a command, an add-in) and an ID; when a command is executed, these are stored in the MRU. When we're building the palette, we use the MRU entries to request the recent commands and put them into the palette (fetching each from the correct provider) before building the rest of the palette.

The MRU doesn't follow any fancy "frecency" algorithms; it is just a top-10 list of recently executed commands, and executing any command moves it to the top. 

Only executing a command _from the Palette_ adds it to the MRU; that is, the MRU won't give you a list of your top executed commands from other sources, such as menus or keyboard shortcuts. There are arguments to be made either way for this one, but looking at other palettes suggests that this behavior is the most expected.

Currently, only built-in commands and add-ins participate in the MRU, even though the palette contains other kinds of entries, such as Visual Editor commands and user preferences. I did this because the Visual Editor is very contextual and it seems possible, even easy, to fill the MRU with Visual Editor commands and then wind up with no MRU at all when you don't have a visual editor open. If this turns out to be a problem we could give the Visual Editor its own MRU, etc., but that felt like gold plating.

### QA Notes

Most of this code is isolated to the Command Palette. To compare behavior before/after this change, use the _Remember recently used items in Command Palette_ setting (defaults to on); to clear the MRU to start with a clean slate, run the _Clear recently executed command list_ command.

title: Sanitize the CSL that we receive from Pubmed
description:
fixes @rstudio#8625

-> we were previously not santizing the CSL
-> pubmed is sending a license field which pandoc is choking on (and doesn’t appear to be expected in well formed csl json, see https://github.com/citation-style-language/schema)
-> If present, we now sanitize that field out before we send the CSL to the bibliography


### Intent
Pubmed is including a 'license' field which doesn't appear to be an expected part of CSL Json. When we use Pandoc to read this CSL Json, it fails because of the presence of this field.

### Approach
We already sanitize the CSL that we receive from some providers (who don't always return well formed CSL). Add stripping of the license field to this sanitization and use the sanitizer when we receive CSL from Pubmed.

### QA Notes
Bug was a great catch. Because we generate CSL-JSON/CSL-YAML using Pandoc and generate Bibtex ourselves (or using better bibtex if that option is enabled), testing the variety of bibliography formats was a great idea. Good practice to continue including verifying that things work correctly with better bibtex.

title: also use tinytex when compiling .Rnw-generated .tex files
description: ### Intent We added the ability to use [tinytex](https://yihui.org/tinytex/) a while back, when compiling standalone `.tex` files. This PR extends that to also work with the `.tex` files rendered from a Sweave (`.Rnw`) document. ### Approach Relatively straight-forward application + use of the existing `runTinytex()` function; now used to render the `.tex` file generated after weave. ### QA Notes Ensure that the `tinytex` R package is installed and in use: ``` options(timeout = 3600) library(tinytex) tinytex::install_tinytex() ``` Ensure that you've configured RStudio to use tinytex when rendering `.tex` files: Then try creating a `.Rnw` document, and then rendering it. For example: ````` \documentclass{article} \begin{document} <<>>= print(1 + 1) @ \end{document} ````` Confirm that the rendered PDF is opened after successful compilation, and that the Compile PDF tab (next to the console) reports that tinytex was used: Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2788.

title: rebuild compilation database when compiler changes
description:
### Intent

For projects using C++ source files, RStudio maintains some internal state describing how files in that project should be compiled. This data was not being invalidated when the compiler was changed, leading to cases where a new compiler was being used with old compiler flags, which were not always compatible and lead to issues.

### Approach

Include the compiler's `--version` output as part of the compilation database, and invalidate the database if that changes. (The compiler is queried from R via `R CMD config {CC/CXX}`. This check is not perfect, but should be "good enough" for 99% of users.)

### QA Notes

This is a bit challenging to test. You will have to:

1. Create a project using C++ sources,
2. Edit some C++ files within the project, and confirm that C++ diagnostics are working as expected,
3. Change the default compilers used by R (this can be done via `~/.R/Makevars`),
4. Restart RStudio, and try editing files in the project again. Confirm that the correct diagnostics are emitted.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8588.

title: convert condition messages to UTF-8 when handling in notebook
description: ### Intent Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8546. ### Approach Ensure that condition messages, as captured when notebook mode is active, are converted to UTF-8. Also refactor some of the global condition handling code. Rather than build a string to be executed at the top level, we instead use a regular R function to define the associated call, and then extract the body of that function and execute that at the top level. IMHO, this makes the implementation much easier to maintain and tweak. Also add some helper functions, `nativeToUtf8()` + `utf8ToNative()`, to be used in the future when explicit conversion is required. ### QA Notes This should be tested on Windows, in an R Markdown document. First, instruct RStudio to translate messages to Korean with: ``` Sys.setlocale(locale = "Korean") Sys.setenv(LANGUAGE = "ko") ``` Then, try loading a package and confirm that the output is properly encoded and displayed as Korean: Note that it is expected here that part of the message is not translated here, as no translation is defined for this part of the message output. You can also test explicitly with message / warning output: ``` msg <- gettextf("Attaching package: %s", "dplyr") message(msg) warning(msg) ```

title: Respect "tab key always moves focus" pref in visual editor
description:
### Intent

Respect the accessibility setting "Tab Key Always Moves Focus" in visual mode chunks. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8584.

### Approach

This wasn't working because the code that tracks this pref is in the `AceEditorWidget` class. The Ace instance used in the visual editor is not wrapped in an `AceEditorWidget` and so it does not track the pref.

The fix is pretty simple: we just track the pref ourselves in the visual mode chunk. 

### QA Notes

This should track the preference not only at startup but also as the preference is changed in real time (e.g., try changing the setting in Global Options and confirm that the open editors are affected).

title: Add preference governing pipe operator style
description:
### Intent

Adds a new user preference which can be used to make the *Insert Pipe Operator* command insert an R 4.1 native pipe, `|>`, rather than a magrittr style pipe, `%>%`. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/101965273-e831ae00-3bc8-11eb-8972-143ec15885f0.png)

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8534.

### Approach

Add the pref and consult it before inserting a pipe. 

As usual, dialog space is an issue; there was no room for this in its natural location (under Editing), so the "Save when sourcing" pref was moved to the Saving tab (arguably a more natural home) to make room. 

At some point, we may want to add this pref to the computed layer, such that instead of always defaulting to magrittr style pipes, we automatically default to `|>` when R supports it. However, since compatibility with the tidyverse (and exact R version support) are still murky, this preference is currently only for early adopters and defaults to off. 

### QA Notes

Test via notes in #8534.

title: Implement previous/following chunk execution commands outside chunks
description:
### Intent

Makes the "Execute Previous Chunks" and "Execute Subsequent Chunks" commands work correctly in visual mode when the cursor is outside a code chunk. 

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8500
Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8275

### Approach

This fix is not trivial since a good deal of plumbing is required. In particular, these (and most other) code execution commands currently presume you're already in a code editor. So here's what we do now:

1. The code that synchronizes the current code editor position has been plumbed so that it now returns the position it found, or `null` when the position isn't inside a code editor.
2. If the Execute Next or Execute Previous commands are run when the position isn't inside a code editor, we find the nearest code editor (in the requested direction), and use it as a virtual position for executing the command. 

### QA Notes

This one is worth testing lots of edge cases on: top/bottom of document, when there are no chunks at all, when all the chunks are below/above the cursor, when the cursor is actually inside a chunk, when the cursor is just before/after one, etc.

title: adapt test script to changes in #8614
description:
### Intent

Ensure that `rsession` tests can still run even with the changes in #8614.

### Approach

Make sure `R_HOME`, `R_DOC_DIR` and `R_LIB_DIR` are always defined. In addition, force `rsession` to use a version of `libR.dylib`, since we explicitly don't link directly to the R library (so users can choose different versions of R at runtime).

### QA Notes

No QA; this is just to get tests up and running again.

title: try reloading main window if R not yet ready
description: ### Intent Fix an issue where the Desktop client would be ready and attempting to connect to R before R itself was ready to receive connections. ### Approach Similar to the last approach, retry attempts to connect to the R session a couple times. This PR also makes it easier to test this case, by allowing one to instruct the R session to sleep on startup for a brief period of time (effectively simulating a "slow" session startup). ### QA Notes On macOS, test with the following: ``` export RSTUDIO_SESSION_SLEEP_ON_STARTUP=5 /Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/RStudio ``` You should see a temporary "initializing R" window first: The session should later load successfully after a brief pause. You can also test the extreme case, with: ``` export RSTUDIO_SESSION_SLEEP_ON_STARTUP=60 /Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/RStudio ``` In this case, you should eventually see the "cannot connect to R" error page, but if you wait 60 seconds you should be able to retry and successfully connect. Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8270.

title: forward C++ completion context to embedded editor
description:
### Intent

Fix https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8618, in which C/C++ code blocks don't work in the visual editor.

### Approach

This happens because the completion context for C/C++ isn't initialized inside the code chunks in the visual editor. The fix is to forward the parent editor's completion context, which gives the completion manager access to information such as the path to the file being edited that isn't available in embedded editors. 

### QA Notes

Test via notes in #8618.

title: Fix various virtualscroller autoscrolling bugs
description:
### Intent

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8544
Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8504
Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8529
Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8552

Wanted to get #8568 also in here but there's some weirdness related to GWT going on 😢 

### Approach

The weird Tibble related bugs were due to how I was counting the number of items in a bucket. A super wide Tibble is a ton of unique `span` elements that can all be on a single line. This caused the calculation of how large a bucket is to be wildly inaccurate so it didn't know if it was scrolled all the way up or down. The `isBucketFull` function in `virtualscroller.js` solves this by just counting newlines in the `innerText` which seems to work pretty well for now, though I did notice a performance hit which might need some attention.

The console always scrolling to the bottom is a...more complex issue. It happens in a lot of places based on a whole bunch of different events and there are a few different `scrollToBottom` insertion points that are hard to grab in a catch all. The `BottomScrollPane` makes a lot of assumptions based on events that happen entirely within GWT and the state doesn't seem to update cleanly between pure JS and the GWT event loop. I refactored out some of the built in autoscrolling and conditionally moved that to virtualscroller.js but there is still more work to be done. This [comment](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8568#issuecomment-745748922) in #8568 shows some of the complexity inherent in having the content and scrolling managed in multiple places.

### QA Notes

The most important thing in testing this will be to ensure that nothing with the Limit Console Output feature turned off is broken. Always good to be a little extra cautious when changing rerouting old code.

title: fix macOS server dev builds
description:
### Intent

Fix RStudio Server development builds on macOS.

### Approach

Pass along `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` when launching the `rsession` process in development server builds, as we do on desktop.

### QA Notes

No QA testing required; developer only.

title: Fix Inconsistent Emoji Spacing
description:
### Intent

Visual mode renders text (including emoji) using a proportional font. This allows emoji to render at varying width, which can cause issues for certain emoji (e.g. the keycap emoji):

![Screen Shot 2020-11-20 at 8 28 25 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/261654/99811249-e5d0bc80-2b12-11eb-9627-677183193f9d.png)

This fix switches rendering to use of a fixed width font which should make the spacing consistent:

![Screen Shot 2020-11-20 at 8 28 44 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/261654/99811235-e0737200-2b12-11eb-9293-478f7cf448a7.png)


### Approach

The visual editor uses a fixed width font to render the emoji. In addition, I've updated other UI that displays emoji (completion, insert emoji dialog) to also use the fixed width font. Review the emoji rendering and exclude any emoji that don't render well using the new fixed width font (just a few).

### QA Notes

This fix should address rendering of emoji in visual mode as well as the supporting UI. It also switches the rendering of symbols in the insert symbol dialog to use a fixed width font (since the grid is shared between symbols and emoji). This shouldn't cause any issues, but if you notice anything strange with insert symbol, this could be related.

Makes it easier to bootstrap macOS dev machines by defaulting to installation of pre-built Crashpad binaries.

### Approach

On MacOS, modify the common bootstrap script so that it uses pre-built binaries by default.

### QA Notes

title: don't use virtual console for inline chunk output
description:
### Intent

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8465.

### Approach

Disable virtualized console for outputs generated from inline code chunks. Also add a safety fix in virtualscroller.js to ensure we do have a scroller element to inspect when adding output.

title: End previous mathjax renders before starting a new one
description:
### Intent

Fix #7947 

### Approach

Make sure that `MathJax.endRender` is called before `MathJax.renderLatex` executes. The issue was pretty easy to track down once I had a good repro, thanks Karl!

### QA Notes

Make sure that #7947 doesn't occur anymore using the repro that Karl posted at the bottom of the ticket.

title: Remove unintended chunk delimiters from visual chunk code
description:
### Intent

This change addresses an issue in which accidentally pasting a whole chunk (delimiters and all) into an existing visual mode chunk can corrupt the document.

Closes #8452.

### Approach

Ideally we'd have more fault tolerance in the parser (so the document could not become corrupt), but that would involve a much more ambitious change than is possible at this point in the release. So, instead, we treat the symptoms: when we're generating Markdown, we skip over chunk delimiters inside chunks to avoid the problematic nesting.

### QA Notes

Note that this change *only* addresses the easiest way to get yourself into this situation (pasting chunk delimiters into a visual mode chunk). It does not address the underlying issue, and you will still see trouble if you start off with a document that *already* contains mismatched/nested chunks (such as the one in the bug) and attempt to put it into visual mode.

title: use more robust test for writable library
description:
### Intent

In some cases, RStudio might mis-detect a non-writable R library as writable. This PR intends to be a bit more robust to those cases.

### Approach

Rather than trust the POSIX permissions, check that we can explicitly create and remove a dummy file within the library directory. (This is necessary since, in some cases, POSIX permissions might report that a directory is writable even if the user doesn't actually have write access to that directory.)

### QA Notes

Unfortunately, not sure how to reproduce, but this was reported as occurring with an installation of R living on a NFS.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/2184.

title: Fix installation from Windows path containing multibyte chars not from system codepage
description:
### Intent

- Fixes #8421
- Targeting Juliet-Rose since this issue has been around forever

### Approach

- Turn on NSIS Unicode support

### QA Notes

- Try installing on Windows with the setup package in a folder containing characters not in the current system language (e.g. a folder named 鬼 on an English system)
- Can do this by creating a user with that username, but also simply by creating a folder with that name and moving the setup .exe into it before running

title: revert to creating strings in native encoding by default
description:
### Intent

This was discovered as part of fixing https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8435, and reverts part of an older PR: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/7263

In particular, as part of that PR, we made a change so that strings were ~converted~ marked as UTF-8 by default here:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/d1289249b11e0d12d2be12b3ceb701c41f110cec#diff-1c101207d4078bdd9f5c46490672cf8b04cbbad2db4b10671ab88906af5aee26R1041

In hindsight, this isn't a great choice because it breaks our own usages of the form:

```
RFunction(".rs.foo")
    .addParam(string_utils::utf8ToSystem("string")))
```

because we effectively end up with a string in the native encoding, but we mark it as though it were UTF-8.

### Approach

Until we can take the time to audit usages of `RFunction` + `systemToUtf8()` (and other usages of `r::sexp::create(<string>)`), we should revert the default behavior to treating strings as though they are in the native encoding, since we do that intentionally in a number of places.

In the meantime, we can (as we did in my prior PR) explicitly use `addUtf8Param()` when we want to pass in UTF-8 strings, and `callUtf8()` when we want to ensure the returned string is UTF-8 encoded.

### QA Notes

Nothing specific to test; any issues would hopefully be caught in a normal certification pass on Windows.

title: use UTF-8 strings in a few more places
description:
### Intent

While testing on a Windows account with a user with non-English letters, I noticed a couple more issues with handling of filenames:

```
Error in file.exists(index) : 
  file name conversion problem -- name too long?
Error in file.exists(index) : 
  file name conversion problem -- name too long?
Error in file.exists(index) : 
  file name conversion problem -- name too long?
Warning message:
In list.files(cacheDir) :
  unable to translate 'C:/Users/Cr<e8>me Br<fb>l<e9>e/Desktop/renv/.Rproj.user/24A05536/explorer-cache' to native encoding
```

From what I understand, this is caused by (failed?) attempts to convert UTF-8 strings to the native encoding, as opposed to just using the UTF-8 strings as-is.

### Approach

Augment our `RFunction` class with a new `addUtf8Param()` function, which is used to add strings (or string-like things) which should be UTF-8 encoded.

### QA Notes

Testing this is somewhat broad: it would be worth checking that RStudio functions without issue on Windows, for a user whose user name has accented characters. (I tested with an account name Crème Brûlée.

Closes #8435.

title: set load hook for 'matplotlib.pylab'
description:
### Intent

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8414.

### Approach

Ensure our `show()` hook is injected for both of `matplotlib.pyplot` and `matplotlib.pylab`.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8414.

title: fix closeAllSourceBuffersWithoutSaving to silently close modified unsaved buffers
description:
### Intent

- Fixes #8425
- Original fix didn't handle unsaved but modified buffers properly and would still prompt

### Approach

- use lower-level internal API that handles this case properly 

### QA Notes

- a fix to the original PR here: #8432

title: Disable virtualized console for chunk output in markdown files
description:
### Intent

Fix chunk output throwing errors in markdown files with virtualized console turned on.

Fixes #8418 
Fixes #8416 

### Approach

Just had to disable Virtualization in the ChunkOutput.

### QA Notes

title: fix precedence in null check
description:
### Intent

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8198.

### Approach

Use parentheses to properly guard against `null` position when accessing its values. (🤦 )

### QA Notes

Test via @R-Hannibal's notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8198.

title: fix regression in completion of methods attached to list objects
description: ### Intent Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8423. ### Approach A recent PR regressed this: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/7fd3ff2ba1b579952baceaddd6fcb2ca4c88d186#diff-f198a504f201904479c929e2e53ea3c82c2e83f60bad4dc7e518249fefc41938R598-R600 The `.rs.getAnywhere()` function actually does evaluate "safe" R statements; e.g. those of the form `foo$bar`, which is necessary when retrieving completions for e.g. R6 methods since we typically have calls of the form `object$method(...)`. ### QA Notes With `|` indicating the cursor position, test that autocompletion results are shown as expected here: ``` test <- function(x, y, z) {} callbacks <- list(f = test) callbacks$f(|) ```

title: scroll cursor into view only after render
description:
### Intent

When the Ace cursor is moved, we need to wait for Ace to render the updated cursor before it can be scrolled into view.

### Approach

Scroll the cursor into view after render, rather than after execution of a command.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8300.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8300.

title: sync editing outline location before R Markdown render
description:
### Intent

When we render R Markdown docs, we pass the location of the cursor, which is later used to infer a slide to navigate to when previewing presentations. However, the location of the cursor in source mode is used, so it doesn't reflect the user's cursor position if they're in visual mode, resulting in incorrect slide navigation. This change addresses that issue.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8301. 

### Approach

This is a relatively scoped fix meant to address this specific issue. Prior to rendering R Markdown docs, we now move the cursor in source mode to an approximation of where it is in visual mode (same outline item, which is all we need for slide selection). 

### QA Notes

This change affects only R Markdown presentations (not R Presentations).

title: avoid stomping on rainbow parens state with raw strings
description:
### Intent

In our tokenizer, we keep track of both the rainbow parentheses count as well as the complement for a raw string (if any). Those were using the same indices into the state array, and so could stomp on each other in some cases.

(Note: I experimented with both using an object to keep track of this state, as well as a "named" array, but both seemed to have problems; likely based on how Ace uses + manipulates that array. We could fix it with an Ace patch, but that's definitely out of scope for 1.4)

### Approach

Use a different index for raw strings.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8302.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8302.

title: Avoid migrating ODBC drivers from scratch path
description:
### Intent

RStudio Desktop Pro defaults cause users to install our professional ODBC drivers into the user scratch path (`~/.rstudio-desktop/odbc` in prior versions). When we migrate those drivers to the new user scratch path in RStudio 1.4, it can break user code that contains references to the full path of the drivers in the old scratch path. The intent of this change is to avoid that problem.

### Approach

This changes takes the conservative approach of excluding that specific folder (`odbc`) from migration. 

### QA Notes

Ensure that the `odbc` folder is not migrated to the new scratch path (e.g. `~/.local/share/rstudio`) and that professional drivers installed by previous version of RStudio continue to work. 

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/2065.

title: use dictionaries with encoding marked as UTF-8
description:
### Intent

As per https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/7218, we discovered a small set of dictionaries were encoded as UTF-8, but were not actually marked with `SET UTF-8` to indicate the files themselves are UTF-8 encoded. This caused issues with certain dictionaries.

### Approach

Manually fix those dictionaries, and then upload the fixed dictionaries.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/7218.
Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/7218.

title: Change visual mode key command from ctrl+shift+F12 to ctrl+shift+F4
description:
### Intent

Old key command had a conflict with nextTab.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/7717

### QA Notes

Ensure new key command Ctrl+Shift+F8 works correctly.

title: Ensure current find result/match is visible in visual mode
description:
### Intent

This change addresses an issue in which the editor doesn't scroll to reveal the current match during a Find operation. 

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8298.

### Approach

There are two major challenges here:

1. The search result may not be present in the DOM yet (the Ace editor doesn't render it until its next render loop)
2. The search result may not be a direct child of container we need to scroll

So, to address them:

1. If the search result hasn't surfaced in the DOM yet, use a `MutationObserver` to wait for it to appear, then scroll to it.
2. If the search result is not a direct child of the scroll container, compute its position inside the container and use that as an offset.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in #8298.

title: support updated ansi_console_mode pref value
description:
### Intent

The stored preference value for `ansi_console_mode` changed, but the R-level accessor did not. The R-level accessor should be updated.

### Approach

Handle both the old version of the preference (just in case) as well as the new, current version.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8323.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8323.

title: use UTF-8 path when restoring global environment
description:
### Intent

On Windows, users might be working within paths / projects that cannot actually be represented in the current locale. This can cause various issues.

### Approach

Use UTF-8 paths instead.

### QA Notes

Test that RStudio functions as expected (and you can save + load an R workspace) on Windows when the path contains non-ASCII characters; e.g. letters or words from a language not using the Latin alphabet.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8321.

title: handle multiline tokens with binary ops
description:
### Intent

Certain tokens (strings, quoted identifiers) can span multiple lines. This can cause issues in some cases where our R parser fails to properly bind the binary operator to that token.

### Approach

Properly handle multi-line tokens.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8307.
Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8307.

title: force promises in S3 methods table on unload
description:
### Intent

When a package is unloaded and later re-installed, sometimes older pieces of the previously-loaded package can stick around. For registered S3 methods, these might be promises holding data relevant only to the previously-installed copy of that package. This can cause strange errors to be emitted to the R console, and that package to fail to load, when later loading that package.

### Approach

Before unloading the package, force any existing promises, so they can evaluate in the right context (and be properly re-registered / replaced when the namespace is later reloaded).

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8265.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8265.

title: register Enter handler only on textbox
description:
### Intent

The handler here was being registered on the entire widget, making it active for both the textbox and the Select button. This was preventing the Select button from reacting to Enter keypresses. 

### Approach

Scope the handler to the textbox only.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8331.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8331.

title: implement python auto-outdent
description:
### Intent

Use auto-outdent to fix the indentation of certain lines as the user types -- in particular, when insertion of `else` would require out-denting to match the indentation of a matching `if`. Similarly for `except` and `try`.

![python-outdent](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1976582/97062978-22c88400-1552-11eb-8c7a-21afda207e07.gif)

### Approach

Check for outdenting on `:` insertion and space insertion, and handle outdent by replacing that line's indent with the matching previous line's indent.

### QA Notes

Test that outdenting works as expected. Try typing some of the sample code at:

https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html
https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/controlflow.html

Closes #8178. Not for 1.4.

title: Fix jumpy scroll/cursor/selection action with large code chunks
description:
### Intent

This change addresses an issue in which clicking inside a large code chunk (when the cursor is offscreen) in the visual editor can generate unwanted scroll jumping/selection.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8332. 

### Approach

There are two small changes necessary to resolve this issue:

1. First, we were formerly obtaining the cursor geometry from the focused element, a hidden `<textarea>`. However, the cursor the user actually sees is a painted-on `ace_cursor` element, so now we get more accurate geometry from there.
2. Second, we were scrolling the document while Ace considered the mouse to be down. Ace treats this as a selection-generating event. We now avoid trying to auto-scroll the cursor into view while the mouse is down.

### QA Notes

The code affected here is intended to help keep the cursor in view when navigating with the keyboard, so ensure that still works correctly.

title: ensure profiler resources path is UTF-8
description:
### Intent

Attempts to open projects with non-ASCII characters in the pathname could fail in some cases. This was caused by an attempt to create a directory associated with a mis-encoded path on startup, which (in some cases) could be an error rather than a warning.

### Approach

Ensure that the profiler path is UTF-8 encoded, and also treat errors as warnings so they don't prohibit session start.

### QA Notes

On Windows: test that projects with multibyte characters can be created / opened.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8256.

title: Avoid intermittent hang on visual editor close
description:
### Intent

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8291.

The source of this bug is a while loop that is intended to skip past editors that don't need to be rendered. In some pathological (and timing-dependent) situations, the entire remainder of the render queue consists of defunct editors. When this happens, the loop spins endlessly since `shift()` returns `undefined` on an empty array.

### Approach

Ensure that there are items left in the render queue before we try to skip them. 

### QA Notes

Reproducing this bug usually requires a number of tries.

title: add JSON filetype to status bar
description: ### Intent Add JSON to the status bar widget, so that files can be edited as JSON. ### Approach Simple modification of the status bar entry list. ### QA Notes Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8296.

title: fix offset check when reading history
description:
### Intent

When attempting to access the most recent item in the command line history, we would (on occasion) read out of bounds of our history list, leading to a JS exception.

### Approach

Clamp the history offset to the range of the history list.

### QA Notes

Reproduce via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8293.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8293.

title: commit for rstudio/rstudio-pro#2115
handle rainbow paren tokens in C++ outdent
description:
### Intent

Fix https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8165.

### Approach

The C++ outdent check tried to search for an opening bracket of type `paren.keyword.operator`; however, rainbow parentheses drop the `keyword.operator` types. In this case, we really should just look for a token with the `paren` type.

### QA Notes

Test that outdenting of C++ code works as expected, both with rainbow parentheses enabled and disabled.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8165.

title: require restart after changing spelling language
description:
### Intent

When the dictionary language is changed (particularly, if new languages are downloaded and installed), one can get into a state where the set of dictionaries available on the client are then out-of-sync with what is actually available to the session.

The simplest fix to this is to just request the user restart their session if they've changed the spellchecker language.

Fixes part of https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/7218#issuecomment-713770620.

### Approach

Request that the user restarts after changing the dictionary language.

### QA Notes

Check that you are prompted to restart after changing the dictionary language.

title: Hide cursor position in visual mode
description:
### Intent

Hides the cursor position when visual mode is active. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8174.

### Approach

Hide the cursor position widget when entering visual mode, and restore it on exit.

### QA Notes

Test switching modes as well as documents that open initially in each mode.

title: Use Lucida Grande as a fallback on macOS
description:
### Intent

Restore RStudio's appearance on MacOS + Qt 5.15. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8157. 

### Approach

This appears to be broken because Qt isn't detecting any fonts on MacOS (no known cause). When we detect no fonts, we fall back on `sans-serif`, which renders poorly with our UI. As a temporary measure, this change allows us to use Lucida Grande (our preferred font) even if it isn't detected. 

### QA Notes

You could uninstall Lucida Grande if you really want to be evil with this one. This should result in the display of a system sans-serif font like Helvetica (as it did before the change).

title: Visual Mode Insert Citation Fixes
description:
### Intent

Addresses 2 issues with insert citation. 

1) Fuzzy search weighting - we elevate the weight of the citation key and move other less important fields into a secondary bucket. This results in better search matches in most scenarios.

2) Fix a bug whereby empty brackets could be inserted into document when user doesn't select a citation and presses 'insert' in the insert citation dialog.

### Approach

Adjust weights, wrap the actual insert work of the insert citation dialog with a conditional that requires a selection.

### QA Notes

I was only able to reproduce the bug in desktop, the steps to repro are outlined in the commit message.

title: adapt to change in rs_jumpToFunction signature
description:
### Intent

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8170.

### Approach

Adapt call of `rs_jumpToFunction` to new signature, from https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/bdf94052c87d8de2db4dd529a4ee5fe0db6fa7f9.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8170.

title: unset isSaving_ flag on save cancel
description:
### Intent

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8186.

### Approach

Ensures the `isSaving_` flag is set to `false` when a save is canceled.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8186.

title: properly convert line ending pref on read
description:
### Intent

The line ending preference was not properly converted from its internal integer code to the front-end string value on load.

### Approach

Implement the (mirror) mapping for these integer values to String preference values.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8169.

Closes #8169.

title: allow Qt 5.15.x redirects
description:
### Intent

Qt 5.14 added a new type of navigation, [NavigationTypeRedirect](https://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qwebenginepage.html#NavigationType-enum), which we were disallowing in requests to `acceptNavigationRequest()`. This PR allows us to accept redirects.

In addition, prior releases of RStudio needed to work around a Qt bug in `acceptNavigationRequest()`, which basically required us to infer the navigation type in a roundabout way. That workaround is no longer required.

**NOTE**: We should consider whether we want to always allow redirects. If a host is considered "safe", do we also want to consider their redirects (even to a separate host / origin) as safe? Or is the right fix here to just disallow the `marketo` redirect altogether? Or do we whitelist `marketo` but disallow other redirects?

### Approach

Straightforward removal of old workaround + handling of new navigation type.

### QA Notes

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8187. Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8187.

title: default to RStudio PDF viewer on macOS
description:
### Intent

The default PDF previewer had unintentionally been set to (No preview) with RStudio 1.4 on macOS. This was actually caused by us attempting to request a desktop synctex viewer; however, we do not bundle any such viewer on macOS.

### Approach

When computing the PDF previewer preference, choose the RStudio viewer on macOS, and the default synctex viewer otherwise.

### QA Notes

Test that, for a brand new RStudio 1.4 on macOS, that the default previewer is not set to (No preview).

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8124.

title: handle state arrays in getState() method
description:
### Intent

For each line in the document, Ace tracks the current "state" for highlight rules. This is either a string for a single state, or an array giving the set of states that are active for that line. This is typically used for e.g. multi-line strings, where the state tells us that we are (for example) in a double-quoted multiline string, identified by the `qqstring` state.

When rainbow parentheses are activated, we see two main issues:

1. getState() returns an array rather than a string;
2. A dummy `#tmp` state is placed at the front of the state array.

### Approach

This PR handles the two above cases, by ensuring that `getState(row)` returns whatever the "primary" state is.

### QA Notes

Test manually with the test cases in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/master/src/gwt/test/test-multiline-expr.R, and ensure each case works with rainbow parentheses enabled / disabled.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8156. (thanks @melissa-barca for catching that!)

title: fix issue with removal of connection entry
description:
### Intent

Currently, attempting to remove a single connection from the Connections history actually removes _all_ connections from the Connections history. That seems bad. We should not do that.

### Approach

The issue appears to arise in the way we try to modify the JSON Array when removing a connection.

If I understand correctly, we were using the [erase-remove idiom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erase%E2%80%93remove_idiom) here to remove a range of elements from the array, but this seems to not do what we expect here. A safe fix for 1.4 is to just create a brand new JSON array and add JSON elements to that, except for the connection to be removed.

### QA Notes

Follow @ronblum's excellent notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8204.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8204.

title: check that we didn't step off row when building range for multiline expr
description:
### Intent

Fix multine expr case documented in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8156.

### Approach

When finding the 'start' of the current expression, don't step back off the current row when looking for a right bracket.

### QA Notes

Test via notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/8156. See also test cases in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/master/src/gwt/test/test-multiline-expr.R.

Closes #8156.

title: Fix a race condition when displaying the R error page
description:
### Intent
 
Fix the issue that @kfeinauer raised when verifying #7742, as well as a second issue that we found while diagnosing the first.

1st issue: The "Cannot connect to R" page is displayed instead of "Error Starting R" because the session exits before the "Cannot connect to R" page has been displayed.

2nd issue: The R Suicide message is not sent to stderr, which means the real reason that the session failed (cannot access `~/.local/share/rstudio`) is not displayed on the "Error Starting R" page.

### Approach

* Use a mutex and a flag to ensure the race condition always resolves as we desire (once the Error page is displayed, don't load another over top of it).

* Write the R exit reason string to `std::cerr` before exiting the session so the `rstudio` process can retrieve and display the message.

This is what a failure to access `~/.local/share/rstudio` should look like now:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37987486/96808233-4dd59b00-13cd-11eb-9c59-d8a20ad7a463.png)

### QA Notes

See QA notes on #7742.

title: Add support for shift click
description:
### Intent

A user reported that they expected shift+click to result in adding a citation to the basket (which makes sense given that this is a frequently a multiselect gesture). This change will make that happen.

### Approach

A small change to check the shift on the click event and use that to determine what to do.

### QA Notes

This change is low risk as the code path for adding an item to the basket it already used extensively, so this is just calling that code path when shift clicking.
