Note that 'Reload' and 'Inspect Element' are still only shown in development configurations.

title: implement own handling of context menus
description:
With this PR, we build the context menu ourselves rather than requesting that Qt do it for us. In particular, this ensures that we can add Cut, Copy and Paste actions as appropriate.

Reload and Inspect Element are kept out of the menu, except in debug configurations.

title: fix opening of files on desktop
description:
This PR commits one of the cardinal sins: it teaches the client-side what the user's home path is. In this case, it's necessary to do so as otherwise we're stuck threading through a lot of asynchronous code into codepaths that are otherwise synchronous, or we take on the task of figuring out a way to thread client-side aliased paths into window opening APIs (which feels rather dicey).

Teaching the client-side the user's home directory for this particular usage seemed like the lowest-friction way of resolving.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2440, https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2156.

title: be more permissive in search for libssl
description: This PR attempts to search the most common library directories for `libssl`, rather than attempting to hardcode the library path based on the version of SUSE used.

title: add 'Pull with Rebase' command
description: Implements https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2151. The command is hidden in a small dropdown menu next to the `Pull` button. cc: @hadley

title: explicitly ignore '.git' folder on Windows
description:
This PR seeks to resolve an issue where attempts to launch the IDE could fail if the `.git` folder was not marked as hidden. Effectively, the IDE would get deadlocked between the file monitor scanning for changes to the `.git/index.lock` file, and attempts to call `git status` to populate the Git pane.

Resolves #2141.

@jjallaire, let me know if this feels like the right change or if there's a more appropriate place for this fix to live.

Do we want to be resilient against other hidden folders that may become unhidden (e.g. the `.Rproj.user` folder)?

title: disable accessibility by default
description: As per https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1539, it looks like the issue with accessibility-aware rendering in Chromium causing lagginess in the IDE affects a number of users. Because of this, we should consider disabling this by default, but allowing users who require this functionality to re-enable it (by setting the `RSTUDIO_ACCESSIBILITY` environment variable)

title: show invisibles, use tabs as appropriate in .csv, .tsv
description:
This PR:

- Shows invisible characters in `.csv` and `.tsv` files, so one can see what kind of whitespace actually lives in the file;

- Ensures the Tab key inserts a literal Tab in `.tsv` files.

I also wonder if it would be worth overriding the tab width in `.tsv` files -- I often edit with a small tab width (e.g. 2 characters) but that feels insufficient when editing a `.tsv`, where 4 or 8 might feel more natural.

title: Make common RStudio dependencies cacheable
description:
Currently, RStudio builds (in Docker containers) always begin with a clean `rstudio` source folder, into which common dependencies like Pandoc, clang, and mathjax are downloaded and installed to `rstudio/dependencies/common`. This uses up a lot of unnecessarily time and bandwidth. 

This change does the following for common dependencies:

- Installs dependencies to `/opt/rstudio-tools/dependencies` when building in containers.
- Reads dependencies from this folder when building, if it is present, rather than the source folder.
- Removes the code which re-installed dependencies on every build. 

Paths for local development are fully unaffected; this change only affects the paths used when building in dedicated containers.

Partially resolves #1614.

title: Complete work to build outside source tree
description:
This change makes it possible to compile RStudio for Linux in a directory other than `rstudio/package/linux`. After the change, you can run `make-package` in any directory, inside or out of the source directory, to produce a package in that directory. 

The motivation for this change was that producing and testing local builds using Docker was difficult when build artifacts were written to the source tree. Specifically:

- build artifacts were owned by root from the perspective of the host OS, making them difficult to work with
- only a single local build could run at once; trying to run multiple builds caused them to read and write each others' artifacts

After the change, all build artifacts (e.g. `build-Server-RPM` and GWT compiled objects) are written inside the container in `/package`, avoiding permissions issues and making it possible to run multiple builds at once in separate containers for parallel compilation and testing. Only the final package produced by building is copied from the container.

Another change (suggested by @kevinushey) is that the container image is no longer removed when the `docker-compile` build is finished. This makes it possible to open and explore the container's contents and logs in the case of a build failure. Each unique build variant has its own container name which is cleaned and reused on every build, so containers don't stack up. 

In an ideal world, the source directory could be used either as a fully contained folder where all dependencies are stored and all building happens (as on a dev machine), or as a fully read-only folder, reading dependencies from, and writing builds to, other folders (as on a build container). This change does not fully implement the latter, but along with #1614 gets us close enough for most practical purposes.

title: avoid resolving symlinks in 'relativePath'
description:
This PR resolves an issue wherein, within the Files pane, the symlink target was shown rather than the symlink name itself.

This was a v1.2 regression caused by the Boost upgrade, wherein I switched our previous implementation of `relativePath()` to use the new `boost::filesystem::relative()` API. This was primarily prompted by our old implementation failing with gcc-5 and above. Unfortunately, `boost::filesystem::relative()` does a bit too much -- it also normalizes paths and resolves symlinks -- which is undesired in our usages of this function.

Resolves https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2147.

title: allow interruption of subprocesses
description:
NOTE: This PR is not fully baked but wanted to get it up just in case this seems like something worth taking over the finish line for v1.2 (otherwise we can leave for v1.3).

---

This PR allows us to forward interrupts (`SIGINT`) to child processes launched by the R session, thereby making it possible to interrupt system calls (as is possible when running R from a terminal).

The Windows bits are missing; I'm not sure if there's a similar mechanism for attaching to a process on Windows to send an interrupt (or the equivalent Windows analog).

title: Add support for keyring dialog prompts
description: Adds support for `keyring` based dialogs to persist secrets with ease, useful with driver connections. Prompt can be triggered with `rstudioapi::askForSecret()`: Installation can be performed from dialog and secret is persisted for subsequent calls if users choose the "remember" checkbox: Added help redirect and support article already: https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000969634

title: Numeric filter by histograms in data viewer
description:
This change addresses a number of issues when filtering data, including #1833 and #2124. 

Prior to this change, numeric data was filtered using a jQuery UI slider with min and max values set to the the lowest and highest observation in the data. For example, from:

    View(rnorm(100, mean = 100, sd = 10))

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/36396080-1fb14f6a-1571-11e8-8dc6-a1806acb9c49.png)

This made it possible to select an *approximate* range of interest, but it made it hard to select *specific* values, and suffered from excessive precision. After the change, numeric filtering is performed using a brushing histogram, with bins generated by R's own `hist` function.

    View(rnorm(100, mean = 100, sd = 10))

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/36396203-ad9b8732-1571-11e8-9d97-87b48a698966.png)

The text box beneath the histogram is also user-editable; it is now possible to manually enter a specific filter range, or a single value to filter by.

The slider control was the only component we used from jQuery UI, so this change also removes jQuery UI from our dependencies.

title: Updated two more cases where closing socket was not only done once
fix formation of completion vector (#2236)
description: This PR fixes an issue where we erroneously duplicated the contents of a completion vector, when its length had already been appropriately extended.

title: include package providing help topic
description:
When pressing `F1` to retrieve help for a topic, RStudio attempts to evaluate an R expression of the form:

    help(topic = <topic>, package = <package>)

However, because we were not pairing help topics with their package when retrieving help autocompletion results, we were effectively attempting to evaluate

    help(topic = <topic>, package = "")

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2261.

title: Allow building macOS package outside build folder
description:
This change makes two small improvements to building on macOS:

1. The GWT compiled sources are now stored in the build folder rather than the source folder. This means that it is possible to run a `make-package` build without stomping on an active `ant devmode`.

2. It is now possible to run `make-package` from any directory to produce a build in that directory; you can build outside the source tree (as is already possible on Linux).

title: Implement rename in File menu
description:
This small change makes it simple to rename the currently open file in the editor. The command for doing this is currently on the File menu, but could be moved to a document tab context menu if and when we implement one (see #1664). 

Closes #2199.

title: Scroll down after clicking Show More in Connections pane
description:
This change works around an issue in the Connections pane wherein clicking "Show more" to show additional objects caused the scroll position to jump to the top of the list.

In 1.2, this change makes the pane paged into 512 object chunks, as the current 1.2 behavior is to show all the objects (no matter how numerous). It won't affect most users, but will prevent very large databases from overwhelming the DOM. 

In 1.1, where this will be backported pending additional builds, the pane currently begins paging at 25 objects (see the original issue for an explanation of why this occurs). This change makes that 512 objects to accommodate most databases without paging, and fixes the original scroll bug. 

Fixes #2211.

title: avoid use of boost::regex when trimming comments
description: Fixes #2304.

title: git: improve handling of multibyte paths
description:
This PR fixes an issue where attempts to stage a path whose filename is not representable in the active system encoding could fail. We accomplish this by:

- Adding a switch, allowing the `ShellArgs` class to avoid conversion of file paths to the system encoding;
- Using the wide API for creating a system process, and ensuring all the bits passed in are 'wide' (UTF-16) strings.

This PR deserves extra scrutiny since it exercises a heavily used codepath (Windows process creation). Fortunately, the changes are relatively straightforward -- we use `utf8ToWide()` to construct wide strings, and pass those on to the wide Windows APIs as needed.

title: compile with newer OpenSSL variants
description:
re: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1891

This should help ensure that RStudio can compile against both older and newer variants of OpenSSL / Boost. This is based on the upstream Boost change, https://github.com/chriskohlhoff/asio/commit/92bfc623e6a71353dd2c783f4c9fef5591ac550d.

cc: @Mailaender

title: explicitly allocate JSON methods map on heap
description:
This avoids issues where the destructor could be run during an abnormal
process termination, leaving the R session pegging the CPU at 100%.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1881.

title: Fixed Windows unit tests building
description:
The first issue prevented one of the unit tests from building due to include order due to inclusion of Boost Deadline Timer, but this was fixed by simply changing the wait method to a simple thread sleep. Second issue occurred because building a package build for Win64 was not linking the correct x64 OpenSSL lib.

Let me know if there was a reason the OPENSSL_ARCH was not being set by default for x64 - perhaps I am missing something.

title: support reticulate engine in R Notebooks
description:
This PR (alongside https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/pull/143) provides initial support for Python plot output within R Notebooks.

![screen shot 2018-01-03 at 3 26 08 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1976582/34544312-73051b70-f09a-11e7-8aaa-8e886a812c43.png)

Requires https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/pull/143.

There's still some more work to be done to take this over the finish line, e.g.

- Re-draw the plot when the editor surface is resized,
- Tweak the padding around images generated from Python,

but this is a good start.

title: migrate contents file on first properties access
description:
This should resolve https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1623. I believe this is a candidate for the patch release. Copying motivation from that thread:

---

I was able to reproduce this issue in the following way.

1. Create an RStudio project,
1. Open that project with RStudio v1.0,
1. Open a few files in that project,
1. Shut down the IDE,
1. Open the project with RStudio v1.1,
1. Try editing one of the open files,
1. Close and re-open RStudio v1.1,
1. Notice that the open document is empty.

I think this is because we don't fully migrate to the new format on the first transfer of files. On the first open of RStudio v1.1, the sources folder looks like this:

```
$ tree
.
├── per
│   ├── t
│   └── u
├── prop
│   ├── 2646FB5C
│   ├── 28A9DEA3
│   ├── DC6A99FB
│   └── INDEX
└── s-F955001D
    ├── 244D0217
    ├── 88798333
    ├── FAE2342D
    └── lock_file
```

After a close + re-opening of the IDE, it looks like this:

```
$ tree
.
├── per
│   ├── t
│   └── u
├── prop
│   ├── 2646FB5C
│   ├── 28A9DEA3
│   ├── DC6A99FB
│   └── INDEX
└── s-1794F329
    ├── 244D0217
    ├── 244D0217-contents
    ├── 88798333
    ├── 88798333-contents
    ├── FAE2342D
    ├── FAE2342D-contents
    └── lock_file
```

Because those -contents files aren't populated on the first run, we end up with property files written out with no contents after an autosave. To mitigate this, we should extract the contents out of each properties file during migration and write the associated -contents file.

title: allow case-only renames (closes #1886)
description:
This PR ensures that case-only renamings, e.g.

    .rprofile -> .Rprofile

can succeed when executed through the `renameFile` command.

title: allow UTF-8 R literals
description: Fixes #1910. Rather than hex-escaping character literals, we just allow plain old UTF-8 literals as those work as expected with R >= 3.0.0 (which we now require for newer versions of RStudio)

title: install patchelf for package builds
description: This PR installs `patchelf` for package builds (only if it hasn't already been installed through some other mechanism).

title: save / restore help pane position
description:
Save the scroll position as part of the virtual history used by the Help
pane.

Closes #1919.

title: Render ctrl+based shortcuts in menus correctly on macOS
description:
`QKeySequence` renders Ctrl using the macOS "command" icon. However, we want menu shortcuts to show the literal Ctrl symbol (^); this change replaces Ctrl with Meta on macOS when populating menus.

http://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qkeysequence.html

title: Make self-contained output compatible with Pandoc 2
description:
This change makes the minimal changes necessary to make `pandocSelfContainedHtml` work under Pandoc 2, in the case wherein `RSTUDIO_PANDOC` has been set to use Pandoc 2. In particular, it adapts to the following breaking changes in Pandoc 2:

1. The `<!DOCTYPE html>` header was treated as HTML and passed through, unmodified, in Pandoc 1. In Pandoc 2, it is treated as Markdown and escaped.

2. In Pandoc 2, the HTML converter warns loudly if no title is present in the metadata. 

To address these, respectively:

1. We now use an HTML template that includes the `DOCTYPE` header. If the `DOCTYPE` header is also present in the input HTML, it is removed. 

2. We pass a dummy title metadata field into the converter. It is not used in the template, so it isn't present in the output. 

These changes are also compatible with Pandoc 1, so RStudio can work with either version. 

Fixes #1756.

title: failure to lock source database should not be fatal
description: This should resolve https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1690. Note that the comment above this routine seems to indicate that this is the expected behavior: if we fail to lock an older, orphaned source database, that should not be fatal.

title: inherit project config from non-active projects only
description: Part of https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1552; eligible for backport to v1.1-patch.

title: Bundle OpenSSL on MacOS
description:
Fixes #1600.

## Background

RStudio 1.1 was built on a Mac Mini running Mavericks. Apple included an (old) copy of OpenSSL with Mavericks, with the accompanying headers. It continues to ship that very old copy of OpenSSL today in MacOS, presumably for compatibility with apps built on older MacOS (like ours) but no longer includes headers.

When Apple formally removed all the OpenSSL development headers in El Capitan (in favor of the [LibreSSL](http://www.libressl.org/) fork), we kept RStudio building on our development machines by building and linking against a non-Apple OpenSSL. 

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/34755a49383433202e758e1cd1f3a49ff0220e2d/src/cpp/core/CMakeLists.txt#L185-L203

## Missing OpenSSL

Now that we're building Mac releases on newer machines, we can no longer build our release against OpenSSL 0.9.8, at least not without doing some real gymnastics to keep and build against a copy of the headers (probably ill-advised anyway since this version of OpenSSL isn't receiving security or maintenance updates). 

The RStudio 1.2 build, since it's built against a non-Apple OpenSSL, now actually *requires* that non-Apple OpenSSL to be present at runtime -- so the 1.2 build actually has a hard dependency on Homebrew OpenSSL, and it won't launch on any machine that doesn't have it. 

## Bundling

This change resolves the problem by including OpenSSL as part of RStudio on MacOS. It does three things:

1. Copies the OpenSSL binaries into the RStudio app bundle, and installs them with RStudio.
2. Changes the runtime paths inside the binaries so that they can find each other. 
3. Changes the `RStudio` and `rsession` executables so that they locate the OpenSSL libraries relative to their own path via `@executable_path`. 

It isn't uncommon to bundle OpenSSL inside Mac apps; a quick scan of my own system found a bunch of OpenSSL copies installed in a similar manner:
    
    $ find . -iname libssl*.dylib
    ./TeX/TeXworks.app/Contents/MacOS/libssl.1.0.0.dylib
    ./VMware Fusion.app/Contents/Library/VMware OVF Tool/lib/libssl.1.0.1.dylib
    ./VMware Fusion.app/Contents/Frameworks/libssl.1.0.1.dylib
    ./Microsoft Remote Desktop.app/Contents/Frameworks/libssl.1.0.0.dylib
    ./zoom.us.app/Contents/Frameworks/libssl.1.0.0.dylib
    ./Last.fm.app/Contents/MacOS/libssl.1.0.0.dylib
    ./pgAdmin 4.app/Contents/Frameworks/libssl.1.0.0.dylib
    ./Processing.app/Contents/Java/modes/java/libraries/video/library/macosx64/libssl.dylib

We also already bundle OpenSSL on Windows, and as such it's already part of our NOTICE file.

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/560aeb25f6634b3187082280e192d595ebc047be/NOTICE#L667-L794

title: Fixed a bug where empty responses were not sending Content-Length: 0
description: Before, if an empty response was written, no content-length header would be written, causing an invalid http response. This makes sure that if no content-length header is present on the response, an empty one is sent.

title: build Windows sources with MSVC
description: This PR moves us over from building with MinGW to MSVC, as required by Qt 5.9.2 and QtWebEngine (Chromium).

title: candidate fix for slowness on NFS
description:
This is a candidate fix for the slowness observed by some Windows users running on networked filesystems, re: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1592.

In v1.1, we introduced a feature that attempts to respect a parent project configuration when opening a file located outside of the current project. We do this by looking up the filesystem for files with the extension `.Rproj`, which implies recursively listing the contents of directories until a directory is found.

Unfortunately, there were two problems:

1) Newly-created documents don't have a path; calling `resolveAliasedPath()` on those returns the home directory;

2) We never anchored the lookup to a suitable path (ie, the user's home directory, or the parent of that directory)

This meant that opening a new file would trigger a recursive listing of all files within the home directory (and parent directory where permissions allowed), and I suspect this may be a very slow operation on certain NFS configurations.

This PR attempts to alleviate both issues.

This is a candidate for the v1.1 patch release, if we can confirm it does alleviate the slowness observed.

title: fix crash when executing certain malformed chunk headers
description:
This change fixes a problem reported here, in which executing a chunk with a malformed header can lead to a crash:

https://community.rstudio.com/t/quick-way-to-crash-rstudio/1358

The actual problem is somewhat deep, and has to do with how error conditions affect notebook chunk execution. In this case, the ordering is such that the chunk's execution context is connected, but never disconnected, and so it keeps receiving console input events when no longer on the heap, leading (predictably) to a crash. This shouldn't be possible.

However, this warrants fixing for 1.1, so I'm proposing this more targeted fix to begin with, which simply eliminates the source of this specific error so that it can't set off the dominos.

title: pass continuation by value, rather than reference
description:
This PR should fix an issue where crashes were seen when the project template indexer was running on R libraries containing a large number of R packages.

The crash was occurring because we were trying to construct a `boost::cref()` based on an object on the stack, and that object would already be out of scope by the time the continuation was to be executed. The fix is to simply pass in the continuation by value, since it (as it's just a `boost::function`) is copyable already.

title: Upgrade to gcc 4.7 for Ubuntu Precise builds
ensure we're in a project before trying to use project config
description:
This PR should fix an issue where attempts to set some editor settings (e.g. tab width) would not be respected when no project was open.

Because this code path did not properly verify that we were within a project, we ended up propagating the 'default' project configuration options, and using those to override whatever global settings that might've already been set by the user.

Should be a candidate for v1.1 backport.

title: Remove multiple instances of pagedtable.js
description:
From http://www.gwtproject.org/javadoc/latest/com/google/gwt/core/client/ScriptInjector.FromUrl.html:

```
Warning: This class does not control whether or not a URL has already been injected into the document. The client of this class has the responsibility of keeping score of the injected JavaScript files.
```

title: Use unicode-aware isLetter function in R tokenizer
description:
This change fixes a unit test failure with GWT 2.8. In particular, the identifier which begins with a Unicode letter `\u00C1qc1` is no longer recognized as an identifier and instead causes an error in the tokenizer.

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/master/src/gwt/test/org/rstudio/studio/client/common/r/RTokenizerTests.java#L109

It turns out that the `isLetter()` function in GWT does not support non-ASCII characters, even though Java is supposed to do so; see this GWT issue for details: https://github.com/gwtproject/gwt/issues/1989

Since `isLetter()` doesn't do the right thing here, the fix is to use our own `isLetter()` which is unicode-aware.

title: Remove most usages of String.equals()
description:
Since upgrading to Java 8 / GWT 2.8.1, we've had a number significant regressions stemming from new behavior in `String.equals()`.

Snippets entirely broken: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/1690899038ed5090be44b2afa2b247c2246182d2
Can't save new documents: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/58d880a6890ee39f2508113bf4858c85e01fa015

What changed? In GWT 2.7, the generated JavaScript code made it okay to run `lhs.equals(rhs)` *even if `lhs` was null*. This is no longer okay, and throws a `NullPointerException`. 

In most cases, we tried to guard against this usage by ensuring that `lhs` was not null before calling `.equals()` on it. However, since no runtime error ensued from incorrect usage, we don't know how effective the guards are, and there are probably dozens or more of these bugs hiding in all corners of the product. 

This change replaces every instance of `lhs.equals(rhs)` with `lhs == rhs` (when lhs is a `String`), which gives us the most GWT 2.7-like behavior (i.e. it just returns false if `lhs` is `null`). Unfortunately such a change was not possible to make fully mechanically, and in the interest of brevity I've not removed the following usages of `String.equals()`:

- Cases wherein it is immediately obvious that `lhs` is a variable that cannot be `null` at the given point in control flow
- Cases wherein `lhs` is a string constant or static variable

There's always some risk in changing large swaths of code like this, but in my view it reduces risk on the balance given the behavior change (feedback/discussion welcome).

title: allow 'Open' to navigate into selected directory
description: This PR fixes a small issue in the web file dialogs wherein clicking on a directory, and then pressing the `Open` button, would not navigate into that directory.

description: Prevents... to instead...

title: tweak trimming of executed code
description:
This PR tweaks how we trim executed code -- in particular, we no longer trim leading whitespace from the first line, which should improve the display of executed code. See e.g.

![screen shot 2017-10-06 at 1 44 27 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1976582/31297931-b9cad02a-aa9c-11e7-8b66-02af12df1509.png)

description: See https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1565.

title: Cache and replay app launch environment
description:
This change fixes a problem in all RStudio Desktop releases on Ubuntu Xenial in which no commands that start a new session (open project in new session, etc.) work.

The underlying issue is that the desktop release of Xenial comes with its own version of Qt. When RStudio is first launched, this isn't a problem, as its `RPATH` causes the RStudio version of Qt to be used. However, during startup, RStudio invokes `prepareEnvironment`, which in turn sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to include the system library folders. Now subsequent launches of RStudio don't work because they inherit this `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, which overrides the `RPATH` and causes the nascent RStudio process to load the wrong Qt libraries and fail to start. 

The fix is to cache the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` that's used when RStudio starts, and to temporarily restore it when new instances of RStudio are started. The `ApplicationLaunch` object encapsulates this new functionality. 

While this bug existed in 1.0, the fact that several commands simply don't work make it a 1.1 candidate.

title: detect 'mavericks or greater'
description: This PR should resolve an issue where the Xcode 9.0 update (which cases command line tools to become missing) would cause issues with the Git pane showing up. With this, RStudio should appropriately detect the `/usr/bin/git` 'stub' on newer macOS platforms and prompt for installation of build tools.

title: add 'purrr' cheat sheet
description:
See also: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-web/pull/11

This PR adds a link to the `purrr` cheat sheet, and also a general `Browse Cheatsheets...` link to open the set of cheat sheets available at https://www.rstudio.com/resources/cheatsheets/.

title: work harder to infer desired remote
description:
This PR tries harder to select an appropriate remote in the 'Create Branch' dialog:

1. If the current branch has a tracking remote, then we'll select that as the remote to use in the create branch dialog.

2. If the active branch has no tracking remote, then we'll default to a remote called `origin` (if it exists).

3. All else fails, we'll just use the first remote in the list (the current behavior).

title: Compute version before initiating build
improve NSE detection for dplyr
description:
This PR updates the non-standard evaluation detection system to better understand S3 dispatch + `rlang` idioms for non-standard evaluation. This should fix spurious warnings seen with the latest versions of `dplyr` + other packages using `tidyselect` when diagnostics are all enabled.

title: backup attempt for file locking
description:
(note: if this PR feels misguided I think we can just close)

This PR implements a 'second attempt' mechanism for link-based file locking. If the `::link()` system call fails for some reason, we then instead try to write the lockfile using `::open()`, `::write()` and `::close()` system calls.

By calling `::open(O_CREAT | O_EXCL)`, we ensure that the call only succeeds if the process that attempts to create the file truly was the one that created the file and acquired the file descriptor. (Not all NFS support these semantics, but for the ones that do but don't support hard links, this would be a way out)

title: Add support for collaborative publishing
description:
This change adds support for collaborative publishing (updating content owned by other RStudio Connect users) to RStudio. At a high level, this feature works by showing users all the deployment records (not just their own). When attempting to update content owned by another user, the deployment dialog shows both the source and destination accounts:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/28339252-6335820c-6bc0-11e7-942f-beae7fb0b1e4.png)

It also contains a rollup of some other tweaks to the publishing experience:

- R Markdown documents are no longer rendered before being published. This feature was well-intentioned but in practice the feedback was that it created confusion (as two render logs are visible), delays (as docs that were expensive to render published slowly), and frustration (e.g. when trying to publish a doc that could only render on the server).

- The publish dialog no longer allows you to switch accounts when updating content. This caused more confusion that convenience (as it turned the update into a create without sufficient fanfare). 

- Element IDs have been added to much of the publish workflow to make it possible to drive it from Selenium. 

- When showing the list of deployments for an app, we show the server and the username associated with the deployment. This helps disambiguate similarly named deployments, and lets you know when you're updating something owned by someone else.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/28339353-c26e21e8-6bc0-11e7-9679-c4eb0d44bfcd.png)


Depends on, and must not be merged before, https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/190.

title: use '-z' for machine-parsable git status output
description:
This PR fixes a bug where paths containing backslashes would not be handled correctly in the RStudio Git interface.

`git` documents `core.quotepath` as (https://www.kernel.org/pub/software/scm/git/docs/git-config.html), emphasis mine:

> Commands that output paths (e.g. ls-files, diff), will quote "unusual" characters in the pathname by enclosing the pathname in double-quotes and escaping those characters with backslashes in the same way C escapes control characters (e.g. \t for TAB, \n for LF, \\ for backslash) or bytes with values larger than 0x80 (e.g. octal \302\265 for "micro" in UTF-8). If this variable is set to false, bytes higher than 0x80 are not considered "unusual" any more. **Double-quotes, backslash and control characters are always escaped regardless of the setting of this variable.** A simple space character is not considered "unusual". **Many commands can output pathnames completely verbatim using the -z option.** The default value is true.

Given that `-z` is effectively an alias for `--porcelain`, with the added bit of completely disabling path quoting, I think that's the right fix here.

Because we use a `WaitForMethod` to accomplish this (request a document save and then wait for that to finish), it's prudent that the completion event is fired regardless of whether we save successfully or not. (Otherwise, we risk getting the `rsession` stuck waiting for an event that will never come)

@jmcphers, could you review? I wanted to avoid touching the plumbing around saves; let me know if you think there's a cleaner way forward. (see the logic within `onRequestDocumentSave()`)

The result is that text files without a known mime-type encoded directly in RStudio cannot be opened under macOS High Sierra; e.g.

![ddqrbeaxgaau2to](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1976582/27549689-aaaac834-5a51-11e7-8f82-c8deafad67aa.jpg)

While it's possible that Apple will fix this bug before they ship macOS High Sierra, this PR should guard us in case that behavior leaks into Apple's next OS release.

title: use 'etc/ldpaths' for rJava on macOS as well
description:
This PR fixes an issue where `rJava` can fail to load when running with R 3.4.0 under RStudio on macOS.

Although this issue was originally reported by a Homebrew R user, one can actually reproduce this with R 3.4.0 installed from CRAN, using the CRAN `rJava` binary as well. Compare:

```
kevin@cdrv:~/Library/R/3.4/library/rJava/libs
$ otool -L rJava.so
rJava.so:
        rJava.so (compatibility version 0.0.0, current version 0.0.0)
        @rpath/libjvm.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1.0.0)
        /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.4/Resources/lib/libR.dylib (compatibility version 3.4.0, current version 3.4.0)
        /System/Library/Frameworks/CoreFoundation.framework/Versions/A/CoreFoundation (compatibility version 150.0.0, current version 1259.0.0)
        /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1226.10.1)
```

```
kevin@cdrv:~/Library/R/3.3/library/rJava/libs
$ otool -L rJava.so
rJava.so:
        rJava.so (compatibility version 0.0.0, current version 0.0.0)
        /System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Versions/A/JavaVM (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1.0.0)
        /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/lib/libR.dylib (compatibility version 3.3.0, current version 3.3.0)
        /System/Library/Frameworks/CoreFoundation.framework/Versions/A/CoreFoundation (compatibility version 150.0.0, current version 855.17.0)
        /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1197.1.1)
```

If I understand correctly, `rJava` with R 3.3.x (and below) uses the system Java installation, while newer versions attempt to use `libjvm` from the `@rpath`. This is eventually discovered on the `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH` which is set when R is run from the console, but since RStudio (prior to this PR) was not harvesting this environment variable, it would now fail in RStudio.

Altogether, I think this implies that this PR could actually be a candidate for the patch release, since the underlying issue is that, with R 3.4.0 from CRAN, `rJava` does not work by default under RStudio.

This PR introduces support, when pasting through middle-click, for the global mouse selection to and from RStudio Desktop on Linux (where supported). This is done by detecting whether a `"paste"` event was issued in response to a middle click, and if so, ensuring that clipboard data from the selection clipboard is used instead.

This should imply that one can select text within an Ace instance, and then middle-click in a separate application to copy + paste that text to the new application (or vice-versa).

This change makes two improvements to Ctrl+R reverse incremental search:

- The scope of the search is now limited to the current project's console history (it does not search the entire history archive). This makes it much faster to find and to re-use commands inside the same project, at the expense of making it more difficult to re-use commands from other projects.

- The search results now exclude obvious duplicates (i.e. identical, consecutive commands).

title: Enable builds for newer Debian releases and SuSE
description:
This change enables two new builds from the containerized build system.

## Xenial (Qt 5.4.2)

We currently use a release of Qt which is built against `libgstreamer0.10` (a dependency of `QtWebKit`). Unfortunately, this library has been deprecated and has been entirely removed from the repositories in newer Linux distributions. The replacement is `libgstreamer1.0`; which is [not at all ABI compatible with libgstreamer0.10](https://abi-laboratory.pro/tracker/timeline/gstreamer/). 

Fortunately, Qt can be built against `libgstreamer1.0` with some effort. I've done so (using the Qt 5.4.2 source code, and system configurations in [these docker files](https://github.com/jmcphers/qt-gst10)). The recompiled Qt libraries are packaged and uploaded to S3. 

It's now necessary to produce two desktop builds -- one for Trusty and earlier releases, using the stock Qt 5.4.0 (now identified by a new `-trusty-` in the .deb name, and one for Xenial and newer releases, using recompiled Qt 5.4.2 (identified by `-xenial-` in the .deb name). 

## SuSE

We have built RPMs for SuSE/SuSE Enterprise Linux from the CentOS machines on EC2; this change restores that behavior to the containerized build system.

cc @stevenolen: note that after these changes we use two more containers that we did previously.

title: Apply themes to loading panel and improvements

title: Serialize RPCs so that files open in a predictable order
description:
This small change fixes an issue in which opening multiple files at once in RStudio causes them to load in an apparently random order. The reason this happens is that opening a file involves a series of RPCs; these RPCs are all made at once and compete with each other. 

The fix is to apply some simple queuing behavior to the two RPCs which are invoked when opening a  file, so that we don't have more than one of each in flight at once.

See https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/1036.

With modern handling dark themes contextually. - Scope themes in satellites to only source satellites, this makes satellites consistent with dialogs, say for the git satellite. - Fix dirty indicator in tabs spotted by @kevinushey - Linux had broken borders across panes under new themes and firefox rendered incorrectly some. title: implement virtualization for data grid; use with object explorer
description: NOTE: This PR is not quite yet ready to go, but is ready for some initial review. This PR implements DOM virtualization of a GWT DataGrid, ensuring only that the currently visible rows are drawn when rendering the data grid, and that the DOM is refreshed in response to scroll events. The goal is to allow the user to scroll through very large R objects without too much IDE lag when many rows are available. We implement virtualization in the following way: 1. After the user has scrolled, we figure out what rows are currently in view, and how many rows are currently not visible above / below the current viewport. We tell GWT to only draw the visible rows (+ a bit of extra padding rows, for scrolling). 2. We add a top + bottom rows for padding, and set their heights such that the scroll position represented to the user matches what they would've seen if we had just drawn the row. (E.g. instead of drawing 100 rows of height 24px, we just draw 1 row of height 2400px). One other major performance optimization -- I now use GWT sprites in the object explorer view, rather than plain old `` -- previously, each attempt to append an image in this way would actually trigger a browser `GET` request, requiring a reparse of the base64 image data included in the `src` tag! Moving to GWT Sprites (using CSS `background-image`) seems to circumvent this.

This PR should help alleviate an issue where git commands could fail (especially on networked filesystems) due to the presence of an `index.lock` file when attempting to run Git.

We accomplish this by polling on the presence of the `index.lock` file for one second (once every `100ms`). Although this won't be bullet-proof, it should still catch the vast majority of our git timing issues.

title: GWT bg highlighter; highlight incrementally
description:
This PR seeks to remove a source of 'laggy typing' that can occur when editing large R Markdown documents. This PR moves the document background highlighter to GWT code (mostly as a straight port from JavaScript to GWT).

Previously, updates to the background highlighting of a document were done entirely synchronously, with the whole document updated at once. With the move to GWT, we now ensure that marker updates are sent by a background timer that re-schedules itself until the entire document has been highlighted. This should help reduce 'laggy typing' in very large R Markdown documents when typing near the top of the document.

In this PR, we also introduce a couple of `JsVector` classes that act the same as their `JsArray` counterparts, but expose more of the native JavaScript array functionality. Note that the `JsVector` 'specializations' for primitive types (e.g. `int`) are auto-generated from the 'generic' form.

This change addresses a frequently reported usability issue in the publish dialog; namely, that when publishing apps that have a lot of files, the list of files displayed to deploy is too long and awkward.

title: build boost using custom 'rstudio_boost' namespace
description:
NOTE: Not yet ready for merge, but ready for some review + discussion.

---

This PR attempts to build RStudio using a custom build of Boost which uses the `rstudio_boost` namespace, rather than the `boost` namespace. This should help resolve crashes where R packages making use of Boost inadvertently end up using / calling symbols within the `rsession` process, and a mismatch in Boost versions causes a crash.

Some overview: The `bcp` utility basically allows us to copy Boost headers to a new folder, with the `boost` namespace renamed (using `rstudio_boost` in this case), and an alias back to `boost` used. This is literally done by just replacing calls of the form (for example)

```cpp
namespace boost {
```

with e.g.

```cpp
namespace rstudio_boost{} namespace boost = rstudio_boost; namespace rstudio_boost{
```

in the Boost sources.

While the `boost` namespace is declared as an alias for `rstudio_boost`, it's still necessary for us to change our code to re-define things in the `rstudio_boost` namespace in our sources. This is done by using the macro `RSTUDIO_BOOST_NAMESPACE` and toggling that to `rstudio_boost` or `boost`, depending on whether we're building against the system Boost or our own bundled Boost.

title: Improve VirtualConsole performance and correctness
description:
This change rewrites most of the VirtualConsole class, and its usages, with the goal of solving two underlying issues which have resulted in a variety of bugs:

1. **Insertion into the VirtualConsole is usually O(n^2)**, and is always O(n^2) when the data contains control characters, as the console has no means of pounding over existing data besides a full-on redraw.

2. **Mixing different styles of output in the same console leads to problems**. In the R console, the virtual console is only used for regular output, not error output. For this reason, control characters don't work correctly in error output, and it is not possible for different output classes to co-exist in a single line of output, or overwrite each other.

There are two primary strategies used to resolve these issues:

1. **Let the VirtualConsole connect with the DOM directly**. The VirtualConsole now manages the DOM node which contains all of the textual output. It knows where each character is represented. When data needs to be overwritten, it can locate the DOM nodes which contain that data and update them in place.

2. **Use an efficient data structure to represent the contents of the console.** Rather than maintaining a second buffer which holds the assigned class of every emitted character, a TreeMap is used to remember each region of emitted text. This makes it efficient to locate arbitrary regions of text for replacement when control characters demand it.

title: avoid git's octal encoding for paths with non-ASCII chars
description:
This PR fixes an issue where paths containing multibyte characters were not handled correctly when received from Git on Windows.

By default, Git for Windows uses a so-called 'quoted octal encoding' for paths not representable in the ASCII character set, as described in https://github.com/msysgit/msysgit/wiki/Git-for-Windows-Unicode-Support#Disable_quoted_file_names. Since we never discover / re-encode those names, we use them incorrectly.

The fix here involves disabling `core.quotepath`, and relying on Git to return UTF-8 encoded paths (note that Git does indeed print paths using UTF-8 encoding here, even on Windows).

title: allow both 'template.yml', 'template.yaml' for R Markdown templates
description:
Currently, R Markdown templates look for a template YAML file called `template.yaml`. This PR allows users to define either `template.yml` or `template.yaml` for R Markdown templates.

The main motivation for this:

1. We've mainly standardized on using `.yml` as the extension for YAML files (e.g. `config.yml`, `_site.yml`)

2. The default extension used by RStudio for YAML files is `.yml`, making it somewhat easier to create a skeleton YAML file with the wrong extension.

title: allow 'Activate Console' to activate active tab
description:
This PR will ensure that e.g. `Ctrl + 2` activates the active tab in the Console pane, rather than always activating the Console 'tab' in the console pane. The intention here is to allow `Ctrl + 2` to focus the terminal, if that is what is currently active + visible to the user.

This PR also adds a secondary behavior -- pressing `Ctrl + 2` multiple times now toggles through the active tabs in the Console pane; this can be useful when e.g. using 'Find in Files' output. One can now type `Ctrl + 2` to focus that pane, then use the keyboard to navigate through + select entries in that pane.

title: fix up chunks with leading spaces in name
description:
This PR fixes cache entries that were errantly written with leading spaces, rather than leading zeroes, by an older version of the IDE. This can cause a couple issues:

1. Notebook outputs are not populated in the generated `.nb.html` file when the name is incorrectly written in this way;

2. The IDE can actually crash if it attempts to construct a link to a non-existent cache resource; e.g. for `.png`s in the cache. (This is likely a toolchain interaction issue; if we attempt to serve content that doesn't exist, this causes a Qt exception that crashes)

This PR fixes up all file entries in the cache on init -- basically crawling for files whose names start with spaces, and changing those to be `0`s instead.

Note that the issue that could cause these incorrect cache entries to be generated was fixed with https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/546868c6b6ffd56a4961a513af64f0ff9cbef906, but we may still need this change for users who had generated notebooks with RStudio v1.0.44 (to fix an older, busted cache).

title: Use new package indexing to supply R Markdown templates
description:
Prior to this change, showing a list of R Markdown document templates involved starting up an asynchronous instance of R and streaming its output to the client. In addition to being somewhat complex, this is somewhat wasteful since it's done every time the dialog opens, and we now have a shared package indexing system that can be used instead.

This change removes all of the old classes and events that supported the R Markdown document template discovery process, and replaces them with a simpler class that uses the package indexer to discover packages.

title: Use a plot reaply object for each unique satellite chunk
description: While refreshing multiple satellite chunks, as in: Not all chunks were being resized, in general, satellite chunks: 1. First, they get refreshed with the output from the notebook, which usually does not match the right resolution. 2. Each satellite chunk requests a render of the plot with the right resolution. The problem was not in (1) but rather than in (2), since multiple chunks request a plot render and the plot renderer was static, only one was successfully rendering.

title: enable request log (ctrl+tick) in satellite windows

title: avoid spellcheck overflow when adding puncutation
description:
This PR should resolve an issue where attempting to replace a misspelled word with that same word + punctuation would cause a stack overflow.

![spellcheck](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/22847971/c54e607c-efa5-11e6-93e7-449e590ad0d3.gif)

Note that the stack overflow leaves the editor unusable (it seems to no longer responds to any input).

The fix ensures that the next spellcheck check starts after the replaced word, rather than with the replaced word.

title: Respond appropriately to renames of open files
description:
This change fixes a problem wherein renaming an open file, using the Files pane, causes RStudio to immediately alert you that the file has been deleted and offer to let you continue your work (saving over the old file name) or close the editor. 

After the change, files renamed inside the Files pane are treated similarly to a Save As; the file's path is updated on the client and server. 

This change also removes the `SaveInitiatedEvent`, for no reason other than that I noticed it wasn't used.

title: Clean up orphaned data viewer cache entries
description:
A couple of customers have asked about the size of their data viewer cache folders. These cache entries get created when data viewer tabs are opened, and destroyed when those tabs are closed.

However, since closing a tab interactively is the *only* way the cache entries ever get cleaned up, there are pathological scenarios in which they could become orphaned or persist indefinitely.

This change seeks to address the issue in two ways:

1) Use a session-specific folder to store the viewer cache. This does imply that the 1.0 - 1.1 upgrade will invalidate your old viewer cache, but this is okay since we've already taken a change to 1.1 which uses a wholly different source database folder, so no tabs referring to the old cache will open.

2) After RStudio starts up, take a look at all of the open documents and all of the data in the cache, and remove any data which does not correspond to an open document (effectively a garbage collection step).

title: avoid using 'list.dirs' (performance)
description:
This PR avoids using `list.dirs()` when retrieving package completions, as that call can be surprisingly expensive (especially on networked file systems). Even on my Macbook Pro (with an SSD), I see:

```
> system.time(list.files(.libPaths()))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.000   0.001   0.001 
> system.time(list.dirs(.libPaths()))
   user  system elapsed 
  0.067   0.135   0.202 
```

I'm not sure why `list.dirs` would be so much slower here, but we should avoid using it regardless.

title: Don't save before knitting/rendering unless document is dirty
description: This change fixes an issue wherein rendering an R Markdown document would save it unnecessarily, which is annoying for users who use external editors with RStudio (as the external editors then warn that the file has been changed when it hasn't).

title: implement highlighting for markdown in roxygen

This PR adds highlighting for the Markdown constructs supported in the new release of Roxygen (6.0.0).

title: Add support for RCNTXT layout changes in R 3.3.3
description: RStudio's debugger relies on knowledge of the layout of the `RCNTXT` structure in memory. Unfortunately, this will change again in R 3.3.3. This change adds the new layout, and uses it if the R version is >= 3.3.3.

title: set up environment for Python virtualenv
description:
This PR adds a basic level of support for Python virtual environments.

The basic workflow (as I understand it) for Python virtual environments is to basically just call a script called `bin/activate`, which sets up some environment variables (notably, the `VIRTUAL_ENV` and `PATH` environment variables).

In this PR, we basically mock that process, by executing the venv'ed Python executable with those environment variables active.

title: avoid collisions with 'major', 'minor' macro leakage
description:
On some systems, the `<sys/types.h>` header exports two function macros, `major()` and `minor()`. This can cause issues in translation units that attempt to use these as function, or variable, names. Unfortunately, it's not easy to see how this header can sneak in -- e.g. on some systems, attempting to include the `<iterator>` header pulls that in. 

This PR attempts to rename any usages of `major` or `minor` as `versionMajor` and `versionMinor`, respectively.

The overarching goal here is to ensure that RStudio can build on FreeBSD (as requested by some users).

title: Add support to import white space delimited tables in data import
description: Users have reported the old import dialog allowed them to import tables like: ``` Column_1 Column_2 Column_3 1 A X 2 B Y ``` Which is currently not possible, but could be implemented using `readr::read_table`. Therefore, this PR: 1. Replaces "Whitespace" delimiter to use `readr::read_table` 2. Adds new `Other...` option for other characters and for those users that might want to use `read_read_delim` with a space. Notice that other users have reported that they would like to use `read.table` to avoid installing `readr`, this is being tracked as a separate issue to consider separately.

title: propagate R_LIBS when building website
description: A more scoped version of the previous PR -- we set `R_LIBS` before calling into the build website tools.

title: Allow resizing columns in the data viewer
description:
This change makes it possible to resize columns in the data viewer by clicking and dragging borders between cells in the data grid. It also adds `title` elements to cells in the viewer, so that it is possible to read strings too long to fit in the grid by hovering over the cell. 

Ordinarily, the data viewer sizes columns adaptively to the data, to the extent that scrolling through a large data set can cause column widths to change to reflect the currently loaded data. However, once a column is sized manually, it is presumed that it should remain at that size regardless of the data in the grid. Consequently, resizing a column causes the viewer to (transparently) enter a manual size mode in which column sizes are fixed.

title: resolve emacs click positioning issue w/mathjax
description:
This PR should resolve an issue where attempts to click on a line in the Ace editor would occasionally select the character immediately above. Two things are required to reproduce:

1. Emacs keybindings must be active,
2. A Mathjax line widget must be showing above the click position.

Gif for demonstration:

![mathjax](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/21824506/93634458-d734-11e6-94fc-7aa2d36f3d7a.gif)

The fix here just removes the Emacs-specific click offset handling; in theory this implies that clicks might behave a little less Emacs-y but I think it's unlikely most users will notice.

For reference, the default `screenToTextCoordinates` behavior is defined here: https://github.com/ajaxorg/ace/blob/f757c8568fba3e59392383e332519e5570f54e1e/lib/ace/virtual_renderer.js#L1415-L1425

The chief difference I can see is the use of `Math.round()` versus `Math.floor()`, so my guess is that something about how we are fudging the offsets for line widgets is causing issues -- however, this seems like the simpler fix.

title: Factor/encapsulate portions of SessionMain into translation units
description:
This change factors ~1,800 lines of code from SessionMain.cpp into 9 separate translation units.  The motivator for this change was an exploratory change to support notebook console input that didn't work out; I wanted to push console input into the queue directly, but since all of the console input was handled privately in SessionMain, it was helpful to extract that piece out into its own translation unit. It depended on a number of other private pieces of SessionMain not related to console input, so those needed to go into translation units too; predictably this lead to a network effect that caused me to briefly get distracted factoring SessionMain into smaller units.

The resultant change doesn't truly reduce coupling very much, but it does add some encapsulation and reusability, and hopefully maintainability.

This is designed to be low risk (avoid logic changes, just move code), and I ran with it for a week or so without any ill effects, but the sheer number of lines makes it difficult to review, and in retrospect I don't think it's the right time to take a change of this nature given our proximity to release. This PR is a reminder to pick it for analysis when we're ready to take larger changes again.

title: unification of package extension code
description:
This PR seeks to unify the code driving the various indexers into a single indexer object. The general idea is now that:

1. We have a single indexer object that is responsible for discovering installed packages + extensions within,

2. 'Workers' can be registered on this indexer object that, given a package directory, do some 'work' (ie -- reading + parsing a specific type of `.dcf` file).

The overall outcome -- rather than having multiple indexer objects individually crawling the R library for package extensions, we now have a single indexer crawling the R library, and this indexer delegates to the registered workers.

The code handling registries has not yet been unified; this is less of a priority since the main goal of this PR is to avoid having multiple indexers running in tandem.

title: add support for package-provided project templates
description:
NOTE: PR not quite ready for merge, but most components ready for review.

---

This PR implements support for package-provided project templates. This PR basically provides an interface for RStudio to discover and call various 'skeleton' functions that packages can provide. A brief look:

![screen shot 2016-11-21 at 2 49 03 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/20503908/afa7f62a-aff9-11e6-86b7-8f39b93fdeb5.png)

Packages can define a project template by creating one or more skeleton descriptions in the `rstudio/templates` folder. The project template descriptions should be DCF files with the form e.g.

```
Binding: Rcpp.package.skeleton
Title: R Package using Rcpp
Subtitle: Create a new R Package using Rcpp
Caption: Create R package using Rcpp

Parameter: module
Widget: CheckBox
```

That is, each DCF file should contain an initial DCF record containing information about the skeleton function, and then 0 or more descriptions of widgets that can be used to power the widget.

This changes makes it possible for RStudio Server administrators to indicate permissible hosting frame origins, using a new `www-frame-origin` option, which defaults to `none`, a secure default which indicates that RStudio should not load inside a frame.

The option is a thin wrapper over the `X-Frame-Options` HTTP header, and can emit all of the legal values for the header (including omitting it entirely). 

The new option is documented in the RStudio Server admin guide.

title: split source database files into contents + properties
description:
This PR splits the source database files into two files: one containing the document properties, and one containing the document contents. This PR should allow us to update the document properties without forcing a (potentially large) re-write of the file's contents as well.

The scheme used here attempts to be backwards compatible with the old source database scheme. We achieve this in the following way -- for a document with ID `abc123`, we:

1. Write the document properties to the same file as we would have before (`abc123`),
2. Write the document contents (if requested) to a side-car file (`abc123-contents`).

When reading a document from the source database, we construct the same JSON payload as used before; that is:

1. We read the document properties as JSON (note that for older versions of the source database this will include document contents),
2. If the `-contents` sidecar file exists, then we will inject those document contents into the JSON payload.

With this split, we now try to detect if we really need to write the document contents to file -- we only write the document contents in the source database if those contents have actually changed, and attempts to modify document properties do not update the document contents.

@jjallaire @jmcphers let me know if this all sounds sensible, or if you think an alternate approach is warranted here. Initial testing seems to indicate that this does work as expected, but definitely a close look is warranted!

title: fix backslash escaping in 'Test Package'
description:
This PR fixes an issue when attempting to run `Test Package` in R packages which are not using `devtools` / `testthat` for unit tests. Note that the problem only came to light with the fix in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/1b3228a89cfbe565a5444b16a0493f5229bc756.

Ironically, with the previous 'broken' escape functionality, we were sending code to the shell like:

```
list.files(pattern = '$1$1.R$1')
```

which was parsed by the shell fine and handled by R, although did not actually filter the set of files correctly. After this fix, we were constructing the pattern as e.g.

```
"list.files(pattern = '\\\\.R\$')"
```

However, we need to double-escape the backslashes here, as otherwise R will only see

```
> list.files(pattern = '\.R$')
```

and that will produce an error like:

```
==> Sourcing R files in 'tests' directory

Error: '\.' is an unrecognized escape in character string starting "'\."
Execution halted

Exited with status 1.
```

title: improve discovery for RStudio main window

The fix here ensures that the `$RStudio` main window object is initialized by the SatelliteManager (which only exists on the main window), and satellites now search for a window providing that object.

title: respect active codepage for console output
description:
NOTE: should probably chat realtime just to ascertain if we want to take this + if so what other work might be necessary (also we might prefer to take this for v1.1 instead).

---

This PR resolves a Windows console text rendering issue wherein attempts to convert console output to UTF-8 could fail if the current locale had been changed from the default system locale.

To reproduce, on an English Windows system, try running the following code:

```R
Sys.setlocale(locale = "Russian")
text <- "Привет мир"
text
```

You should see something like:

```
> locale <- Sys.setlocale(locale = "Russian")
> text <- "Привет мир"
> text
[1] "Ïðèâåò ìèð"
```

Note that this issue is unique to RStudio (RGui produces the correct text here).

The issue here is that RStudio has assumed the default system codepage (CP1252 on my system), and converted from that to UTF-8 when returning console output. This PR ensures that we use the active codepage specified by the locale when converting console output.

We might want to tweak the logic here to avoid calling `l10n_info()` so eagerly, but I'm not sure if there's a direct way to detect locale changes on Windows in an application.

The fix is to remove the `fill = false` property to allow the html inside the iframe to grow as needed and then the html widget chunk will grow in size. With fix:

title: update pagedtable.js from rmarkdown to enable notebook preview
description:
Need follow up from https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/commit/ee5d8d4db58d02f249ef7627189cd87c87455de5 to allow `pagedtables` to render in notebook preview mode.

Preview does not render since the notebook preview injects (indirectly) the `js` resources from `rmarkdown` but generate the chunks in the `ide`. When `rmarkdown` introduced the `[data-pagedtable="false"]` attribute, the  `ide` code was not generating it as `data-pagedtable="false"` which made preview not find the `datatables`.

Some cases worth walking through (all fine with this change now):
 1. **old-ide old-markdown**: Works fine, both `js` scripts are the same.
 2. **new-ide new-markdown**: Works fine, both `js` scripts are the same.
 3. **old-ide new-markdown**: In this case, the old-ide does not assign `false` and new-markdown looks for `false` and the preview breaks. This is fixed with this PR.
 4. **new-ide old-rmarkdown**: In this case, the old-rmarkdown is going to look for the attribute `[data-pagedtable]` without caring about its default, so even when set to `false` in the ide, this would work fine.

title: Add padding to html files to prevent qt bug

Let me know your thoughts to iterate on this if needed.

title: Enable recording profiler state while ran as profvis command
description:
Currently, when one runs:

``` r
x <- profvis::profvis({

The state of the ide does not change into "profiling" since the `Rprof` hook was added through `registerNotifyHook` which registers this hook in the environment, not the namespace (thanks @kevinushey for explaining this). The bug that this fixes is a corner case tracked by fogbugz 5689, in which starting the profiler, then starting another profile with `profvis` and then stopping the profiler would cause us to try to read a file that was not created and a not very useful error to trigger as a pop up.

title: bugfix for chunks rendered with 'results = "hold"'
description:
This PR fixes an R Notebook issue where attempts to render plots in a chunk with `results = "hold"` would produce verbatim HTML (ie, wrapped in `<pre><code>`), rather than the expected HTML output.

This occurs because `knitr` attempts to reorder all character results, pasting them at the end:

https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/9fc0c6143605612ad32e04da0d34708d02747817/R/block.R#L205-L208

When an R Notebook generates plot outputs, it generates raw HTML as a length-one character vector with the `knit_asis` class -- because the underlying object is still `character`, `knitr` grabs those and 'paste'd them at the end (thereby losing the class and the special rendering we desire).

I'll try to distill this into a reproducible example in case we can demonstrate that some changes are needed in `knitr`.

Note that we still do not respect the `results = "hold"` attribute; this just ensures that the Notebook is generated as expected.

title: save + restore document selection
description:
NOTE: not quite ready for merge (see comments at end)

This PR attempts to save + restore the document selection for documents opened in the IDE.

---

The main snag to handle here -- we need to detect if the document has changed between the time the user saved the document with RStudio, and is opening it now; otherwise, we could end up attempting to restore a bogus cursor position. (separate comments from @jmcphers suggest that this likely isn't worth worrying about)

As an aside, the document position is currently only saved when the document is saved; we might instead want to do this somewhat more eagerly as currently navigation in a file without actually mutating the document won't save the cursor position. This may be fine, however.

We may also want to hide this behavior behind a UI preference, although I think this behavior will be preferred in most circumstances.

title: Re-enable use of system proxy on Windows
description:
This change fixes a long-standing bug on Windows in which HTML widgets that use external resources (e.g. googleVis and leaflet) do not work if the network connection is proxied.

The fix is basically just to reinstate code that was previously disabled. @jcheng5 's comments indicate that it was disabled due to crashes with authenticating proxies, which no longer appear to be a problem; simulating an authenticating proxy does prevent the requests from succeeding (as we do not supply any UI for injecting a username or password), but the failures are handled cleanly in QtWebKit and do not result in a crash. It seems very possible that the crash was a bug in Qt that has since been fixed in 5.4.

cc @jcheng5 @jjallaire

title: [WIP] initial work porting to QWebEngine
description:
NOTE: not ready to merge! I don't think we'll take this work to completion right away but hopefully this will give us a starting point once we get v1.0 + patches out the door.

This represents some of the early work + investigation into porting to QtWebEngine (and hence Chromium as the rendering engine). This version currently compiles, but lots of code that needs to change has been stubbed out. The main changes that need to be made (some already outlined by @jjallaire, and discussed on https://wiki.qt.io/Porting_from_QtWebKit_to_QtWebEngine):
1. Re-write our calls to the synchronous API `evaluateJavascript` to the asynchronous `runJavascript`, and see if we can adjust any of the APIs where we attempt to make synchronous calls to JavaScript to run asynchronously (or through some other mechanism).
2. Rewrite our uses of `QNetworkAccessManager` -- most of the APIs we might've used there before should now live in the `QWebEnginePage`.
3. Remove our usages of `QWebElement` and friends, and find an alternative -- these synchronous APIs are no longer available.
4. The `addToJavaScriptWindowObject()` method is no longer available -- it looks like we'll need to look at the [`QWebChannel`](http://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qwebchannel.html) class for bridging the C++ / JavaScript worlds now.

Note that I also looked at using Qt 5.7, but since that version seems to require C++11 support we would likely want to stay on Qt 5.6.1 for now (especially since Qt has deemed it a LTS release).

title: allow 'Ctrl+[Shift]+Tab' to navigate tabs on Desktop
description:
This PR does what it says on the tin; it allows `Ctrl+Tab` to navigate tabs forward, and `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` to navigate tabs backward, when using the desktop IDE. (We don't enable this in the browser since we can't / shouldn't -- this is reserved for navigating browser tabs)

(sorry for deltas -- I moved commands around to be more logically sorted together; the only changes are the addition of two new bindings)

title: clear incremental search position when activating Find/Replace
description:
This PR resolves an issue where opening the Find / Replace bar could re-initiate a previous search session. For example, in this document:

```
abc
def
abc
def
abc
```
1. Press `Cmd+F`, and search for the term `abc`,
2. Press `Cmd+G` twice to select the final instance of `abc`,
3. Press `Cmd+1` to send focus to the source editor,
4. Navigate the cursor back to the start of the document,
5. Press `Cmd+F` again.

The 'saved' search position from the previous search session is used / restored, even though this is likely not what was intended (the search session was implicitly ended when the Find/Replace bar lost focus).

We should double-check that this isn't an intentional behavior for other uses of the Find/Replace bar before merging this.

title: implement 'Ctrl+Click' navigation for web links, v2
description:

This PR subsumes the work done in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/763. Now, all Ace editors get an associated background URL highlighter -- this is basically a background worker that runs on a timer, and detects web links with a `http://` or `www.` prefix, underlines them, and provides Ctrl+Click handling for them.

Note: I originally investigated implementing this through the use of smart tokenization highlight rules, but because detecting the 'end' of a URL is somewhat non-trivial + would require changes to _all_ highlighters we want to use, this seemed like a better route to take. It also provides the foundation for a 'Go to file' behavior for e.g. the source references displayed during `testthat` check failures.

Quick demo of how things look -- mousing over the link while holding Ctrl / Cmd turns the cursor into a pointer, indicating a click target.

title: Notebook: Add support for knitr default chunk options
description:
This change makes it possible to set knitr chunk options in the setup chunk, and have them respected in every other chunk in the document. For instance, to hide messages and warnings and continue after errors by default:

``````
```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, 
                      warning = FALSE,
                      error = TRUE)
```
``````

The general idea is:
1. After the setup chunk finishes executing, all the knitr chunk options are dumped as json into the notebook cache. 
2. When a chunk begins executing, it receives both its own options _and_ the set of default options from the cache. 
3. Most places that read options now select from the chunk's own options and then use the default options as a fallback.

There are also some changes here to make it easier to store data in the notebook metadata (`chunks.json`), as this file now also contains the default chunk options and is likely to be used to store other notebook-specific document properties in the future.

title: refine multiline execution logic

I've also added a little test file that we can use (manually) to test that execution works as expected.

title: Add UI pref to allow multi-line execution in R scripts

While listening to @hadley demo at the UseR 2016 keynote, I noticed that he manually selected multi-line expressions in R scripts to execute them with Cmd+Enter and had the thought that some people might prefer the multi-line execution behavior everywhere. 

This change allows users to opt in, via a UI pref, to the same behavior in R scripts that already exists in R Markdown documents: automatic execution of multi-line statements.

title: Align notebook plots with input
description:
This change brings plot output beneath the line of code which generated the plot. This is unfortunately not straightforward because it requires backtracking. For instance, consider the following chunk of code:

```
1: plot(cars)
2: lines(stats::lowess(cars))
3: y <- 1
4: z <- 2
5: plot(iris3)
```

The rule knitr follows is that the plot is attached to _the last line that wrote to the graphics device_ prior to the creation of a new plot. In this case, plots should be attached to lines #2 and #5. Unfortunately, we don't know that the plot should be attached to line #2 until line #5 is evaluated, since any of the following lines could conceivably also write to the device.

The fix is to emit a placeholder ordinal whenever a line places output on the graphics device (using logic similar to knitr). When a new plot is generated, we backtrack to the last emitted placeholder ordinal and insert a plot there. 

Another improvement made by this change is moving to a graphics device option. Formerly, we actually opened the notebooks graphics device when every chunk was executed and then closed it when the chunk was done; now we just set the `device` option so that it's created on demand. 

(Hold until we're ready to take post-UseR changes)

title: use knitr hooks to handle notebook serialization; implement new cache hydration scheme
description:
NOTE: This PR is still not quite ready for merge, but I think it's getting ready for review -- we still need a lot more testing / validation and also error handling + recovery in the new system. This PR uses `knitr` hooks to power serialization, rather than just dumping an encoded version of the cache into the document. We do this in two ways: #### .Rmd -> .nb.html This will be used to create a `.nb.html` file directly from a `.Rmd` file -- basically using a standard `rmarkdown::render()`, with a custom `html_notebook` format. When creating a `.nb.html` file directly from a `.Rmd`, we annotate various `knitr` hooks to effectively place annotations around every piece of output generated. This allows us to detect e.g. chunk starts + ends, plot outputs, HTML outputs, and so on. We also inject relevant metadata as needed. For example, a widget might now be output as: ```
...
``` #### -> .nb.html This is used for generating a `.nb.html` file on save, based on items within the cache. This implies that the `.nb.html` document generated should match what the user sees within RStudio on save. We accomplish this by overriding the (newly-added) `evaluate` hook -- rather than evaluating the R code within a chunk, we use the `evaluate` hook to pull outputs from the cache, and inject those into the document instead. A lot of work is done to annotate cache resources in a way similar to the serialization scheme above, but we likely need to test + confirm that this is all done as expected. ## TODO - [x] Override `evaluate`, or wait for the next version of `knitr` to hit CRAN, so that we can get `evalute` hooks; - [x] Investigate whether we can stop using `trace()` / `untrace()` for placing hooks (use `pre_knit` hook to capture + annotate hooks in addition to what `render_markdown()` does) - [x] Investigate handling of chunks which produce no output (see: https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/1204) - [x] Investigate handling of non-R chunks (we should make sure the serialization scheme handles this sensibly) - [x] Are we able to merge this before interleaving of console IO + plot output is handled?
