title: use html_notebook from dev version of rmarkdown
description:
This PR accompanies https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/691. The goal here is to:
1. Move the 'guts' of notebook generation to the `rmarkdown` package, and
2. Keep the 'notebook from cache' stuff within RStudio, but allow it to work through the `evaluate` hook.

Together with the `rmarkdown` PR, this will imply that:
1. An `rmarkdown::render()` on a `.Rmd` will use the `html_notebook` format, and will work regardless of RStudio;
2. The (already existing) augmented `evaluate` hook will be used as necessary when generating `.nb.html` files form the cache.

There is likely still some dust that needs to settle but I think these two PRs should be good to go (there may be a bit more churn on the master branches for each as needed).

Note that a lot of code is deleted here as effectively that code has been moved to the `rmarkdown` package.

title: Implement display list-based plot resizing for notebooks
description:
This change improves the appearance of plots in notebooks in three ways:
1. Plots are now drawn for the notebook's exact width. Plots were formerly drawn at a fixed width and height and scaled to the editor surface using traditional image scaling.
2. The device pixel ratio is now respected, so plots appear sharper on Retina displays. 
3. When the editor is resized, plots are redrawn to fit the new width from a persisted display list.

Display lists are persisted as `.snapshot` files inside the notebook cache; the display lists are written along with the plot's image. A resize causes the image to be recomputed from the display list.

To avoid tying up the main thread during resize, the resizing is performed by a separate R process, which receives the list of `.snapshot` files on standard input and outputs the resized `.png` filenames to standard output, where they're picked up and sent to the client as they become available.

title: use new rmarkdown's 'output_source'
description:
NOTE: hold this PR pending some more testing.

This PR implements cache item injection using the `output_source` hook provided by `rmarkdown`. Essentially, a cleaned-up version of the code we were injecting into the `evaluate` hook has now been moved to `output_source`, and we remove a bunch of unneeded code (as that code has been moved to `rmarkdown`.

We should make sure we sync an `rmarkdown` version bump and pin to that before merging this PR.

title: fix cut, copy, paste command handling in Emacs mode
description:
Not quite ready for merge, but wanted some code so we could chat about the issue + make sure I have everything straight in my head.

---

There are a number of related issues in our Emacs mode on Qt:
1. We attempt to bind some commands with a `C-c` prefix (e.g. `C-c C-v` to get help for the item under cursor), but `C-c` is caught at a very low level and turned into a copy command (before GWT even gets to see it)
2. The ShortcutManager always eats `C-c` and `C-x`, even if an Ace is not the target of the current keydown event. This breaks attempts to e.g. copy or cut from non-Ace elements in the IDE when Emacs mode is on.
3. The 'Cut', 'Copy' and 'Paste' commands don't always work when invoked from a menu, as these get translated into the corresponding keypresses (e.g. `C-x`, `C-c`, `C-v`); if Ace handles it while a Vim / Emacs keyboard handler is active, it will use those bindings in lieu of an actual copy / paste.

@jjallaire, do you recall if there's a reason why we just emit the appropriate keypresses on these commands, rather than executing the 'real' copy / cut / paste command at a lower level?

In short, the goal of this PR is to:
1. Make sure that `C-c` and `C-v` have the correct behaviour whether executed within Ace or within a separate input field, and
2. Make sure that Cut, Copy and Paste always do the right thing regardless of the active editor mode.

title: debounce 'onContentSizeChanged()' calls
description:
This PR improves the performance of the console in response to large amounts of console input by debouncing both `onContentSizeChanged()` and `scrollToBottom()` requests (using the `TimeBufferedCommand`).

Previously, `scrollPanel_.onContentSizeChanged()` was called eagerly in response to _all_ console IO, which placed heavy strain on the browser when re-sizing the console history + other dependent UI elements; by placing this in the `TimeBufferedCommand` as well we ensure that these resize requests only happen at most once every 5ms during the execution of large amounts of R code.

title: Retry opening rsession port for up to 1s
description:
Found a "crash" on session restart while debugging an Spark package. However, this issue manifest in other packages as well, for instance, see `finalizer` workaround in this package: https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/branch-1.4/R/pkg/R/sparkR.R#L212

Technically speaking this is not a crash, what happens is that the rsession gets restarted using the same port, the port happens to be already in use by the old rsession which is releasing resources, and RStudio quits when the rsession can't be initialized.

We know this is caused by the rsession port being in used from rsession.log entries that look like this:

```
14 Apr 2016 20:13:06 [rsession-javierluraschi] ERROR system error 48 (Address already in use); OCCURRED AT: rstudio::core::Error rstudio::core::http::initTcpIpAcceptor(SocketAcceptorService<boost::asio::ip::tcp> &, const std::string &, const std::string &) /Users/javierluraschi/RStudio/rstudio/src/cpp/core/include/core/http/TcpIpSocketUtils.hpp:103; LOGGED FROM: int main(int, char *const *) /Users/javierluraschi/RStudio/rstudio/src/cpp/session/SessionMain.cpp:3250
```

The proposed fix is to wait for up to 1s for the port to become available during boot. If the time expires, the same error triggers.

An alternate fix that was explored was to wait for the port to be release; however, exploring that fix proved to be more complicated than I would expected. The exploration of this fix is available here: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/commit/dd67b9f71357ee8864dd32d53558d9d85865dd62

Finally, we could also explore changing the port number when the rsession restarts; however, I'm less aware of the implications of that change.

From all, the less-risky fix would be to take this change making RStudio more resilient to port issues while booting.

title: explicitly find git executable
fix Windows hang when errors emitted from graphics device
description:
This PR fixes a hang on Windows when errors are emitted when generating plots (e.g. through `GEplayDisplayList()` or `GEcopyDisplayList()`).

The fix effectively uses R-level `tryCatch()` rather than C-level `R_ToplevelExec()` to trap errors. For reasons unknown to me, `R_ToplevelExec()` (as used in `r::exec::executeSafely`) is not sufficient in trapping these errors -- likely, this is a bug in the SJLJ error handling in the new MinGW toolchain distributed with Qt, as this code has lived and run fine for a long time with older versions of RStudio (e.g. 0.98 and older).

For whatever reason, ensuring that the error handlers are attached in R code (through `tryCatch()`) side-steps this problem.

title: cache decoded line's size rather than recomputing at each stage
description:
This PR fixes an issue where attempting to search through files with long lines (e.g. base64 encoded content) would cause a quadratic re-computation of the number of UTF-8 characters in the line as matches were discovered in the line.

Rather than computing the number of UTF-8 characters from start to end on each match, we cache and update the size as we go along.

The net result is that Tab now transfers between the text box and the directory widget, skipping over the (somewhat bogus) focusing of the 'path breadcrumb' widget in the header, and making it easy to switch to and from directory widget focus vs. text box focus.

This PR implements 'quick find next' functionality (similar to that of Sublime Text). It allows you to add multiple find targets to the selection, using multiple cursors. description:
This PR does two things:

1) Allows Ctrl (and Meta, on OS X) + Enter to confirm the current commit, and
2) Allows Cmd (on OS X) for the various scrolling hotkeys.

A nice-to-have for users who don't want to touch the mouse when done writing their commit message.

title: don't index 'node_modules' directory
description: This PR avoids indexing the `node_modules` directory for a project (as this directory can often be quite large and is generally full of things that shouldn't be touched directly).

title: consolidate '.rs.scalar()' methods
description:
This PR consolidates the `.rs.scalar()` and `.rs.nullOrScalar()` methods into a single method. Some motivation:

1) R throws an error if you attempt to set a class on `NULL`;

2) A user reported an error occurring from this method (unfortunately without a stack trace) due to a call to `.rs.scalar(NULL)` -- unfortunately, we do not know where that `NULL` came from. Odds are this would either work fine, or pass along the error further upstream, but in that case it's likely that we would get better logging of the error (after receiving an unexpected result on the client side).

Adding this as a PR first just to sanity check that there's not a reason why we might want to preserve the existing behavior (since `.rs.scalar()` is quite commonly used)

title: add (devmode-only) session suspend command
description: This PR adds the `suspendSession()` command and places it within the `Session` menu, but enables it only for SuperDevMode. This should make it a bit easier to debug suspend-resume related bugs.

title: prevent backspace when 'body' target of event
description:
This PR seeks to (safely) prevent Backspace keypresses from causing a browser 'Back' event.

In a previous commit, we attempted to suppress all backspace handling by the browser -- however, this breaks editing with editable fields (e.g. text areas, inputs, and otherwise). This PR implements a more targeted suppression of backspace: if the `body` element is the target of a backspace keydown event, only then do we suppress it.

Tested with Chrome + FireFox on OS X, and this seems to handle the main cases.

title: don't display chunk toolbars for chunks that lie within folds
description: This PR fixes an issue where chunk toolbars would still get drawn for R chunks within a folded Markdown section.

title: improve keyboard navigation in directory widget
description:
This PR improves keyboard navigation in the file selection widgets (e.g. on `Open File...`):

1) You can type the name of the directory you wish to navigate to (prefix matching); the first prefix match is selected, and a timer clears the current prefix 'buffer' after 1 second;

2) Backspace now navigates to the parent directory (if available),

3) The widget is focused on open (so that keyboard navigation will immediately work)

We also now ensure backspace can't perform a browser back action when the IDE has focus.

title: SVN: perform non-recursive revert
description: This PR fixes an issue where attempts to 'revert' changes to a directory (ie, changes to its properties; for example, ignore properties) would cause a recursive revert, thereby reverting all changes files within that directory.

title: more permissive httpdport-as-function detection
description:
This PR checks directly whether `tools:::httpdPort` is a function, rather than introspecting on the R / SVN revision.

This seems necessary in some cases as some users might build R from sources without setting / propagating the SVN revision (it looks like it defaults to `-99` in that case).

title: avoid window reload in ace preview
description: This PR fixes an issue where the Ace editor preview would vanish after changing the zoom level in the appearance preferences pane. My fix is to just use the font sizer (which works fine) and scale the font size by the selected zoom level.

title: avoid using temp files in code preview for data import
description:
This PR adds two options to the data import options request:
- `canCacheData`: If `TRUE`, allows data import code generation to cache data for URLs
- `cacheDataWorkingDir`: If `TRUE`, makes data import use the `getwd()` instead of the temp directory

It also adds a `preview_data_import_clean` RPC to clean up temp files when the dialog closes (notice that OS also have policies to clean the temp directory, but it's a good practice for data import to clean up this proactively as well).

Couple changes in the data import process:
- Preview code always sets `canCacheData` to `FALSE` to allow users to import fresh data with clean code that does not rely on temp files.
- Preview code for XLS does set `canCacheData` to `TRUE`; however, it also sets `cacheDataWorkingDir` to `TRUE` to allow users to download datasets directly into their working directory.

title: Fix 'project not found' issue with other users' unshared projects
description:
This change fixes an issue which occurs when users open projects that belong to other users, but which are not actually shared -- that is, they don't use the project sharing features, but can still be opened due to ordinary filesystem permissions.

The problem has to do with the project ID mapping table. When we detect that we're opening another user's project, we attempt to clean out any local knowledge of the project ID so that we can insert a shared project ID. If, however, there is no shared project ID (and there won't be in this case since the project has not been shared), a new local ID is generated. Without a stable local ID, the project cannot be opened.

The fix is to avoid stomping on the local ID of a project unless there actually exists a shared ID with which to replace it.

There are two implications to note here:
1. It is possible to have two users in a project at once _without_ using project sharing. Since most project sharing features require synchronized project IDs and sharing metadata, they will not work in this configuration. 
2. It is now possible to upgrade from a project shared only at the filesystem level to one formally shared in RStudio -- for instance, if you're working in a project already and want to take advantage of sharing features. When this happens we need to synchronize the project IDs to enable the use of distributed events, etc.. This code already existed as a temporary measure but we should now considered it permanent (I've removed the TODOs).

We will want to do some sanity checking on whether the shared project features degrade gracefully in this scenario (i.e. shared at filesystem level only), and verify that upgrading to a formally shared project is possible.

title: ensure prefix keys don't cause beeps
description:
This PR should ensure that prefix keys don't cause beeps.

This does affect code that runs on every keystroke, so we should double-check that this is doing what's expected. Just to outline how the keyboard shortcut manager works here and how a keydown event is handled:
1. An event previewer looks at keydown events, and appends the keys pressed to the keybuffer,
2. We search through the active keymaps to find an active command bound to the current keybuffer state,
3. If a command is found, the keybuffer is cleared and that command is executed,
4. Otherwise, the keybuffer is kept alive.

This PR effectively ensures that if the keybuffer is 'alive', and is actually the prefix of some mapping in our keymaps, then the browser doesn't see the event. Note that the `swallowEvents` function basically looks at keys at the 'final' point before the browser would handle it (hence it being a sort of 'post-view' handler)

Note that if Ace handles a keydown event, it also emits a signal that we use to ensure the global keybuffer is cleared as well.

title: Avoid integer truncation while computing console width
description:

The problem is caused by fractional character widths on high DPI displays and GWT integer truncation, with the result that the width is computed as if characters were narrower than they really are (e.g. `7px` rather than `7.5px`).

title: fix 'pending' check for bindings; update editor mode on prefs change
description:
This PR fixes two issues:
1. It looks like the editor mode was not always synchronized (in the ShortcutManager) after the editor mode was changed in the EditingPreferencesPane, even though it was changed in the underlying Ace instance. This meant that certain RStudio commands would not be properly toggled on/off when the mode was changed.
2. The 'pending' check in the ShortcutManager did not work properly -- it merely checked to see if there were _any_ commands available in the following key sequence, but it did not confirm whether any of those commands were actually enabled. This meant that e.g. `Ctrl+C` would be logged as a 'pending' key sequence, even though the underlying commands would only be accessible in Emacs mode.

I discovered this while in Vim mode: attempting to return to normal mode (with `Ctrl+C`) and then save (with `Cmd + S`) failed, as the shortcut manager expected there to be more commands available after `Ctrl+C`. So, instead of looking for commands bound to `Cmd+S`, it looks for commands bound to `Ctrl+C Cmd+S`, which then fails.

title: improve shortcut dispatch (mediate Ace + RStudio interactions)
description:
NOTE: Not quite ready for merge, but this PR fixes a number of issues that arise when attempting to use Emacs keybindings (currently, it's possible for the RStudio keybuffer and the Ace keybuffer to get out of sync, causing oddness with dispatch for commands taking multiple keys). I think we will want to take this for the coming release.

---

Previously, the `ShortcutManager` attempted to figure out who + if would handle a particular set of keys, primarily by using its own internal Ace command manager. However, this doesn't work in the presence of multiple Ace key handlers (since each of those constitutes its own command manager + key handler). Overall, this dance is done to ensure that our own RStudio keybuffer, and Ace's internal keybuffer, stay in sync.

This PR simplifies the scheme greatly -- instead of having the ShortcutManager attempt to monitor Ace keypresses (by using its own version of an Ace command manager), we instead listen for command execution events fired by Ace. In other words, we allow RStudio to tell Ace if a command has been executed (so it can clear its internal keybuffer), and Ace to tell RStudio if an Ace command has been executed (so we can clear the ShortcutManager's keybuffer).

This way, we ensure that after 'some' command has been executed (either Ace or RStudio), the keybuffers are cleared and kept in sync.

title: Create missing stdout/stderr streams if necessary
description:
This change is a third attempt to correct an issue observed for the 2nd and following users on Remote Desktop installations.

It's similar in spirit to the last attempt (https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/452). The difference is that, instead of attempting to get `QProcess` to connect `stderr`/`stdout`, this change detects the case where `stderr` and/or `stdout` are disconnected and "creates" them (by creating a stream for the standard descriptor and assigning it directly). 

This allows us to tolerate the error case without any changes in behavior in the non-error case (i.e. if `stdout` and `stderr` have real file descriptors, the logic works exactly as before). 

This change has been tested on Windows 2012 R2 (both on desktop and over RDP with another RStudio session active), on Windows 8, and Windows 7.

title: Ensure rsession process is created with stdout/stderr
description:
This is a fix for the `ERROR_INVALID_BLOCK` issue seen by second Remote Desktop users and probably deserves some explanation.

The call which is actually failing for RDP users is this one:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/01329097a054c48dd3f2ddee9ef600b9c420dc62/src/cpp/core/system/Win32OutputCapture.cpp#L90

```
  if (::_dup2(fd, _fileno(fpStdFile)) != 0)
      return systemError(errno, ERROR_LOCATION);
```

Some careful disassembly indicates that for the first RDP user, `_fileno(fpStdFile)` returns 1 and 2 for stdout and stderr, respectively. For the second user, however, it returns -2 for both! 

According to https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/zs6wbdhx.aspx: "If stdout or stderr is not associated with an output stream (for example, in a Windows application without a console window), the file descriptor returned is -2."

So it doesn't seem to have anything to do with pipes at all--the problem is simply that the second user's rsession doesn't _have_ stdout or stderr streams, which is why it's so exceedingly difficult to redirect them. 

Why might this be? Well, Qt added some options in 5.4 around managing child process output; compare:

http://doc.qt.io/qt-4.8/qprocess.html#ProcessChannelMode-enum
http://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qprocess.html#ProcessChannelMode-enum

It's hard to tell without a deep dive into the `QProcess` internals, but it appears that there's a bug in Qt 5.4 wherein `QProcess::SeparateChannels` doesn't allocate stdout/stderr streams for the 2nd RDP user. Somewhat unintuitively, then, forwarding the streams for the parent process makes them consistently available for the child process (rsession) to capture.

title: Address pipe read errors on startup for multi-user configs
description:
This change fixes an intermittent error on startup for the 2nd (and following) users on multi-user Windows systems. 

For the 2nd user, the file descriptor on the read end of the pipe for `stderr` appears to become invalid during boot in some situations (due to invalidation of the underlying operating system handle, for reasons which are unclear). This causes `_read` to fail every time it attempts to read the descriptor. Since we just keep trying this can result in either a crash (when the `-1` return value from `_read` is interpreted as a large number of bytes read due to an implicit cast to `unsigned`), or a spin (since we log the error and continue, then encounter it again). 

The fix is to implement some fault tolerance: if we can't read from the pipe, we close it, and try to establish a new pipe on the output stream. In practice this new pipe works almost all the time; in the case where it doesn't, we wait very briefly and try again, up to 16 times. 

In my testing I was only able to observe a retry once, and only during boot (i.e. it doesn't seem that the descriptor is invalidated during the normal course of operations). My guess is that there's a boot timing issue here (which might also explain the intermittency).

@jjallaire , could you give this a sanity review? We should probably backport this as soon as we feel comfortable with it; we only have one report of the associated crash in the wild but my guess is that it's because not enough users have tried 448 yet.

description:
The guts of this PR: we now look for 'separate statements' when providing for indentation in all cases. For example, previously, we produced this indentation:

One slight bonus is that this PR should (marginally) improve the performance of indentation code as we now perform less look-behind when attempting to produce an indentation for the next line (which implies e.g. reformat actions should be faster)

title: Improve performance of virtual console when highlighting large output
description:
This change increases the performance of the `VirtualConsole` for large outputs.

Formerly, every time output was added to the console, the console was effectively redrawn from scratch: a new HTML string was created from the content and injected into the DOM. This is expensive, but always correct, and sometimes necessary because control characters in the output can cause it to overwrite (nearly) arbitrary areas of existing content. Unfortunately it's also effectively an _O(n^2)_ method--fast when the input is small but eventually very slow. 

This change contains two optimizations, which bring console output back to linear time in most cases:
- The 95% case is that the output to be added contains no control characters other than newlines. In this case, we now emit the new content directly as new text nodes (or `<span>`, as appropriate) appended to the DOM. We can do this without making a pass over the old content, so it's fast.
- In the case that output with control characters has been processed, we do a redraw, but more cheaply: instead of emitting one character at a time through a `SafeHtmlBuilder`, we now just scan for indices of character runs with identical classes, and emit them directly to the DOM (as text nodes, to mitigate XSS risk). 

Further optimization is possible here, but with questionable returns--in particular, it would actually be possible to just manipulate state incrementally in the DOM as deltas only (doing away with the rebuild phase entirely) but since control characters are relatively rare this offers a lot of regression risk without a huge performance gain.

title: ensure namespaced objects resolved from that namespace
description: This fixes a bug where e.g. `dplyr::filter` could be resolved as `stats::filter`.

title: fix formula skipper
description:
This fixes an issue @hadley saw re: erroneous lint in formulas, e.g.

```
classifly(data, variable ~ other)
```

I think this PR is safe enough to take for v0.99 but am fine leaving it for the next release as well if we prefer to be conservative.

title: Update to Qt 5.4.1 on Windows
description: This change causes us to start building against Qt 5.4.1 on Windows.

title: suppress 'CTRL + ALT + SHIFT + click'
description:
Currently, an exception is thrown by Ace on the combination of `CTRL + ALT + SHIFT` + click. The exception leaves the editor in a bad state (dead, stale cursors left over; active cursor is no longer visible)

I tried to investigate whether this could be fixed at the Ace level, but the fix did not seem immediately obvious (or easy to do without risk of regression).

This PR just suppresses that particular event to avoid that exception.

title: resolve 'Ctrl+Shift+P' conflict
description: Changes the select/expand to matching keyboard shortcuts to 'Ctrl+Shift+<Alt>+E' instead, to avoid overriding 'run previous chunk'.

title: make the R completion engine more unicode-aware
description:
This PR adds some provisioning for unicode support (piggybacking on the `ace/unicode` package).

Fixes completions following unicode characters:

![screen shot 2015-04-30 at 3 51 53 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/7423994/dc2d6f24-ef50-11e4-9d2e-6b463f3b4a65.png)

Also ensures that such variables containing unicode letters are 'syntactic' (and so does not quote the completion, as it would be successfully parsed by R even without backticks). Other unicode symbols will style require quoting (e.g. ∞).

title: bugfix for 'else-if' in parser
description:
This fixes a bug where the parser incorrectly flagged and `else` following an `if` statement as erroneous, e.g.

![screen shot 2015-03-31 at 10 18 49 am](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/6928084/76dbabca-d7a6-11e4-8734-4fc44b78f3c0.png)

The issue here is that the parser was jumping out of the if statement too soon -- it believed the end of the expressions was here:

``` R
Encoding(object) <- "UTF-8"
               ^
```

title: use ant to concatenate ace support files
description:
(sorry -- accidentally placed this on master first; wanted to make this a PR just to be sure that anything I'm doing in the ant build file will work with the versions of `ant` across our build systems)

This PR adds an `acesupport` target that simply concatenates all of the `acesupport`-related JavaScript files together, and uses that target for `devmode`. This should make it much easier to debug exceptions that occur within our `acesupport.js` code.

title: Fixes for indentation in multi-mode documents
description:
NOTE: Let this brew a day or two to think about whether this really is the best solution...

This PR brings a couple of fixes:

It ensures that chunk headers and footers are _not_ tokenized into the underlying code model, e.g.

``````
- ```{r}
+ foo <- function(x) {
+     x + 1
+ }
- ```
``````

Previously, the header / footer bits were entering the code model, and so the indentation logic would get confused (and believe that e.g. there was an un-finished symbol, ```, hanging around.)

The reindent logic is moved into GWT code. This was necessary for one main reason -- one change in the Ace default mode API that we tried to step over was the fact that the `getNextLineIndent()` prototype changed -- it is now, by default,

```
getNextLineIndent(state, line, tab)
```

rather than

```
getNextLineIndent(state, line, tab, tabSize, row)
```

However, we rely quite heavily on more than just the current line for computing the current indent (we needed that row parameter), so we work around this by fudging the cursor position (so that, in the context of a `getNextLineIndent()` call, we can assume the cursor is at least on that line).

title: add vim close all
description: Adds `:qa` and `:qa!` as methods for closing all documents (interactively or non-interactively).

title: respect '--library=' in R CMD INSTALL
description:
NOTE: probably leave this one for next preview (after we merge in new Ace).

This PR adds some parsing on the `--library=` argument to `R CMD INSTALL`, which we use with e.g. the `buildAll()` command.

TODO: need to handle `devtools::dev_mode()` (and probably `packrat` mode as well); ie, if devtools or packrat mode is on, ignore `--library` switch.

title: determine whether semicolon insertion appropriate on '(' insertion
description: This PR brings 'smarter' `(` insertion to the C++ mode -- if the user inserts a `(` and we can ascertain that they are making a function call (rather than defining a function), then we automatically insert  `();` rather than just `()`.

title: Autocompletion for server.R, ui.R with shiny documents
description:
NOTE: not quite ready for merge, but putting this up here for now.

This provides autocompletion results in `server.R`, `ui.R` by parsing the companion document for relevant completions.

title: roxygen-aware commenting
description: This PR brings ROxygen-aware commenting for the R and C++ modes. Whenever an uncommented selection has lines that begin with an '@', when we comment that line out, we use the Roxygen delimiter (`#'` or `//'`) to comment the selection.

title: add explicit hotkeys for 'cmd+up', 'cmd+down'
description: This adds explicit hotkeys for moving the cursor to the start / end of the document with CTRL (CMD) + Up, Down.

title: separate completion list and help into separate popups
respect indentation + selection for single line commenting
description: ![commenting](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5079721/f4e1b234-6e6b-11e4-88f1-9280b500f22b.gif)

title: guard against null / emptiness in JSON object
description: This avoids exception errors when completion of a chunk option with no completions available.

title: Move ACE textarea behind rather than in front of content (for editor)
Workaround for Safari 8 text antialiasing
description:
Yosemite comes with a new version of Safari that causes text to be composited on the GPU more frequently. When text is composited on the GPU the antialiasing is done with an algorithm that produces a much lighter font weight.  

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/470418/4741018/aac3e0d6-5a12-11e4-8491-6c066ddf297f.png)

Elements with `position: fixed;` are particularly prone to trigger this behavior; in fact, the presence of a single visible fixed-position element is enough to trigger the poor behavior for any element it may overlap. The workaround implemented here is to slightly raise the `z-index` of the ACE editor's input `textarea`, which has `position: fixed`:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/470418/4741027/c0aba35c-5a12-11e4-9cc9-0de88ca27596.png)

title: Use absolute URL to open rendered PDFs
description: This fixes a bug wherein PDFs were not displayed when RStudio Server is serving pages behind a path other than `/`. Formerly, the PDF.js viewer was loading a server-relative URL (e.g. `/rmd_output/1/`); this change makes that URL absolute (e.g. when RStudio Server is running behind `/rstudio/`, `http://server/rstudio/rmd_output/1`).

title: Improved C++ indentation for the IDE
description:
This PR brings improved C++ indentation to the IDE.

Relative to the previous PR, this one relies on a combination of simple heuristics for indentation, as well as a more robust token-based indentation scheme.

A number of utilities were factored out from the R code model, but I neglected to actually change the R code model itself (!) because I am still cautious about touching parts of that machinery which I do not understand (except in cases of pre-existing bugs).

@jmcphers also mentioned that we may consider back-porting some of these rules for e.g. the JavaScript mode -- it would be useful to make the IDE a strong environment for JavaScript development in the future as well (e.g. for advanced Shiny users).

title: Fix clipboard copy in IE10+
description:
This change fixes a problem in IE10+ in which the copy command doesn't work in the ACE editor component. 

The problem is a result of IE's treatment of the `beforecopy` and `copy` events. In IE, the clipboard data from ACE (i.e. the selection contents) is successfully recorded in ACE's handler for the `beforecopy` event, but then immediately cleared in the `copy` event. 

The fix is to suppress the `copy` event when two conditions hold:
- The current browser is IE, and  
- The text on the clipboard is the text ACE thinks should be on the clipboard 

Suppressing the event leaves intact the clipboard data loaded in `beforecopy`.

title: Unload packrat after calling it to check project context
description:
This fixes a bug whereby RStudio would _always_ load packrat into the current session, even if the project was not using packrat.

NOTE: I feel a little bit uncomfortable about this change; I wonder if instead we should have our own shims that check the 'packrat status' of a project without calling into packrat itself (which forces a packrat load)

title: Handle null or empty source file attributes gracefully
'Fuzzy' file finding -- search on subsequence
description:
(Note: leave for September branch)

This implements a 'fuzzy' finder for files through the `CTRL + .` file finder -- we now match on subsequences, rather than just the start of strings.

This allows, for example:

`rcle`

to match

`roclet-collate.R`

A scoring system is used to weigh matches as well, so the most likely intended results go on top.

title: Convert .Rproj file extension to associated UTI on 'Open Project'
description:
This fixes a bug wherein spotlight search failed within 'Open Project'... dialogs. If the file extension is `.Rproj`, we pass the associated Uniform Type Identifier, rather than the extension itself, so that search functions correctly.

NOTE: I took the UTI from a sample `.Rproj` file with e.g. `mdls devtools.Rproj`, which gave back:

```
<...>
kMDItemContentType             = "dyn.ah62d4rv4ge81e6dwr7za"
kMDItemContentTypeTree         = (
    "dyn.ah62d4rv4ge81e6dwr7za",
    "public.data",
    "public.item"
)
<...>
```

and so that is how I obtained the ID; however, I think there must be some better method of programmatically getting the UTI, but I haven't been able to figure it out. But we should double-check that it's consistent across different OS X versions.

EDIT: Using a [custom base32 decoder](http://play.golang.org/p/sW5oTXs4Bl), we can see that the string encodes:

```
?0=6:1=rproj
```

which is a compact way of storing from identifier information, alongside the extension (hence why it works)

title: Fix parentheses in shortcut check
description: On keyboard layouts without a meta key, the magrittr shortcut path was being triggered on CTRL + SHIFT + (any key) due to operator precedence / lack of parentheses in check.

title: Remap magrittr keyboard shortcut
description:
This PR remaps insertion of the magrittr pipe operator to META + SHIFT + M (CTRL + SHIFT + M on Windows). The key `M` should be mapped unambiguously across international keyboard layouts (double-checked with Danish, German, French)

I didn't place this in `Commands.java` because AFAICS that forces insertion only in the current source document (and can't be inserted in the console window). I imagine this is also why the `<-` insertion shortcut is not in there.

title: Add hotkey for magrittr's pipe
description: This inserts `%>%`, a new line, then reindents on `CMD + SHIFT + .` or `META + SHIFT + .`

title: Work around missing 'extern' on R_running_as_main_program for R-devel
description: This allows RStudio to successfully build with the R-devels missing an `extern` on `R_running_as_main_program`.

title: Fix some bugs in the outdenting for R code in non-R modes
description:
NOTE: Definitely leave this one for later as it touches the code indentation and may have broken things I haven't been able to test yet...

This fix has a few components:
1. In 'r_matching_brace_outdent', the autoOutdent method attempted to
   access the code model through 'this'. Unfortunately, 'codeModel' is not
   actually available through 'this' since the reference is bound before it
   ever gets to know about the code model. A simple fix here is to add
   the code model to those function signature. (from what I see, before, an
   exception would be thrown but silently swallowed up by its caller)
2. The 'checkOutdent' and 'autoOutdent' were not matching the signatures
   correctly. This is understandable since the signature in our
   RMatchingBraceOutdent diverged from that of Ace's MatchingBraceOutdent.
   This is now fixed.
3. Although I don't really know why, the way that the
   RMatchingBraceOutdent was mixed in to 'r.js' didn't seem to work (?), so
   I followed the pattern in the other files.

Ironically, the combination of the two bugs above made R code
indentation for closing '}' work fine, but broke it in other modes.

Ultimately, this fixes a bug where reindenting R code within an .Rmd,
.Rnw, or .cpp file would produce formatted e.g. like:

```
for (i in 1:10) {

    }
```

ie, the closing brace offset is now properly aligned in these files. It
(should) preserve indentation behaviour in vanilla R modes.

title: Show ShinyApps deployment dialog in preview window for Shiny docs/apps
description:
This change makes it possible to initiate a deployment to ShinyApps directly from the preview windows for Shiny docs and Shiny apps. 

The change works as follows:
- The ShinyApps singleton (which knows how to show the dialog and fire corresponding events) is now initialized in these specific satellite windows 
- The main frame is now passed (via JS callbacks) the output of the deployment dialog (chosen account, app name, etc.), which it uses to fire the same deployment initiation event fired by the dialog when it's running in the main frame.

title: Index more file types (.py, .sh, .sql, .Rprofile)
description:
(It looks like my editor is too aggressive about whitespace)

This branch adds `.py`, `.sh`, `.sql` and `.Rprofile` as MIME types -- this ensures, for example, that they are picked up in the `Go to File/Function` dialog `(CTRL + .)`

title: Improve ShinyApps deployment
description:
This change improves the ShinyApps deployment process, and prepares it for handling deployment of Shiny documents. There are two main changes here:
- The dialog now lists the files to be deployed.
- The deployment now takes place in a child process, with output streamed to a new console tab.

There are also a couple of changes under the hood:
- The code that creates a child R process, maintains its running state, accepts termination, etc. has been factored into a new class, `AsyncRProcess`. This class is used to manage the R processes for HTML preview, R Markdown, R Markdown template discovery, and Shiny application deployment. 
- It is now possible for any tab in the IDE to become busy, and temporarily uncloseable. To do this, the `WorkbenchTab` just needs to inherit from `ProvidesBusy`, and fire a `BusyEvent` when its busy state changes.

title: Clarify template creation UI
description:
Several people were confused by the template creation UI; this change attempts to make the experience less confusing:
1. The "create directory" checkbox has been removed; the template is now in full control of this option. 
2. If a template does not require a new directory (i.e. `create_dir` is unset or false), it is no longer necessary to give a location or name for the template before creating it; instead, the template's contents are read into an unsaved editor buffer (just like other new R Markdown documents) and no changes are made on disk. 
3. If a template does require a new directory, then the directory picker UI appears with explanatory text. 

Note that this implies that a template _must_ set `create_dir` if it contains more than `skeleton.Rmd`. Other heuristics are possible here (for instance, we could check for multiple files and override `create_dir` when they are present).

title: Preserve scroll positions in Shiny documents
description:
This change gives Shiny documents the same scroll preservation behavior as other R Markdown documents. It works as follows:
1. An independent script, `rsiframe.js`, broadcasts a frame's scroll position and anchors to its parent as they change, and accepts commands to change the scroll position and anchor.
2. RStudio injects `rsiframe.js` when running a Shiny document, using the `extra_dependencies` argument.  
3. When viewing a Shiny document, RStudio interacts with `rsiframe.js` instead of attempting to access the protected content of the document itself. 

Note that while this fixes scroll preservation, it does not fix slide navigation. We have some work to do there since the data we need to build the navigation needs to be built into a new client event (it is not available when the Shiny document starts since there hasn't yet been a completed render at that point).

title: Add IDE support for Shiny documents
description:
This change adds IDE support for Shiny documents. Rough overview:

Shiny documents are identified via a `runtime: shiny` key in their YAML front matter. They have the following special treatment in the editor UI:
- Knit becomes 'Run Document' (shortcut key is the same)
- The format options dialog no longer allows format switching

The same process that services regular R Markdown render now also handles Shiny documents. When run with a Shiny document, the process stays alive (and the console tab remains open for viewing output) while the Shiny app is running. As with regular Shiny applications, the lifetime of the process is tied to the Shiny document viewer window: closing the window will terminate the process, and vice-versa. 

When a document that contains Shiny application objects is rendered in a static R Markdown doc, the IDE picks up the warning string emitted and displays some UI that allows the user to re-render as a Shiny doc to see the dynamic content. It's also possible to see the static content, or to permanently mark the doc as a Shiny doc.

Two work items that were on the border (we can put these on master later if we think they're worthwhile):
- Preservation of anchors and scroll positions doesn't work in Shiny documents. There are two challenges involved:
  - Shiny documents have a different origin on the desktop, and so it's not possible to read or write their scroll position because of cross-site scripting rules. (This could be surmountable by implementing a back-channel method that uses native desktop code to read and write the positions)
  - Shiny documents are loaded asynchronously, so we don't know when the content is ready to have its scroll position adjusted. In the worst case here we could have Shiny post a message when it's ready (as we do for `disconnected`). 
- Debugging could be challenging because the code runs out of process. We discussed implementing a 'run for debug' option that runs it in process.

title: Discover and create documents from R Markdown templates
PDF.js refresh
description:
This change updates PDF.js to the latest version (tip as of 3/12/2014), and changes the way PDF.js is integrated to simplify future updates. Changes to the architecture include the following:
- PDF.js is now cloned directly from the Mozilla repo (rather than our own with Mozilla as an upstream repo).
- Rather than being reconstructed by GWT UiBinders and script injection, the PDF.js application and its dependencies are now served as static resources from the session resources directory, using a new request handler for `/pdf_js`. 
- Coupling to specific elements and methods in the PDF.js viewer (which are subject to change) is encapsulated in a new class, `PdfJsWindow`. This class also injects the appropriate event handlers and modifies the UI slightly to suit the RStudio use case.
- The `PDFViewer` class now serves as the interface between PDF.js and RStudio proper, and is responsible for maintaining the state of the viewer and handling events from both the viewer window and GWT.

title: Feature/rmd dialog asthetics
Simplify R Markdown creation experience and organize options
description:
This change removes the format options entirely from the New R Markdown dialog. Instead, the dialog now lists the available formats, with radio buttons to choose the default.

It also contains several improvements to the format options dialog:
- Formats are now grouped into tabs, with the goal of making them easier to find and eliminating the need for scrollbars for formats with many options.
- Several new format options (mostly advanced ones) have been exposed, and UI widgets to represent those options have been added.

title: Feature/advanced rmd options
Add integration with the 'rmarkdown' package
description:
This change adds hooks on the UI and server to support the rmarkdown package. In particular:
- The **Knit** command now uses rmarkdown to render the document, if the document is an R Markdown file and the rmarkdown package is installed.
- New code on the server runs the render in a separate R process, and a new console tab in the client shows the output of the process as it runs. 
- A new satellite window shows the render output (limited to HTML for now, with PDF as supported inline by the browser), modified to use the rmarkdown-supplied version of the MathJax library if necessary.

title: ShinyApps UI integration
description:
This change adds UI support for the ShinyApps package, if it's installed. The following commands are supported via a new ShinyApps menu under Tools when a Shiny file is open: 
- _Deploy App_: Also available on global toolbar. Shows existing deployments of current directory, and allows the user to re-deploy over any existing deployment or create a new deployment. Largely UI sugar to form a `deployApp` command.
- _Terminate App_: Terminates the application deployed from the current directory, if one is running. When we support Configure I expect this will look more like a task-manager (i.e. a full list of all apps from all accounts with configure/terminate invokable on any app); for now it relies on context. 
- _Manage Accounts_: Always available. Connects and/or disconnects accounts.

For now I've re-used an icon for deploy, but we should consider making a new one for this and possibly the other commands (esp. if ShinyApps is going to get logo/branding assets).

title: Improve top-level debugging experience
description:
This change alters the way top-level debugging works. The change has the following user-facing benefits:
- Stepping at the top level now works exactly like stepping through a function--loop bodies are stepped through one iteration at a time, etc. This was a common request on the support forum and the motivation for the work.
- The interface for top-level debugging now matches exactly with the interface for function debugging; the console experience is identical (it's a standard R environment browser at which one can use 'n', 'c', etc.)
- The file being sourced appears on the callstack, so it is possible to see e.g. the line from which an error arises.
- Breakpoints can now be set _within_ top-level sub-expressions, such as loops or anonymous functions. It was previously only possible to set breakpoints on the outermost expressions in the file.
- Future improvements to the function debugging experience (added by R core or ourselves) will carry over to top-level debugging without additional engineering work.

Previously, top-level debugging worked by having the server and the client step through each of the top-level expressions in the file together (breaking up the `parse` and `eval` steps). After each expression was evaluated, the client and server stopped to see whether a breakpoint had been hit or breakpoints needed to be injected. 

This approach works differently. The core of the work is in `makeSourceEquivalentFunction`, and works roughly as follows:
1. The file is parsed into an expression tree.
2. The expressions are wrapped into a function that evaluates them in the global environment.
3. Source references are created and copied into the function so that the parsed expressions map seamlessly back into the file being sourced.
4. Breakpoints (top-level and otherwise) are injected into the function. (This uses the server knowledge of breakpoints originally introduced to implement Shiny breakpoints.)
5. The function is executed.

This is not a simple operation, but once performed, it significantly reduces the amount of bookkeeping and state that needs to be maintained during top-level debugging; there is a little special treatment of the source-equivalent function, but the debugger is no longer required to have a special "top-level debugging" state.

Finally, this is all done synchronously on the server without client interaction; previously, `debugSource` needed to run at the console and be seen by the IDE to work effectively. This puts into place the architecture we will need to make `debugSource` a drop-in replacement for `source` if we decide to do that work.

title: allow sub-sections within scope tree; bold text in popup
description:
This PR seeks to allow for sub-sections in the scope tree, and also bolds their text in the scope tree display:

![screen shot 2015-05-27 at 6 22 08 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/7850952/5a5b2d44-049d-11e5-9d79-1b3430157864.png)

More globally, I think the display of the scope tree could use an overhaul. What do you think about prefixing each entry with the associated icon as well? (This might be too heavy-weight as well, but I feel like we need a bit more visual 'stuff' to separate sections from functions etc.)

title: provide file-local mechanism for controlling linter
description:
There were a couple requests for this based on the initial preview release containing diagnostics, so I thought I would go ahead and put in the scaffolding for this.

This PR allows for file-local settings to be applied to the linter -- currently, only `style` is recognized.

The goal is to allow a syntax like e.g.

``` R
#> style: false

if(1){}   ## doesn't complain about style warnings now
```

to control various settings in the linter. It'd be good to hear some ideas for different options we could specify; e.g. I think it would be useful to have something like (open to better names):

```
style: true/false
syntax: true/false
diagnostics: syntax/core/all
```

Thoughts? I'd really like some version of this to be part of v0.99 just so that even for users who opt into the 'heavier' diagnostics, they have a simple file-local mechanism for adjusting if desired.

We could also add something like `suppress: [foo, bar, baz]`, to allow users to suppress various warnings for symbols with some names.

title: Allow successful compilation with libc++ (C++11) / boost 1.58
description:
@howarthjw, can you confirm that this branch builds with the updated `libc++` / Boost 1.58? I imagine your motivation is that you want RStudio added to the `fink` project -- is that correct?

@jjallaire, do you think this trimmed down PR would be okay to merge, or would you prefer not? (Eg. if the motivation here was that a version of RStudio might be released built against an untested toolchain, should we prefer to avoid that?)

title: Update keyboard.htm
description: Updating since Ctrl+L is actually the correct command for clearing the console in OS X RStudio

title: reduce staggering in help display
description:
This improves the completion display by removing the staggering in argument help.

Before:

![screen shot 2015-04-24 at 2 06 37 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/7328862/c2775756-ea8d-11e4-97c8-3003663f9a93.png)

After:

![screen shot 2015-04-24 at 2 25 40 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/7328868/cebbf684-ea8d-11e4-85ab-2862c5cf0d61.png)

title: enable intra-file navigation with F2
indentation heuristics to detect statement-level indentation
description:
This PR fixes a minor indentation issue where single-level indentation (without assignment operators) wouldn't be respected; e.g. previously indentation produced this:

```
x <- 1
    y
|
```

Now, the cursor is appropriately indented to match the indentation of `y`.

title: allow JSON as text file type
description: This allows e.g. `file.edit("test.json")` to work; currently, the IDE disallows editing of JSON files (as it believes they are binary files)

title: Ensure 'defined but not used' warnings only displayed on 'explicit' actions
description: This ensures the background lint task does not show 'defined but not used' warnings, to help avoid showing false positives while the user is working.

title: Diagnostics refinements
description:
NOTE: not ready for merge, but getting close + worth looking at the overall implementation. There's still a lot of cleanup required...

This PR brings a large number of refinements to the diagnostics engine. The most noteworthy change here is the growth of the asynchronously built completions database, to now encompass more general package + function information (that we can use to determine whether a particular function performs NSE, and so on).

To handle this, we now have the classes `PackageInformation`, `FunctionInformation` and `FormalsInformation` that we use, and populate, from the various 'sources' of code, whether it's from the source document or from the search path itself.

The net result is that, for example, with this code:

```
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, cyl))
```

The diagnostics framework can use that database to figure out that `aes` performs non-standard evaluation, even without having the load the `ggplot2` namespace in that current session.

title: improve shiny function inference
description:
This PR improves how we detect whether a particular function is a Shiny 'input' or 'output' function in a couple ways.
1. We assume that a function is a shiny 'input' function if it has a formal named 'inputId', and
2. We assume that a function is a shiny 'output' function if it has a formal named 'outputId'.

This, presumedly, allows both `shiny` and companion add-on packages (that might generate their own inputs) to work as well, presuming they follow this formula.

We also check our completion database, in the case that shiny is not loaded, to see if we have it within there -- if we do, then we can still provide completions (even if shiny is not loaded / attached).

cc @jcheng5 -- do you think the aforementioned method is appropriate enough for guessing whether something is a shiny input/output function?

title: safely get function body
description: This PR avoids using the `BODY_EXPR` macro, and instead goes through R to get the function body.

title: Provide a mechanism for getting project-level diagnostics
description:
This PR provides `.rs.lintProject()` as an (internal) entry-point for linting all R files within a package and displaying the source marker output. For example, here's what I see on linting `packrat`:

![screen shot 2015-04-06 at 4 18 04 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/7014334/88d28476-dc78-11e4-8f22-90b9fd784b5e.png)

I think this is the 'minimal' bit of work we should put in for project linting (we may want to wire up a button somewhere to perform this action as well; perhaps in the `Build` tools or something to that effect)

title: Improve internal match.call; provide optimizations for hot code paths

title: avoid evaluation (and copying) of data in completion
description:
A user reported that completions were slow following `$` for large data.frames, e.g. `diamonds$`. This PR fixes that.

Outline: for a large object, the call

```
call("$", object, name)
```

will force a copy of `object` (and `name`, but that is less important), which can be prohibitively expensive for large datasets. This PR fixes this by instead passing a quoted symbol, rather than 'the real object', to ensure that we don't force a copy of the data when getting completions.

title: refine formula completions
description:
This PR refines the previous formula completions PR by:

Ensuring that formula completions are made available within an explicit `formula =` argument, as in

```

```

and, expanding the scope whereby we infer that a particular function is requesting 'argument' completions, so that e.g.

```
lm(data = mtcars, formula = mpg ~ cyl + |
```

will still produce completions from the names of `mtcars`. (Previously, this only worked when `formula` was an unnamed, or positionally matched, argument)

title: Minor tweaks to R mode indentation
description:
This PR further refines indentation in R modes, by conditionally indenting on assignment operators when appropriate.

Briefly, the indentation code works as follows:
1. Find an opening `[`, `(`, or `{` to provide for indentation.
2. If we find a `(` or `[`, we can use that for indentation (re-using pre-existing indentation code),
3. If we find a `{`, then we backtrack and attempt to first indent on an assignment operator (`=`, `<-`) first; otherwise, we indent based on the found `{` (plus indentation).

I also added some new tests to the R auto-indent and we now pass on all tests.

One of the main 'features' in this PR -- if we choose to vertically align, then we indent:

``` R
if (a &&
    b &&
    c)
```

and

``` R
plot(x = x +
         1,
     y = y +
         2
)
```

; ie, we can better discriminate on what is providing the 'scope' for a current expression.

title: Audit + clean up token walking code in the R code model
description:
This is an attempt to audit + clean up some of the token walking code we have in the R code model.

Quick outline -- there are a small number of 'very hot' code paths which other functions rely on. These are member functions of the `TokenCursor` object.
1. `moveToPreviousToken()`
2. `moveToNextToken()`
3. `bwdToMatchingToken()`
4. `fwdToMatchingToken()`

On success, they move the token cursor as named and return `true`; on failure they don't touch the token cursor and return `false`.

Most other functions are built on top of these 4 in the form of e.g. `while (cursor.moveToPreviousToken())`, so it is essential that they stop either at the start, or end, of the document.

The pre-existing code was a bit cluttered, so I've re-written and commented my steps here and I think it should at least be a step in the right direction.

@jmcphers, can we do a quick review of this?

title: fix r completions in cpp mode
description:
Completions inside of R chunks in C++ mode, e.g.

```
/*** R

*/
```

were broken in C++ mode -- there, we were erroneously grabbing the C++ code model, rather than the R code model, and attempting to use that for completions. We now ensure that anything using the R completion frameworks grabs the R code model, rather than the 'primary' code model.

Somewhere along the line (e.g. if we plan on adding any more code models, or more embedded modes) we should consider making `CodeModel` an abstract class with e.g. `RCodeModel`, `CppCodeModel` extending those.

title: Add a 'fuzzy file search' widget
description:
Not ready for merge, but ready for discussion -- @jjallaire, maybe we can chat on Monday?

![file-search](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5232998/9ae2ea30-7719-11e4-888e-8928f0c1b241.gif)

This PR adds a file search widget that can (currently) be used as a more powerful method of obtaining filename completions. The general idea:
1. The user hits `CMD + SHIFT + P` to pop up the search widget,
2. The client gets all files available within the current project from the server,
3. The client narrows and displays the top ~20 matching results based on their query, using fuzzy matching,
4. The user can click or select a file entry to insert that into the source editor.

An obvious problem we see currently with e.g. RStudio is that long files will trail off-screen, but the fact that this works speedily even with RStudio itself means it should be useful for other projects as well.

The main reason I have this as a separate widget rather than as part of the built-in completion framework -- the current completion UI attempts to display _all_ available completions, so the user can scroll and whatnot as necessary. This widget is more restricted in that it _only_ displays the top 20 matches, and the onus is on the user to type a narrow enough query to identify the file they want (or at least narrow to 20 candidates). This allows us to effectively display and narrow a larger set of candidate completions.

Let me know if you think this would be useful, and have any other ideas for e.g. display, UI, and so on.

3. Respect the 'show signature tips' option.
4. Don't let event propagate on escape when sigtip is showing (this ensures that e.g. if the sigtip is showing in the console and we hit escape, we dismiss the tip without clearing the console)

title: Signature tooltip positioning and anchoring
description:
NOTE: Not ready for merge -- this is more a 'proof of concept' of an idea I had re: automatically updating the signature tooltip. @jjallaire, let me know if you think this looks work exploring -- if so, I think it will be the last major autocompletion feature for this initial push.

In this PR, I introduce lazy tracking for the signature tooltip -- as the cursor is moved around, the signature tooltip is updated (if necessary) to represent the function scope the cursor currently lies in. The signature tooltip is placed above the associated function. See:

![sigtip-tracking](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5210594/a7cb5e62-7584-11e4-97fa-fcb229fdaa92.gif)

Implementation summary: we put the logic that finds the current function 'scope' in a timer. We reset and reschedule that timer on every event, so that the event is only actually run if the user pauses for a pre-set amount of time. To find the function scope, we use the tokens to find the opening parenthesis establishing the current 'argument' scope and produce a tooltip from there.

This PR also brings in the anchored selection work in the Cpp completion tooltip, whereby moving the cursor outside of an anchored selection will close the tooltip.

description:
### Intent

- Fixes #6524

Since RStudio 1.2 we've been showing the wrong symbol for the <kbd>Return</kbd> key in the Mac desktop IDE's menus. We were showing the symbol for <kbd>Enter</kbd>, instead.

### Approach

title: Disable virtual scrolling when screen reader mode toggled on
description:
### Intent
- Fixes #7788

When virtual scrolling feature was added, it broke the "Focus Console Output" command, which is used by screen-reader users to quickly get focus on and read console output. It broke it whether or not the virtual scrolling feature was enabled.

### Approach

Undid the change that was breaking "Focus Console Output" when virtual scrolling was disabled.

When user toggles on screen reader mode, we now disable the virtual scrolling mode, as the way it dynamically structures the HTML presents potential problems to screen reader users (including breaking the focus output command).

Finally, if screen reader mode is on and virtual scrolling also happens to be on, give a live announcement warning when an attempt is made to use the unusable "Focus Console Output" command.

### QA Notes

- Start screen reader and start RStudio Server
- Turn on screen reader mode if not already on
- Generate a bit of console output, e.g. `cat("one\ntwo\n")`
- Try to use the "Focus Console Output" command when (1) virtual scrolling is enabled (Global Options / Console / Limit console display to a subset...) and (2) when it is disabled.
    - When virtual scrolling is disabled, focus should be moved to the console output and you can navigate it with screen reader commands as you could in RStudio 1.3.
    - When virtual scrolling is enabled, you should get a warning announcement about the focus console output command not being available when virtual scrolling is enabled.
- Now, turn off screen reader support (RStudio restarts). Turn on virtual scrolling if it happens to be off. Now turn screen reader mode back on (RStudio restarts) then confirm that virtual scrolling has been turned off.

title: Only close current main menu level when hitting ESC key
description:
### Intent

- Fixes #6327
- Makes RStudio Server main menu behave more like a Windows desktop application main menu

### Approach

- Required adding a custom option in GWT's MenuBar class, see https://github.com/rstudio/gwt/pull/6
- This new behavior is off by default (opt-in) and only using it on the main menu
- Removed code that deselected the top-level menu button (e.g. "File") when closing it's popup; this was code from initial RStudio commit in 2010 and was working around an issue in older version of GWT and I could not find a case where it is still necessary

### QA Notes

- On RStudio Server, use the main menu via both keyboard shortcuts (e.g. <kbd>Alt+Shift+F</kbd> on Windows/Linux or <kbd>Ctrl+Opt+F</kbd> on Mac, move around with arrows, then hit ESC key
- The current menu level should then close, selecting the parent menu
- Try this in cases where a menu has submenus, too
- Try use ESC key right after invoking menu with the shortcut (before you use any arrow keys); ESC in that case should just collapse the submenu, leaving the menu item (e.g. File) itself selected; if you hit ESC a second time, when the submenu is already hidden, THEN the menu item itself should lose selection
- Note that the existing problem of where focus goes after you close the entire menu via ESC is covered by a separate issue, #6197
- Also do some checking around behaviors where the menu is displayed, and you click elsewhere in the RStudio UI with the mouse; make sure the menus close and are no longer showing as selected (e.g. the "File" button isn't highlighted)
- Only RStudio Server is impacted by these code changes, not desktop

title: fix opening external files on Big Sur with spaces in filename or path
description:
### Intent

- RStudio fails to open external files with spaces in their filesnames and/or paths (PDFs, Word Docs, etc.) when clicked on in the Files pane on RStudio Desktop running on Big Sur
- Fixes #8506

### Approach

- The fix was to have Mac desktop use the same code as other desktop platforms for opening files; namely, `QDesktopServices::openUrl()`
- This changes how PDFs are opening; instead of forcing them to always use Preview, they will now use whatever is registered in the system (e.g. Acrobat); there was a comment about problems with Acrobat 10, but Acrobat 10 is from 2010 and current version of Acrobat works fine

More details:

- On Mac desktop only, when opening an external file, RStudio has been creating a process to run "open filename"; other desktop platforms instead use QDesktopServices::openUrl()
- Based on comments, the reason was to work around a problem with Acrobat 10 crashing when it was registered as PDF file app, so the code was forcing use of Preview
- On Big Sur only, for reasons I couldn't quite figure out, this failed if there were spaces in the path or filename and the files wouldn't open (any files including Word Docs, etc., not just PDFs)
- I tried various combinations of escaping the path, including wrapping in single quote, double quotes, using URL encoding of the spaces (%20), putting a backslash before the spaces, and none of these helped

### QA Notes

- macOS desktop-specific fix, no code changes for Server or desktop for Linux or Windows
- Primarily, try opening various files from the Files pane including files in folders with spaces in the name, and files with spaces in their filenames
- For files that RStudio doesn't support editing, the externally registered program should open
- Test on both Big Sur, and on down-level macOS (I did sanity test on Big Sur 11.0.1 and most recent Catalina)
- Try with and without Adobe Acrobat installed (ideally with some older versions if you can track them down)

title: Fix default folder for per-user install on WIndows
description:
### Intent

- Fixes #8598
- On Windows, a non-elevated (per-user) install can be triggered via group policy or by running the installer as follows:

`cmd.exe /c "set __COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker && RStudio-1.4.1100.exe"`

- The installer chooses user's documents folder as the default location; this goes against modern Windows recommendation for a per-user install (and causes problems with sync clients)

### Approach

- Use the %LocalAppData%\Programs folder as the default for a per-user install

### QA Notes

- On a Windows machine without an existing RStudio install, run the installer as shown above to trigger a per-user install
- The default folder should now be in user's %appdata%\Local\Programs folder, not in Documents
- Note to uninstall a per-user install performed this way, you must run the uninstall.exe using the same trick or it will mess up and leave a phantom entry in add-remove programs; this wouldn't happen on a system where group policy was used to force this behavior
- Also try a regular install to ensure an elevated (all-users) install goes to program files as before

title: Fix Electron desktop on Windows (blank window)
description:
### Intent

Launching dev build of Electron on MS-Windows was giving a blank screen, with exceptions being thrown by GWT indicating the desktop hooks are undefined.

### Approach

Preload code assumed that argument added via `additionalArguments` mechanism when creating `BrowserWindow` was guaranteed to be last item in `process.argv`; it was not on Windows. Webpack was appending `/prefetch:1`, and the code then tried to use this as the list of apiKeys to attach, thus attaching none of them.

Fixed by using a prefix `--apiKeys=` to identify this argument, and looking for that instead of assuming the position.

### Automated Tests

Added unit test for new routine `firstStartingWith`.

### QA Notes

Can now launch Electron IDE on Windows and see... the IDE.

title: Fix Close All Except Current with unsaved files
description:
### Intent

Fixes #8295 

Certain combinations of opening files with "dirty" files (requiring a prompt to save) prevent `Close All Except Current` from closing all columns. 

### Approach

Previously we set the active editor to keep track of the editor to leave open and reset it when a change was triggered by the prompt to save other editors. We were only resetting the variable tracking the active editor and not which editor was actually active in `DocTabLayoutPanel`. This fix selects the active editor when it is set manually.

There was also an issue with multiple columns that left all the tabs open when the current editor was in the left most column due to columns being removed while iterating the column list. We now iterate over the list of column names rather than the columns themselves to make sure we reach each one while closing tabs. This is a marginally slower approach but shouldn't be noticeable since the column list size should always be small (currently always less than 5).

### QA Notes

There are good examples in #8295 but we also need to make sure things work as expected with multiple columns open.

description:
### Intent

When working on RStudio Electron on an M1 Mac, the app will fail to launch if you generate the native code build using no explicit RSTUDIO_TARGET, e.g.:

`cmake ../cpp`

This fails because the config here becomes RSTUDIO_DEVELOPMENT but doesn't include RSTUDIO_DESKTOP (by design on an M1 Mac only), and the required `rdesktop-dev.conf` file is thus not generated.

It does work if you generate with `-DRSTUDIO_TARGET=Electron` but shouldn't really need to do that, just like you don't when working on Qt desktop.

Eventually, on Mac, we'll automatically set RSTUDIO_ELECTRON as the target when none is specified, but not ready for that just yet.

### Implementation

title: Use native M1 Java if available when building on M1 Mac
description:
### Intent

We use Intel Java even when building on M1. Noticed while working on Electron build and documenting [how to setup a dev machine on M1 Mac](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/M1-Mac-Dev-Machine-Setup).

This works, but is slower than a native M1 Java when building GWT. On my M1 Mini, took 11 minutes for a full GWT build with Intel, down to 7 minutes with the M1 Java. Only tried once so not particularly scientific.

Homebrew doesn't install an M1 JDK, nor is it available (for JDK8 or 11, at least), directly via https://adoptium.net/ (formerly https://adoptopenjdk.net/). See also: https://github.com/AdoptOpenJDK/homebrew-openjdk/issues/530

### Approach

Update make-package to prefer the `zulu-11` JDK if installed, otherwise use what it's currently using. Note that M1 Mac can use the M1 Java even when building for Intel (GWT build output is JavaScript, not native code).

Not bothering to install this M1 JDK on the actual build machines for now. Saving a few more minutes would be nice but don't want to mess with it right now. Just speeding up dev workflow.

### Automated Tests

None, dev / build tweak.

title: Add i18n for menu headings and commands
description:
### Intent

This PR enables i18n for the menu headings and command headings/descriptions that are defined in the `Commands.cmd.xml` file.  Shortcuts in that file have not been addressed here.

Only English is generated at this time, so no end-user visible changes should be noticed.

> This was originally submitted as an external PR here: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/9507
> 
> Getting it staged for merge was proving tricky, so agreed to take ownership of final tweaks and moved the changes onto this local branch instead of a fork.

### GWT Dev Workflow Changes (IMPORTANT: IDE DEVS MUST READ)

If you have not modified `Commands.cmd.xml` then nothing changes. You can build GWT using any of the usual `ant` commands (`draft`, `devmode`, `desktop`, or just plain `ant`).

If you change `Commands.cmd.xml` in any way, including whitespace, then `ant` will trigger the localization scripts and regenerate the support files. These modified files must be committed with modified `Command.cmd.xml`. Failure to do this will break the build.

The quickest way to ensure you've done this is `ant generate-i18n`. This will ensure the loc files match the current Commands.cmd.xml without the overhead of a full GWT build.

The localization scripts are written in Python (v3 required), and require some packages. These are specified in `rstudio/src/gwt/tools/i18n-helpers/commands.cmd.xml/requirements.txt`. These can be installed using `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

On Windows, I had to follow steps here to install the requirements (i.e. I had to download and install prebuilt binary): https://stackoverflow.com/questions/33785755/getting-could-not-find-function-xmlcheckversion-in-library-libxml2-is-libxml2

### Implementation Details

The need to run the localization scripts is gated on an MD5 checksum of `Commands.cmd.xml`. It is generated by `ant` and stored in `Commands.cmd.xml.MD5`. If the checksum matches, then the localization scripts will not execute.

If working on a Windows machine, the Commands.cmd.xml file will be checked out with Linux LF line-endings, not CR/LF. Otherwise the checksum won't match. This is configured via a .gitattributes file included in this PR.

#### Full Implementation Details

See original notes in https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/9507 for implementation details, as well as how to try out the localization process.

### Automated Tests

No automated tests were added.

### QA Notes

For now, just verify that the English UI is functioning normally (menus should look the same as before).

title: Unsync source column count
description:
### Intent

Closes #8107 

Adding or removing a column should not affect other instances of RStudio the user is running. Previously any changes made to the `additional_column_count` in `global-prefs.json` were made immediately, but now changes are only made on startup and when the IDE is writing to the preference file. This allows the column state to be saved between sessions, while preventing columns being added/removed in an active session without user prompt.

### Approach

I removed the `panes` user preference handler that was syncing the two instances. Now the column count is only updated when requested by the user in that session.

### QA Notes

If the user ends a session with three columns, their next session should start with three columns. However, when running two instances of RStudio, the column counts should not be in sync.

Original ticket has good repo notes.

title: use graphics device backend type when set, to allow for ragg rendering of NB plot
description:
### Intent

Address the issue in #9931. 

```
plot(1, main = "あいう ABC", xlab = "あいう ABC")
```
should be able to render properly with Japanese characters when ragg is the graphics device, whether the plot is being rendered in the console or inline as a notebook chunk.

### Approach

`.rs.createNotebookGraphicsDevice` function should respect and pass along the graphics device type, if it has been set. We can read it in directly from `getOption("RStudioGD.backend")`. 

The user can set the default device by either adding `options(RStudioGD.backend='ragg')` to their .Rprofile, or in the IDE by going to Tools > Global Options > Graphics and selecting AGG under Backend (after installing `ragg`). 

If the device has been set in the knitr chunk options, it will render using that device when knit, but to render properly inline, the user must set the RStudio graphics device backend explicitly.
