title: Asynchronous library completions for search path
description:
Not quite ready for merge -- @jjallaire, I'll need your help to fill in a few missing pieces + verify I am doing some mutex locking safely / sanely. I still need to fill in some bits on the R side + later fix merge conflicts.

This PR brings asynchronous completions for search path items from `library` calls. The idea is this:
1. We scan the source document for `library`, `require` calls,
2. We collect those package names,
3. We launch an R process that gets the namespace exports from those packages,
4. We send the results back as JSON (which we then decode appropriately),
5. We then store all completions on the server, and provide them for autocompletion lookups.

To facilitate this, the `RSourceIndex` class now has a (singleton) static member `completions_`, which maps package names to completion items. The `AsyncRCompletions` is the driving class (it inherits from `AsyncRProcess`) and makes the necessary R call to generate completions. For simplicity, we try to ensure that only one async completions R process is running at a time, but make it possible to kick off new updates as frequently as necessary.

Basically, we treat the `AsyncRCompletions` class as a single singleton process, which attempts to make (thread-safe) updates to the `completions_` static member of `RSourceIndex`.

Note that this currently does not work for unsaved documents -- I was under the impression that the document ID would be sufficient for locating the server-side cache of unsaved documents but it appears I was incorrect or am missing some pieces.

Main question for now -- when would it be appropriate to attempt an update of the completions index?

It also appears that I'll need to do something specifically to handle suspend + resume; it seems like some insidious / bad things can happen there, especially if there is an async process running while we suspend.

title: enable 'generic' magrittr pipe completions
description:
This PR allows us to produce autocompletions for 'generic' piped functions, e.g.

```
(1:10) %>% rnorm(|
```

The logic is as such:
1. The `getAutocompletionContext` function understands how to find the evaluation context previous to the cursor, so it would find in this case `(1:10) %>% rnorm`. This gets passed down as the first element of `string`, and also is similarly assigned for the `functionCallString`.
2. We strip out everything at and previous to a `pipe` to get the actual function name we want completions for.
3. We let the pre-existing logic run as is.

We also add some special casing for `group_by(foo, |`, so that names from `foo` are completed.

title: fix for token cursor creation
Consolidate token cursor functionality
description: Previously, there was a split in the token cursors -- an internal version was defined for the R code model, and a separate set was defined for the C++ code model. This PR unifies the implementations by moving the relevant logic from the token cursor defined in the R code model into the 'base' token cursor class, and uses that.

title: default true for strip trailing whitespace; add newline
initial work on own package skeleton
description:
NOTE: not ready for merge; ready for comments.

This implements a trimmed-down version of `package.skeleton()` which creates a package which should pass `R CMD check`.

There are a couple things we have to make a decision on:

```
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... WARNING
Non-standard license specification:
  What license is it under?
Standardizable: FALSE
```

Do we want a default license?

```
* checking for missing documentation entries ... WARNING
Undocumented code objects:
  ‘hello’
```

Should we include an example `.Rd` file for our automatic 'hello_world' function? (Do we want a hello world function?) Any other tweaks we could make to the `DESCRIPTION` file -- e.g. respect any `devtools.*` options?

title: Make "variable" singular, where appropriate.
better handling of preproc statement indentation
description:
This PR does a few minor things:
1. Preprocessor lines are pushed to the start of line, so they don't have their own indent, and are skipped for the purposes of determining the indentation of other lines.
2. `default:` is properly aligned as with `case 'x':` statements (it had been left out)

title: fuzzy file searching within project
description:
NOTE: Not ready for merge, but ready for discussion. This work supersedes #235 by integrating the same functionality into the existing completion popup display.

![file-search](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5273923/c9006466-7a42-11e4-9bc0-997b50ac2099.gif)

To make this efficient, we re-work the completion display a little bit:
1. We display a maximum of 100 completions in the UI popup, and display a `Completion list is truncated` message below if there are too many to display, to ensure a fast UI response.
2. If there are too many completions (> 2000), then we do not even bother sorting the list, as this will be too slow. However, when it is not too large we use a priority queue to obtain a partial sort of the top 100 items.

There is still work to be done in handling the situation where the number of files is too large to produce completions for the whole subtree of a path; likely through using `listFiles`.

As an aside -- should we consider distinguishing files and directories in the popup icon?

title: respect assignment indentation
description:
This fixes an indentation bug noted by @hadley with e.g. this indentation:

``````
```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
```

  * XYZ

    ```{r}
    a <- 1
|
    ```
``````

This PR adds a new code path to the `getNextLineIndent` call -- if the 'regular' lookups fail, we fall back to finding the nearest assignment operator, and then using the indentation of the object being assigned to.

This also implies that indentation rules now operate like:

``` R
x <- 1
    y <- 2
    |
```

rather than aligning to the first column.

title: Remove duplicated completions on suggestion
More implicit acceptance of autocompletions
description:
This PR does two things:
1. We implicitly accept the selected completion if it's an identical match to the current token, and there are no other prefix matches.
2. We do a bit more work to wrangle hiding / showing of the help popup properly.
3. We dismiss the popup on `<modifier> + ENTER`, just in case the popup showed in between the time the user has typed some characters, and press 'CMD + ENTER', for example.

title: delay auto-popup; don't show if token matches only possible completion
description:
This PR tweaks the presentation of automatic popups a bit. We use a single timer that is re-scheduled and cancelled as necessary, and if we see more than 400ms of inactivity from the user then we go ahead with an auto-popup.

We also forego displaying the completion list if there is only one available completion and the token matches that exactly.

title: check for preceding whitespace on insertion
description: This makes the `%>%` and `<-` insertion rules a bit smarter about whitespace -- we only insert a preceding space if there isn't already whitespace before the cursor, or if the cursor is not at the start of the line.

title: don't insert newline with magrittr pipe
fix bug where help might display in corner
description:
This fixed a bug that might cause the help to display in the top left corner of the screen.

As part of a 'hack' to handle backspace in the completion list, we display the popup off-screen, but allow the current 'completion context' to remain active. This ensures that the current set of completions can be displayed if you mistype a token and later hit backspace.

We now double-check that the completion list is actually on-screen before displaying help.

title: Add DataTables-based viewer for tabular data
description:
This change implements a new viewer for tabular data (`data.frame` and friends). The viewer takes the place of the existing data viewer. It's built on the popular [DataTables](http://datatables.net/) library.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/470418/5309164/cd6c8244-7bd4-11e4-9dd3-2af5e162787a.png)

DataTables provides virtualized scrolling of large datasets, fixed headers with sort UI, and maintenance of view state, but all of the interesting data-related work (sorting, filtering, etc.) happens in R. The DataTables client bundles the client state and sends it to the server, which returns the slice of visible rows requested.

(Not ready for merge; needs review)

title: don't auto-popup following '(' in comment
description: This fixes an issue where e.g. `#' @param data(` could trigger autocompletions.

title: Add a hotkey for vertically aligning consecutive assignments
description:
This PR adds a hotkey `(CMD|CTRL) + SHIFT + A` for automatically vertically aligning consecutive assignments within a selection.

![auto-align](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5240977/0ec4bf10-78c7-11e4-8278-2c956d66f5bb.gif)

This works by doing the following:
1. We identify ranges of consecutive lines containing one of the three assignment operators `<-`, `<<-` and `=` within the current selection,
2. We separate each line in the range into pieces `start`, `delimiter`, `end`,
3. We pad the start pieces with whitespace up to the largest 'start' piece,
4. Then add the delimiter (right-justified for multiple 'types' of delimiters in the same range),
5. Then add the end (potentially right-justified if all bits are numbers).

To avoid erroneously matching assignment operators in a string, e.g. `"this = that"`, we 'mask' strings on the line by replacing anything within quotes with the character `x`. However, we do not do anything special for multi-line strings.

title: update to gwt 2.7
'Insert parens' option + respect insert matching
description: This adds a UI pref controlling whether we insert parentheses following a function completion, and also ensures that the insertion behaviour respects the 'insert matching' pref for R and C++ modes.

title: Augmented completions for arguments, packages
description:
NOTE: Not ready for merge, but putting this up as a PR for now.

The sum of this PR: we now keep track of the current 'active' argument when completing functions, so that we can provide argument specific completions. Right now, we use it for:
- `"pkg"`, `"package"` -- package name completions.

This implies that we get better completions 'for free' in e.g. `browseVignettes`, `packageVersion`, and so on.

title: add 'set working dir as project dir' button
description:
This PR adds a small icon to the left of the Project button in the global toolbar that sets the current directory to the project directory.

![screen shot 2014-11-22 at 4 03 18 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5156117/1f732cb4-7261-11e4-90e8-e1e6db77d999.png)

The icon will be hidden if there is no active project. If we take this, we might want to use a different icon as well.

title: Disable auto-popup within strings
description:
This disables automatic popups within (single-line) strings.

Note that the `isEndOfLineInRStringState` is a trimmed version of `stripBalancedQuotes`, so we have some rough guarantees that the algorithm there is correct (we've been using it for a while in the IDE already)

title: Autocompletion for install.packages
description:
Note that I had already written the install.packages completions infrastructure code; this PR just wires that up to the pre-existing package cache.

You should double-check that I am properly handling mutexes and whatnot on the (singleton) packages cache -- all calls to the cache are locked through a mutex so I do believe that it should be safe, but let me know if you think I missed anything.

title: R completion help + signature tooltip
description:
This PR modifies the help popup, and brings in a signature tooltip, as part of the autocompletions.

![popup](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5150232/5b1e3966-7185-11e4-8a6e-1c76536d93e5.gif)

Main bits to notice:
1. The completion list and help are now separate popups, and resize independently (although they align at the top).
2. The signature tooltip stays on-screen while within the function call -- we track paren insertion to determine when the user has left the function call (or escape on mouse clicks, `{`, etc.)

@jjallaire, you mentioned that you would be willing to take this work and then refactor it into a common display for the C++ popup -- any other comments re: styling / display here?

title: provide file completions in '[...](|)' for markdown documents
description: This provides completions for links in R Markdown documents. Links are generated relative to the directory of the R Markdown file (and no completions are generated if the file has not yet been saved).

title: don't allow width collapsing in completion popup
description:
This fixes a visual 'bug' where the left cell of the popup would collapse when the window width was too small, producing a display like:

![screen shot 2014-11-22 at 4 00 27 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/5156111/b86ef390-7260-11e4-9a74-c2a433b789c4.png)

We set the `min-width` property to ensure that table cell resizing rules don't override our width setting.

title: Push data directly to clipboard on Safari (for linewise copy bug in 8)
description: Safari 8.0 has a bug wherein the text placed on the clipboard when copying or cutting from a TEXTAREA may include an extra newline if the text copied ends with a newline. This change works around that bug by (for Safari only) pushing data to the clipboard directly instead of relying on the browser to copy data placed into a TEXTAREA.

title: Boost 1.56
description:
In Boost 1.56 a new boost module `core` was introduced.[1] This broke usage of `core::`. With this fix the ambiguous naming is avoided. I assume it is just a temporary fix until someone brings up a smarter solution not modifying that many files.

I tested RStudio in desktop mode build as release. Since this fix only contains some renaming `namespace core` to `namespace rstudiocore` and `core::` to `rstudiocore::` it should be downward compatible. Renaming was just the easiest way of not breaking something along the way.

[1] http://www.boost.org/users/history/version_1_56_0.html

title: wire in completions for reference classes
description: This gives us completions on `$` and `@` for reference classes and reference object generators.

title: don't let R completion manager preview keypress when not in R mode
description:
This forces the RCompletionManager to verify that the cursor is in R mode before attempting to produce automatic R completion popups.

Note that this just disables auto-popup in the 'tex' mode of `.Rnw` documents; the user can still explicitly request R completions outside of an R chunk. I haven't yet identified where the R cursor check is made for `.Rmd` files, since you cannot request R completions outside of an R chunk there.

title: better completion popup key handling
description: This fixes a bug whereby movement keys would 'get stuck' by the auto-popup mechanism when no completions were actually available. We alleviate this problem by only grabbing those key events and sending them to the completion popup if it actually has completion values.

title: limit number of evaluations when inferring completion type
description:
This fixes an undesired behaviour where `rsession` could lock up while attempting to evaluate a large number of items to infer completion types. We do two things:
1. We first limit the names we want to evaluate using fuzzy matching on the token (previously, we just evaluated all the potential names, then narrowed the list -- this should be more efficient),
2. We only perform evaluation to get types if we have less than 200 entries in the object (should be good enough 99.9% of the time).

I think we should do some similar throttling in the UI as well; e.g. don't do automatic popup completions if the completion list is over some size -- but allow the user to request it explicitly. Note that e.g. with 10000 completion items to display this will lock up the UI for a couple seconds, though.

title: Avoid comment insertion behaviour when popup showing
description:
This fixes a bug with the recent addition where completion of an Roxygen autocompletion would both complete the Roxygen tag, and also automatically go ahead and insert an Roxygen comment continuation.

It also fixes tab insertion (if the cursor is at `#' |`, then TAB should insert a literal tab rather than do completion -- we automatically pop up completions on `@` anyhow.)

title: continue comments on newline
description:
This implements an option re: continuation of comments related to the discussion we had with @hadley. With the option enabled, pressing enter when within a comment continues the comment, while pressing shift + enter exits the comment.

I'm thinking a bit about whether it would be suitable to add e.g. a little tooltip / popup that explains the functionality in the settings screen as well.

title: remove alternating handler
description:
This one seems a bit bizarre -- I am not sure why we would have a keydown handler that ignores half of the events, but...

The rationale for this: in the fuzzy finder (CTRL + .), only half of the up events were 'eaten' -- see https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/master/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/codesearch/CodeSearch.java#L174-L191 -- which implies that, half the time, pressing up would in fact allow the up command to go back to the text box and hence move the cursor from the end to the start.

This probably needs a more targetted fix, though -- any idea why we want to ignore half of the keydown events here?

title: shift+enter for searching backwards in find-replace
navigate to file:row:column with fuzzy file finder
description:
This adds a feature whereby users can navigate to specific rows / columns of a file in the 'fuzzy finder' using e.g.

```
<query>:<row>:<column>
```

title: More work for R autocompletions
description:
There's currently a lot stuffed into this PR -- and one thing I'd like to sort out before we merge is how far we want to take the evaluation of e.g. generic expressions (function calls) for completions.

Summary of new bits in this PR:
1. We record a few more completion types, mainly relating to S4 and R5 classes.
2. We parse the `Slots` help field so that we can display help for e.g. S4 classes, or occasionally (constructor) S4 functions where arguments are left undefined in lieu of documentation provided for a slot of the same name.
3. We have a generic utility for getting an appropriate help topic from an object -- this ensures that e.g. `x$foo <- dir`, `x$foo` gives help for `dir`. We do this by finding the namespace the function was defined in, looking for the object name in that namespace with the same definition, and then getting help based on that object name + package.
4. We parse the description lists in options, so we get help popups on the autocompletion results in e.g. `options()`.
5. Fuzzy narrowing for completion results -- an initial set of completions popped up are based on prefix-matching, but one can now narrow the set of completion results using the 'fuzzy' matching mechanism.

There are also a couple minor fixes re: C++ indentation, completion popup presentation.

title: Tweaks to the help RPC call
description:
This modifies the `get_help` RPC call to be more restrictive on when help is shown. It should help to eliminate 'spurious' help from e.g. variables named identically to functions, and so on.

Currently, we support help for functions, function arguments, and packages -- in the future, we could imagine adding support for data sets as well.

Note that I've changed the `QualifiedName` parameter `pkgName` to `source`, which is now more appropriate given that `QualifiedName`s can now come from many 'sources' -- that string combined with the type should provide enough information to resolve where a particular qualified name is from.

title: Avoid popup flickering on new suggestions
description:
This fixes the popup flickering in a simple way -- we do not hide an existing popup window when we go to get new suggestions from the server. This ensures that:
1. The old popup should remain for the duration of the RPC call, and
2. The popup will automatically be cleared and updated once that RPC call has returned.

title: Fixes for autocompletion within comments, roxygen
description:
NOTE: We can wait until I've also populated this with popup fixes as well for merge.

This PR brings some fixes:
1. We ensure that completions after a `$` or `@` never gets completions from outside contexts,
2. We never provide completions within comments (we may want to tweak this in the future to only disable automatically popped up completions, but allow triggered completions),
3. We only provide Roxygen completions within an roxygen comment (may want to modify similar to above later)

title: check for multiline autocompletion pref in filter
description: (Sorry, missed this in the last PR -- we check the input in two places before giving completion suggestions.)

title: Option for tab to provide multiline autocompletions
description: Let me know if you think this is a good idea (one user actually requested this already on the help forums), and then I can clean up merge conflicts and ping you when ready.

title: Other completion exceptions + small fixes
description: I'll consolidate the next set of features into one PR, but for now this should eliminate any exceptions seen.

title: check that completion from cache is not null in 'usingCache'
Use source index to get completions from current package
description:
NOTE: This could use some review as I'm not fully aware of the most 'idiomatic' ways of generating R objects / lists from C++ code.

This PR generates autocompletions from the source index when working on a package project.

title: Feature/cmd shift k
Remove function auto-popup; fix errors when trying to get help
More R autocompletion additions
description:
- Allow for automatic popup of help in the source editor, but not within the console
- Infer the completion type when the RPC call is executed, and return that as part of the response
- Pop up autocompletion results after hitting enter within a function definition
- Infrastructure for icons in completion popup

title: Tweaks for the new R autocompletion
description:
- Fix function name lookup for the scope tree (for eg. `x[["foo"]] <- function() { ... }`, the associated 'name' of the function is chosen as `x[["foo"]]` -- but note that the debugger is unable to debug such functions)
- Avoid duplicates for scoped variable completions
- Pop up autocompletions after `::`, `$`, `@`
- Some fixes for help popup / lookup (but most of that will be changing with the new UI)
- Some tweaks to file / path completion (continue showing completions after a `/` is inserted to complete a directory)
  Ensure that autocompletion for e.g. `debug(stats::rno|` does not auto-insert parens
- Some miscellaneous code cleanup

title: Limit max.print to be at most 10000
description: If .Rprofile has max.print set to a low value like 100 (common if the user routinely works with datasets that lock up the screen for minutes at a time even with 10000 rows), then just calling options(max.print = 10000) will silently override their wishes.

title: Extract function name from label when setting breakpoints
description: The new function labels that include the function's signature break function breakpoints, which use the label to locate the function by name.

title: Eliminate compiler warnings; add '-Wsign-compare' for OSX
description: Fixes some compiler warnings, and also added `-Wsign-compare` explicitly for OS X (clang).

title: Fix RPubs upload error "invalid 'n' argument"
description:
Fixes a pretty bad bug where 25-75% of RPubs publish attempts seem to fail with this error message.

It seems to have started sometime in the last few weeks, probably when I revamped the RPubs production servers after shellshock. The production servers started returning some (but not all) HTTP responses using [chunked transfer encoding](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chunked_transfer_encoding):

> Chunked transfer encoding is a data transfer mechanism in version 1.1 of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) in which data is sent in a series of "chunks". It uses the Transfer-Encoding HTTP header in place of the Content-Length header, which the earlier version of the protocol would otherwise require.[1] Because the Content-Length header is not used, the sender does not need to know the length of the content before it starts transmitting a response to the receiver. Senders can begin transmitting dynamically-generated content before knowing the total size of that content.
> 
> The size of each chunk is sent right before the chunk itself so that the receiver can tell when it has finished receiving data for that chunk. The data transfer is terminated by a final chunk of length zero.

The readResponse function was expecting every response to have a Content-Length, so it would choke on chunked responses. This is easily fixed in the case of method="curl", as curl handles decoding the chunks for us; we just need to know not to look for a Content-Length, no big deal. In the case of method="internal" though, we need to do the chunk decoding ourselves. Still not too big of a deal, we don't have to worry too much about being fast or robust here as it's <100 bytes of pure-ASCII JSON that's being returned in every case.

title: Include function return types in scope tree
description:
This PR adds a couple more bits:
1. The return type is included in the scope tree,
2. The trailing return type (if declared as e.g. `-> decltype()`) is returned as well,
3. Fill in a missing bit so that `lambda`s properly get their icon.

I think this is probably the limit as far as pure-JavaScript solutions go here; if I revisit this later I'll investigate making async calls to libclang so we can get some nicer formatting, handling of macros, and so on.

![screen shot 2014-10-27 at 8 31 44 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1976582/4803185/0a528bda-5e53-11e4-8807-584efdda8fdf.png)

title: Avoid duplication of environment variables (for Yosemite)
description:
(Maybe overkill, but gives a place to start)

This works around duplicate environment variable issues (specifically `PATH`) on OS X. This ensures that, when setting an environment variable, all environment variables with that name are removed and then the new one is set.

title: Add 'Alt+Enter' as shortcut to execute selection without moving cursor
description: Could be potentially useful -- but I still need to make sure that `Alt + Enter` isn't already tied to other actions within the various browsers / OS / settings we support.

title: Don't attempt to generate a description for null external pointers
description: This fixes an issue caused by the way external pointer objects work in R. When an object containing an `EXTPTRSXP` is saved, the value of the external pointer is not saved. When that object is loaded, it comes back to life with a `null` external pointer, and if routines that access that pointer without checking it, crashes ensue.

title: Add new themes to Preferences->Appearance dialog
description:
Added neon.css and existing (but unused) .css themes to AceThemes.java
and AceThemesResources.java, changed size of Preferences dialog box to
accomodate extended theme list.
![Screen Shot 2013-02-05 at 11 57 37 AM](https://f.cloud.github.com/assets/1776358/128311/56d8f0ea-6fb5-11e2-8b16-c00fa58a7c99.png)

title: update Cobalt style to make strings green
description:
This patch allows Cobalt style to better differenciate between Strings and variables.
Like the Cobalt style of Gedit, Strings now appear in green.

title: modifications to support FreeBSD
description:
First two commits aren't FreeBSD specific but are required, final commit adds a few things to support FreeBSD.

I've tested this on FreeBSD 9.0-RELEASE for both server and desktop versions.
- gcc-4.6.4
- R-2.15.0 and R-2.15.1
- qt-4.8.2

title: Justacec/remove projects from menu
description:
Previously I had looked for a way to clear out the list of recently used projects from the projects popup menu.  I was instructed that the only way I could do so was to remove my settings directory and start fresh.  I decided that this morning I would see if I could add a menu option to the projects menu to clear this out.  After some investigation I saw that most of the code was already in place.  I have added in the necessary code to do the minimum thing which is to simply clear the MRU list for the projects.

As indicated earlier, this is the minimum thing that can be done.  I think that there a several possible improvements:
1. Allow the user to selectively remove individual popup items from a dialog window that would be dedicated to the management of the MRU instance for projects. (Or have action buttons on each project MRU item, say a little "x" symbol, that the user could click which would remove the need for a popup.)  
2. Do a sanity check and automatically remove the MRU item if the corresponding project file does not exist.
3. A combination of 1 and 2.
4. Remove the menu separator and the menu item to clear the contents if there are no current items in the MRU list.

title: Continuous Integration with TravisCI
description:
Adds a first TravisCi configuration. It currently just makes sure RStudio Desktop can be successfully built.
The script part can of course be extended to compile other variants of the project and to also execute some tests.

It currently takes about 40 minutes to build the project from scratch.
Problem though is that the test fails if the build time exceeds 50 minutes and that can sometimes happen. But maybe this all does not make sense for the project and you have your own CI solution somewhere.

title: Break on Error: improve heuristics for locating the error origin
description:
This change fixes a recently reported bug in which the wrong frame in the callstack is chosen as the source of the error.

Today, the Break on Error code presumes that the error is raised with `stop(...)`. In this situation, we don't want to show the frame for `stop` itself; we want to show the frame that invoked `stop`. RStudio uses a baked-in offset that correctly locates this frame.

However, primitive functions can raise an error _without_ calling `stop`. In this situation, there are fewer frames on the stack between the error handler and the frame that we want to show, and the baked-in offset is wrong.

The fix is to presume that the function raising the error is the very last one before we reach error-handling code. Most of the time, this will be `stop`, and when it is, we'll go one frame further. (We'll now also deal more gracefully with `stopifnot`).

title: Bugfix/deep codesign
Fix runaway recursion resulting from Step Into
description:
This change fixes a problem reported by @tareefk in which stepping into a call while debugging at the top level can cause a runaway recursion tail that eventually exhausts the stack and crashes the session.

The problem is in the way that R handles the Step Into command. It has a global variable `R_BrowserLastCommand` that stores the last command entered at the `Browse[N]>` prompt. When this variable is set to `'s'`, the next function executed--_no matter what it is_--will be debugged. 

There are operations we perform on every console prompt (including building the environment pane if necessary) that can trigger R code to run. When that code runs, it runs R functions, and because `R_BrowserLastCommand` is still `s`, those functions get debugged. When they're debugged we get a new debug prompt, which makes the functions run again, and so on, and so forth. 

We let the R Core team know about this bug a few months ago (see [R-Project Bug 15770](https://bugs.r-project.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=15770)), and they fixed it: https://github.com/wch/r-source/commit/8b672fe4f178aac0d2bea64097befb36b9f824f3. Unfortunately the fix applies to functions parsed and executed at the console, not (always) to functions that are invoked via the C API that RStudio calls. 

Two other small notes:
- This problem existed in R 3.1, but seems to be easier to hit now (possibly new changes in R 3.1.1). 
- Any part of the code where we evaluate R statements or execute R expressions at a time when the user could be debugging needs to be guarded. This is a lot of surface area. I've covered the major chokepoints but it might be worth a backlog item to look for others.

title: Fix getpwuid errors on systems using winbind
description:
Hi,

I've been trying to get RStudio Server to run in an enterprise environment where users are authenticated via pam_winbind. I have the same problems that others have already reported, see this thread and the one linked from there:

http://support.rstudio.org/help/discussions/problems/914-pam-authentication-and-winbind-revisited

What was going wrong here is that pam_winbind talks to winbindd through a socket, and you close all open file descriptors - https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/master/src/cpp/server/util/system/PosixSystem.cpp#L396 - before determining the current user a few lines later. Simply moving the getpwuid call before the file descriptor closing worked around the issue at hand for me, but of course getpwuid will remain broken in the child process, so maybe a more general fix should be considered...

ciao,
Thomas

title: Support for debugging without source references
description:
This change introduces the ability to use the source debugger on functions that don't have source references. In most cases, it can show and step through code just as if the code had references.

Showing deparsed functions requires few changes, but simulating source references for those functions to create accurate debug highlighting and stepping is a little more involved. There are two distinct strategies used to simulate references for functions whose content is deparsed rather than derived from actual source references:
1. For the currently executing function, the debug outputs from R (i.e. the statements printed at the console) are captured and located in the deparsed function representation. In nearly all cases this enough to uniquely identify the executing segment; in cases where it is not, an educated guess is made--i.e. when stepping, the next statement is the most likely target, and closer statements are preferred.
2. For all other functions, the highlighting is derived from deparsed calls--we look for the call object that invoked the next context, deparse it, and find it in the deparsed invoker. 

No change has been made to which functions are considered "internal" (even though these are debuggable now). Because there are pathological cases in which the highlight matching could be off, we also now show a warning bar when debugging in deparsed code.

Display Packrat pending actions in the Action Center
description:
This change suggests snapshot, restore, or clean actions in the Action Center according to the state reported by Packrat. Rough overview:
- The server tracks the last known resolved state of the Packrat lockfile and libraries.
- When the current state is not the last known resolved state, the server asks Packrat for a list of actions that would resolve the state. This list is included in the package state sent to the client.
- The client shows the list of actions in the Action Center, along with a button to perform groups of actions. 

It's stable enough to build on, although it does not contain all of the aesthetic changes we've discussed and will likely still require some tuning for accuracy.

title: Automatic snapshotting for Packrat projects
description:
This change enables automatic snapshotting for Packrat projects. The automatic snapshot is performed asynchronously by a separate R process, and performs exactly the same operations as Packrat's existing automatic snapshot mechanism (in fact it retrieves these operations from Packrat). Packrat's existing automatic snapshot mechanism takes a snapshot every time a command is executed; the goal of this change is generally to enable automatic snapshotting but to snapshot only when the library has undergone a meaningful change. 

Once the restore dialog changes are in, we can plug them into the new client event emitted when a restore is needed.

title: Package pane improvements for Packrat
description:
This change has two main effects:
- Show packrat status in the packages pane when packrat mode is on.
- Restore (to the greatest degree reasonable) the existing code and appearance of the packages pane when packrat mode is off.

The former is largely accomplished by using `list_packages_packrat`, a new RPC that returns an augmented version of the data returned by `list_packages` (`PackageInfo` -> `PackratPackageInfo`). 

The latter uses a few more if statements than I'd like. In most circumstances I think better architecture would use a class derived from `PackagesPane` to extend the pane with Packrat-specific actions and logic, but since this class is not instantiated directly it's a little less obvious how to create the right instance at runtime (later we'd also need to swap instances out on the fly); let me know if you feel the current approach needs rethinking.

title: Add keyboard shortcut reference card overlay
description:
Creates a "quick reference" keyboard shortcut card that can be displayed from the Help menu, or via `Alt+Shift+K`. 

The card is built from the existing keyboard shortcut information in `Commands.cmd.xml`, with two additions:
- The shortcuts are now organized into groups (`<shortcutgroup>`). This has no effect on their runtime operation but permits the shortcuts to be declaratively separated.
- There is a new type of shortcut: unbound shortcuts. These are distinguished from regular shortcuts by the the lack of a bound command `refid`, and exist only for documentation of shortcuts that are handled outside of the shortcut manager (e.g. ACE shortcuts). 

When the reference card is invoked, the shortcuts are sorted by group and displayed in a translucent overlay, which is dismissed after being acknowledged by any keypress or mouse click. 

This doesn't replace the existing keyboard shortcut docs, since not all the keyboard shortcuts that exist would fit on a screen, and some of the situations in which shortcuts can be used and/or instructions for invoking them are too complex to summarize in the reference card.

title: Justacec/code block
description:
I have been wanting to have the ability to execute the code contained in a section.  Currently I have to highlight the code I want to execute and then hit the execute button.  While this works it is time consuming.  Additionally, organizing an analysis into logical blocks (sections) that correspond to different phases of the analysis is very convenient and has proven to be very productive in Matlab.  

In this implementation, if the cursor is positioned inside a valid code block and the "Run Code Section" menu option is selected, R will execute the code inside the bounds of the current section (the section that contains the active cursor).  The action can also be initiated by using the "Alt+Enter" hotkey which is similar to the "Command+Enter" hotkey for a single line or a selected block.  I have also added an icon to the icon bar just above the editor to highlight this new feature.

In this discussion a code section is defined by the standard "## <Name> ----" format.

title: Fix bug: debugger can show base environment on launch
description:
This bug occurs when no function on the callstack has source references; the easiest way to repro is to call debug(foo::bar); foo::bar(), where foo is a package for which source references are not available, and bar is a function in that package.

The problem is that RStudio walks the callstack looking for a function containing source references, and when it reaches the end and still hasn't found one, it returns the last function it examined. In this specific case what we actually want it to do is to return the top of the stack, so that the user has some context for the debugger (even if they don't have sources available).

The fix is to detect when we're in this case (no sourcerefs anywhere), and to:

a) debug in the context of the top function on the stack, and

b) show internal functions in the UI (since there are no other kind on the stack)

title: Fix user-reported annoyances in debugging features

title: prevent osx mavericks AppNap when the R console is busy
description:
This adds support for calling the AppNap API on OSX Mavericks to indicate that RStudio shouldn't be put in a low-power-consumption state when the R console is busy. See this discussion:

https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-mac/2013-December/010581.html

See also this description of AppNap:

https://developer.apple.com/library/mac/releasenotes/MacOSX/WhatsNewInOSX/Articles/MacOSX10_9.html

We take a conservative approach here, flagging RStudio as active but indicating that the full system can still go to sleep. This essentially provides the pre-Mavericks behavior (a running R console didn't count as something the system would stay awake for). We could indicate that the system itself shouldn't sleep, but this seems aggressive as it could result in a user's machine (surprisingly) never going to sleep when something as innocuous as a running httpuv application is keeping the R console busy.

title: Fix debug stepping problems when debugger is invoked from R RPC calls
description:
A recent change for error management broke this scenario. We don't want to see error management functions on the callstack, so we hide them (and in fact all `addRpcHandler` functions). We also don't update line numbers in this case since we don't want the editor to show the RStudio error handler, which is technically the function on top of the stack. 

The fix is just to avoid treating user functions as hidden when they are invoked _by_ a debugger internal function.

title: Fix wrong value display for a special case of evaluated promises
description:
Garrett found a bug at JSM in which the wrong value is shown for an object in the environment pane. It happens when the following are all true:
- The object is a promise
- The object is assigned a new value in the _same statement_ in which it is first evaluated
- That statement is stepped over (vs. being run past)

In this case, we'll wind up showing the value of the evaluated promise rather than the new value assigned to the object.

The fix is to stop tracking variables as unevaluated promises once we've processed an assignment to a variable of the same name.

title: Fix problems in advanced package breakpoint use
description: Set and clear breakpoints in multiple function copies when developing a package, or when the breakpoint being set is part of a package.

title: Fix problems related to breakpoints in packages
description:
- Fix: Console warnings sometimes appear on package load
- Fix: It isn't possible to set a breakpoint in packages that aren't on the search path

After talking with Joe and Hadley, I believe that there is still one more fix needed to make foreign package breakpoints feel seamless: we need to set breakpoints on every copy of the function if more than one copy exists, so that the breakpoint will get hit no matter which copy is invoked. This fix is nontrivial and will require a few hours of coding and testing. If you'd prefer to wait for that fix to merge the branch, I should have it in by EOD today.

title: Add grid view for environment pane
description:
This change factors the embedded `ScrollingDataGrid` out of the formerly monolithic class `EnvironmentObjects`, and replaces it with an new abstraction, `EnvironmentObjectDisplay`. There are two implementations of `EnvironmentObjectDisplay`:
- `EnvironmentObjectList`, which contains the existing view of the environment.
- `EnvironmentObjectGrid`, which contains a new view that shows the environment as a grid.

The change also includes the environment selector, and code to support listing and switching between arbitrary environments.

title: Add contextual error UI and IDE-provided error handlers
Fix highlighting bug when returning to unfiltered state; make highlight color more subtle
Filter objects in the environment by name or value
Improve environment pane handling of large objects and long vectors
description:
This change includes the following fixes:
- Support for long vectors. These were previously problematic primarily because we called `Rf_length` directly. I've moved a large chunk of the variable description logic from C++ to R, which allows us to just use R's `length()` without creating a need for us to know about and depend upon this particular R internal.  
- Improved handling of large objects. When an object is large, we no longer do anything that directly accesses its value (e.g. calling `str()`). Instead, we print the class, element count, and size--e.g. "Large list (129 elements, 8.5 Mb)". The threshold for large objects is set somewhat arbitrarily at 500K. 
- Quieting errors from `str()`. Previously if `str()` threw an error we'd print it to the console; since `str()` is not perfect it does throw errors in some edge cases (Hadley has found some S4 MethodDescriptions it chokes on). We now eat these since the errors aren't user actionable.
- Improved handling of pathological objects. It is no longer necessary in most cases to pass the `SEXP` representing an object through the RStudio -> R interface, so language objects and symbols are now more robust.  (Hadley has supplied an ample number of pathological objects over the last few months. :-))
- Minor UI improvements--when an object's value experiences a simple change, its cell in the environment pane will pulse light blue very briefly. (This might be too noisy, let's talk about whether this is useful or the right treatment). Object tooltips now also include the size of the object.

One other note on long vectors: It is possible that we'll have to fix `r::sexp::length` and/or all our direct use of `Rf_length` so that large vectors can be safely passed through any RStudio codepath, but a brief audit turned up no usage of these functions in places where a long vector `SEXP` seems useful and/or likely. If you do think that this is something we need to undertake, happy to do so.

I understand that properly deciding if an object is a data frame requires checking all `class` members, not only the first (cf. `getSingleClass()`). title: Fix legacy user ID test on server builds
description:
### Intent

`LegacyObfuscatedUserIdPreservesPreviousBoundary`, added in #19153, fails on server builds. It expects the fixed IDs `"1003e"` and `"fffff"`, which are correct only for desktop builds. Server builds define `RSTUDIO_SERVER`, and `OBFUSCATE_USER_ID` then changes each ID. On a server build, the test gets `"9e1a7"` and `"c83bf"`. The `core Tests` stage in rstudio-pro CI fails on this test.

### Approach

The test no longer compares with fixed strings. First, it sets the minimum uid to 0 and gets the ID for the boundary uid, `1000 + 0xFFFFF`. With a minimum of 0, no uid above `0xFFFFF` is remapped, so this is the ID from before the boundary fix. Then, with a minimum uid of 1000, the test checks that:

- `legacyObfuscatedUserId()` gives this old ID for the boundary uid.
- `legacyObfuscatedUserId()` and `obfuscatedUserId()` give different IDs for the boundary uid.
- The two functions give the same ID for the other uids in the existing loop.

`ObfuscatedUserIdRemapsLargeUidsUpToMaxUid` already checks the new ID for the boundary uid, so this test does not check it again.

### Automated Tests

This PR changes only the test. I did not build `rstudio-tests` locally. A standalone copy of `obfuscatedUserIdImpl()` ran the new checks with both forms of `OBFUSCATE_USER_ID`:

| Build | Old ID | New ID | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Server | `9e1a7` | `c83bf` | pass |
| Desktop | `1003e` | `fffff` | pass |

The server values are the same as the values in the failed rstudio-pro run. If `legacyObfuscatedUserId()` also remaps the boundary uid, the first check fails.

### QA Notes

None. The change is only in a unit test.

### Documentation

None.

### Checklist

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` (not applicable: test-only change)
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility) (not applicable)
- [x] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [ ] This PR passes all local unit tests (not run locally; see Automated Tests)

title: Keep the Console pane's selected tab on Focus Next/Previous Pane
description:
Fixes #19183.

Focus Next Pane (F6) and Focus Previous Pane (Shift+F6) no longer switch the Console pane to its Console tab when another tab, such as Terminal, is selected there.

- `PaneManager.focusWindow()`: a stray `;` made the Console branch always run `activateConsole` and return. With it removed, the Console pane's selected tab stays selected and gets `setFocus()`. First, the Console window is raised through `WindowFrame.onEnsureVisible(new EnsureVisibleEvent(false))`, which restores a minimized pane and moves an active zoom to it without selecting the tab again. Selecting it again would rerun the tab's `onSelected()`, and Terminal's starts a shell when none is open. The `ensureVisible(true)` call now runs only for TabSet panes, the only ones that reached it before.
- `TerminalPane.setFocus()` was empty. It now focuses the selected terminal, using the deferred focus-and-retry that tab selection already used, now shared as `focusTerminal()`. With no terminal, or one that still hasn't loaded after the retry, it focuses the pane's first control.

`e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/layout/focus_adjacent_pane.test.ts` walks Shift+F6 into the Console pane with Terminal, Console, and Background Jobs selected, with the pane minimized, with another pane zoomed, and after the last terminal exits, where it checks that no new terminal starts.

Related problems found while investigating, not addressed here: #19191, #19192, #19193.
